# 牛津短语动词词典


1148 个动词，3528 个义项。例句里加粗的是当前这条短语动词。


<table>
<thead><tr><th>动词</th><th>短语动词</th><th>释义</th><th>例句</th></tr></thead>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>abide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈbide by sth (formal)</b></td><td class="c3">接受；遵照；遵循(规章制度等)<br><span class="en">to accept a rule, a Law, an agreement, a decision, etc. and obey It</span></td><td class="c4">Members must <b>abide by</b> the rules of the club.<br>会员必须遵守俱乐部的规定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>abound</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈbound in/with sth</b></td><td class="c3">大量存在；盛产；富于<br><span class="en">to have a lot of sth; to contain a lot of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The rivers there <b>abound in</b>/with fish.<br>那儿的河里有许多鱼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>abstain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>abˈstain from sth<br>abˈstain from doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">避免；克制<br><span class="en">to decide not to do or have sth, especially sth that you like or enjoy, because it is bad for your health or considered morally wrong</span></td><td class="c4">Pregnant women are advised to <b>abstain from</b> alcohol.<br>建议孕妇戒酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>accede</b></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcede to sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">反对之后转而答应；应允(请求)<br><span class="en">to agree to or allow sth that sb has asked for, often after you have opposed it for a while</span></td><td class="c4">The government <b>acceded to Public pressure to</b> review the tax.<br>政府在公众压力下同意检讨税制。<br>Have all our requests been <b>acceded to</b>?<br>我们的请求全部被接受了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>account</b></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcount for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指；事故或自然灾害发生之后了解；查明下落或；命运<br><span class="en">to know where sb/sth is or what has happened to them, especially after an accident or a natural disaster</span></td><td class="c4">All the people who were working in the building have now been <b>accounted for</b>.<br>当时正在大楼里工作的人现在都有了下落。<br>There are three files that I can't <b>account for</b>.<br>有三份文件我找不到。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcount for sth</b></td><td class="c3">说明；是…的原因<br><span class="en">to explain how or why sth happened; to be the explanation for sth</span></td><td class="c4">How do you <b>account for</b> the fact that the box has disappeared?<br>盒子不见了，你如何解释。<br>Poor hygiene may have <b>accounted for</b> the spread of the disease.<br>卫生状况差可能是这种疾病蔓延的根源。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcount for sth</b></td><td class="c3">构成(比例或数量)<br><span class="en">to be a particular part of sth; to be a particular amount</span></td><td class="c4">Car crime <b>accounted for</b> 28% of all reported offences.<br>汽车犯罪占所有举报罪案的28%。<br>Wages <b>account for</b> less than half of the budget.<br>工资开支在预算中所占比例不到一半。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcount for sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指计算成本时考虑到；估计；顾及<br><span class="en">to consider particular facts or circumstances when you are making a decision about sth, especially when you are calculating the cost of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The cost of the film was <b>accounted for</b> in the calculation of the cost of the service.<br>服务成本中计入了胶片的费用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>accustom</b></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈcustom sb/yourself to doing sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使适应；习惯于<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself familiar with sth; to become used to sth</span></td><td class="c4">It took a while for her eyes to <b>accustom</b> themselves to the dark.<br>过了一会儿，她的眼睛才适应了黑暗。<br>It shouldn't take long to <b>accustom</b> your students to working in groups.<br>你的学生应该很快就会习惯分组学习的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ace</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ace sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打败；战胜(以获得重要地位)<br><span class="en">to defeat sb in order to obtain an important position or rank</span></td><td class="c4">The company <b>aced out</b> its biggest rival to win the contract.<br>公司挫败最大的对手，贏得了合同。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ache</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈache for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">渴望；热盼<br><span class="en">to have a strong desire for sb/sth or to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas <b>aching for</b> home.<br>我归心似箭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>acquaint</b></td><td class="c2"><b>acˈquaint sb/yourself with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使了解；使认识<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself familiar with or aware of sth</span></td><td class="c4">He decided to take his son along and <b>acquaint</b> him with the business.<br>他决定带上儿子，让他熟悉一下生意。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>act</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈact as sth</b></td><td class="c3">充当(角色)；担任(工作)；起…作用<br><span class="en">to perform a particular role or function</span></td><td class="c4">Will you <b>act as</b> interpreter for us?<br>你做我们的翻译好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈact on sth (also ˈact upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">遵照…行事；根据…办理<br><span class="en">to do sth as a result of advice, information, instructions, etc. that you have received</span></td><td class="c4">The police were <b>acting on</b> information from a member of the public.<br>警方根据一名群众的举报采取了行动。<br>I was just <b>acting on</b> instructions.<br>我不过是奉命行事而已。<br>If my advice had been <b>acted</b> <b>upon</b>, this would never have happened.<br>当初要是听从我的建议，绝对不会发生这种事情。o8n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌact sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">将…表演出来<br><span class="en">to perform a story or events that have happened or might happen, as if you are performing a play</span></td><td class="c4">The teacher read a story and the children <b>acted it out</b>.<br>老师讲故事，孩子们把故事表演出来。<br>She <b>acted out</b> her fantasies of pop stardom in front of her bedroom mirror.<br>她在卧室镜子前手舞足蹈，幻想自己成了流行歌星。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌact ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">捣蛋；调皮；淘气<br><span class="en">to make sb annoyed by behaving badly, trying to get attention, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The kids have been <b>acting up</b> all day.'<br>孩子们一整天都在闹个没完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌact ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">机器或身体部位出毛病；不正常<br><span class="en">if a machine or part of the body acts up, it does not work as it should</span></td><td class="c4">The car's <b>acting up</b> again.<br>车又坏。<br>My ankle is <b>acting up</b> (= is painful and causing problems).<br>我的脚踝疼了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>add</b></td><td class="c2"><b>add ˈon<br>ˌadd ˈon to sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">扩建；增建(房屋等)<br><span class="en">to build an extra room or rooms on to a house or other building</span></td><td class="c4">They decided to <b>add on</b> rather than move.<br>他们决定把房子打建一下，不搬走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌadd sth ˈon<br>ˌadd sth ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">附加；添加<br><span class="en">to attach sth extra</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>added</b> £2 on to the bill.<br>他在账单上加了两。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈadd to sth</b></td><td class="c3">增加；添加；扩大<br><span class="en">to increase the size, amount, number, etc. of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Taking the children with us would only <b>add to</b> our problems.<br>带上孩子只会给我们添乱。<br>The food at the hotel is of a very high standard. <b>Add to</b> this the quality of the rooms and the service and it is clear why this is such a popular hotel.<br>这家旅馆的饭菜很上档次，加上客房以及服务质量也很好，难径会大受欢迎。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>add toˈgether<br>add sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">合成；汇合而成；累加而成<br><span class="en">to come together to produce sth; to join two or more things, numbers, etc. together to produce sth</span></td><td class="c4">The games, the dancing and the good food all <b>added together</b> to make a memorable occasion.<br>游戏、 舞蹈和美食共同成就了一段难以忘怀的经历。<br>When all the different factors are <b>added together</b>, I can understand her decision.<br>综合考虑各种因素，我能够体谅她的决定。<br><b>Add the two numbers together</b> and divide by three.<br>把两数相加，再除以三。l。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌadd ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">合计达；总额为；总值是<br><span class="en">if two or more numbers or figures add up to sth, they make a total of sth total sth (especially business) to reach a particular number or amount when added together</span></td><td class="c4">The cost of all the equipment you need for a baby <b>adds up to</b> a considerable sum.<br>婴儿所需物品的费用总数相当可观。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌadd ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">显示；意味着；结果<br><span class="en">to show sth; to have a particular meaning or result</span></td><td class="c4">His evidence didn't really <b>add up to</b> much (= gave us very little information).<br>他的证词其实说明不了什么问题。<br>All in all, it <b>adds up to</b> a pretty desperate situation.<br>总而言之，这意味着形势相当危急。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>agree</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈgree to sth</b></td><td class="c3">答应；同意；允许<br><span class="en">to say yes; to say that you will do what sb wants or that you will allow sth to happen</span></td><td class="c4">Do you think hell <b>agree to</b> their proposal?<br>你认为他会接受他们的提议吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈgree with sb</b></td><td class="c3">赞同；与…持同样观点<br><span class="en">(about/on sth) to have the same opinion as sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>agreed with</b> them about the need for change.<br>他与他们看法一致，认为需要变革。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈgree with sb</b></td><td class="c3">使惬意；使健康；适合<br><span class="en">to make sb feel happy or healthy</span></td><td class="c4">You look great! Marriage obviously <b>agrees with</b> YOu.<br>你容光焕发啊！显然婚姻生活让你非常滋润。<br>Mushrooms don't <b>agree with</b> me (= they make me feel ill/sick).<br>我吃了蘑菇就会感觉不适。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈgree with sth (grammar)</b></td><td class="c3">在数；性或人称方面与…致；呼应</td><td class="c4">In French, adjectives <b>agree with</b> their nouns.<br>在法语中，形容词必须与其名词保持一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>aim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈaim at sth<br>ˈaim at doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">致力追求；努力取得；目的在于<br><span class="en">to try to achieve sth; to have sth as your aim</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>aiming at</b> a sports scholarship.<br>她在争取获得一项体育奖学金。<br>We need to <b>aim at</b> increasing exports.<br>我们要努力增加出口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈaim sth at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">言行针对；指向；以…为对象<br><span class="en">if you aim sth at a particular person or group, you do or say sth that you intend to have an effect on them</span></td><td class="c4">The advertising campaign is <b>aimed primarily at</b> young people.<br>这次广告宣传活动主要是针对年轻人。<br>I was not <b>aiming my remarks at</b> you.<br>我的话不是冲你说的。态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>alight</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈlight on/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">突然注意到；意外发现；碰巧想到<br><span class="en">to notice sb/sth suddenly; to find or think of sth by chance</span></td><td class="c4">My eye <b>alighted on</b> an old book.<br>我的目光突然落到一本旧书上。<br>He finally <b>alighted on</b> a solution.<br>他最后灵机一动想出一个解决办法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>allow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>alˈlow for sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…包括在内；考虑到；顾及<br><span class="en">to include sth when you are calculating sth or planning sth</span></td><td class="c4">Add an extra ten minutes to your journey time to <b>allow for</b> the traffic.<br>考虑到交通状况，你的行程得额外多算十分钟。<br>This had not been <b>allowed for</b> in the budget.<br>预算没有把这个考虑在内。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>amount</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈmount to sth not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The cost of the trip <b>amounted</b> to well over £500.<br>这次旅行的费用远远超过了500英镑。<br>The money I pay in tax <b>amounts</b> to about 40% of my salary.<br>交税用掉我工资的40% 左右。<br>It all <b>amounts</b> to a lot of hard work.<br>这一切意味着大量艰苦的工作。<br>The information we have doesn't <b>amount</b> to much.<br>我们掌握的信息没多大价值。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>amp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>amp sth ˈup <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">提高…的音量；增强；放大<br><span class="en">to make sth louder or stronger</span></td><td class="c4">The crowd <b>amped up</b> their approval when he started to sing.<br>他刚开口唱歌，人群就爆发出巨大的欢呼声。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>angle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈangle for sth often</b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>angling</b> for an invitation.<br>她正设法弄一张请柬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>answer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>answer ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">自辩；抗辩；反驳<br><span class="en">to defend yourself against sth bad that sb has said about you</span></td><td class="c4">It's not fair to criticize without giving her the chance to <b>answer back</b>.<br>批评她却不给她机会辦白，有失公平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>answer ˈback<br>answer sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">小孩还嘴；犟嘴<br><span class="en">if a child answers back or answers you back, they reply rudely</span></td><td class="c4">He's a rude little boy, always <b>answering his mother back</b>.<br>他年纪小，脾气坏，老是和妈妈顶嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈanswer for sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…承担责任；因…受到责备<br><span class="en">to be responsible for sth bad; to accept the blame for sth</span></td><td class="c4">She has a lot to <b>answer for</b>.<br>她负有很大的责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈanswer to sb (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">为某事对…负有责任；向…作出交代<br><span class="en">to have to explain your actions to sb; to show that your actions are right or reasonable</span></td><td class="c4">You will <b>answer to</b> me for any damage to the car.<br>汽车有任何损坏，我都找你负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈanswer to sth</b></td><td class="c3">被称作；叫做<br><span class="en">to be called sth; to recognize a name as your own</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>answer to</b> either Susan or Sue.<br>叫我苏珊或是苏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ante</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ante ˈup<br>ˌante ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">付清(欠款中应摊的份额)<br><span class="en">to pay a share of an amount of money that a group of people owe</span></td><td class="c4">The check arrived and we all <b>anted up</b>.<br>账单到了，我们都付清了各自的欠款。<br>Some parents <b>ante up</b> big bucks to send their kids to prep school.<br>有些父母拿出大笔钱送子女上预科学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>appeal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>apˈpeal for sth/sb<br>apˈpeal for sb</b></td><td class="c3">恳求；呼吁<br><span class="en">to do sth to make a serious and urgent request for sth/sb or for sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">The government has <b>appealed for</b> calm.<br>政府呼吁保持镇静。<br>The police <b>appealed for</b> witnesses to come forward.<br>警方呼吁目击者出来作证。<br>The victim's family has <b>appealed for</b> help in tracking down the killer.<br>受害者家属请求帮助抓捕凶手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>apˈpeal to sb</b></td><td class="c3">使感兴趣；受…欢迎；对…有吸引力<br><span class="en">if sth appeals to you, you like it or find it interesting and attractive</span></td><td class="c4">The prospect of camping didn't <b>appeal to</b> me.<br>我对露营的想法没有兴趣。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>apˈpeal to sth</b></td><td class="c3">通过入情入理的劝说打动<br><span class="en">to try to persuade sb to do sth by reminding them that it is a good, reasonable thing to do</span></td><td class="c4">Maybe if you <b>appeal to</b> her better nature (= her kindness), you can get her to help.<br>也许你央求她发发善心，就能得到她的帮助。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>apply</b></td><td class="c2"><b>apˈply for sth</b></td><td class="c3">通常以书面形式申请；寻求得到<br><span class="en">to make a formal request, usually in writing, for sth such as a job or a place at college, university, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>applied for</b> a new passport.<br>我申办了一本新护照。<br>My has <b>applied for</b> a place at Warwick University.<br>我儿子已申请就读沃里克大学。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>apˈprise sb of sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">将…通知…；向…告知…<br><span class="en">to inform sb of sth</span></td><td class="c4">We were fully <b>apprised of</b> the situation.<br>我们完全知晓了当时的状况。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>argue</b></td><td class="c2"><b>argue sb ˈinto sth<br>ˌargue sb ˈinto doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">说服…做…<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to do sth by giving them a large number of reasons why they should do it</span></td><td class="c4">Imanaged to <b>argue him into</b> going back home to talk to his parents.<br>我终于说服他回家去和父母对话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌargue sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">常指；激烈地彻底辩论；辩个明白<br><span class="en">to discuss all the details of an idea, a plan, etc., often in an excited or angry way, until you reach a decision</span></td><td class="c4">The issues have all been <b>argued out</b> at great length.<br>这些问题经过了很长时间的辩论，均已得到解决。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>arrive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>arˈrive at sth</b></td><td class="c3">达成(协议)；作出(决议)；得出(结论)<br><span class="en">to agree on sth or to find sth after discussing and thinking about it</span></td><td class="c4">They had both <b>arrived at</b> the same conclusion.<br>他俩得出了同样的结论。<br>It didn't take long to <b>arrive at</b> a decision.<br>没过多久便作出了决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>arse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>arse aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE,A,slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">鬼混；闲荡；混日子<br><span class="en">to behave in a silly or annoying way and waste time instead of doing what you are supposed to be doing</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>arsing about</b> and give me my bag.<br>别瞎闹了，把我的包还给我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ascribe</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈscribe sth to sb</b></td><td class="c3">认为作品；言论等出自某人<br><span class="en">to consider that sth has been written, painted, spoken or created by a Partcular person</span></td><td class="c4">This play is usually <b>ascribed to</b> Shakespeare.<br>这部戏剧通常被认为是莎士比亚创作的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ask</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈask after sb</b></td><td class="c3">问候；问好；探问<br><span class="en">to ask for news about sb and how they are, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Did she <b>ask after</b> me in her letter?<br>她在信中问起我了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ask sb ˈback (to sth) <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一起外出后邀请…去自己象<br><span class="en">to invite sb to come back to your house with you for a drink, etc. when you are both out together</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>asked him back</b> for a coffee.<br>回来时我邀请他来我家喝杯咖啡。<br>We couldn't have <b>asked</b> for better weather.<br>天气再好不过了。<br>A beautiful house, husband and children. What more could you <b>ask</b> for?<br>漂亮的房子、丈夫和孩寸。你还能再著望什么呢。<br><b>Ask</b> for the station if you get lost.<br>如果迷路了，就问去车站的路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ask sb ˈin/ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">邀请…进(尤指家里)来<br><span class="en">to invite sb to come into the room or building that you are in, especially your home</span></td><td class="c4">Aren't you going to <b>ask me in</b>? It's cold out here.<br>你不请我进屋吗？外面很冷。<br>She <b>asked me into</b> her office for a chat.<br>她请我进她的办公室聊聊。<br>We must <b>ask the neighbours in</b> for coffee.<br>我们应该请邻居来家里喝杯咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ask sb ˈover/ˈround (BrE) (AmE ˌask sb aˈround)</b></td><td class="c3">邀请…来家里做客<br><span class="en">to invite sb to come and visit you in your home</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>asked me round</b> for dinner.<br>她请我去她家吃饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>aspire</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈspire to sth</b></td><td class="c3">渴望得到；有志成就<br><span class="en">to have a strong desire to gain or achieve sth</span></td><td class="c4">He's never really <b>aspired to</b> great wealth.<br>他从未真正渴求过巨额财富。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>associate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>asˈsociate with sb</b></td><td class="c3">与(不被认同的人)密切交往；和…厮混<br><span class="en">to be involved with or spend a lot of time with sb or with a group of people, especially people that sb else does not approve of</span></td><td class="c4">I don't like the people you <b>associate with</b>.<br>我不喜欢你结交的那些人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>asˈsociate yourself with sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">表示赞同<br><span class="en">to say that you agree with sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">They do not want to <b>associate themselves with</b> spending cuts and tax increases.<br>他们不想表态赞成削减经费和增税。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>attend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>atˈtend to sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">处理；应付；照顾；护理<br><span class="en">to deal with or take responsibility for sth; to give practical help to sb who needs it</span></td><td class="c4">I have some urgent business to <b>attend to</b>.<br>我有一些急事要处理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>attribute</b></td><td class="c2"><b>atˈtribute sth to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…归因于；认为…是由于<br><span class="en">to consider that sth is caused by a particular person or thing</span></td><td class="c4">His success can be <b>attributed largely to</b> hard work.<br>他的成功可以说主要是靠勤奋。<br>She said she was not going to <b>attribute</b> blame or seek revenge for what had happened.<br>事已至此，她说不想怨天尤人或寻求报复。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>auction</b></td><td class="c2"><b>auction sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">拍卖处理(尤指不再需要的物品)<br><span class="en">to sell sth at an auction, especially sth that sb no longer needs or wants</span></td><td class="c4">The house and all its contents will be <b>auctioned off</b> next week.<br>下周将拍卖掉这所房子和房中所有物品。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>avail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈvail yourself of sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常为改善状况使用；利用<br><span class="en">to make use of sth; to take advantage of sth, usually to improve your situation</span></td><td class="c4">Guests are encouraged to <b>avail themselves of</b> all the hotel's facilities.<br>欢迎客人使用宾馆的各种设施。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>average</b></td><td class="c2"><b>average ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">达到平均数；最终持平<br><span class="en">to result in a fair or equal amount over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">Sometimes I do the cooking and sometimes my flatmate does. It <b>averages out</b> over a month.<br>有时我做饭，有时室友做饭。一个月下来，我们做饭的次数不相上下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>average ˈout at sth</b></td><td class="c3">平均数为；平均达到<br><span class="en">to have a particular amount as the average over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">The time she spends practising the piano <b>averages out at</b> about an hour a day.<br>她练钢琴的时间为平均每天一小时左右。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>awaken</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈwaken to sth<br>aˈwaken sb to sth (formal)</b></td><td class="c3">使意识到；(使)察觉到；(使)醒悟到<br><span class="en">to become aware of sth, or to make sb become aware of sth, and its possible results</span></td><td class="c4">People are gradually <b>awakening to</b> their rights.<br>人们正逐渐意识到自己的权利。<br>The public has been <b>awakened to</b> the full horror of the situation.<br>公众完全认识到了这一状况多么恐怖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbag sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把(通常指大量物品)装进袋里<br><span class="en">to put sth, usually large amounts of sth, into a bag or bags</span></td><td class="c4">The vegetables are <b>bagged up</b> on the farm and then sent out to the market.<br>疏莱在农场装袋后，发送到市场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbail ˈout<br>bail ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从即将坠毁的飞机中跳伞；紧急跳伞<br><span class="en">to jump out of a plane that is going to crash, using a parachute (=a large piece of cloth that opens out like an umbrella and makes people fall slowly and safely)</span></td><td class="c4">The crew just had time to <b>bail</b> <b>out</b>.<br>机组人员刚好来得及跳伞逃生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbail ˈout<br>bail ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">退出；不再参与<br><span class="en">to escape from a situation that you no longer want to be involved in</span></td><td class="c4">The actor who was supposed to be playing the part <b>bailed</b> <b>out</b>.<br>原定饰演这个角色的演员不干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbail sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">从船里往外舀水<br><span class="en">to throw water out of a boat with a container or with your hands</span></td><td class="c4">The boat will sink unless we <b>bail out</b>.<br>我们要是不排水，船可要沉了。<br>They started <b>bailing the boat out</b>.<br>他们动手把船舱的水舀出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>balance</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbalance A against B</b></td><td class="c3">权衡；斟酌；比较两个计划；论点等的价值或重要性<br><span class="en">to compare the value or importance of one plan, argument, etc. against another</span></td><td class="c4">You must <b>balance</b> the high salary <b>against</b> the long working hours.<br>你必须权衡高工资和长工时两者的利弊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>balance ˈout<br>ˌbalance sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使均等；平衡；相当<br><span class="en">if things that are very different or have opposite effects balance out or you balance them out, they become equal in amount or value</span></td><td class="c4">If you eat a variety of food, protein and carbohydrate will <b>balance out</b> over a week.<br>如果饮食多样化，一星期后蛋白质和碳水化合物就会均衡了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ball</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ball sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…採成团<br><span class="en">to make sth that is usually flat into the shape of a ball</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>balled up</b> the paper and tossed it in the garbage.<br>她把纸揉成一团，扔到垃圾桶里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>balls</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈballs-up n <span class="tag">(A, slang, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">混乱；一团糟；一塌糊涂</td><td class="c4">I made a real <b>balls-up</b> of my exams.<br>我考砸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>band</b></td><td class="c2"><b>band toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">团结；联合；携手<br><span class="en">to form a group and act together in order to achieve sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>band together</b> to fight these reforms.<br>斗争。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bandage</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbandage sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">绷带包扎<br><span class="en">to wrap a bandage around a part of the body that is injured</span></td><td class="c4">Joe <b>bandaged me up</b> until the doctor came.<br>乔在医生到来前用绷带包扎好了我的伤口。I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bandy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bandy sth aˈbout (also ˌbandy sth aˈround especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">轻率地传播；散布；谈论</td><td class="c4">The stories being <b>bandied about</b> are completely false.<br>那些道听途说的谣言完全是子虚乌有。<br>Hes not paid anything like the £4000 a week figure being <b>bandied</b> <b>around</b>.<br>他每周挣四千英镑的说法完全不靠谱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bang</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bang aˈround (also,bang aˈbout especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">重手重脚地走动；乒乓作响地来来去去<br><span class="en">to move around noisily</span></td><td class="c4">We could hear them <b>banging</b> <b>about</b> upstairs, moving things.<br>我们能听到他们在楼上咣当咣当地来回挪动东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbang aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">连续地猛砸；猛击<br><span class="en">to hit sth repeatedly with a lot of force or energy</span></td><td class="c4">She picked up the hammer and began <b>banging away</b>.<br>她拿起锤子用力敲打起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbang aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">心脏等怦怦作晌<br><span class="en">if sth such as your heart bangs away, it makes very loud regular sounds</span></td><td class="c4">My heart was <b>banging away</b> like a drum.<br>我的心像打鼓一样，扑通扑通直跳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bang aˈway at sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">努力工作；致力于<br><span class="en">to work very hard at sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>banged away all day at</b> her assignment.<br>她一整天都在埋头做作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bang sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">猛摔；砰地一扔<br><span class="en">to put sth down quickly and with a lot of force so that it makes a loud noise</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>banged his fist down</b> on the table.<br>他砰地一拳砸在桌子上。<br>She <b>banged the phone down</b> (= ended the telephone conversation) before I could explain.<br>我还没来得及解释，她就啪地挂断了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbang ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">不小心撞；碰着<br><span class="en">to crash into or hit sb/sth violently, usually by mistake</span></td><td class="c4">He ran around the corner and <b>banged into</b> an old lady who was coming the other way.<br>他跑过拐角，一下子撞上了迎面走来的一位老太太。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbang ˈon about sb/sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">啰唆；絮叨<br><span class="en">to talk or write a lot or in a boring way about sth</span></td><td class="c4">Pat is always <b>banging on about</b> politics.<br>帕特总是没完没了地谈论政治。<br>She keeps <b>banging on about</b> how wonderful her son is.<br>她逢人便讲她的儿子有多优秀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bang ˈout sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">高声奏出<br><span class="en">to play music very loudly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>banged out</b> the tune on the piano.<br>他在钢琴上响亮地弹奏那首曲子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bang ˈout sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">仓促写成；匆匆写就；粗制滥造(文章等)<br><span class="en">to write sth very quickly and without taking much care</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>bangs out</b> four novels a year.<br>她一年可以赶写出四部小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌbanged ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">被拘留；被关进牢房<br><span class="en">to be locked up or put in prison</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>was banged up</b> in a Singapore jail for six months.<br>他在新加坡坐了六个月牢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bank</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbank on sb/sth doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">依靠；指望；信赖<br><span class="en">to rely on sb/sth; to be confident that sth will happen</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>banking</b> on the train being on time.<br>他指望火车会准点。<br>She might already have cleaned up the mess, but / wouldn't <b>bank</b> on it.<br>她或许收拾过了，但是我不能打包票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bargain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbargain sth aˈway <span class="tag">(rare)</span></b></td><td class="c3">廉价交换；亏本；交易<br><span class="en">to give away sth valuable or important in exchange for sth less valuable or important</span></td><td class="c4">The leaders refused to <b>bargain away</b> the freedom of their people.<br>领导人拒绝拿人民的自由做交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>doing sth<br>ˈbargain for/on sb/sth doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">准备好(做某事)；预料到<br><span class="en">to expect or be prepared to do sth; to expect sth to happen or sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">We hadn't <b>bargained</b> for such bad weather.<br>我们没想到天气这么糟糕。<br>I hadn't <b>bargained</b> on taking the kids with us.<br>我原本没打算让孩子们和我们一起去。<br>I didn't <b>bargain</b> for Jake being at the party.<br>我没料到杰克会来参加聚会。<br>When he tried to argue with Kate, he got more than he had <b>bargained</b> for.<br>他试图和凯特争辩，不料却招架不住。<br>What I hadn't <b>bargained</b> for was that very few people would speak English.<br>我没想到的是没几个人肯说英语。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>barge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>barge ˈin (on sb/sth)<br>barge ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">擅自闯入；冒味介入<br><span class="en">to enter a place or join a group of people quickly and rudely, without being asked</span></td><td class="c4">Sorry to <b>barge</b> in, but...<br>抱歉冒昧打扰，可是…。<br>She <b>barged</b> in on our meeting without knocking.<br>我们开会时，她门也不敲就闯了进来。<br>He just <b>barged</b> Chis way) <b>into</b> the room.<br>他径直闯进了屋子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>barge ˈin (on sb/sth)<br>barge ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">插嘴；打岔；打扰<br><span class="en">to interrupt what sb is doing or saying, especially when you have not been invited to join in</span></td><td class="c4">As soon as I paused for breath, Bart <b>barged</b> in.<br>我刚停下来喘口气，巴特便抢过了话头。<br>You can't just come <b>barging</b> <b>into</b> our conversation!<br>你不能这么冒冒失失地打断我们的谈话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbark sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">大声说出；咆哮<br><span class="en">to shout sth loudly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>barked out</b> instructions to her secretary.<br>她扯着嗓子对秘书发号施令。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>base</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbase sth on sth also ˈbase sth upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">把…基于；以…次…的基础；以为…的根据<br><span class="en">to use or have an idea, an experience, etc. as the point from which sth can be developed</span></td><td class="c4">She is <b>basing</b> the prosecution case on the evidence of two witnesses.<br>她是依据两名目击者的证词提起诉讼的。<br>What's the design <b>based</b> on?<br>这一设计的蓝本是什么。<br>The report has been <b>based</b> <b>upon</b> inaccurate information.<br>这份报告所依据的信息不准确。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbash sb/sth aˈbout <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛打；暴打；粗暴对待<br><span class="en">to hit or strike sb/sth and treat them/it in a rough way</span></td><td class="c4">The mugger had <b>bashed her about</b>.<br>行凶抢劫者对她拳打脚踢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbash aˈway (at sth) <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">持续努力；持之以恒(专注于)<br><span class="en">to work very hard at sth for a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>bashed away</b> at the article without a break from 11 until 6.<br>我从 11 点到6点一刻不停地写那篇文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bash sth ˈin <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打破；打坏；撞毁<br><span class="en">to break or destroy sth by hitting it violently</span></td><td class="c4">The window had been <b>bashed in</b>.<br>窗户打碎了。日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bask</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbask in sth</b></td><td class="c3">享受<br><span class="en">to enjoy the good feelings that you have when other people praise or admire you, or when they give you a lot of attention</span></td><td class="c4">He had always <b>basked in</b> his parents' attention.<br>他一直尽享父母的关爱。<br>I never minded <b>basking in</b> my wife's reflected glory(= enjoying the praise, attention, etc. she got).<br>生活在妻子的光环中，我感到与有荣焉，从不介怀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbat sth aˈround <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在采取行动前考虑；讨论；推敲计划；想法等<br><span class="en">to talk about or discuss plans or ideas, etc. before you decide what to do</span></td><td class="c4">Were just <b>batting some ideas around</b>.<br>我们只不过是在聊聊一些想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>batten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>batten sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">固定；钉住(以防风暴)<br><span class="en">to fasten sth firmly in order to prevent damage by storms or winds</span></td><td class="c4">They managed <b>batten down</b> the shutters and doors before the hurricane hit.<br>赶在飓风来袭前，他们总算钉牢了百叶窗和屋门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>batter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbatter sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">以连续猛击砸；砸毁<br><span class="en">to hit sth repeatedly until it breaks and falls down</span></td><td class="c4">The only way to get in was to <b>batter the door down</b>.<br>要想进去只能把门砸开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bawl</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbawl sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">痛骂；厉声教训<br><span class="en">to speak angrily to sb because they have done sth wrong</span></td><td class="c4">My boss <b>bawled me out</b> for being late.<br>我迟到了，给老板训了一顿。ˌ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bawl sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">怒吼；大叫；高声歌唱<br><span class="en">to say or sing sth very loudly or in an angry voice</span></td><td class="c4">She doesn't give you an order. She <b>bawls it out</b>.<br>她吩附什么事情，总是大喊大叫。<br>The children <b>bawled out</b> the songs.<br>孩子们扯着嗓子唱歌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>be</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈafter sth</b></td><td class="c3">追求；追逐<br><span class="en">to be trying to get or obtain sth</span></td><td class="c4">Several people in the office <b>are after</b> the same job.<br>办公室里有几个人在争同一个职位。<br>She's being too nice. I wonder what she's <b>after</b>.<br>她友好得过了头。我倒想知道她图的是什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈat sth</b></td><td class="c3">忙于；专注于<br><span class="en">to be busy doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>been at</b> his essay all night.<br>他整夜都在写文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">外出(尤指度假或出差)<br><span class="en">to not be at home, especially when you are on holiday/vacation or on a business trip</span></td><td class="c4">We'll <b>be away</b> for the month of August.<br>我们八月份要外出。<br>He's <b>away</b> on business at the moment.<br>他出差去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be beˈhind sb</b></td><td class="c3">支持；做…的后盾<br><span class="en">to give sb your support</span></td><td class="c4">Don't forget that we're <b>behind</b> you all the way.<br>记住我们会一直支持你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be beˈhind with sth</b></td><td class="c3">拖欠付账；交租金等；耽搁；逾期<br><span class="en">to be late doing sth, such as paying a bill, your rent, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I'm <b>behind</b> with my college assignments.<br>我没及时完成大学作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">计算机系统出故障；(计算机)停机<br><span class="en">if a computer system is down, it is not working</span></td><td class="c4">Surely your computer isnt <b>down</b> again?<br>你的计算机不会又坏了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈdown on sb</b></td><td class="c3">对…苛责；对…不公<br><span class="en">to treat sb severely or unfairly</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>been really down on</b> me lately.<br>他最近特别跟我过不去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈdown to sb</b></td><td class="c3">是…的责任<br><span class="en">to be the responsibility of sb</span></td><td class="c4">It's <b>down</b> to you to help them now.<br>现在该你帮助他们了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/go ˈdown with sth</b></td><td class="c3">染(病)<br><span class="en">to have or catch an illness</span></td><td class="c4">Gill's <b>down</b> with flu.<br>吉尔患了流感。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">当选(政治职位)<br><span class="en">to be elected to a political position</span></td><td class="c4">The Democrats <b>are in</b> for another term.<br>民主党人获选连任。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈin for sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">即将面临(尤指令人不快的事)；势必遭受<br><span class="en">to be going to experience sth soon, especially sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">She's in <b>for</b> a shock.<br>她会大吃一惊的。<br>It looks like we're in <b>for</b> a storm.<br>看来我们要遭遇暴风雨了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">爱好；对…感兴趣<br><span class="en">to have a taste for or an interest in sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Are you into</b> jazz?<br>你喜欢爵士乐吗。<br>He's <b>been into</b> trains since he was a small boy.<br>他从小就喜爱火车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">离开；(匆忙)走开<br><span class="en">to leave; to go, especially in a hurry</span></td><td class="c4">I must <b>be off</b>.<br>我得走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">食物变质<br><span class="en">to have gone bad and not be fit to eat or drink</span></td><td class="c4">This milk <b>is off</b>.<br>牛奶坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…不感兴趣；不再喜欢<br><span class="en">to have no interest in sb/sth; to have stopped liking sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She can't be well. She's <b>been off</b> her food all week.<br>她一定是生病了。她整个星期都没胃口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">打完(电话)<br><span class="en">to have finished speaking on the telephone</span></td><td class="c4">Isn't he <b>off</b> the phone yet?<br>他电话还没打完吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈon sb</b></td><td class="c3">饮料；食物；票等由…支付；由…付账<br><span class="en">if sth such as drinks, food, tickets, etc. are on sb, they are paid for by that person</span></td><td class="c4">The drinks <b>are on</b> me tonight.<br>今晚的酒水钱我来付。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">在服用药物；毒品等<br><span class="en">to be taking medicine, a drug, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>been on</b> the pill for ten years.<br>她服避孕药有十年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈon about sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">谈论；唠叨；意思是<br><span class="en">to talk about sth, often in a boring way; to mean sth</span></td><td class="c4">He's always on <b>about</b> how much money he earns.<br>他总爱唠叨他赚多少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈonto sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">盯上(犯错者)；追捕(违法者)<br><span class="en">to become aware that sb has done sth wrong or illegal and be urying to catch them</span></td><td class="c4">The police aren't <b>onto</b> us yet.<br>警察还没盯上我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">找到；发现有用的线索；有益的事物<br><span class="en">to have found or discovered sth that could have very good results for you or for sb else</span></td><td class="c4">She could <b>be onto</b> something (= she might have discovered sth that will prove important).<br>她可能有了重大发现。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">罢工<br><span class="en">to have stopped work as a protest and be on strike</span></td><td class="c4">The postal workers <b>are still out</b>.<br>邮政职工还在罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不流行；过时<br><span class="en">to be no longer in fashion</span></td><td class="c4">Black <b>is out</b> this year.<br>今年不时兴黑色。<br>Politeness seems to <b>be out</b> of fashion these days (= no one is polite any more).<br>如今讲礼貌似乎已经过时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈout for sth<br>be ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">力图；一心一意要；竭力寻求<br><span class="en">to do sth to be trying very hard to do sth or to get sth</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>out</b> for revenge.<br>他一心要报复。<br>Everyone's just <b>out</b> for what they can get these days (= they are trying to get things for themselves).<br>如今每个人都只顾谋求私利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">用光；耗尽；使枯竭<br><span class="en">to have used up a supply of sth and have nothing left</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>out</b> of sugar.<br>我们的糖吃完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">病愈；恢复健康<br><span class="en">to have returned to health after an illness</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>over</b> the flu now.<br>他的流感好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈpast it <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">年老无用；年老；无趣<br><span class="en">to show that you think sb is so old that they can no longer do anything useful or interesting</span></td><td class="c4">The children laughed at him and said he <b>was past it</b>.<br>孩子们嘲笑他，说他年老不中用了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈthrough (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">和某人接通电话<br><span class="en">to be connected to sb on the telephone</span></td><td class="c4">You're <b>through</b> to the manager now.<br>您可以和经理通话了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈthrough (with sb/sth) <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使用完(某物)；做完(某事)；(与某人)分手<br><span class="en">to have finished using or doing sth; to have finished a relationship with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Aren't you <b>through</b> yet? Youve been ages!<br>你还没完成？你真是没完没了。<br>He promised he <b>through</b> with drugs.<br>他保证过不再吸毒。<br>Keith and I <b>are through</b>.<br>基思和我吹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">海等<br><span class="en">of the wind, the sea, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">In the morning the wind <b>was up</b> and we got ready for a day's sailing.<br>早晨风更大了，我们为一天的航行作好了准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">饮料；饭菜等<br><span class="en">of a drink, a meal, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Tea's <b>up</b>! Come and get it.<br>茶沏好了！过来喝吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">进行中<br><span class="en">(with sb) used to say that sth is happening, especially sth unusual or unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">You look terrible! What's <b>up</b>?<br>你气色很不好！出什么事儿了。<br>I couldn't understand what <b>was up</b> with George.<br>我不明白乔治是怎么了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup against sb</b></td><td class="c3">比赛；竞争等；中对手是<br><span class="en">to be playing against sb in a game, competition, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We're up <b>against</b> some tough competition this year.<br>今年我们面临激烈的竞争。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup for sth</b></td><td class="c3">作次…的考虑对象；是…的候选人<br><span class="en">to be considered for sth, especially as a candidate for a job, in an election, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She's up <b>for</b> promotion.<br>她就要升迁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈup for sth</b></td><td class="c3">供出售；待售<br><span class="en">to be for sb to buy</span></td><td class="c4">I see your house <b>is up for</b> sale.<br>我看到你的房子要出售。<br>A Picasso <b>is up for</b> auction.<br>有一幅毕加索的画要拍卖。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i be ˈup to sb</b></td><td class="c3">是…的责任；是…的职责<br><span class="en">to be sb's responsibility or duty</span></td><td class="c4">It's up <b>to</b> you to make sure the house is kept tidy.<br>保持房屋整洁是你的责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i be ˈup to sb</b></td><td class="c3">符合期待；达到<br><span class="en">to be as good as people expect</span></td><td class="c4">Was your meal up <b>to</b> standard?<br>你的饭菜够标准吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbear ˈdown on sb/sth also ˌbear ˈdown upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">来势汹汹地冲向；逼近<br><span class="en">to move towards sb/sth in a determined or threatening way</span></td><td class="c4">A crowd of journalists <b>bore</b> <b>down</b> on the minister.<br>一群记者冲向部长。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbear ˈdown on sb/sth also ˌbear ˈdown upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">问题或困境深深烦扰；严重影响<br><span class="en">if a problem or a difficult situation bears down on you, it makes you feel very worried and has a severe effect on you</span></td><td class="c4">The drought is <b>bearing</b> <b>down</b> very hard on farmers.<br>早情让农民忧心忡忡。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbear on/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">涉及；影响<br><span class="en">to be connected with sb/sth; to have an effect on sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">This decision <b>bears directly on</b> our everyday lives.<br>这一决定直接影响我们的日常生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbear with sb</b></td><td class="c3">耐心对待；容忍<br><span class="en">to be patient with sb</span></td><td class="c4">She's under a lot of strain.Just <b>bear with</b> her.<br>她承受着很大压力，对她宽容一些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>beat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">使后退；使后撤<br><span class="en">to make sb move backwards away from sth</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>beaten back</b> by the flames.<br>火焰迫使她退了回去。<br>They tried to <b>beat the enemy back</b>.<br>他们试图击退敌军。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat ˈdown (on/upon sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">阳光曝晒；直射<br><span class="en">if the sun beats down, it shines with great heat</span></td><td class="c4">The sun <b>beat down</b> all afternoon from a clear sky.<br>整个下午晴空当头，骄阳似火。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat ˈdown (on/upon sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">雨倾盆而下；倾泻<br><span class="en">if rain beats down, it falls with great force</span></td><td class="c4">The rain was <b>beating down</b> on them.<br>大雨浇在他们身上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一伙人<br><span class="en">of a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">We saw Pictures on the news of a bunch of kids <b>beating down</b> an older guy.<br>我们看到几张新闻照片，帮孩子对一个上了岁数的男子拳打脚踢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat sb/sth ˈdown (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">与…讨价还价；杀…的价<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to reduce the price of sth; to get sb to accept a lower price for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Chris tried to <b>beat them down</b> to a lower price.<br>克里斯试图跟他们把价格砍下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>beat sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用力打倒；把…打翻在地<br><span class="en">to hit sth hard, often many times, until it falls down</span></td><td class="c4">The police had to <b>beat the door down</b>.<br>警察不得不把门砸开。<br>People are hardly <b>beating the door down</b> to get her latest book (= they are not rushing to buy it).<br>人们并没有争相购买她最近出版的书。<br>Two women tried to <b>beat down</b> the flames.<br>两名女子试图把火苗扑灭。回町。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>beat sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">驱走；逐回<br><span class="en">to drive sb/sth back or away by fighting</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>beat off</b> an attack by the rebel army.<br>他们击退了叛军的进攻。<br>He tried to <b>beat the thugs off</b> with a stick.<br>他想用棍子赶走那帮暴徒。四日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用鼓；等敲打出(节奏)<br><span class="en">to produce a rhythm by hitting sth such as a drum repeatedly</span></td><td class="c4">He used his jacket to <b>beat out</b> the flames.<br>他用夹克衫把火扑灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>beat sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">攫取；猎取<br><span class="en">to get sth from sb by cheating Or taking full advantage of a situation</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>beat me out of</b> $500.<br>他骗了我500元。<br>Book now before somebody else <b>beats</b> you to it!<br>请从速订购，以防别人捷足先登。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeat sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">毒打；踢打<br><span class="en">to hit or kick sb repeatedly</span></td><td class="c4">Her husband used to <b>beat her up</b>.<br>她丈夫以前常对她大打出手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>beaver</b></td><td class="c2"><b>beaver aˈway (at sth) <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">拼命工作；努力工作<br><span class="en">to work very hard at sth</span></td><td class="c4">She's been <b>beavering away</b> at her homework for hours.<br>她连续几个小时都在忙着做作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>become</b></td><td class="c2"><b>beˈcome of sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">发生于；降临到…身上<br><span class="en">to happen to sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">I wonder what <b>became of</b> the people who Lived next door.<br>我不知道以前住在隔壁的人怎么样了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bed</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbed ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">临时；在某处睡下；投宿；过夜<br><span class="en">to lie down to go to sleep somewhere you do not normally sleep</span></td><td class="c4">Young people <b>bedded down</b> in doorways.<br>年轻人就睡在各家各户的门口。<br>The new players have <b>bedded down</b> well in the team.<br>新队员已经很好地融入了这支队伍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>beef</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbeef ˈup sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">扩大；加强；增强<br><span class="en">to make sth bigger, stronger, more interesting, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Security has been <b>beefed up</b>.<br>安全措施得到了加强。<br>The company has been trying to <b>beef up</b> its image.<br>公司一直致力于改善形象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>beg</b></td><td class="c2"><b>beg ˈoff<br>ˌbeg ˈoff sth<br>beg ˈoff doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">推掉；请求免除该做；或答应做的事<br><span class="en">to ask to be excused from sth; to say that you cannot do sth that you are expected or have promised to do</span></td><td class="c4">She was asked to work the weekend shift but she tried to <b>beg off</b>.<br>要让她上周末班，可她竭力想推掉。<br>He <b>begged off</b> visiting his grandparents.<br>他把看望爷爷奶奶的事推掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>believe</b></td><td class="c2"><b>beˈlieve in sth<br>beˈlieve in doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">认为…正确；认为…有益；赞同<br><span class="en">to feel that sth is right or valuable; to approve of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Do you <b>believe in</b> capital punishment?<br>你赞成死刑吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>belong</b></td><td class="c2"><b>beˈlong to sb not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The house <b>belonged</b> to my cousin.<br>这座房子是我亲戚的。<br>That land <b>belongs</b> to the golf club.<br>那块地属于高尔夫俱乐部。9。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>beˈlong to sb not</b></td><td class="c3">工作；任务等归…负责；是…的责任<br><span class="en">if a job, a duty, etc. belongs to you, it is your responsibility</span></td><td class="c4">The job of disciplining a child <b>belongs</b> to the parents.<br>管教孩子是父母的职责。<br>The credit for our success <b>belongs</b> to the staff (= they made us successful).<br>我们的成功归功于全体职员。<br>Latvia already <b>belongs</b> to the European Union.<br>拉脱维亚已经加入欧洲联盟。<br>These three turtles all <b>belong</b> to one species.<br>这三只龟都是一样的品种。<br>Writers like him <b>belong</b> to a different generation.<br>他这一类作家属于另一代。四。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>belt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>belt sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">很快喝掉；狂饮<br><span class="en">to drink sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>belted down</b> his beer.<br>他把啤酒一饮而尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbelt ˈout sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">高声演唱；大声演奏<br><span class="en">if you belt out a song or a piece of music, you sing or play it loudly</span></td><td class="c4">Nobody can <b>belt out</b> a tune like she can.<br>她歌喉暸亮，无人能比。<br>A radio <b>belted out</b> pop music.<br>收音机以高音量播放流行音乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>bend ˈover<br>ˌbend ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">俯身；弯腰<br><span class="en">to lean over; to bend from the waist</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Bend over</b> and touch your toes.<br>弯下腰去触摸你的脚趾。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>big</b></td><td class="c2"><b>big sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">高度赞扬；竭力；推荐<br><span class="en">to praise or recommend sb/sth strongly</span></td><td class="c4">He's been <b>bigging up</b> the on his radio show.<br>他在自己的广播节目中极力推荐那张。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>big it ˈup (for sb/sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指通过鼓掌；欢呼等宣示热情；表示支持<br><span class="en">to show enthusiasm and support for sb/sth, especially by clapping, shouting,etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Big it up</b> for the boys in the band!<br>请鼓掌欢迎乐队的小伙子们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbill sb/sth as sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…称之为；把…宣传为<br><span class="en">to describe sb/sth in a particular way; to advertise sb/sth as sth</span></td><td class="c4">Some patlents are receiving what has been <b>billed as</b> a revolutionary treatment.<br>有些病人正在接受所谓的革命性治疗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bind</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbind sb ˈover (law)</b></td><td class="c3">勒令…具结保证(不再违法)<br><span class="en">to warn sb that they will have to appear in court if they break the law again</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>bound over</b> to keep the peace.<br>他被责令具保不再闹事。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbind sb to sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使立誓做；使受(法律文书)约束<br><span class="en">to force sb to do sth by making them promise to do it or making it part of a legal document</span></td><td class="c4">The company directors are <b>bound to</b> secrecy(= they have promised not to say anything) about the future of the company.<br>公司董事对公司的未来负有保密义务。<br>The band found they were <b>bound to</b> the contract.<br>乐队发现他们被合同束缚住了。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bind sth ˈup (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用长布条缠绕；围裹<br><span class="en">to tie a long thin piece of material around sth to protect it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>bound up</b> his wounds with bandages.<br>她用绷带给他包扎好了伤口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bitch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bitch sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">怒骂；痛骂<br><span class="en">to criticize sb angrily</span></td><td class="c4">The teacher <b>bitched me out</b> for being late.<br>因为迟到，老师劈头盖脸说了我一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bite</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bite ˈback (at sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">回咬；报复；反击<br><span class="en">to react when sb has harmed you and try to harm or criticize them</span></td><td class="c4">If you criticize him, he'll <b>bite back</b>.<br>如果你批评他，他会反过来攻击你的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bite ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">咬入；划进；刺入<br><span class="en">to cut or press into the surface of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The collar bit <b>into</b> his neck.<br>衣领勒着了他的脖子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bite sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">咬下；咬掉<br><span class="en">to cut sth off by biting it</span></td><td class="c4">She bit <b>off</b> a piece of chocolate.<br>她啃下一块巧克力。<br>His finger had been bitten <b>off</b> by a dog.<br>他的手指让狗给咬断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>black</b></td><td class="c2"><b>black ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">短暂昏厥；失忆<br><span class="en">to become unconscious or lose your memory for a short time</span></td><td class="c4">The pain hit him and he <b>blacked out</b>.<br>他疼得晕了过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blank</b></td><td class="c2"><b>blank ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不知所措；一片茫然<br><span class="en">informa if you blank out or your mind blanks out, you cannot remember anything or you become confused</span></td><td class="c4">I hope I don't <b>blank out</b> in the exam.<br>但愿考试时我脑子里不会一片空白。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblank sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">刻意忘却(令人不快的事)<br><span class="en">to deliberately forget sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">Your childhood may have been difficult but you can't just <b>blank it out</b>.<br>童年时代或许艰难，但是不能就这么从记忆中抹去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblank sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用墨水等掩盖；遮盖(文字)<br><span class="en">to cover sth written or printed, for example, with black ink so that it cannot be read</span></td><td class="c4">All the names in the report had been <b>blanked out</b>.<br>报告中所有的名字都已涂掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blare</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblare ˈout<br>ˌblare sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">音乐高声；奏出；(收音机等)大声播放(音乐)<br><span class="en">if music blares out, or a radio, etc. blares out music, it is produced or played very loudly</span></td><td class="c4">Music was <b>blaring out</b> from somewhere.<br>不知从何处传来喧嚣的音乐。<br>The radio was <b>blaring out</b> rock music.<br>收音机正在以高音量播放摇滚乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blast</b></td><td class="c2"><b>blast aˈway (at sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">砰砰射击；猛烈轰击<br><span class="en">if a gun or sb using a gun blasts away, the gun fires loudly and continuously</span></td><td class="c4">The machine guns <b>blasted away</b> all night.<br>机关枪射击声彻夜不停。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblast sb/sth aˈway <span class="tag">(less frequent)</span></b></td><td class="c3">击毙；炸死(某人)；炸毁；炸开(某物)<br><span class="en">to kill sb or remove sth or break it apart violently, for example with a gun, bombs, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They have <b>blasted away</b> the side of this beautiful valley to make a road.<br>为了修路，他们把这座美丽峡谷的 -侧炸开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblast ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">航天器发射；升空<br><span class="en">when a spacecraft blasts off, it leaves the ground and goes up into space</span></td><td class="c4">The rocket <b>blasted off</b> at 7.28 p.m.<br>晚上7时28分火箭发射升空了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblend ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">与周围环境等协调；相称<br><span class="en">(with sth) if sth blends in with sth else or with its surroundings, it looks Similar to it/them or matches well</span></td><td class="c4">The curtains <b>blend in</b> perfectly with the carpet.<br>窗帘和地毯搭配完美。<br>The new office block doesn't <b>blend in</b> well with its traditional surroundings.<br>新办公大楼与传统风格的周边环境格格不入。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblend sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">烹饪</td><td class="c4">Heat the butter gently and then <b>blend in</b> a little flour.<br>把黄油小火加热，然后掺入少许面粉。<br>He <b>blended in</b> the charcoal lines to make the picture look softer.<br>他以炭笔线条晕染，使画面显得更柔和些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblend ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">与…融为一体；与…相互交融<br><span class="en">to look or sound so similar to sth that it is difficult for anyone to see or hear it</span></td><td class="c4">The animals can <b>blend into</b> the long grass.<br>这些动物在长草丛中很难分辨。<br>The new development should <b>blend into</b> its surroundings.<br>新开发项目应该与周围环境协调一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblink sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">眨眼睛挤掉<br><span class="en">to clear sth from the eyes by blinking (= closing and opening your eyes quickly)</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>blinked away</b> a tear.<br>他眨了眨眼睛，挤掉泪水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblink sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">忍住泪水<br><span class="en">to try to control your tears</span></td><td class="c4">I found myself <b>blinking back</b> tears during his speech.<br>在他演讲过程中我一直忍着不让眼泪掉下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bliss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bliss ˈout<br>bliss sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使感到轻松；感到喜悦<br><span class="en">to feel very happy and relaxed; to make sb feel this</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>blissing out</b> over my scrambled eggs.<br>我吃着炒鸡蛋，感到乐不可支。<br>Those old black and white movies <b>bliss me out</b>.<br>那些黑白老电影使我欣喜若狂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>block</b></td><td class="c2"><b>block sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">停车间距过小而把…困住；把…堵住<br><span class="en">to stop a vehicle from being driven away by parking too close to it</span></td><td class="c4">You're <b>blocking that Mini in</b>.<br>你停的车把那辆宝马微型车给挡住了。<br>Somebody had parked in front of me, <b>blocking me in</b>.<br>有人把车停在我前面，把我的车堵住了。<br>Iwas <b>blocked in</b> by two lorries so I had to leave the car and walk.<br>我的车被两辆大货车夹在中间不能动弹，我只好下车步行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblock sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">设立路障等拦堵；封锁<br><span class="en">to close a road or another place by placing a barrier across it to stop sb/sth going in or coming out</span></td><td class="c4">The police <b>blocked the street Off</b>.<br>警察封锁了这条街道。<br>The Pipe had been <b>blocked off</b> to prevent further leaks.<br>为防止继续渗漏，管道被堵上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblock sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">遮挡光线或；噪声；遮盖；掩盖<br><span class="en">to stop light or noise from coming in; to cover or hide sth</span></td><td class="c4">The trees <b>blocked out</b> much of the sunlight.<br>树木挡住了大部分的阳光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>block sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">堵塞；封住(孔洞等)<br><span class="en">to fill sth such as a hole completely so that nothing can get through it</span></td><td class="c4">All the windows had been <b>blocked up</b>.<br>所有窗户都封死了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblot sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌblot sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">刻意忘掉；不去想(尤指令人不快的事)<br><span class="en">to avoid remembering sb/sth or thinking about sb/sth, especially sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">He wanted to <b>blot out</b> the memory.<br>他想抹去那段记忆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblot sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">遮挡(光线或噪声)；遮盖；掩盖<br><span class="en">to stop light or noise coming in; to cover or hide sth</span></td><td class="c4">Dark clouds were <b>blotting out</b> the sun.<br>乌云渐渐遮蔽了太阳。B。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">给…留下深刻印象；震撼；使高兴<br><span class="en">to impress sb a lot; to surprise or please sb</span></td><td class="c4">I saw her performance on Broadway last year and it just <b>blew me away</b>.<br>我去年在百老汇看过她的演出，印象十分深刻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">轻易打败；轻松战胜<br><span class="en">sport to defeat sb easily</span></td><td class="c4">Mitchell <b>blew away</b> the other runners.<br>米切尔轻而易举地战胜了其他赛跑选手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow sb/sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">用炸药或枪杀死；除掉；摧毁<br><span class="en">to kill sb or remove or destroy sth with bombs or with a gun</span></td><td class="c4">He threatened to <b>blow us away</b>.<br>他威胁说要把我们统统枪毙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>blow ˈdown<br>.blow sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">被吹倒；掀翻<br><span class="en">if sth blows down, or the wind blows it down, it falls to the ground because of the force of the wind</span></td><td class="c4">An old oak tree had <b>blown down</b> in the storm.<br>暴风刮倒了一棵老橡树。<br>Hundreds of trees have been <b>blown down</b> this winter.<br>今年冬天有数百棵树被吹倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE, informa)</span></b></td><td class="c3">放屁<br><span class="en">to let air from the body escape through your bottom</span></td><td class="c4">Who Just <b>blew off</b>?<br>刚才谁放的屁？K。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>blow ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">推掉(本该做的事)；取消原定要做的；变卦<br><span class="en">to decide not to do sth you should do or were planning to do</span></td><td class="c4">Jessica <b>blew off</b> her classes on Friday afternoon to go shopping.<br>杰西卡星期五下午旷课去逛商店了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>blow sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…爽约；不赴约去见(某人)<br><span class="en">to disappoint sb by not meeting them as arranged</span></td><td class="c4">We were supposed to 80 out yesterday, but he <b>blew me off</b>.<br>我们约定昨天外出的，可他放了我的鸽子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>blow ˈout<br>ˌblow sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">被吹灭；熄灭<br><span class="en">if a fame blows out or sb/sth blows it out, it is put out by the wind or some air</span></td><td class="c4">There was a sudden gust of wind and the candle <b>blew out</b>.<br>突如其来的一阵风把蜡烛吹灭了。<br>She took a deep breath and <b>blew out</b> all the candles.<br>她深吸一口气，吹熄了所有蜡烛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不愿与…发展关系；甩掉<br><span class="en">(for sb) (bre, slang) to tell sb that you do not want to have a relationship with them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>blew me out</b> for Chris, but I still fancy him.<br>他甩了我而选择了克丽丝，但是我仍喜欢他。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">吹出；呼出<br><span class="en">to breathe sth out from your mouth</span></td><td class="c4">She inhaled and then <b>blew the smoke out</b>.<br>她吸了一口，接着吐出了烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow itself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">风暴减弱；停止<br><span class="en">if a storm blows itself out, it loses its force and stops</span></td><td class="c4">By morning the storm had <b>blown itself out</b>.<br>到了早上，风暴就逐渐停了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">风暴减弱；停止<br><span class="en">if a storm blows over, it becomes less strong and stops</span></td><td class="c4">We sheltered in a barn until the storm <b>blew over</b>.<br>我们躲在谷仓里，直到风暴平息。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblow ˈover<br>blow sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">被吹倒；掀翻<br><span class="en">if sb/sth blows over or the wind blows sb/sth over, he/she/it falls to the ground because of the force of the wind</span></td><td class="c4">One of the trees had <b>blown over</b> in the storm.<br>其中一棵树在风暴中刮倒了。<br>The fence had been <b>blown over</b> in a storm.<br>篱笆在一次风暴中刮倒了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>blow ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">爆炸；被炸毁<br><span class="en">to explode; to be destroyed by an explosion</span></td><td class="c4">The bomb <b>blew up</b> as experts tried to defuse it.<br>专家们试图拆除引信时，炸弹爆炸了。<br>The car <b>blew up</b> when it hit the wall.<br>汽车撞墻后炸毁了。<br>A Tow has <b>blown up</b> over the leaking of information to the press.<br>向新闻界泄路消息引发了一场轩然大波。<br>His attitude annoyed me and I <b>blew up</b>.<br>他的态度令我生厌，于是我发火了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈblow-up n</b></td><td class="c3">狂怒；争吵<br><span class="en">an occasion when sb becomes very angry; an argument</span></td><td class="c4">The tensions between them ended in a big <b>blow-up</b>.<br>他们之间关系紧张，结果使他们大吵一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>blow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">给…充气<br><span class="en">to fill sth with air or gas</span></td><td class="c4">You need to <b>blow up</b> the tyres on your bike.<br>你该给自行车轮胎打气了。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bluff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbluff it ˈout <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指诚信受到怀疑时蒙混过关<br><span class="en">to lie to sb in order to get out of a difficult situation, especially when they suspect you are not being honest</span></td><td class="c4">If he asks any difficult questions, youll have to <b>bluff it out</b>.<br>他要是问些难题，你就只能靠蒙混过关了。<br>I know everything so there's no point trying to <b>bluff it out</b>.<br>我什么都知道，所以别企图蒙骗下去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blunder</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblunder ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">因笨拙或看不见撞上<br><span class="en">to walk into sb/sth because you are awkward or unable to see</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>blundered into</b> a tree.<br>她不小心撞上了一棵树。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblunder ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">无意之中陷入困境；步入险境<br><span class="en">to accidentally find yourself in a difficult or dangerous place or situation</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>blundered into</b> a dangerous area of the city after losing her way.<br>她迷路之后不知怎么就到了城市的危险地带。<br>He had innocently <b>blundered into</b> a private dispute.<br>他稀里糊涂地卷入了一场私人纠纷。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>blurt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌblurt sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">脱口而出；随口说出<br><span class="en">to say sth suddenly and without thinking carefully</span></td><td class="c4">He found himself <b>blurting out</b> the whole story to her.<br>他在不经意中就把事情从头到尾全都告诉了她。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>board</b></td><td class="c2"><b>board sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用木板封闭(门窗)<br><span class="en">to cover a window or a door with boards</span></td><td class="c4">All the windows had been <b>boarded up</b>.<br>所有窗户都用木板封牢了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bob</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbob ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">迅速冒出；浮出<br><span class="en">to come to the surface quickly</span></td><td class="c4">She dived in and <b>bobbed up</b> a few seconds later in the middle of the pool.<br>她潜入水中，几秒钟后在游泳池中央猛地钻出水面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbob ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">突然出现<br><span class="en">to appear suddenly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>bobbed up</b> from behind the fence.<br>她从篱笆后面突然冒了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bog ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">陷于停顿；停滞不前<br><span class="en">to be unable to make progress</span></td><td class="c4">The bill <b>bogged down</b> after being passed by Congress.<br>议案在国会通过之后难以推行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌbogged ˈdown (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">沉入泥沼(或沼泽)；受困无法前进<br><span class="en">to be/get stuck in mud or wet ground; to become stuck in sth and unable to make progress</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>got bogged down</b> in the mud.<br>汽车陷入泥潭中动弹不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌbogged ˈdown (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">陷入困境；停滞不前<br><span class="en">to be unable to make progress in an activity</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>get bogged down</b> in details.<br>不要纠缠于细枝末节。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>boil</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌboil aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">液体烧干<br><span class="en">if a liquid boils away, it boils until there is nothing left</span></td><td class="c4">The water in the saucepan had all <b>boiled away</b>.<br>炖锅里的水煮干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌboil sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">熬浓；炖浓<br><span class="en">to make a liquid less in quantity by boiling it</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Boil the report down</b> to the key points.<br>把报告归纳为几个要点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>boil ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">液体煮溢；潽出<br><span class="en">if a liquid in a pan, etc. boils over, it boils and flows over the side of the pan</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let the milk <b>boil over</b>.<br>别把牛奶煮谱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>boil ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">怒火；争论等恶化；失控<br><span class="en">(into sth) (Informal) if anger, an argument, etc. boils over,it changes and becomes very violent and difficult to control</span></td><td class="c4">The unrest could <b>boil over</b> into civil war.<br>骚乱有可能失控，进而演变成内战。<br>She interrupted swiftly before his temper could <b>boil over</b> again.<br>没等他再次动怒，她便急忙把话岔开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bolt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbolt sth ˈon (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">后期添加；添附<br><span class="en">to add sth to sth else at a later stage</span></td><td class="c4">Statistics should be an integral part of the course and not just <b>bolted on</b> afterwards.<br>统计学应是本课程不可分割的一部分，而不是后来补加的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bomb</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbomb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">惨败；一败涂地<br><span class="en">to fail very badly</span></td><td class="c4">The movie <b>bombed out</b> at the box office.<br>这部电影票房惨淡。单独使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bone</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bone ˈup on sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">学习；温习<br><span class="en">to study sth; to look again at sth you already know</span></td><td class="c4">I must <b>bone up on</b> my French before we 80 to Paris.<br>我们去巴黎之前，我一定得把法语捡起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>book</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˌbooked ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">人没有空闲<br><span class="en">if a person is booked up, they have no time available</span></td><td class="c4">He can't see you tomorrow, he's <b>booked</b> up.<br>他明天日程排满了，无法见你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>boom</b></td><td class="c2"><b>boom ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">声音或嗓音浑厚有力地发出<br><span class="en">if a sound or sb's voice booms out, it makes a loud, deep noise</span></td><td class="c4">His voice <b>boomed out</b>, announcing the winners.<br>他用浑厚响亮的声音宣布获胜者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>boom ˈout sth</b></td><td class="c3">浑厚有力地说<br><span class="en">to say sth in a loud deep voice</span></td><td class="c4">The trainer <b>boomed out</b> instructions through a loudhailer.<br>教练通过扩音器用浑厚有力的嗓音发出指令。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>boot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>boot ˈups boot sth ˈup (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">使(计算机)启动<br><span class="en">if a computer boots up, or sb boots it up, it is turned on and becomes ready to use</span></td><td class="c4">My machine isn't <b>booting</b> up properly.<br>我的机器不能正常启动。<br>When you <b>boot</b> up, a menu will appear on the screen.<br>启动之后，屏幕上会显示一个菜单。<br><b>Boot</b> the computer up and enter your password.<br>打开计算机，输入你的密码。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>border</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈborder on sth also ˈborder upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">毗邻；邻接；与…接壤<br><span class="en">to share a border with another country or region; to be next to a place</span></td><td class="c4">Many states formerly <b>bordering</b> on the have now joined.<br>原先与欧盟毗邻的多个国家现已加入欧盟。<br>Slovenia <b>borders</b> on Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia.<br>斯洛文尼亚与意大利、奥地利、匈牙利和克罗地亚接壤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈborder on sth also ˈborder upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">近乎；接近<br><span class="en">to come close to being sth</span></td><td class="c4">Her self-confidence <b>borders</b> on arrogance.<br>她自信得近乎傲慢。<br>Our task <b>borders</b> on the impossible.<br>我们的任务几乎不可能完成。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bore</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbore ˈinto sb/sth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">盯住看；瞪着眼看；目不转睛地看<br><span class="en">if sb’s eyes bore into sb/sth, they stare in a way that makes sb feel uncomfortable</span></td><td class="c4">His blue eyes seemed to <b>bore into</b> her.<br>他的一双蓝眼睛似乎要看穿她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>boss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌboss sb aˈround (also,boss sb aˈbout especially BrE) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…发号施令；对…颐指气使；对…呼来唤去<br><span class="en">to tell sb what to do in a determined or unpleasant way</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>bossing his wife around</b>.<br>他总是对妻子指手画脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>botch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>botch sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…弄坏；把…搞槽<br><span class="en">to spoil sth by doing it badly; to do sth badly</span></td><td class="c4">Instead of fixing my computer, he's <b>botched it up</b> completely.<br>他没有修好我的计算机，反倒把它彻底弄坏了。</td></tr>
