<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bottle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bottle sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">掩饰；隐藏(感情)<br><span class="en">to keep your feelings, especially sadness or anger, hidden and not tell other people how you are feeling</span></td><td class="c4">Tell someone how you're feeling, instead of <b>bottling it all up</b>.<br>找人说说你的感受，不要一味闷在心里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bottom</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bottom ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">市场；价格或恶劣局势达最低点；停止恶化；探底<br><span class="en">if markets, prices or bad situations bottom out, they reach their lowest point and then stop getting worse</span></td><td class="c4">The recession has finally <b>bottomed out</b>.<br>经济萧条局面终于开始好转。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bounce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bounce aˈround <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">居无定所；无固定工作<br><span class="en">to live or work in many different places without developing a routine</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>bounced around</b> for a few years, living in friends'basements.<br>他很多年居无定所，常住在朋友家的地下室里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bounce sth aˈround <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">人探讨；商议<br><span class="en">to discuss sth with other people</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>bouncing some new ideas around</b>.<br>我们正在讨论一些新想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bounce sth ˈoff sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向(某人)试探性地透簬(想法)<br><span class="en">to tell sb else your ideas to find out what they think about them</span></td><td class="c4">We were able to share problems and <b>bounce ideas off</b> each other.<br>我们共同探讨了问题并相互交流了想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bow ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">点头；欠身(以示敬意)；鞠躬<br><span class="en">(to/before sb/sth) to move your head or the top part of your body forwards or downwards as a sign of respect</span></td><td class="c4">He refused to <b>bow down</b> before the king.<br>他拒绝向国王鞠躬。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bow ˈout<br>ˌbow ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">退出；告别(成功的事业等)<br><span class="en">to stop doing an activity or a job that you have been doing successfully, often for a long time</span></td><td class="c4">After thirty years in politics, he feels it is time to <b>bow out</b>.<br>由于已从政三十年，他觉得是引退的时候了。<br>Smith will <b>bow out</b> of professional football at the end of the season.<br>本赛李末史密斯将告别职业足球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbow to sth</b></td><td class="c3">勉强同意做(或接受)；屈从于<br><span class="en">to agree unwillingly to do sth or to accept sth that sb else wants you to</span></td><td class="c4">The government eventually <b>bowed to</b> public pressure.<br>政府最终向公众压力低头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bowl</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bowl sb ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">撞倒；撞翻<br><span class="en">to run into sb and knock them down</span></td><td class="c4">The explosion <b>bowled us all over</b>.<br>爆炸把我们全都震倒在地。<br>Philip <b>bowled us all over</b> by deciding to go into advertising.<br>菲利普决定投身广告业，我们对此都大为吃惊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>box</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbox sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">阻碍<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from doing what they want, especially by creating rules or other difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">The President unable to act because the Democrats were <b>boxing him in</b>.<br>总统受到民主党人的掣肘，无法采取行动。<br>She was <b>boxed in</b> by rules and regulations.<br>她被规章制度束缚了手脚。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbox sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">围困；封堵<br><span class="en">to prevent a person or a vehicle from moving by surrounding them/it with other people or vehicles</span></td><td class="c4">You can't park here-you're <b>boxing that car in</b>!<br>这里不能停车——你挡了那辆车的路。<br>He couldn't overtake the leader because he was <b>boxed in</b> by the other runners.<br>他无法超越领跑者，因为其他运动员把他的路堵住了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbox ˈouts<br>box sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">篮球</td><td class="c4">If we don't start <b>boxing</b> <b>out</b>, we'll lose every game!<br>如果我们不开始挡人抢篮板球，我们会输掉每场比赛。<br>We tried to <b>box</b> him <b>out</b> every time he went up for a shot.<br>每当他跳起投篮，我们都全力挡人抢他的篮板球。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>box sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使不能参加活动；业务等<br><span class="en">(of sth) (ame) to force sb into a situation in which they can no longer take part in an activity, business, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The Senator accused them of trying to <b>box him out</b> of the Republican convention.<br>那名参议员指责他们试图将他排除在共和党大会之外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>box sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…装箱；把…裝盒<br><span class="en">to put sth in a box or boxes</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>boxed up</b> all the old baby clothes to send to her niece.<br>她把所有的旧婴儿服都装箱寄给侄女。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>branch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>branch ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">道路分岔；岔开<br><span class="en">if a road or path branches off, it leaves a larger one and goes in a different direction</span></td><td class="c4">She followed the path until it <b>branched off</b>.<br>她沿着小路一直走到岔道口。<br>Over the bridge a road <b>branches off</b> to the right.<br>过了桥有一条往右去的岔道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbranch ˈout (into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">涉足新领域；开拓新业务<br><span class="en">to begin to do a new job or an activity that you do not usually do</span></td><td class="c4">The company is <b>branching out</b> into Europe.<br>公司正在拓展欧洲业务。<br>She's leaving the company to <b>branch out</b> on her own.<br>她要离开公司独自创业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>break</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">脱离；脱开<br><span class="en">(from sth) if an object breaks away from sth that is holding it in place, it becomes separated from it</span></td><td class="c4">The boat had <b>broken away</b> from its moorings.<br>船起锚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">脱逃；挣脱<br><span class="en">(from sb) to escape suddenly from sb who is holding you or keeping you prisoner</span></td><td class="c4">The prisoner <b>broke away</b> from the guards.<br>犯人挣脱了看守。3。<br>Two states <b>broke away</b> from the federation.<br>两个州脱离了联邦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">人群中离开；脱开<br><span class="en">(from sb/sth) to move away from a group of people or a crowd</span></td><td class="c4">She managed to <b>break away</b> from the pack (= in a race) and establish a lead.<br>她总算甩开了其他赛跑选手，确立了领先优势。<br>He <b>broke away</b> from the group and came over to talk to us.<br>他离开那。<br>We (= our car) <b>broke</b> down on the motorway.<br>我们在高速公路上抛锚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">拋弃(可惯)；破除(传统)；破旧立新<br><span class="en">(from sb/sth) to reject a tradition or the usual way of doing things and do sth new and different</span></td><td class="c4">The company is trying to <b>break away</b> from its traditional image.<br>公司正试图摆脱其传统形象。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>break ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">车辆等出故障；出毛病<br><span class="en">if a vehicle, etc. breaks down, it stops working because of a fault</span></td><td class="c4">The washing has <b>broken down</b> again.<br>洗衣机又坏了。<br>We (= our car) <b>broke down</b> twice on the way home.<br>在回家的路上我们的车抛锚了两次。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>break ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">谈判；婚姻等失败；破裂<br><span class="en">if talks, a marriage, etc. break down, they fail</span></td><td class="c4">Negoriations between the two sides have <b>broken down</b>.<br>双方的谈判破裂了。<br>Their marriage <b>broke down</b> after three years.<br>结婚三年后，他们分手了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>break ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">情不自禁地哭起来<br><span class="en">to lose control of your feelings and start crying</span></td><td class="c4">As she drove away, I just <b>broke down</b> and wept.<br>她开车远去时，我不。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>break ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">健康恶化；崩溃<br><span class="en">if your health breaks down, it becomes very bad</span></td><td class="c4">Her health <b>broke down</b> as a result of the strain.<br>她因过度劳累，身体垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>break ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">分成若干；部分<br><span class="en">(into sth) to be divided into parts so that it is easier to discuss, to analyse or to deal with</span></td><td class="c4">My weekly budget <b>breaks down</b> as follows: 50% for rent, 20% for food, 10% for travel, and 20% for everything else.<br>我每周的预算分项列明如下：租金 50%,食物 20%,交通 10%,其他 20%。<br>The job <b>breaks down</b> into seven parts.<br>这项工作分为七部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">打倒；砸破<br><span class="en">to make sth fall down or open by hitting it hard</span></td><td class="c4">They had to get the police to <b>break the door down</b>.<br>他们不得不请警察来撞开门。<br>The question can be <b>broken down</b> into two Parts.<br>这个问题可以分为两部分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k, break ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">非法闯入；强行进入<br><span class="en">to enter a building illegally or by force</span></td><td class="c4">Somebody <b>broke</b> in last night and stole the and video.<br>昨天夜里有人闯进屋里，偷走了电脑和录像机。<br>Mary <b>broke</b> in: Y's not her fault!'<br>玛丽插嘴说：“这不是她的错！1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbreak-in n</b></td><td class="c3">非法闯入；强行进入</td><td class="c4">There has been a series of <b>break-ins</b> in the area.<br>这个地区接二连三发生了数起破门入户案件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">训练(马匹)<br><span class="en">to train a person so that they get used to a new job or situation; to train a horse so that you can ride it</span></td><td class="c4">We try to <b>break newcomers in</b> gently.<br>我们努力让新手逐渐适应环境。<br>The horses hadn't been <b>broken in</b>.<br>那些马还没经过训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把(新鞋)逐渐穿得合脚<br><span class="en">if you break in new shoes or boots, you wear them until they become comfortable</span></td><td class="c4">It took me weeks to <b>break in</b> these new boots.<br>我穿了几个星期后，这双新靴子才渐渐合脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>break ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">非法强行闯入(建筑)；撬开(汽车)<br><span class="en">to enter a building, open a car, etc. illegally and by force</span></td><td class="c4">A thief can <b>break into</b> a car in under ten seconds.<br>窃贼十秒钟之内就能把车撬开。<br>Three houses in our street have been <b>broken into</b> this week.<br>我们这条街本星期有三户人家被盗。<br>Her <b>face</b> broke into a huge smile.<br>她立刻笑容满面。<br>The audience <b>broke into</b> applause.<br>观众爆发出热烈的掌声。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>break ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">干扰；扰乱(思路)<br><span class="en">to interrupt sb's thoughts</span></td><td class="c4">Her mother's voice <b>broke into</b> her thoughts.<br>她母亲的说话声打断了她的思绪。四。<br>She is trying to <b>break into</b> journalism.<br>她正努力跻身新闻界。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">结束；终止(关系等)<br><span class="en">to end sth such as a relationship</span></td><td class="c4">Britain threatened to <b>break off</b> diplomatic relations.<br>英国威胁要断绝外交关系。<br>They were having an affair but she <b>broke it off</b>.<br>他们原本有私情，但是她甩了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">预备好；备妥用品；食物；饮料等<br><span class="en">to get sth ready to be used, drunk</span></td><td class="c4">It is useful to <b>break out</b> results by state.<br>把结果按州分类大有益处。<br>She <b>broke</b> off a piece of chocolate and gave it to me.<br>她掰下一块巧克力给了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbreakout n</b></td><td class="c3">信息的分类；归类<br><span class="en">the separation of information into categories in order to study it more closely</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Breakouts</b> were organized into ten regions.<br>信息按十个地区分类。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break ˈout in/into sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然布满汗水<br><span class="en">to suddenly become covered in sth such as sweat</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>broke out in</b> a cold sweat at the thought of the trial.<br>一想到审判，他冒出一身冷汗。<br>My skin has <b>broken out in</b> an itchy rash.<br>我的皮肤上突然起了一片令人发痒的皮疹。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreak ˈthrough <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">获得；初次重要成功；取得重大新发现；突破<br><span class="en">to achieve your first important success in sth; to make an important or new discovery</span></td><td class="c4">Scarlett Johansson <b>broke through</b> as a star with Lost in Translation.<br>斯嘉丽•约翰逊因影片《迷失东京》而崭簬头角，成为一颗新星。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">超过；超越(某一水平)<br><span class="en">to become greater in size or quantity than a particular level</span></td><td class="c4">Unemployment figures have <b>broken through</b> the three million barrier.<br>失业人数突破了三百万大关。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">学校或学生期末放假<br><span class="en">if a school or the children in it break up, school closes for the holidays at the end of a period of the school</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>break up</b> for Christmas next week.<br>我们下个星期放假过圣诞节。<br>Have the schools <b>broken up</b> yet?<br>学校放假了吗？2。<br>There are rumours that the band is <b>breaking up</b>.<br>据传那支乐队要散伙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break ˈup<br>.break sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使(集团或家庭)分解；分裂<br><span class="en">(into sth) if a group of people or a family breaks up, or sb breaks it up, the members separate and do not stay together</span></td><td class="c4">The conference <b>broke up</b> into discussion groups.<br>会议进行分组讨论。<br>She had never intended to <b>break up</b> his family.<br>她从未想过要拆散他的家庭。<br>The Soviet Union began to <b>break up</b> in 1991.<br>苏联于 1991 年开始解体。<br>Police <b>broke up</b> the demonstration.<br>警察驱散了示威人群。o1。<br>The ship <b>broke up</b> on the rocks.<br>船触礁撞散了架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>break sb ˈup <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使纵声大笑<br><span class="en">to make sb laugh a lot</span></td><td class="c4">Watching my grandson blow bubbles just <b>broke me up</b>.<br>看着孙子吹泡泡，让我乐不可支。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbreak with sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">分歧与…绝交；与…决裂<br><span class="en">to end your connection Or relationship with sb/sth because you no longer agree with them</span></td><td class="c4">Nick <b>broke with</b> his father to set up his own firm.<br>尼克与父亲分道扬镳，创办了自己的公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbreak with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">摈弃；破除传统；成例等；破旧立新<br><span class="en">to reject sth such as a tradition or the past and decide to do sth different</span></td><td class="c4">The new directors are eager to <b>break with</b> the past.<br>新一届董事急于与过去决毅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>breathe</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreathe ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">吸气<br><span class="en">to take air into your lungs through your nose or mouth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Breathe in</b> through your nose as you stretch up.<br>伸展于臂，用鼻子吸气。<br>He <b>breathed in</b> deeply and then spoke.<br>他深吸了一口气，开始讲话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreathe sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">吸入气体；烟雾；气味等<br><span class="en">to take air, smoke, a smell, etc. in through your nose or mouth</span></td><td class="c4">We walked along the beach, <b>breathing in</b> the sea air.<br>我们沿着海滩漫步，呼吸着海边的空气。o0。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>breathe sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">为…注入生机；活力或；热情<br><span class="en">to fill sth with life, energy or enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">She has <b>breathed fresh life into</b> the movie industry.<br>她给电影业注入了新的活力。o时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>breathe ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">呼气<br><span class="en">to send air out of your lungs through your nose or mouth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Breathe out</b> slowly through your mouth as you stand up.<br>站起来时，用嘴巴缓缓呼气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>breathe sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">呼出气体；烟雾等<br><span class="en">to send air, smoke, etc. out through your nose or mouth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Breathe the air out</b> slowly and steadily.<br>平稳地徐徐呼气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>breeze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>breeze ˈin<br>ˌbreeze ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻盈而自信地走入；信步走入；飘然而至<br><span class="en">to arrive somewhere or enter a place in a relaxed, cheerful and confident way</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>breezed in</b> and greeted everyone with a smile.<br>她一阵风似的飘进来，向大家微笑致意。<br>He <b>breezed into</b> the office and announced he was leaving.<br>他潇洒地走进办公室，宣布他要走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbreeze ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易通过；轻松完成<br><span class="en">to succeed in doing sth very easily</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>breezed through</b> the first exam.<br>她毫不费力地通过了第一次考试。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brew</b></td><td class="c2"><b>brew ˈup<br>ˌbrew sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">沏(茶)；煮(咖啡)<br><span class="en">to prepare a hot drink of tea or coffee</span></td><td class="c4">Come into the kitchen while I <b>brew up</b>.<br>我在煮咖啡，你就到厨房来吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrick sth ˈin/up</b></td><td class="c3">用砖填补(洞)；用砖堵住(洞)<br><span class="en">to fill in or block an opening with bricks</span></td><td class="c4">The fireplace had been <b>bricked in</b> some years before.<br>壁炉几年前用砖封上了。<br>Somebody had <b>bricked up</b> all the doors and windows.<br>有人用砖封堵了所有的门窗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brief</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrief aˈgainst sb</b></td><td class="c3">提供有损(某政客)名誉的信息<br><span class="en">to give information about sb, especially a politician, that is intended to damage their reputation</span></td><td class="c4">The minister accused her office of <b>briefing against</b> her.<br>部长指责部下泄露旨在诋毁她名誉的信息。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brighten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>brighten ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">天气好转；放晴<br><span class="en">if the weather brightens up, it becomes clearer and brighter</span></td><td class="c4">After a dull start, it should <b>brighten up</b> later.<br>刚开始是阴天，过会儿就会晴朗起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>brim ˈover (with sth) usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">He filled my glass so full it was <b>brimming</b> <b>over</b>!<br>他把我的杯子斟得太满了！都溢出来了。<br>Her eyes were <b>brimming</b> <b>over</b> with tears.<br>她热泪盈眶。</td></tr>

<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bring</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sth aˈbout</b></td><td class="c3">导致；引起<br><span class="en">to make sth happen</span></td><td class="c4">What has <b>brought about</b> this change?<br>这一变化是如何造成的。<br>His nervous breakdown was <b>brought about</b> by stress.<br>他神经崩溃是压力所致。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">带上…(去某处)；把…带来<br><span class="en">to bring sb/sth somewhere with you</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>bring my sister along</b> to the party?<br>我能带妹妹来参加聚会吗。<br>She <b>brought some CDs along</b>.<br>她带了些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…送回(某处)；送…回家<br><span class="en">to return sb to a place; to take sb home</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>bring him back</b> (= to make him return) to the matter in hand.<br>她试图让他回过头来处理手头上的事情。<br>Putting the driver of the car in prison won't <b>bring my sister back</b> (= return her to life).<br>把汽车司机关进监狱也不会让我姐姐复活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">恢复…的工作(或职位)；使复原<br><span class="en">to put sb back in their old job or position</span></td><td class="c4">United have <b>brought back</b> their old manager.<br>联队重新起用从前的主教练。<br>The economic recovery will <b>bring</b> down unemployment.<br>经济复苏将降低失业率。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">回忆起；使记起<br><span class="en">to make you remember sth or think about it again</span></td><td class="c4">Talking about his death <b>brought it all back</b> to me.<br>说起他的死，就让我想起过去的一切。<br>The phot <b>brought back</b> happy memories.<br>这些照片唤起了美好的回忆。<br>Can you <b>bring me something back</b>?<br>替我带点东西回来好吗？限度。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbring sb/sth before sb/sth (law)</b></td><td class="c3">把…提交；珽审；将…提交讨论<br><span class="en">to present sb for judgement; to present sth to sb/sth for discussion or a decision</span></td><td class="c4">Children should not be <b>brought before</b> a court.<br>儿童不应在法庭上受审。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使沮丧；使不悦<br><span class="en">to depress sb; to make sb unhappy</span></td><td class="c4">Spending New Year alone <b>brought me right down</b>.<br>独目一人过新年让我闷闷不乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">拿下来；使降低<br><span class="en">to take sb/sth from a higher to a lower level</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>brought all the boxes down</b> from the attic.<br>他们把所有箱子从阁楼上搬了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使倒地；使坠落；跌倒<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth fall to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>brought down</b> in the penalty area.<br>他在禁区内被撞倒。<br>Their plane was <b>brought down</b> by a violent storm.<br>他们的飞机遇强烈风暴坠毁了。<br>When she fell, she <b>brought him down</b> with her.<br>她倒下的时候把他也带倒了。<br>He <b>brought down</b> the bird with a single shot.<br>他一枪就射落了那只鸟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使政府；领导人等倒台；打倒；击败<br><span class="en">to make a government, a leader, etc. lose power or be defeated</span></td><td class="c4">The scandal <b>brought the government down</b>.<br>这件丑闻导致政府垮台。四B。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sth ˈdown on/upon sb <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给…带来(令人不快的事)；连累<br><span class="en">to make sth unpleasant happen to sb as a result of your actions</span></td><td class="c4">He had <b>brought nothing but trouble down on</b> the family.<br>他尽给家里添乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈforth <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, formal, rare)</span></b></td><td class="c3">生(孩子)<br><span class="en">to give birth to sb</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>brought forth</b> a son.<br>她生了个儿子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈforth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">产生；导致<br><span class="en">to produce sth; to make sth happen</span></td><td class="c4">Her remarks <b>brought forth</b> a harsh response.<br>她的话招致严厉的回应。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈforward</b></td><td class="c3">将(日期或时间)提前<br><span class="en">to move sth to an earlier date or time</span></td><td class="c4">Well have to <b>bring</b> the date of the final game <b>forward</b>.<br>我们得把决赛日期提前。四e。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring ˈin sth<br>ˌbring sb ˈin sth</b></td><td class="c3">挣得；为…賺得<br><span class="en">to make or earn money for sb</span></td><td class="c4">How much is she <b>bringing in</b> every month?<br>她每月挣多少钱。<br>His job only <b>brought him in</b> a small income.<br>他的工作收入微薄。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">让…参与尤指提供意见；帮助等</td><td class="c4">Can we deal with this without <b>bringing the police in</b>?<br>我们不报警私下处理这件事行不行？r'd。<br>Experts were <b>brought in</b> to advise the government.<br>政府请来专家出谋划策。<br>Could you <b>bring us some tea in</b>?<br>请给我们端些茶来好吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">采用；施行(新法规)<br><span class="en">to introduce a new law</span></td><td class="c4">A new law was <b>brought in</b> to improve road safety.<br>实施了新法以加强道路安全。<br>New controls were <b>brought in</b> to limit spending and borrowing.<br>实行了新的管制措施以限制开支和借款。四。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">收(作物)<br><span class="en">to pick or cut and collect crops to be stored</span></td><td class="c4">Farmers haven't been able to <b>bring the harvest in</b> because of the weather.<br>天气不好，农民未能收割庄稼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在讨论；谈话；等中包括；提及<br><span class="en">to include or mention sb/sth in a discussion, conversation, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Why do you always have to <b>bring Pete into</b> it (= mention Pete when we are discussing sth)?<br>你怎么张口闭口就是皮特？I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">完成；做成(困难的事)<br><span class="en">to manage to do sth difficult successfully</span></td><td class="c4">England were close to victory, but they couldn't quite <b>bring it off</b>.<br>英格兰队离胜利仅一步之遥，但是最终仍功败垂成。<br>Thompson, the goalkeeper, <b>brought off</b> a superb save.<br>新守门员汤普森完成了一个精彩扑救。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb ˈon (BrE) (AmE ˌbring sb allong)</b></td><td class="c3">帮助(学习者)进步；提高(学习者)的水平<br><span class="en">to help sb to develop or improve when they are learning to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>bring on</b> the young players quickly.<br>我们需要帮助年轻选手尽快提高水平。<br>There's no time to <b>bring</b> employees along gradually.<br>没有时间按部就班地培训雇员了。</td></tr>

What's <b>brought this on</b> (= has made you so upset)?<br>你很少这么心神不宁。怎么回事？D8J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使更加自信；使不再羞怯<br><span class="en">to help sb to be more confident and less shy</span></td><td class="c4">He's good at <b>bringing out</b> nervous interviewees.<br>他善于帮助紧张的面试者放松下来。<br>A year at college has really <b>brought her out</b> of herself.<br>年的大学生活确实让她开朗了不少。<br>I hoped that university would <b>bring him out</b> of his shell.<br>我希望上大学会让他活泼开朗起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb ˈout in sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(皮肤)冒出(汗水等)；使(皮肤)布满(斑点等)<br><span class="en">to make sb's skin be covered in sth such as sweat or spots</span></td><td class="c4">Tomatoes <b>bring me out in</b> a rash.<br>我吃西红柿会出皮疹。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">把…带到(尤指象里)<br><span class="en">to take or bring sb/sth to a particular place, especially sb's home</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Bring your chair over</b> and sit with us!<br>把椅子搬过来，和我们坐一块儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring A and B toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使(双方)握手言和；和好如初；团结；联合<br><span class="en">to help two people or groups to end an argument; to unite two people or groups</span></td><td class="c4">The crisis <b>brought</b> the family closer <b>together</b>.<br>这场危机使一家人关系更融洽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring A and B toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">介绍两人相识；帮助两人交往<br><span class="en">to introduce two people who have never met; to help two people come together socially</span></td><td class="c4">It was me who <b>brought</b> them <b>together</b>.<br>是我给他俩牵线搭桥的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">聚集；使集合<br><span class="en">to collect a group of people or objects together in one place</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>brought</b> up (=1 grew up) on a farm.<br>我是在农场长大的。<br>They <b>brought</b> their children up very strictly.<br>他们对孩子管教很严。<br>We were <b>brought</b> up to be polite and do what we were told.<br>从小家里就培养我们懂礼貌和听话。0a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb/sth ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">将…运到较高的位置；尤指楼上；举起；抬起<br><span class="en">to move sb/sth to a higher place, especially up the stairs</span></td><td class="c4">Breakfast was <b>brought up</b> to our room.<br>早餐送到了我们的房间。<br>Callum is downstairs. Shall 1 <b>bring him up</b>?<br>卡勒姆在楼下。要不要我把他带上来。<br>She <b>brought her hand up</b> and slapped him.<br>她举起手扇了他一耳光。<br>I <b>brought the cup up</b> to my lips and took a sip of coffee.<br>我把杯子送到唇边，抿了一口咖啡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">举起；抬高<br><span class="en">to move sth from a lower to a higher position</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>brought up</b> her hand to protect her face.<br>她抬起手护住脸部。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">提出(话题)供讨论<br><span class="en">to mention a subject and start to talk about it</span></td><td class="c4">Every time I <b>bring the matter up</b>, he changes the subject.<br>每当我提起这件事，他就会转移话题。<br>Owen got another goal, <b>bringing the score up</b> to 4-0.<br>欧文又进一球，把比分扩大为4:0。回助。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bring sb ˈup against sth</b></td><td class="c3">使意识；面临；面对<br><span class="en">to make sb realize sth or face sth and deal with it</span></td><td class="c4">This case <b>brings us up against</b> the problem of punishment in schools.<br>这件事使我们直面学校体罚的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbring sb/sth ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助…达到标准；使达标<br><span class="en">to help sb/sth to reach an acceptable level or standard</span></td><td class="c4">They have now <b>brought the football ground up to</b> the required safety standards.<br>他们现在把足球场改建得符合规定的安全标准了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brown</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrown sth ˈout <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对特定机器；地域等减少供电(或供水)；对…实行供电(或供水)管制<br><span class="en">to reduce the amount of electrical power, water, etc. that is supplied to a particular machine, area, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Servers were <b>browned out</b> by the increase in Internet traffic.<br>互联网流量增大，造成服务器几乎瘫痪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>browse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>browse ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">浏览；随意翻阅<br><span class="en">to look through a book, a magazine, etc. without paying close attention or reading everything</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>browsed through</b> the newspaper while she waited.<br>她边等边浏览报纸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>brush</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush aˈgainst/by/ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">轻触；掠过<br><span class="en">to touch sb/sth lightly when you move close to them/it</span></td><td class="c4">The cat <b>brushed against</b> Alison's leg.<br>那只猫蹭了蹭艾莉森的腿。<br>He <b>brushed by</b>/past me and ran out.<br>他和我擦肩而过，跑了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>brush sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把推到一边<br><span class="en">to push sb/sth to one side</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>brushed</b> a strand of hair <b>aside</b>.<br>她把一绺头发捋开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>brush sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">不听；漠视；对…不以为然<br><span class="en">to refuse to listen to sb/sth or treat them/it as important</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>brushed my protests aside</b> and paid the bill.<br>他不顾我的反对，把账单付了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush sth</b></td><td class="c3">擦掉</td><td class="c4">She <b>brushed</b> a stray hair away from her face.<br>她拂开脸上的一缕散发。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>brush sb/yourself ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指跌倒后拂去…衣服上的尘土；掸干净<br><span class="en">to clean sb/yourself by brushing their/your clothes with your hand, especially after they/you have fallen</span></td><td class="c4">She stood up and <b>brushed</b> herself <b>down</b>.<br>她站起来，拍去身上的灰尘。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">刷干净<br><span class="en">to clean sth by brushing it thoroughly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Brush your coat down</b> to get the mud off.<br>把你外套上的泥巴刷刷干净。<br>The children were taught how to <b>brush down</b> their ponies.<br>大人教孩子们如何把他们的小马刷干净。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>brush ˈoff<br>ˌbrush sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">被刷去；拂去<br><span class="en">if mud, dust, etc. brushes off, or you brush it off, it is removed by brushing</span></td><td class="c4">We were able to <b>brush the dirt off</b> quite easily.<br>我们很容易就把灰尘掸掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">理睬；(毫不客气地)漠视<br><span class="en">to refuse to listen to sb; to ignore sb in a rude or unkind way</span></td><td class="c4">He tried to explain to her, but she <b>brushed him off</b> impatiently.<br>他要向她解释，可她很不耐烦，对他爱搭不理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">刷净；拂净<br><span class="en">to clean sth quickly by brushing it</span></td><td class="c4">He picked up his hat and <b>brushed it off</b> quickly.<br>他捡起帽子，马上把它掸干净。<br>She <b>brushed off offers</b> of help from her friends.<br>朋友们主动提出帮忙，她拒绝了。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbrush sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">梳理(头发等)<br><span class="en">to brush sth, especially hair, thoroughly to remove knots or to make it straighter</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>brushed out</b> her hair, washed her face and got into bed.<br>她梳好头，洗好脸，就上床了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bubble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bubble ˈover (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">充满；充溢着兴奋；热情；想法等<br><span class="en">to be full of excitement, enthusiasm, ideas, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>bubbling over</b> with excitement.<br>他们兴奋不已。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bubble ˈunder<br>ˌbubble ˈunder sth</b></td><td class="c3">有望走红；有望大获成功；可能大红大紫<br><span class="en">if sth is bubbling under, it is already fairly suc cessful but is not yet as successful as other things of the same kind, although it is likely to be so soon</span></td><td class="c4">This is our list of songs <b>bubbling under</b>.<br>这是我们认为可能会窜红的歌曲名单。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bubble ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">液体沸腾；冒泡；发出冒泡声<br><span class="en">ifa liquid bubbles up from the ground, etc., it rises up in the form of bubbles or making the sound of bubbles</span></td><td class="c4">Water <b>bubbled up</b> from the pool.<br>池塘里咕嘟咕嘟地冒水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbuck for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">极力谋求；拼命争取(尤指要职)<br><span class="en">to try in a determined way to win or gain sth you want very much, especially an important position</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>bucking for</b> a Cabinet post in the Nixon administration.<br>当时他千方百计想在尼克松政府谋得一个内阁职务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>buck ˈup <span class="tag">(old-fashioned BrE informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">表示催促快点；抓紧<br><span class="en">to tell sb to hurry up</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Buck up</b>! Well be late.<br>别磨蹭！我们要迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>buck ˈup<br>buck sb ˈup <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使振作；振奋<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb, more cheerful</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Buck up</b>! There's no school tomorrow!<br>打起精神来！明天不用上学了。<br>He <b>bucked up</b> when I said he could go.<br>我说他可以走了，他便来了精神。<br>A day out will <b>buck you up</b>.<br>到外面转一天，你就会有精神头了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bucket</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbucket down <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">下暴雨<br><span class="en">to rain heavily</span></td><td class="c4">It <b>bucketed down</b> all day.<br>整整下了一天倾盆大雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buddy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuddied ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">与…亲近；携手工作<br><span class="en">to/with sb/sth (ame, informal) to become friendly with sb or work closely with another person</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>buddied up</b> to Julie, hoping to get to know her brother.<br>她和茱莉套近乎，希望结识她的哥哥。I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>budget</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbudget for sth</b></td><td class="c3">预留…的费用；编制…的预算<br><span class="en">to plan to save or provide an amount of money for a particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">These extra costs have not been <b>budgeted for</b>.<br>这些额外开销没有编入预算。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>buff ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">显得健美<br><span class="en">to make yourself look fit and attractive</span></td><td class="c4">Youll need to spend some time in the gym if you want to <b>buff up</b> for your summer holiday.<br>要想在暑期度假时展现健美身材，你就得花点时间在健身房锻炼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuff sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用软布擦亮；擦净<br><span class="en">to polish sth with a soft cloth</span></td><td class="c4">Wax isn't as durable as a varnish and it needs <b>buffing up</b> occasionally.<br>蜡不如清漆耐用，还需要不时用软布擦拭。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bug</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbug ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">告诫对方别烦人；滚开<br><span class="en">to tell sb to stop bothering you</span></td><td class="c4">Should I tell him to <b>bug off</b>, or try to help?<br>我是该叫他滚蛋呢，还是该帮一帮他呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbug ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">眼睛圆睁；瞪大<br><span class="en">if your eyes bug out, they suddenly open fully because you are surprised or excited</span></td><td class="c4">They just sat there with their eyes <b>bugging out</b> as if they'd never seen a woman yell at a man before.<br>他们坐在那里，目瞪口呆，仿佛以前从未见过一个女人冲着男人大喊大叫。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbug ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指若干士兵<br><span class="en">of a group of soldiers, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">When the radio went down, a couple of units <b>bugged out</b>.<br>无线联络中断后，几个小队逃跑了。I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbug ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">心烦意乱；怒气冲冲<br><span class="en">(about/over sth) to become very upset or angry</span></td><td class="c4">He came over to my house, <b>bugging out</b> about something.<br>他来到我家，人显得很烦躁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bugger</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bugger aˈbout/aˈround (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, A,slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">鬼混；胡闹<br><span class="en">to waste time doing stupid or unimportant things; to behave in a silly way</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>buggering about</b> and let's get on with it.<br>别晃荡了，我们继续干正事吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbugger ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">走开；离开<br><span class="en">to go away</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Bugger off</b> and leave me alone.<br>滚开，别烦我。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>build</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuild sth ˈin<br>ˌbuild sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使成为体系；计划等的组成部分<br><span class="en">to make sth a fixed and permanent part of a system, a plan, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Safeguards against fraud are <b>built into</b> the system.<br>该系统植入了防欺诈的设置。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuild sth ˈin<br>ˌbuild sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…建造在…里；使固定于较大的；物件<br><span class="en">to make sth a fixed and permanent part of sth larger</span></td><td class="c4">The flash is <b>built into</b> the camera.<br>闪光灯设在照相机内。<br>This dishwasher can be <b>built in</b>.<br>这款洗碗机可以嵌入安装。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbuild on sth. also ˈbuild upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">在…的基础上发展<br><span class="en">to develop further from sth that you have already achieved</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>build</b> on last year's success.<br>我们要在去年取得成功的基础上再接再历。<br>This course <b>builds</b> on existing skills.<br>这门课程是对现有技能的提高。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbuild sth on sth (also ˈbuild sth upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">把…作为…的基础；把…建立在…的基础上<br><span class="en">to base sth on sth; to use sth as the basis or foundation for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Our company has <b>built its reputation on</b> the quality of its products.<br>我们公司的信誉建立在过硬的产品质量上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>build sth ˈout <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">改造；装修建筑；房屋；房间等<br><span class="en">to finish a building, house, room, etc. which already exists in a basic form, to suit the needs of the people who wil be using it</span></td><td class="c4">Building several offices at a time costs 10% to 20% less than <b>building out</b> a single suite.<br>一次性建造几间办公室，比改装一个套间要便宜 10% 到 20%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>build sth ˈout <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">扩展；扩建新系统；企业或计算机网络<br><span class="en">to develop or expand a new system, business or computer network</span></td><td class="c4">Our strategy is to <b>build out</b> the network in over 200 cities statewide.<br>我们的战略是将这一网络延伸至全国200多座城市。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>build sth ˈround sth (BrE) + A R<br>build ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增大；增强；增多<br><span class="en">to become greater, stronger or larger in number</span></td><td class="c4">Queues of traffic are <b>building</b> up after the accident.<br>车祸之后，车辆排起了长龙。<br>I could feel the anger <b>building</b> up inside me.<br>我感觉到心中怒火越烧越旺。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>build ˈup (to sth)<br>ˌbuild yourself ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">逐步准备(比赛等)<br><span class="en">to gradually prepare yourself for sth such as a race or competition</span></td><td class="c4">Start gently and <b>build</b> up to the more strenuous exercises.<br>开始时轻松点，逐渐过渡到高强度的训练。<br><b>Build</b> up slowly until you can jog for 30 minutes.<br>逐步增加时间，直到能慢跑30分钟。<br><b>Build</b> yourself up to the day of the performance.<br>好好为演出那天作准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuild sb/yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增进(健康)；增强(体质)<br><span class="en">to make sb healthier or stronger</span></td><td class="c4">She gave me lots of vitamins and minerals to <b>build</b> me up.<br>她让我服用很多维生素和矿物质，以增强体质。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bully</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbully sb ˈinto sth<br>ˌbully sb ˈinto doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">胁迫某人做某事<br><span class="en">to force sb to do sth by frightening them or threatening them</span></td><td class="c4">You can't <b>bully me into</b> saying anything!<br>你休想逼我说出一个字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bum</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbum aˈround sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在…闲逛；瞎混<br><span class="en">to travel somewhere with no particular plans</span></td><td class="c4">After I left school, I <b>bummed around</b> the world for a year.<br>毕业后我在世界各地游荡了一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbum sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使恼怒；使心烦<br><span class="en">to annoy sb</span></td><td class="c4">I was really <b>bummed out</b> that there were no tickets left.<br>票卖光了，我火冒三丈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bump aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">依然如故；毫无起色；徘徊不前<br><span class="en">to continue in the same way as before, without making any progress or improvement</span></td><td class="c4">United are still <b>bumping along</b> in the Third Division.<br>联队仍在丙级队里晃荡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbump ˈinto sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">碰见；偶遇<br><span class="en">to meet sb by chance</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>bumped into</b> an old friend in town today.<br>今天在城里我与一位老友不期而遇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbump ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">不小心碰上；冲撞<br><span class="en">to hit sb/sth by accident</span></td><td class="c4">In the dark I <b>bumped into</b> a chair.<br>在黑暗中我撞到了一把椅子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bump sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">谋杀；杀害<br><span class="en">to murder sb</span></td><td class="c4">He admitted <b>bumping off</b> Baines.<br>他承认杀了贝恩斯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bump sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">增加；提升<br><span class="en">to increase or raise sth</span></td><td class="c4">The company <b>bumped their prices up</b> by 10%.<br>公司提价 10%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bundle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbundle sb ˈoff (to sth .. )</b></td><td class="c3">把…匆匆送走；强行把…打发(到某处)<br><span class="en">to send sb somewhere in a hurry or when they do not want to go</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>bundled her son off</b> to school.<br>她急匆匆地把儿子送到学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bundle ˈup (in sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">穿得暖和<br><span class="en">to dress in warm clothes</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Bundle up</b>! It's freezing outside!<br>多穿点！外面很冷。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>bundle sth ˈup/toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">捆扎；打包<br><span class="en">to put or tie things together in a pile</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>bundled up</b> her clothes and pushed them into a cupboard.<br>她把衣服包起来，塞进衣橱。<br>The papers were all <b>bundled together</b>, ready to be thrown away.<br>报纸全部捆好了，准备扔掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bung</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbung sth ˈup (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用某物堵塞；阻塞<br><span class="en">to stop sth from moving or flowing through sth by putting sth in or across it</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>bunged the sink up</b> with tea leaves.<br>她倒的茶叶把水槽堵住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bunk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bunk ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指在；不舒适的地方将就过夜；勉强投宿；暂时睡下<br><span class="en">to lie down to sleep somewhere, especially somewhere uncomfortable or for only one night</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>bunked down</b> in an old barn for the night.<br>那晚我们凑合睡在一个旧谷仓里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buoy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuoy sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">鼓励；鼓劲<br><span class="en">to make or keep sb cheerful and confident</span></td><td class="c4">Winning the match <b>buoyed the ream up</b>.<br>比赛获胜使该队欢欣鼓舞。<br>She was <b>buoyed up</b> by her father's praise.<br>父亲的赞扬给她增添了信心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>buoy sth ˈup (finance)</b></td><td class="c3">保持(价格)处于高位；维持(价格)在可接受的水平<br><span class="en">to make or keep prices at a high or acceptable level</span></td><td class="c4">Share prices were <b>buoyed up</b> by the news.<br>这个消息使股价冲上高位。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>burn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>burn aˈway<br>burn sth aˈway to disappear as</b></td><td class="c3">使烧毁；烧光<br><span class="en">a result of burning; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">Half the candle had <b>burnt away</b>.<br>这支蜡烛燃烧掉了一半。<br>The fire had <b>burned away</b> part of the roof.<br>火灾使一部分屋顶被焚毁。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">火势减弱；变小<br><span class="en">if a fire burns down, it becomes less strong and burns with smaller flames</span></td><td class="c4">They sat by the fire, watching it slowly <b>burn down</b>.<br>他们坐在火边，看着火头逐渐变小。<br>She threatened to <b>burn the house down</b>.<br>她威胁要把房子烧掉。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>burn sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">烧掉；烧除<br><span class="en">to remove sth by burning</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Burn the old paint off</b> before repainting the door.<br>先把门上的旧漆烧掉，再刷新油漆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>burn sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">通过锻炼消耗(能量)<br><span class="en">(also ˌburn sth ˈup) to use energy by exercising</span></td><td class="c4">Walking briskly can <b>burn off</b> a lot of calories.<br>快步走能消耗很多卡路里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn ˈout<br>burn sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">因机器使用过度或过热出故障；损坏<br><span class="en">if a machine or part of a machine burns out or sb/sth burns it out, it stops working because it has been used too much or has got too hot</span></td><td class="c4">The clutch has <b>burnt out</b>.<br>离合器因过热而失灵了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn ˈout<br>ˌburn itself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">因燃料耗尽熄灭<br><span class="en">to stop burning because there is no more fuel</span></td><td class="c4">Blow out the candles before they <b>burn out</b>.<br>把蜡烛吹灭，免得烧完。<br>By the time the fire brigade arrived the fire had <b>burnt</b> (<b>itself</b>) <b>out</b>.<br>消防队赶到时，火已经(自己)熄灭了。“。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把…烧成空架子<br><span class="en">to destroy sth completely by fire, so that only the outside or the frame is left</span></td><td class="c4">Two cars were <b>burnt out</b> in the crash.<br>撞车事故中有两辆汽车被烧毁。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">被焚毁；被烧掉<br><span class="en">to be destroyed by heat</span></td><td class="c4">The spacecraft <b>burned up</b> as it entered the earth's atmosphere.<br>宇宙飞船进入地球大气层时被烧毁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburn sb ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">激怒；使大怒<br><span class="en">to make sb very angry</span></td><td class="c4">The way he treats me really <b>burns me up</b>.<br>他那么对待我，实在把我气疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>burrow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈburrow in sth</b></td><td class="c3">在容器中搜寻；摸索<br><span class="en">to search for sth among things in a container</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>burrowed in</b> her pocket and eventually found a few coins.<br>她在口袋里摸来摸去，终于找到了几枚硬币。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>burst</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburst ˈin (on sb/sth)<br>burst ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">闯入；闯进房间打断<br><span class="en">to enter a room, a building, etc. suddenly and noisily, interrupting the people who are In it</span></td><td class="c4">The door suddenly flew open and Mia <b>burst</b> in.<br>门突然开了，米娅猛地闯了进来。<br>She ran down the stairs and <b>burst</b> <b>into</b> the kitchen.<br>她跑下楼梯，一头扎进了厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈburst into sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然爆发；突然…起来<br><span class="en">to start producing or doing sth suddenly and with great force</span></td><td class="c4">The aircraft <b>burst into</b> flames (= suddenly started to burn).<br>飞机一下子燃烧了起来。I。<br>The cab's engine <b>burst into</b> life (= suddenly started to work).<br>出租车的引擎猛地发动起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈburst on/onto sth also ˈburst upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">突然显现；突然；在…出现<br><span class="en">to appear somewhere suddenly in a dramatic or unusual way</span></td><td class="c4">A major new talent has <b>burst</b> on/<b>onto</b> the tennis scene.<br>一名能力出众的新秀在网球界突然崭露头角。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌburst ˈout<br>burst ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然跑出<br><span class="en">to leave a room, a building, etc. suddenly and noisily</span></td><td class="c4">The door opened suddenly and a man <b>burst out</b> of the house.<br>门突然打开，一名男子从屋里冲了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>burst ˈout doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然开始做某事<br><span class="en">to begin doing sth suddenly</span></td><td class="c4">We looked at one another and <b>burst</b> <b>out</b> laughing.<br>我们相互瞧着对方，突然大笑起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>burst ˈthrough<br>ˌburst ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">闯过；突破<br><span class="en">to move suddenly through a door, a barrier, etc. with great force</span></td><td class="c4">The car drove fast up to the road block and <b>burst through</b>.<br>汽车快速开到路障前，一下子冲了过去。<br>She <b>burst through</b> the door pursued by two men.<br>她突然冲出门去，后面两名男子紧追不舍。<br>The sun <b>burst through</b> the clouds.<br>太阳破云而出。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bust</b></td><td class="c2"><b>bust ˈup (with sb) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">夫妻；朋友分手；散伙<br><span class="en">if a couple or two friends bust up, they have an argument and separate</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>bust up</b> after five years together.<br>他们在一起五年后分道扬镳了。<br>I <b>bust up</b> with Tim a while ago.<br>不久前我和蒂姆分手了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbust-up n <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">争吵；吵架</td><td class="c4">We had a huge <b>bust-up and now</b> we're not talking.<br>我们大吵了一顿，现在不说话了。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>bustle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbustle aˈbout/aˈround<br>ˌbustle aˈbout/aˈround sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在…或为…忙得团团转；东奔西跑<br><span class="en">to move about somewhere in a busy or hurried way</span></td><td class="c4">She was already <b>bustling</b> <b>about</b>, getting dinner ready for the family.<br>她已经在忙着为家人准备晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>butt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>butt ˈin <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">插嘴；打断<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) to rudely interrupt sb when they are speaking</span></td><td class="c4">He apologized for <b>butting in</b> on our conversation.<br>他为打断了我们的谈话道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>butt ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">粗鲁的说法滚开；别管闲事<br><span class="en">used to tell sb rudely to go away or not try to influence matters which do not concern them</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Butt out</b>! It's none of your business.<br>别多嘴多舌！这不关你的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>butter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbutter sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以甜言蜜语拍…的马屁；讨好；巴结<br><span class="en">to say nice things about sb because you want them to do sth for you or give you sth</span></td><td class="c4">We'd better <b>butter him up</b> a bit before we ask for his help.<br>我们最好先给他戴个高帽，再求他帮忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>button</b></td><td class="c2"><b>button ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常指因为讲话过多突然住口；闭上嘴<br><span class="en">to stop talking suddenly, often because you have said too much already</span></td><td class="c4">She was giggling with her friends, when the teacher told them to <b>button up</b>.<br>她正与朋友们咯咯说笑，老师要他们闭嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>button ˈup<br>ˌbutton sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">扣上纽扣；给…系上纽扣<br><span class="en">to be fastened with buttons; to fasten sth with buttons</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>buttoned up</b> his coat.<br>他扣好了外衣的纽扣。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>button sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">处理…的遗留问题；了结<br><span class="en">to finish dealing with the final parts or details of sth complicated</span></td><td class="c4">She went home for the funeral and to <b>button up</b> her father's financial affairs.<br>她回家参加葬礼，并计划了结父亲的财务事宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>buy sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">买回；购回(售出物品)<br><span class="en">if sb buys sth back, they buy again sth that they have sold earlier to sb else</span></td><td class="c4">The bank will supply and <b>buy back</b> foreign currency.<br>银行将提供并回购外汇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbuy-in n</b></td><td class="c3">扑克牌</td><td class="c4">It is important to get total Congressional <b>buy-in</b> from the beginning.<br>在开始阶段就获得因会的完全赞同十分重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuy ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">从众；随大溜<br><span class="en">to accept sth that many other people believe</span></td><td class="c4">We don't <b>buy into</b> the myth that money is the answer to everything.<br>我们不会人云亦云地相信金钱万能的神话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuy sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">收买；贿赂(某人不做某事)<br><span class="en">to pay sb to stop them acting against you, causing trouble for you, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They had to <b>buy Brennan off</b> to stop him from talking.<br>他们不得不花钱封住布伦南的口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>buy sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">为获得全部股份购买…的股份<br><span class="en">to buy part of a company, business, etc. from sb else so that you own all of it and control it</span></td><td class="c4">I want to <b>buy her out</b> and have the house to myself.<br>我想买下她名下的那部分产权，独自拥有这幢房子。<br>The company was <b>bought out</b> by two German businessmen.<br>公司的全部股份都被两个德国商人买下了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>buy sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">全部买下；尽量买进<br><span class="en">to buy quickly all of sth or as much as you can</span></td><td class="c4">They've <b>bought up</b> all the land in the area.<br>他们收购了这个地区的全部土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>buzz</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuzz aˈbout/round<br>buzz aˈbout/ˈround sth especially BrE</b></td><td class="c3">在…或为…忙得团团转；跑东跑西<br><span class="en">to move around quickly and actively</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>buzzed</b> <b>round</b> (the kitchen).<br>她(在厨房)忙得团团转。<br>The photographer <b>buzzed</b> around, checking the light.<br>摄影师奔来跑去，忙着检查灯光。<br>Questions <b>buzzed</b> <b>round</b> inside my head.<br>请多疑问萦绕在我的心头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌbuzz ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不太礼貌的说法滚开；走开<br><span class="en">to tell sb, not very Politely, to go away</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Buzz off</b>,I'm trying to work!<br>滚远点，我正干活呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>calculate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcalculate on sth<br>ˈcalculate on doing sth <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指作为计划的一部分指望；依赖；期待<br><span class="en">to depend or rely on sth happening or being true, especially as part of a plan</span></td><td class="c4">The developers are <b>calculating on</b> consumers'desire for better and better technology.<br>开发人员寄希望于消费者会需要越来越好的技术。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>call</b></td><td class="c2"><b>call aˈround<br>ˌcall aˈround sb/sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">四处(给…)打电话<br><span class="en">to telephone a number of different people, usually to try to get information</span></td><td class="c4">He's been <b>calling around</b> trying to get the best price on a computer.<br>他正四下打电话，想找到买计算机的最优价格。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把(某人)叫到别处去；叫走(某人)<br><span class="en">to ask sb to stop doing what they are doing and go somewhere else to deal with sth</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>called away</b> to the phone.<br>有人叫他去接电话。<br>She was <b>called away</b> from the meeting to deal with an emergency.<br>她被叫出会场去处理一件急事。总是用于被动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>call ˈback<br>ˌcall sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">给…再打电话；回电话<br><span class="en">to telephone sb again or to telephone sb who telephoned you earlier</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Kate</b> phoned. Can you call her back?<br>凯特来电话了。你给她回个电话好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sth ˈdown (on/upon sb) <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">祈求(某人受到)某惩罚；使(某人)遭受…灾祸<br><span class="en">to ask God, etc. to make sth unpleasant happen to sb because of sth bad they have done to you; to make sth bad happen to sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>called down</b> curses on them.<br>他诅咒他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall for sb <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">去某人家接(某人)<br><span class="en">to go to sb’'s home, for example, and take them or go with them somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">Shall I <b>call for</b> you at eight?<br>我八点钟过来接你好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall for sth</b></td><td class="c3">需要；要求有(行动或品质)<br><span class="en">if a situation calls for a particular action or quality, it needs or requires it</span></td><td class="c4">This <b>calls for</b> a celebration!<br>这得庆贺一下。<br>What she's doing <b>calls for</b> great skill and courage.<br>她的工作需要很高的技能和勇气。<br>Tougher action by the government is <b>called for</b>.<br>政府应该采取更加严厉的行动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall for sth</b></td><td class="c3">气象预报预报(会有某种天气)<br><span class="en">(of a weather forecast) to predict a particular type of weather</span></td><td class="c4">The forecast today <b>calls for</b> mostly sunny conditions with a light wind.<br>天气预报说今天以晴天为主，有微风。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall for sth<br>ˈcall for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">公开要求；向…呼吁<br><span class="en">to do sth to demand publicly that sth should be done</span></td><td class="c4">The group has <b>called for</b> a boycott of the elections.<br>该团体号召抵制选举。<br>The other directors have <b>called for</b> him to resign.<br>其他董事已要求他辞职。<br>A total ban on nuclear weapons has been <b>called for</b>.<br>人们呼吁全面禁止核武器。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sth ˈforth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">激起；导致(反应)<br><span class="en">to produce a particular reaction</span></td><td class="c4">Her remarks have <b>called forth</b> harsh criticism in the media.<br>她的话招致媒体的严厉批评。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">召来；请来某人来提供建议；帮助维修等<br><span class="en">to ask sb to come and help, give advice, repair sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Youll have to <b>call a plumber in</b> to look at this.<br>你得请水暖工过来瞧瞧。<br>Bomb disposal experts were <b>called in</b> to get rid of the device.<br>请来了拆弹专家拆除这个装置。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">召回(有问题的产品)<br><span class="en">to order or request the return of a product that has a fault</span></td><td class="c4">The manufacturers have <b>called in</b> the faulty goods.<br>制造商已召回次品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">喊走(攻击人的狗等)；撤走(搜查的士兵等)<br><span class="en">to order soldiers, dogs, etc. to stop attacking sb, searching for sb/sth, etc</span></td><td class="c4">Please <b>call your dog off</b>.<br>请把你的狗叫走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>call sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">取消；放弃<br><span class="en">to cancel or abandon sth that has been planned or that has already started</span></td><td class="c4">The meeting was <b>called off</b> at the last minute.<br>会议临到最后取消了。<br>Police called off the search <b>for</b> the climbers at dusk.<br>黄昏时分，警方停止了对登山者的搜救。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall on/upon sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用(力气)；鼓起(勇气)<br><span class="en">to use your strength, courage, etc. in order to achieve sth or deal with a problem</span></td><td class="c4">She had to <b>call on</b> all her reserves of courage to face the ordeal.<br>她不得不鼓足全部勇气，直面这一严峻考验。四B。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcall on/upon sb</b></td><td class="c3">恳请；请求；呼吁<br><span class="en">to do sth ormal to make a serious or urgent request to sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>call upon</b> all parties to respect the results of the election.<br>我们呼吁所有党派尊重选举结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打电话请病假<br><span class="en">to telephone to say that you are ill/sick and will not be coming to work</span></td><td class="c4">If you always <b>call out</b> on Mondays it looks suspicious.<br>如果你老是星期一打电话请病假，会显得很可疑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>call ˈout (to sb)<br>call sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">对某人呼喊<br><span class="en">to shout or say sth loudly in order to get sb's attention or help</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>called</b> <b>out</b> to her, but she carried on walking.<br>他大声叫她，但她还是继续走。<br>He woke in the night, <b>calling</b> <b>out</b> her name.<br>他夜里醒来，呼唤着她的名字。<br>They <b>called</b> <b>out</b> the numbers of the winning tickets.<br>他们高声宣读中奖的券号。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">紧急时召唤某人(帮助)<br><span class="en">to ask sb to come to help you, when there is an emergency</span></td><td class="c4">We had to <b>call out</b> an electrician.<br>我们不。<br>Troops were <b>called out</b> to deal with the riot.<br>已调集部队前往平息骚乱。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">批评；指责<br><span class="en">(for sth) (ame) to criticize sb's actions</span></td><td class="c4">Critics are <b>calling the company out</b> for releasing such shabby software.<br>评论家抨击该公司发布了如此蹩脚的软件。ˈ。<br>How much is the plumber's <b>call</b>-<b>out</b> charge?<br>请水暖工上门需要多少钱？词。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">叫…过来；让…过来<br><span class="en">to call sb to come over to where you are, because you want to speak to them, give or show them sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Call the waiter over</b>.<br>把服务员叫过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall ˈround <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">到别人家里短暂地拜访；探访<br><span class="en">to visit sb at their home for a short time</span></td><td class="c4">I just <b>called round</b> to say hello.<br>我只是过来打个招呼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">征召(服役或参战)<br><span class="en">to officially ask sb to go to do training in the army, navy or air force or to fight in a war</span></td><td class="c4">When the war began, he was too old to be <b>called up</b>.<br>战争爆发时，他已超过应征入伍的年龄。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcall sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">从计算机；中调出；调用<br><span class="en">(computing) to obtain information that is stored on a computer</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>called up</b> all the files he had worked on.<br>她调出他处理过的所有文件。o0。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>calm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>calm ˈdown<br>.calm sb/yourself ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使镇静下来；安静下来<br><span class="en">if sb calms down, or you calm them down, they stop being angry or excited and become calm</span></td><td class="c4">There was nothing we could do to <b>calm her down</b>.<br>我们无法让她平静下来。<br>He went for a walk to <b>calm himself down</b>.<br>他出去散步，好让自己的情绪平复下来。<br>Jack was so shocked that he had to be <b>calmed down</b> by his wife and son.<br>杰克惊呆了，他的妻儿不得不过来安抚他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>calm ˈdown<br>ˌcalm sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">平静下来；使(局势)趋于平静<br><span class="en">to become calmer; to make a situation calmer</span></td><td class="c4">The whole fuss will have <b>calmed down</b> by tomorrow.<br>这一切忙乱到明天就会平息下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>camp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcamp ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">路宿；宿营；(暂时)睡地板<br><span class="en">to sleep outside, usually in a tent; to sleep on the floor somewhere for a short time</span></td><td class="c4">If there is nowhere to stay, well have to <b>camp out</b>.<br>如果无处过夜，我们只能鐸宿。<br>People <b>camped out</b> in the school hall to escape the foodwater.<br>人们暂时在学校礼堂睡地铺，以躲避洪水。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcamp it ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">过分做作<br><span class="en">to behave in a very exaggerated manner, especially to attract attention to yourself or to make people laugh</span></td><td class="c4">He enjoys <b>camping it up</b>.<br>他喜欢哗众取宠。<br>I really <b>camped it up</b> in the final scene.<br>在最后一幕我的表演确实有些过火。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cancel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcancel ˈout<br>ˌcancel sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">抵消；对消<br><span class="en">if two or more things cancel out or one cancels out the other, they are equally important, but have an opposite effect on a situation so that the situation does not change</span></td><td class="c4">The gains and losses are expected to <b>cancel out</b>.<br>预计得失参半。<br>Our expenditure and profits <b>cancel each other out</b>.<br>我们的开支和盈利相互抵消。<br>The job is hard work, but this is <b>cancelled out</b> by the fact that the people are so nice.<br>虽然工作很辛苦，因为大家都很友善，这也就算不了什么了。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cannon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcannon ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">移动中的人；车辆等<br><span class="en">of a moving person, vehicle, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She stopped suddenly and I almost <b>cannoned into</b> her.<br>她突然停下来，我差点撞上她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcannon ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">移动中的物体撞上…后弹开<br><span class="en">if sth moving cannons off sb/sth, it hits them/it by accident and with great force and then goes off in a different direction</span></td><td class="c4">The ball <b>cannoned off</b> his leg into the goal.<br>球碰到他的腿，弹入球门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>capitalize</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcapitalize on sth also ˈcapitalize upon sth less frequent, more formal</b></td><td class="c3">利用；凭借<br><span class="en">to use sth to gain further advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">The opposition tried to <b>capitalize</b> on popular discontent over the new law.<br>反对党试图利用公众对新法律的不满情绪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>care</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcare for sb</b></td><td class="c3">喜欢<br><span class="en">to like or love sb</span></td><td class="c4">I just want to be loved and <b>cared for</b> by somebody.<br>我只是想有人爱我，在乎我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>carry</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarry sb/sth aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">把…往前带；把…往前推<br><span class="en">to take or move sb/sth forward</span></td><td class="c4">His body had been <b>carried along</b> by the river.<br>他的尸身随河水漂流。<br>The crowd was so thick that she was <b>carried along</b> with it.<br>人群挤得水泄不通，她只能随着人流往前移动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry sb/sth aˈway/ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">把…抬走；把…冲走<br><span class="en">to support the weight of sb/sth and take them/it away</span></td><td class="c4">A strong current <b>carried the dinghy away</b>.<br>一阵激流卷走了小艇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarry sb ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使回想起来；陷入回忆<br><span class="en">to remind sb of sth that happened in the past</span></td><td class="c4">The song <b>carried her back</b> to her childhood.<br>这首歌令她回想起自己的童年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">抓获；俘获<br><span class="en">to capture sb</span></td><td class="c4">The enemy <b>carried off</b> many prisoners.<br>敌人抓了很多俘虏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">廠得；获得<br><span class="en">to win sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>carried off</b> most of the prizes.<br>她贏得了大多数奖项。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">成功地应对；轻而易举地处理<br><span class="en">to succeed in doing sth difficult; to deal with a difficult situation successfully</span></td><td class="c4">She's the only person I know who can wear a dress like that and <b>carry it off</b>!<br>穿着那样的裙子又若无其事的，我认识的人中只有她一个！1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarry sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续；承接<br><span class="en">to continue sth, especially sth that sb else has begun</span></td><td class="c4">Our children will <b>carry this tradition on</b> after us.<br>我们的子孙会将我们的这一传统传承下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">从事；开展(活动)<br><span class="en">to do the activity mentioned</span></td><td class="c4">We're trying to <b>carry on</b> a very important conversation!<br>我们正要进行一次很重要的谈话呢。<br>They <b>carried on</b> a correspondence for over forty years.<br>他们之间的通信延续了四十多年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">经营业务；生意<br><span class="en">to carry on a business/ trade</span></td><td class="c4">It's hard to <b>carry it on</b> when your heart's no longer in it.<br>如果心思不在上面，要进行下去是很困难的。1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcarry-out n</b></td><td class="c3">饭店的外卖；外带；食物<br><span class="en">a meal that you buy cooked from a restaurant and take away to eat somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">Let's get a <b>carry-out</b>.<br>我们来份外卖吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarry sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">延期；延迟<br><span class="en">to delay sth until a later time</span></td><td class="c4">The game had to be <b>carried over</b> until Wednesday.<br>比赛不得不推迟至星期三。<br>You can <b>carry over</b> 4 days' leave to next year.<br>你可以把4天的假挪到下一年休。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarry ˈthrough (on/with sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">履行；实现承诺；约定或安排<br><span class="en">to do and finish what you have promised, agreed or arranged to do</span></td><td class="c4">He convinced us that he would <b>carry through</b> with/on his promise.<br>他使我们相信他会兑现自己的诺言。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>carry sth ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">成功完成；顺利实现<br><span class="en">to finish a task, a plan, etc. successfully</span></td><td class="c4">She was determined to <b>carry through</b> her plans.<br>她决心完成计划。<br>Once Helen has started a task, shell <b>carry it through</b> to the end.<br>海伦一旦开始一项工作，就会把它做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cart</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cart sb/sth aˈway/ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">费劲地送走<br><span class="en">to take sb/sth away with some difficulty if</span></td><td class="c4">Two players were <b>carted off</b> to hospital.<br>好不容易才把两名运动员送到医院。<br>The police arrived and <b>carted 40 rioters off</b> to jail.<br>警察赶到，把40名聚众闹事者扭送到监狱。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>carve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcarve sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用刀伤害(人)；用刀划伤(脸)<br><span class="en">to wound sb or their face badly with a knife</span></td><td class="c4">He got <b>carved up</b> outside the pub last night.<br>昨天夜里他在酒吧外面被人用刀刺伤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcash ˈin (on sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">从中牟利；捞取好处<br><span class="en">to gain an advantage from a situation in a way that people think is wrong or dishonest</span></td><td class="c4">Many businesses <b>cashed in</b> on the massive public interest in her death.<br>很多公司利用公众对她去世的广泛关注来牟利。<br>The new law means video pirates can no longer <b>cash in</b> by selling illegal copies.<br>新法律意味着录像盜版者不能再靠销售非法拷贝賺钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcash sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…兑成现金；将…兑现<br><span class="en">to exchange sth for money</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Cash in</b> any remaining travellers' cheques when you return.<br>回来后把旅行支票余额兑现吧。<br>You will lose money i you <b>cash your policy in</b> early.<br>提前兑现保险单会亏钱的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcash ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常指提前把保险单；不动产或股票兑成现金(或套现)<br><span class="en">to exchange sth such as an insurance policy, property or shares money, often before you are supposed to do</span></td><td class="c4">With house prices still rising, many people are tempted to <b>cash out</b> while they can.<br>房价还在上涨，很多人想趁此时机把房子售出变现。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcash ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">纸牌；轮盘赌等</td><td class="c4">I actually won at the roulette table, so I <b>cashed out</b> and went home.<br>实际上我赌轮盘赢了，所以我把筹码兑换成现金，打道回府。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cast</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cast aˈround (BrE also ˌcast aˈbout) (for sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">四处寻觅；冥思苦想<br><span class="en">to look around you to try to find sth; to try very hard to think of sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>cast about</b> for an escape route.<br>他到处寻找逃跑路线。<br>He was desperately <b>casting around</b> for an excuse.<br>他绞尽脑汁找借口。<br>The company is having to <b>cast around</b> feverishly for ways to cut its costs.<br>公司迫切需要找到一些降低成本的途径。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcast sb/sth aˈside <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">抛弃；漠视<br><span class="en">to get rid of or give no attention to sb/sth that you no longer want or need</span></td><td class="c4">She just <b>cast him aside</b> when she got bored.<br>她觉得厌烦时就对他不理不睬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcast sth aˈside <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…丟在一边<br><span class="en">to throw sth to one side</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>cast aside</b> the newspaper impatiently.<br>他不耐烦地把报纸扔到一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcast sth aˈside <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">摒弃；消除负面的感觉；态度等<br><span class="en">to get rid of feelings, attitudes, etc.that are bad or negative, or that stop you achieving sth</span></td><td class="c4">He COSt <b>aside</b> all his inhibitions.<br>他抛开了一切禁忌。<br>The speakers <b>cast modesty aside</b> and talked about their success.<br>演讲者大言不惭地谈起他们的成就。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be,cast aˈway (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">船只失事后流落(至某处)<br><span class="en">to be left somewhere after your ship has been destroyed at sea</span></td><td class="c4">What would you do if you were cast <b>away</b> on a desert island?<br>如果失事后漂流到荒岛上，你会怎么办。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcast sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(眼睛)向下看<br><span class="en">if you cast your eyes down, you look down</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>cast her eyes down</b> modestly while Jack was talking about her.<br>杰克说到她的时候，她谦恭地垂下目光。</td></tr>
