<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be, cast ˈdown (by sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因…沮丧；不愉快<br><span class="en">to be sad or unhappy about sth</span></td><td class="c4">He is not easily <b>cast</b> <b>down</b>.<br>让他垂头丧气可不容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcast sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">脱下(衣服)扔到一边<br><span class="en">to take off a piece of clothing and throw it to one side</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>cast off</b> their clothes and jumped in the pool.<br>他们脱掉衣服，跳进游泳池。<br>It's time to <b>cast off</b> those winter blues and burst into spring!<br>该丢掉那些冬天的忧郁投入春天的怀抱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cast sb/sth ˈout ˌcast sb/sth ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">驱逐；逐出<br><span class="en">to drive sb away; to get rid of sb/sth, especially by using force</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>cast</b> <b>out</b> by society.<br>她被社会抛弃了。<br>He claimed to be able to <b>cast</b> <b>out</b> demons.<br>他自称能驱魔。<br>The villagers had been <b>cast</b> <b>out</b> of their homes.<br>村民被赶出了家园。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈoutcast n</b></td><td class="c3">被冷落的人；被排斥的<br><span class="en">a person who is not accepted by other people and who sometimes has to leave their home and friends</span></td><td class="c4">She felt like a social <b>outcast</b>.<br>她感觉像是被社会抛弃了。<br>He was treated like an <b>outcast</b> by the other children.<br>他受到其他孩子的排斥。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cast sb/sth ˈup (on sth) <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">海水把…冲上岸<br><span class="en">if the sea casts sb/sth up on the land, it carries them/it in and leaves them/it there</span></td><td class="c4">A whale bone was <b>cast up</b> on the beach.<br>块鲸骨被冲到海滩上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cast sb/sth ˈup (on sth) <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(眼睛)向上看<br><span class="en">if you cast your eyes up, you look up</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>cast her eyes up</b> to the ceiling and sighed.<br>她抬头望着天花板，叹了口气。町。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>catch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>catch sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">引诱…犯错误；发觉…干错事；发现…所知甚少<br><span class="en">to trick sb into making a mistake or doing sth wrong; to discover that sb does not know much or is doing sth wrong</span></td><td class="c4">The test isn't designed to <b>catch you out</b>. It's to see how much youve learnt.<br>这个测验目的不是要故意刁难你们，而是想了解你们学到了多少东西。<br>She reacted like a child <b>caught out</b> in a lie.<br>她的反应就像一个说谎被揪住的小孩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>catch sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使突陷；困境<br><span class="en">if a situation, bad weather, etc. catches sb out, it surprises them and puts them into a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">The snow <b>catches us out</b> every year (= we are not prepared for it).<br>大雪每年都让我们猝不及防。<br>Many investors were <b>caught out</b> by the collapse of the company.<br>众多投资者由于该公司倒闭而突然陷入困境。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcatch ˈup (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">了解发生；的事情<br><span class="en">to find out about things that have happened</span></td><td class="c4">Come and stay for a few days, so that we have a chance to <b>catch up</b>.<br>来住几天吧，这样我们就有机会聊一聊最近的事情。<br>I want to <b>catch up</b> with all your news.<br>我想知道你的全部近况。<br>We've got a lot of <b>catching up</b> to do after all this time.<br>这么长时间过后，我们有很多情况要去了解。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>catch sb ˈup (on sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">告诉某人发生的；事情<br><span class="en">to tell sb about catch sb/sth up bre → things that have happened</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>catch me up</b> on the news Later.<br>过会儿你再告诉我新消息吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>catch ˈup on sth</b></td><td class="c3">补做；赶做(未做的事)<br><span class="en">to spend extra time doing all the work, tasks, etc. that you should have done earlier</span></td><td class="c4">I spent the weekend <b>catching up on</b> lost sleep.<br>我利用周末补上了觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcatch ˈup with sb</b></td><td class="c3">终于查到(某人)；终于；把(某人)绳之以法<br><span class="en">if the police or people in authority catch up with sb, they finally find out that he/she has done sth wrong and punish him/her</span></td><td class="c4">They were involved in burglary for years before the police <b>caught up with</b> them.<br>警察最终抓住他们时，他们已入室盗窃好多年了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcatch ˈup with sb</b></td><td class="c3">产生曾经设法回避；的问题<br><span class="en">(also ˌcatch ˈup on sb less frequent) if sth you have done or sth that has been happening to you catches up with you, it starts to cause you problems that you have so far managed to avoid</span></td><td class="c4">His past is finally <b>catching up with</b> him.<br>他的过去终于让他吃到了苦头。<br>The late nights were beginning to <b>catch up with</b> her.<br>熬夜的习惯开始让她品尝恶果了。3。<br><b>Catch up with</b> you later!<br>回头找你聊聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cater</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcater for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">提供…所需；专为…而设<br><span class="en">to provide everything that sb, a group of people or a situation needs or wants</span></td><td class="c4">The careers service <b>caters for</b> the needs of young people and adults.<br>就业服务特别为青少年和成年人而设。<br>The resort also <b>caters for</b> winter sports.<br>这个度假胜地也适合进行冬季运动。<br>Their every need was <b>catered</b> to.<br>对待他们是有求必应。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cave</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcave ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">房顶；墙壁等塌落；塌陷；坍塌<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) if a roof, wall, etc. caves in, it falls down and towards the centre</span></td><td class="c4">The roof of the tunnel <b>caved in</b> on the workmen.<br>隧道顶部塌方，压住了作业人员。<br>Under his fierce questioning she <b>caved in</b> and told him the truth.<br>在他严厉质问下，她招架不住，告诉了他真相。四时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcave-in n</b></td><td class="c3">房顶；墻壁等塌落；塌陷；坍塌<br><span class="en">the fact of a roof, wall, etc. caving in</span></td><td class="c4">For the people inside the tunnel there was a serious risk of flooding or a <b>cave-in</b>.<br>隧道里的人面临透水或塌方的巨大危险。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>centre</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sb/sth also ˈcentre upon sb/sth<br>ˈcentre sth upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">注意力或思想集中；倾注于；把(注意力或思想)集中于<br><span class="en">to give a lot of attention or thought to one particular activity, idea or person, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The discussions <b>centred</b> on the hostage issue.<br>讨论围绕人质问题展开。<br>The group has <b>centred</b> its attention on the need for reform.<br>该小组将其注意力集中在改革的必要性上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chalk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>chalk ˈup sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">获得；赢得成功；胜利；比赛等；写下；记录成就；分数等<br><span class="en">to achieve a success, a victory, a score in a game, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The team has <b>chalked up</b> its fifth win in a row.<br>该队已连赢五场比赛。<br>This week Dee Brothers <b>chalked up</b> 100 years of business in this town.<br>本周迪伊兄弟公司在本城开业已经100。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchalk sth ˈup to sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…归因于<br><span class="en">to think that sth happens as a result of sth else</span></td><td class="c4">We can <b>chalk our recent victores up to</b> a lot of luck.<br>我们可以把近期的胜利归功于运气好。<br>When the goal was disallowed they <b>chalked it up to</b> a bad referee decision.<br>进球被判无效，他们认为这纯属裁判错判。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chance</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈchance on/upon sb/sth (formal)</b></td><td class="c3">不期而遇；偶然发现<br><span class="en">to meet chance on/upon sb/sth (formal) to meet sb or find sth when you do not expect to</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>chanced upon</b> a volume of Japanese poetry in a bookshop.<br>他在书店不经意间发现了一部日语诗集。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>change</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange sth ˈback (into/to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把(钱)换成(原货币)<br><span class="en">to exchange an amount of money into the system of money (currency) that it was in before</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>change these dollars back</b> into sterling?<br>我可以把这些美元兑换回英镑吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange ˈdown (into/to sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开车减速换低一挡；挂低速挡<br><span class="en">to control the speed of a vehicle by changing to a lower gear</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Change down</b> into second as you approach the corner.<br>靠近拐角时，减至二挡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>change ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">换(衣服)<br><span class="en">to put on different clothes</span></td><td class="c4">We quickly <b>changed into</b> our swimsuits.<br>我们迅速换上了游泳衣。<br>I didn't bring anything to <b>change into</b>.<br>我没带替换的衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange ˈinto sth<br>ˌchange sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使变成；变为<br><span class="en">to change, or to make sb/sth change, into sth different</span></td><td class="c4">The castle has <b>changed into</b> a hotel.<br>城堡改成了旅馆。<br>The handsome prince was <b>changed into</b> a frog.<br>英俊的王子被变成了青蛙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>change ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">更换；换掉(衣服)；更衣<br><span class="en">to take off the clothes you are wearing and put on different ones</span></td><td class="c4">I must <b>change out of</b> these wet clothes before I get a chill.<br>我得换掉这身湿衣服，免得着。<br>She <b>changed out of</b> her suit as soon as she came home.<br>她一回到家就换下了套装。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">改用；换用<br><span class="en">(from sth) (to sth) to stop using one system or thing and start using another</span></td><td class="c4">The magazine <b>changed over</b> from pink paper to white in 1917.<br>该杂志1917年把粉色纸张改换成了白色。<br>We're <b>changing over</b> to a new computer system.<br>我们正要改用新的计算机系统。<br>Can we <b>change over</b>?<br>我们换个合吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈchangeover n</b></td><td class="c3">体制等的改变；转变；变更<br><span class="en">a change from one system or thing to another</span></td><td class="c4">The <b>changeover to the new</b> system will take place gradually.<br>向新制度的过渡将循序渐进。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange ˈover/round <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对调；交换；调换位置或；工作<br><span class="en">if two people change over/round, they move to where the other person was before or do what the other person was doing</span></td><td class="c4">Can you and Phil <b>change round</b>? You're too tall to stand in the front row.<br>你和菲尔互换一下位置好吗？你个子太高，不宜站在前排。<br>When you get tired of driving we can <b>change over</b>.<br>要是你开车累了，我们可以轮着开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchange ˈup (into/to sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开车换高一挡；换挂高速挡<br><span class="en">to control the speed of a vehicle by changing to a higher gear</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Change up</b> into fourth gear now.<br>现在加速到第四挡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>charge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcharge sb with sth<br>ˈcharge sb with doing sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使承担职责；责任或任务<br><span class="en">to give sb a duty, responsibility or task</span></td><td class="c4">A solicitor was <b>charged with</b> administering the estate.<br>一名律师受委托管理这份财产。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>charm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>charm sth ˈout of sb</b></td><td class="c3">利用魅力从…处获取<br><span class="en">if you charm money or information out of sb, you obtain it by using your power to please or attract people</span></td><td class="c4">She managed to <b>charm</b> £20 <b>out</b> of him.<br>她施展魅力从他那里弄到了20 英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chase</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchase ˈafter sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">追求；向…求爱<br><span class="en">to try to persuade sb to have a romantic or sexual relationship with you</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>chasing after</b> younger women.<br>他总是在追逐年轻的女性。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chase ˈafter sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">追逐；追赶<br><span class="en">to run, drive, etc. to try to catch sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>chased after</b> the thief but he got away.<br>他们追赶那个小偷，但他还是逃掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chase sb/sth aˈway/off/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">赶走；驱逐<br><span class="en">to force sb/sth to run away by running after them or threatening them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>chased the attackers away</b> by firing shots into the air.<br>他朝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchase sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">催促；催办；敦促<br><span class="en">to contact sb and remind them to do sth they have said they would do or that they ought to do</span></td><td class="c4">It is his job to <b>chase up</b> clients with outstanding debts.<br>他的工作是向客户追债。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchat sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向…搭讪；与…调情<br><span class="en">to talk in a friendly way to sb because you are sexually attracted to them</span></td><td class="c4">Who was that girl you were <b>chatting up</b> last night?<br>昨晚你搭讪的那个女孩是谁？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cheat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcheat sb of sth (also,cheat sb ˈout of sth)</b></td><td class="c3">骗出<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from having sth, especially in an unfair or dishonest way</span></td><td class="c4">He had <b>cheated the taxman of</b> £60 000.<br>他骗税务员少收了6万英镑。<br>He was <b>cheated out of</b> his rightful inheritance.<br>有人骗走了他本应获取的遗产。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcheat on sb</b></td><td class="c3">对(伴侣)不忠；背着(配偶)偷情<br><span class="en">to secretly have sex with sb who is not your regular partner</span></td><td class="c4">He was the last to know that she had been <b>cheating on</b> him.<br>她早已红杏出墙，而他却是最后一个才知道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>check</b></td><td class="c2"><b>check ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在旅馆；机场等登记；报到<br><span class="en">(at sth) to go to an official desk at olay around (informal) to have a sexual a hotel, an airport, etc. and tell sb that you have arrived</span></td><td class="c4">After <b>checking in</b>, we went out for a meal.<br>登记之后，我们就出去吃饭了。<br><b>Check in</b> at desk 25 an hour before take-off.<br>请在飞机起《前一小时到 25 号台办理登机手续。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>check sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在旅馆；机场等为…登记；给…办理入住(或登机)手续<br><span class="en">to take sb's name when they arrive at a hotel or an airport, look at their ticket, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Write all the names of the guests in this book as they are <b>checked in</b>.<br>为客人办理入住手续时，把他们的名字都记在这个本子上。<br>All the passengers have been <b>checked in</b>.<br>已为所有乘客办妥登机手续。<br>She's <b>checked into</b> a private clinic for drug rehabilitation.<br>她住进了一家私人诊所戒毒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcheck sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">经查对无误在清单项目旁做记号；打钩<br><span class="en">to put a mark beside items on a list to show that they are correct, present or have been dealt with</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>checked</b> everyone's name <b>off</b> as they arrived.<br>他在每位来宾姓名旁都打了个钩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcheck on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">检查；核实；确认(是否正常等)<br><span class="en">to make sure that sb is safe, happy, etc.or that sth is progressing as it should be</span></td><td class="c4">Do you always <b>check on</b> future employees?<br>你总是调查将要雇用的人员吗。<br>Will you <b>check on</b> his address?<br>你核实一下他的住址好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>check ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">事实等查对；无误；言之成理<br><span class="en">if facts, etc. check out, they can be shown to be correct or true</span></td><td class="c4">His story doesn't <b>check out</b>.<br>他的说法站不住脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>check ˈout<br>ˌcheck ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">结账离开；办清手续后离开旅馆；医院等<br><span class="en">to leave a hotel, a hospital, etc. where you have been</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>checked out</b> this morning.<br>她今天上午退房了。<br>He decided to <b>check out</b> of the hospital and go home.<br>他决定出院回象。<br>He can't just <b>check out</b> on us like that!<br>他不能就这样离开我们。<br>Let's <b>check out</b> of here.<br>咱们离开这儿吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>check ˈout<br>ˌcheck sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在商店结账；为…结账<br><span class="en">if you check out in a shop/store, or sb checks you out, you find out how much you have to pay and give sb the money</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>check out</b> at aisle eight.<br>您可以在第八通道付款。<br>The girl who <b>checked me out</b> looked at me strangely.<br>给我结账的姑娘奇怪地打量了我一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcheckout n</b></td><td class="c3">超市的收银台；付款处</td><td class="c4">There were huge queues at the <b>checkout</b>.<br>付款处排起了长队。0a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>check sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">为(人或动物)做体检<br><span class="en">to examine a person or an animal to make sure that they are healthy; to examine a machine, etc. to make sure it is working correctly</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>Checked over</b> the house, looking for damp or rot.<br>我们仔细检查了房屋，查看是否有受潮或破朽之处。<br>The doctor <b>checked him over</b> and said he was fit and healthy.<br>医生內他做了检查后，说他十分健康。<br>You should get someone to <b>check the letter over</b> for you.<br>你应该找人帮你把信件校对一下。<br>The Health and Safety Officer went <b>over</b> the whole school, <b>checking</b> every fire door.<br>卫生与安全官员仔细巡查了整个学校，查看了每扇防火门。<br>The sergeant looked him <b>over</b> and told him to polish his shoes.<br>中士仔细打量了他一番，告诉他把鞋子擦擦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cheer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcheer sb ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">比赛；中为…呐喊助威；为…欢呼打气<br><span class="en">to encourage sb, especially sb in a race or competition, by shouting</span></td><td class="c4">The crowd <b>cheered the runners on</b>.<br>观众为赛跑运动员加油鼓劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>cheer ˈup<br>ˌcheer sb/yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使振作精神；振奋起来<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb/yourself, happier .or more cheerful</span></td><td class="c4">She seems to have <b>Cheered up</b> since Saturday.<br>星期六以来，她似乎情绪好了一些。<br>Nothing could <b>cheer him up</b>.<br>没什么事情能让他高兴起来。<br>She bought some chocolates to <b>cheer herself up</b>.<br>她买了些巧克力来鼓励一下自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcheer sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使(房间等)明亮；使宜人<br><span class="en">to make a room, etc. brighter and more cheerful</span></td><td class="c4">Flowers always <b>cheer up</b> a room.<br>房间一有花就明快不少。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cheese</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cheese sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使烦恼；使厌烦<br><span class="en">to make sb annoyed or bored</span></td><td class="c4">Mike's car got vandalized, which <b>cheesed him off</b> no end.<br>迈克的车遭人故意毁坏，这让他沮丧透顶。<br>We were feeling a bit <b>cheesed off</b> and didn't know what to do with ourselves.<br>我们感到有点苦恼，不知如何是好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chew</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchew sth ˈover (also ˈchew on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">仔细考虑；详细讨论<br><span class="en">to think about or discuss sth carefully and in detail</span></td><td class="c4">He spent the weekend <b>chewing over</b> the problem.<br>他利用周末细致斟酌了这个问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchew sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使不自信；使不愉快；使不成功；终结…的职业生涯<br><span class="en">to make sb less confident, happy or successful; to end sb's career</span></td><td class="c4">The company has <b>chewed up</b> numerous chief executives over the years.<br>这些年来，该公司断送了众多首席执行官的前程。<br>The media just <b>chews celebrities up</b> and spits them out.<br>媒体对名人总是横加贬责。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchew sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">细嚼；嚼碎<br><span class="en">to bite sth until it is completely soft or destroyed</span></td><td class="c4">The baby <b>chewed the cookie up</b> and swallowed it.<br>小孩把饼干嚼碎，咽了下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchew sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">机器使损坏；毁坏<br><span class="en">if a machine chews sth up, it damages or destroys it</span></td><td class="c4">The cassette player' <b>chewed the tape up</b> again.<br>放音机又卡带了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>chill ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">放松；冷静；镇静<br><span class="en">to relax completely and not get upset or excited about anything</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Chill out</b>! We'll get there on time!<br>别担心！我们会按时赶到的！独使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chime</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchime ˈin (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">插话；(以…)打断；谈话<br><span class="en">to join in a conversation suddenly or interrupt sb</span></td><td class="c4">He kept <b>chiming in</b> with his own opinions.<br>他不断插话，发表自己的见解。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chime ˈin with sth<br>ˈchime with sth</b></td><td class="c3">与…一致；与…相似<br><span class="en">to agree with sth; to be similar to sth</span></td><td class="c4">His policies <b>chimed in with</b> the national mood at the time.<br>他的政策与当时的国民心态相吻合。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchip aˈway at sth</b></td><td class="c3">不断地削或凿；不断削弱<br><span class="en">to make sth smaller or weaker by continuously breaking small pieces off it</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>chipping away at</b> the rocks, looking for fossils.<br>他在不停凿岩石寻找化石。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chip ˈin (with sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">凑份子；凑钱<br><span class="en">(also ˌchip ˈin sth) to give some money so that a group of people can buy sth together</span></td><td class="c4">Has everyone <b>chipped in</b> for the present?<br>购买礼物的份子钱，大家都交了吗。<br>The company has <b>chipped in</b> with a $200 donation.<br>公司凑了200元捐款。<br>Let's all <b>chip in</b> five dollars.<br>咱们每人都凑五元钱吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchip ˈoff<br>chip ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…剥落<br><span class="en">if paint or a surface chips off, it comes off in small pieces</span></td><td class="c4">The varnish is <b>chipping</b> <b>off</b>.<br>清漆开始剥落了。<br>Most of the paint had <b>chipped</b> <b>off</b> the gate.<br>门上的油漆大部分都掉光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>choke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchoke sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">克制；抑制(强烈的感情或逆耳的言语)<br><span class="en">to try to stop yourself from showing a strong emotion, or saying sth that might upset sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>choked back</b> his tears.<br>他强忍住眼泪。<br>A protest rose to her lips, but she <b>choked it back</b>.<br>抗议的话到了嘴边，却又被她咽了回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>choke sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">奶碍；阻止<br><span class="en">to prevent or stop sth</span></td><td class="c4">High interest rates have <b>choked off</b> investment.<br>高利率阻碍了投资。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchoke ˈup<br>.choke sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使哽咽；说不出话来<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb, so upset that you/they are unable to speak</span></td><td class="c4">That song really <b>chokes me up</b>.<br>那首歌简直让我泣不成声。<br>He gets <b>choked up</b> just remembering the day she left.<br>一想起她离开的那天，他就哽咽着说不出话来。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈchop at sth<br>ˌchop aˈway at sth</b></td><td class="c3">瞄准…砍；对准…劈去<br><span class="en">to aim blows at sth with a sharp heavy tool</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>chopped at</b> the undergrowth with their machetes.<br>他们抡着大刀砍灌木必。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chop sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">砍倒；砍下(树木等)<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a tree fall down by cutting it at the base with a sharp tool</span></td><td class="c4">They're <b>chopping down</b> thousands of trees every year.<br>他们每年砍伐几干棵树。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chop sth ˈoff<br>ˌchop sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…上砍掉；斩下<br><span class="en">to remove sth by cutting it with a sharp heavy tool</span></td><td class="c4">The king had his head <b>chopped off</b>.<br>国王下令砍了他的头。<br>She <b>chopped a branch off</b> the tree.<br>她从树上砍下一根树枝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">切细；剁碎<br><span class="en">to cut sth into small pieces with a knife or a sharp tool</span></td><td class="c4">Shall we <b>chop these logs up</b> for firewood?<br>我们要把这些木头劈成柴吗？1。<br><b>Chop up</b> the onion into small pieces.<br>把洋葱切碎。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchow ˈdown (on sth) <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大吃<br><span class="en">to eat a lot of food</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>chowed down</b> on fried chicken and salad.<br>我们大吃炸鸡和色拉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>chuck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchuck sth</b></td><td class="c3">不充分利用；浪费<br><span class="en">a way bre, informal to not make good use of sth; to waste sth</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>chucking</b> all her money away on presents for him.<br>她把钱都乱花在给他买礼物上了。<br>It's too good an opportunity to <b>chuck</b> away.<br>这是个大好机会，不能错过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchuck sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">丢弃；抛弃<br><span class="en">to throw sth away because you no longer want or need it</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>chucked</b> the old sofa away.<br>我们扔掉了旧沙发。<br>Don't <b>chuck</b> yesterday's paper <b>out</b>. I still haven't done the crossword.<br>昨天的报纸可别扔了。我还没有做填字游戏呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈchuck it down (also ˈchuck down, ˈchuck down sth less frequent) <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">下暴雨<br><span class="en">to rain very heavily</span></td><td class="c4">It was <b>chucking it down</b> outside.<br>外面大雨倾盆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchuck sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">附送<br><span class="en">to include sth extra with what you are selling or offering without increasing the price</span></td><td class="c4">If you buy the freezer and the fridge well <b>chuck in</b> a toaster.<br>购买冰柜和冰箱附送一台烤面包机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chuck sth ˈin/ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">放弃；中断工作；课程等<br><span class="en">to decide to stop doing sth such as a job or a course of study</span></td><td class="c4">What made you decide to <b>chuck in</b> your course?<br>你为什么决定中断这门课程？01。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchuck sb ˈout<br>ˌchuck sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">强迫…离开处所；工作等；撵走；辞退<br><span class="en">to force sb to leave a place, a job, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Her parents <b>chucked her out</b> when she got pregnant.<br>她怀孕后，父母把她赶出了家门。<br>She failed her exams and was <b>chucked out</b> of college.<br>她几门考试不及格，被大学开除了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchuck sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">否决；拒绝接受计划；提议等<br><span class="en">to reject a plan, a Proposal, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The committee <b>chucked my proposal out</b>.<br>委员会杏决了我的提议。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>chuck ˈup<br>ˌchuck sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">呕吐；吐出<br><span class="en">to bring food you have eaten back out of your mouth</span></td><td class="c4">The smell made me want to <b>chuck up</b>.<br>这气味令我作呕。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>churn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>churn sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">批量生产；大量炮制<br><span class="en">to produce sth quickly in large amounts</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>churns out</b> trashy romantic novels.<br>她大量炮制毫无价值的言情小说。<br>They <b>churn out</b> 3 000 identical toy trains every day.<br>他们每天生产3000辆同样的玩具火车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>churn sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使不安；使担忧；使害怕；使生气<br><span class="en">to make sb feel very WPset, worried, frightened or angry</span></td><td class="c4">When I drove away from the house for the last time, I was <b>churned up</b> inside.<br>我最后一次驾车离开那所房子时，心中十分郁闷。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌchurn sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">掀起；搅动(泥或水)；使翻腾<br><span class="en">to move sth such as mud or water around and damage or disturb the surface</span></td><td class="c4">Cars and motorbikes had <b>churned up</b> the field.<br>汽车和摩托车在地上留下一道道车辙。海。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>claim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>claim sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">要回；索回<br><span class="en">to ask for sth to be returned to you</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Claim your expenses back</b> from the company.<br>费用请向公司报销。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clam</b></td><td class="c2"><b>clam ˈup (on sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不敢作声；绝口不谈；拒不开口；守口如瓶<br><span class="en">to refuse to speak about sth because you are afraid, or want to keep it secret</span></td><td class="c4">He always <b>clams up</b> when we ask about his family.<br>我们问起他的家庭，他总是沉默不语。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clamp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclamp ˈdown<br>ˌcamp ˈdown on sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">严厉弹压；镇压犯罪活动；抗议示威等<br><span class="en">to become strict about sth in order to prevent sth happening, especially a crime, a protest, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The government intends to <b>clamp down</b> on drug smuggling.<br>政府拟严厉打击贩毒活动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>clamp sth ˈon<br>ˈclamp sth on sb/sth <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">强令(…)接受；强制执行<br><span class="en">to force sb to accept sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">The army <b>clamped on</b> a curfew after the riots.<br>骚乱过后军队实行了宵禁。<br>The army <b>clamped a curfew on</b> the refugee camps.<br>军队对难民营实施宵禁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>claw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈclaw at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">用爪子或指甲抓<br><span class="en">to ury to catch sb/sth or scratch or tear sb/sth with claws or with your nails</span></td><td class="c4">The cat <b>clawing at</b> the door.<br>猫在挠门。<br>She tried to <b>claw at</b> his face.<br>她试图抓他的脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>claw sth ˈback <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">设法捞回；努力挽回<br><span class="en">to work hard to get sth back that you have lost</span></td><td class="c4">They're trying to <b>claw back</b> their share of the market.<br>他们正在想方设法夺回市场份额。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>claw sth ˈback <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常指通过税收收回已支付；给民众的钱款<br><span class="en">if a goverment claws back money it has paid to people, it gets it back, usually by taxing them</span></td><td class="c4">The government are <b>clawing back</b> age allowances in tax.<br>政府正在通过税收收回老年补助金。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clean</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclean sth ˈoff<br>ˌclean sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…上把…刷掉；把…抹去；把(污垢)除掉<br><span class="en">to remove sth from the surface of sth by brushing,rubbing, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She couldn't be bothered to <b>clean</b> her make-up of.<br>她懶得卸妆。<br>How can I <b>clean red wine off</b> the carpet?<br>怎样清除地毯上的红酒污渍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>clean sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌclean sb/sth ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">花掉(钱财)；买光(存货)<br><span class="en">to use up or take all sb’s money; to take or buy the whole supply of sth that sb has</span></td><td class="c4">Buying drinks for everyone <b>cleaned me out</b>.<br>为大家购买饮料把我的钱花得一干二净。<br>It's been a great year for sales. We're completely <b>cleaned out</b> (= we've sold all our supply).<br>今年销售情况很好。我们的库存全部卖光了。<br>The stall was <b>cleaned out</b> of newspapers by 8.00 a.m.<br>上午八点报摊的报纸就卖光了。<br>Burglars had <b>cleaned the place out</b> (= had stolen everything).<br>窃贼把那里偷光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclean sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">彻底清洁…的内部<br><span class="en">to clean the inside of sth thoroughly</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>clean the stables out</b> every day.<br>我们每天彻底清扫马厩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclean sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">消除(犯罪或不道德行为)；清理；整顿<br><span class="en">to remove criminals, crime or immoral behaviour from a place or an organization</span></td><td class="c4">The mayor is determined to <b>clean up</b> the city and make it a safer place to live.<br>市长决心整治好这座城市，使人们安居乐业。<br>The company is trying to <b>clean up</b> its image.<br>公司正努力改善形象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>clear aˈway<br>ˌclear sth aˈway <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…清除掉(以留出空间)<br><span class="en">to remove things that you have been using and no longer need in order to leave a clear space</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>clear your books away</b>?<br>把你的书收起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>clear sb aˈway <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">赶走；撵走<br><span class="en">to make sb leave a place</span></td><td class="c4">The police <b>cleared the demonstrators away</b>.<br>警察驱散了示威者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>clear ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">离开；溜掉；逃走<br><span class="en">to go or run away</span></td><td class="c4">Youve no right to be here. <b>Clear off</b>!<br>你无权呆在这里。走开。<br>He <b>cleared off</b> as soon as he heard the police car.<br>听到警车声他便马上溜走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>clear ˈout<br>ˌclear ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">迅速离开<br><span class="en">to leave a place quickly</span></td><td class="c4">I told him to <b>clear out</b> of the house by Monday.<br>我叫他星期一前搬出这所房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>clear ˈup<br>ˌclear sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">打扫；清理<br><span class="en">to make sth clean and neat</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Clear up</b> the mess in here before you go.<br>把这里乱糟糟的东西拾掇整齐再走。<br>The antibiotics should <b>clear up</b> the infection.<br>抗生素应该能治好这种感染。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>climb</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclimb ˈdown (over sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">承认错误；作出让步<br><span class="en">to admit that you are wrong or have made a mistake; to change your position in an argument</span></td><td class="c4">The president was forced to <b>climb down</b> and issue an apology.<br>总统被迫妥协并致歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cling</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcling to sth<br>.cling ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">不愿放弃；坚持<br><span class="en">to be unwilling to stop doing, believing or thinking about sth; to be unwilling to get rid of sth</span></td><td class="c4">I still <b>cling to</b> the hope that he's alive.<br>我始终抱着希望，他仍然活着。<br>She's <b>clinging on to</b> the past.<br>她对过去依然难以释怀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>clock ˈin/ˈon<br>ˌclock sb ˈin/on <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">时间；上班打卡<br><span class="en">to record the time that you arrive at work, especially by putting a card into a machine; to do this for sb or check the time they arrive at work</span></td><td class="c4">We arrived and <b>clocked on</b> for the night shift.<br>我们到了单位，就打卡上夜班。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclock ˈin at sth</b></td><td class="c3">持续；花费(时间)；花掉；耗费(金钱)<br><span class="en">to last or take a particular amount of time; to cost a particular amount of money</span></td><td class="c4">The fastest runner <b>clocked in at</b> 3 minutes 40 seconds.<br>最快的赛跑选手用了3分40秒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclock sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">达到某一数字；或数量<br><span class="en">to win or achieve a particular number or amount</span></td><td class="c4">We've <b>clocked up</b> 500 miles (= we've travelled 500 miles) today.<br>我们今天的行程达到500英里。<br>The company has <b>clocked up</b> record exports this year.<br>公司今年出口创了纪录。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclog ˈup (with sth)<br>ˌclog sth ˈup (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用…塞满；把…阻塞<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sth, blocked so that nothing can move</span></td><td class="c4">The pipe had <b>clogged</b> up (with mud).<br>管道被(泥)堵住了。<br>The roads were <b>Clogged</b> up with traffic.<br>道路交通堵塞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>close</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">逼近；包围<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) to come nearer to and surround sb/sth in a frightening way or in order to attack them</span></td><td class="c4">The enemy is <b>closing in</b>.<br>敌人渐渐通近了。<br>The fog was <b>closing in</b> on us.<br>我们逐渐被大雾笼罩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">白昼逐渐变短；渐短<br><span class="en">when the days close in, they gradually become shorter</span></td><td class="c4">The days/nights are <b>closing in</b> now that autumn/fall is here.<br>秋天来临，白天越来越短天黑得越来越早。<br>The evenings are <b>closing in</b> fast.<br>天黑得越来越早。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose sth ˈoff (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">隔离；封堵<br><span class="en">to put sth across the entrance to a road, a room, etc. so that people cannot go in</span></td><td class="c4">Police have <b>closed the area off</b> to traffic.<br>警方封锁了这一地区的交通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈclose on sb/sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">赛跑等中缩短同…的距离；逼近<br><span class="en">to make the distance between you and sb/sth else smaller, for example in a race</span></td><td class="c4">I was slowly <b>closing on</b> the runner ahead of me.<br>我慢慢追上了跑在我前面的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈclose on/over sth</b></td><td class="c3">遮盖；握紧；箍紧<br><span class="en">to surround sth, covering it or holding it tightly</span></td><td class="c4">His fingers <b>closed over</b> the money.<br>他的手紧紧地攥着那些钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">商店停业甩卖；歇业抛售<br><span class="en">if a shop/store closes out, it sells everything very cheaply before it stops operating as a business</span></td><td class="c4">The store is <b>closing out</b> on Monday with discounts of up to 75%.<br>这家商店星期一要停业，商品折价甩卖，最大折扣达到 75%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">遮蔽；屏蔽光线；声音<br><span class="en">to prevent light, sound, etc. from entering a place</span></td><td class="c4">We need a curtain up there to <b>close out</b> the light.<br>我们得在那儿挂幅帘子遮挡光线。0日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclose ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">关闭；闭合<br><span class="en">to close completely</span></td><td class="c4">His eye had swollen and <b>closed up</b>.<br>他的眼睛肿得睁不开了。<br>The cut took a long time to <b>close up</b> (= to heal).<br>伤口过了很长时间才愈合。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>close ˈup<br>ˌclose sth ˌup</b></td><td class="c3">暂时关门；锁门<br><span class="en">to shut and lock a building completely for a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>closes the shop up</b> at 5.30.<br>他5点 30 分关店门。<br>They <b>closed the house up</b> and rented an apartment in the city.<br>他们把那所房子锁上，在城里租了套公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>club</b></td><td class="c2"><b>club toˈgether (to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">凑份子；凑钱<br><span class="en">if people club together, they each give an amount of money so that the total can be used for a particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>clubbed together</b> to buy their teacher a present.<br>他们凑钱给老师头了个礼物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>clue</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌclue sb ˈin (on/about sth) <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">就某事为(某人)提供消息<br><span class="en">to give sb information about sth</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>clue me in</b> on the facts of the case?<br>你能告诉我这件案子的实情吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cluster</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcluster aˈround sb/sth (BrE also ˌcluster aˈbout/ˈround sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">聚集在…周围；围聚着<br><span class="en">to form a group around sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">People <b>clustered around</b> the market stalls.<br>人们围拢在市场货摊周围。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>coax</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcoax sb ˈinto sth<br>ˈcoax sb into doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">哄劝某人做某事<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to do sth by talking to them gently</span></td><td class="c4">Can we <b>coax you into</b> singing for us?<br>我们能请您为我们唱歌吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>coax sb ˈout of sth<br>ˌcoax sb ˈout of doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">哄劝某人不做某事<br><span class="en">to persuade sb not to do sth by talking to them gently</span></td><td class="c4">Try to <b>coax him out of</b> resigning.<br>尽量好言好语地说服他不要辞职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cock ˈup<br>.cock sth ˈup <span class="tag">(slang, BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…搞糟；把…弄得一塌糊涂<br><span class="en">to spoil or ruin sth by doing it badly or by making a mistake</span></td><td class="c4">You've really <b>cocked up</b> this time.<br>你这次确实弄得糟糕透顶。<br>The travel agency completely <b>cocked up</b> the arrangements.<br>旅行社把行程安排搞得乱七八糟。<br>Don't <b>cock things up</b> again!<br>别把事情再搞砸了！ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>coil</b></td><td class="c2"><b>coil ˈup<br>ˌcoil sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">将…卷起；盘起<br><span class="en">to wind into coils; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">The snake <b>coiled up</b> in the sunshine.<br>蛇在阳光下盘了起来。<br>He <b>coiled the rope up</b> neatly.<br>他把绳子整齐地卷起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>colour</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcolour sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">用笔给…着色；为…上色<br><span class="en">to fill a shape, an area, etc. with colour, using pencils or pens</span></td><td class="c4">Why don't you <b>colour the pictures in</b>?<br>你为什么不给这些画涂色呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>comb</b></td><td class="c2"><b>comb sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">梳理(头发)<br><span class="en">to use a comb to remove knots from your hair or to make it neat</span></td><td class="c4">My hair's so long that it takes me ages to <b>comb it out</b>.<br>我的头发太长，梳好要花很长时间。四町。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>come</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome aˈbout</b></td><td class="c3">发生<br><span class="en">to happen</span></td><td class="c4">It's hard to understand how the accident <b>came about</b>.<br>很难理解事故是怎么发生的。<br>Can you tell us how it <b>came about</b> that you decided to strike?<br>你能告诉我你们为什么决定罢工吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come aˈcross<br>ˈcome across sth</b></td><td class="c3">走过房间；道路；河流；等而来到；过来<br><span class="en">to cross a room, a road, a river, etc. towards the place where the speaker is</span></td><td class="c4">When youve done your homework, <b>come across</b> to my house and well listen to some music.<br>你完成作业后就来我家，我们听听音乐。<br>She waved and <b>came across</b> the room to talk to me.<br>她向我招招手，然后从房间那头走过来和我说话。<br>She <b>came across</b> a pile of old photographs while she was clearing the attic.<br>她清理阁楼时偶然发现了一沓旧照片。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">到达；出现<br><span class="en">to arrive or appear somewhere; to start to exist, happen or be available</span></td><td class="c4">When the right opportunity <b>comes along</b>, he'll take it.<br>只要有合适的机会，他会抓住的。<br>There are new designs <b>coming along</b>.<br>新款即将面世。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌcome ˈwith informal</b></td><td class="c3">跟随；同去<br><span class="en">to go somewhere with sb</span></td><td class="c4">We're going to the pub.Do you want to <b>come</b> along?<br>我们要去酒吧。想起去吗。<br>You'd better <b>come</b> along with me to the police station.<br>你最好跟我去趟警察局。3一。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come aˈlong<br>.come aˈlong sth</b></td><td class="c3">沿…过来<br><span class="en">to move forward or from one end of sth to the other, towards the speaker</span></td><td class="c4">The lorry was <b>coming along</b> the road at great speed.<br>货车一路飞驰而来。o町。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome aˈround sth (BrE also ˌcome ˈround sth)</b></td><td class="c3">绕过(拐角)；走弯道<br><span class="en">to move or travel around a corner</span></td><td class="c4">The bus <b>came</b> <b>round</b> the bend too fast.<br>公共汽车在弯道处开得太快。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome at sb</b></td><td class="c3">逼近；迫近(以袭击某人)<br><span class="en">to move towards sb as if you are going to attack them</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>came at</b> me with a knife.<br>她拿看刀丁向我扑来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome at sth</b></td><td class="c3">处理；应付问题；困难等<br><span class="en">to approach, think about.or try to deal with a question, problem, etc. in a particular way</span></td><td class="c4">We're getting nowhere. Let's try <b>coming at</b> the problem from a different angle.<br>我们这样会毫无进展，还是换个角度考虑这个难题吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come aˈway<br>.come aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">离开；离去<br><span class="en">to leave a place or a person</span></td><td class="c4">Jane <b>came away</b> from the meeting feeling angry and upset.<br>简又气又急地离开了会场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come aˈway<br>.come aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">脱离；脱落<br><span class="en">to become separated from sth</span></td><td class="c4">He pulled at the door handle until it <b>came away</b> in his hands.<br>他一直拽着门把手，最后把它拽了下来。<br>The plaster had started to. <b>come away</b> from the wall.<br>灰泥已开始从墙上脱落。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome aˈway with sth</b></td><td class="c3">带着某种感觉；印象或结果离开<br><span class="en">to leave a place with a particular feeling, impression or result</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>came away from the championship with</b> three medals.<br>她在锦标赛上获得了三枚奖牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>come ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">回来；返回<br><span class="en">to return to the place where the speaker is</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Come back</b> here at once!<br>马上回到这儿。<br>Did she say when she was <b>coming back</b>?<br>她说过何时回来吗。<br>Why don't you <b>come back</b> to my place for a coffee?<br>为什么不来我这里喝杯咖啡呢。<br>They <b>came back</b> from the trip relaxed and happy.<br>他们旅行归来，轻松愉快。<br>Well <b>come back</b> for the car tomorrow.<br>我们明天回来取汽车。<br>Her confidence <b>is</b> starting to come back slowly.<br>她正慢慢恢复自信。<br>Do you think trams will <b>come back</b>?<br>你看有轨电车会重获新生吗？5。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>come ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">突然回忆起；回想起<br><span class="en">(to sb) to return to your memory, often suddenly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Its</b> all coming back to me now.<br>现在我全都回想起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>come ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">回击；驳斥<br><span class="en">(at sb) (with sth) to reply to sb quickly, strongly or angrily</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>came back</b> at the speaker with some questions.<br>她用提问来反驳发言人。<br>He <b>came back</b> straight away, telling me what he thought of me.<br>他立刻还击，说出了他对我的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈby<br>ˌcome ˈby sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…旁经过；走过<br><span class="en">to pass sb/sth without stopping</span></td><td class="c4">Some kids on bikes <b>came by</b>, but they didn't notice me.<br>一些孩子骑着自行车从旁边过去了，可他们没注意到我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈby<br>ˌcome ˈby sth</b></td><td class="c3">短暂看望；来串门<br><span class="en">to come to visit sb for a short time in a relaxed or informal way</span></td><td class="c4">Thanks for <b>coming by</b> yesterday.<br>谢谢你昨天来看我。<br><b>Come by</b> on your way home from work.<br>你下班回家的路上过来坐坐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome by sth</b></td><td class="c3">设法得到；偶然得到<br><span class="en">to manage to get sth; to receive sth by chance</span></td><td class="c4">Jobs are hard to <b>come by</b> these days.<br>如今找工作很难。<br>Information about the company was not easy to <b>come by</b>.<br>这家公司的相关资料不容易弄到手。<br>How did you <b>come by</b> that cut on your hand?<br>你手上的伤口是怎么弄的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>come ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">雪等<br><span class="en">of rain, snow, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The rain was <b>coming down</b> harder now.<br>雨下大了。<br>The committee <b>came down</b> against the proposal.<br>委员会表态反对这项提议。<br>Voters <b>came down</b> firmly in favour of reform.<br>选民表示坚决支持改革。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>come ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">剧院帷幕落下(表示演出结束)<br><span class="en">when the curtain in a theatre comes down, it is the end of the performance</span></td><td class="c4">When the curtain <b>came down</b>, we all rushed for the exits.<br>演出一结束，我们纷纷冲向各个出口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>come ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">愉快或兴奋过后平静下来<br><span class="en">(from sth) informal to stop having the pleasant feelings and excitement that sth such as an enjoyable experience or a drug produces</span></td><td class="c4">The party was so good I haven't really <b>come down</b> yet.<br>晚会太棒了，我现在还沉浸其中不能平静。<br>He still hasn't <b>come down</b> from the caffeine.<br>他仍未从咖啡因带来的兴奋中平静下来。10。<br>Can you <b>come down</b> another $30?<br>你能再便宜 30元吗？11。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈdown to sb (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">从…流传下来<br><span class="en">to be passed to sb from sb who lived in the past</span></td><td class="c4">The family estate <b>came down to</b> her from her grandfather.<br>家产是祖父留给她的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈdown to sth</b></td><td class="c3">可归结为；可归纳为<br><span class="en">to be able to be explained as one simple, important question or point</span></td><td class="c4">It all <b>comes down to</b> a matter of priorities in the end.<br>归根到底，这都是孰先孰后的问题。<br>When it <b>comes down to</b> it (= the most important fact is), we can't afford to go.<br>关键是我们去不起。<br>What it <b>comes down to</b> is a choice between money or happiness.<br>这可以归结为一个问题，就是要金钱还是要幸福。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">来接某人；来取某物以；带到另一处<br><span class="en">to come to sb's home,or to the place where sb/sth is in order to take them/it somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">The police <b>came for</b> him this morning.<br>警察今天上午把他带走了。<br>Have you <b>come for</b> the parcel?<br>你是来取包裹的吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈforth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出现；产生<br><span class="en">to appear or be produced</span></td><td class="c4">He struck the rock and water <b>came forth</b>.<br>他敲打岩石，水就涌出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈforward (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">主动提供帮助；信息等<br><span class="en">to offer to give help, information, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Police have asked witnesses to <b>come forward</b>.<br>警方呼吁目击者出来作证。<br>We're hoping that a sponsor will <b>come forward</b> with the extra money.<br>我们希望有赞助者捐助额外资金。<br>No one <b>came forward</b> to claim the reward.<br>无人前来领奖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome from sth</b></td><td class="c3">来自；产自<br><span class="en">to start in a particular place or be made from a particular thing</span></td><td class="c4">Most of the wines that we sell <b>come from</b> France.<br>我们出售的葡萄酒大多产自法国。<br>Does your information <b>come from</b> a reliable source?<br>你的消息来源可靠吗。<br>Where's that terrible noise <b>coming from</b>?<br>那讨厌的噪音是从哪里来的？93%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">海水涌向陆地；涨潮<br><span class="en">when the sea comes in, it moves towards the land</span></td><td class="c4">The tide was <b>coming in</b> fast.<br>潮水迅速上涨。g0。<br>We've got more work <b>coming in</b> than we can handle.<br>工作不断增加，让我们应接不暇。<br>I met all the trains that <b>came in</b> from London.<br>从伦敦来的所有列车都是我接的。<br>We've got just enough money <b>coming in</b> each month to pay the bills.<br>我们每月的收入刚好够支付账单。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">可提供；可利用<br><span class="en">to become available</span></td><td class="c4">English strawberries usually <b>come in in</b> June.<br>英格兰的草莓通常在六月上市。<br>New jobs are <b>coming in</b> all the time.<br>新的职位不断涌现。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">法律或规则开始生效<br><span class="en">if a law or a rule comes in, it is introduced and begins to take effect</span></td><td class="c4">New legislation <b>coming in</b> next month will tackle low pay.<br>下月实施的新法规将着手解决低工资的问题。6。<br>I wish he wouldn't keep <b>coming in</b> with his stupid suggestions.<br>我希望他不要没完没了地提出愚蠢的建议。<br>If you want to <b>come in</b> on the deal, you need to decide now.<br>如果你想加入这项交易，现在就得决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">电话；信件或消息<br><span class="en">of a phone call, letter or message</span></td><td class="c4">The rain's <b>coming in</b> through that hole.<br>雨水从那个洞漏进来。<br>The sun was <b>coming in</b> at the windows.<br>阳光从窗户射进来。<br>When you <b>come in</b> the door, youll find Reception on your left.<br>你一进门就能看到左边的接待处。<br>She <b>came into</b> the room crying.<br>她哭着进了房间。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin<br>ˌcome ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">到办公室或工作地点去工作<br><span class="en">to go to an office or the place where you work, in order to do some work</span></td><td class="c4">Are you <b>coming into</b> the office tomorrow?<br>你明天去办公室吗？o8。<br>Trolleybuses first <b>came in in</b> 1923.<br>无轨电车最早出现于 1923 年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈin for sth</b></td><td class="c3">遭受；招致<br><span class="en">to receive sth, especially sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">The government has <b>come in for</b> severe criticism from all sides.<br>政府遭到各方的严厉批评。<br>The company <b>came in for</b> a lot of stick (= a lot of criticism) with their advertising campaign.<br>公司的广告宣传活动备受指摘。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈin with sb (on sth), .come ˈin (with sb) on sth</b></td><td class="c3">加入；入伙<br><span class="en">if sb comes in with you, they join you in a particular project, activity, business, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Do you want to <b>come</b> in with me on Joe's present?<br>你愿意和我凑份子给乔买礼物吗。<br>My brother hoped I would <b>come</b> in with him when he started his own business.<br>哥哥希望我和他一起创业。<br>Do you want to <b>come</b> in on the deal?<br>你想参与这笔交易吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始存在(或发生等)<br><span class="en">to begin to exist, happen, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The cherry trees are <b>coming into</b> blossom.<br>樱桃树开花了。<br>The band only <b>came into</b> being in 2005.<br>这支乐队 2005年才成立。<br>When do the new regulations <b>come into</b> force/effect?<br>新规章制度何时生效。<br>A variety of factors <b>come into</b> play when choosing an employee.<br>挑选雇员要考虑各种各样的因素。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">获得；继承(遗产)<br><span class="en">to receive a large sum of money when sb dies</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>came into</b> a fortune when her cousin died.<br>表兄去世后她继承了一大笔财产。<br>This bike <b>comes into</b> its own on rough ground.<br>这辆自行车在颠簸的地面上才能显示出它的优势。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome from sth<br>ˈcome from doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">由…引起；是…的结果<br><span class="en">to happen as a result of sth</span></td><td class="c4">I told him no good would <b>come</b> of it.<br>我告诉过他不会有任何好的结果。<br>He promised to help, but I don't think anything will <b>come</b> of it.<br>他答应帮忙，但我想他只是说说而已。<br>That's what <b>comes</b> of not listening to my advice!<br>那就是不听我劝的下场。<br>I had the feeling of satisfaction that <b>comes</b> from <b>doing</b> a difficult job well.<br>我有那种圆满完成一项棘手工作的满足感。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">可拆除；可拆卸<br><span class="en">to be able to be removed</span></td><td class="c4">Does this knob <b>come off</b>?<br>这个旋钮能卸下来吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈoff<br>.come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…掉下；脱落<br><span class="en">to become separated from sth</span></td><td class="c4">The handle <b>came off</b> in my hand.<br>把手掉在我手里了。A。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈoff<br>.come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…掉下；落下<br><span class="en">to fall from sth</span></td><td class="c4">She braked sharply and <b>came off</b> her bike.<br>她猛一剎闸，从自行车上摔了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈoff<br>.come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">下台；退场<br><span class="en">to leave the stage, the sports field, etc. during a play or a game</span></td><td class="c4">Two players <b>came off</b> just before half time.<br>在上半场即将结束之前，有两名队员下场了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈoff<br>.come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从交通工具上下来；离开(道路)<br><span class="en">to leave sth such as a vehicle or a road</span></td><td class="c4">She looked tired as she <b>came off</b> the plane.<br>她下飞机时显得很疲惫。<br>Come off (the motorway) at junction <b>five</b>.<br>在五号交叉路口驶离(高速公路)。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈoff<br>.come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从价格中削减<br><span class="en">if an amount of money comes off a price, the price becomes lower by that amount</span></td><td class="c4">Two pence a litre is <b>coming off</b> the price of petrol.<br>汽油价格每升将要下调两便士。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">停止服药；吸毒；饮酒等<br><span class="en">to stop using sth; to stop taking a drug, medicine, alcohol, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">It's time she tried to <b>come off</b> sleeping pills.<br>她该设法戒掉安眠药 T。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">热量；气味；风等<br><span class="en">of heat, a smell, the wind, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">There was a mist <b>coming off</b> the sea.<br>海上起雾 J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">圆满渡过一段；成功时期；(一段糟糕时期之后)恢复正常<br><span class="en">to have just completed a very successful period of time or returned to normal after a bad period</span></td><td class="c4">Farmers are <b>coming off</b> another tough year.<br>农民又熬过了困难的一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始讨论(某一话题)<br><span class="en">to start talking about or discussing a topic</span></td><td class="c4">The sun <b>came</b> out in the afternoon.<br>下午出太阳了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">出版；发行；发表<br><span class="en">to be published or produced</span></td><td class="c4">Her new novel's just <b>come</b> out.<br>她的新小说刚出版。9。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">显示；显现<br><span class="en">to be shown clearly</span></td><td class="c4">His arrogance <b>comes</b> out in every speech he makes.<br>每次讲话时他的傲慢都溢于言表。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">和某人外出社交<br><span class="en">(with sb) to go somewhere with sb for a social event</span></td><td class="c4">Will you <b>come</b> out to dinner with me tonight?<br>你今晚和我出去吃饭好吗？7。<br>He tried to pay her a compliment but it <b>came</b> out all wrong.<br>他本想称赞她，可是话一出口却全变味了。9 +。<br>Only one member of staff <b>came</b> out and said that the working conditions were unsatisfactory.<br>只有一名职员挺身而出，指出工作条件不能令人满意。11。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈout<br>ˌcome ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">离开；从…出来<br><span class="en">to leave a place or appear from inside a place</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Come out</b>! I know you're in there!<br>出来吧！我知道你在里面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈout<br>ˌcome ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…掉下；脱落<br><span class="en">if an object comes out of sth, it is removed from the place where it is fixed or becomes separated from sth</span></td><td class="c4">Her tooth <b>came out</b> when she bit into the apple.<br>她咬苹果时崩掉了牙齿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>come ˈout<br>ˌcome ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">污渍或污垢被洗掉；被清除<br><span class="en">if a mark or some dirt comes out, it is removed from sth by washing or cleaning</span></td><td class="c4">The bloodstains won't <b>come out</b> of my shirt.<br>我衬衫上的血迹洗不掉。<br>It was a very expensive skirt, but most of the colour <b>came out</b> when I washed it.<br>这条裙子很贵，可一洗颜色就快褪光了。4 +。<br>His reputation <b>came out</b> undamaged.<br>结果他的声誉并未受损。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈout at sth</b></td><td class="c3">共计；合计<br><span class="en">to add up to a particular cost or sui</span></td><td class="c4">The total bill <b>comes out at</b> over a thousand pounds.<br>账单金额总计超过一千英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈout in sth</b></td><td class="c3">皮肤上布满疹子；粉刺等<br><span class="en">if a person comes out in sth such as spots, their skin becomes covered in them •</span></td><td class="c4">The cream made her face <b>come out in</b> a rash.<br>用了这种乳箱后，她脸上起了皮疹。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">艰难时期之后恢复正常<br><span class="en">to return to normal after a difficult time</span></td><td class="c4">The country is slowly <b>coming out of</b> recession.<br>该国正慢慢走出经济衰退。2 t0。<br>The book <b>came out of</b> her travels in Japan.<br>这本书取材于她在日本的游历经历。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从总数中扣减；减掉<br><span class="en">to be taken away from a total amount</span></td><td class="c4">The money will have to <b>come out of</b> your wages.<br>这笔钱只能从你的工资中扣除。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈout with sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">说出(尤指令人吃惊或无礼的话)<br><span class="en">to say sth, especially sth surprising or not polite</span></td><td class="c4">I can't believe the things he <b>comes out with</b>!<br>我难以相信他居然说出这种话。<br>When I asked her why she was late, she just <b>came out with</b> a load of nonsense.<br>我问她为何迟到，她的回答不看边际。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">从…过来<br><span class="en">(to sb/sth) to move across a room, a road, an ocean, etc. towards where the speaker is</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Come over</b> and meet my husband.<br>过来见见我丈夫吧。<br>When are you <b>coming over</b> to England again?<br>你何时再次来英国呢。<br>Lots of people are <b>coming over</b> from America for the wedding.<br>很多人要从美国来参加婚礼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">通常指到家中短暂造访；顺便来访<br><span class="en">(to sth) to visit sb for a short time, usually at their home</span></td><td class="c4">Her son only <b>comes over</b> to see her occasionally.<br>她的儿子只是偶尔来看看她。<br>Our new neighbours <b>came over</b> to our house last night.<br>昨天晚上新邻居到我们家来了。3 +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">感觉；情绪等<br><span class="en">of a feeling, a mood, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She hasn't <b>come</b> round from the anaesthetic yet.<br>她尚未从麻醉中苏醒过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈover to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">转到…方面来；改变立场(或看法等)<br><span class="en">to leave one group of people in order to join a competing group; to change from one opinion to another</span></td><td class="c4">Some of their members have <b>come over to</b> our side.<br>他们的一些成员转变立场，站到了我们这边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈpast<br>ˌcome ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">从说话者前经过<br><span class="en">to pass in front of the speaker or the place where the speaker is</span></td><td class="c4">Charlie <b>came past</b> on his bike.<br>查利骑自行车从我身边经过。<br>Do you want to <b>come</b> round for lunch?<br>你来家里吃午饭好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come ˈpast<br>ˌcome ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">改变立场；改变观点<br><span class="en">(to sth) (informal) to agree to sth that you were against before; to change your opinion about sth</span></td><td class="c4">Shell never <b>come</b> round to our way of thinking.<br>她决不会改变观点转而同意我们的想法。<br>Don't push him; he'll <b>come</b> round in time.<br>别催他，他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">进入(房间或建筑物)；(从…房间)进入另；一房间；(尤指请某人)进来<br><span class="en">(to sth) (informal) used especially to ask sb to enter a room or a building, or move from one room to another</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Come through</b> to my office.<br>到我办公室来吧。<br>We're going to buy a new car when the insurance money <b>comes through</b>.<br>收到保险金之后，我们打算买辆新车。<br>Hess still waiting for his divorce to <b>come through</b>.<br>他还在等候批准离婚。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈthrough<br>ˌcome ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">穿过；越过；通过<br><span class="en">to enter and cross a room, an area of land, a town, a country, etc.; to pass through sth</span></td><td class="c4">Put sth over the hole to stop the rain <b>coming through</b>.<br>把洞堵上，免得漏雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈthrough<br>ˌcome ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">重病后康复；避免严重伤害；安然度过<br><span class="en">to get better after a serious illness; to avoid serious injury or damage</span></td><td class="c4">He's very ill but his doctors expect him to <b>come through</b> the operation.<br>他病得很重，但医生估计手术后能挺过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈthrough<br>ˌcome ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">露出；探出<br><span class="en">to start to appear from under or behind sth</span></td><td class="c4">The baby's front teeth were <b>coming through</b>.<br>婴儿的门牙露头了。<br>The sun's <b>coming through</b> the clouds at last.<br>太阳终于拨云而出。<br>Most of the students <b>came through</b> (the exam) with flying colours (= were very successful).<br>大多数学生考试成绩优秀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome to sb</b></td><td class="c3">闪现在脑海<br><span class="en">if an idea comes to you, it suddenly enters your mind</span></td><td class="c4">The idea <b>came to</b> me in the middle of the night.<br>我在半夜时突然想到了这个主意。<br>It suddenly <b>came to</b> her that she had been wrong.<br>她突然。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome to sb</b></td><td class="c3">不动产等<br><span class="en">of money, Property, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">All my money will <b>come to</b> you when I die.<br>我死后我的钱全归你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come to yourˈself <span class="tag">(old-fashioned)</span></b></td><td class="c3">恢复常态<br><span class="en">to retur to your normal state</span></td><td class="c4">It took her a while to <b>come to</b> herself again.<br>她过了一会儿才回过神来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome to sth</b></td><td class="c3">共计；达到；等于<br><span class="en">to add up to sth; to be equal to sth</span></td><td class="c4">The bill <b>came to</b> $50.<br>账单金额是50元。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome to sth</b></td><td class="c3">达到(某一状况)；得出(结果)<br><span class="en">to reach a particular state or condition; to arrive at sth</span></td><td class="c4">We both <b>came to</b> the same conclusion.<br>我们均得出同样的结论。<br>All her dreams had <b>come to</b> nothing.<br>她所有的梦想都破灭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>come toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">合成一体；结合；联合<br><span class="en">if two or more people or things come together, they form one group or one piece</span></td><td class="c4">Several local groups <b>came together</b> to fight the proposed housing development.<br>一些当地组织联合起来反对规划中的房产开发。<br>During the last three days of rehearsals, everything <b>came together</b>.<br>在最后三天的排练中，各部分都衔接起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈunder sth</b></td><td class="c3">归入；归类<br><span class="en">to be included within a particular group or collection of things</span></td><td class="c4">Several different types of schools <b>come under</b> the heading of private schools.<br>一些学校可归到“私立学校” 类。<br>She's <b>come under</b> intense pressure to change her mind.<br>她承受着要她转变想法的巨大压力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>come ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">植物<br><span class="en">of plants</span></td><td class="c4">The first snowdrops are just <b>coming up</b>.<br>第一茬雪花莲刚破土发芽。<br>Bubbles were <b>coming up</b> to the surface.<br>气泡不断冒出水面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>come ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指意外地发生<br><span class="en">to happen, especially when not expect it</span></td><td class="c4">Something urgent has <b>come up</b>; I have to go.<br>突然有了急事，我得走了。<br>Opportunities like this don't <b>come up</b> every day.<br>这种机遇不是每天都有的。<br><b>Coming up</b> next is the news.<br>以下是新闻报道。<br>My sister hardly <b>comes up</b> to my shoulder.<br>妹妹还不到我的肩膀。<br>His scarf <b>came up</b> over his eyes.<br>他的围巾表住了眼睛。<br>Police are still <b>coming up</b> empty-handed in the search for the missing girl.<br>警方搜寻失踪女孩仍无进展。<br>That was a wonderful meal! Youve <b>come up</b> trumps again.<br>这顿饭好极了！你又露了一手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup against sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">面对；碰到(难缠的人或麻烦事)<br><span class="en">if you come up against sb/sth, you have to face sb/sth that is difficult</span></td><td class="c4">We expect to <b>come up against</b> a lot of opposition to the scheme.<br>我们预料这个计划会遭到很多人的反对。<br>Youll <b>come up against</b> the reigning champion in the next round.<br>你下一轮将与卫冕冠军交锋。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup for sth</b></td><td class="c3">接近(期限)<br><span class="en">to come to the time when sth must be done</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>coming up for</b> retirement soon.<br>他很快就要退休了。<br>She <b>comes up for</b> re-election next year.<br>她明年将再度参加选举。<br>When does your contract <b>come up for</b> renewal?<br>你的合同何时到期续约。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup. on sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">接近(某时间或年龄)<br><span class="en">to be almost particular time or age</span></td><td class="c4">It's <b>coming</b> up on your bedtime.<br>你该睡觉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">接近某地；年龄或时段<br><span class="en">to approach a particular place, an age or a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">You're <b>coming up to</b> a busy road now.<br>你正开上拥挤路段。<br>It's just <b>coming up to</b> half past twelve.<br>就快到十二点半了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">达到；符合(认可的水平或标准)<br><span class="en">to reach an acceptable level or standard</span></td><td class="c4">The performance didn't <b>come up to</b> our expectations.<br>演出没有我们预想的那么好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcome ˈup with sth</b></td><td class="c3">想到(主意)；找到(答案或解决方法)<br><span class="en">to think of an idea, an answer to a question or a solution to a problem</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>came up with</b> a great idea for increasing sales.<br>她想出了增加销售量的绝妙主意。四J。<br>He always <b>comes up with</b> the goods (= does what he is expected to do) on the day.<br>他总是能准时交差。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcome with sth</b></td><td class="c3">包括在…之中；是…的一部分<br><span class="en">to be included with or as part of sth</span></td><td class="c4">A new car <b>comes with</b> the job.<br>做这份工作配有一辆新车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>complain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>comˈplain of sth</b></td><td class="c3">诉说(病情或疼痛)；主诉<br><span class="en">to say that you feel ill/sick or are suffering from a pain</span></td><td class="c4">Several children <b>complained of</b> severe stomach pains.<br>有几个孩子说肚子疼得厉害。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>conceive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈceive of sth</b></td><td class="c3">构思；想出主意；计划等；设想<br><span class="en">to form an idea, a plan, etc. in your mind; to imagine sth</span></td><td class="c4">I cannot <b>conceive of</b> any Situation in which your pian would work.<br>我想象不出你的计划怎么可以成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cone</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcone sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">用锥形路标关闭道路或道路；的一部分<br><span class="en">to close a road or part of a road with cones</span></td><td class="c4">Part of the road was <b>coned off</b> while repairs were done.<br>维修期间，用锥形路标封闭了一段公路。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>confess</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈfess to sth<br>conˈfess to doing sth sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指正式地或向警方供认；坦白；交代<br><span class="en">to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done sth wrong or illegal</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>confessed to</b> the murder.<br>她承认犯有谋杀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>confide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈfide in sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…吐露；向…倾诉(秘密等)<br><span class="en">to tell sb a secret or a piece of information that you would not tell other people</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>confide in</b> you?<br>你能保证不说出去吗。<br>Do you have a friend that you can <b>confide in</b>?<br>你有可以说知心话的朋友吗？o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>confine</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈfine sb/sth to sth<br>conˈfine yourself to sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…限制在…以内；将…局限于某一活动；主题；地域等<br><span class="en">to keep sb/sth/yourself inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The work will not be <b>confined to</b> the Glasgow area.<br>这一工作不会仅限于格拉斯哥地区。I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be conˈfined to sth</b></td><td class="c3">被关在…里；被限制于(狭小或封闭的空间)<br><span class="en">if a person or an animal is confined to a place, they are kept in a small or closed space and not allowed to go out</span></td><td class="c4">The children <b>were confined to</b> their rooms for the evening.<br>晚上孩子们不能出房门。<br>The soldiers concerned <b>were confined to</b> barracks (= had to stay in the barracks, as a punishment).<br>有关的士兵只能在营房内活动，不能外出. 2。<br>He <b>was confined to</b> a wheelchair after the car accident.<br>自那场车祸之后，他只能坐轮椅代步。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>confront</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈfront sb with sth</b></td><td class="c3">使面临；使遭遇；使对付困难或令人不快的人；事物<br><span class="en">to make sb face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>confronted her with</b> a choice between her career or their relationship.<br>他要她在事业和两人关系之间作出选择。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be conˈfronted with sth</b></td><td class="c3">面对；正视；对付<br><span class="en">to have sth in front of you that you have to deal with or react to</span></td><td class="c4">Most people when <b>confronted</b> with a horse will pat it.<br>大多数人遇见马都会拍拍它。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>conk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌconk ˈout <span class="tag">(informal or humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">车辆或机器停止运转；出故障；失灵<br><span class="en">if a vehicle or a machine conks out, it stops working</span></td><td class="c4">Our car <b>conked out</b> 5 miles from home.<br>我们的车在离家 5 英里的地方抛锚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>connive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈnive at/in sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对(自己明知错误的事)视而不见；纵容<br><span class="en">to ignore or seem to allow sth that you know is wrong</span></td><td class="c4">Most of the fieldwork consisted of making tape general is accused of <b>conniving in</b> a plot to topple the government.<br>将军被指控默许了一起颠覆政府的阴谋。<br>Her brother is believed to have <b>connived at</b> her murder.<br>据信她的哥哥没有制止她杀人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>consent</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈsent to sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">赞成；准许<br><span class="en">to agree to sth or give your permission for sth</span></td><td class="c4">He reluctantly <b>consented to</b> their marriage.<br>他勉强同意了他们的婚事。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>consist</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈsist in sth<br>conˈsist in doing sth <span class="tag">(formal not used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时</td><td class="c4">A home does not <b>consist in</b> its architecture and decoration.<br>家之所以为家，并不在于其建筑与装潢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>consort</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈsort with sb <span class="tag">(formal or humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…来往；结交(尤指不合适的人)<br><span class="en">to spend time with sb, especially sb that other people do not approve of</span></td><td class="c4">The nurses are instructed not to <b>consort with</b> their patients.<br>护士得到指示不得与病人交往。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>contend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈtend with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">应对；应付(困境或不好打交道的人)<br><span class="en">to have to deal with a difficult person or situation</span></td><td class="c4">If we leave at eight, well have to <b>contend with</b> the rush-hour traffic.<br>如果八点钟出发，我们就会遇上交通高峰。<br>He's had a lot of serious problems to <b>contend with</b>.<br>他有很多棘手的问题要解决。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>content</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈtent yourself with sth</b></td><td class="c3">安于；满足于(现状)；对…不求更好<br><span class="en">to accept and be satisfied with sth and not try to have or do sth better</span></td><td class="c4">The crowd <b>contented themselves with</b> shouting insults.<br>那群人只顾着破口大骂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>contribute</b></td><td class="c2"><b>conˈtribute to sth</b></td><td class="c3">助长；促成；加剧<br><span class="en">to help to cause sth</span></td><td class="c4">The stress of losing his job <b>contributed to</b> his death.<br>失业的压力是导致他死亡的因素之一。<br>The Prime Minister <b>contributed to</b> his own downfall by failing to control his government.<br>首相未能管理好政府，加速了他本人的下台。</td></tr>
