<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cook</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcook sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指麻利地做饭；烹饪<br><span class="en">to cook sth, especially very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">In half an hour she had managed to <b>cook up</b> some delicious chilli.<br>她半小时内做好了美味可口的辣椒。<br>They <b>cooked up</b> the story between the two of them.<br>他们俩共同编造了这套谎话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cool</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cool ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">失去兴趣；失去热情<br><span class="en">to become less interested or enthusiastic</span></td><td class="c4">Our relationship was going well, but then Laura seemed to <b>cool off</b>.<br>正当我们的关系进展顺利时，劳拉却似乎冷淡下来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cool ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">变凉；冷却下来<br><span class="en">if sth hot cools off, it becomes cooler</span></td><td class="c4">Leave the engine to <b>cool off</b> before you touch it.<br>等发动机冷却了才能碰它。<br>The union and the employers failed to reach an agreement within the <b>cooling</b>-<b>off</b> period.<br>工会和资方在冷却期内未能达成协议。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>coop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be .cooped ˈup (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">被关(在…里)；被禁闭<br><span class="en">if a person or an animal is cooped up, they/it are kept in a small place or inside a building</span></td><td class="c4">We've been cooped <b>up</b> (indoors) for hours because of the rain.<br>这场兩使我们(在屋里)被困了几个小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cop ˈout<br>ˌcop ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">逃避；放弃(应做的事)<br><span class="en">to avoid or not do sth that you should be doing, because you are afraid, shy, lazy, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">You can't just <b>cop out</b> of difficult decisions.<br>你不能因为难以决定就回避。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>copy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcopy sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">抄写下来<br><span class="en">to write sth exactly as it is written somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">We copied <b>down</b> what the teacher had written on the blackboard.<br>我们把老师写在黑板上的东西抄了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcopy sb ˈin (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">信件；电邮等抄送某人<br><span class="en">to make sure that sb receives a copy of a letter, an email, etc.that you are sending to sb else</span></td><td class="c4">Please <b>copy me in</b> on all correspondence.<br>请把所有来信都抄送给我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>copy sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">重新抄写；复写；复印<br><span class="en">to write sth out again; to make a copy of sth that is already written or printed</span></td><td class="c4">She copied <b>out</b> a recipe she found in a library book.<br>她把在图书馆的书上找到的食谱抄了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cordon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cordon sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">封锁(某地区)；在…设警戒线<br><span class="en">to stop people going into an area by forming a line or ring around it with police, soldiers, objects, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Police <b>cordoned off</b> the area until the bomb was defused.<br>警方封锁了这个地区，直至炸弹被拆除。<br>The roads were <b>cordoned off</b>.<br>这些道路被封了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cost</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cost sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">估算…的成本<br><span class="en">to estimate how much money will be needed for sth</span></td><td class="c4">We'll have to <b>cost the work out</b> before we make a decision.<br>在作决定之前，我们得估算一下这项工作的成本。<br>Have you <b>costed out</b> how much it will be to hire another member of staff?<br>你估算过再雇用一名职员的开销吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cosy ˈup to sb <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…套近乎；和…攀交情；讨好<br><span class="en">to try to become friendly with sb, especially in order to gain an advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">She's only <b>cosying up to</b> him because she needs his help.<br>她讨好他，只不过因为她需要他帮忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cotton</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcotton ˈon (to sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">理解；领会；意识到<br><span class="en">to come to understand or realize sth without being told directly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>cottons on</b> very quickly.<br>她领悟力强。<br>It took him a while to <b>cotton on</b> to what I was trying to say.<br>过了一会儿，他才明白我想说什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cough</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cough ˈup<br>.cough sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不情愿地付账；给钱<br><span class="en">to pay for sth or give sb money unwillingly</span></td><td class="c4">You owe me £20. Come on, <b>cough up</b>!<br>你欠我20英镑。快点，掏钱吧。<br>Don't <b>cough up</b> the money until the job's finished.<br>活儿干完以前不要掏钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>count</b></td><td class="c2"><b>count aˈgainst sb</b></td><td class="c3">对…不利<br><span class="en">to be a disadvantage to sb</span></td><td class="c4">I'm sure that being late for the interview <b>counted against</b> me.<br>我肯定面试迟到对我不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcount ˈdown (to sth)<br>ˌcount sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">倒计时；倒数<br><span class="en">to be waiting for an important or exciting day, event, etc. and be counting the number of days, minutes, etc. there are before it</span></td><td class="c4">The whole world was <b>counting</b> <b>down</b> to the new millennium.<br>全世界都在倒计时迎接新千年的来临。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcount sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">算入；包括<br><span class="en">to include sb in a group or an activity</span></td><td class="c4">If youre going to the theatre, you can <b>count me in</b>.<br>你们要是去看戏，算我一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>count ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">报数<br><span class="en">if people count off, they say loudly in order the numbers they have been given</span></td><td class="c4">He made everyone <b>count off</b>.<br>他让大家报数。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>count on sb/sth doing sth (also ˈcount upon sb/sth, etc. more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">依赖；倚靠；指望(某人做某事)；相信；预期；期待(某事发生)<br><span class="en">to rely on sb to do sth; to expect sth to happen and make plans in an appropriate way</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>count</b> on me!<br>我决不辜负你。<br>I'm <b>counting</b> on your support.<br>我就靠你支持啦。<br>She can be <b>counted</b> <b>upon</b> to contribute good ideas.<br>她总能想到好点子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcount sb ˈout<br>.count sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不把…算入；不包括<br><span class="en">to not include sb in a group or an activity</span></td><td class="c4">You may enjoy those games, but you can <b>count me out</b>.<br>你们可能喜欢那些比赛，但别把我算在内。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcount sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">逐一数出；清点<br><span class="en">to count coins, etc. one by one and put them somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>counted out</b> the exact money (on the counter).<br>他清点了(柜台上的)零钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>couple</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcouple sb/sth with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…与…连接起来<br><span class="en">to link one person, thing or situation with another</span></td><td class="c4">The large number of new graduates, <b>coupled with</b> high unemployment, means that there is fierce competition for jobs.<br>应届毕业生很多，再加上失业率很高，这意味着求职竞争激烈。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cover</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcover sth ˈover (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以…覆盖；遮掩<br><span class="en">to cover sth completely, especially to hide or protect it</span></td><td class="c4">Put the bulbs in a bowl and <b>cover them over</b> with soil.<br>把球茎放入盆中，上面盖上土。<br>The shopping mall is <b>covered over</b> with an enormous glass roof.<br>购物中心上方罩着巨大的玻璃顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcover ˈup<br>ˌcover yourself ˈup (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">加衣；穿着(某衣物)<br><span class="en">to Put on more clothes</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure you <b>cover up</b> before going out in the sun.<br>烈日下外出之前，一定要多穿衣服把身体包住。<br><b>Cover yourself up</b>.It's cold.<br>穿暖和点，天气很冷。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcover ˈup (for sb/sth)<br>cover sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">为…掩饰；隐瞒错误；罪行；真相<br><span class="en">to try hard to stop people finding out about a mistake, a crime, etc.; to hide the truth about sth</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>covering</b> up for her.<br>他总是护她的短。<br>The government's attempts to <b>cover</b> up the scandal failed.<br>政府企图掩盖丑闻，但没有得逞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>cover sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">盖住；遮住<br><span class="en">to put sth over sb/sth in order to hide or protect them/it</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>cover up</b> ugly pipes with wooden boxes.<br>你可以用木盒包住这些难看的管子。<br>There was something on the table <b>covered up</b> with a cloth.<br>桌子上有东西用布罩着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrack ˈdown<br>.crack ˈdown on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…采取严厉措施；制裁；镇压<br><span class="en">to try harder to prevent people breaking a rule, using sth harmful, committing a crime, etc. and deal severely with those who do</span></td><td class="c4">Police are <b>cracking down</b> hard on drug dealers.<br>警方正在严厉打击毒贩。<br>The government is <b>cracking down</b> on misleading food labelling.<br>政府正采取严厉措施取缔误导性食品标签。» ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrack ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因压力身体或精神垮掉；崩溃<br><span class="en">to become physically or mentally ill because you are under pressure</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>cracking up</b> under the strain.<br>压力过大，她快要吃不消了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcrack-up n <span class="tag">(AmE informal a)</span></b></td><td class="c3">精神崩溃<br><span class="en">period of mental illness caused by pressure</span></td><td class="c4">She was never the same again after her <b>crack-up</b>.<br>精神崩溃后她就像换了个人。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrack ˈup<br>ˌcrack sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使大笑起来<br><span class="en">to start laughing a lot; to make sb laugh a lot</span></td><td class="c4">Everybody <b>cracked up</b> when he fell over.<br>他摔了一跤，引起众人一阵哄笑。<br>She's not as good as she's <b>cracked up</b> to be.<br>她并不像人们说得那么好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcrack-up n <span class="tag">(AmE informal a)</span></b></td><td class="c3">逗趣的人</td><td class="c4">She was always the class <b>crack-up</b>.<br>她在班上总是很风趣。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crank</b></td><td class="c2"><b>crank sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大量快速制成；粗制滥造<br><span class="en">to produce sth quickly and in large amounts</span></td><td class="c4">The plant can <b>crank out</b> about 63 cars an hour.<br>这家工厂每小时约可生产63辆汽车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrash ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">轰隆一声倒下(或落下)<br><span class="en">to fall with a very loud noise</span></td><td class="c4">Passengers had a lucky escape when a huge tree <b>crashed down</b> onto a bus.<br>大树哗啦一声砸倒在公共汽车上，幸好乘客有惊无险。<br>John's hand came <b>crashing down</b> on the table (= he hit the table hard with his hand).<br>约翰的手砰的一声拍在桌子上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>crash ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或驾驶员<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or a driver</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>crashed into</b> a wall.<br>车子猛地撞到了墙上。<br>I <b>crashed into</b> the back of the car in front.<br>我砰的一声与前车追尾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrash ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因极度疲劳入睡；睡去<br><span class="en">to. go to sleep because you are very tired</span></td><td class="c4">I was so tired I <b>crashed out</b> in an armchair.<br>我疲惫不堪，在扶手椅上睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrash ˈout of sth (sport)</b></td><td class="c3">在比赛中惨败出局<br><span class="en">to lose a game vet badly and so not be able to continue to take part in a competition</span></td><td class="c4">England <b>crashed out of</b> the World Cup.<br>英格兰队在世界杯比赛中惨遭淘汰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crawl</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcrawl with sb/sth usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The place is <b>crawling</b> with cops!<br>这地方到处是警察。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cream</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcream sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">提取(精华)；选取(最好的人或物)；取走一定；数额的钱款<br><span class="en">to take away the best people or things in a group or an amount of money, usually for your own advantage</span></td><td class="c4">The best pupils are <b>creamed off</b> into special classes.<br>最优秀的学生都编入特别班。<br>The company's directors are <b>creaming off</b> the profits.<br>公司的董事们分享了利润。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crease</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrease ˈup<br>ˌcrease sb ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使大笑起来<br><span class="en">to start laughing; to make sb start laughing</span></td><td class="c4">We all <b>creased up</b> when we saw her hat!<br>看到她的帽子，我们都爆笑起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>credit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcredit A with B<br>ˈcredit B</b></td><td class="c3">认为…负责某事(或做某事)；把某事归功于<br><span class="en">to A to believe that sb/sth is responsible for sth or for doing sth, especially sth good</span></td><td class="c4">Bach is <b>credited</b> with performing the first solo on a piano.<br>巴赫被认为是第一个表演钢琴独奏的人。<br>She <b>credits</b> her good looks and intelligence to her father's side of the family.<br>她认为自己的美貌和才智遗传自父亲的血统。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcredit A with B<br>ˈcredit B</b></td><td class="c3">认为…有(某品质或优点)<br><span class="en">to consider that sb/sth has a particular good quality or characteristic</span></td><td class="c4">Numerous health benefits are <b>credited</b> to this natural oil.<br>人们认为这种天然油对健康好处良多。态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>creep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep ˈin<br>.Creep ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐；发生；逐步影响<br><span class="en">to start happening or affecting sb/sth gradually</span></td><td class="c4">More and more foreign words are <b>creeping into</b> the language.<br>越来越多的外来词渗透到这种语言中来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使害怕；使不安<br><span class="en">to make sb feel frightened and not safe</span></td><td class="c4">The way that man was watching us really <b>creeped me out</b>.<br>那个男人看着我们的样子把我吓坏了。<br>I was a little <b>creeped out</b> by their first video.<br>他们的第一部录像使我有点受惊了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">感觉悄悄袭来；(表情)慢慢流簬<br><span class="en">if a feeling creeps over you, or an expression creeps over your face, it gradually affects you</span></td><td class="c4">A feeling of tiredness began to <b>creep over</b> her.<br>她渐渐开始感到疲惫。<br>A sly smile crept <b>over</b> her lips.<br>她的嘴角露出一丝狡點。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">价格；数量等逐渐增长<br><span class="en">if a price, anl amount, etc. creeps up, it rises very gradually</span></td><td class="c4">House prices are starting to <b>creep up</b>.<br>房价在逐渐上涨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">缓慢而悄悄地接近<br><span class="en">(on sb) to move nearer to sb/sth slowly and quietly without being seen or heard</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>creep up</b> on me like that!<br>别那样蹑手蹑脚地靠近我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcreep ˈup on sb</b></td><td class="c3">事件；日期等不知不觉到来；不受注意地临近<br><span class="en">if an event, a date, etc. creeps up on you, it arrives before you are really ready for it</span></td><td class="c4">The exams just seemed to <b>creep up on</b> me.<br>考试似乎不知不觉就到了。2i a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrop ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">意外地出现；发生<br><span class="en">to appear, happen, eic. when it is not expected</span></td><td class="c4">Her name Keeps <b>cropping up</b> everywhere.<br>她的名字不断在各种场合出现。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cross</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cross sb/sth ˈoff<br>ˌcross sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从名单或清单上画掉；勾销；删去<br><span class="en">to remove sb's name or an item from a list by drawing a line through it because you have dealt with them/it or they are/it is no longer involved</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Cross off</b> any items we've already got.<br>把我们已有的物品都画掉。<br>Jane won't be coming, so we can crass her <b>off</b> the list.<br>简不来了，我们可以把她的名字从名单上删掉了。s v+n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcrouch over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">俯身接近<br><span class="en">to bend over sb/sth so you are near them/it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>crouched over</b> the injured man, checking his wounds.<br>她弯下腰，检查伤员的伤口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crowd</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrowd ˈin (on sb)</b></td><td class="c3">高楼；高山等给(某人)压迫感<br><span class="en">if high buildings, mountains, etc. crowd in, they seem to surround you and threaten you or have a strong effect On</span></td><td class="c4">The high walls seemed to <b>crowd in</b> (on her).<br>四周的高墻似乎(向她)压了过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrowd sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把…(从…中)挤出去<br><span class="en">(of sth) if a number of people or things crowd out other people or things, they are present in such large numbers that there is no room for anyone or anything else</span></td><td class="c4">Tourists are <b>crowding the regular customers out</b> of the bar.<br>酒吧挤满游客，老主顾都进不去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>crumple</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcrumple sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把(纸片等)揉成一团<br><span class="en">to crush sth, especially a piece of paper, into a ball</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>crumpled his letter up</b> without even looking at it.<br>她连看都没看就把他的信揉成一团。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cry</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcry for sth</b></td><td class="c3">呼吁；呼救<br><span class="en">to ask for or demand sth in a determined or urgent way</span></td><td class="c4">The families of the victims are <b>crying for</b> justice.<br>受害者家属强烈呼吁伸张正义。<br>Listen! That sounds like somebody <b>crying</b> (= calling) for help.<br>听！那声音像是有人在喊救命。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cry ˈoff<br>.cry ˈoff sth<br>.cry ˈoff doing sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">食言；违背约定<br><span class="en">to decide not to do sth you have promised or agreed to do</span></td><td class="c4">We'd arranged to go together but Luis cried <b>off</b> at the last moment.<br>我们说好一起去的，可路易斯事到临头又变卦了。<br>Why did you <b>cry off</b> training last night?<br>昨晚的训练你为什么说来又没来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cry ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">因伤痛；惊恐；惊讶等大叫；叫喊<br><span class="en">to make a loud sound without words because you are hurt, afraid, surprised, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She cried <b>out</b> in/with pain.<br>她疼得大叫。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cry ˈout against sth</b></td><td class="c3">强烈抗议；大声疾呼反对<br><span class="en">to protest strongly about sth</span></td><td class="c4">People have been <b>crying out against</b> this abuse for years.<br>多年来人们一直在激烈谴责这一陋习。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcry ˈout for sth usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The group is <b>crying</b> <b>out</b> for new members.<br>该组急需新成员。<br>The whole system was <b>crying</b> <b>out</b> for a radical review.<br>整个体系亟待彻底检讨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cuddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>cuddle ˈup (to/against sb)<br>cuddle ˈup together</b></td><td class="c3">偎依着(某人)；紧靠在一起<br><span class="en">if children, pets, etc. cuddle up, they sit or lie close to each other or sb else, because they need warmth or comfort, or want to show affection</span></td><td class="c4">Jack <b>cuddled</b> up to his mother.<br>杰克依偎着母亲。<br>The cubs <b>cuddle</b> up <b>together</b> for warmth.<br>幼兽挤在一起取暖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>culminate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈculminate in sth (also ˈculminate with sth less frequent) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以…告终；达到…终点<br><span class="en">to end with a particular result or conclusion, or at a particular point</span></td><td class="c4">The negotiations <b>culminated in</b> an agreement acceptable to all sides.<br>谈判最终达成了各方均能接受的协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>curl</b></td><td class="c2"><b>curl ˈup<br>be ˌcurled ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">蜷曲<br><span class="en">to lie down or sit down with your back curved and your knees and arms close to your body</span></td><td class="c4">The cat was <b>Curled up</b> asleep under the bush.<br>猫在灌木下蜷成一团睡觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>curl ˈup<br>be ˌcurled ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">书页；叶子等的边缘卷起；卷曲<br><span class="en">if the edges of pages, leaves, etc. curl up, they bend towards the middle</span></td><td class="c4">The pages had all <b>curled up</b> at the corners.<br>书页的页角都卷起来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>curl sth ˈup<br>ˌcurl yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使蜷曲<br><span class="en">to bend sth/yourself into a tight curved shape</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>curled himself up</b> under the covers and went to sleep.<br>他蜷缩在被子底下睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>curse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcurse sb ˈout (also ˌcuss sb ˈout) <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">咒骂；诅咒<br><span class="en">to swear at sb because you are angry with them</span></td><td class="c4">She came up to me after school and just started <b>cussing me out</b>.<br>放学后她走到我身边开始骂我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>curtain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcurtain sth off (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用帘子把；房间的一部分隔开<br><span class="en">to separate part of a room with a curtain or curtains</span></td><td class="c4">A corner of the room was <b>curtained off</b>.<br>屋子的一角用帘子隔开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>cut</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sth aˈway (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">从…切除；割掉；剪去<br><span class="en">to remove sth by cutting with a knife or a sharp tool</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Cut away</b> any dead branches.<br>把枯枝全砍掉。ˈ。<br>We've had to <b>cut</b> back on staff to save money.<br>为了省钱，我们必须裁员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>cut ˈdown (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">削减；降低(…的数量)<br><span class="en">to reduce the amount or quantity of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Recycling <b>cuts down</b> on waste.<br>废品回收能减少浪费。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>cut ˈdown (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">少用；少买<br><span class="en">to use or buy less of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor's told me to <b>cut down</b> on fatty foods.<br>医生建议我少吃高脂肪食物。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(formal, BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">致…死亡；令…殒命<br><span class="en">to kill sb</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>cut down</b> by pneumonia at an early age.<br>他因肺炎早逝。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sb/sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使当众出丑；使出洋相；使丢人现眼<br><span class="en">to make sb feel or look stupid, especially in front of other people</span></td><td class="c4">He always <b>cuts her down</b> in front of his friends.<br>他总是在他的朋友面前让她难堪。<br>She's always <b>cutting down</b> my lifestyle.<br>她动不动就嘲笑我的生活方式。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">削减；降低(数量)<br><span class="en">to reduce the amount or quantity of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Measures were introduced to <b>cut down</b> the number of road accidents involving children.<br>已采取措施减少涉及儿童的交通事故的发生。<br>The policy aims at <b>cutting down</b> exhaust emissions.<br>这项政策旨在控制废气排放。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">发动机；马达或设备<br><span class="en">of an engine, a motor or a piece of equipment</span></td><td class="c4">If the power fails, the generator will <b>cut in</b>.<br>万一断电，这台发电机就会自动发电。<br>She saw some friends in line and <b>cut in</b> with them.<br>她看见队列里有几个朋友，于是插了进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sb ˈin (on sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">让…參与并分享利润<br><span class="en">to include sb in a deal and give them a share of the profits</span></td><td class="c4">Do you think we can <b>cut Harris in</b> on the deal?<br>你看我们可以让哈里斯加入进来做这笔买卖吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">切入；切开口子<br><span class="en">to make a mark, an opening or a wound in sth with a knife or a sharp object</span></td><td class="c4">Make some pencil guidelines before you <b>cut into</b> the wood.<br>先用铅笔画出标线，再在木头上锯个口子。<br>The rope was <b>cutting into</b> her wrists (= because it was very tight).<br>绳子勒破了她的手腕。<br>The independent stations are <b>cutting into</b> our audience.<br>独立电视台开始与我们争夺观众了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>cut sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">剥夺…的继承权<br><span class="en">to refuse to let sb have any of your money or property after you die</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>cut his son off</b> without a penny.<br>他完全剥夺了儿子的继承权。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">阻碍；阻挡；堵住<br><span class="en">to block or get in the way of sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The police <b>cut off</b> all their escape routes.<br>警方切断了他们所有的逃跑路线。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">发动机或马达突然；熄火；停止运转<br><span class="en">if an engine or a motor cuts out, it suddenly stops working</span></td><td class="c4">One of the aircraft's engines <b>cut out</b>.<br>飞机的一个发动机突然停止运转。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈcut-out n <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">切断电路的断流器；保险装置</td><td class="c4">A <b>cut-out</b> stops the kettle boiling dry.<br>断流器使电水壶不致干烧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut ˈout<br>ˌcut ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">车辆或驾驶员<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or a driver</span></td><td class="c4">Did you see the way the car in front <b>cut out</b>?<br>你看见前面那辆车是怎样猛冲出去的吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使变得不必要<br><span class="en">to make sth unnecessary</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Cut out</b> some of the administration by computerizing your records.<br>用计算机处理记录，减少一些办事手续。<br>The new fast train service <b>cuts out</b> the need for a long bus journey.<br>有了新的高速列车，就不必坐长途汽车了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sth ˈout<br>ˌcut sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…剪下；切下；裁剪<br><span class="en">to remove sth you want from sth larger by cutting; to cut the shape of sth from a piece of material, paper, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Simply <b>cut out</b> and return the coupon.<br>剪下优惠券并寄回即可。<br>She <b>cut the article out</b> of the newspaper.<br>她从报纸上剪下了那篇文章。<br>The children enjoy <b>cutting shapes out</b> of coloured paper.<br>孩子们喜欢用彩纸剪出各种形状。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut sth ˈout<br>ˌcut sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">删减；删节(文字等)<br><span class="en">to leave sth out of a piece of writing, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>cut out</b> the unimportant details.<br>你可以删掉无关紧要的细节文字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">克服(困难)；冲破(阻碍)<br><span class="en">to overcome a difficulty that is preventing you from making</span></td><td class="c4">Once you <b>cut through</b> the technical language the report is easy to understand.<br>你弄通了术语，报告就容易理解了。<br>The yacht <b>cut smoothly through</b> the waves.<br>帆船平稳地破浪前进。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sth ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">开辟穿越…的；小道<br><span class="en">to make a path or passage through sth by cutting</span></td><td class="c4">They had to use their knives to <b>cut a path through</b> the undergrowth.<br>他们不得不用刀在灌木林中劈出一条小路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌcut ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；卖弄；插科打诨<br><span class="en">to behave in a noisy, silly way, especially to try and make people laugh</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>cut up</b> in class.<br>他在班上调皮捣蛋了。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使伤心；使悲痛；使难受<br><span class="en">to make sb very emotionally upset</span></td><td class="c4">She's still very <b>cut up</b> about the divorce.<br>她仍为离婚痛苦不已。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sb/sth ˈup (BrE) (AmE,cut sb/sth ˈoff)</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或驾驶员<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or a driver</span></td><td class="c4">Did you see how he <b>cut me up</b>?<br>你看见他怎么抢我的道了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>cut sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">切碎；剁碎；剪碎<br><span class="en">to divide sth into small pieces with a knife or a sharp tool</span></td><td class="c4">Who's going to <b>cut up</b> the vegetables?<br>谁来切蔬菜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dab</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdab at sth (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用…轻触；轻搽；轻拍(尤指脸部)<br><span class="en">to touch sth, especially your face, several times, quickly and lightly</span></td><td class="c4">She was crying and <b>dabbing at</b> her eyes with a handkerchief.<br>她边哭边用手绢轻轻擦眼睛。<br>He gently <b>dabbed at</b> his cuts with a piece of cotton wool.<br>他用一块药棉轻轻按了按伤口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdab sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">轻快地擦掉；抹掉(水渍等)<br><span class="en">to remove sth such as a mark caused by a liquid with quick, light move. ments</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Dab the coffee off</b> with your handkerchief.<br>用手帕擦去咖啡污渍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdab sth ˈon (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用…轻涂；轻敷<br><span class="en">to put sth on a surface with quick, light movements</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Dab the paint on</b> with a sponge.<br>用海绵轻轻涂上颜料。<br>She <b>dabbed on</b> a little perfume.<br>她轻轻地搽了一点香水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dabble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdabble in sth</b></td><td class="c3">涉足；涉猎；尝试(活动或体育运动)<br><span class="en">to take part in an activity or a sport, but not very seriously</span></td><td class="c4">She swims twice a week and has been <b>dabbling in</b> weight training.<br>她每周游泳两次，偶尔还练一下举重。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dam</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdam sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">筑坝拦(河水)<br><span class="en">to stop the water flowing in a river by building a dam across it</span></td><td class="c4">The stream was <b>dammed up</b> to form ornamental lakes.<br>小河上建坝蓄水，形成了装饰性的湖泊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>damp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>damp sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使(火)减弱；熄灭<br><span class="en">to make a fire burn more slowly or stop burning</span></td><td class="c4">Firefighters were <b>damping down</b> the embers hours later.<br>几小时后，消防队员基本扑灭了余烬。<br>He put sand on the fire to try to <b>damp it down</b>.<br>他试图用沙子把火压灭。<br>The fire had been <b>damped down</b> but not extinguished.<br>火势得到了控制，但尚未熄灭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dangle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdangle sth beˈfore sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">用…引诱；利用…吊某人胃口<br><span class="en">to offer sb sth very attractive to try to persuade them to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">It's the biggest financial incentive ever <b>dangled before</b> British footballers.<br>这是对英国足球运动员前所未有的最大经济诱惑。可用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>dash aˈround (also ˌdash aˈbout/ˈround especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">四处奔忙；到处奔波<br><span class="en">to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy</span></td><td class="c4">At the scene of the accident, people were <b>dashing</b> <b>about</b> all over the place.<br>在事故现场，人们急匆匆地来回奔忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>date</b></td><td class="c2"><b>date ˈback (also ˌdate ˈback to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">追溯到；起始于</td><td class="c4">It's a tradition that <b>dates back</b> at least a thousand years.<br>这一传统至少可以追溯到一千年前。<br>Her problems <b>date back</b> to her childhood.<br>她的这些问题从小就有了。<br>The town <b>dates back</b> to Roman times.<br>这座城镇始建于古罗马时代。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdate from sth</b></td><td class="c3">自…至今；从…开始<br><span class="en">to have existed since a particular time in the past</span></td><td class="c4">It is a beautiful vase <b>dating from</b> about 1715.<br>这是一个漂亮的花瓶，大约制作于 1715年。<br>The strike was the latest stage in a dispute which <b>dated from</b> 2004.<br>这次罢工是始自2004年的纠纷发展到最新阶段的结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dawn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdawn on sb also ˈdawn upon sb more formal</b></td><td class="c3">使开始明白；使开始理解；使渐渐领悟<br><span class="en">if an idea, the truth or a fact dawns on you, you realize it for the first time</span></td><td class="c4">It suddenly <b>dawned</b> on us that we were lost.<br>我们突然意识到我们迷路了。<br>The answer finally <b>dawned</b> on me.<br>我最终找到了答案。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>deal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdeal sb ˈin <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">让…加入(活动)；把…算入<br><span class="en">to include sb in an activity</span></td><td class="c4">It sounds like a great plan! <b>Deal me in</b>!<br>这计划听上去很棒！算我一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>deal sb out<br>ˌdeal sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不让…加入(活动)；不把…算入<br><span class="en">to not include sb in an activity</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>deal me out</b> of this. I don't want to get involved in anything illegal.<br>你不要把我算在内。我不想卷入任何违法的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdeal sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把…分发(给…)<br><span class="en">to share sth among a number of people, groups of people or organizations</span></td><td class="c4">Well <b>deal out</b> the proceeds to several charities.<br>我们将把收益分贈给几个慈善机构。<br>Severe penalties are <b>dealt out</b> to persistent offenders.<br>惯犯会受到严惩。<br>They're very difficult people to <b>deal</b> with.<br>他们这些人很难缠。<br>We have to <b>deal</b> with students and handle a load of Paperwork as well.<br>我们必须接待学生，同时还得完成大量案头工作。<br>Most patients are <b>dealt</b> with within four weeks.<br>大多数病人可在四周内得到治疗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdeal sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">整治；惩处<br><span class="en">to take appropriate action to punish sb who has done sth wrong</span></td><td class="c4">Your father will <b>deal</b> with you when he gets home.<br>你爸爸回家后会收拾你的。<br>Athletes found guilty of taking drugs were swiftly <b>dealt</b> with.<br>被检测出服用禁药的运动员立刻受到了处罚。<br>It is best to <b>deal</b> directly with foreign suppliers.<br>最好和国外供应商直接交易。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdeal with sth</b></td><td class="c3">解决；应付；处理<br><span class="en">to solve a problem, carry out a task, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The next programme <b>deals with</b> the subject of divorce.<br>下个节目将讨论离婚这一话题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>debar</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈbar sb from sth<br>deˈbar sb from doing sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">阻止<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from sth, joining an organization, going somewhere, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Students who have not paid their fees will be <b>debarred from</b> taking examinations.<br>未交费的学生将不得参加考试。<br>He was <b>debarred from</b> holding public office.<br>他被禁止担任公职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>deck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdeck sb ˈout<br>ˌdeck yourself ˈout (in/as/like sth)</b></td><td class="c3">通常为特定场合穿戴；打扮；穿着；戴着<br><span class="en">to put on interesting and brightly coloured clothes or jewellery, usually for a special occasion</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>decked himself out</b> in his best suit.<br>他穿上了自己最好的那套西裝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>declare</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈclare for sb/sth <span class="tag">(BrE formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">宣布支持；声明赞成<br><span class="en">to say publicly that you support sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Otto the Bald <b>declared for</b> the Emperor.<br>秃头奥托公开表态支持皇帝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈclare for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">政客宣布参选<br><span class="en">(of a politician) to announce that you will take part in an election for a particular office</span></td><td class="c4">Yesterday she <b>declared for</b> Governor in a press conference.<br>昨天在记者招待会上，她宣布参加州长竞选。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈclare for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">运动员宣布参加(选秀)<br><span class="en">(of a sports player) to announce that you will take part in the system by which teams choose players from a ranked group (the draft)</span></td><td class="c4">He's been thinking about <b>declaring for</b> the draft since last year.<br>自去年起，他一直在考虑宣布参。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dedicate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdedicate sth to sb</b></td><td class="c3">在作品开头把…题献给…<br><span class="en">to say at the beginning of a book, a piece of music or a performance that you are doing it for sb, as a way of thanking them or showing respect</span></td><td class="c4">This book is <b>dedicated to</b> my parents.<br>谨以此书献给我的父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdedicate yourself/sth to sth<br>ˈdedicate yourself/sth to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">把时间；精力等用于；投身于<br><span class="en">to give a lot of your time and effort to a particular activity or purpose because you think it is important</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dedicates</b> herself to her work.<br>她全身心投入工作。<br>He <b>dedicated</b> his life to helping the poor.<br>他毕生致力于帮助穷人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>defer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈfer to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">依从；顺从<br><span class="en">rather formal to accept sb's opinion or do what they suggest because you respect them</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>defer to</b> your judgement in these matters.<br>我尊重你对这些事的判断。<br>We are happy to <b>defer to</b> the committee's wishes.<br>我们乐于遵从委员会的意愿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>deliver</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈliver on sth</b></td><td class="c3">履行(诺言)；实施(威胁)；践约<br><span class="en">if you deliver on a promise, a threat or an agreement, you do what you have said you would do, or what you are expected to do</span></td><td class="c4">Can he be trusted to <b>deliver on</b> his promises?<br>能相信他会信守诺言吗。<br>They failed to <b>deliver on</b> the agreement.<br>他们违背了协议。p时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>delve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdelve ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">追究；探究；追查<br><span class="en">to try hard to find out more information about sth</span></td><td class="c4">We should not <b>delve too deeply into</b> this painful matter.<br>我们不应该过分深究这件令人痛苦的事。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>depart</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈpart from sth</b></td><td class="c3">违反；背离；不合(常规)<br><span class="en">to behave in a way that is different from what is usual or expected</span></td><td class="c4">The teachers are not encouraged to <b>depart from</b> the syllabus.<br>教师最好不要偏离教学大纲。<br>They <b>departed from</b> tradition and got married in a hotel.<br>他们突破传统，在旅馆结了婚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>deprive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈprive sb/sth/yourself of sth</b></td><td class="c3">剥夺；使丧失；使不能；享受<br><span class="en">to prevent sb/sth from having sth important; to take sth away from sb</span></td><td class="c4">In prison they were starved and <b>deprived</b> of sleep.<br>在狱中，他们忍饥挨饿，而且睡眠不足。<br>The baby's brain had been <b>deprived</b> of oxygen during the birth.<br>这个婴儿出生时大脑敏氧。<br>There is no need to <b>deprive yourself of</b> food on this diet.<br>按照这个规定饮食不必禁食。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>derive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈrive sth from sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…衍生；起源于；源自<br><span class="en">to come or develop from sth</span></td><td class="c4">Washington <b>derives its name from</b> the first president.<br>华盛顿得名于美国首任总统。<br>The name of the mountain appears to be <b>derived from</b> an old Norse word.<br>这座山的名称似乎是源于一个古挪威词。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>descend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be desˈcended from sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">是…的后裔<br><span class="en">to be related to sb who lived a long time ago</span></td><td class="c4">He Claimed he <b>was descended from</b> the Vikings.<br>他声称自己是维京人的后代。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>desˈcend into sth</b></td><td class="c3">陷入(糟糕的境地)<br><span class="en">to get into a very bad condition or state</span></td><td class="c4">The situation has <b>descended into</b> total chaos.<br>局面变得一片混乱。<br>There were fears that the country was <b>descending into</b> turmoil or even civil war.<br>人们担心国家会逐渐陷入动乱，甚至会爆发内战。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>desˈcend on sb/sth also desˈcend upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">突然涌到；大批到达<br><span class="en">to arrive somewhere, especially suddenly and unexpectedly and in large numbers</span></td><td class="c4">Dozens of police <b>descended</b> on the building.<br>数十名警察突然进入这座大楼。<br>A large woman in a hat was <b>descending</b> on them.<br>一个戴帽子的高大女人向他们冲过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>desˈcend to sth</b></td><td class="c3">降低身份去；竟做出；堕落到…地步<br><span class="en">to do or say sth that makes people lose their respect for you</span></td><td class="c4">If you insult him back, you <b>descend to</b> his level.<br>你要是反过去侮辱他，就是跟他一般见识了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>detract</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈtract from sth not</b></td><td class="c3">通常不用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">These revelations should not <b>detract</b> from his achievements.<br>不应该因这些被揭露的内幕而贬低他的成就。<br>Her tattered clothes in no way <b>detracted</b> from her beauty.<br>破衣烂衫丝毫无损她的美貌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>devolve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈvolve on/to/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">工作；职责；权力或责任<br><span class="en">of work, duties, power or responsibility</span></td><td class="c4">All the responsibility has <b>devolved upon</b> him.<br>所有责任都落到了他肩上。<br>Additional powers will <b>devolve to</b> the regional governments.<br>将向地方政府下放更多的权力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈvolve sth to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">将工作；职责；权力或责任交给；移交(下属或下层)<br><span class="en">to give work, duties, power or responsibility to sb with less authority than you</span></td><td class="c4">More powers are gradually being <b>devolved to</b> the regions.<br>正逐步向地方下放更多的权力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>devote</b></td><td class="c2"><b>deˈvote yourself to sb/sth deˈvote yourself to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">投身于；致力于；专心于<br><span class="en">to spend a large part of your time, energy and attention on a particular activity, especially sth good</span></td><td class="c4">After her marriage, she couldn't <b>devote</b> herself totally to her music.<br>她婚后无法全身心投入音乐事业。<br>They had <b>devoted</b> themselves entirely to building up their business.<br>当时他们一心一意想把自己的企业做大做强。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>diddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diddle aˈround <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">虚度光阴；无所事事；混日子<br><span class="en">to spend your time doing things that are not important</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>diddling around</b> and do some work!<br>别晃悠了，干点正。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>die</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdie ˈback (also ˌdie ˈdown)</b></td><td class="c3">枝叶枯萎(根部仍存活)<br><span class="en">if a plant dies back, its leaves die, although the roots are still alive</span></td><td class="c4">The leaves <b>die back</b> in winter.<br>叶子到冬天就枯萎了。<br>The fire had <b>died down</b> by the morning.<br>到早晨，火就慢慢熄灭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>die ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">相继死去；先后；死去<br><span class="en">if a group of people or animals die oft, they die one by one over a short period of time until there are none left</span></td><td class="c4">The survivors are dying <b>off</b> daily.<br>幸存者正在一天天地相继去世。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>die ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">家族；种族；物种等逐渐消亡；死光；灭绝<br><span class="en">if a family, race, type of animal, etc. dies out, there are no longer any members left alive</span></td><td class="c4">There are several theories about why dinosaurs <b>died out</b> so suddenly.<br>关于恐龙为何突然灭绝，有几种说法。<br>Many plants and animals are in danger of dying <b>out</b>.<br>很多动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dig</b></td><td class="c2"><b>dig ˈin<br>.dig ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始吃；开吃<br><span class="en">to begin to eat</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Dig in</b> while it's hot!<br>趁热吃吧。<br>As soon as the food arrived he <b>dug in</b> hungrily.<br>食物一端来，他便狼吞虎咽地吃起来。<br>They <b>dug into</b> the pizza hungrily.<br>他们风卷残云股吃起比萨饼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>dig ˈin<br>.dig ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始认真对待；大干起来<br><span class="en">to begin to do sth in a way that shows that you are determined to continue or finish it, even if it is difficult</span></td><td class="c4">He looked at the stack of work and <b>dug in</b> straight away.<br>他看了看堆积如山的工作，便立即埋头干了起来。<br>She <b>dug into</b> the reports and finished them before the meeting.<br>她全力以赴开始读报告，在开会前读完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>dig ˈin<br>ˌdig yourself ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">掘壕固守；挖掩体隐蔽<br><span class="en">to make a safe place for yourself in the ground and prepare for the enemy to attack</span></td><td class="c4">The troops <b>dug in</b> and organized their defences.<br>部队挖掘掩体并组织防守。<br>The marines were <b>dug in</b> on the front line.<br>海军陆战队士兵在前线挖战壕隐蔽起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>dig sb/sth ˈout ˌdig sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中挖掘出<br><span class="en">to get sb/sth out of a place by digging the ground around them/it</span></td><td class="c4">It took them three hours to <b>dig</b> him <b>out</b> of the rubble.<br>他们花了三个小时才从瓦砾中把他挖出来。<br>The car was buried in snow and had to be <b>dug</b> <b>out</b>.<br>汽车被雪埋住了，只好挖出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdig sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指在建筑物等；前开掘；平整(土地)<br><span class="en">to break the ground into small pieces, especially before building sth, taking sth from underneath it, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Some Roman remains were found under a car park which was being <b>dug up</b>.<br>一处正在开挖的停车场下面发现了一些古罗马遗迹。四。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dine</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdine on sth</b></td><td class="c3">吃(某种食物)<br><span class="en">to eat a particular type of food</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>dined on</b> freshly caught fish in a floating restaurant.<br>我们在一家水上饭店品尝了刚捕到的鱼。<br>They <b>dined on</b> a bland diet of soup and bread.<br>他们饮食清淡，只吃汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdine ˈout on sth <span class="tag">(BrE, humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为了炫耀讲述(亲身经历)<br><span class="en">to tell people of sth that has happened to you in order to impress them</span></td><td class="c4">She only actually said one sentence to Brad Pitt but she <b>dined out on</b> it for years.<br>实际上她和布拉德•皮特只说过一句话，但是多年来她一直把这事儿挂在嘴上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>dink aˈround <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">混日子；无所事事；游手好闲<br><span class="en">to waste time doing unimportant things and not get very much done</span></td><td class="c4">They came home from war to find all ther friends <b>dinking around</b> and going nowhere.<br>他们从战场归来，发现所有朋友都在混日子，不思进取。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdip sth ˈin/into sth<br>ˌdip sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">飞快地把…放入(液体)又取出；用…浸一浸<br><span class="en">to put sth very quickly into a liquid and take it out again</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dipped her toes cautiously into</b> the sea.<br>她小心翼翼地用脚趾试了试海水。<br>The fruit had been <b>dipped in</b> chocolate.<br>水果蘸丁巧克力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdip ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">草草翻阅；稍加浏览<br><span class="en">to read or watch only small parts of a book, magazine, programme, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The continuous news services are intended for people to <b>dip into</b>.<br>不问断的新闻报道是为了便于人们随时瞅上几眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>disagree</b></td><td class="c2"><b>disaˈgree with sth<br>disaˈgree with doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">不赞成；反对<br><span class="en">to disapprove of sth and think it is bad or wrong</span></td><td class="c4">We totally <b>disagree with</b> the ban on fox hunting.<br>我们完全不赞同猎狐禁令。<br>She <b>disagrees with</b> keeping animals locked up in cages.<br>她反对把动物锁在笼子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dish</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdish sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">广泛发出；大量发出<br><span class="en">to give sth out to large numbers of people or in large amounts</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>dishing out</b> advice to people.<br>他总是好为人师。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdish sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把(食物)分到盘里<br><span class="en">to serve food to sb by putting it on plates</span></td><td class="c4">He's busy <b>dishing out</b> the dinner.<br>他忙着给大家分晚饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>mom,dish it ˈout <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">批评；攻击<br><span class="en">to criticize sb or attack them</span></td><td class="c4">He was good at dishing it <b>out</b>. It was time he learned what it felt like.<br>他就知道指责别人。这下该轮到他来尝尝这个滋味了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dispense</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diˈspense with sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">摈弃；省却<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth; to stop using sb/sth because they are/it is no longer necessary</span></td><td class="c4">The programme <b>dispensed with</b> its most popular presenter.<br>这个节目最受欢迎的主持人被撤掉了。<br>His services can now be <b>dispensed with</b>.<br>现在可以不用他帮忙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dispose</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diˈspose of sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打发走某人；处理；掉某物<br><span class="en">to get rid of safely disposed of sb/sth that you do not want</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>dispose of</b> the evidence.<br>她试图销毁证据。<br>They decided to <b>dispose of much of</b> their property.<br>他们决定卖掉大部分财产。<br>Ensure that all the waste is properly and safely <b>disposed of</b>.<br>一定要确保所有废料得到安全妥善的处理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dissolve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>disˈsolve into sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然大笑起来；大哭起来<br><span class="en">to suddenly start to laugh or cry</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>dissolved into</b> fits of laughter.<br>他们不禁哄笑起来。<br>I <b>dissolved into</b> giggles.<br>我情不自禁地咯咯笑了。<br>When I mentioned his name, she <b>dissolved into</b> tears.<br>我提起他的名字，她不禁潸然泪下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>dive ˈin dive ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">不假思索地全情投入；全力以赴<br><span class="en">to start doing sth with enthusiasm and without stopping to think</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dived</b> in with a question before I had finished speaking.<br>我话还没讲完，她便迫不及待地提了个问题。<br>They had <b>dived</b> <b>into</b> the new business without thinking it through.<br>未经慎重考虑，他们就投身办起了新企业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>dive ˈin dive ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">大吃起来<br><span class="en">to start eating with enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">As soon as the food was served, she <b>dived</b> in.<br>食物一端上来，她就大口大口地吃了起来。四时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>divest</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diˈvest yourself of sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">抛弃；处置(不要或无用的东西)<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth you no longer want or that is no longer useful</span></td><td class="c4">She managed to <b>divest herself of</b> the unwanted property.<br>她设法处理掉了那件不需要的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>divide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diˈvide sth into sth</b></td><td class="c3">用(一数)除(另一数)<br><span class="en">if you divide a number into another number, you find out how many times the first number is contained in the second</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>divide 300 into</b> 1270?<br>用300 除1270,你知道得几吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>divorce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>diˈvorce sb/sth from sth</b></td><td class="c3">使人；思想；主题；等与…分离；保持…与…分开<br><span class="en">to separate a person, an idea, a subject, etc. from sth; to keep two things separate</span></td><td class="c4">They believed that art should be <b>divorced from</b> politics.<br>他们认为艺术应该脱离政治。<br>When he was depressed, he felt utterly <b>divorced from</b> reality.<br>心情沮丧时，他感到完全脱离了现实。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>divvy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdivvy sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">分担；分享(尤指金钱)<br><span class="en">to divide or share sth, especially money, between a number of people</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>divvied up</b> the bill.<br>他们分摊了账单费用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>do</b></td><td class="c2"><b>do aˈway with sb/yourself <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">杀死；除掉(某人)；自杀<br><span class="en">to kill sb/yourself</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to do <b>away</b> with herself.<br>她企图自杀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do aˈway with sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">废除；除去；结束<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth; to stop doing or having sth</span></td><td class="c4">They've <b>done away with</b> the uniform at our school.<br>我们学校取消了校服。<br>A lot of the paperwork could easily be <b>done away with</b>.<br>许多文案工作不难削减。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do sb ˈdown<br>ˌdo yourself ˈdown <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">贬低某人；贬低自己<br><span class="en">to criticize sb or yourself in a way that makes them/you appear more stupid or less able than they/you really are</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>do him down</b>, he's a good worker.<br>别贬损他，他干活挺好。<br>She's always <b>doing herself down</b>.<br>她总是自我贬低。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdo for sb/sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">毁掉；破坏(某物)；伤害；杀死(某人)<br><span class="en">to damage or destroy sth; to injure or kill sb; to put sb/sth in a situation so bad that they/it have no chance of returning to normal</span></td><td class="c4">The last bout of Pneumonia nearly <b>did for</b> her.<br>上次肺炎发作差点要了她的命。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdone for adi <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">麻烦很大；十分危险；彻底完蛋<br><span class="en">in serious trouble or danger; having no chance of succeeding at sth</span></td><td class="c4">After three days trapped in the cave they thought they were <b>done</b> for (= they thought they would die).<br>在洞里困了三天后，他们觉得求生无望了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdo sb ˈin <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使筋疲力尽；使极度疲乏<br><span class="en">if sth does you in, it makes you feel extremely tired</span></td><td class="c4">That's <b>done me in</b>, lifting all those boxes.<br>搬完那些箱子后，我都累垮了。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(身体某部位)受伤<br><span class="en">to injure a part of your body</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>did his back in</b> playing tennis.<br>他打网球伤了腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打扫；油漆；装饰(房屋等)<br><span class="en">to clean or paint and decorate a room, a house, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>done the whole house out</b> in yellows and greens.<br>他把房子全刷成了黄色和绿色。<br>They had the hall <b>done out</b> in striped wallpaper.<br>他们在大厅贴了条纹墙纸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用不止；当手段阻止某人获得；剥夺<br><span class="en">to prevent Sb from getting or keeping sth they ought to have, in an unfair or dishonest way</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>do me out of</b> my inheritance.<br>她企图阻止我继承进产。<br>The residents of the home have been <b>done out of a lot of</b> money.<br>居住在这里的人被卷走了很多钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>do sb ˈover <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">暴打；毒打；狠揍<br><span class="en">to attack sb and beat them severely</span></td><td class="c4">They threatened to <b>do her over</b> if she didn't pay.<br>他们威胁说，如果她不交钱就揍她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>do sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">包起来；捆起来；包裹(在…里面)<br><span class="en">(in sth) to make sth into a package</span></td><td class="c4">She was carrying some books <b>done up</b> in brown Paper.<br>她拿着用牛皮纸包着的几本书。<br>We're having the kitchen <b>done up</b>.<br>我们在整修厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdo with sb/sth be/have ˈdone with it</b></td><td class="c3">尤指尽快了结；了断<br><span class="en">to finish dealing with sth unpleasant, especially as quickly as possible</span></td><td class="c4">Just tear up the contract and be <b>done</b> with it.<br>干脆把合同撕掉了事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdo sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">与否定词连用；或用于疑问句把…放在<br><span class="en">used with negatives and in questions to talk about where sb has put sth</span></td><td class="c4">What have you <b>done with</b> my shoes?<br>你把我的鞋搁哪儿了。<br>I haven't <b>done anything with</b> your keys (= I haven't moved them).<br>我根本没动过你的钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dob</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdob sb ˈin (to sb) <span class="tag">(BrE AustralE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向…揭发；检举<br><span class="en">to tell sb about sth bad that another person has done</span></td><td class="c4">Kay wasn't sure who had <b>dobbed her in</b> to the teachers.<br>凯拿不准是谁向老师告了她一状。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dole</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdole sth ˈout (to sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给…分发；发放钱款；食物等<br><span class="en">to give money, food, etc. to a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">She quickly <b>doled out</b> the food.<br>她很快把食物发完了。<br>The money was <b>doled out</b> to them on a weekly basis.<br>每周给他们发一次钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>doll</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌdolled ˈup (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">梳妆打扮</td><td class="c4">She <b>was all dolled up</b> in a black dress and pearls.<br>她着实打扮了一番，穿了一件黑色连衣裙，还佩戴着珍珠饰品。<br>I <b>got dolled up</b> for the party.<br>我打扮好了要去参加聚会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>doss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdoss aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">混日子；游手好闲；无所事事<br><span class="en">to spend your time doing nothing or very little</span></td><td class="c4">Everyone <b>dosses about</b> in geography classes.<br>上地理课时大冢都不当回事儿。<br>He just <b>dossed around</b> for a year before he got a job.<br>他晃荡了一年才找了份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>doss ˈdown <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在地板等；不舒适的地方将就着睡<br><span class="en">to sleep on the floor or somewhere uncomfortable because you have nowhere else to sleep</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>dossed down</b> on Tony's floor after the party.<br>聚会后，我们凑合着睡在托尼冢的地板上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be dotted a bout/aˈround<br>be ˌdotted aˈbout/aˈround sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">散落；分布(在…)</td><td class="c4">A few farms <b>were dotted about</b> in the valley.<br>峡谷中零星地散布着几个衣场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdot A on/over B<br>ˈdot B with A</b></td><td class="c3">把…撒在…上；在…上撒…<br><span class="en">to spread very small amounts of sth in different places on a surface</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Dot</b> the suncream on your face in tiny quantities and rub it in well.<br>在脸上搽少量防晒箱，然后揉匀。<br><b>Dot</b> the top of the cake with small sweets.<br>在蛋糕上面撒些糖粒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈdotted with sth</b></td><td class="c3">散布着；…星罗棋布<br><span class="en">if an area is dotted with things or people, they are spread around in several places</span></td><td class="c4">The hillside <b>was dotted with</b> houses.<br>山坡上到处是住宅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dote</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdote on sb (also ˈdote upon sb more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">溺爱；过分喜爱<br><span class="en">to feel or show very great love for sb and ignore their faults</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>dote on</b> their daughter.<br>他们对女儿宠爱有加。<br>He was <b>doted on</b> (by his sisters).<br>他受到(姐妹们的)宠爱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>double</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdouble as sth<br>ˌdouble ˈup as sth</b></td><td class="c3">兼任；兼作<br><span class="en">to have a second function in addition to the main use</span></td><td class="c4">The garage <b>doubles as</b> his workshop.<br>车库同时又充作他的工作间。<br>The school secretary <b>doubled up as</b> the nurse.<br>学校秘书兼任护士。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>double ˈback (on yourself, itself, etc.)</b></td><td class="c3">折回；往回走<br><span class="en">to turn around and go back in the direction you have come from</span></td><td class="c4">The road ahead was flooded so we had to <b>double back</b> to find another way around.<br>前面的路被水淹了，我们只好原路返回，再找条路绕过去。<br>The line of trees <b>doubles back</b> on itself at a bend in the river.<br>那排树在河道拐弯处折了回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>double ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">与另一人合用；同享<br><span class="en">(with sb/on sth) to form pairs in order to share sth</span></td><td class="c4">Weve only got one room left; youll have to <b>double up</b> with Peter.<br>我们只剩下一个房间，你只好与彼得合住了。<br>There were enough guitarists to <b>double up</b> on parts (= two played each part).<br>吉他手足够两人一组分别演奏乐曲的不同声部。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>double ˈup/over (in/with sth)<br>ˌdouble sb ˈup/ˈover (in/with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">因疼痛等(使)弓背；弯腰<br><span class="en">to bend your body suddenly or quickly because you are in pain, for example; to make sb bend their body in</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>doubled</b> up in/with pain.<br>他痛得蜷起身子。<br>She <b>doubled</b> up with laughter.<br>她笑弯了腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>doze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdoze ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">尤指白天打瞌睡；打盹儿<br><span class="en">to go to sleep, especially during the day</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>dozed off</b> during the film.<br>他看电影时打起盹儿来。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>draft</b></td><td class="c2"><b>draft sb ˈin<br>ˌdraft sb ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">选派；调遣(去某处执行特殊任务)<br><span class="en">to choose people and send them somewhere for a task</span></td><td class="c4">Extra police are being <b>drafted in</b> to control the crowds.<br>当局正在额外抽调警察去控。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>drag sb/sth/yourself aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使勉强离开(或停止…)<br><span class="en">to make sb or yourself stop doing sth when they/you do not really want to</span></td><td class="c4">She was enjoying herself at the party so much, I couldn't <b>drag</b> her <b>away</b>.<br>她在聚会上玩得兴高采烈，我没法拉她走。<br>He couldnit <b>drag</b> his eyes <b>away</b> from her face.<br>他无法把目光从她脸上移开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使降格；使品德；地位等下降(到…)<br><span class="en">(to sth) to bring sb down to a lower standard of behaviour, or a lower social or economic level</span></td><td class="c4">I'm worried .the other children will be <b>dragged down</b> to his level (= because his behaviour is so bad).<br>我担心其他孩子会跟他学坏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sb/sth ˈin<br>ˌdrag sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…牵扯在内；把…卷进困境；把…拖下水；连累<br><span class="en">to make sb or sth become involved in a difficult or unpleasant situation when they do not want to be involved</span></td><td class="c4">When violence breaks out in the streets, innocent people are always <b>dragged in</b>.<br>街头暴力总会映及无辜。<br>Don't <b>drag me into</b> your argument!<br>别把我卷入你们的争论。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sb ˈoff (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">强行带走某人(到…)<br><span class="en">to take sb somewhere by force</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>dragged off</b> to the head teacher's offrice.<br>我被拽到校长室。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag ˈon <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">进展缓慢；拖得过久<br><span class="en">to progress very slowly and take too long</span></td><td class="c4">The day <b>dragged on</b> interminably.<br>白天漫长难挨，似乎没个完。<br>Negotiations between the two sides <b>dragged on</b> through the summer.<br>双方的谈判拖了一个夏天。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不必要地拖延；使持续过久<br><span class="en">to make sth last longer than it should</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dragged the meeting out</b> for as long as possible.<br>她尽可能地把会议时间拉长。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sth ˈout of sb</b></td><td class="c3">强迫…说出；套…的话<br><span class="en">to make sb give you information they do not want to give you</span></td><td class="c4">They eventually <b>dragged a confession out of</b> her.<br>他们终于逼迫她招了供。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrag sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">提起(别人不愿回忆的事)<br><span class="en">to mention in a conversation an unpleasant fact from the past that sb would prefer to forget</span></td><td class="c4">It all happened years ago. There's no point <b>dragging it up</b> now.<br>那都是些陈年旧事了。现在不提也罢。<br>She's <b>dragged up</b> that story just to embarrass me.<br>她抖出那件事就是为了使我难堪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dragoon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>draˈgoon sb into sth, draˈgoon sb into doing sth <span class="tag">(formal or humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">强迫某人做某事<br><span class="en">to force sb to do sth that they do not want to do</span></td><td class="c4">We were <b>dragooned</b> <b>into</b> the football team.<br>我们迫不得已参加了足球队。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>drain aˈway/off<br>drain sth aˈway/ˈoff (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">流走；使(从…)流走<br><span class="en">if a liquid drains away/off, or sb drains it away/off, it flows away</span></td><td class="c4">The water <b>drained away</b> down the plughole.<br>水经出水孔排走了。<br>I <b>drained the water away</b> and hung up the blouse to dry.<br>我放掉水，把衬衫挂起来晾干。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>draw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>draw ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">尤指因害怕退缩；后退；畏避<br><span class="en">to move away from sb/sth, especially sb/sth that makes you</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>drew back</b> from the window in case anyone saw her.<br>她从窗口缩回，免得被人看见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>draw sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">减少；消耗(尤指钱款)<br><span class="en">to reduce the amount of sth, especially money, by using it and spending it</span></td><td class="c4">Higher production costs will <b>draw down</b> cash gains from rising farm prices.<br>生产成本上升会减少农产品涨价带来的现金收益。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdraw sth from sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中获得<br><span class="en">to get sth from a particular source</span></td><td class="c4">Many artists and poets have <b>drawn their inspiration from</b> the landscape.<br>众多艺术家和诗人从自然风光中取灵感。<br>At times of crisis, we <b>drew strength from</b> each other.<br>危难时刻我们彼此鼓劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>draw ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The nights are <b>drawing in</b> fast now.<br>天黑得越来越早了。<br>It was the end of September and the days had begun to <b>draw in</b>.<br>当时是九月末，白天开始变短了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>draw ˈin<br>ˌdraw ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">列车到站；进站停靠<br><span class="en">if a train draws in, or draws into a station, it slowly enters a station and stops at the platform</span></td><td class="c4">The London train <b>drew in</b> late.<br>发自伦敦的列车到站时晚点了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">深吸；迅速吸入(一口气)<br><span class="en">if you draw in a breath, you breathe deeply or quickly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>drew in</b> a deep breath at the magical sight of the city below.<br>她俯视迷人的城市景色，不禁深深地吸了一口气。<br>He <b>drew in</b> his breath sharply.<br>他猛吸了一口气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">抽出；排掉(液体)<br><span class="en">to remove some liquid from a larger amount</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>drew off</b> a glass of beer.<br>他倒了一杯啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>draw ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">时光或季节<br><span class="en">of a time or a season</span></td><td class="c4">As night <b>drew on</b>, it became clear he wasn't coming.<br>夜渐深了，显然他是不会来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">After March the evenings started <b>drawing out</b>.<br>三月过后，夜晚开始来得迟了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw ˈout<br>draw ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">列车离站；出站<br><span class="en">if a train draws out or draws out of a station, it begins to move and slowly leaves the station</span></td><td class="c4">I arrived in time to see the train <b>drawing out</b>.<br>我赶到时正好看到火车徐徐离站。<br>The train <b>drew slowly out</b> of the station.<br>火车缓缓开出车站。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">拖延；拉长会议；活动等<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a meeting or an event last longer than usual or longer than it should</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>drew the interview out</b> to over an hour.<br>他们拖拖沓沓面试了一个多小时。<br>The process is likely to be <b>drawn out</b> over several months.<br>这一过程有可能拖几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>draw sth ˈout<br>ˌdraw sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从银行；账户取(钱),提(款)<br><span class="en">to take money out of a bank account</span></td><td class="c4">How much money did you <b>draw out</b>?<br>你取了多少钱。<br>Several thousand pounds had been <b>drawn out</b> of the account.<br>有几千英镑从这个账户提走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw ˈup<br>ˌdraw sth/sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使停下；停止<br><span class="en">to come to a stop; to make sth/sb/yourself stop</span></td><td class="c4">A taxi <b>drew up</b> outside.<br>出租车在外面停了下来。<br>He <b>drew the car up</b> at the front door.<br>他把车停在前门。<br>He was walking towards the door when a loud knock <b>drew him up</b> sharply.<br>他朝门走去，响亮的敲门声令他猛地收住脚步。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdraw sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">拟就；草拟<br><span class="en">to make or write sth that needs careful planning</span></td><td class="c4">My solicitor is <b>drawing up</b> the contract.<br>我的律师正在起草合同。<br>Clear guidelines need to be <b>drawn up</b>.<br>需要拟订明确的指导方针。<br>Weve <b>drawn up</b> a plan of action.<br>我们制订了行动计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dream</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdream sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">因幻想；而虚度(光阴)<br><span class="en">to spend time in a lazy way, thinking about things you would like to do but not actually doing anything</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dreamt her life away</b>, never really achieving anything.<br>她一辈子都在想入非非，到头来一事无成。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdream of sth</b></td><td class="c3">渴望；向往；梦想<br><span class="en">to imagine and think about sth that you would like to happen</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>dreams of</b> running her own business.<br>她梦想自己当老板。<br>It was the kind of trip most of us only <b>dream</b> about.<br>这是我们大多数人只能梦想的旅行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdream ˈon <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">痴心妄想<br><span class="en">to tell sb that you are certain that what they have just said will not happen</span></td><td class="c4">You want a pay rise?<b>Dream on</b>!<br>你想加薪？白日做梦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>dream sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">凭空想出；虚构出尤指不切实际的计划；想法等<br><span class="en">to have an idea or think of a plan, especially one that is not very practical</span></td><td class="c4">The scheme was <b>dreamed up</b> by a local businessman.<br>这个计划是一个当地商人异想天开弄出来的。<br>Trust you to <b>dream up</b> a crazy idea like this!<br>你这个人就是会想出这种荒唐的主意来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dredge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdredge sth ˈup <span class="tag">(usually disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">重提(令人不快的往事)<br><span class="en">to mention sth that sb has forgotten or wants to forget because it is unpleasant or embarrassing</span></td><td class="c4">She always <b>dredges up</b> that embarrassing story.<br>她老是翻出那件令人尴尬的事。<br>He managed to <b>dredge up</b> a smile.<br>他勉强挤出笑来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dress</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdress ˈdown (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">身着便服；穿着便装<br><span class="en">to wear clothes that are less formal than those you usually wear or those that are usually worn in a particular situation</span></td><td class="c4">He deliberately <b>dressed down</b> for the party.<br>他有意穿便装参加聚会。<br>More and more people are <b>dressing down</b> for the office these days.<br>如今，越来越多的人上班不穿正装。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdress sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">责骂<br><span class="en">to criticize sb angrily for sth wrong that they have done</span></td><td class="c4">The sergeant <b>dressed down</b> the new recruits.<br>中士把新兵狠狠骂了一通。<br>They <b>dressed</b> themselves up as cartoon characters.<br>他们装扮成了卡通人物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdress ˈup (in sth)<br>ˌdress yourself ˈup (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">身着盛装；穿着；正装<br><span class="en">to wear special or more formal clothes than you usually do or than those usually worn in a particular situation</span></td><td class="c4">Don't bother to <b>dress</b> up-come as you are.<br>用不着穿礼服一 —就穿平时的衣服来吧。<br>She <b>dressed</b> herself up in a grey suit for the court appearance.<br>她穿了一套灰色西装出庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdress sth ˈup (as sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…粉饰(成…)；把…美化(內…)<br><span class="en">to make sth seem different or better than it really is by the way that you present it</span></td><td class="c4">Youre sacking me. Don't try to <b>dress it up</b> as a career move.<br>你是要解雇我。别美其名日职业变动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drift</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrift aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐疏远；生疏起来<br><span class="en">to become less close or less friendly with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Over the Years we just <b>drifted apart</b>.<br>年复一年，我们就这么日渐疏远了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrift ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">睡着；入睡<br><span class="en">to fall asleep</span></td><td class="c4">She soon <b>drifted off</b>.<br>她很快便入睡了。<br>I <b>drifted off</b> to sleep on the sofa while I was watching the football.<br>我看足球赛时在沙发上睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrill sth into sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…反复灌输<br><span class="en">to make sb learn or understand sth by repeating it frequently</span></td><td class="c4">We had multiplication tables <b>drilled into</b> us at school.<br>以前我们上学得反复背诵乘法表。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>drink sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">迅速喝光<br><span class="en">to drink all of sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He filled a cup with cold water and drank it <b>down</b> in one gulp.<br>他盛了一杯凉水，一饮而尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drink ˈin sth</b></td><td class="c3">尽情；地欣赏；陶醉于<br><span class="en">to look at, listen to or experience sth with great pleasure and interest</span></td><td class="c4">She wandered the streets, <b>drinking in</b> the atmosphere.<br>她漫步街头，乐在其中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drink ˈup<br>drink sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…喝完<br><span class="en">to finish all of a drink</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Drink up</b>. It's time to 80.<br>喝干吧，该走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈdriving at sth</b></td><td class="c3">试图表达；试图说<br><span class="en">to try to express or say sth</span></td><td class="c4">What's he <b>driving</b> at?<br>他什么意思。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drive sb/sth aˈway (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">令人却步；驱使…离开<br><span class="en">to make sb not want to go to a particular place or be with a particular person; to make sb/sth leave a place</span></td><td class="c4">Rising prices are <b>driving customers away</b>.<br>不断上扬的价格使顾客望而却步。<br>His violent behaviour has <b>driven all his family away</b>.<br>他的暴力行为把家人全吓跑了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drive sb/sth ˈoff<br>ˌdrive sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">赶走；驱赶…(离开…)<br><span class="en">to force sb/sth to move away from a particular place</span></td><td class="c4">The army was <b>driven off</b> by the fierce attacks of the rebels.<br>部队在叛军的猛烈攻击下被迫转移。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrive ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">驱车继续行驶<br><span class="en">to continue driving either without stopping or after stopping for a short time</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>drove on</b> until we came to an open square full of cafes.<br>我们一直开到一个到处都是小餐馆的露天广场才停下车。<br>Paula stopped to let Philip out of the car before <b>driving on</b>.<br>葆拉停车让菲利普下车，然后又继续。</td></tr>
