<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drive sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌdrive sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">赶走；使消失；使离开<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth leave or disappear</span></td><td class="c4">They're hoping that their competitive prices will <b>drive out</b> the rival company.<br>他们希望以具有竞争力的价格逼退对手公司。<br>They tried to <b>drive her out</b> of the village.<br>他们试图把她赶出村庄。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drone</b></td><td class="c2"><b>drone ˈon (about sth)</b></td><td class="c3">唠叨；累絮叨叨地说<br><span class="en">to talk about sth for a long time in a boring way</span></td><td class="c4">I nearly fell asleep while he was <b>droning on</b>!<br>他啰哩啰唆地讲个没完，我差点睡着。<br>She <b>droned on</b> for hours about the uses of the present tense.<br>她没完没了地啰唆现在时的用法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drool</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdrool over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">情地看；迷恋地看<br><span class="en">to look at sb/sth in a way that shows you like and admire or want them/it, often in a silly or exaggerated way</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>drooling all over</b> you at the party!<br>晚会上他一直在痴迷地打量你！?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>drop aˈway <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">地面往下猛然变陡<br><span class="en">if the ground drops away, it slopes down steeply away from where you are</span></td><td class="c4">The seabed suddenly <b>dropped away</b> and I was waist deep in the water.<br>海床突然陡直向下，我掉进了齐腰深的水里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drop aˈway <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">减弱；消失<br><span class="en">to become less strong or disappear</span></td><td class="c4">He felt his dark mood <b>dropping away</b>.<br>他觉得他不再悲观了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrop ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐落在同伴等；的后面<br><span class="en">if a person in a group drops back, they move to a position further back behind other people, often because they are not able to stay at the front</span></td><td class="c4">The original leader in the race has now <b>dropped back</b> to third place.<br>比赛开始时领先的选手现在掉到了第三名。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drop beˈhind<br>drop be hind sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">落后(于…)；落在…之后<br><span class="en">if sb drops behind or drops behind sb/sth, they move to a position behind other people</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>dropped behind</b> to walk with Sam.<br>他落到后面，和萨姆一道走。<br>We cannot afford to <b>drop behind</b> our competitors.<br>我们不能落在竞争对手后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdrop-down n</b></td><td class="c3">下拉菜单</td><td class="c4">Select the item you want from the <b>drop-down</b>.<br>从下拉菜单中选择所需项。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrop ˈin (on sb/at .. ),.drop ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">顺便；看望一下(某人)；顺便到(某处)一会儿<br><span class="en">to pay a short, informal visit to sb, often without arranging this in advance</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Drop</b> in any time you're passing.<br>你路过就顺便进来坐坐。<br>She <b>drops</b> in on her parents at least once a week.<br>她一周至少去看父母一次。<br>I <b>dropped</b> <b>into</b> the pub for a quick drink on my way home.<br>回家路上，我顺便进酒吧匆匆喝一杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drop sb/yourself ˈin it <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使陷入困境；使尴尬<br><span class="en">to put sb in a difficult or embarrassing situation</span></td><td class="c4">She got herself out of trouble by <b>dropping</b> Laura in it.<br>她把劳拉扯进去，自己甩掉了麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>drop ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">打盹儿；小睡<br><span class="en">to fall into a light sleep</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>dropping off</b> in front of the TV.<br>他看电视老是打瞌睡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdrop-off (in sth) n</b></td><td class="c3">下降；减少</td><td class="c4">Managers are concerned by a recent <b>drop-off</b> in sales.<br>最近销售额下滑让经理们忧心忡忡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,drop sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">停车让(某人)下去；(顺路)递送(某物)<br><span class="en">to stop and let sb get out of a car, etc.; to deliver sth to a place, often when you are on the way to somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">Could you drop me <b>off</b> at the station?<br>你在车站让我下车好吗。<br>She dropped <b>off</b> some clothes at the dry-cleaner's.<br>她顺路把一些衣服送到了干。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdrop-off n</b></td><td class="c3">停车下客(或卸货)站点；停车下客(或卸货)<br><span class="en">a place where vehicles can stop for people to get out, or where sth can be left; the action of doing this</span></td><td class="c4">It is easier to get a taxi at passenger <b>drop-off</b> points than at flight arrival stands.<br>在下客站叫出租车比在航班进港候客处容易。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdropout n</b></td><td class="c3">退学者；辍学者</td><td class="c4">He might be a college <b>dropout</b> but he's made a fortune in business.<br>他可能没完成学业，但却经商发了财。<br>There is a high <b>dropout</b> rate from some college courses.<br>有些大学课程的弃学率很高。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdropout n</b></td><td class="c3">拒绝主流社会者；抵制现实社会的人<br><span class="en">a person who rejects the accepted ideas, morals and values of society</span></td><td class="c4">Many of the town's <b>dropouts</b> hang around the square.<br>这个小镇很多脱离主流社会的人爱在广场上闲荡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrop ˈover <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">串门；(到某人家)小坐<br><span class="en">to visit sb for a short time at their home, without arranging a time in advance</span></td><td class="c4">Why don't you <b>drop over</b> this evening?<br>你今晚过来坐坐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drown</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrown sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">声音盖过；压过<br><span class="en">if a sound drowns out sb/sth,it is so loud that they/it cannot be heard</span></td><td class="c4">The music was <b>drowning</b> conversation.<br>音乐开到了最大音量，掩盖了谈话声。<br>Her reply was <b>drowned out</b> by a passing motorbike.<br>她的回答淹没在路过摩托车的轰鸣声中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>drum</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrum sth ˈinto sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…反复灌输；对…再三；讲述<br><span class="en">to make sb remember sth by repeating it often</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>drummed road safety into</b> them before letting them out on their bicycles.<br>他再三叮嘱他们要注意道路安全，然后才让他们骑自行车出去。<br>Traditional values were <b>drummed into</b> him from an early age.<br>他从小就被反复灌输了传统价值观。<br>I had it <b>drummed into</b> me that I shouldn't talk to strangers.<br>我曾被不断告诫不要与阳生人讲站。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdrum sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">竭力争取；兜揽<br><span class="en">to work hard to get sth</span></td><td class="c4">Were launching a campaign to <b>drum up</b> more business.<br>我们正要开展活动，以招揽到更多生意。<br>We couldn't <b>drum up</b> enough cash to keep the club going.<br>我们无法争取到足够的现金来维持俱乐部的运转。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dry</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdry ˈout ˌdry sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使变干；干透<br><span class="en">to become very or too dry; to make sth become very or too dry</span></td><td class="c4">Water the plant regularly and don't let the soil <b>dry</b> <b>out</b>.<br>经常给植物浇水，别让土壤干掉了。<br>The wind and the sun had dried <b>out</b> my skin.<br>风吹日晒使我的皮肤变得干燥。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>dry ˈupi ˌdry sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">擦干；拭干盘<br><span class="en">to dry dishes after they have been washed</span></td><td class="c4">Tia <b>dry</b> up if you wash the dishes.<br>你洗盘子，我来揩干。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dude</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdude yourself ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">精心打扮<br><span class="en">to make yourself more attractive and try to impress people by wearing expensive or special clothes</span></td><td class="c4">He really <b>duded himself up</b> for the party.<br>他为参加聚会着实修饰了一番。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>duff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>duff sb ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛踢；狠揍<br><span class="en">to hit or kick sb severely</span></td><td class="c4">A couple of guys <b>duffed him up</b>.<br>几个家伙给了他一阵拳脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>duke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌduke it ˈout (with sb) <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">攥紧；拳头打(某人)<br><span class="en">to fight with sb using your hands tightly closed</span></td><td class="c4">You can't settle every argument by <b>duking it out</b>.<br>你不能靠拳头解决每一次争吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dummy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌdummy ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不吭声；缄默<br><span class="en">to say nothing</span></td><td class="c4">If he <b>dummies up</b>, just try a little persuasion.<br>如果他闭口不说，稍微劝劝他就是了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdump on sb<br>ˈdump sth on sb <span class="tag">(slang, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…倾诉；找…诉说<br><span class="en">to tell sb all your problems</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>dumps on</b> me every time she throws him out.<br>他每次给她赶出来，就找我诉苦。<br>She keeps phoning me and <b>dumping all her problems on</b> me.<br>她不断地给我打电话，向我大倒苦水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dwell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈdwell on sth also ˈdwell upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">细想；唠叨；不能释怀(尤指令人不快的事)<br><span class="en">to think or talk about sth for too long, especially sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">It's time you stopped <b>dwelling</b> on the past.<br>别再沉溺于往事之中了。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>dwindle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>dwindle aˈway (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐变少；渐渐缩小<br><span class="en">to become gradually less or smaller</span></td><td class="c4">The audience for this kind of music has <b>dwindled away</b> to nothing.<br>此类音乐的听众日渐减少，现已所剩无几了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ease</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ease ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">利润；价格等略微回落；稍降；回调<br><span class="en">(business) if profits, prices, etc. ease back, they become a little lower, especially after they have been high</span></td><td class="c4">The company's profits <b>eased back</b> from £15.1 million to £14.7 million.<br>公司利润从1510万英镑下滑到1470万。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ease ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">把某事放缓；放松<br><span class="en">(on sth) if sb eases back, they go a little slower, do sth with a little less energy, are less strict, etc. than before</span></td><td class="c4">The team played aggressively in the first half of the game, but were able to <b>ease back</b> in the second.<br>该队在上半场比赛中咄咄逼人，但在下半场攻势稍微有些放缓。<br>The government should <b>ease back</b> on farming restrictions.<br>政府应该放宽农业限制。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌease ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐减轻；渐渐舒缓<br><span class="en">to gradually become less strong or unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">Eventually the rain started to <b>ease off</b>.<br>雨势终于开始减弱了。<br>The pain <b>eased off</b> after a few hours.<br>几个小时后疼痛减轻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌease ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">减速；放松<br><span class="en">to go slower or make less effort</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>eased off</b> in the last lap and still won.<br>他在最后一圈放慢了速度，但还是赢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ease ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">减速；松弛；减少<br><span class="en">(on sth) to go slower or make less effort; to do sth less</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor told him to <b>ease up</b>.<br>医生让他放松点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>eat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐毁掉<br><span class="en">to gradually damage or destroy sth over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">Something was <b>eating away</b> the foliage.<br>有东西在蚕食叶子。<br>The stone had been <b>eaten away</b> by pollution.<br>石头因污染遭到腐蚀。<br>The sea is <b>eating away</b> the coastline.<br>海水侵蚀着海岸线。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat aˈway at sb</b></td><td class="c3">精神上长期折磨；烦扰<br><span class="en">to worry sb over a long period of time</span></td><td class="c4">Jealousy is <b>eating away at</b> him.<br>嫉妒令他备受煎熬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat aˈway at sth</b></td><td class="c3">侵蚀；腐蚀；逐渐毁掉<br><span class="en">to gradually damage or destroy sth over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">Pollution is <b>eating away at</b> the stone.<br>污染腐蚀着石头。<br>Resentment ate <b>away</b> at their relationship.<br>怨恨逐渐破坏了他们的关系。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在象里吃饭<br><span class="en">to have a meal at home rather than at a restaurant</span></td><td class="c4">Are you <b>eating in</b> tonight?<br>你今晚在家吃饭吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈeat into sth</b></td><td class="c3">逐步腐蚀；逐渐损毁<br><span class="en">to gradually damage or destroy sth</span></td><td class="c4">Woodworm had <b>eaten into</b> most of the furniture.<br>大部分家具都遭虫蛀了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈeat into sth</b></td><td class="c3">消耗；花掉；耗费(尤指大部分的金钱或时间)<br><span class="en">to use or take away a large part of sth valuable, especially money or time</span></td><td class="c4">My work began to <b>eat into</b> the weekends.<br>我的工作开始占用周末时间了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">快点吃；吃干净<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to eat quickly or to eat everything they have been given</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Eat up</b>! Youll be late for school.<br>快点吃！你上学要迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeat sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">情感折磨；困扰<br><span class="en">if an emotion such as anger, etc. eats sb up, it worries them all the time and they cannot think of anything else</span></td><td class="c4">The anger was <b>eating her up</b> inside.<br>她怒不可遏。<br>The van really <b>eats up</b> petrolgas.<br>这辆客货车很耗油。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ebb</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌebb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐减弱；开始消失<br><span class="en">to gradually become weaker and begin to disappear</span></td><td class="c4">His confidence <b>ebbed away</b>.<br>他渐渐丧失了信心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>edge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>edge ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">价格等逐步上涨<br><span class="en">if prices, etc. edge up, they gradually increase</span></td><td class="c4">Inflation is <b>edging up</b>.<br>通货膨胀不断加剧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>edit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>edit sth ˈout<br>ˌedit sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从书；节目等中删除；去掉<br><span class="en">to remove words or phrases from a book, programme, etc. before it is published or shown</span></td><td class="c4">He must have <b>edited</b> a lot of the interview <b>out</b>.<br>他肯定大量删减了采访内容。<br>Read through your work and <b>edit out</b> anything irrelevant.<br>通读一下你的作品，删去无关的内容。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>egg</b></td><td class="c2"><b>egg sb ˈon (to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">鼓动；挑唆；撺掇<br><span class="en">to encourage sb to do sth,especially sth stupid or wrong</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Egged on</b> by his classmates, he climbed a bit higher.<br>在同学们的怂恿下，他又爬高了一点。<br>The other lads were <b>egging them on</b> to fight.<br>其他小伙子在鼓动他们打架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>eke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>eke sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">省出…再用；节约使用；勉力维持<br><span class="en">to make a small supply of sth last longer by using only a little at a tme or by adding sth else to it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>eked out</b> the stew to make another meal.<br>她省出一些炖菜，留到下一顿吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>elaborate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>eˈlaborate on/upon sth</b></td><td class="c3">详尽解释；详细描述<br><span class="en">to explain or describe sth in a more detailed way</span></td><td class="c4">He said he was resigning but did not <b>elaborate on</b> his reasons.<br>他说他准备辞职，但是没有详谈原因。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>embark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>emˈbark on/upon sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始；着手；从事新的；重要的或艰难的事情<br><span class="en">to start to do sth new, important or difficult</span></td><td class="c4">The government has <b>embarked upon</b> a programme of reforms.<br>政府已开始实施改革计划。<br>He travelled for a year, before <b>embarking on</b> graduate studies.<br>他旅行一年后才去读研究生。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>empty</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌempty ˈout<br>ˌempty ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">地方空出来；(某场所的人)走空<br><span class="en">if a place empties out, or people empty out of a place, it becomes empty of people</span></td><td class="c4">At 11.30 the restaurant <b>emptied out</b> (= people left it).<br>到 11:30 餐厅已空无一人。<br>People were emptying <b>out</b> of bars and clubs.<br>酒吧和夜总会里的人纷纷散去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>empty sth ˈout<br>ˌempty sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从容器中将…全部取出；腾空(容器)<br><span class="en">to remove all the things from inside a container</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>emptied the bag out</b> onto the table.<br>他把袋子里的东西全放到桌上。<br>Don't <b>empty the bath water out</b>!<br>别把洗澡水排掉！01。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>encroach</b></td><td class="c2"><b>enˈcroach on sth (also enˈcroach upon sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">侵占(个人时间等)；打扰(正常生活等)<br><span class="en">to use up too much of sb's time, personal life, etc.; to begin to affect sb</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to prevent her work from <b>encroaching too far on</b> her private life.<br>她尽力避免工作过多影响她的私生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>endow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>enˈdow sb/sth with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给予；賦予某种特质；责任等<br><span class="en">to give sb sth, such as a particular quality, responsibility, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>endowed their children with</b> remarkable names.<br>他们给孩子们取了很独特的名字。<br>The job <b>endows its holder with</b> great prestige.<br>做这份工作的人会有很高的声望。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>enˈdow sb/sth with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">认为…具有(某种特质)<br><span class="en">to imagine or believe that sb/sth has a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>endowed certain plants with</b> almost magical healing qualities.<br>他们认为某些植物具有近乎神奇的疗效。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be enˈdowed with sth</b></td><td class="c3">自然赋予；天生具有某种技能；特质；特征等<br><span class="en">to naturally have a particular skill,quality, feature,etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>is endowed with</b> both intelligence and good looks.<br>他天生才智过人，相貌出众。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>engage</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be enˈgaged on/upon sth (formal)</b></td><td class="c3">正在做；投入(活动等)<br><span class="en">to do sth; to be involved in doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>is engaged on</b> a biography of his father.<br>他在写他父亲的传记。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>enter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈenter into sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与某人开始讨论；着手处理<br><span class="en">(with sb) to begin to discuss or deal with sth</span></td><td class="c4">The government agreed to <b>enter into</b> negotiations.<br>政府同意进行谈判。<br>It is vital that the contract be freely <b>entered into</b>.<br>自由签订本合同是至关重要的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈenter on/upon sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始；着手<br><span class="en">to make a start on sth; to begin sth</span></td><td class="c4">The economy <b>entered on</b> a period of sustained growth.<br>经济进入了持续增长期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>entitle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>enˈtitle sb to sth</b></td><td class="c3">賦予某人权利<br><span class="en">to give sb a right to have or do sth</span></td><td class="c4">This ticket <b>entitles you to</b> a free meal.<br>凭这张票可免费吃一顿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>equate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>eˈquate to sth</b></td><td class="c3">相当于；等于<br><span class="en">to be equal to sth</span></td><td class="c4">Do my qualifications <b>equate to</b> any in your country?<br>我的资历在你们国家有对等的吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>eˈquate sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…和…等同看待<br><span class="en">to consider that sth is the same as sth else, or equal in value or importance</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>equates success with</b> material wealth.<br>他认为成功等同于物质财富。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>etch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈetched into/on sth<br>be ˈetched with sth</b></td><td class="c3">感情显繹在(脸上)；(脸上)显露出(感情)<br><span class="en">if a feeling is etched into/on sb's face or sb's face is etched with a particular feeling, that feeling can be seen very clearly</span></td><td class="c4">Tiredness and despair <b>were etched into</b> his face.<br>疲惫与绝望刻在他的脸上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>even</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeven ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">道路等变平坦；(局势等)趋于稳定<br><span class="en">if sth evens out, it becomes level or steady after a period when it has gone up and down or changed a lot</span></td><td class="c4">The path <b>evens out</b> further on.<br>这条小路再向前就平坦了。<br>House prices will eventually <b>even out</b>.<br>房价最终将趋于平稳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>even sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">平分；平摊<br><span class="en">to spread sth equally over a number of people or a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>even out</b> the work among the staff.<br>她尽量把工作平均分配给员工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>expand</b></td><td class="c2"><b>exˈpand on sth also exˈpand upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">详论；充分阐述<br><span class="en">to give more information or details about sth you have said or written</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>expand</b> on your earlier statement?<br>请详细说明一下你前面阐述的部分好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>eye</b></td><td class="c2"><b>eye sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向…拋媚眼；(色迷迷地)打量<br><span class="en">to look at sb in a way that shows that you are interested in them, especially in a sexual way</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>eyeing up</b> all the women at the party.<br>他色迷迷地打量着晚会上所有的女人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌeye sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">渴望地或饶有兴趣地盯；着(某物)<br><span class="en">to look closely at sth, because you want it or are interested in it</span></td><td class="c4">Are you <b>eyeing up</b> that strawberry tart?<br>你眼馋那块草莓馅饼吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>face</b></td><td class="c2"><b>face sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">毅然决然地应对；挫败<br><span class="en">to oppose or defeat sb by dealing with them directly and confidently</span></td><td class="c4">The President is determined to <b>face down</b> his critics.<br>总统决心给指责他的人以迎头痛击。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌface ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">冰球</td><td class="c4">The teams <b>face off</b> at 2.30.<br>两队在2:30开始比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌface ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">准备开始辩论或战斗；比赛<br><span class="en">to get ready to argue, fight or compete with sb</span></td><td class="c4">The candidates <b>face off</b> in a Democratic Primary today.<br>民主党候选人初选辩论今日举行。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌface ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">房间或建筑物的窗户面向；面对；正对<br><span class="en">if a room or a building faces onto sth, the windows look in that direction</span></td><td class="c4">The front bedroom <b>faces onto</b> a main road.<br>前面卧室的窗外就是大马路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>factor</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfactor ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…有影响<br><span class="en">to have an influence on sth</span></td><td class="c4">The report will <b>factor into</b> the committee's decision.<br>报告将影响委员会的决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>factor sth ˈout<br>ˌfactor sth out of sth <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把(某因素)排除在外<br><span class="en">to not include a particular fact or situation when you are calculating sth, or thinking about or planning sth</span></td><td class="c4">When inflation is <b>factored out</b>, the trade deficit fell 12.8%.<br>撇开通货膨胀因素，贸易赤字下降了 12.8%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fade</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfade aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐变弱(或模糊)；渐趋消失<br><span class="en">to gradually become less strong, clear or frequent and disappear</span></td><td class="c4">His footsteps gradually <b>faded away</b>.<br>他的脚步声渐渐听不到了。<br>Her enthusiasm will soon <b>fade away</b>.<br>她的热情很快会消失。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfade ˈout<br>ˌfade ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">安静下来；逐渐减弱；逐渐消失<br><span class="en">to become quieter, weaker, etc. and gradually disappear</span></td><td class="c4">The Protest eventually <b>faded out</b>.<br>抗议终于逐渐平息了。<br>She looked a strong candidate, but then <b>faded out</b> of the picture.<br>她一度看上去像个有实力的候选人，但后来却逐渐无声无息了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfade ˈout<br>ˌfade sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">画面淡出；渐隐；(声音)渐弱；使画面；声音淡出；渐弱<br><span class="en">if a sound or a picture in a film/movie, etc. fades out or sb fades it out, it gradually becomes quieter or less clear</span></td><td class="c4">Near the end of the song he <b>faded out</b> the music.<br>他在歌曲的末尾把音乐逐渐减弱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fake</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfake sb out <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">蒙骗；(以假动作)迷惑<br><span class="en">to trick sb; to make sb think you are going to do one thing and then do another</span></td><td class="c4">He thought I was going to turn left, but I <b>faked him out</b>.<br>他以为我要向左拐，可我让他上当了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fall</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">剥落；掉落<br><span class="en">(from sth) to break off or separate from a surface</span></td><td class="c4">The plaster was <b>falling away</b> in big chunks.<br>灰泥大块大块地剥落。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">地面；道路等<br><span class="en">of land, a road, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The ground <b>falls away</b> abruptly to the right.<br>右边的地势陡降。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐消失；逐渐消散<br><span class="en">to gradually disappear</span></td><td class="c4">Gradually, all his cares and worries <b>fell away</b>.<br>久而久之，他的忧愁烦恼全都烟消云散了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">赛跑落后<br><span class="en">to fail to stay with people at the front in a race</span></td><td class="c4">Betts had been leading, but <b>fell back</b> with ten laps to go.<br>贝茨原本一路领先，可还剩 10 圈时却落在后面了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈback on sb/sth (also,fall ˈback upon sb/sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">求助于；借助于；转而依靠<br><span class="en">to use sb/sth when the situation is difficult or other people/things have failed</span></td><td class="c4">It's very hard if you have no family to <b>fall back on</b>.<br>没有家人可依靠的话，生活会十分艰难。<br>He could always <b>fall back on</b> his old jokes.<br>他总会搬出他那些老掉牙的笑话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall beˈhind with/in sth</b></td><td class="c3">拖欠(付款)；没有；及时做<br><span class="en">to not do sth or pay sth at the right time</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>fell behind with</b> the rent.<br>她拖欠了租金。<br>He began <b>falling behind in</b> his schoolwork.<br>他开始不按时做作业了。<br>Her legs were so weak that she <b>fell</b> down on her knees.<br>她双腿虚弱难支，突然跪倒在地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall beˈhind with/in sth</b></td><td class="c3">落下；垂到地面<br><span class="en">to drop to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">His trousers were <b>falling</b> down.<br>他的裤脚拖到了地面。<br>A lump of the ceiling <b>fell</b> down.<br>天花板掉下了一小块。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall beˈhind with/in sth</b></td><td class="c3">想法；论点；方法等<br><span class="en">of an idea, an argument, a method, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">That's where the theory <b>falls</b> down.<br>这就是该理论不能自圆其说之处。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈdown on sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">没有把…做好；把…搞槽<br><span class="en">to fail to do sth correctly or successfully</span></td><td class="c4">The suggestion was that he was <b>falling down on</b> the job.<br>言外之意是他活儿干得不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall for sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">倾心于；迷恋<br><span class="en">to be attracted to sb/sth; to fall in love with sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fell for</b> a young student.<br>他爱上了一个年轻学生。<br>We <b>fell for</b> the farmhouse as soon as we saw it.<br>我们对那幢农舍一见倾心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall for sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…信以为真<br><span class="en">to be tricked into believing sth is true when it is not</span></td><td class="c4">You didn't <b>fall for</b> that old trick, did you?<br>你没被那个老花招迷惑住吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fall ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">顶部或天花板塌落；坍塌<br><span class="en">if a roof or a ceiling falls in, it drops to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">The roof of the cave <b>fell in</b>.<br>洞顶塌了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈin with sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">加入；开始与…有牵连<br><span class="en">to join sb; to become involved with sb</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>fell in with</b> a bad crowd.<br>她结交了一帮坏人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈin with sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指勉强地同意；赞同<br><span class="en">to agree to or support a plan or an idea, especially when you do not really want to</span></td><td class="c4">He always expects me to <b>fall in with</b> his plans.<br>他总以为我会赞成他的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">进入(某种状态)<br><span class="en">to begin to be in a particular state</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fell into</b> a deep sleep.<br>他沉睡过去。<br>The chair had <b>fallen</b> over.<br>椅子倒了。<br>She <b>fell into</b> conversation with her neighbour.<br>她和邻居聊上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">数量减少；(质量)下降<br><span class="en">to decrease in quantity or quality</span></td><td class="c4">Attendance has <b>fallen off</b> recently.<br>最近出席人数下滑。<br>The standard of cooking <b>fell off</b> when the old chef left.<br>原来的厨师离开后，烹饪水平下降了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall on sb/sth also ˈfall upon sb/sth more formal <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">责任或职责落在…身上；由…承担<br><span class="en">to be the responsibility or duty of a particular person or organization</span></td><td class="c4">Most of the cost <b>fell</b> on us.<br>大部分费用由我们负担。<br>When he died, the responsibility of the bussiness <b>fell</b> on his son.<br>他去世以后，企业由他儿子负责管理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall on sb/sth also ˈfall upon sb/sth more formal <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">视线落在…上<br><span class="en">if your eyes fall on sb/sth, you suddenly see or notice them/it</span></td><td class="c4">My eye <b>fell</b> on a letter she had left on the table.<br>我突然看见她留在桌上的一封信。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall on sb/sth also ˈfall upon sb/sth more formal <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">袭击；向…进攻<br><span class="en">to attack sb/sth with energy or enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">The children <b>fell</b> on the food with cries of delight.<br>孩子们欢叫着扑向食物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall on sb/sth also ˈfall upon sb/sth more formal <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与某人光；某事吵架；闹翻<br><span class="en">(with sb) (over/about sth) (especially bre) to have an argument with sb and stop being friendly with them</span></td><td class="c4">It's not worth <b>falling</b> out about this.<br>为这事争吵不值得。<br>Why have you <b>fallen</b> out with him?<br>你为什么和他吵翻了。<br>They <b>fell</b> out over their father's will.<br>他们为父亲的遗嘱吵了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">几乎被…绊倒<br><span class="en">to hit sb/sth with your foot when you are walking or running and fall or almost fall</span></td><td class="c4">Mind you don't <b>fall over</b> the boxes.<br>小心别让箱子绊倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfall ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">落空；失败；化为泡影<br><span class="en">to fail to be completed; to not happen</span></td><td class="c4">Our travel plans have <b>fallen through</b>.<br>我们的旅行计划泡汤了。<br>The deal <b>fell through</b>.<br>交易告吹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall to sb (to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">职责或；责任落在…身上；由…承担<br><span class="en">to become the duty or responsibility of a particular person</span></td><td class="c4">The task of telling them the news <b>fell to</b> me.<br>把这件事通知他们的差事落到了我头上。<br>It <b>falls to the police to</b> ensure that demonstrations are well organized.<br>警方负责保证示威活动有序进行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall to sth<br>ˈfall to doing sth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始做；干起来<br><span class="en">to start doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">Little Red Riding Hood and the wolf <b>fell to</b> talking.<br>小红帽和大灰狼交谈起来。<br>They <b>fell to</b> it with gusto.<br>他们兴致勃勃地干了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfall under sth</b></td><td class="c3">属于；归入…之中<br><span class="en">to belong to or be included in a particular group of things</span></td><td class="c4">What heading do these items <b>fall under</b>?<br>这些项目列入哪个类别。<br>The education system <b>fell under</b> the control of the church.<br>教育体系受教会控制。四B。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>familiarize</b></td><td class="c2"><b>faˈmiliarize sb/yourself with sth</b></td><td class="c3">使…熟悉；了解<br><span class="en">to teach sb about sth or to learn about sth until you know it well</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>familiarized</b> myself with everyone's name before the meeting.<br>我在开会前熟悉了一下每个人的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fan</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfan ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">散开；成扇形展开<br><span class="en">to spread out over an area from a central point</span></td><td class="c4">Searchers <b>fanned out</b> over the area where the missing child was last seen.<br>搜寻人员在失踪儿童最后出现的地方四散寻找。<br>Five main roads <b>fan out</b> from the village.<br>五条干道从这座村庄通往四面八方。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fan sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">鸟展开(羽毛)<br><span class="en">if a bird fans out its feathers, it spreads them out</span></td><td class="c4">The peacock <b>fanned out</b> its tail.<br>孔雀开屏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fancy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfancy sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">装饰；装点<br><span class="en">to make sth look more attractive by adding decoration to it</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>fancied up</b> the dress with some pearls.<br>我在连衣裙上装点了一些珍珠。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>farm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfarm sb ˈout (to sb) <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">托(某人)照看(尤指小孩)；寄养<br><span class="en">to arrange for sb you are responsible for, especially a child, to be cared for by other people</span></td><td class="c4">When he was little, he was often <b>farmed out</b> to family friends.<br>他年幼时经常交由他家的朋友照看。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fart</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfart aˈround (BrE also,fart aˈbout)(A, sang)</b></td><td class="c3">混日子；鬼混<br><span class="en">to waste time, especially by behaving in a silly way</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>farting around</b> and behave yourself!<br>别晃荡了，干点正事吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fasten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfasten on sb/sth<br>ˈfasten sth on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">盯住；把(视线)停留在…上<br><span class="en">if your eyes fasten on sb/sth, or you fasten your eyes on sb/sth, you look at them for a long time</span></td><td class="c4">AlL eyes in the room <b>fastened on</b> me.<br>一屋子的人都盯着我看。<br>She <b>fastened her gaze on</b> him.<br>她久久地凝视着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfasten on/onto sth also ˈfasten upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">握住；抓紧<br><span class="en">to hold sth firmly</span></td><td class="c4">The cheetah's jaw <b>fastened</b> on the gazelle's throat.<br>猎豹死死咬住羚羊的喉咙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfasten on/onto sth also ˈfasten upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">把(注意力或兴趣)集中于；对…锲而不舍<br><span class="en">to choose sth and give it all your attention or interest</span></td><td class="c4">When she <b>fastens</b> on an idea, there's no stopping her.<br>她一旦打定主意，什么也不能阻止她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fasten ˈup<br>ˌfasten sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…扣紧；系牢</td><td class="c4">The dress <b>fastens up</b> at the front.<br>这条连衣裙是在前面系扣的。9。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fatten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fatten ˈup<br>ˌfatten sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使长胖；养肥；育肥<br><span class="en">to become fatter; to give an animal or a person a lot of food so that they become fatter</span></td><td class="c4">The sheep <b>fattened up</b> quickly.<br>羊上膘很快。<br>We're <b>fattening the livestock up</b> for slaughter.<br>我们要把这些牲畜养肥，准备以后宰杀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fax</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfax ˈin<br>ˌfax sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…以传真发送<br><span class="en">to send a fax to an organization, a company, a television or radio programme, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Viewers are invited to <b>fax in</b> with their comments.<br>欢迎观众发传真来提出意见。<br>Orders can be either Phoned or <b>faxed in</b> to us.<br>可给我们打电话或发传真订货。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfax sth ˈon (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把(收到的传真)转发(给…)<br><span class="en">to send a fax that you have received to sb else for them to see or deal with</span></td><td class="c4">Please email or <b>fax this on</b> to a friend.<br>请把此条信息用电子邮件或传真转发给朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fax sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">以传真散发(信息)<br><span class="en">to send a fax to a large number of people at the same time</span></td><td class="c4">Draft proposals will be <b>faxed out</b> for comment at the end of May.<br>草案将在5 月底用传真发给大冢评议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>feed</b></td><td class="c2"><b>feed ˈback (into/to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">反过来带动；反过来影响<br><span class="en">if sth feeds back to/into sth, it returns to the place, situation, idea, etc. that it started from and has an effect, usually a good one, on its development</span></td><td class="c4">Rising import prices tend to <b>feed back</b> into domestic prices.<br>进口价格上升会导致国内价格上涨。<br>What the audience says <b>feeds back</b> into the development of the programme.<br>观众的反馈有助于这个节目的改进。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>feed sth ˈin<br>ˌfeed A ˈinto B<br>feed B with A</b></td><td class="c3">将…放进(机器)<br><span class="en">to put sth into a machine</span></td><td class="c4">Youll need to <b>feed the paper in</b> by hand.<br>你得手动进纸。<br>He <b>fed coins into</b> the meter.<br>他往停车收费器里投入硬币。<br>He <b>fed</b> the meter with coins.<br>他往停车收费器里投入硬币。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfeed ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">对(事物的发展)产生影响<br><span class="en">to have an influence on the development of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The report's findings will <b>feed into</b> company Policy.<br>报告结论将影响公司政策。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfeed on/off sth</b></td><td class="c3">动物等<br><span class="en">of an animal, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">This bat <b>feeds on</b> fruit.<br>这种蝙蝠吃水果。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>feed ˈthrough (to sb/sth/into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">在…身上逐渐产生影响<br><span class="en">to reach sb/sth after going through a process or a system</span></td><td class="c4">Rises in prices <b>feed through</b> to higher wage claims.<br>物价上涨导致人们要求加薪。<br>It will take time for the higher rates to <b>feed through</b> to investors.<br>提高利率的效应需要一些时日传导到投资者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfeed sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">增加进食养胖；养壮；(增加喂食)养肥<br><span class="en">to give extra food to a person or an animal to make them stronger and more healthy</span></td><td class="c4">You need <b>feeding up</b> a bit.<br>你需要多吃点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>feel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfeel sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指间接地揣測；探明；摸清(某人的看法等)<br><span class="en">to try to discover sb's views, opinions, etc. on sth, especially in an indirect way</span></td><td class="c4">You have to <b>feel them out</b> and figure out whether they want to talk to you.<br>你得探探他们的口气，弄清他们是否想与你交谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfeel ˈup to sth<br>feel ˈup to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">觉得(身体上或精神上)能胜任<br><span class="en">to feel capable of doing sth, physically or mentally</span></td><td class="c4">I don't really <b>feel up to</b> seeing anyone.<br>我实在没心情见任何人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fence</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfence sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">用栅栏等围住；圈住<br><span class="en">to surround sth with a fence</span></td><td class="c4">The grounds are <b>fenced in</b> by barbed wire.<br>那些地用带刺铁丝网围住了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfence sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">用栅栏等隔开<br><span class="en">to separate one area from another with a fence, often to stop people or animals from entering</span></td><td class="c4">Weve <b>fenced off</b> the vegetable patch to stop the rabbits from getting in.<br>我们把菜地围了起来，不让兔子进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fend for yourˈself</b></td><td class="c3">照料自己；自谋生计；独自谋生<br><span class="en">to take care of yourself without needing any help from other people</span></td><td class="c4">We were brought up to <b>fend for</b> ourselves when we were still quite young.<br>我们很小的时候就学习自已的事自己做。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fend sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">躲开；抵挡<br><span class="en">to defend or protect yourself from sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The minister had to <b>fend off</b> some awkward questions.<br>部长不得不回避一些尴尬的问题。<br>She managed to <b>fend her attackers off</b> for some time.<br>她设法抵挡了一阵，令袭击者难以靠近。<br>She held up her arm to <b>fend him off</b>.<br>她抬起賂膊挡开他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ferret</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌferret ˈout sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">搜出；查获<br><span class="en">to discover sth by searching thoroughly or asking a lot of questions</span></td><td class="c4">She's determined to <b>ferret out</b> the truth.<br>她决心查明真相。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fess</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fess ˈup (to sth)/(to sb) (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">承认；坦白(过错)<br><span class="en">to admit that you have done sth wrong</span></td><td class="c4">Come on, <b>fess up</b>. 1 know there's something you're not telling me.<br>快点，招了吧。我知道你有事瞒着我。<br>How many stolen cars did they <b>fess up</b> to?<br>他们供认偷了多少辆车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fetch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfetch ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">偶然来到；意外到达<br><span class="en">to arrive somewhere by chance</span></td><td class="c4">The boat finally <b>fetched up</b> on a sandy beach.<br>船最后停到了一处沙滩上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fiddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fiddle aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">虚度光阴；鬼混<br><span class="en">to spend your time doing nothing or doing sth that is not important</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>fiddling around</b> in the garage.<br>他在车库没事瞎忙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fight</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fight ˈback sth</b></td><td class="c3">克制(情感)；忍住(不做某事)<br><span class="en">to try hard not to show your feelings or not to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>fight back</b> the tears.<br>她强忍住泪水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfight ˈdown sth</b></td><td class="c3">抑制；忍住(即将发作的情绪)<br><span class="en">to try hard not to show an emotion that you are starting to feel</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fought down</b> a rush of panic.<br>他强压住心头的一阵恐慌。<br>She <b>fought down</b> the anger that was rising in her.<br>她压下胸中燃起的怒火。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfight sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">抵抗；击退<br><span class="en">to resist sb/sth or make them/it go away, by fighting against them/it</span></td><td class="c4">She managed to <b>fight her attackers off</b>.<br>她设法打跑了袭击她的人。<br>The company <b>fought off</b> tough competition.<br>公司挫败了强有力的竞争。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fight ˈout sth<br>fight it ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">打出个结果；争辦个明白<br><span class="en">to fight or argue about sth until it is settled</span></td><td class="c4">The teams <b>fought out</b> a 0-0 draw.<br>两队0:0打成了平局。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>figure</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfigure on sth<br>ˈfigure on sb/sth doing sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…考虑在内；计划<br><span class="en">to include sth in your plans; to plan sth</span></td><td class="c4">We hadn't <b>figured on</b> a long delay at the airport.<br>我们没有估计到在机场会耽搁很久。1。<br>Can you <b>figure</b> out what's going on?<br>你能搞清楚现在的情况吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>file</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfile sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把(文件等)归档<br><span class="en">to put papers, documents, etc. away in a place where you can find them easily</span></td><td class="c4">Everything is <b>filed away</b> in drawers.<br>所有的文档都存放在抽屉里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfill sb ˈin (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">向…提供(详情)<br><span class="en">to give sb all the details about sth that has happened</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>fill me in</b> on what's been happening while I was away?<br>把我外出期间发生的情况详细告诉我好吗？E。<br><b>Fill in</b> the blank spaces with one of these words.<br>选词填空。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfill ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">长大；变丰满；长肥<br><span class="en">to become larger, rounder or fatter</span></td><td class="c4">The baby's filed <b>out</b> a lot recently.<br>婴儿最近胖多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfill sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">扩充；增补<br><span class="en">to make sth larger or more complete</span></td><td class="c4">We'll need to <b>fill the story out</b> to make a full page article.<br>我们得把这篇报道扩充成一篇整版的文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfill sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">装满(汽油等)<br><span class="en">(with sth) to fill your vehicle with Petrol/gas, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I need to <b>fill</b> up with petrol before we go.<br>我们出发前，我得加满油。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfill sb/yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使吃个饱；尽情地吃<br><span class="en">to give sb a lot of food so that they feel full; to eat as much as you can</span></td><td class="c4">The meals at school never <b>fill</b> me up.<br>学校的饭菜从未让我填饱过肚子。<br>Eat lots of pasta to <b>fill yourself up</b>.<br>多吃通心粉，吃饱肚子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>finish</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfinish ˈoff (with sth)<br>finish sth ˈoff (with sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以…结束；完成<br><span class="en">to have sth as the last part of sth; to make sth end by doing one last thing</span></td><td class="c4">After a delicious meal we <b>finished</b> <b>off</b> with coffee and mints.<br>吃完美味可口的饭菜之后，我们喝了咖啡，吃了薄荷糖。<br>I have to go now, can I leave you to <b>finish</b> <b>off</b>?<br>我得走了，你留下收尾好吗。<br>Her outfit was <b>finished</b> <b>off</b> with navy shoes.<br>她穿上藏青色的鞋子，整装完毕。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>finish sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使垂头丧气；使筋疲力尽；使支撑不下去<br><span class="en">to make sb unhappy, tired, etc.that they cannot continue what they are doing</span></td><td class="c4">Running in that heat nearly <b>finished him off</b>.<br>冒着那种酷热跑步差点让他撑不住。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfinish sb/sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">毁掉；杀死尤指已严重受伤者或严重；受损的事物<br><span class="en">to destroy or kill sb/sth, especially sb/sth that is already injured</span></td><td class="c4">He thought the soldiers would come back and <b>finish him off</b>.<br>他以为那些士兵会回来干掉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfinish sb/sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打败；挫败(对手)<br><span class="en">(sport) to defeat a person or team that you are competing against</span></td><td class="c4">Murray <b>finished him off</b> in three sets.<br>穆雷直落三盘击敗了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfinish sb/sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用完；用光(尤指食物或饮料)<br><span class="en">to use the last part of sth, especially food or drink</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>finished off</b> all the ice cream!<br>他把所有冰激凌一扫而光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfinish sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…作最后加工；用…最后的部分<br><span class="en">to do the last part of sth; to use what is left of sth</span></td><td class="c4">He stayed home to <b>finish up</b> his assignment.<br>他呆在家里完成作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfinish with sth</b></td><td class="c3">不再需用(某物)<br><span class="en">to no longer need to use sth</span></td><td class="c4">Can you wash your cup when you've <b>finished with</b> it?<br>杯子用过后洗洗好吗。<br>Can I keep the book a little longer? I haven't <b>finished with</b> it yet.<br>我能把书再保留一段时间吗？我还没看完呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfinish with sth</b></td><td class="c3">不再做(某事)<br><span class="en">informaf to stop doing sth because you no longer want to do it or enjoy it</span></td><td class="c4">He said he was <b>finished with</b> football.<br>他说他再也不踢足球了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fire</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfire sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">射击<br><span class="en">to shoot a bullet from a gun</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fired off</b> a volley of shots.<br>他举枪连射。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfire sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">发动；启动机器；设备；计算机程序等<br><span class="en">to start a machine, piece of equipment, computer program, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>fire up</b> one of the generators.<br>我们需要启动一台发电机。<br>Let me <b>fire up</b> another window (= on the computer screen).<br>让我再开一个窗口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>firm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>firm sth ˈup <span class="tag">(also,firm up less frequent)</span></b></td><td class="c3">落实；敲定安排；协议等<br><span class="en">if sb firms up an arrangement, an agreement, etc. it becomes more definite or less likely to change</span></td><td class="c4">Prices will <b>firm up</b> later this year.<br>今年晚些时候会确定价格。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fish</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfish for sth often</b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Are you <b>fishing</b> for compliments?<br>你是拐弯抹角想让我说奉承话吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfish sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌfish sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中取出；拖出<br><span class="en">to take or pull sb/sth out of somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fished some change out</b> of his pocket.<br>他从衣兜里摸出一些零钱。<br>Several days later his car was <b>fished out</b> of the river.<br>几天后他的车从河里打捞了上来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>fit ˈin (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">与…协调；融合<br><span class="en">if sth fits in, it looks pleasant or suitable with other things or in a particular place</span></td><td class="c4">The building doesn't <b>fit in</b> with the surrounding area.<br>该建筑和周围环境格格不入。<br>It's an old house, but our furniture <b>fits in</b> well.<br>房子是旧的，可和我们的家具很搭配。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>fit ˈin (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">和睦相处；适应<br><span class="en">to live or work easily and naturally with a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">Tim never <b>fitted in</b> at college.<br>蒂姆一直没能适应大学生活。<br>Jane <b>fitted in</b> well with the rest of the staff.<br>简和其他职员相处融洽。<br>She's <b>fitted into</b> the team well.<br>她已经完全融入该队。3。<br>I like to <b>know</b> where I fit in and what I have to do.<br>我想知道我的岗位和任务是什么。<br>Where do I <b>fit into</b> all this?<br>在这当中我该发挥什么作用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfit ˈin with sth</b></td><td class="c3">活动或事情与…相宜；适合<br><span class="en">if an activity or event fits in with sth else, they exist or happen together in an easy or convenient way</span></td><td class="c4">My job <b>fits in with</b> looking after my family.<br>我的工作不耽误照顾家庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfit sb/sth ˈout (also,fit sb/sth ˈup) (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">向…提供所需物品如衣服；食物；装备等<br><span class="en">to supply sb/sth with the clothes, food, equipment, etc. they need</span></td><td class="c4">The ship had to be firted <b>out</b> before the voyage.<br>轮船出航前一定要配备好必需品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfit sb ˈup (for sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">诬陷某人(犯有某项罪行)；嫁祸于某人<br><span class="en">to make sb appear to be guilty of a crime that they have not committed</span></td><td class="c4">They're trying to <b>fit me up</b> for the theft.<br>他们企图把偷盗的罪名栽到我头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fix</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfix on sth</b></td><td class="c3">选定；决定<br><span class="en">to decide to choose sth</span></td><td class="c4">We haven't <b>fixed on</b> a date for the meeting yet.<br>我们尚未确定会议日期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfix sth on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">集中目光；思想；注意力等于；全神贯注于<br><span class="en">if you fix your eyes or your mind on sb/sth, you look at or think about them/it with great attention</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>fixed her eyes on</b> his face.<br>她凝视着他的脸。<br>His attention was <b>fixed on</b> a dark car.<br>他目不转睛地盯着一辆黑色轿车。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfix sb ˈup<br>ˌfix yourself ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给…准备；向…提供；安顿<br><span class="en">(with sth) to arrange for sb to have sth; to provide sb with sth</span></td><td class="c4">I can <b>fix you up</b> with somewhere to stay.<br>我可以给你安排住处。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfix sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">安排；组织；提供；准备<br><span class="en">to arrange or organize sth; to arrange for sb to have sth</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>fixed your holiday up</b> yet?<br>你安排好假期了吗。<br>Shall we <b>fix up</b> a meeting for next week?<br>我们下个星期开个会好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fizzle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfizzle ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">顺利开始后最终失败；终成泡影；虎头蛇尾<br><span class="en">to fail or to end in a weak or disappointing way, often after having started strongly</span></td><td class="c4">The romance <b>fizzled out</b> after a month.<br>这段恋情一个月后就结束了。<br>The coup attempt soon <b>fizzled out</b>.<br>政变不久就失败了。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflag sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">挥手示意(人或车)停车<br><span class="en">to signal to the driver of a moving vehicle to stop, usually by waving your arm</span></td><td class="c4">He managed to <b>flag down</b> a passing motorist.<br>他招手让一位过路的司机把车停下来。<br>The police were <b>flagging down</b> all heavy goods vehicles.<br>警察在挥手阻拦所有重型货车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflash sth aˈround (also,flash sth aˈbout especially BrE) <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">炫耀；炫示(尤指金钱或珠宝)<br><span class="en">to show sth valuable, especially money or jewellery to people, or let them see it, to impress them</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>flashing your money around</b>.<br>别到处炫富了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflash ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">回想；回项<br><span class="en">if your mind or your thoughts flash back to sth that happened in the past, you suddenly remember it</span></td><td class="c4">My mind <b>flashed back</b> to my first day at college.<br>我回忆起上大学第一天的情景。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflash ˈby/ˈpast<br>ˌflash ˈby/ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">飞驰；飞逝；掠过<br><span class="en">to go or pass very quickly; to go very quickly past sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The days just <b>flashed by</b>.<br>日子转眼就过去了。<br>She watched the scenery <b>flash past</b> the train window.<br>她看着风景在火车窗外飞掠而过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflash ˈforward (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">电影；等闪前；预叙；提前叙述未来事件<br><span class="en">if a book, flm/move etc. flashes forward, it describes or shows sth that will happen at a later time</span></td><td class="c4">The movie then <b>flashes forward</b> to wartime London.<br>电影接着超前叙述，穿插战时伦敦的镜头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈflash on sth <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">回忆起；意识到<br><span class="en">to remember or realize sth</span></td><td class="c4">I suddenly <b>flashed on</b> how horrible that day had been.<br>我突然意识到，那一天是多么的糟糕透顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flatten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>flatten sth/yourself aˈgainst/on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把身体或身体部位紧贴于；平贴于<br><span class="en">to press your body or part of your body on or against sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>flattened</b> her nose and lips <b>against</b> the window.<br>她把鼻子和嘴唇紧贴在窗户上。<br>I <b>flattened</b> myself <b>against</b> the wall to let them pass.<br>我身体紧靠着墙，让他们通过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflatten ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">道路；土地等逐渐变平<br><span class="en">if a road, an area of land, etc. flattens out, it gradually becomes flat</span></td><td class="c4">After Oxford the countryside <b>flattens out</b>.<br>过了牛津以后，乡村逐渐开阔起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflatten ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">停止增长(或上升)<br><span class="en">to stop growing or going up</span></td><td class="c4">Sales have <b>flattened out</b> in the last few years.<br>在过去几年，销售额趋于平稳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflatten sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使变平<br><span class="en">to make sth completely flat</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>flattened out</b> the crumpled letter on the desk.<br>她在写字台上把皱巴巴的信展平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flesh</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflesh sth ˈout (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以细节或信息充实论据；构思；绘画等<br><span class="en">to add more details or information to an argument, an idea, a drawing, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">You need to <b>flesh out</b> the bones of your idea a bit more.<br>你需要进一步充实完善你的想法。<br>They must be prepared to <b>flesh out</b> their strategy with some details.<br>他们必须准备为策略增加一些细节。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflick sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速关闭；啪一声关上(电器等)<br><span class="en">to switch sth off quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>flicked</b> the light of.<br>他啪的一声关了灯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>flick sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">迅速开启；啪一声打开(电器等)<br><span class="en">to switch sth on quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>flicked on</b> the air conditioning.<br>他轻轻一按打开了空调。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflick ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">浏览；翻阅；快读<br><span class="en">to turn the pages of a book, etc. quickly, or look through a pile of papers, etc. without reading everything</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>flicked through</b> a magazine while he waited.<br>他边等边翻看杂志。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fling</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfling yourself into sth</b></td><td class="c3">致力于；一心扑在…上<br><span class="en">to start to do sth with a lot of energy, enthusiasm and effort</span></td><td class="c4">When they split up she flung herself <b>into</b> her work to try to forget him.<br>他们分手后，她全身心投入工作，试图忘掉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfling sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">匆忙脱下<br><span class="en">to take clothes off quickly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Flinging off</b> her coat, she sank into an armchair.<br>她随手脱掉大衣，一下子坐在扶手椅上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfling sth ˈon <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">匆忙穿上<br><span class="en">to put clothes on quickly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">Just <b>fling a COat on</b> over your pyjamas.<br>在睡衣外面披件外套就行了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈflip for sb/sth <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始迷恋；对…怦然心动<br><span class="en">to begin to like sb very much; to suddenly become very excited about sth attractive, pleasant, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>flipped for</b> his red hair and freckles.<br>她突然迷上了他的红头发和雀斑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>flip ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">变得异常愤怒或激动；狂热；情绪失控<br><span class="en">to become very angry, excited or enthusiastic about sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>flipped out</b> because I was late.<br>因为我迟到，她大发雷𩃀。<br>People are <b>flipping out</b> over these new digital cameras.<br>人们狂热追捧这些新型数码相机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>flip ˈover<br>flip sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">使翻倒；翻转<br><span class="en">to turn over, or to turn sth over, onto the other side or upside down</span></td><td class="c4">The dolphin <b>flipped</b> <b>over</b> onto its back.<br>海豚翻了个身，肚皮朝上。<br>A huge wave <b>flipped</b> the dinghy <b>over</b>.<br>一阵巨浪打翻了小艇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈflip through sth</b></td><td class="c3">浏览；翻看<br><span class="en">to turn over the pages of a book, etc. quickly, or look through a pile of papers, etc. without reading everything</span></td><td class="c4">He fipped <b>through</b> the phot quickly.<br>他匆匆翻阅了那些照片。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflog sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">低价倾销；甩卖<br><span class="en">to sell sth cheaply because you want to get rid of it or because you need the money</span></td><td class="c4">We buy them cheaply and then <b>flog them off</b> at a profit.<br>我们低价购入，然后甩卖获利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flood</b></td><td class="c2"><b>flood ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">想法或记忆突然重现脑海；涌上心头<br><span class="en">if a thought or a memory floods back, you remember sth suddenly and it affects you strongly</span></td><td class="c4">Suddenly all my fears came <b>flooding back</b>.<br>所有的恐惧突然又重新向我袭来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflood ˈin ˌflood ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">水等注入；涌入(某处)<br><span class="en">if water, etc. floods in or floods into a place, it moves to fill or cover it</span></td><td class="c4">He opened the door and water came <b>flooding</b> in.<br>他一打开门，水就冲了进来。<br>Sunshine <b>flooded</b> <b>into</b> the room.<br>阳光酒满房间。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflood sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">洪水迫使…离开家园<br><span class="en">to force sb to leave their home because of a flood</span></td><td class="c4">We were <b>flooded out</b> by a burst water main.<br>由于自来水总管道破裂发了大水，我们被迫离开了家。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflood ˈover/through sb</b></td><td class="c3">感情强烈影响；强烈感染(某人)<br><span class="en">if a feeling floods over/through you, it affects you very strongly</span></td><td class="c4">A great sense of relief <b>flooded through</b> her.<br>她感到如释重负。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flounder</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflounder aˈround(BrE also ˌflounder a ˈbout)</b></td><td class="c3">挣扎前行；艰苦移动<br><span class="en">to struggle to move or get somewhere because it is difficult, or because you do not know where you are going</span></td><td class="c4">People were <b>floundering</b> about in the water, shouting and screaming.<br>人们呼喊尖叫，在水中扑腾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈflow from sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出自；由…引起<br><span class="en">to come or result from sth</span></td><td class="c4">What benefits might <b>flow from</b> joining the European Union?<br>加入欧盟会带来什么益处呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflow ˈthrough to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">到达；影响<br><span class="en">to reach sb/sth or have an effect on them/it</span></td><td class="c4">It will take time for the drop in manufacturing costs to <b>flow through to</b> consumers.<br>生产成本下降一段时间后，消费者才能从中获益。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flunk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflunk ˈout<br>flunk ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因不及格(从…)退学<br><span class="en">to have to leave school or college because your marks/grades are not good enough</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>flunked out</b> (of college) last year.<br>他去年(从大学)退学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flush</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflush sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">用水冲掉<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth with a sudden quick flow of water</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>flushed the unused tablets away</b>.<br>她冲掉了未服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflush sth ˈout<br>flush sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…(从…)冲掉；(用水)清除<br><span class="en">to wash sth out; to get rid of sth with a rush of water</span></td><td class="c4">Drink lots of water to <b>flush the poisons out</b> of your body.<br>要大量饮水以排出体内毒素。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>flutter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌflutter ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">飘落<br><span class="en">to move gently through the air to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">Wind shook the branches and several leaves <b>fluttered down</b>.<br>风吹动树枝，几片叶子飘落下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fly</b></td><td class="c2"><b>aˈbout, ˌfly aˈbout sth especially BrE usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时近<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Rumours have been <b>flying</b> around the office.<br>办公室里谣言四起。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfly ˈby/past</b></td><td class="c3">时间飞逝<br><span class="en">when time flies by/past, it seems to pass very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">When you have lots of things to do, time just flies <b>past</b>.<br>很多事情要做时，就觉得时间过得飞快。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfly ˈby/past</b></td><td class="c3">旅程过得飞快<br><span class="en">when miles, etc. fly by/past, a journey by car, bus, train or bicycle seems to pass very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">As the miles flew <b>past</b> and we got closer and closer to the sea, the kids got more and more excited.<br>旅程飞快，我们越来越接近大海，孩子们越来越兴奋。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fly ˈin/out<br>fly ˈinto sth<br>fly ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">乘飞机来到；离开(某地)；飞抵；飞离<br><span class="en">to arrive/leave a place by plane</span></td><td class="c4">Several heads of state flew <b>into</b> London last night for talks with the Prime Minister.<br>数位国家元首昨晚飞抵伦敦，将与首相举行会谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfly sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">用飞机运来；运走；空运<br><span class="en">to bring sb/sth by plane to a place or take them away</span></td><td class="c4">Food supplies are being flown <b>out</b> immediately.<br>食物补给立刻空运走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfly ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然；发怒；突然变得怒不可遏<br><span class="en">if sb flies into a temper, etc., they suddenly become extremely angry</span></td><td class="c4">He flies <b>into</b> a rage when you mention her.<br>你一提起她，他就大发雷霆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfly ˈoff<br>ˌfly ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…飞脱；甩出；突然脫落<br><span class="en">to come off sth suddenly and with force</span></td><td class="c4">The jolt caused her glasses to <b>fly Off</b>.<br>那一阵颠簸把她的眼镜震掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fob</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fob sb ˈoff (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">敷衍；应付<br><span class="en">to try to make sb stop asking questions or complaining by giving them answers or excuses that are not true</span></td><td class="c4">Don't try to <b>fob me off</b> with excuses.<br>休想找借口哄骗我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fob sb ˈoff (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">货不对版或以次充好地把货物骗；售给<br><span class="en">to give sb sth that is different from or not as good as what they want</span></td><td class="c4">We thought we'd been <b>fobbed off</b> with inferior goods.<br>我们认为对方出售劣质商品骗我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fob sth ˈoff on/onto sb <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把不想要的；商品或假货骗售给<br><span class="en">to trick sb into accepting sth that you do not want or sth that is not genuine</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>fob all her junk off onto</b> me.<br>她想方设法向我兜售她的所有垃圾商品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfog ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">玻璃表面被雾气笼罩<br><span class="en">if a glass surface fogs up, it becomes covered with steam or drops of water so that it is difficult to see in or through it</span></td><td class="c4">The windscreen started to <b>fog up</b>.<br>挡风玻璃开始蒙上雾气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fold</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfold sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">折叠收起<br><span class="en">to fold sth and put it away</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>folded the newspaper away</b>.<br>她把报纸叠起收好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfold sth ˈback, ˈover, ˈdown, etc.</b></td><td class="c3">折叠；对折<br><span class="en">to bend sth back, over, down, etc. so that one part of it lies flat on another</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>folded</b> the corner of the page over to mark his place.<br>他折起书页一角以作记号。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfold A in B<br>ˈfold B round/over A</b></td><td class="c3">用…包裹<br><span class="en">to wrap sb/sth in sth</span></td><td class="c4">She gently <b>folded</b> the baby in a blanket.<br>她轻轻把婴儿裹在毯子里。<br>She <b>folded</b> a blanket <b>round</b> the baby.<br>她用毯子把婴儿裹了起来。<br>He <b>folded</b> her in his arms (= he put his arms around her).<br>他将她。<br>She <b>folded</b> the letter up and put it in her pocket.<br>她把信折叠起来，塞进衣兜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>follow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfollow ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">是…的必然结果；因…而起<br><span class="en">(from sth) to continue or result from sth in a natural or logical way</span></td><td class="c4">Listen carefully to the answer and make sure that your next question <b>follows on</b>.<br>仔细听答案，一定要据此回答下一个问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfollow ˈup on sth<br>ˌfollow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">对…采取进一步行动；跟进<br><span class="en">(with sth) to take further action about sth</span></td><td class="c4">You should <b>follow your letter up</b> with a phone call (= you should write first and then telephone).<br>你写信后还应该再打个电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfollow ˈup on sth<br>ˌfollow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">追查；探究<br><span class="en">to find out more about sth sb has told you or suggested to you</span></td><td class="c4">The police are <b>following up</b> all the leads.<br>警方正在追查每一条线索。<br>It's worth <b>following up</b> his idea.<br>值得顺着他的思路继续研究。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>force</b></td><td class="c2"><b>force ˈback sth</b></td><td class="c3">竭力压抑(情感)<br><span class="en">to try very hard not to show an emotion</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Forcing back</b> the tears, she nodded and smiled.<br>她强忍泪水，点头微笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌforce sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">勉强咽下(食物或饮料)<br><span class="en">to make yourself eat or drink sth when you do not want to</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>forced down</b> her breakfast.<br>她勉强吃下早饭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈforce sth on sb (also ˈforce sth upon sb more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">强迫(某人)接受；把…强加于人<br><span class="en">to make sb accept sth they do not want to</span></td><td class="c4">I didn't want to take the money, but she <b>forced it on</b> me.<br>我并不想接那钱，可她硬塞给我。<br>Teachers feel that changes are being <b>forced on</b> them.<br>教师们感觉这些变革是强加他们身上的。o时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈforce itself on sb (also ˈforce itself upon sb more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">使一日了然<br><span class="en">if sth forces itself on you, you cannot avoid becoming aware of it</span></td><td class="c4">When he read the letter, the truth <b>forced itself on</b> him.<br>他读了来信，一切都明白了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌforce sth ˈout of sb</b></td><td class="c3">尤指通过脚迫迫使某人讲某事<br><span class="en">to make sb tell you sth, especially by threatening them</span></td><td class="c4">I managed to <b>force the truth out of</b> him.<br>我总算逼他说出了真相。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>force sth ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">强行通过；仓促通过(法律或计划)<br><span class="en">to get a new law or plan officially accepted, even though some people do not want it</span></td><td class="c4">The party wants to <b>force through</b> new environmental taxes.<br>该党想强行通过新设环境税。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>forge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>forge aˈhead</b></td><td class="c3">速前行</td><td class="c4">He <b>forged ahead</b>, panting and breathless.<br>他上气不接下气地向前奔跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>forge aˈhead</b></td><td class="c3">进展神速<br><span class="en">(with sth) to make progress quickly</span></td><td class="c4">The company is <b>forging ahead</b> with its plans.<br>公司的计划正顺利推进。<br>Jane's language skills enabled her to <b>forge ahead</b> on the career ladder.<br>简的语言技能使她在职场上平步青云。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fork</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fork ˈout (for sth)<br>fork sth ˈout for/on sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指不；情愿地(为…)大把掏钱；破费<br><span class="en">to pay a lot of money for sth, especially when you do not want to</span></td><td class="c4">I had to <b>fork</b> <b>out</b> for a cab home.<br>我不得不花冤枉钱，乘出租车回家。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>foul</b></td><td class="c2"><b>foul ˈups foul sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…搞糟；坏了事<br><span class="en">to do sth badly; to spoil sth, especially by making mistakes</span></td><td class="c4">The team can't afford to <b>foul</b> up in this game.<br>该队输不起这场比赛。<br>He admitted he'd completely <b>fouled</b> things up.<br>他本认自己把事情彻底搞砸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>found</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfound sth on sth also ˈfound sth upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">把…基于；把…建立在…上<br><span class="en">to base sth On sth</span></td><td class="c4">Their conclusions were largely <b>founded</b> on guesswork.<br>他们的结论大部分是基于猜测。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>freeze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>freeze sb/sth ˈout ˌfreeze sb/sth ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">排挤；排斥(使不能参与活动等)<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from being part of a group or taking part in an activity, business, etc. by being very unfriendly or making things very difficult for them</span></td><td class="c4">American rice farmers complained that their crops were being <b>frozen</b> <b>out</b> of the market.<br>美国水稻种植者抱怨他们的产品正被挤出市场。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfreeze ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">因紧张；害怕或兴奋动弹；一动不动；惊呆；吓傻<br><span class="en">if sb freezes up, they are so nerfrightened or excited that they are unable to move</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas so nervous 1 <b>froze up</b>.<br>我紧张得愣住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>freshen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfreshen sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使洁净宜人；使令人耳目一新<br><span class="en">to make sth look cleaner and more attractive</span></td><td class="c4">A coat of paint will <b>freshen this room up</b>.<br>刷一层油漆，这房间将会焕然一新。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>frighten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>frighten sb/sth aˈway/off<br>ˌfrighten sb/sth aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…(从…)吓走<br><span class="en">to make a person or an animal go away by making them feel afraid</span></td><td class="c4">I sometimes use a gun to <b>frighten dogs away</b> from the hens.<br>我有时用枪把狗从母鸡群里吓跑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>frighten sb/sth aˈway/off<br>ˌfrighten sb/sth aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…吓得不敢(做某事)；使却步<br><span class="en">to make a person or an organization so nervous that they are no longer interested in sth or no longer want to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">Investment companies have been <b>frightened off</b> by fear of losing money.<br>由于担心资金损失，投资公司望而却步。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>front</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfront for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">代表(某个集团或组织)出面；为(秘密或非法活动)作掩护<br><span class="en">to represent a group or an organization in order to hide a secret or an illegal activity or protect the person who is controlling it</span></td><td class="c4">The police could not discover who he was <b>fronting for</b>.<br>警方无法查出他的幕后主使是谁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfront ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">建筑物面对；朝向<br><span class="en">if a building fronts onto sth, it faces it</span></td><td class="c4">The apartment <b>fronts onto</b> the beach.<br>这套公寓面对海滩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>frost</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfrost ˈover/ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">蒙上霜；结霜；起霜<br><span class="en">to become covered with frost</span></td><td class="c4">All the windows <b>frosted up</b> overnight.<br>一夜之间所有窗户都结丁箱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>frown</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfrown on sb/sth also ˈfrown upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">不赞成；反对<br><span class="en">to disapprove of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Some restaurants <b>frown</b> on men not wearing jackets.<br>有些餐馆不接待没穿外套的男子。<br>Such behaviour is <b>frowned</b> <b>upon</b>.<br>这种行为是不允许的。语态。</td></tr>
