<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fuck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>fuck aˈround (BrE also ˌfuck aˈbout) (with sth) <span class="tag">(A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">闲荡；瞎混<br><span class="en">to waste time by behaving in a silly way</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>fucking around</b> and give me a hand.<br>别瞎胡闹了，帮帮我吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>fuck ˈoff <span class="tag">(A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">滚开；滚远点<br><span class="en">used to tell sb very rudely to go away</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Fuck off</b> and leave me alone!<br>滚开，别烦我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfuck sb ˈover <span class="tag">(AmE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">苛待；不公平对待<br><span class="en">to treat sb very badly or unfairly</span></td><td class="c4">The company promised me a big pay-off but they really <b>fucked me over</b>.<br>公司答应给我一大笔酬金，可实际上却耍了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fuel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfuel ˈup<br>ˌfuel sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">给(车辆等)加燃料；加油<br><span class="en">to put fuel into a vehicle</span></td><td class="c4">I need to <b>fuel up</b> before I begin the trip.<br>我上路前得加足油。<br>People in a hurry can <b>fuel up</b> their cars and themselves in one stop.<br>着急的人可一站搞掂，停车加油、 进食两不误。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fumble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌfumble aˈround (also ˌfumble aˈbout especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">笨拙地移动；粗手笨脚地做；胡乱摸索寻找<br><span class="en">to move awkwardly, especlally using your hands to do sth or to find sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>fumbled around</b> in the dark trying to find the lamp.<br>他摸黑找灯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>furnish</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfurnish sb/sth with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给…提供；向…供应<br><span class="en">to supply or provide sb/sth with sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>furnished him with</b> the facts surrounding the case.<br>她向他透露了与该案有关的实情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>fuss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfuss at sb <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常令人生厌地抱怨；嘀咕<br><span class="en">to complain to sb about sb/sth very often in an annoying way</span></td><td class="c4">She's always <b>fussing at</b> me about my smoking.<br>她总唠叨我抽烟的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈfuss over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…关怀备至；对…过分体贴<br><span class="en">to pay a lot of attention, or too much attention, to sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She likes to have someone to <b>fuss over</b>.<br>她喜欢对别人瞎操心。<br>When she gets nervous she <b>fusses over</b> unimportant details.<br>她一紧张就纠缠细枝末节。<br>I hate being <b>fussed over</b>.<br>我讨厌别人对我关心过度。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gabble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gabble aˈway/ˈon (about sth)</b></td><td class="c3">急促不清地说；唠唠叨叨地说<br><span class="en">to talk quickly and for a long time about sth so that people find it diffcult to understand you or become bored</span></td><td class="c4">Someone on the radio was <b>gabbling away</b> in a foreign language.<br>收音机里有人在叽里呱啦地说外语。<br>Nicola <b>gabbled on</b> about her boyfriend for hours.<br>妮古拉喋喋不休地谈论她的男友有好几个小时了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gad</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gad aˈbout/aˈround</b></td><td class="c3">四处闲逛；游手好闲<br><span class="en">to go to different places looking for fun and excitement, especially when you should be doing sth else</span></td><td class="c4">It's about time he stopped <b>gadding about</b> and settled down.<br>他该结束游荡生活安顿下来了。8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgain in sth</b></td><td class="c3">增加；增长(某种品质)<br><span class="en">to get more of a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">The students are slowly <b>gaining in</b> confidence.<br>学生们正慢慢增加自信。o时J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gallop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gallop ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">匆忙地做；急促地说<br><span class="en">to do or say sth very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>gallop through</b> your speech as if you can't wait to finish.<br>讲演时别那么急，好像迫不及待要一下说完似的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gamble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gamble sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">赌掉；输光<br><span class="en">to lose sth such as money, your possessions, etc. by risking it/them on a card game, horse race, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>gambled away</b> all our money.<br>她把我们的钱输得精光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gang</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gang ˈup (against/on sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指为反对；恐吓或伤害某人联合起来；拉帮结派<br><span class="en">to join together, especially to oppose, threaten, hurt or frighten sb</span></td><td class="c4">My brothers are always <b>ganging up</b> on me.<br>我的兄弟们总是合伙对付我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gather</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gather sth toˈgether/up</b></td><td class="c3">归拢；收拢(分散的东西)<br><span class="en">to bring together objects that have been spread around</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>gathered together</b> her belongings and left.<br>她收拾好自己的行李就走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gaze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgaze at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">盯着；凝视<br><span class="en">to look steadily at sb/sth for a long time, either because you are very interested or surprised, or because you are thinking of sth else</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>gazed lovingly at</b> her baby.<br>她爱意绵绵地注视着她的宝宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgear sth to/towards sb/sth<br>ˈgear sth</b></td><td class="c3">使与…相适应；使适合于<br><span class="en">to/towards doing sth to make or change sth so that it is suitable for a particular need or an appropriate level or standard</span></td><td class="c4">The programme is clearly <b>geared to</b> a teenage audience.<br>这个节目显然是针对青少年观众的。<br>We try to <b>gear our services to</b> customers' requirements.<br>我们竭力按顾客的要求提供服务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gee</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gee sb ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">激励；鼓励(某人加倍努力等)<br><span class="en">to encourage sb to work harder or faster or to perform better</span></td><td class="c4">Their success last week will <b>gee the team up</b>.<br>上周的胜利将激励该队再接再厉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gen ˈup<br>.gen sb/yourself ˈup (on sth) <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">了解(情况)；向…提供(情报)<br><span class="en">to find out about sth; to get or give sb information on sth</span></td><td class="c4">I must <b>gen myself up</b> for the interview.<br>我必须为参加面试作好准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>get</b></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈbove yourself <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行时<br><span class="en">often used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She's been <b>getting a bit above</b> herself since winning that award.<br>她获奖后有点得意忘形了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈcross (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">信息传达；传递给；某人<br><span class="en">to be communicated to sb or understood by sb</span></td><td class="c4">The message is finally <b>getting across</b> to the public.<br>这一信息终于传达给了公众。<br>The only way to <b>get across</b> the lake is by boat.<br>过湖的唯一办法是乘船。<br>Can we <b>get across</b> the city without having use the subway?<br>我们不乘地铁能穿过市。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get sth aˈcross (also ˌget sth ˈover less frequent) (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">向某人传达；把…讲清楚<br><span class="en">to communicate sth to sb; to make sth clear to sb</span></td><td class="c4">He's not very good at <b>getting his ideas across</b> to the class.<br>他不太会讲课。<br>You'll have to think of new ways of <b>getting your message across</b> effectively.<br>你得琢磨新方法把你的意思表达清楚。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth aˈcross sth (also,get sb/sth over sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…送过路；墙等；使通过<br><span class="en">to move sb/sth, or to help sb/sth move, from one side of sth such as a road, river, bridge, wall, etc. to the other</span></td><td class="c4">We've <b>got to get supplies across</b> the border somehow.<br>我们必须想办法把供给品运过边境。<br>We <b>got</b> all the injured soldiers <b>across</b> the river.<br>我们把所有伤员都送过河了。<br>Billy <b>got</b> the pony <b>over</b> the jumps with difficulty.<br>比利费劲地骑着马驹跳过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈafter sb <span class="tag">(informal, AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不断督促；一再敦促<br><span class="en">to keep asking or telling sb to do sth, often in an annoying way</span></td><td class="c4">She's been <b>getting after</b> me to take a vacation.<br>她一直催着我休假。<br>I had to <b>get after</b> Jack to clean his room.<br>我不得不一再催促杰克打扫他的房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈafter sb <span class="tag">(informal, AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">追捕；搜捕<br><span class="en">to try to catch sb, especially after they have committed a crime</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>get after</b> drug users more.<br>我们需要抓捕更多吸毒者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈhead<br>.get aˈhead of sb</b></td><td class="c3">走在…前面；领先；胜过；取得成功<br><span class="en">to make more progress than other people, companies, etc.; to become successful in your life or career</span></td><td class="c4">It isn't easy to <b>get ahead</b> in this business.<br>在这一行想出类拔萃并非易事。<br>By doing extra homework, he soon <b>got ahead</b> of his classmates.<br>通过多做额外功课，他很快就在班上名列前茅了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈlong <span class="tag">(informal often used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行时</td><td class="c4">One more coffee and then I must <b>get along</b>.<br>再喝一杯咖啡，我就得走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈround (BrE also ˌget aˈbout)</b></td><td class="c3">到处走动；周游<br><span class="en">to move from place to place; to go to lots of different places</span></td><td class="c4">You certainly <b>get around</b>! Paris one minute, Berlin the next.<br>你真是个大旅行家啊！前一分钟在巴黎，下一分钟又到了柏林。<br>She can use my car to <b>get around</b> while she's here.<br>在这里逗留期间，她可以开我的车到各处转转。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈround (BrE also ˌget aˈbout)</b></td><td class="c3">消息；信息等<br><span class="en">of news, a piece of information, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The news of her resignation soon <b>got around</b>.<br>她辞职的消息很快传开了。<br>Word SOOn <b>got around</b> that they were having an affair.<br>关于他们关系暧昧的流言很快就传开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">消息；信息等<br><span class="en">of news, a piece of information, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">News soon <b>gets round</b> the office.<br>消息很快在办公室传开了。<br>It didn't take long for the rumour to <b>get</b> all around town.<br>没过多久，谣言就传遍了全镇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈget at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">接触；取得；达到<br><span class="en">to reach or obtain sb/sth; to find a way of entering a place, talking to sb, looking at sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The files are locked up and I can't <b>get at</b> them.<br>文件锁起来了，我搞不到手。<br>I cant <b>get at</b> my inheritance until I'm 21.<br>我满21 岁才能得到遗产。<br>Put it in a place where it can be <b>got at</b> easily.<br>把它放在容易拿到的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈget at sth</b></td><td class="c3">获悉；了解；发现<br><span class="en">to learn, discover or find out sth</span></td><td class="c4">We've <b>got to get at</b> the truth.<br>我们必须查明真相。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>get aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">得以离开(某处)<br><span class="en">(from sth/ ..) to succeed in leaving a place</span></td><td class="c4"><b>It</b> was midday before we finally managed to get away.<br>到中午时分我们终于脱身。<br><b>I</b> won't be able to get away from the office before seven.<br>我七点钟前无法离开办公室。s 2。<br>You're not <b>getting away</b> from me so easily!<br>我绝不会这么轻易放过你的！3。<br>Will you manage to <b>get away</b> this year?<br>你今年能出去度假吗？4。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get aˈway from sth<br>.get aˈway doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">改变(做事方式)；转换(话题)<br><span class="en">to start doing sth in a different way or talking about a different subject</span></td><td class="c4">The club should <b>get away from</b> its old-fashioned image.<br>这个俱乐部应该改变过时的形象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get aˈway with sth</b></td><td class="c3">携(赃物)潜逃；盗走<br><span class="en">to steal sth and escape with it</span></td><td class="c4">Thieves raided the bank and <b>got away with</b> £50 000.<br>盗贼洗劫了银行，卷走了 5万英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>get ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">返回；回家<br><span class="en">(from/to sth/ . ) to return, especially to your home</span></td><td class="c4">What time did you <b>get back</b> last night?<br>你昨晚几点到家的。<br>We only <b>got back</b> from our trip yesterday.<br>我们昨天才旅行回来。<br><b>It</b>'ll take us ten minutes to get there and five minutes to get back.<br>我们去那里要用十分钟，回来要用五分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth ˈback (to sth/ . )</b></td><td class="c3">把…带回；送…回(某处)<br><span class="en">to take sb/sth back to a place after they have been away from it</span></td><td class="c4">Well <b>get her back</b> home before midnight.<br>我们会在午夜前把她送回家。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>get sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">取回；索回；重新得到丢失的物品；花费的钱；借出；的物品等<br><span class="en">to obtain sth again after you have lost it, spent it, lent it to sb, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Shess <b>got her old job back</b>.<br>她已恢复原职。<br>I never lend people books; you never <b>get them back</b>.<br>我的书从不外借借出去就收不回来了。<br>There isn't much of a chance of <b>getting the wallet back</b> (= it has been stolen).<br>寻回失窃的皮夹机会不大。</td></tr>

<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈoff with sb<br>.get ˈoff together <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">事业上获得成功<br><span class="en">(in sth) to be successful in your career</span></td><td class="c4">She's keen to <b>get</b> on in her career.<br>她很想干一番事业。<br>Having contacts is the only way to <b>get</b> on in the art world.<br>建立关系网是在艺术界取得成功的唯一途径。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈoff with sb<br>.get ˈoff together <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在…上有进展<br><span class="en">(also,get aˈlong) (with sth) used to talk about sb is doing a task, managing a situation, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">How's Jan <b>getting</b> on at college?<br>简在大学怎么样了。<br>How did you <b>get</b> on in your exams?<br>你考试怎么样了？5。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈoff with sb<br>.get ˈoff together <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">时间</td><td class="c4">Did Jack manage to <b>get</b> on?<br>杰克最后上车了吗。<br>Did anyone see Sue <b>getting</b> onto the bus?<br>有没有人看见休上公共汽车。<br>He <b>got</b> on his bike and rode <b>off</b>.<br>他骑上自行车走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">得到；获得(名额等)<br><span class="en">to gain a place on a course, a committee, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I was very lucky to <b>get onto</b> the course.<br>能够上这门课程，我很幸运。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">掃到(或抹到等)…上；落到…上<br><span class="en">(also,get ˈonto sth) to be dropped, rubbed, etc. on sth; to fall on sth</span></td><td class="c4">How did that mud <b>get</b> on the carpet?<br>那块泥巴是怎么掉到地毯上去的。<br>Be careful that the oil doesn't <b>get onto</b> your clothes.<br>小心别把油蹭到衣服上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈget on sth<br>ˈget sb on sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指在办公室打电话；打电话与(某人)联系<br><span class="en">used especially in offices to mean to make telephone calls, or to contact sb by phone</span></td><td class="c4">I couldn't <b>get him on</b> the phone all day.<br>我打了一天电话都联系不上他。<br>Shall I <b>get her on</b> the line?<br>要不要我打个电话给她？语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">设法穿上；戴上<br><span class="en">to put on, or to manage to put on, an item of clothing, jewellery, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Get your coat on</b> and we'll go for a walk.<br>穿上外套，我们散步去。<br>M) finger's swollen and I can't <b>get my ring on</b>.<br>我的手指肿了，戒指戴不上。<br><b>Get the kettle on</b> and make us a nice cup of tea.<br>烧壶水，给我们沏杯香茶吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth ˈon sth (also,get sb/sth ˈonto sth less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">设法把…放到…上面<br><span class="en">to manage to put sb/sth onto a place</span></td><td class="c4">It took four people to <b>get the piano on</b> the stage.<br>用了四个人才把钢琴搬上舞台。<br><b>Get him onto</b> a chair and call an ambulance.<br>把他抬到椅子上，叫辆救护车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈon at sb</b></td><td class="c3">不断批评<br><span class="en">to criticize sb a lot</span></td><td class="c4">She's always <b>getting on at</b> me.<br>她动不动就唠唠叨叨地数落我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始讨论；转而谈论(新的话题)<br><span class="en">to begin to discuss a new subject</span></td><td class="c4">We somehow <b>got</b> onto the subject of exams.<br>我们不知怎么就谈起了考试。<br>It's time we <b>got</b> onto the question of cost.<br>我们该讨论成本问题了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb ˈonto sth<br>get sb ˈon to sth</b></td><td class="c3">尝试(尤指有害的事)；教唆<br><span class="en">to introduce sb to sth, especially sth harmful</span></td><td class="c4">Who <b>got her onto</b> drugs in the first place?<br>首先，是谁教她吸毒的？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">消息等泄路；泄漏<br><span class="en">if news, etc. gets out, it becomes known, even though people are trying to keep it a secret</span></td><td class="c4">I word <b>gets out</b> there'll be trouble.<br>要是走漏了风声就麻烦了。<br>When it <b>got out</b> that we'd won the lottery, we couldn't escape press photographers.<br>我们中彩的事传出去后就躲不开摄影记者了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get ˈout<br>get ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从汽车；电梯；房间；屋子里等出来；出去<br><span class="en">to leave or go out of a place such as a car, a lift, a room or a house</span></td><td class="c4">The car door opened and a tall man <b>got out</b>.<br>车门开了，一个高个男人下了车。<br>I have a lot of trouble <b>getting out</b> of bed in the mornings.<br>我早晨总不想起床。<br>Close the door to stop the heat <b>getting out</b>.<br>把门关上，免得热气跑出去。<br><b>Get out</b> and don't come back!<br>滚出去，别回来了。<br>Do you need help <b>getting out</b> of the bath?<br>你从浴缸出来要人帮忙吗。<br>The thieves must have <b>got out</b> through the window.<br>窃贼一定是从窗户逃出去的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get ˈout<br>get ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">离开某个地方；机构等以避开困难；或危险<br><span class="en">to leave a place, an organization, etc. in order to avoid difficulty or danger</span></td><td class="c4">They were able to <b>get out</b> of the country before the war started.<br>在战争爆发前他们设法离开了这个困家。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb ˈout<br>get sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助(或促使)某人离开(某处)<br><span class="en">to help or make sb leave a place</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Get everyone out</b> (= out of a building) quickly!<br>让大家赶快出来！o1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">困难；地说出；勉强地说<br><span class="en">to say sth with difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">She was laughing so much she could hardly <b>get the words out</b>.<br>她笑得几乎说不出话来。<br>I wanted to tell him how I felt, but I couldn't <b>get it out</b>.<br>我想告诉他我的感受，可我难以启齿。<br>He started to <b>get his wallet out</b> (of his pocket) but I insisted on paying.<br>他伸手(从衣兜)掏皮夹，可我坚持要付账。<br>She <b>got out</b> her cigarettes and offered me one.<br>她拿出香烟，给了我一支。<br>I can't <b>get the red wine out</b> of the carpet.<br>我除不掉地毯上的红酒污渍。四E。<br>You'll feel better once youve <b>got it all out</b> of your system.<br>你发泄完就会感觉好些的。<br>Try to <b>get out</b> of the habit of eating between meals.<br>尽量改掉正餐之间吃东西的习惯。日。<br>How are we going to <b>get out</b> of this mess?<br>我们如何摆脱这种混乱局面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>b<br>get ˈout of sth<br>.get sb/yourself ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">使解脱出来；摆脱困境<br><span class="en">to escape from a particular state or condition, especially a bad or unpleasant one; to make or help sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">Jack always uses his wits to <b>get out of</b> trouble.<br>杰克总能随机应变摆脱麻烦。<br>The situation is <b>getting out of</b> control.<br>局面即将失控。<br>Who can <b>get us out of</b> this mess?<br>谁能帮我们摆脱这种混乱局面。<br>This new job should help me <b>get out of</b> debt.<br>这份新工作应当能帮我还清债务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sth ˈout of sb</b></td><td class="c3">通过劝说或威胁从(某人处)得到<br><span class="en">to obtain sth from sb, usually by persuading or threatening them</span></td><td class="c4">The police have <b>got a confession out of</b> her.<br>警方逼她招了供。<br>It's not worth trying to <b>get money out of</b> him!<br>求他给钱不值得！1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">解决；克服；控制<br><span class="en">to deal with or gain control of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Eddy's got to learn to <b>get over</b> his shyness.<br>埃迪必须学会克服羞怯心理。<br>I think the problem can be <b>got over</b> without too much difficulty.<br>我想这个问题不太难解决。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈover yourself <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">有自知之明；不再自以为是<br><span class="en">to realize that you are not as good, important, etc. as you think you are</span></td><td class="c4">She needs to <b>get over</b> herself!<br>她应该知道自己有几斤几两。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">设法使通过；过去<br><span class="en">to manage to move sb/sth past sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">I couldn't <b>get</b> the baby's buggy <b>past</b> the car parked on the pavement.<br>人行道上停了辆车，我没法把婴儿车推过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使通过而不被注意；拦下或抓住<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth go past sb/sth without being noticed, stopped or caught</span></td><td class="c4">You won't <b>get any goals past</b> him!<br>你不可能把球踢进他的球门的。<br>How did you <b>get your article past</b> the editor?<br>你的文章是如何通过编辑审查的？语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈround sb (also ˌget aˈround sb especially AmE)</b></td><td class="c3">通过讨好卖乖说服；使依顺<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to let you do or have sth, or to do what you want, often by being nice to them</span></td><td class="c4">Til try and <b>get round</b> my dad tonight and persuade him to give us a lift.<br>我今晚会想法哄爸爸开心，说服他让我们搭个便车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>get ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">耗尽<br><span class="en">to use up the amount or quantity of sth mentioned</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>gets through</b> forty cigarettes a day.<br>她每天抽四十支香烟。<br>Have we <b>got through</b> all that milk already?<br>我们把那些牛奶全喝光了吗？2。<br>We must <b>get through</b> the syllabus before the end of the year.<br>年底前，我们必须完成教学大纲。<br>There are a lot of jobs to be <b>got through</b>.<br>有很多活儿要干。e。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌget sb ˈthrough<br>get sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮某人挺过去；帮某人挺过(难关)<br><span class="en">to help sb survive a difficult or unpleasant experience or period in their life</span></td><td class="c4">I'm depending on luck to <b>get me through</b>.<br>我准备靠运气挺过去。<br>A good breakfast will help you <b>get through</b> the morning.<br>早餐吃好，能应付一上午。<br>These grades should just <b>get me through</b>.<br>能得这些分数我就通过了。<br>A stroke of luck may <b>get us through</b> to the final.<br>如果走运我们可能进入决赛。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sth ˈthrough (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">设法把…送；抵(某人处或某地)<br><span class="en">to manage to send sth to a person or place</span></td><td class="c4">I really need to <b>get a message through</b> to them.<br>我真的需要给他们传条信息。<br>We must <b>get food through</b> to the hungry.<br>我们必须把食物送到忍饥挨饿的人们手中。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈget to sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始影响(某人)的情绪；使厌烦；使生气；使困扰<br><span class="en">to begin to annoy, anger, upset or affect sb, even though they try not to let it</span></td><td class="c4">His constant nagging is beginning to <b>get to</b> her.<br>他的唠叨不休开始使她不胜其烦。<br>Don't let her <b>get to</b> you.<br>别让她影响你的情绪。<br>Seeing him so sad really <b>got to</b> me.<br>看见他悲痛欲绝，我实在于心不忍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈget to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">做起(某事)来；开始做(某事)<br><span class="en">to reach the point where you do sth; to begin to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>got</b> to thinking that perhaps she wouldn't come after all.<br>他开始琢磨着也许她根本不会来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get toˈgether (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">与某人碰头；会面；聚集<br><span class="en">to meet with sb for social purposes or to discuss or organize sth</span></td><td class="c4">The management should <b>get together</b> with the union to discuss their differences.<br>资方应与工会一起开个会讨论他们的分歧。<br>Local residents have <b>got together</b> and started a petition.<br>当地居民集合起来发起请愿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get toˈgether (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">与某人建立关系<br><span class="en">to begin a relationship with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Did you two <b>get together</b> (with each other) at university?<br>你们俩是上大学时(相互)结识的吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">召集；聚集(人员)；收集；汇集(物品)<br><span class="en">to bring people or things together in one place</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>getting a band together</b>.<br>我们正在组建一支乐队。<br>Can you <b>get the money together</b> by Friday?<br>你到星期五能把钱收齐吗。<br>Do you think you can <b>get together</b> a proposal by next week?<br>你觉得到下个星期你能拟出计划吗。<br>I haven't <b>got anything together</b> for the trip.<br>我根本没开始收拾旅行用品呢。<br>The government needs to <b>get its act together</b> on unemployment.<br>政府需要有条理地应对失业问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌget yourself toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">设法控制感情<br><span class="en">to manage to control your feelings in a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">She paused outside the door to <b>get herself together</b>.<br>她在门外停了一会儿，打算稳定一下情绪。<br>He <b>got</b> up slowly from his chair.<br>他从椅子上缓缓地站起身来。<br><b>Get</b> up off the floor!<br>从地板上起来！2。<br>He doesn't <b>get</b> up to see me very often.<br>他不常来看我。<br>I won't be able to <b>get</b> up there until Wednesday.<br>我星期三之前不能上那儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get ˈup<br>.get sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使起床<br><span class="en">to get out of bed; to make sb get out of bed</span></td><td class="c4">What time do you usually <b>get up</b>?<br>你通常几点起床。<br>Could you <b>get me up</b> early tomorrow?<br>明天你早点叫我起床行吗。<br><b>Get up</b>, you lazy thing!<br>快起床，你这懒骨头！2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>get ˈup<br>.get ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">爬上；登上…的；顶部<br><span class="en">to climb to the top of sth such as a hill, steps, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">How did the cat <b>get up</b> there?<br>那只猫是怎么爬到那上面的。<br>He can't really <b>get up</b> the stairs on his own.<br>他根本不可能自己爬上楼梯的。<br>We used ropes to <b>get up</b> the mountain.<br>我们用绳索登上了山顶。<br>I had to <b>get up</b> on the desk and shout to get somebody's attention.<br>我不得不爬到书桌上大喊，以引起大家的注意。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">振作(精神)；焕发(斗志)<br><span class="en">to make yourself feel excited, full of energy, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>getting up</b> a party for her birthday.<br>我们正在筹备她的生日聚会。1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">派遣(某人)北上；运送(某物)北上<br><span class="en">(to sth) to send or move sb/sth to another place, often a place further north in the country</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>get somebody up</b> there straight away.<br>我们需要立刻派人上那里去。<br>How can we <b>get all our equipment up</b> to Leeds?<br>我们怎么把所有的设备搬到利兹。<br>How did you <b>get the bed up</b> the stairs?<br>你是怎么把床搬上楼的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">建起；将…立起<br><span class="en">to build sth; to put sth into a standing position</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>got the building up</b> in just a few months.<br>他们只用了几个月就建成了那幢楼。<br>Can you <b>get the tent up</b> while 1 go and find water?<br>我去找水，你搭帐篷好吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">到达(某一阶段)<br><span class="en">to reach a particular point</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>got up to</b> page 72 last lesson.<br>我们上一节课学到第72页。<br>What have you kids been <b>getting up to</b>?<br>你们这些孩子在折腾什么。<br>The boys are lively and <b>get up to</b> mischief all day.<br>男孩子们活泼好动，整天都在调皮捣蛋。<br>She's been <b>getting up to</b> her old tricks again!<br>她又在故伎重演了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈwith sb</b></td><td class="c3">与某人发生；关系；发生性关系<br><span class="en">to start a relationship with sb, usually a sexual relationship •</span></td><td class="c4">She knew my brother was trying to <b>get with</b> her.<br>她知道我弟弟在竭力追求她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get ˈwith sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…亦步亦趋；随波逐流与…保持一致；全盘接受<br><span class="en">to start to behave or think in a way that sb else wants you to behave or think; to accept sth as being true or right</span></td><td class="c4">They never had a hit because they refused to <b>get with</b> the publicity machine.<br>他们一直没有红极一时的曲目，因为他们拒绝听从宣传营销人员的摆布。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>get with the ˈprogram <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">需要改变<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to change their attitude and start doing what they are supposed to be doing</span></td><td class="c4">You need to <b>get with the programme</b>!<br>你要改一改了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gin</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gin sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">杜撰；编造；伪造<br><span class="en">to invent sth or create sth that is artificial in order to achieve a goal</span></td><td class="c4">Presidents will do anything in an election year to save the economy, including <b>gin up</b> inflation.<br>在大选之年，总统会为拯救经济不择手段，包括制造通货膨胀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ginger</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ginger sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使活泼<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth more active, interesting or exciting</span></td><td class="c4">Some dancing would <b>ginger up</b> the Party.<br>跳跳舞可以活跃聚会气氛。<br>They need some excitement to <b>ginger them up</b> a bit.<br>需要来点刺激让他们打起精神。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>give</b></td><td class="c2"><b>give sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">婚礼上</td><td class="c4">Her father <b>gave her away</b>.<br>她父亲把她交给了新郎。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把(嬰儿或孩子)送人收养<br><span class="en">to give a baby or a child to another person to take care of as their own child</span></td><td class="c4">She had never understood why her mother had <b>given her away</b>.<br>她一直不理解母亲为什么把她送给别人收养。<br>He never <b>gives very much away</b> about himself.<br>他对自己的情况从不多言。<br>She had <b>given away</b> state secrets to the enemy.<br>她向敌人泄露了国家机密。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>give sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把…赠送出<br><span class="en">to give sth to sb as a gqift</span></td><td class="c4">He decided to <b>give</b> most of his money <b>away</b>.<br>他决定捐出他大部分的钱财。<br>We have 200 tickets to give away <b>free</b> to our viewers.<br>我们有200张票免费贈送给观众。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>give sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">让对手；轻易取得(选举或竞赛)的胜利<br><span class="en">to do sth in an election or competition that allows the other side to win easily</span></td><td class="c4">We could have <b>away</b> state secrets to the enemy.<br>她向敌人泄露了国家机密。<br>His voice <b>gave him away</b> (= showed who he really was) .<br>他的嗓音透露出他的身份。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>give sth ˈback (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">归还；送还(原主)<br><span class="en">to return sth to its owner</span></td><td class="c4">You can't have it. <b>Give it back</b>!<br>你不能要。把它还给人象。<br>Have you given back the money you borrowed <b>from</b> your father?<br>借你父亲的钱，你还了吗。<br>The new lam <b>gives some power back</b> to the people.<br>新法将部分权力还给了人民。<br>Eventually I <b>gave</b> in to temptation and had an ice cream.<br>我最后经不起诱惑，吃了冰激凌。2。<br>She <b>gives</b> in to the children all the time to avoid arguments.<br>她一直让着孩子们，免得争吵。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give sth ˈin (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">呈上；交上<br><span class="en">to hand sth to sb in authority, for example a teacher</span></td><td class="c4">Please <b>give your test in</b> (to the teacher) when you've finished.<br>试卷做完后，请交上来(给老师)。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgive onto sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">窗等朝向；通往<br><span class="en">if a door, a window, etc. gives onto sth, it has a view of it or leads directly to it</span></td><td class="c4">French windows <b>give onto</b> a balcony.<br>落地窗通向阳台。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">耗尽；用完<br><span class="en">to come to an end; to be used up</span></td><td class="c4">My patience finally <b>gave out</b>.<br>我终于忍无可忍了。<br>We were fine until the batteries in the torch <b>gave out</b>.<br>手电筒的电池用光之前我们还好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">发出；放出光；热等<br><span class="en">to produce sth, such as light or heat</span></td><td class="c4">That lamp doesn't <b>give out</b> a lot of light.<br>那盏灯不够亮。<br>The leader of the opposition has <b>given out</b> that she is resigning.<br>反对派领导人已经宣布她即将辞职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give ˈover <span class="tag">(BrE informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">住手<br><span class="en">to tell sb to stop doing sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Give over</b>! I can't work with you shouting like that.<br>打住吧！你那么嚷嚷让我无法工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give sth ˈover to sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…专用于(某种活动或用途)<br><span class="en">to use sth only for a particular activity or purpose</span></td><td class="c4">The newspapers <b>gave six pages over to</b> the tragedy.<br>报纸用了六个版面专门报道这一惨剧。<br>Much of the countryside is <b>given over to</b> agriculture.<br>乡下有许多土地用于农业。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give sb ˈupi</b></td><td class="c3">与(某人)断绝关系；不再与(某人)交往<br><span class="en">to stop having a friendship or a relationship with sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>gave</b> her up for a younger woman.<br>他为了一个年轻女子而抛弃了她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give sb ˈupi</b></td><td class="c3">把(婴儿)送人抚养<br><span class="en">to give a baby to sb else to bring up</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>gave</b> the baby up for adoption.<br>她把婴儿送给别人收养。<br>Shed <b>given</b> up all hope of seeing him again.<br>她已经不抱任何希望能再次见到他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give yourself ˈup (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">自首；投降<br><span class="en">to allow yourself to be arrested or captured</span></td><td class="c4">After a week on the run he <b>gave himself up</b> to the police.<br>逃跑一周后，他向警方投案自首了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give ˈup on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对(某人)不再抱希望；不再指望(某人)改变<br><span class="en">to lose hope that sb will get better, change, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">His teachers seem to have <b>given up on</b> him.<br>他的老师们似乎认为他不可救药了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>give ˈup on sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对(某事)不再抱希望<br><span class="en">to stop hoping that sth wil be successful or will happen</span></td><td class="c4">I haven't <b>given</b>-up on my marriage yet.<br>我对我的婚姻还抱有希望。<br>Have you <b>given up on</b> the idea of emigrating?<br>你打消了移民的念头了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>glance</b></td><td class="c2"><b>glance ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">球等擦过；掠过<br><span class="en">if a ball, etc. glances off sth, it touches it lightly and moves away from it in a different direction</span></td><td class="c4">The ball <b>glanced off</b> the goalpost into the net.<br>球擦着门柱入网。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈglance ˈover/ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">粗略地看；浏览<br><span class="en">to look at or read sth very quickly and not very thoroughiy</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>glance over</b> this document for me?<br>你能帮我把这份文件过目一下吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>glaze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>glaze ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">眼睛变呆滞；发呆<br><span class="en">if a person's eyes glaze over, the person begins to look very bored or tired</span></td><td class="c4">Her eyes <b>glazed over</b> when they started talking about football.<br>他们开始谈足球时，她变得无精打采。<br>I started to <b>glaze over</b> at that point.<br>那时我就开始发愣了。也可作单独使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>glory</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈglory in sth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以…为快；从…中得到快乐<br><span class="en">to take pleasure in sth</span></td><td class="c4">She seemed to <b>glory in</b> his failure.<br>她似乎对他的失败幸灾乐祸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gloss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gloss ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">淡化处理；轻描淡写；掩盖<br><span class="en">to treat sth such as a problem, mistake, etc. as if it was not important and avoid discussing it in detail</span></td><td class="c4">The manager <b>glossed over</b> the teams recent defeat.<br>主教练对该队最近的失败闪烁其词。<br>The movie <b>glosses over</b> the real issues of the war.<br>这部电影掩饰了战争的真正问题。<br>This question has been <b>glossed over</b> by politicians.<br>政客们对这一向题遮遮掩掩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gobble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gobble sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一下用光；很快耗尽(尤指金钱)<br><span class="en">to use all of sth, especially money, very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">The rent <b>gobbles up</b> half his earnings.<br>租金用去了他一半的收入。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>gobble sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">吞并；兼并(公司)<br><span class="en">if a business, company, etc. gobbles up a smaller one, it takes control of it</span></td><td class="c4">Small family businesses are being <b>gobbled up</b> by larger firms.<br>小型家庭企业正被大公司吞并。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>goof</b></td><td class="c2"><b>goof aˈround <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">费光阴做傻事<br><span class="en">to waste your time doing sily or stupid things</span></td><td class="c4">Come on, quit <b>goofing aroundthis</b> is serious.<br>快点儿，别浪费时间了—这是正经事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grab</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrab at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">试图抓住；试图握住<br><span class="en">to try to take hold of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>grabbed at</b> the branch, missed and fell.<br>她想抓住树枝，却失手跌落下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrab at sth</b></td><td class="c3">抓住；利用(机会)<br><span class="en">to take advantage of an opportunity to do or have sth</span></td><td class="c4">Hell <b>grab at</b> any excuse to avoid doing the dishes.<br>他会找出任何借口来逃避洗碗。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grapple</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrapple with sth</b></td><td class="c3">设法应付(困境)；竭力解决(难题)<br><span class="en">to try to deal with a difficult situation or solve a difficult problem</span></td><td class="c4">This is an issue that is being <b>grappled with</b> by the council.<br>这个问题正由市议会寻求解决。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grasp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrasp at sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指因；不满现状急切抓住(机会)<br><span class="en">to try to take advantage of an Opportunity; especially because you are unhappy with the present situation</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>grasped at</b> any hope of escape.<br>他不放过任何逃生的希望。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grass</b></td><td class="c2"><b>grass sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">使长满草；在…上种草<br><span class="en">to cover an area of ground with grass</span></td><td class="c4">The garden had been <b>grassed over</b>.<br>花园里长满了草。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>grass sb ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informa)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向警方或当局告发；检举<br><span class="en">to inform the police or sb in authority about a crime or sth bad that sb has done</span></td><td class="c4">My girlfriend <b>grassed me up</b>.<br>女友出卖丁我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grey</b></td><td class="c2"><b>grey sth ˈout (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">在计算机屏幕上以灰色显示表示该；选项不可选<br><span class="en">to show writing, etc. in a faint colour on a computer screen to show that a particular option cannot be chosen</span></td><td class="c4">That option is <b>greyed out</b>.<br>那个选项是灰色的，不可用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grind</b></td><td class="c2"><b>grind sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">长期折磨；欺压<br><span class="en">to treat sb in an unkind way or annoy them for a long time until they can no longer defend themselves or fight back</span></td><td class="c4">The villagers had been ground <b>down</b> by years of Poverty.<br>多年来村民饱受贫困之苦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>grind sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">大量生产；粗制滥造<br><span class="en">to produce sth in large quantities over a long period of time, especially sth that is not interesting or of good quality</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>grinds out</b> a novel a month.<br>他每月都拼凑出一部小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grope</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrope for sth</b></td><td class="c3">摸索；搜索<br><span class="en">to try hard to find sth</span></td><td class="c4">I stepped in the door and <b>groped for</b> the light switch.<br>我迈进门，摸索着寻找电灯开关。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gross</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gross sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使恶心；使嫌恶<br><span class="en">to make sb feel disgusted</span></td><td class="c4">His greasy hair really <b>grosses me out</b>!<br>他油乎乎的头发实在令我恶心！ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ground</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈgrounded in/on sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…为基础；基于<br><span class="en">to be based on sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Is the story grounded in</b> fact?<br>这是真人真事吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>grow aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐疏远；变得生疏<br><span class="en">to become less close to sb in a relationship</span></td><td class="c4">We used to be good friends, but weve <b>grown apart</b>.<br>我们曾经很要好，可现在疏远了。8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>grow ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">毛发等剪去或受损后重新长出<br><span class="en">if hair, fur, etc.grows back, it starts to grow again after it has been cut or damaged</span></td><td class="c4">His hair <b>grew back</b> thicker after it fell out.<br>他头发脱落后，新长出的头发反而更密了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈgrow on sb</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐；被…喜爱；越来越被…喜欢<br><span class="en">if sb/sth grows on you, you gradually like them/it more and more</span></td><td class="c4">That painting's really <b>grown on</b> me.<br>那幅画实在让我越来越喜欢了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>grow ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">长大成人<br><span class="en">when a person grows up, they become an adult</span></td><td class="c4">Kate's <b>growing up</b> fast.<br>凯特长得很快。<br>Oh, grow up (= behave <b>in</b> a more sensible way) and stop making such a fuss!<br>喂，懂事点，别这么闹了。<br>He was a difficult teenager, but <b>grew up</b> to be a responsible adult.<br>他十几岁时很难相处，可长大成人后很有责任心。2。<br>Mel and <b>I</b> grew up together.<br>梅尔和我是一起长大的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>grow ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐发展；日渐形成<br><span class="en">to develop gradually</span></td><td class="c4">The town had <b>grown up</b> around the abbey.<br>这座小镇是环绕修道院发展起来的。<br>A cult had <b>grown up</b> around him.<br>逐渐形成了一种对他的狂热崇拜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>grub</b></td><td class="c2"><b>grub sth ˈout/ˈup <span class="tag">(rare)</span></b></td><td class="c3">从地里掘出；挖出<br><span class="en">to dig sth out of the ground</span></td><td class="c4">Thousands of miles of hedgerows have been <b>grubbed up</b>.<br>几千英里的树篱被挖了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>guard</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈguard against sth<br>ˈguard against doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">防止(某事)；避免(做某事)<br><span class="en">to do sth to prevent sth happening or to protect yourself from sth</span></td><td class="c4">Clean the wound to <b>guard against</b> the danger of infection.<br>清洗伤口，以防感染。<br>We should <b>guard against</b> the possibility of this happening again.<br>我们应该提防此类事情再次发生。<br>Regular exercise can help to <b>guard against</b> heart disease.<br>经常锻炼有助于预防心脏病。<br>This danger must <b>guarded against</b>.<br>必须防范这一危险。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>guess</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈguess at sth</b></td><td class="c3">猜想；估计；臆断<br><span class="en">to try to imagine sth or make a judgement without knowing all the facts</span></td><td class="c4">We can only <b>guess at</b> the reason for his actions.<br>我们只能推测他行动的原因。<br>Her feelings can only be <b>guessed at</b>.<br>她的感觉如何，只能猜测。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gum</b></td><td class="c2"><b>gum sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, rare)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用黏性物质粘住；黏住<br><span class="en">to fill sth with a sticky substance so that it cannot move or work</span></td><td class="c4">My eyes were all <b>gummed up</b>.<br>我的眼睛睁不开了。<br>The substance <b>gummed the machine up</b>.<br>这东西把机器粘得转不动了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>gun</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈgunning for sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">只用于进行时<br><span class="en">only used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>been gunning for</b> me since I came to work here.<br>我来这里工作后，她一直借机找茬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhack sth aˈbout <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">乱砍；乱剪；(粗暴或随意地)改变<br><span class="en">to cut or change sth in a rough and careless way</span></td><td class="c4">The hairdressers have <b>hacked her hair about</b> a bit.<br>理发师把她的头发削得有点儿乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhack at sth<br>hack</b></td><td class="c3">猛砍；猛剪；乱劈</td><td class="c4">She's really <b>hacked at</b> my hair. It's a complete mess.<br>她实在是对我的头发下了狠手，剪得一塌糊涂。<br>He was <b>hacking away at</b> the trees with an axe.<br>他用斧子对着那些树猛砍。<br>Don't <b>hack at</b> it! Cut it carefully!<br>不要乱剪！剪得仔细些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhack sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">砍倒；砍伐树木<br><span class="en">to cut a tree, etc. roughly so that it falls to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">They are <b>hacking down</b> the forests to sell the timber.<br>他们在砍伐森林以售卖木材。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhack sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使极其恼怒；使非常生气<br><span class="en">to make sb feel extremely annoyed or irritated</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>hacked off</b> with the whole situation.<br>他对整个局面大为恼火。<br>She always wants me to be there. That really <b>hacks me off</b>.<br>她总是要我呆在那儿。这让我苦恼不已。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhack sth ˈoff<br>ˌhack sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…(从…上)砍下来；(从…上)削掉<br><span class="en">to cut sth off sth with rough heavy blows</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>hacked off</b> the dead branches.<br>他们把枯树枝砍掉了。<br>He <b>hacked the padlock off</b> the door.<br>他把门上的挂锁砸掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhack sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…剁成大块<br><span class="en">to cut sth very roughly into large pieces</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>hacked up</b> the meat with a large knife.<br>他用大刀把肉剁成大块。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhail from .. <span class="tag">(formal not used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时</td><td class="c4">Which part of Ireland does he <b>hail</b> from?<br>他来自爱尔兰的哪个地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ham</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌham it ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">表演得夸张做作；表演得过火<br><span class="en">to act in a deliberately artificial or exaggerated way</span></td><td class="c4">The actors were really <b>hamming it up</b>.<br>演员们表演得太夸张。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hammer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhammer aˈway at sth</b></td><td class="c3">不懈努力；孜孜以求；重复论及<br><span class="en">to work hard in order to finish or achieve sth; to repeat sth again and again</span></td><td class="c4">He kept <b>hammering away at</b> the same point all through the meeting.<br>他开会自始至终都在再三强调同一观点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhammer sth ˈin<br>ˌhammer sth ˈinto sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…反复灌输<br><span class="en">to force sb to learn sth by repeating it many times</span></td><td class="c4">They have had English grammar <b>hammered into</b> them.<br>他们通过接受反复灌输学会了英语语法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhammer sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">反复讨论出(一致意见)；充分研讨出(决定)<br><span class="en">to discuss a plan, a deal, etc. for a long time and with great effort, until sth is decided or agreed on</span></td><td class="c4">I took weeks to <b>hammer out</b> an agreement.<br>经过多个星期的反复讨论才达成协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hand</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hand sth aˈround <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…归还给原先或；合法的拥有者；国家等<br><span class="en">+ the person, country, etc. who used to have it or who owns it legally</span></td><td class="c4">The territory was <b>handed</b> back to Egypt.<br>领土归还给了埃及。<br>These skills have been <b>handed</b> down from generation to generation.<br>这些技术一直世代相传。<br>He's got no one to <b>hand</b> the family house on to.<br>他没有后代继承他家的房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hand sth aˈround <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">法庭等<br><span class="en">of a court, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The judge <b>handed</b> down a sentence of six years.<br>法官宣布判处六年徒刑。助。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>hand sth ˈin (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">提交；呈交；上交书面材料；失物等<br><span class="en">to give a piece of work to sb, such as a teacher, so that they can correct, read or deal with it; to give sth to sb in authority because it belongs to them or is lost</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure you <b>hand in</b> your homework on time.<br>一定要按时交家庭作业。<br>Hand your room <b>keys</b> in by 10 a.m.<br>上午10点前交房间钥匙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhand ˈover to sb<br>ˌhand sth ˈover to sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…移交(权力或责任)<br><span class="en">to give sb else your position of power or authority; to give sb else the responsibility for dealing with a particular situation</span></td><td class="c4">I am resigning and <b>handing over to</b> my deputy.<br>我要辞职了，由我的副手接任。<br>My father has <b>handed over the business to</b> me.<br>我父亲把企业交给了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ally ˌhand sth aˈround</b></td><td class="c3">分发；传递(尤指食物和饮料)<br><span class="en">to offer or pass sth (especially food and drink) to each person in a group of people or in a room</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>hand</b> round the sandwiches, please?<br>请分发一下三明治好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hang</b></td><td class="c2"><b>k,hang aˈround (BrE also,hang a bout/ˈround) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">等待；等候</td><td class="c4">Sorry to keep you hanging <b>around</b> for so long.<br>对不起，让你等了这么久。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sb<br>hang aˈbout/ˈround together <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人常呆在一起；泡在一块儿<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of time with sb or with a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">Bob and Tim hang around <b>together</b>.<br>鲍勃和蒂姆形影相随。<br>I don't like the kind of people she hangs <b>about</b> with.<br>我不喜欢她交往的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">畏缩不前；望而却步<br><span class="en">to not move forwards because you are nervous or afraid</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hung back</b>, afraid to go near the dog.<br>她站在原地，不敢走近那条狗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">留下；留在原处<br><span class="en">to stay behind in a place such as a school or an office after most of the other people have left</span></td><td class="c4">My friends rushed out, but I <b>hung back</b> to talk to the teacher.<br>朋友们急忙跑出去了，可我留下来找老师谈话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">退缩；迟疑<br><span class="en">to be unwilling to do sth; to hesitate</span></td><td class="c4">This is a great opportunity. We can't afford to <b>hang back</b>.<br>这是个绝好的机会。我们可不能再犹豫了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hang ˈon to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">保留；不卖掉；不放弃；不丢失<br><span class="en">to keep sb/sth; to not sell, give away or lose sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Hang on to</b> the receipt in case you want to change the dress.<br>留着发票，万一你想退换连衣裙时用。<br>You can <b>hang on to</b> the book for a bit longer if you want.<br>你想的话，可以暂时留着这本书。<br>The company seems to be incapable of <b>hanging on to</b> its staff.<br>公司似乎无法留住员工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">泡在某处；(和某人或群体)泡在一起</td><td class="c4">Where does he <b>hang out</b> these days?<br>他这些天常去哪儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">闲散；歇闲<br><span class="en">to spend time relaxing, doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">Weve just been <b>hanging out</b> and listening to music.<br>我们闲来无事，在听音乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hang sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把(衣服)晾；出去；把(旗帜等)挂出去<br><span class="en">to attach things that you have washed to a piece of string or rope outside so that they can dry; to attach sth such as a flag outside a window or in a street</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>hung</b> the washing :<b>out</b>?<br>你把洗好的衣服晾出去了吗。<br>Many houses <b>hung out</b> a banner supporting the march.<br>很多住房外惹挂了支持游行的横幅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhang ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">困扰；使苦恼<br><span class="en">if a problem, a threat or sth sad hangs over you, you think about it or worry about it a lot</span></td><td class="c4">A question mark <b>hangs over</b> the future of the club (= no one knows what is going to happen).<br>俱乐部的未来还是个问号。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hang toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">连贯；相符；一致<br><span class="en">to be well organized and fit together well; to have parts that all agree with each other</span></td><td class="c4">The book doesn't really <b>hang together</b>.<br>这本书结构不太紧密。<br>This account of what happened doesn't <b>hang together</b>.<br>对事件的这一描述前后矛盾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>hang ˈup<br>.hang sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…悬挂起来<br><span class="en">to attach sth from the top to a hook, a piece of string, etc. so that the lower part is free or loose; to be attached in this way</span></td><td class="c4">My dress <b>is</b> hanging up in the wardrobe.<br>我的连衣裙挂在衣柜里。<br>Shall <b>I</b> hang your coat up?<br>我帮你把外套挂起来好吗。<br>He took off his suit and hung <b>it</b> up carefully.<br>他脱掉西装，小心地挂了起来。p。<br><b>I</b> was so upset I hung up the phone.<br>我十分生气，挂断了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhang-up n</b></td><td class="c3">令人尴尬或烦恼的情感问题；心理障碍</td><td class="c4">He's got a real <b>hang-up</b> about his height.<br>他对自己的身高确实有心理障碍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhang with sb <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人泡在一块儿；厮混<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of time with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Are you still <b>hanging with</b> those loser guys?<br>你还和那些不成器的家伙混在一起吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hanker</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhanker after/for sth</b></td><td class="c3">渴望得到；渴求<br><span class="en">to want sth very much</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>hankered after</b> city life.<br>他向往城市生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>happen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhappen aˈlong/ˈby <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">意外来到；碰巧出现<br><span class="en">to arrive or appear unexpectedly</span></td><td class="c4">A police car <b>happened along</b> just at that moment.<br>就在那时，一辆警车出乎意料地出现了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhappen on/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(old-fashioned)</span></b></td><td class="c3">偶然发现(某物)；碰巧遇见(某人)<br><span class="en">to find or meet sb/sth by chance</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>happened upon</b> the book I wanted in a second-hand bookshop.<br>在一家二手书店我碰巧发现了我想要的那本书。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hark ˈback to sth</b></td><td class="c3">重提；忆起(过去的事)<br><span class="en">to talk about or remember sth that happened in the past or was mentioned before</span></td><td class="c4">You can't keep <b>harking back to</b> the past.<br>你不能没完没了地念叨从前。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>harp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌharp ˈon (about sth)<br>ˈharp on sth</b></td><td class="c3">喋喋不休地谈论；啰唆个没完<br><span class="en">nformal to keep talking about sth in a way that other people find annoying</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>harping</b> on the same theme.<br>他总是翻来覆去地念叨同一个话题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>harsh</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈharsh on sb <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">批评；责难<br><span class="en">to criticize sb</span></td><td class="c4">In his blog he <b>harshed on</b> actresses who jump on the anti-war bandwagon.<br>他在博客上指责了那些追随反战潮流的女演员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hash sth ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">仔细商定<br><span class="en">to discuss sth in detail for a long time in order to reach an agreement</span></td><td class="c4">They are still <b>hashing out</b> the details of the contract.<br>他们还在反复商讨合同的细节。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hatch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhatch ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">虫等孵出；破壳；而出；(蛋)孵化<br><span class="en">when a bird, an insect, etc. hatches out, it comes out of the egg; when an egg hatches out, it breaks open and a bird, an insect, etc. comes out</span></td><td class="c4">The chicks <b>hatch out</b> after fifteen days.<br>小鸡的孵化期是十五天。<br>Have the eggs <b>hatched out</b> yet?<br>那些蛋孵化了吗。<br>When will the caterpillars <b>hatch out</b>?<br>幼虫什么时候孵化出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>haul</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhaul sth ˈin <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">贏得；挣得<br><span class="en">to win or earn sth</span></td><td class="c4">The thirty-year-old <b>hauled in</b> five gold medals.<br>这位三十岁的选手摘得五枚金牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>haul sb ˈoff (to sth/ ..) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">强行带走某人(到某处)<br><span class="en">to take sb somewhere by force</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>hauled him off</b> to jail.<br>他们押送他去了监狱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>haul sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把某人提交法庭审判<br><span class="en">to make sb appear in court to be judged</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>hauled up</b> on a charge of dangerous driving.<br>他被控危险驾驶，交由法院审判。语态。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>have</b></td><td class="c2"><b>have sth aˈgainst sb/sth (also have; got sth aˈgainst sb/sth) not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">I don't know what she <b>had against</b> me.<br>我不知道她反感我什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>g<br>have sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">收回；要回(借出或被拿走的东西)<br><span class="en">to receive sth that has been borrowed or taken from you</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>have the book back</b> by Thursday?<br>星期四之前能把书还给我吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>have sb ˈin (also have,got sb ˈin)</b></td><td class="c3">让某人来(家里或办公室)工作<br><span class="en">to have sb doing some work in your home or office</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>had the inspectors in</b> on Tuesday.<br>我们星期二接受检查员检查了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>have sth ˈin (also have,got sth ˈin) not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Do we <b>have enough food in</b> for the holiday?<br>我们的食物足够整个假期之用吗。<br>I wanted to get a new swimsuit, but the store didn't <b>have any in</b> yet.<br>我想买件新游泳衣，可商。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>have sth ˈon sb/sth (also have,got sth ˈon sb/sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">not used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>had a red jacket on</b>.<br>她身穿红色夹克衫。<br>He <b>had nothing on</b>.<br>他一丝不挂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>have sb ˈup (for sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(內某事)出庭受审<br><span class="en">informaf to accuse sb of sth and bring them to court to be examined by a judge</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>had up</b> for dangerous driving.<br>他因危险驾驶被送上法庭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hawk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhawk sth aˈbout/aˈround/round sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">沿街叫卖；(在…)兜售<br><span class="en">to try to sell things by going from place to place asking people to buy them</span></td><td class="c4">Pirate copies of their were being <b>hawked around</b>.<br>有人在街上兜售他们。<br>They <b>hawked their newsletter around</b> student bars.<br>他们在学生小卖部推销他们的小册子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>heal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌheal ˈup/ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">伤口等愈合；痊愈<br><span class="en">if a cut, a wound, etc. heals up/over, it closes and becomes healthy again</span></td><td class="c4">Her leg took a long tume to <b>heal up</b>.<br>她的腿过了很久才痊愈。<br>The cut has <b>healed over</b> now.<br>伤口现已愈合。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>heap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>heap sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">堆放<br><span class="en">to put sth into a pile</span></td><td class="c4">A huge pile of washing was <b>heaped up</b> in a corner.<br>角落里放了一大堆待洗衣物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hear sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">听某人把话讲完<br><span class="en">to listen until sb has finished saying what they want to say</span></td><td class="c4">I know you don't believe me, but please <b>hear me out</b>!<br>我知道你不相信我，可是请听我说完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>heat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>heat ˈup (AmE) - R<br>heat ˈup<br>ˌheat sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使变暖；变热<br><span class="en">to become warm or hot; to make sth warm or hot</span></td><td class="c4">The pipes will expand as they <b>heat up</b>.<br>管子变热就会膨胀。<br>We can <b>heat up</b> the soup in the microwave.<br>我们可以把汤放在微波炉里热。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hedge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hedge sth aˈbout/aˈround/ˈround with sth <span class="tag">(BrE formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以…限定；限制<br><span class="en">to surround and limit sth with conditions or restrictions</span></td><td class="c4">Employment is <b>hedged around with</b> legislation nowadays.<br>如今雇工受法律约束。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhedge sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">围绕着；约束住<br><span class="en">to surround sb/sth with sth; to restrict the freedom of sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">The cathedral is <b>hedged in</b> by other buildings.<br>大教堂四周有建筑物环绕。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>help</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhelp sth aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">加速；促进<br><span class="en">to try to make sth happen more quickly or easily</span></td><td class="c4">My mother always says that a cup of tea <b>helps things along</b>.<br>我母亲总是说喝杯茶效率高。<br>His father's name <b>helped along</b> his career in the early days.<br>他父亲的名气为他早年的事业铺平了道路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>help sb ˈoff/ˈon with sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮某人脱去；穿上衣服<br><span class="en">to help sb to take off or put on a piece of clothing, such as a coat</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>helped him on with</b> his dressing gown.<br>她帮他穿上了晨衣。<br>My dad said he'd <b>help</b> me out with money.<br>我爸爸说他会借钱给我救急的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhelp sb to sth<br>ˈhelp yourself to sth</b></td><td class="c3">为某人；或自己取用(食物或饮料)<br><span class="en">to give sb/yourself some food or drink</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>help anyone to</b> more chicken?<br>再给哪位来点鸡肉好吗。<br>Please <b>help yourselves to</b> salad.<br>吃色拉请自己米。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hem</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hem sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">包围；框住；制约<br><span class="en">to surround sb/sth with sth so that they cannot move freely</span></td><td class="c4">The thick trees <b>hemmed them in</b> on all sides.<br>他们四周密林环绕。<br>The ship was <b>hemmed in</b> by the ice.<br>船的四周都是冰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>herd</b></td><td class="c2"><b>herd toˈgether<br>.herd sb/sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使成群结队移动<br><span class="en">to move or make sb/sth move in a particular direction</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>herded together</b> into trucks and driven away.<br>他们被一起赶上卡车带走了。语态。</td></tr>

<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hide aˈway<br>hide yourself aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">躲起来；躲藏<br><span class="en">to go to a place secretly because you do not want anyone to find you</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hid herself away</b> until she felt better.<br>她躲了起来，直到心情好些。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hide ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">躲避；隐匿(以避开某人)<br><span class="en">to go to a secret place to escape from sb who is trying to find you</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>hid out</b> in the woods.<br>他藏在树林中。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hike</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhike sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">拉起；提起(衣服)<br><span class="en">to lift or pull up a piece of clothing that you are wearing</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>hiked up</b> his trousers and waded into the water.<br>他提起裤子趟进水里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hinge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhinge on sth also ˈhinge upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">随…而定；受…影响；依…而定<br><span class="en">if an action, a result, etc.hinges on/upon sth, it depends on it completely or is strongly influenced by it</span></td><td class="c4">The success of the project <b>hinges</b> on how well everyone works together.<br>这个项目能否成功取决于大家的合作情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hint</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhint at sth</b></td><td class="c3">暗示；示意；透露<br><span class="en">to suggest in an indirect way that sth is true or likely</span></td><td class="c4">In his speech the Prime Minister <b>hinted at</b> an early election.<br>首相在讲话中暗示会提前举行选举。<br>The problem was only <b>hinted at</b>.<br>这个问题只是从侧面提到过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hire</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hire sb ˈout<br>ˌhire yourself ˈout (to sb) (as sth)</b></td><td class="c3">安排聘用；(作为…)受雇(于)<br><span class="en">to arrange for sb to work for sb else; to arrange to work for sb</span></td><td class="c4">The agency <b>hires out</b> Cleaning staff.<br>这家代理公司派出清洁人员提供服务。<br>He <b>hires himself out</b> to farmers at harvest time.<br>到了收获季节，他就给农场主当雇工。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hire ˈon<br>hire sb ˈon <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">受雇(担任某职位)；雇用(某人)<br><span class="en">to take a particular job or position; to give sb a job</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hired on</b> as a claims adjuster with an insurance company.<br>她受聘于一家保险公司任理赔核算员。<br>We've <b>hired on</b> thirty new staff members this month alone.<br>仅在本月我们就聘用了三十名新员工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhire sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">出租；把…租给某人<br><span class="en">to allow sb to use sth for a short period of time in return for payment</span></td><td class="c4">The club will <b>hire out</b> tennis rackets to guests.<br>俱乐部向客人出租网球拍。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhit sb for sth (also,hit sb ˈup for sth) <span class="tag">(slang, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向某人索要(尤指金钱)<br><span class="en">to ask sb for sth,especially money</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>hit us for</b> a commission as well.<br>他们还向我们索取佣金呢。<br>Does he always <b>hit you for</b> cash when he wants new clothes?<br>他想买新衣服时总是向你伸手要钱吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hit it ˈoff (with sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人一见如故；投缘；合得来<br><span class="en">if two people hit it off with each other, they like each other and become friendly immediately</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>hit</b> it of from the start.<br>我们一开始很投缘。<br>She didn't really <b>hit it off with the office</b> manager.<br>起初她和办公室经理真有点合不来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhit on sb <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与某人搭讪；调情<br><span class="en">to talk to sb in a way that shows you are sexually attracted to them</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>hitting on</b> my girlfriend!<br>他居然调戏我的女友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hitch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hitch sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">拉起；提起(衣服)<br><span class="en">to pull up a piece of your clothing</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>hitched up</b> our skirts and climbed over the wall.<br>我们提起裙子，翻墙而过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhive sth ˈoff (into/to sth) (business)</b></td><td class="c3">把(一部分)分离出来；卖掉公司；的一部分<br><span class="en">to separate sth from a larger group; to sell part of a</span></td><td class="c4">Some of the firm's operations have been <b>hived off</b> into a separate company.<br>公司的部分业务已经剥离出来，成立了一家公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hoist</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hoist sb/sth ˈup<br>ˌhoist yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用绳索等特殊裝置或费劲；地升起；扯起<br><span class="en">to raise sb/sth/yourself to a higher position or level, often with difficulty or using ropes or special equipment</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hoisted the box up</b> onto the shelf.<br>她吃力地把箱子搬到搁板上。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hold</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">按下；摁住</td><td class="c4">He was <b>held down</b> and kicked by the two men.<br>两个男人按住他，踢他了几脚。<br><b>Hold the mouse button down</b> as you move the cursor.<br>移动光标时，按住鼠标键。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">努力保住工作；职位等<br><span class="en">to manage to keep a job, position, etc. even though it may be difficult for you to do so</span></td><td class="c4">He doesn't seem able to <b>hold down</b> a full-time job.<br>他似乎无力保住一份全职工作。p a。<br>The rate of inflation must be <b>held down</b>.<br>通货膨胀率必须控制在低水平上。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhold sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…固定在里面<br><span class="en">to keep sth inside a place so that it cannot fall out or escape</span></td><td class="c4">The straps <b>hold the baby in</b> securely.<br>带子把婴儿安全地系在里面。o1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">抵抗；抗击<br><span class="en">to resist an attack by an enemy or an opponent</span></td><td class="c4">How long do You think you can <b>hold off</b> the attack?<br>你认为这轮进攻你能顶多长时间。<br>He <b>held off</b> a late challenge from Davies to win the race.<br>他在后程较量中顶住了戴维斯的冲击，贏得了比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>hold ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">等一下；停一下<br><span class="en">used to ask sb to wait or stop for a short time</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Hold on</b>! That doesn't sound right.<br>等一会儿！这听上去不对劲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>hold ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">困境或险境中生存下来；坚持住；挺住<br><span class="en">to survive in a difficult or dangerous situation; to continue doing sth although it is difficult</span></td><td class="c4">They managed to <b>hold on</b> until help arrived.<br>他们总算撑到了救援到来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">固定(某物的位置)<br><span class="en">to keep sth in position so that it cannot fall off</span></td><td class="c4">It is these nuts and bolts that <b>hold the wheels on</b>.<br>就是这些螺母和螺栓把轮子固定住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈonto sb/sth<br>hold ˈon to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…留下来；不失去<br><span class="en">to keep sth/sb; to not lose sth/sb</span></td><td class="c4">The party will <b>hold on to</b> its majority at the next election.<br>该党在下次选举中将保持其多数优势。<br>She's a good worker. You should <b>hold on to</b> her.<br>她很能干。你应该把她留住。<br>You must pass the ball and not <b>hold onto</b> it.<br>你得把球传给别人，不要黏球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhold ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">钱款；供应品等持续保有；未耗尽<br><span class="en">if money or supplies, etc. hold out, they last or remain</span></td><td class="c4">Do you think the fine weather will <b>hold out</b>?<br>你认为好天气会持续下去吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhold ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">拒绝；拒不接受<br><span class="en">(against sth) to refuse to accept sth that you do not agree with</span></td><td class="c4">We can't <b>hold out</b> against industrialization any longer.<br>我们不能再拒绝工业化了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈout sth</b></td><td class="c3">提供(机会)；给予(希望)；有可能<br><span class="en">to offer a chance, hope or possibility of sth</span></td><td class="c4">He may come, but I don't <b>hold out</b> much hope.<br>他也许会来，可我不抱很大希望。<br>This method seems to <b>hold out</b> the greatest promise of success.<br>这种方法似乎最有希望成功。<br>You must be Kate,' he said, <b>holding out</b> his hand.<br>绳子。<br>He <b>held</b> on to the back of the chair to stop himself from falling.<br>他抓住椅背，避免摔倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhold ˈout for sth</b></td><td class="c3">为得到更大利益拖延达成协议；拒绝让步<br><span class="en">to deliberately delay reaching an agreement in the hope that you will gain sth; to refuse to accept anything less than what you are asking for</span></td><td class="c4">Union leaders are <b>holding out for</b> a better deal.<br>工会领导人拒不让步，以期达成更有利的协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈout on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">拒绝告诉(或给予)某人<br><span class="en">to refuse to tell or give sb sth</span></td><td class="c4">You promised to give me the money. Stop <b>holding out on</b> me.<br>你答应过给我钱的。不许赖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">搁置；推迟<br><span class="en">to leave sth to be dealt with later</span></td><td class="c4">We decided to <b>hold the matter over</b> until the next meeting.<br>我们决定将此事延迟到下次会议处理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhold to sth</b></td><td class="c3">坚持意见；信念等<br><span class="en">if you hold to an opinion, a belief, etc., you do not change it</span></td><td class="c4">She always <b>holds to</b> her principles.<br>她始终坚持自己的原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhold sth to sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…靠近…放；把…放在…旁边<br><span class="en">to place sth close to sth else</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>held a knife to</b> her throat.<br>他用刀顶着她的喉咙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold toˈgether<br>ˌhold sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使.保持团结<br><span class="en">to remain, or to keep sb/sth, united</span></td><td class="c4">The coalition has <b>held together</b> for longer than expected.<br>联盟坚持的时间超出预料。<br>Strong bonds of loyalty <b>hold the family together</b>.<br>忠诚的纽带有力地把全家人凝聚在一起。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold toˈgether<br>ˌhold sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">未破碎；完好无损<br><span class="en">to remain in one piece; to stay in good condition</span></td><td class="c4">It's a miracle that his car is still <b>holding together</b>.<br>他的车依然完好，真是个奇迹。<br>His trousers were <b>held together</b> by safety pins.<br>他的裤子是用安全别针别在一块儿的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">支持住；承受住；支撑住<br><span class="en">to remain healthy, in good COTldition or working effectively, especially when there are difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">Sales have <b>held up</b> well, in spite of economic aufficulties.<br>尽管遇到了经济困难，销售额还相当可观。<br>How did your tent <b>hold up</b> in the storm?<br>你的帐篷是如何挺过风暴的？2。<br>He <b>held up</b> his trophy as the crowd applauded.<br>在众人的掌声中，他举起奖杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">支撑；使不垮下<br><span class="en">to support sb/sth and prevent it/them from falling</span></td><td class="c4">Her trousers were <b>held up</b> with string.<br>她的裤子是用带子吊着的。<br>She phoned to say she'd been <b>held up</b> at the office.<br>她打来电话说，她在办公室脱不开身。<br>I don't want to <b>hold you up</b>.<br>我不想耽误你的时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">持枪抢劫人；银行；商店等<br><span class="en">to rob a person, a bank, a shop/store, etc. using a gun</span></td><td class="c4">Have caught the people who <b>held up</b> the bank?<br>他们抓到持枪打劫银行的人了吗？语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hold sb/sth ˈup as sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…作为…的例子<br><span class="en">to present sb/sth as an example of sth</span></td><td class="c4">My mother <b>held up my cousin as</b> an example of a good student.<br>我母亲把我表哥看作优秀学生的典范。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhold with sth</b></td><td class="c3">同意；赞成<br><span class="en">to agree with or approve of sth</span></td><td class="c4">I don't <b>hold with</b> these new theories on education.<br>我不赞同这些新的教育理论。</td></tr>
