<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hole</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hole ˈup<br>be,holed ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">躲藏<br><span class="en">to hide somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">The thieves <b>holed up</b> in an empty warehouse.<br>盗贼躲在一个空仓库里。<br>The police couldn't find out where the gang were <b>holed up</b>.<br>警方查不到那个团伙的藏身处。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hollow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hollow sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">挖空；挖出孔<br><span class="en">to make a space inside sth by removing part of it</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>hollowed out</b> the pumpkin and put a candle in it.<br>我们把南瓜挖空，在里面插了根蜡烛。o a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hollow sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">挖洞(成某物)<br><span class="en">to form sth by making a hole in sth else</span></td><td class="c4">The waves have <b>hollowed out</b> caves along the cliff.<br>海浪拍击峭壁，形成了一个个岩洞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>home</b></td><td class="c2"><b>home ˈin on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">移向；朝向；导向<br><span class="en">to move or be aimed straight towards sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>homed in on</b> me as soon as she saw me.<br>她一看见我就向我直奔过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>home ˈin on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把注意力集中于；全神贯注于<br><span class="en">to turn all your attention to sth</span></td><td class="c4">The lawyer <b>homed in on</b> the inconsistencies in her story.<br>律师将注意力集中在她的陈述中前后矛盾的地方。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hook</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hook sb ˈinto sth<br>hook sb ˈinto doing sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">说服某人做；某事<br><span class="en">informaf to persuade sb to do sth when they do not want to</span></td><td class="c4">I didn't want to be involved but I got <b>hooked into</b> helping.<br>我原本不想参与，可架不住劝，还是帮了忙。<br>He tried to <b>hook me into</b> going with them.<br>他试图劝我跟他们一道去。总是用于被动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hook ˈup (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">同意(与某人)搭档工作<br><span class="en">to agree to work with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Weve <b>hooked up</b> with a firm in Ireland.<br>我们答应了和爱尔兰的一家公司合作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hook ˈup (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">与某人结识；联系上<br><span class="en">to meet sb and spend time with them</span></td><td class="c4">On vacation we <b>hooked up</b> with some Texans.<br>度假时我们结交了一些得克萨斯人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hook ˈup<br>ˌhook sb/sth ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使接通(电子设备或电源)<br><span class="en">to connect sb/sth to a piece of electronic equipment or to a power supply</span></td><td class="c4">All the speakers <b>hook up</b> to a single amplifier.<br>所有喇叭都接在同一个扩音器上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hook sb ˈup with sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用(贵重礼物)向(某人)行贿<br><span class="en">to give sb a valuable gift because of their job or Position</span></td><td class="c4">My clients from the music industry often <b>hook me up with</b> free tickets.<br>音乐界的客户经常用赠票巴结我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hoover</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hoover sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用真空吸尘器吸(灰尘等)<br><span class="en">to remove dust, dirt, etc. from a carpet or floor with a Hoover</span></td><td class="c4">The and Canada usually <b>hoover up</b> all the gold and silver medals.<br>美国和加拿大通常会囊括所有金银牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>horn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>horn ˈin <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">粗暴地打断(别人的谈话)<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) to rudely interrupt sb when they are speaking</span></td><td class="c4">She kept trying to <b>horn in</b> on our conversations.<br>她老是无礼地打断我们的交谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>horn ˈin <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">干涉(与己无关的事情)<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) to interfere in a situation that does not concern you</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>horning in</b> on my private life!<br>不要干涉我的私生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hot ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">更趋活跃；激烈起来<br><span class="en">also ˌheat ˈup informal to become more lively or exciting</span></td><td class="c4">Things are <b>hotting up</b> as the election approaches.<br>随着选举临近，渐渐出现了一片热闹的景象。<br>As the pace <b>hotted up</b>, he dropped back into third place.<br>随着节奏加快，他滑落到了第三名。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>huddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>huddle toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">靠拢在一起(以取暖或寻求保护)<br><span class="en">to move, stand or sit close to one another for warmth or protection</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>huddled together</b> for warmth.<br>我们挤在一起取暖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>huddle ˈup (against/to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">蜷缩；紧挨着(以取暖或寻求保护)<br><span class="en">to press yourself into a small space for warmth or protection</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>huddled up</b> against him to keep warm.<br>她蜷起身紧挨着他来保暖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hunger</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhunger after/for sth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">渴望得到；渴求<br><span class="en">to have a strong desire for sth and try to get it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hungers after</b> wealth and Prestige.<br>她渴求名利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hunker</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hunker ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">蹲坐<br><span class="en">to sit on your heels with your knees bent up in front of you</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>hunkered down</b> around the fire.<br>我们围绕火堆蹲坐着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hunker ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始努力(工作或学习)<br><span class="en">to start to work at sth or study very hard</span></td><td class="c4">It's time you <b>hunkered down</b> and started studying.<br>你该全身心地投入学斗丁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hunt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>hunt sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">追捕；抓捕<br><span class="en">to search for sb until you find or catch them</span></td><td class="c4">He vowed to <b>hunt down</b> the killer.<br>他发誓要捉拿凶手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hunt sth ˈdown/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">经过千辛万苦搜寻出；寻找到<br><span class="en">to find sth after a long and difficult search</span></td><td class="c4">I managed to <b>hunt out</b> those files you wanted.<br>我总算找到了你要的文件。<br>Can you <b>hunt down</b> his phone number for me?<br>你能帮我查到他的电话号码吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈhunt for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">寻找；寻求<br><span class="en">to look for sth that is dif. ficult to find</span></td><td class="c4">She is still <b>hunting for</b> a new job.<br>她仍在寻觅一份新工作。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hurry</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhurry sb/sth aˈlong</b></td><td class="c3">催促(某人)；加快(某事)<br><span class="en">to do or say sth to make sb move or work faster; to do sth to make sth happen faster</span></td><td class="c4">Try to <b>hurry things along</b> a bit.<br>尽量加快点速度。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhurry ˈon (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">喋喋不休(不让别人开口)<br><span class="en">to continue speaking, without allowing anyone to interrupt or speak</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>hurried on</b> to the next topic before I could object.<br>我还没来得及提出异议，她就继续讲下一个话题了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>hurry ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">赶快；麻利点<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to move or do sth more quickly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Hurry up</b>, we have to leave in five minutes!<br>利索一点，我们五分钟后就得走了。<br>I wish the bus would <b>hurry up</b> and come.<br>我希望公共汽车能快点来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>hurry sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">催促(某人)；加快(某事)<br><span class="en">to encourage sb to move or work faster; to do sth to make sth happen faster</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Hurry your brother up</b> or well be late.<br>催一下你弟弟，不然我们要迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hush</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhush sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">隐瞒；遮掩(丑闻等)<br><span class="en">to hide information about a situation, especially sth bad or shocking, because you do not want people to know about it</span></td><td class="c4">The government tried to <b>hush the affair up</b>.<br>政府试图隐瞒此事。<br>The scandal was <b>hushed up</b>.<br>这桩丑行被捂住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>hype</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌhype sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">夸张地宣传；大肆炒作<br><span class="en">to advertise or talk about sb/sth in an exaggerated way in order to get a lot of public attention for them/it</span></td><td class="c4">His latest movie is being <b>hyped up</b> by the media.<br>媒体正大肆炒作他最新的电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ice</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ice sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">冰冻；冰起来<br><span class="en">to put ice on, around, or in sth to keep it cold</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>iced down</b> the champagne?<br>香槟你冰镇了没有。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ice ˈover/ˈup<br>be icedˈover/up</b></td><td class="c3">覆盖着一层；结冰<br><span class="en">to become covered by a layer of ice</span></td><td class="c4">The road had <b>iced over</b> during the night.<br>道路夜间结了冰。<br>The windscreen had <b>iced up</b>.<br>挡风玻璃上结了一层冰。<br>The lake was <b>iced up</b>.<br>湖面结冰了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>identify</b></td><td class="c2"><b>iˈdentify sb with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">认为某人是…；认为某人与…有密切联系<br><span class="en">to consider sb to be sth or to be closely connected with sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The last thing she wanted was to be <b>identified with</b> her parents.<br>她最讨厌别人将她和父母联系在一起。<br>Many of these artists were closely <b>identified with</b> Cubist painting.<br>这些艺术家中的很多人被看作属于立体主义画派。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>idle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌidle sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">混时间；无所事事<br><span class="en">to spend time doing nothing very important</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>idled away</b> their time watching television.<br>他们看电视消磨时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>imbue</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈbue sb/sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">賦予(某特点)；灌输；使充满(强烈感情等)<br><span class="en">to fill sb/sth with a strong feeling, quality, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He managed to <b>imbue his employees with</b> team spirit.<br>他成功地激发了员工的团队精神。<br>The painting is <b>imbued with</b> energy and life.<br>这幅画充满活力与生机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>immerse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈmerse sb/yourself in sth</b></td><td class="c3">使沉浸于；醉心于；投入<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb become, completely involved in sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>immersed</b> himself in his studies.<br>他潜心研究。<br>I was completely <b>immersed</b> in the story.<br>我完全沉浸在故事中。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>impinge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈpinge on sb/sth also imˈpinge upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">对…造成严重；影响(尤指负面影响)<br><span class="en">to have a strong effect on sb/sth, especially a bad one</span></td><td class="c4">She didn't allow her personal problems to <b>impinge</b> on her work.<br>她不让个人问题妨碍工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>impose</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈpose on sb</b></td><td class="c3">强人所难；勉强某人<br><span class="en">to expect sb to do sth for you or spend time with you when they do not have much time, or when it may not be convenient for them</span></td><td class="c4">Tim never says No', so people are always <b>imposing on</b> him.<br>蒂姆从不拒绝别人，所以别人常常要他做这做那。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>impress</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈpress sth on sb (also imˈpress sth upon sb more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">向某人强调某事；的重要性或严重性<br><span class="en">to emphasize to sb how important or serious sth is</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>impressed on</b> her staff the importance of keeping accurate records.<br>她向员工强调准确记录的重要性。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈpress sth/itself on sth also imˈpress sth/itself upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">给…留下深刻印象；使铭记<br><span class="en">if impresses sth on or sth impresses itself on your mind, memory, etc., it has a great effect on you so that you do not forget it</span></td><td class="c4">His words <b>impressed</b> themselves on my memory.<br>他的话我铭记在心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>improve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈprove on sth also imˈprove upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">完善；改进<br><span class="en">to achieve or produce sth of a better standard or quality than sth else</span></td><td class="c4">There are a few points in your work that you could <b>improve</b> on.<br>你的工作中有几个地方有待改进。<br>The Kenyan girl <b>improved</b> on her previous best performance (= in a race).<br>那名肯尼亚女选手超越了自己以往的最好成绩。<br>These results cannot be <b>improved</b> <b>upon</b>.<br>这些成果无法超越。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>impute</b></td><td class="c2"><b>imˈpute sth to sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常指不公平地将…归咎于；认为…具有(某种特质)<br><span class="en">to say, often unfairly, that sb/sth is responsible for sth, or has a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">Why do you <b>impute selfish motives to</b> her?<br>为什么你认为她是出于私心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>incline</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈcline to/towards sth<br>inˈcline sb</b></td><td class="c3">使倾向于<br><span class="en">to/towards sth formal to tend to think or behave in a particular way; to make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">Her love of languages <b>inclined her towards</b> a career as a translator.<br>她对语言的热爱促使她当了翻译。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>indulge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈdulge in sth</b></td><td class="c3">沉迷于；沉湎于；沉溺于<br><span class="en">to allow yourself to have or do sth that you like, often sth that is bad for you</span></td><td class="c4">He now has time to <b>indulge in</b> his favourite hobby: Photography. It's a luxury that can only be indulged in from time to time.<br>这种奢侈只能偶尔享用一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>inform</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈform on sb</b></td><td class="c3">举报；告发<br><span class="en">to give evidence about sb or accuse sb of sth, to the police or sb in authority</span></td><td class="c4">One of the gang <b>informed on</b> the rest.<br>团伙中的一人告发了其他人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>infringe</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈfringe on sth (also inˈfringe upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">限制；侵害；侵犯某人的自由；权利等<br><span class="en">to limit sb's freedom, rights, etc</span></td><td class="c4">The media is accused of <b>infringing on</b> people's privacy.<br>媒体被指责侵犯人们的隐私。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>infuse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈfuse A into B<br>inˈfuse B with A <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">赋予；注入；使充满(某种特质)<br><span class="en">to fill sb/sth with a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">His arrival <b>infused</b> new life and energy <b>into</b> the team.<br>他的到来为团队注入新的生气和活力。<br>Her work is <b>infused</b> with anger.<br>她的作品充满了激愤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>insist</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈsist upon sth, inˈsist upon doing sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">坚决要求；坚持主张<br><span class="en">to demand sth and refuse to be persuaded to accept anything else</span></td><td class="c4">They are <b>insisting</b> on a meeting tomorrow.<br>他们坚持明天开会。<br>I always <b>insist</b> on skimmed milk.<br>我从来只喝脱脂牛奶。<br>He <b>insisted</b> on walking home with her.<br>他执意要和她一起走回家。<br>This format must be <b>insisted</b> on.<br>必须使用这一格式。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>interest</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈinterest sb in sth</b></td><td class="c3">劝某人做某事；使某人对某事感兴趣<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to buy, do or eat sth</span></td><td class="c4">Could I <b>interest you in</b> this model (= of car), Sir?<br>先生，您有兴趣看看这款车吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>interfere</b></td><td class="c2"><b>interˈfere with sb <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出于猥亵目的触摸(幼童)<br><span class="en">to touch a child in a sexual way</span></td><td class="c4">We don't want to <b>interfere with</b> your plans.<br>我们不想打乱你的计划。2 t0。<br>The evidence has been <b>interfered with</b>.<br>有人对证据动了手脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>inure</b></td><td class="c2"><b>iˈnure sb/yourself to sth</b></td><td class="c3">使习惯于；使适应(令人不快的事物)<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth get used to sth unpleasant so that they are no longer strongly affected by it</span></td><td class="c4">The prisoners quickly became <b>inured</b> to the harsh conditions.<br>囚犯很快便适应了恶劣的条件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>invalid</b></td><td class="c2"><b>invalid sb ˈout<br>invalid sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(因病或因伤)离职(或退役)<br><span class="en">to make sb leave a job, especially in the armed forces, because they are ill/sick or injured</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>invalided</b> <b>out</b> of the army because of his injuries.<br>他因伤从部队退役了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>inveigh</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈveigh against sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛烈抨击；痛骂</td><td class="c4">The article went on to <b>inveigh against</b> political correctness and all the perceived evils of the modern world.<br>该文继而痛斥“政治正确”这一观念以及现代社会各色罪恶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>invest</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈvest in sth <span class="tag">(informal, often humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">购买有用之物；尤指；贵重物品<br><span class="en">to buy sth or spend money on sth useful, especially sth expensive</span></td><td class="c4">It's time we <b>invested in</b> a new sofathis one is falling to bits.<br>我们该买新沙发了—这一套都快散架了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈvest sb/sth with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使似乎具有(某种特质)<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth seem to have a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">Being the boss <b>invests her with</b> a certain glamour.<br>当上老板似乎为她平添了几分魅力。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>involve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>inˈvolve sb in sth</b></td><td class="c3">使经历；使陷入(尤指不快之事)<br><span class="en">to make sb experience or do sth, especially sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">The new exams have <b>involved teachers in</b> a lot of extra work.<br>新的考试给老师们带来大量额外工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>iron</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌiron sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">熨平；烫平(衣服等的皱褶)<br><span class="en">to remove the folds that you do not want from clothes, etc. by using an iron</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Iron out</b> all the creases.<br>熨平所有的褶皱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>itch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈitch for sth usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">They were just <b>itching</b> for a fight.<br>他们摩拳擦掌，想打上一架。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jabber</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jabber aˈway informalto speak or talk quickly in</b></td><td class="c3">急促兴奋地说话</td><td class="c4">She <b>jabbered</b> <b>away</b>, trying to distract his attention.<br>她喋喋不休，想分散他的注意力。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jack sb aˈround <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">搪塞；怠慢；浪费某人的时间<br><span class="en">informaf to treat sb in a way that is deliberately not helpful to them or wastes their time</span></td><td class="c4">Let's go. We're being <b>jacked around</b> here.<br>我们走。这里的人在敷衍我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>jack sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">停止；放弃(尤指工作)<br><span class="en">to stop doing sth, especially your job</span></td><td class="c4">She decided to <b>jack in</b> her job.<br>她决定辞职。<br>After such a bad day I feel like <b>jacking it all in</b>.<br>这么倒霉的一天下来，我什么都不想干了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>jack sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">千斤顶托起(车辆等)<br><span class="en">to lift sth such as a vehicle off the ground using a special device (a jack)</span></td><td class="c4">The wholesalers have <b>jacked up</b> their prices.<br>批发商提价了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get jacked ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">毁坏；损坏<br><span class="en">to be ruined or spoiled</span></td><td class="c4">My <b>is all jacked up</b> right now.<br>我的电脑现在完全坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get jacked ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">紧张；激动<br><span class="en">to be nervous or excited</span></td><td class="c4">The whole school <b>is jacked up</b> about the game tonight.<br>全校的人都为今晚的比赛兴奋不已。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get jacked ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">喝醉<br><span class="en">to be drunk</span></td><td class="c4">Don't drive i youre too <b>jacked</b> up.<br>喝得烂醉了就别开车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jet</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jet ˈoff (to .. )</b></td><td class="c3">乘飞机去(尤指远方)<br><span class="en">to fly somewhere, especially somewhere far away</span></td><td class="c4">They're <b>jetting off</b> to Florida tomorrow.<br>他们明天要飞往佛罗里达。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jog aˈlong <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">缓慢平稳地进行<br><span class="en">to continue in a steady way, with little or no excitement or progress</span></td><td class="c4">For years the business just kept <b>jogging along</b>.<br>多年来生意一直不温不火。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>join</b></td><td class="c2"><b>join ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">与…会合<br><span class="en">(with sb/sth) to meet or combine with sb/sth to do sth together</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>joined up</b> with the rest of the party later.<br>他们后来与团队的其他人会合了。<br><b>Join up</b> the dots to see the picture.<br>把这些点连接起来就能看出图形了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈjoin with sb (in sth/in doing sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人一起(做某事)<br><span class="en">to do or say sth with sb else or with a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">Parents <b>joined with</b> teachers to protest against the closure of the school.<br>家长和教师联合抗议关闭学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jolly</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jolly sb aˈlong <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一直给…鼓劲<br><span class="en">to keep encouraging sb in a friendly way</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>jolly him along</b> but he couldn't forget his problems.<br>她一直鼓励他，但他忘不掉自己的问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>juice</b></td><td class="c2"><b>juice sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使更生动；使更激动人心；使更有趣</td><td class="c4"><b>Juice up</b> your talk with pictures.<br>用图片使你的演讲更活泼些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jumble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jumble sth ˈup/toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使混乱；使杂乱<br><span class="en">to mix things up in a confused way</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure you don't <b>jumble everything up</b>.<br>一定不要把东西全都弄乱了。<br>The details of the accident were all <b>jumbled together</b> in his mind.<br>他把事故细节记得颠三倒四。<br>All her papers had been <b>jumbled up</b>.<br>她的文件都搞乱套了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jump ˈout at sb</b></td><td class="c3">对某人来说非常显眼；显而易见<br><span class="en">to be very easy to see; to be noticeable</span></td><td class="c4">The headline <b>jumped out at</b> me.<br>我一眼就看见了醒目的标题。<br>The mistakes are so obvious they <b>jump out at</b> you.<br>这些错误十分显眼，一眼就看到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>jump ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">坐着突然起身；一跃而起<br><span class="en">to stand quickly and suddenly when you have been sitting</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>jumped up</b> off the floor.<br>他一下子从地板上站了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>jut</b></td><td class="c2"><b>jut ˈout (from sth)<br>jut ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…突出；伸出<br><span class="en">to stand out from sth; to stick out further than the surrounding surface</span></td><td class="c4">The tops of the flooded houses <b>jutted</b> <b>out</b> of the water.<br>遭水淹的房屋只有屋顶露出水面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>keel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>keel ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">倒下<br><span class="en">to fall over</span></td><td class="c4">The boat <b>keeled over</b> in the strong winds.<br>船在大风中翻了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>keep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkeep ˈafter sb (about sth/to do sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一再要求；反复提醒(某人做某事)<br><span class="en">to ask or tell sb repeatedly to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>keeps after</b> me to fix the TV.<br>她总是唠叨着让我修电视机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈat sth<br>ˌkeep sb ˈat sth</b></td><td class="c3">使继续努力；坚持干<br><span class="en">to continue to work hard at sth, or to make sb work hard at sth, particularly sth which is difficult or takes a long time</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep at</b> it, youve nearly finished!<br>别松劲，你马上就要完成了。<br>He <b>kept them at</b> the job until it was finished.<br>他让他们一直干到把活干完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>keep aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">避免靠近；远离</td><td class="c4"><b>Keep</b> away from me!<br>离我还点。<br>The police told us to <b>keep</b> well away from the area.<br>警察让我们避开那个地区。<br>We turned off the lights to <b>keep</b> the mosquitoes away.<br>我们关了灯，以免招蚊子。<br>Her parents are <b>keeping her away</b> from school for a few days.<br>她的父母让她这几天不去上学。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sb/sth ˈback (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使(与…)保持距离；避免；走近<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth remain at a distance from sb/sth; to prevent sb from moving forwards</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep the children back</b> from the fire.<br>别让小孩靠近炉火。<br>The police were trying to <b>keep back</b> the crowds.<br>当时警察正设法阻挡人群靠近。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">保留；预留<br><span class="en">to keep a part of sth to use later</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>kept some money back</b> to pay the bills?<br>你留出付账单的钱了吗。<br><b>Keep</b> a piece of cake <b>back</b> for Alex.<br>给亚历克斯留块蛋糕。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>keep sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使保持在低水平；抑制…的增长<br><span class="en">to make sth remain at a low level; to avoid increasing sth</span></td><td class="c4">We're trying to <b>keep</b> costs down.<br>我们正努力保持低成本。<br>He exercises a lot to <b>keep</b> his weight down.<br>他一个劲地锻炼，以控制体重。<br><b>Keep</b> your voice down!<br>小点声。<br>She <b>Kept</b> her eyes down while he was talking.<br>他讲话时她一直没拾眼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkeep from doing sth<br>ˈkeep yourself from doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">忍住不做某事<br><span class="en">to prevent yourself from doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">She bit her Lip to <b>keep</b> from laughing.<br>她咬着嘴唇，以免笑出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkeep sb from sth<br>ˈkeep sb from doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">阻止；某人做某事<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let me <b>keep you from</b> your work.<br>我可不想妨碍你工作。<br>Her pride <b>kept her from</b> crying in front of them.<br>她的自尊心不允许她在他们面前哭出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkeep sth from sb</b></td><td class="c3">告诉；隐瞒<br><span class="en">to avoid telling sb sth</span></td><td class="c4">I think he's <b>keeping secrets from</b> me.<br>我想他有秘密瞒着我。<br>Are you <b>keeping something from</b> us?<br>你有什么事儿瞒着我们吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sb ˈback (AmE also ˌkeep sb beˈhind)</b></td><td class="c3">罚(学生)课后留校<br><span class="en">to make a child stay after normal school hours as a punishment</span></td><td class="c4">The teacher <b>kept</b> them all in after school.<br>老师罚他们全部课后留校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sb ˈback (AmE also ˌkeep sb beˈhind)</b></td><td class="c3">不许(孩子)出门；留(孩子)在室内</td><td class="c4">I'm <b>keeping</b> the children in because it's raining outside.<br>外面下着雨，所以我让孩子们呆在屋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sb ˈback (AmE also ˌkeep sb beˈhind)</b></td><td class="c3">不让出院；使继续住院<br><span class="en">to keep sb in hospital</span></td><td class="c4">She's much better, but they're <b>keeping</b> her in overnight.<br>她好多了，但他们让她在医院住一夜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">克制；抑制(感情)<br><span class="en">to stop yourself expressing an emotion</span></td><td class="c4">He could hardly <b>keep in</b> his anger.<br>他几乎掩饰不住愤怒之情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkeep ˈin with sb <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…保持友好关系；不断讨好<br><span class="en">to continue to be friendly with sb, especially in order to gain some advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>keeps in with</b> anyone who might be useful to him.<br>只要是对他可能有用的人，他就一直巴结着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkeep ˈoff <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">雪等未下<br><span class="en">if rain, snow, etc. keeps off, it does not fall, even though it looks as if it might</span></td><td class="c4">The party will go ahead provided the rain <b>keeps Off</b>.<br>如果不下雨，聚会将照常举行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈoff<br>ˌkeep ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">不去(某处)<br><span class="en">to not go onto a particular area</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep off</b> (the grass)!<br>勿践踏(草坪)!°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈoff sth<br>keep sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">使戒忌食物或饮料；香烟<br><span class="en">to not eat, drink or smoke sth; to not let sb eat, drink or smoke sth</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor's told me to <b>keep off</b> red meat.<br>医生建议我不要吃牛羊肉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈoff sth<br>keep sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">回避(某一话题)；不让(某人)谈论(某一话题)<br><span class="en">to not mention a particular topic; to stop sb talking about a particular topic</span></td><td class="c4">It's best to <b>keep off</b> the subject of politics with my father.<br>最好不要和我父亲谈论政治话题。<br><b>Keep her off</b> the subject of teenage girls!<br>不要让她谈少女这个话题！8J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sb/sth ˈoff<br>keep sb/sth ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使不靠近；使不进入；避免…接触(或伤害)<br><span class="en">to stop sb/sth from coming near or going into (a place); to stop sb/sth from touching or harming sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He covered sandwiches to <b>keep the flies off</b>.<br>他盖上了三明治，免得招苍蝇。<br><b>Keep your animals off</b> my land!<br>别让你的牲口进我的地界。<br>Working helps <b>keep my mind off</b> my problems.<br>工作有助于让我忘掉烦恼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈon<br>keep ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">沿路继续走<br><span class="en">to continue to follow a particular route</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep on</b> until you come to the road.<br>一直往前走到公路。<br><b>Keep on</b> the path until you see a gate.<br>沿这条小路往前，直到看见一道大门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkeep sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续穿着；不脱下；不取下<br><span class="en">to continue to wear sth; to not take sth off</span></td><td class="c4">I was so cold that we <b>kept our socks on</b> in bed.<br>天气很冷，我们在床上没脱袜子。<br><b>Keep the lid on</b> while the tea is brewing.<br>沏茶时不要打开盖子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkeep sth on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">集中注意力于；专注于<br><span class="en">if you keep your mind, eyes, etc. on sb/sth, you fix your attention on them/it</span></td><td class="c4">I can't <b>keep my mind on</b> my work.<br>我没法集中精力工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈout of sth<br>ˌkeep sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">避免；(使)免受…的影响<br><span class="en">to avoid sth; to prevent sb/yourself from being affected by sth</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor has advised me to <b>keep out of</b> the sun.<br>医生建议我不要晒太阳。<br>They always <b>kept their daughter out of</b> the spotlight (= away from the public).<br>他们总是不让女儿拋头露面。<br>I try to <b>keep out of</b> his way.<br>我尽量躲着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不收走(从橱柜等拿出的东西)；把…预备好<br><span class="en">to not put sth away that you have taken out of a cupboard, etc.; to keep sth ready to use</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep the butter out</b> for your dad's breakfast.<br>把黄油留下，给你爸爸吃早餐用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌkeep sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">不进入(某处)；防止…进入(某处)；把…关；在(…的)外面<br><span class="en">to prevent sb/sth from entering a place</span></td><td class="c4">We hung a curtain at the door to <b>keep out</b> the cold.<br>我们在门上挂了条帘子，以防冷气进来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkeep to sth</b></td><td class="c3">不偏离；不离开(道路等)<br><span class="en">to not leave a path, a road, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Keep to</b> the footpath.<br>顺着人行道走。<br><b>Keep to</b> the left (= on a road, etc.).<br>靠左边行走。p。<br>Will you please <b>keep to</b> the subject under discussion?<br>请不要偏离讨论的主题好吗。<br>We must <b>keep to</b> the schedule.<br>我们必须按日程进行。<br>He never <b>keeps to</b> the speed limit.<br>他从不遵守速度限制。<br>Was the agenda <b>Kept to</b> at the meeting?<br>开会时是否严格遵守了议程？e。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>keep ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">雪等持续；不停<br><span class="en">if rain, snow, etc. keeps up, it continues without stopping</span></td><td class="c4">The rain <b>kept up</b> all afternoon.<br>兩下了整整一下午。2。<br>Do <b>keep up</b>! I can't keep repeating everything.<br>跟上，我不能每句话都重复。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>keep ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">与…同步上升<br><span class="en">(with sth) to rise at the same rate as sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Salaries are not <b>keeping up</b> with inflation.<br>工资的增长赶不上通货膨胀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>keep ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">按时完成(必要的任务)；处理好(瞬息万变的局面)<br><span class="en">(with sth) to do all the work necessary in order to finish on time or deal successfully with a situation that changes rapidly</span></td><td class="c4">Things were happening too <b>fast</b> to keep up with.<br>事态发展太快，令人跟不上趟儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkeep sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使熬夜；使不睡觉<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from going to bed or from sleeping</span></td><td class="c4">I hope we're not <b>keeping you up</b>.<br>但愿我们没有耽误你睡觉。<br>The baby <b>kept us up</b> half the night.<br>孩子弄得我们半夜才睡。<br>We <b>kept up</b> a fast pace all the way.<br>我们一路上一直走得很快。<br>The press is <b>keeping up</b> the pressure on the government.<br>报界继续向政府施压。<br>Do you still <b>keep up</b> your Portuguese?<br>你的葡萄牙语还在学着吧？B。<br>They sang songs to <b>keep their spirits up</b>.<br>他们唱歌以保持情绪昂扬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>keep ˈup with sb</b></td><td class="c3">与(某人)保持联系<br><span class="en">to continue to be in contact with sb by writing, phoning or seeing them regularly</span></td><td class="c4">How many of your old school friends do you manage to <b>keep up with</b>?<br>你还和多少老同学保持联络。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>keep ˈup with sth</b></td><td class="c3">了解最新消息；形势等<br><span class="en">to learn about the news, events, etc. that are happening</span></td><td class="c4">Susie likes to <b>keep</b> up with the latest fashions.<br>苏茜喜欢追逐时尚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>keep ˈup with sth</b></td><td class="c3">继续按时支付；继续定时做(某事)<br><span class="en">to continue to pay or do sth regularly</span></td><td class="c4">He couldn't <b>keep</b> up with the repayments on the loan.<br>他无力继续偿还贷款。<br>Are you <b>keeping up with</b> your homework?<br>你还在按时写作业吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>key</b></td><td class="c2"><b>key sth ˈin<br>key sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">用键盘输入(信息)；把(信息)键入(计算机)<br><span class="en">to put information into a computer, using a keyboard</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Key in</b> your personal number.<br>输入你的个人号码。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>key ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">调用；使用(计算机或计算机内存信息)<br><span class="en">to use a computer or information stored on a computer</span></td><td class="c4">A hacker <b>keyed into</b> a vital database at the newspaper's office.<br>一名黑客侵入了这家报社的重要数据库。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkey on sth (also key ˈin on sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">聚焦于；开始关注<br><span class="en">to focus on sth or begin to pay attention to it</span></td><td class="c4">Police dogs <b>keyed in on</b> a briefcase left in the baggage area.<br>警犬盯上了落在行李区的一个公文包。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkey sth to sth/sb</b></td><td class="c3">使适合；与…相关<br><span class="en">to make sth suitable for sth/sb;to link sth with sth else</span></td><td class="c4">The farm was <b>keyed to</b> the needs of the local people.<br>这个农场注意满足当地人的需求。<br>The timing of the concerts was <b>keyed to</b> the World Cup soccer games.<br>这些音乐会是配合世界杯足球赛来安排时间的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈkick against sth</b></td><td class="c3">抗议；抵抗<br><span class="en">to protest about sth or resist sth</span></td><td class="c4">It's no use <b>kicking against</b> the system.<br>反抗体制是没有用的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌkick aˈbout<br>kick aˈbout sth <span class="tag">(informal usually used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时</td><td class="c4">His letter is <b>kicking</b> <b>about</b> somewhere.<br>他的信不知搁哪儿了。<br>The idea has been <b>kicking</b> around for years.<br>这个想法好多年没人提起了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sb aˈround (BrE also ˌkick sb aˈbout) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">粗暴(或不公正地)对待<br><span class="en">to treat sb in an unkind or unfair way</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let the boss <b>kick you around</b>.<br>别让老板欺负你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth aˈround (BrE also ˌkick sth aˈbout)</b></td><td class="c3">踢(球)<br><span class="en">to play with a ball by kicking it with your foot</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>kicking a ball around</b> in the street.<br>他们在街上踢球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈback (to sb) <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">拿出(一定金额)作回扣给；某人<br><span class="en">to pay money illegally in order to get some advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">Contractors winning construction jobs had to <b>kick back</b> two per cent of the contract price to the mafic.<br>赢得建筑工程的承包商得抽出合同成交价款的百分之二作为回扣给黑手党。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick ˈin <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始运作；开始见效<br><span class="en">to start to work or have an effect</span></td><td class="c4">After a couple of minutes the emergency electricity supply <b>kicked in</b>.<br>几分钟后，应急供电系统开始运行了。<br>Youll feel better when the antibiotics <b>kick in</b>.<br>抗生素一起作用，你就会感觉好些的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">踢破；踢倒<br><span class="en">to break sth and make it fall by kicking it</span></td><td class="c4">They had <b>kicked the front door in</b>.<br>他们把前门踹开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick ˈorf</b></td><td class="c3">足球</td><td class="c4">The game <b>kicks</b> off at 7.30.<br>比赛7点 30 分开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick ˈorf</b></td><td class="c3">以…开始<br><span class="en">(with sth) informal to start</span></td><td class="c4">The tour <b>kicks</b> off with a concert in Nottingham.<br>巡回演出以诺丁汉的音乐会为起点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sb ˈoff<br>kick sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">断开某人的(互联网)连接<br><span class="en">computing to break the connection between sb's computer and the Internet, so that they can no longer use the Internet</span></td><td class="c4">I keep getting <b>kicked off</b> the Internet.<br>我上网时总是掉线。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">踢开；踢掉<br><span class="en">to remove sth by kicking</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>kicked off</b> her shoes and lay down on the bed.<br>她踢掉鞋子，躺倒在床上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">以…开始会议；活动等<br><span class="en">(with sth) to begin a meeting, an event, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Who's going to <b>kick off</b> the discussion?<br>谁来起头讨论。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkick ˈon <span class="tag">(BrE, sport)</span></b></td><td class="c3">继续；继续比赛<br><span class="en">to continue playing</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>kick on</b> and take advantage of our lead.<br>我们需要继续踢下去，利用好我们的领先地位。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick ˈout (at sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">尤指因愤怒或不安(向…)踢去<br><span class="en">to kick your foot into the air to try to hit sb, especially because you are angry or upset</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>kicked out</b> wildly at him as he tried to grab her.<br>正当他想一把拽住她时，她发瘋一般地踢他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick ˈout (at sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">作出强烈反应<br><span class="en">to react violently to sb/sth that makes you angry or upset</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>kicked out</b> against traditional ideas about portraits.<br>她猛烈抨击肖像画创作的传统观念。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">踢翻<br><span class="en">to make sth fall on its side by kicking it</span></td><td class="c4">She almost <b>kicked the bucket over</b>.<br>她差点踢翻了水桶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>kick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">扬起尘埃；沙子等<br><span class="en">to make dust, sand, etc. rise into the air</span></td><td class="c4">The horse <b>kicked up</b> a cloud of dust.<br>马蹄踏过扬起一片尘土。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkill sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">大量杀死(动植物等)<br><span class="en">to make a lot of plants, animals, etc.die</span></td><td class="c4">Antibiotics should <b>kill off</b> the bacteria.<br>抗生素应能杀死这种细菌。<br>The plant life was <b>killed off</b> by air pollution.<br>空气污染导致植物大面积死亡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkill sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">除掉；停止<br><span class="en">to get rid of sb/sth; to stop sth</span></td><td class="c4">The hero is <b>killed off</b> in the last chapter.<br>主人公在最后一章被干掉了。<br>It is difficult to <b>kill off</b> old traditions or myths.<br>很难消除旧有传统或错误观念。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>kip ˈdown <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在别处睡下；投宿；过夜<br><span class="en">to sleep in a place that is not your own bed</span></td><td class="c4">Is there anywhere to <b>kip down</b> for the night?<br>晚上有没有地方睡觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kiss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>kiss sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">吻去(悲伤或怒气)<br><span class="en">to stop sb feeling sad or angry by kissing them</span></td><td class="c4">Let mummy <b>kiss away</b> your tears.<br>让妈妈吻掉你的眼泪吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkiss sb/sth ˈoff (as sth)</b></td><td class="c3">认为…很失败(或不重要)<br><span class="en">to consider that sb/sth is a failure or not important</span></td><td class="c4">The record companies <b>Kissed us off</b> as a second-rate punk band.<br>唱片公司认为我们是二流朋克乐队。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌkit sb/sth ˈout (also ˌkit sb/sth ˈup less frequent) (in/with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为…整理行装；配置设备<br><span class="en">to supply sb/sth with the clothes or equipment that they need for a particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">The kids are all <b>kitted out</b> for the new school year.<br>孩子们新学年的文具都准备齐了。<br>The studio is <b>kitted out</b> with modern sound equipment.<br>演播室配备了现代音响设备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>knock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈknockabout n <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一起；踢球<br><span class="en">a period of time spent kicking a ball around with other people</span></td><td class="c4">We had a <b>knockabout</b> in the park.<br>我们在公园踢了会儿球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sb ˈback sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用掉某人一笔钱<br><span class="en">to cost sb a particular amount of money</span></td><td class="c4">Those books <b>knocked me back</b> £50.<br>那些书花了我 50 英镑。<br>That car must have <b>knocked you back</b> a bit!<br>那辆车一定花了你不少钱！语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌknock sth ˈback <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">很快喝掉；一口喝下<br><span class="en">to drink sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>knocked back</b> two pints of beer.<br>他一口气喝了两品脱啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>knock sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">汽车等撞倒；撞死；撞伤<br><span class="en">if a car or another vehicle knocks sb down, it hits them, often killing or injuring them</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>knocked down</b> by a bus.<br>一辆公共汽车把她撞倒在地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>knock sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">撞倒；打倒；推倒<br><span class="en">to hit or push sb so that they fall to the ground or the floor</span></td><td class="c4">The wind was strong enough to <b>knock</b> you down.<br>风大得能把你吹倒。<br>He <b>knocked</b> opponent in the first round (= in boxing).<br>他第一回合就将对手击倒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈknock-down price n</b></td><td class="c3">低价；特价</td><td class="c4">I got these books at a <b>knock-down</b> <b>price</b>.<br>我以优惠价买到了这些书。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌknock sth ˈin<br>ˌknock sth ˈin/ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…锤进；把…敲入<br><span class="en">to make sth enter sth by hitting it, for example with a hammer</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>knocked some nails into</b> the wall.<br>她把一些钉子钉在墙上。<br>She <b>knocked the ball into</b> the net.<br>她击球入网。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sth ˈin sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…上打出(洞等)<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a hole in sth by hitting</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>knocked a hole in</b> the wall for the window.<br>他们在墙上凿了个洞开窗户。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌknock ˈoff<br>knock ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">停止；中断；(尤指)下班；收工<br><span class="en">to stop doing sth, especially work</span></td><td class="c4">What time do you <b>knock off</b>(work) today?<br>你今天几点下班。<br>You could <b>knock</b> this wall down and make one large room.<br>你可以拆了这面墙，改成一个大房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">杀死；除掉<br><span class="en">to murder sb</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>knocked off</b> by another gang.<br>他被另一个团伙干掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">击败；打败<br><span class="en">to defeat sb in a competition or election</span></td><td class="c4">She easily <b>knocked off</b> her Republican opponent in the last election.<br>上次选举中她轻松战胜共和党的对手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈknockout (also ˈknock-out) n</b></td><td class="c3">演出等<br><span class="en">a person, a piece of clothing, a performance, etc. that is extremely attractive or impressive</span></td><td class="c4">Her daughter's an absolute <b>knockout</b>.<br>她的女儿绝对令人倾倒。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>knock sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌknock sb/sth ˈout of sth (sport)</b></td><td class="c3">把…淘汰(出比赛)<br><span class="en">to defeat a person or a team so that they cannot continue in the competition</span></td><td class="c4">France <b>knocked Belgium out</b> of the European Cup.<br>法国队将比利时队淘汰出了欧洲杯赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sb ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">汽车等撞倒；撞死；撞伤<br><span class="en">if a car or another vehicle knocks sb over, it hits them and often kills or injures them</span></td><td class="c4">He got <b>knocked over</b> by a bus.<br>他给公共汽车撞了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock sb ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">抢劫(银行等)<br><span class="en">to rob a bank or other business</span></td><td class="c4">The two men were wanted for <b>knocking over</b> a bank.<br>这两名男子因打劫银行遭到通缉。时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock ˈthrough <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打通(房间的墙壁)<br><span class="en">to knock down the wall between two rooms</span></td><td class="c4">I intend to <b>knock through</b> on the ground floor.<br>我打算把底楼的墙壁打通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock toˈgether <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">两物相撞；碰撞<br><span class="en">if two things knock together, they touch each other with some force and make a sound</span></td><td class="c4">His knees were <b>knocking together</b> with fright.<br>他吓得两腿直哆嗦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>knock ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, sport)</span></b></td><td class="c3">网球等</td><td class="c4">We <b>knocked up</b> for a few minutes before the match.<br>我们赛前练了几分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌknock sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">敲门唤醒<br><span class="en">to wake sb by knocking on their door</span></td><td class="c4">Would you like me to <b>knock you up</b> in the morning?<br>你想让我早晨敲门叫你起床吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>know</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈknow sb/sth as sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…称为；认为…具有(某种特质)；把…看成(某种类型的人或事物)<br><span class="en">to call sb/sth by a particular name; to think that sb/sth has a particular characteristic or is a particular type of person or thing</span></td><td class="c4">She is <b>known to her friends as</b> Beth.<br>她的朋友们叫她贝丝。<br>It became <b>known as</b> the worst local company to work for.<br>它成了雇员公认的当地最差公司。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈknow A from B</b></td><td class="c3">能区分；能辨别(两事物)<br><span class="en">to be able to recognize the difference between two things</span></td><td class="c4">She doesn't <b>know</b> a Rolls Royce from a Renault.<br>她分辨不出劳斯莱斯车和雷诺车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>knuckle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>knuckle ˈdown (to sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始；收心下功夫(做某事)<br><span class="en">to begin to work seriously at sth, usually after a period when you have not worked hard</span></td><td class="c4">It's time to <b>knuckle down</b> (to some hard work).<br>现在得开始努力(刻苦工作)了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌknuckle ˈunder (to sb/sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向…屈服；认输；低头<br><span class="en">to accept or admit defeat and do what you are told or what you have to do</span></td><td class="c4">Those who refused to <b>knuckle under</b> were imprisoned.<br>不肯妥协的人被关了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>kowtow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>kowˈtow to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…卑躬屈膝；俯首帖耳；百依百順<br><span class="en">to show sb/sth too much respect and be too willing to obey them</span></td><td class="c4">I refuse to <b>kowtow to</b> anyone.<br>我绝不会屈从于任何人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lace</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lace ˈup<br>ˌlace sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把鞋带系紧<br><span class="en">to be fastened with laces; to fasten sth with laces</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>laced her shoes up</b>.<br>她系好了鞋带。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlace sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">给(饮料)掺少许酒；毒物<br><span class="en">to put a small amount of sth, such as alcohol, a drug, poison, etc. into a drink</span></td><td class="c4">Someone had <b>laced</b> the cat's milk with alcohol.<br>有人在给猫吃的奶里加了点酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlace sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">使演说；文章等具有(某种特色)<br><span class="en">to put a lot of a particular quality into sth such as a speech, a piece of writing, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The show is <b>laced with</b> black humour.<br>这个节目颇具黑色幽默意味。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ladle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ladle sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用大勺舀出；盛出(很多食物)<br><span class="en">to serve food with a ladle, etc., or in large quantities</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ladled out</b> the Soup.<br>他用大勺分汤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlag beˈhind<br>lag beˈhind sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">落后；落在…后面<br><span class="en">to be behind sb/sth because you are walking more slowly</span></td><td class="c4">Everyone ran down to the beach, but Amy <b>lagged behind</b>.<br>大家都向海滩奔去，只有埃米落在后面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlag beˈhind<br>lag beˈhind sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…方面进展比…缓慢；滞后<br><span class="en">(in sth/in doing sth) to progress or develop more slowly than others</span></td><td class="c4">We are <b>lagging far behind</b> our European competitors in using new technology.<br>在采用新技术方面，我们远远落后于欧洲的竞争对手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>land</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈland in sth<br>ˈland sb/yourself in sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使处于；陷入(困境)<br><span class="en">to get sb/yourself into trouble or a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>landed in</b> court for stealing a car.<br>她因为偷车而要出庭受审。<br>Being too outspoken <b>landed her in</b> trouble.<br>她过于直率，惹了麻烦。<br>How did I <b>land myself in</b> such a mess?<br>我怎么卷入了这样的乱局。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lap sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">欣然接受；全盘接受赞扬；美言等<br><span class="en">to receive sth such as praise or a kind remark with pleasure without thinking about whether it is true or not</span></td><td class="c4">The baby was <b>lapping up</b> the attention he was getting.<br>这个小孩受到别人关注就开心了。<br>She <b>lapped up</b> his flattery.<br>他的恭维话她照单全收了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lap sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">开怀畅饮；高兴地喝干<br><span class="en">to drink all of sth with great enjoyment</span></td><td class="c4">The cat <b>lapped up</b> the cream.<br>猫津津有味地把奶油舔得一干二净。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lark aˈbout/aˈround</b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；傻玩；玩乐<br><span class="en">to enjoy yourself by behaving in a silly way</span></td><td class="c4">Some kids were <b>larking about</b> in the shopping centre.<br>一些孩子在购物中心嬉戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlast sb ˈout <span class="tag">(often humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">活过；寿命超过(某人)<br><span class="en">to live or continue longer than sb else</span></td><td class="c4">My grandmother is so fit and healthy shell probably <b>last us all out</b>!<br>我奶奶身体这么使朗健康，她可能比我们大家都长寿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>latch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlatch ˈon<br>ˌlatch ˈonto sb (also, latch ˈon to sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">纠缠；缠住<br><span class="en">to follow sb around, often when they do not want you with them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>latched onto</b> us and we couldn't get rid of him.<br>他缠着我们，甩也甩不掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>latch sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…付诸一笑；笑话摆脱<br><span class="en">to try to make people think that you do not care about sth, or that it is not serious or important, by making a joke about it</span></td><td class="c4">He laughed <b>off</b> suggestions that he had been approached to be manager of the England team.<br>传闻有人找他当英格兰队的主教练，他一笑置之。<br>It was an embarrassing situation, but she managed to laugh it <b>off</b>.<br>那个场面很尴尬，可她一笑摆脱了窘境。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lay</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lay aˈbout sb (with sth) <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛打；痛骂<br><span class="en">to attack sb violently physically or with words</span></td><td class="c4">He started to <b>lay about</b> me with his walking stick.<br>他开始用拐杖狠狠揍我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay aˈbout sb (with sth) <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">留存备用；积蓄<br><span class="en">(also,lay sth by less frequent) to keep sth to use in the future; to save sth</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>laid</b> anything aside for your old age?<br>你为个人养老有所积攒了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay sth beˈfore sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">呈交；递交；上报(供审议决定)<br><span class="en">to present a proposal, some information, etc. to sb for them to think about and decide on</span></td><td class="c4">The bill was <b>laid before</b> Parliament.<br>议案提交给了国会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；停用<br><span class="en">to put sth down or stop using it</span></td><td class="c4">He stopped writing and <b>laid down</b> his pen.<br>他停止写字，放下钢笔。<br>They refused to <b>lay down</b> their arms.<br>他们拒绝放下武器。<br>Clear guidelines have been <b>laid down</b> for religious teaching in schools.<br>已制订出明确的关于学校宗教教育的指导原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">积聚；积累<br><span class="en">to produce sth that is stored and gradually increases</span></td><td class="c4">If you eat too much, the surplus is <b>laid down</b> as fat.<br>要是吃得太多，过剩的营养就会成为脂肪贮存起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">贮备；贮存(尤指葡萄酒)<br><span class="en">to store sth, especially wine, to use in the future</span></td><td class="c4">She has <b>laid down</b> hundreds of bottles of port.<br>她贮存了上百瓶波尔图葡萄酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay ˈinto sb/sth (with sth) (for sth/for doing sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以…猛揍；痛斥<br><span class="en">to attack sb/sth violently, with words or blows (…)</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>laid into</b> him with her fists.<br>她挥拳狠揍了他。<br>He <b>laid into</b> the government for spending millions of pounds on buildings nobody wanted.<br>他怒斥政府耗费几百万英镑兴建没人要的楼房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay ˈoff sth<br>lay ˈoff doing sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">停止做；有害的事；放弃(有害的事物)<br><span class="en">to stop doing or using sth harmful</span></td><td class="c4">You should <b>lay off</b> alcohol/drinking for a while.<br>你暂时别喝酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">因工作不多暂时遣散；裁减<br><span class="en">to dismiss workers, usually for a short time, because there is not enough work</span></td><td class="c4">We've had to <b>lay off</b> hundreds of workers.<br>我们不得不暂时解雇几百名工人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sth ˈon <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">提供；安排食物；交通；娱乐等<br><span class="en">to provide or arrange sth for sb, for example food, transport or entertainment</span></td><td class="c4">Extra buses were <b>laid on</b> during the train strike.<br>铁路罢工期间增加了公共汽车班次。<br>She had <b>laid on</b> tea for the players.<br>她为运动员提供茶水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sth ˈon sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把(环的或惊人的消息)透露给<br><span class="en">to break bad or surprising news to sb</span></td><td class="c4">Sorry to <b>lay this on</b> you, but he's never coming back.<br>很抱歉地告诉你，他绝对不会回来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">打昏；打晕<br><span class="en">to knock sb unconscious</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>laid his opponent out</b> with a single blow.<br>他一拳就把对手打晕了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">铺开；展开；摊开<br><span class="en">to spread sth out ready to use or so that it can be seen easily</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Lay out</b> all the clothes you want to take.<br>把你要带走的衣服全摆出来。<br><b>Lay all the cards out</b> on the table.<br>把纸牌全摆在桌上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">策划；设计；安排；布置<br><span class="en">to plan how sth should look and arrange it in this way</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>laid the streets out</b> on a grid pattern.<br>他们把街道设计成棋盘状。0 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">花(钱)<br><span class="en">(on sth) informal to spend money</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>laid out</b> thousands renovating house.<br>他花了几千元钱翻新房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlay ˈover (in/at . ) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">乘飞机时在中途稍作停留；短暂滞留<br><span class="en">to stop somewhere for a short time when you are on a journey by plane</span></td><td class="c4">Several passengers were <b>laying over</b> in Chicago for a few hours.<br>几名乘客在芝加哥逗留了数小时。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lay ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">躲藏；闲着<br><span class="en">to hide somewhere or do nothing for a while</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>lay up</b> in a cave until it got dark.<br>他们在洞里一直躲到天黑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>laze</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlaze aˈbout<br>laze aˈbout sth</b></td><td class="c3">闲散地打发；时间；消磨时光<br><span class="en">to spend your time relaxing and doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>lazed</b> <b>about</b> all day.<br>他悠闲地过了一整天。<br>They <b>lazed</b> around the pool in the afternoon.<br>他们在游泳池里懒散地过了一下午。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>laze sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">闲散地打发(时间)；消磨(时光)<br><span class="en">to spend a period of time relaxing and doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>lazed away</b> the summer on the beach.<br>我们在沙滩上懒洋洋地打发了夏日时光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>leak</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌleak ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">秘密泄露<br><span class="en">if secret information leaks out, it becomes known to the public when it should remain secret</span></td><td class="c4">He was worried about what might happen if the news <b>leaked out</b>.<br>他担心万一走漏了风声可能会出乱子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lean</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlean on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">威胁；胁迫<br><span class="en">to try to make sb do sth by threatening them</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas being <b>leaned on</b>.<br>我受到了恐吓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>leap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈleap at sth</b></td><td class="c3">迫不及待地接受；毫不迟疑；地接受<br><span class="en">to accept sth with enthusiasm, without hesitating</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>leapt at</b> the chance of working in Paris.<br>她立刻抓住了去巴黎工作的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leap ˈout at sb</b></td><td class="c3">立刻；进入(某人)的视线；引人注目<br><span class="en">if sth, especially sth written, leaps out at you, you see it immediately</span></td><td class="c4">His name <b>leapt out at</b> me from the page.<br>我在那一页上一眼就看见了他的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leap ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">坐着时突然起身；猛地站起来<br><span class="en">to stand quickly and suddenly when you have been sitting</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>leapt up</b> and ran to answer the door.<br>他一下子站起来跑过去开门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>learn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>leave sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把(想法或问题)搁置；一边<br><span class="en">to not discuss or consider a particular idea or issue</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Leaving aside</b> car parking space, the housing development is well planned.<br>撇开停车位不谈，住宅开发规划得很好。<br>Let us <b>leave aside</b> the question of costs for the moment.<br>我们暂时不谈费用问题吧。<br><b>Leaving that aside</b> .<br>且不说…。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leave sb/sth beˈhind</b></td><td class="c3">死后留下<br><span class="en">to have sb/sth remaining after your death</span></td><td class="c4">He died at the age of 33, <b>leaving behind</b> a wife and three young children.<br>他33岁时去世，留下妻子和三个年幼的孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leave sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">保留；不删书；文章等的内容<br><span class="en">to not remove sth, for example from a book, a piece of writing, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure you <b>leave that paragraph in</b>.<br>一定要保留那个段落。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leave ˈoff<br>ˌleave ˈoff sth<br>ˌleave ˈoff doing sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">停止；中断<br><span class="en">to stop doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">Lee shouted at him, but he wouldn't <b>leave off</b>.<br>李大声喊他，但他不想停下来。<br>Would you <b>leave off</b> what you are doing for a moment?<br>你暂时放下手头的事好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌleave sb/sth ˈoff<br>ˌleave sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">不把…列入；不包括；不含<br><span class="en">to not include or mention sb/sth, especially on a list</span></td><td class="c4">Have I <b>left anyone off</b> the list?<br>我在名单上有没有漏掉什么人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>leave sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续穿着<br><span class="en">if you leave clothes on, you continue wearing them</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Leave your shoes on</b>.<br>不必脱鞋。<br>Do you mind if I <b>leave the tape recorder on</b> while you talk?<br>你说话的时候我把录音机开着，你不介意吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌleave it ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不可能<br><span class="en">used to tell sb that you think what they have said is stupid, or that you do not believe it</span></td><td class="c4">Two million dollars? <b>Leave it out</b>!<br>两百万元？瞎扯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>leave sb ˈout<br>ˌleave sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">不把某人列入；把某人包括在(…)内<br><span class="en">to not include sb deliberately</span></td><td class="c4">It seemed unkind to <b>leave Daisy out</b>, so we invited her too.<br>把黛西排除在外似乎不太好，所以我们也邀请了她。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lend sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把…借出(给某人)<br><span class="en">to allow sb to borrow sth for a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">The reference books cannot be <b>lent out</b>.<br>参考书不得外借。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlend itself/themselves to sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">适合于；适宜于<br><span class="en">to be suitable for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Science in elementary schools <b>lends itself well to</b> learning through play.<br>小学科学课很适合在游戏中学习。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>let</b></td><td class="c2"><b>let sb/sth ˈdown<br>ˌlet yourself ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使略逊一筹；使美中不足<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth/yourself less successful or impressive than they/it/you should be</span></td><td class="c4">Her pronunciation <b>lets her down</b>.<br>她美中不足的是发音不大好。<br>His clothes <b>let him down</b>.<br>他穿着不够得体。<br>If you don't work hard for these exams, you'll only be <b>letting yourself down</b>.<br>你要是不努力准备这些考试，成绩就会不理想。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlet sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；放低；降下<br><span class="en">to make sth go lower</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>let the bucket down</b> on a rope.<br>我们用绳子把吊桶放下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlet sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">让水；等进来<br><span class="en">to allow sth such as water or light to enter a place through a hole</span></td><td class="c4">There was a hole in the roof that <b>let the rain in</b>.<br>屋顶有个洞漏雨。<br>I drew the curtains back to <b>let in</b> some light.<br>我拉开窗帘透透光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be, let ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使置入；使嵌进<br><span class="en">to be put into the surface of sth</span></td><td class="c4">A large window was <b>let</b> <b>into</b> the wall.<br>墙上开了个大窗户。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>let sb ˈoff (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以轻罚从宽处理；放过；免罚<br><span class="en">to punish sb lightly for sth wrong they have done; to not punish sb at all</span></td><td class="c4">She was let off with a <b>fine</b>.<br>她只交了罚款就完事。111。<br>Mum <b>let me off</b> the household chores during exams.<br>考试期间妈妈免了我的家务活儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>let sb ˈoff (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">让某人下车(尤指公共汽车)<br><span class="en">to allow sb to get out of a vehicle, especially a bus</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>let me off</b> here?<br>让我在这儿下车好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>let sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">开(枪)；起爆(炸弹)；燃放(烟花)<br><span class="en">to fire a gun; to make sth explode</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>let off</b> steam by hitting a pillow.<br>他捶打枕头出气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>let ˈon (to sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">透露(给某人)<br><span class="en">to tell sb sth that is supposed to be a secret</span></td><td class="c4">The children knew he was coming, but they didn't <b>let on</b> to anyone.<br>孩子们知道他要来，但他们对谁也没说。<br>There were holes in Jack's shoes, but Kate didn't <b>let on</b> (that) she'd noticed.<br>杰克的鞋子破了几个洞，但凯特假装没看见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlet ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">放学；放假；下班<br><span class="en">when schools, classes, offices, etc. let out, they come to an end and students, workers, etc. go home at the end of a day or a term</span></td><td class="c4">More than 30 000 people are expected in the square after work <b>lets out</b>.<br>预计有3万多人下班后来广场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlet sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">发出(叫声等)<br><span class="en">to give a cry; to make a sound</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>let out</b> a scream of terror.<br>她发出一声恐怖的尖叫。<br>He <b>let out</b> a sigh of relief.<br>他松了口气。日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>let sb/sth ˈpast</b></td><td class="c3">给…让路<br><span class="en">to allow sb/sth to.go past you</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>let me past</b>, please?<br>请让我过去好吗？R。<br>These blinds don't <b>let</b> much light through.<br>这些窗帘不怎么透光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>let sb/sth ˈpast</b></td><td class="c3">通过；许可；批准<br><span class="en">to say that sb/sth is good enough for sth or is correct</span></td><td class="c4">We were worried the council wouldn't let the plans <b>for</b> the new building through.<br>我们担心理事会不会通过兴建新楼房的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>let ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">减弱；减轻<br><span class="en">to become less strong</span></td><td class="c4">The rain showed no sign of <b>letting up</b>.<br>雨没有减小的迹象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>let ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">松懈；停止<br><span class="en">to do sth with less effort or energy than before, or stop doing it</span></td><td class="c4">Doesn't she ever <b>let up</b>?She's been complaining all day.<br>她就不能消停一会儿吗？她抱怨一整天了。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>level</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlevel sth ˈdown/ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使标准；数量等降低(或提高)到同等水平；把…向下(或向上)拉平<br><span class="en">to make standards, amounts, etc. be the same low/high or lower/ higher level</span></td><td class="c4">The government is accused of <b>levelling down</b> standards in schools rather than Levelling them up.<br>政府受到指责，称其全面降低而非提高各学校的标准。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>level ˈoff/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">急剧涨落后平稳下来<br><span class="en">to become level or steady after a periodi of sharp rises and falls</span></td><td class="c4">House prices showed no sign of <b>levelling off</b>.<br>住房价格没有趋稳的迹象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>level ˈoff/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">起伏后变水平；变平坦<br><span class="en">to become level or horizontal after rising or falling</span></td><td class="c4">The road began to <b>level off</b> as we approached the coast.<br>我们接近海岸时，路面开始变得平坦起来。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlevel sth ˈoff/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使平坦；使平整<br><span class="en">to make sth smooth or flat</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Level the ground out</b> before sowing the seed.<br>把地平鳖好再播种。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lick sth ˈoff/ˈup<br>lick sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">舔吃；舔着喝<br><span class="en">to eat or drink sth by moving your tongue over the surface of it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>licked the jam off</b> (the spoon).<br>她舔掉了(勺子上的)果酱。<br>The cat <b>licked up</b> the milk from the dish.<br>猫舔光了碟子里的牛奶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lie</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlie with sb/sth (to do sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">是…的职责；是…的责任<br><span class="en">to be the duty or responsibility of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">It <b>lies with</b> you to accept or reject the proposal.<br>接受还是拒绝这一建议由你决定。<br>The decision on whether to proceed <b>lies with</b> the minister.<br>得由部长决定是否继续进行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lift</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlift ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">火箭等发射；起飞；升空<br><span class="en">(of a rocket, etc.) to rise from the ground into the air</span></td><td class="c4">The rocket <b>lifts off</b> next Monday.<br>火箭下星期 ˈ。<br>She <b>lifted</b> up the box and put it on the table.<br>她把盒子搬起来放到桌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>light</b></td><td class="c2"><b>light ˈout for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">匆匆前往；急切前往<br><span class="en">to go somewhere quickly because you are keen to get there</span></td><td class="c4">At 22 he <b>lit out for</b> Hollywood and was in his first movie the next year.<br>他22岁时迫不及待前往好莱坞发展，第二年出演了第一部电影。<br>The waterfall was <b>lit</b> up at night with pink and green floodlights.<br>夜间的粉色和绿色泛光灯把瀑布映照得光彩夺目。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>light ˈout for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">喜形于色；喜气洋洋<br><span class="en">if a person's eyes or face light up, or sth lights them up, they become bright with excitement or happiness</span></td><td class="c4">Her eyes <b>lit</b> up when she saw them.<br>她看见他们时两眼放光。<br>A smile of delight <b>lit</b> up his face.<br>他脸上露出欣喜的笑容。<br>His face <b>lit</b> up with pleasure.<br>他面露喜色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>light ˈout for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">点燃；开始吸香烟<br><span class="en">to begin to smoke a cigarette, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She took <b>out</b> a cigarette and <b>lit</b> up.<br>她拖出一支香烟点上。<br>He <b>lit</b> up one cigarette after another.<br>他一根接一根地抽着烟。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlight sb ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">反复地打<br><span class="en">to hit or kick sb repeatedly</span></td><td class="c4">If he doesn't watch what he says, someone's going to <b>light him up</b>.<br>他要是满嘴胡扯，会有人揍他的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlight upon sb/sth - ON/ SB/ scoop sb/sth up</b></td><td class="c3">用勺子或类似器皿舀出；挖出(某物)；抱起(某人)<br><span class="en">to move or lift sth with a spoon or similar object; to pick sb up in your arms</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>scooped</b> the child up in his arms.<br>他把孩子抱了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lighten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlighten ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用于；别埋怨；别担心<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to be less serious or to complain or worry less about sth</span></td><td class="c4">Come on, <b>lighten up</b>! It was only a joke.<br>喂，别紧张！这只不过是开玩笑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlighten sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使生动活泼<br><span class="en">to make sth more cheerful and less serious or depressing</span></td><td class="c4">He did his best to <b>lighten things up</b>.<br>他竭尽全力使气氛活跃起来。<br>She tried to <b>lighten up</b> her speech with a few jokes.<br>她说了几个笑话，尽量让讲话轻松愉快一些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>limber</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlimber ˈup (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">体育运动；比赛等前做准备活动；做热身运动<br><span class="en">to do exercise to prepare to take part in a sport, a race, etc.; to warm up</span></td><td class="c4">The players were <b>limbering up</b> for the game.<br>运动员正在为比赛做预备活动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>limit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlimit sth to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使限于…內<br><span class="en">to make sth exist or happen only in a particular place or within a Particular group</span></td><td class="c4">Violent crime is not <b>limited to</b> big cities.<br>暴力犯罪并不局限于大城市。<br>The teaching of history should not be <b>limited to</b> dates and figures.<br>教历史不应局限于讲年代和人物。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>line</b></td><td class="c2"><b>line ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE, sport)</span></b></td><td class="c3">比赛等；前走进场地；入场<br><span class="en">to go onto the sports field at the beginning of a game, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Nobody will <b>line out</b> tomorrow unless they're fully fit.<br>除非状态极佳，否则明天无人出场。<br>They <b>lined</b> up to shake the President's hand.<br>他们站成一排，逐一和总统握手。<br>The runners <b>lined</b> up at the starting <b>line</b>.<br>赛跑运动员在起跑线上站成一排。<br>Local groups are <b>lining</b> up against the new development (= joining together to oppose it).<br>当地团体结成联盟反对新的开发项目。<br>All the residents have <b>lined</b> up behind the caretaker (= they support him).<br>全体居民一致支持看门人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>line ˈup<br>line sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">对齐<br><span class="en">to be, or to put sth, in the correct position in relation to sth else</span></td><td class="c4">The three holes should all <b>line up</b> (with each other).<br>这= 个孔应该全对齐。<br>His CDs were <b>lined up</b> on the shelf.<br>他的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>line ˈup<br>line sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">组织；安排(活动)；安排某人(参与活动等)<br><span class="en">(for sb/sth) to organize an event or an activity; to arrange for sb to do sth at an event, a competition,etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>lined up</b> a band for the Party.<br>他为聚会安排了一支乐队。<br>We've <b>lined up</b> a few things for the weekend.<br>我们为这个周末安排了几件事。<br>They already had a buyer for their car <b>lined up</b>.<br>他们已经为他们的车子找了个买主。</td></tr>
