<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>linger</b></td><td class="c2"><b>linger ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">奄奄一息；苟延残喘<br><span class="en">to remain alive, but becoming gradually weaker</span></td><td class="c4">We should be thankful that she didn't <b>linger on</b>.<br>她没有拖延很久就去世了，我们应该感到宽慰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>liquor</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get liquored ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">喝醉酒<br><span class="en">to be/get drunk</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>got liquored up</b> on Saturday night.<br>星期六晚上我们喝醉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>listen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlisten ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">窃听；愉听；监听<br><span class="en">(on/to sth) to listen to sth or sb</span></td><td class="c4">Have you been <b>listening in</b> on my phone calls?<br>你是不是一直在偷听我的电话。<br>They were sure that the police were <b>listening in</b> to their conversations.<br>他们肯定警方在监听他们的谈话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlisten ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">收听广播节目<br><span class="en">(to sth) to listen to a radio programme,etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Listen in</b> on Friday for our interview with Britney.<br>请于星期五收听我们对布兰妮的访谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>live</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlive by sth</b></td><td class="c3">遵循；遵守信念；原则等<br><span class="en">to follow a particular belief or set of principles</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>lived by</b> giving private lessons.<br>她靠做家庭教师为生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">住在工作(或学习)的地方<br><span class="en">to live at the place where you work or study</span></td><td class="c4">They have a nanny <b>living in</b>.<br>他们有个保姆住在家里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续活着；继续存在<br><span class="en">to continue to live or exist</span></td><td class="c4">He may be dead but his music <b>lives on</b>.<br>他也许死了，但他的音乐永存。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">常吃；以…为主<br><span class="en">to eat a particular type of food very frequently or all the time</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>living on</b> fruit and raw vegetables.<br>她主要吃水果和生蔬菜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">住在工作(或学习)以外的地方<br><span class="en">to live away from the place where you work or study</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>lived out</b> during my final year at college.<br>我念大学的最后一年住在校外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>live ˈout sth</b></td><td class="c3">将(想法)付诸行动；实践(信念)；实现(梦想)<br><span class="en">to do in reality sth that you think about, believe in, dream of, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">On holiday in Texas I <b>lived out</b> my childhood fantasy of being a cowboy.<br>在得克萨斯度假时，我实现了当牛仔的童年梦想。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中幸存下来；经受住；熬过<br><span class="en">to experience sth difficult or unpleasant and survive</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>lived through</b> both world wars.<br>他经历了两次世界大战。<br>It's something I never want to <b>live through</b> again.<br>那是我永远不想再次经历的事情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlive ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">达到；符合<br><span class="en">to behave as well as or be as good or successful as people expect</span></td><td class="c4">The hotel failed to <b>live up to</b> expectations.<br>这家旅馆令人失望。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlive with sth<br>ˈlive with yourself</b></td><td class="c3">忍受；容忍令人不快；的状况<br><span class="en">to accept an unpleasant situation and continue with your life and work</span></td><td class="c4">You might not like the situation, but youll have to learn to <b>live with</b> it.<br>你可能不喜欢这种情况，但你必须学会忍耐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>liven</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌliven ˈup<br>ˌliven sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使愉快起来；活跃起来；兴奋起来<br><span class="en">to become or to make sb/sth more lively, interesting or exciting</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>livened up</b> when Alan asked her to dance.<br>艾伦请她跳舞，她便来了精神。<br>Put some music on to <b>liven things up</b>.<br>放些音乐活跃一下气氛吧。<br>A few pictures would <b>liven up</b> the room.<br>挂几张画会使房间更有生气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>load</b></td><td class="c2"><b>load ˈup (with sth)<br>load sth ˈup (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…装上；装满(尤指车辆)<br><span class="en">to put a lot of things in/on sth, especially a vehicle</span></td><td class="c4">Bring the car to the door and well help you <b>load</b> up.<br>把车开到门口，我们帮你装车。<br>We've <b>loaded</b> up all the furniture and are just about ready to go.<br>我们把所有家具都装上车，正准备出发。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>loan</b></td><td class="c2"><b>loan sth/sb ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把…借出或；租出；把…借给(或租给)<br><span class="en">to lend sth/sb to sb, sometimes in return for money</span></td><td class="c4">Several players have been <b>loaned out</b> to other teams.<br>有几名运动员借调到其他队。<br>Sometimes we <b>loan out</b> these buses.<br>我们有时把这些公共汽车租出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lock yourself aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把自己关起来(躲清静)<br><span class="en">to shut yourself in a place away from other people so that you are not disturbed</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>locked himself away</b> (in his room) until he'd finished his work.<br>他把自己关在房间里，直到把活儿干完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlock sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">警察等在紧急情况下控制出入；封锁建筑物；地区；城市等<br><span class="en">(of the police, etc.) to strictly control who goes in and out of a particular building, area, city, etc. during an emergency</span></td><td class="c4">It would take more officers than we have to <b>lock down</b> the whole city.<br>要封锁整座城市，我们警力不足。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lock sb/sth ˈin<br>ˌlock yourself ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…锁在里面；把…关起来<br><span class="en">to put sb/sth/yourself in a room or building and lock the door</span></td><td class="c4">The prisoners are <b>locked in</b> every night.<br>犯人每晚都被锁在牢房里。<br>He rushed to his bedroom and <b>locked himself in</b>.<br>他冲进卧室，把自己反锁在里面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlock sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">采取措施以确保(成果等)<br><span class="en">to carry out measures to ensure that improvements in a system are permanent</span></td><td class="c4">Formal treaties help <b>lock in</b> the benefits of arms control.<br>正式条约有助于确保军备控制成果不至付诸东流。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈlocked in sth</b></td><td class="c3">陷入；卷入困境或窘境；尤指旷日持久的纷争或诉讼<br><span class="en">to be involved in a difficult or unpleasant situation, especially an argument or a legal battle, that seems unlikely to end soon</span></td><td class="c4">The parents <b>are locked in</b> a bitter legal battle over the future of the twins.<br>父母为双胞胎的将来打起了激烈的官司。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlocked ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">无法摆脱(某一状况)；积习难改<br><span class="en">to be in a particular situation, or behave in a particular way, that you cannot change</span></td><td class="c4">The government is <b>locked into</b> a policy of reducing taxes.<br>政府难以从减税政策中抽身。<br>Older horses can get <b>locked into</b> bad habits.<br>老马难以改掉过去养成的恶习。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lock ˈonto sth (also ˌlock ˈin on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">武器搜寻跟踪；锁定(攻击目标)<br><span class="en">if a weapon that is sent through the air locks onto sth or is locked onto sth that it is aimed at, it finds it and follows it</span></td><td class="c4">The missile can <b>lock onto</b> a target from a kilometre away.<br>导弹能锁定一公里之外的目标。<br>The missile was <b>locked onto</b> the target.<br>导弹锁定了目标。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlockout n</b></td><td class="c3">停工<br><span class="en">a situation when an employer refuses to let workers enter their place of work until they agree to particular conditions</span></td><td class="c4">The strikers faced a <b>lockout</b>.<br>罢工者面临停工的威胁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lock ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">停止正常；工作<br><span class="en">to stop working correctly</span></td><td class="c4">My brakes had <b>locked up</b>.<br>我的刹车卡住了。<br>The computer <b>locks up</b> when I try to load the program.<br>我一加载这个程序，计算机就。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,lock ˈup<br>ˌlock sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">锁好(某处的)门窗<br><span class="en">to make a building safe by locking the doors and windows</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure you <b>lock up</b> before you leave.<br>离开时别忘了锁好门窗。<br>She <b>locked the shop up</b> and went home.<br>她锁好商店的门窗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>log</b></td><td class="c2"><b>logˈin/ˈon<br>log ˈinto/onto sth (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">登录；登入；进入(计算机系统)<br><span class="en">to perform the actions that allow you to begin using a computer system</span></td><td class="c4">The password allows the user to log <b>onto</b> the system.<br>用户输入密码可进入系统。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlog sb ˈin/ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">使登入(计算机系统)<br><span class="en">to allow sb to begin using a computer system</span></td><td class="c4">The system is unable to <b>log you on</b>.<br>系统无法登入。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>loll</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌloll aˈbout<br>ˌloll aˈbout sth</b></td><td class="c3">懒洋洋地；坐着或躺着；站着；无所事事<br><span class="en">to sit, lie or stand in a relaxed way, doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">There were several kids <b>lolling</b> around outside the club.<br>有几个孩子在俱乐部外面闲荡。<br>Jim should get a job instead of <b>lolling</b> around the house all day.<br>吉姆应该找份工作，不应该成天闲在家里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>look</b></td><td class="c2"><b>look aˈcross/ˈover (at/to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">迅速朝(房间)对面看<br><span class="en">to look quickly across a room</span></td><td class="c4">His parents are <b>looking</b> after the children for the weekend.<br>他父母这个周末照看孩子们。<br>Sophie will <b>look</b> after the visitors.<br>索菲会接待客人的。<br>They're old enough to <b>look</b> after themselves now (= they don't need any help).<br>他们现在长大了，能够自立了。<br>He needs to be properly <b>looked</b> after.<br>他需要得到妥善的照顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>look ˈafter sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">处理；对…负责<br><span class="en">to deal with sth; to be responsible for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Their accountant <b>looks after</b> the financial side of things.<br>他们的会计负责财务方面的事。<br>Everything's being <b>looked after</b>.<br>所有的事情都有人负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook aˈhead (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">展望未来；为将来设想<br><span class="en">to think about what is going to happen in the future</span></td><td class="c4">The team is <b>looking ahead</b> to next season.<br>该队正为下个赛季作准备。<br><b>Looking ahead</b> to the weekend, the weather will stay fine.<br>可以预见好天气将持续到周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,look aˈround (BrE also ˌlook ˈround)</b></td><td class="c3">转过头看；回头看</td><td class="c4">The people in front kept <b>looking round</b> at us.<br>前面的人不时回过头看我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌlook ˈround<br>ˌlook ˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">游览；参观(某处)<br><span class="en">to visit a place or a building as a tourist or because you are interested in buying it, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Take your time <b>looking</b> around.<br>慢慢观光吧。<br>I spent the day <b>looking</b> around the town.<br>我白天游览了市区。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook aˈbout/round sth<br>ˌlook aˈbout/ˈround you</b></td><td class="c3">环视；四下察看<br><span class="en">to turn your head in different directions so that you can see sth or see what is there</span></td><td class="c4">She came into the room, <b>looked</b> around, then went out again.<br>她走进房间，四下察看了一下就出去了。<br>He <b>looked</b> <b>round</b> the classroom angrily.<br>他怒气冲冲地环顾教室。1。<br>What are <b>you</b> <b>looking</b> at?<br>你在看什么呢？2。<br>Can <b>you</b> <b>look</b> at this watch for me? I think it might be broken.<br>你能帮我看看这块于表吗？我想可能是坏了。<br>I took the car to the garage to get it <b>looked</b> at.<br>我把车开到修理厂去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook aˈbout/round sth<br>ˌlook aˈbout/ˈround you</b></td><td class="c3">常作为正面或<br><span class="en">used to draw sb's attention to sb/sth, often as an example that you want them to follow or not follow</span></td><td class="c4">I wouldn't take advice from her-just <b>look</b> at the mess she's made of her own life!<br>我不会听她的建议的—— 就看看她把自己的生活搞得有多糟糕吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把视线(从…)移开<br><span class="en">to look in the opposite direction; to turn your eyes away from sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She looked at him then <b>looked away</b>.<br>她看了看他，然后移开了视线。<br>He mumbled a reply and <b>looked away</b> from me.<br>他叽里咕噜地回了一声，就不再正眼看我了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈback (at/on/to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">回首(往事)；回顾<br><span class="en">to think about sth that has happened in your past</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Looking back</b>, I'm not surprised she left.<br>回头想想，我对她的离去并不感到意外。<br>He <b>looked back</b> on his time in England with a sense of nostalgia.<br>他怀恋自己在英格兰的时光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,look ˈdown (at sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">尤指因尴尬；羞怯等垂下目光<br><span class="en">to turn your eyes downwards to the floor, especially because you are embarrassed, shy, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The little boy blushed and looked <b>down</b>.<br>小男孩脸红了，低头向下看。<br>She looked <b>down</b> at her hands.<br>她低头看着自己的双手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i,look ˈdown on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">蔑视；轻视；看不起<br><span class="en">to consider sb/sth as less good or important than yourself</span></td><td class="c4">She tends to look <b>down</b> on people who haven't been to college.<br>她一向瞧不起没读过大学的人。<br>They looked <b>down</b> on our little house.<br>他们对我们的小屋不屑一顾。<br>He was looked <b>down</b> on at school.<br>他在学校被人看扁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,look ˈforward to sth<br>ˌlook ˈforward to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">盼望；期待<br><span class="en">to feel excited about sth that is going to happen because you expect to enjoy it</span></td><td class="c4">Are you <b>looking</b> <b>forward</b> to your trip?<br>你期待着这次旅行吗？r'm。<br>We're <b>looking</b> <b>forward</b> to the concert!<br>我们对音乐会翘首以待。<br>I <b>look</b> <b>forward</b> to hearing from you (= at the end of a letter).<br>盼望着收到你的来信。<br>The President's visit is eagerly <b>looked</b> <b>forward</b> to.<br>人们热切盼望总统来访。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>look ˈin (on sb)</b></td><td class="c3">到某人处短暂拜访</td><td class="c4">Weve been <b>looking</b> for you.<br>我们一直在找你。<br>Are you still <b>looking</b> for a job?<br>你还在找工作吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>look ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">仔细调查；周详地研究；慎重考虑<br><span class="en">to examine sth or consider it carefully</span></td><td class="c4">The committee is <b>looking into</b> the matter.<br>委员会正在调查这一事件。<br>The manager is <b>looking into</b> your complaint.<br>经理正在处理你的投诉。<br>We're <b>looking into</b> the possibility of moving to France.<br>我们正在考虑能否迁往法因。<br>This situation should be <b>looked into</b>.<br>这个情况应该进行调查。<br>Passers-by just <b>looked</b> on as he was attacked.<br>他遭人袭击时路人只在一边袖手旁观。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈonlooker n</b></td><td class="c3">旁观者</td><td class="c4">A crowd of <b>onlookers</b> formed around the fight.<br>大群人围观斗殴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>look ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">表示劝告；尤指有危险小心；留神；注意<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to be careful, especially when there is some danger</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Look out</b>! There's a car coming.<br>当心！有车来了。<br>You're going to burn that <b>food</b> if you don't look out.<br>你要是不看着点，就会把食物煮糊了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈout for sb/yourself</b></td><td class="c3">考虑…的利益；关照<br><span class="en">to take care of sb/yourself and think about their/your own interests</span></td><td class="c4">Once he was in London he had to <b>look</b> <b>out</b> for himself.<br>到了伦敦他就要自己照顾自己。<br>Emilys brothers always <b>looked</b> <b>out</b> for her.<br>埃米莉的兄弟们总是关照她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈout for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">尽力寻找<br><span class="en">to try to find sb/sth or meet sb</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>looking out for</b> Pete but I didn't see him.<br>我当时一直找皮特，可没看见他。<br><b>Look out for</b> this movie at your local multiplex.<br>留意当地影城是否上映这部影片。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈout for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">提防；防备<br><span class="en">to try to avoid sth bad happening or doing sth bad</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Look out for</b> pickpockets.<br>当心扒手。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈout on/over sth</b></td><td class="c3">房间等<br><span class="en">of a room, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Our room <b>looked out over</b> the square.<br>从我们的房间朝外看可俯视广场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>g,look ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">游览；参观<br><span class="en">to make a tour of a place</span></td><td class="c4">We were invited to look <b>over</b> the new classrooms.<br>我们应邀参观了新教室。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>g,look ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">浏览；快速阅读<br><span class="en">to read sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">I need to look <b>over</b> my notes before the test.<br>测验前我得把笔记过一遍。<br>Your tutor will look <b>over</b> your work with you.<br>你的导师会和你一起看一遍你的作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook ˈthrough sb</b></td><td class="c3">对某人视而不见；佯装没认出某人<br><span class="en">to look at sb and not show that you have seen or recognized them</span></td><td class="c4">I smiled at him, but he just <b>looked straight through</b> me.<br>我朝他笑了笑，可他假装没看见我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>look ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">浏览；快速阅读<br><span class="en">to read sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>looked through</b> her notes before the exam.<br>她考试前匆匆看了一下笔记。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>look ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">查看；翻看(一批物品或某物内的东西)<br><span class="en">to examine a collection of things or what is inside sth</span></td><td class="c4">What are you doing <b>looking through</b> my bag?<br>你干吗翻我的包。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlook to sb/sth (for sth/to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">依赖；指望<br><span class="en">to rely on sb/sth or expect sb to provide sth or do sth</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>looked to</b> us for help.<br>他们指望我们提供帮助。<br>We must <b>look to other means to</b> generate the funds we need.<br>我们必须通过别的途径筹集所需资金。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈlook to sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">考虑将来；的事；展望<br><span class="en">to think about sth that will happen in the future</span></td><td class="c4">We are <b>looking to</b> the future with confidence.<br>我们满怀信心地展望未来。<br>Business is <b>looking</b> up at last.<br>生意终于有了起色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlook sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指久别后到某人处拜访；看望；联络<br><span class="en">to visit or contact sb when you are in the place where they live, especially when you have not seen them for a long time</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Look me up</b> next time youre in London.<br>你下次到伦敦时来看我吧。语态。<br>Everyone <b>looks up</b> to her because of who she is.<br>由于她的身份，每个人都敬重她。<br>She was <b>looked up</b> to by the rest of her family.<br>她受到家人的尊敬。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>loom</b></td><td class="c2"><b>loom aˈhead</b></td><td class="c3">危险；困难或令人不快的事情即将出现；逼近<br><span class="en">if sth dangerous, difficult or unpleasant looms ahead, it is likely to happen soon</span></td><td class="c4">Further problems are <b>looming ahead</b>.<br>更多的问题迫在眉睫。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌloom ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">令人惊恐地隐现；赫然耸现<br><span class="en">to appear as a large shape that is not clear, often in a way that seems frightening or threatening</span></td><td class="c4">A shape <b>loomed up</b> out of the fog.<br>雾中出现了一个模糊的身影。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>loosen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌloosen ˈup<br>ˌloosen sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使放松；(使)不拘束<br><span class="en">to become more relaxed and comfortable; to make sb feel like this</span></td><td class="c4">He began to <b>loosen up</b> and enjoy the evening.<br>他开始轻松下来，享受这个夜晚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lose</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lose ˈout (on sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">得不到(需要或觉得应有的东西)<br><span class="en">to be unsuccessful in getting sth that you want or think you should have</span></td><td class="c4">Some youngsters are taking day jobs and <b>losing out</b> on schooling.<br>有些孩子因白天工作而荒废了学业。<br>While the stores make big profits, it's the customer who <b>loses out</b>.<br>商店赚大钱，而吃亏的是顾客。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>lose ˈout to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">生意落到…手里<br><span class="en">to not get the business you expected Or hoped to get, because sb else has got it</span></td><td class="c4">Small stores are <b>losing out to</b> the big supermarkets.<br>小商店的生意都被大型超市抢走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lounge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlounge aˈround<br>ˌlounge aˈround sth (BrE also ˌlounge aˈbout, ˌlounge aˈbout sth)</b></td><td class="c3">懒散度日；游手好闲；在(某处)转悠<br><span class="en">to spend your time in a relaxed way doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">She was always <b>lounging</b> <b>about</b> while the rest of us were working!<br>我们在干活，而她总是到处晃荡。<br>They were <b>lounging around</b> the hotel pool.<br>他们在宾馆的游泳池里消磨时间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>louse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌlouse sth ˈup <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">搞坏；弄糟；办砸<br><span class="en">to spoil or ruin sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>loused up</b>. my promotion chances.<br>他使我失去了晋升的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>lump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>lump A and B toˈgether<br>ˈlump A with B<br>ˈlump A in with B <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…归并在一起；合起来考虑<br><span class="en">to put or consider two or more people or things together in the same group</span></td><td class="c4">A large number of plants are <b>lumped</b> <b>together</b> under the name of herbs'.<br>很多植物被笼统地归于“草本植物”类。<br>You can't <b>lump</b> the elderly and the disabled <b>together</b>.<br>你不能把上年纪的人和残障人士混为一谈。<br>You can't <b>lump</b> the elderly with the disabled.<br>你不能把上年纪的人和残障人士混为一谈。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>luxuriate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>luˈxuriate in sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尽情享受；沉溺于<br><span class="en">to take great pleasure in sth that is very pleasant and relaxing</span></td><td class="c4">Alison likes to <b>luxuriate in</b> a long, hot bath.<br>艾莉森喜欢长时间泡热水澡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmail sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…邮寄出(至某处)；寄来<br><span class="en">to send sth by post/mail to a place where it will be dealt with</span></td><td class="c4">Don't forget to <b>mail in</b> your entry form for the contest!<br>别忘了把比赛报名表寄来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmail sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">批量邮寄<br><span class="en">to send sth to a lot of different people or places at the same time</span></td><td class="c4">Catalogues will be <b>mailed out</b> next week.<br>这些目录将在下周寄出。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>major</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmajor in sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">主修；获得(某一学科)的学位<br><span class="en">to study sth as your main subject at a university or college; to get a degree in that subject</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>majored in</b> chemistry.<br>他学的是化学专业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>make</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake aˈway with sth</b></td><td class="c3">偷走；携(赃物)逃走<br><span class="en">to steal sth and take it away with you</span></td><td class="c4">Thieves <b>made away with</b> a computer and two televisions.<br>小偷窃走了一台计算机和两台电视机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmake for sth not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The two-hour journey to work <b>makes</b> for a long day.<br>上班的两小时路程使工作日很漫长。<br>The large print <b>makes</b> for easier reading.<br>大字体便于阅读。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmake sth of sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">领会；理解<br><span class="en">to have an impression or an understanding of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">What did you <b>make of</b> the play?<br>你觉得这出戏怎么样。<br>I never knew quite what to <b>make of</b> Nick.<br>我向来不大了解尼克。<br>The information we have is so confused, it's hard to <b>make anything of</b> it.<br>我们手头的资料杂乱无章，很难理出头绪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake ˈoff (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">匆忙离开；(尤指)仓皇逃跑；携赃物溜走<br><span class="en">to hurry or rush away, especially when sb is trying to escape or has stolen sth</span></td><td class="c4">The youths <b>made off</b> in a stolen car.<br>小青年们开着偷来的车溜了。<br>Two boys <b>made off</b> with our bags.<br>两个男孩偷走了我们的包。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake ˈout <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用于询问应付；过活<br><span class="en">to ask sb how they have managed or survived in a particular situation .</span></td><td class="c4">How are you <b>making out</b> in your new home?<br>你在新家生活得怎么样。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>make sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">看出；读出；辨出<br><span class="en">to manage to see sb/sth or read sth</span></td><td class="c4">She could just <b>make out</b> the sound of distant voices.<br>她模模糊糊地听到远处有人说话。1。<br>She could not distinguish the <b>make</b> of the car.<br>她认不出这辆车的牌子。<br>I can't <b>make her out</b> at all.<br>我根本摸不透她。<br>He couldn't <b>make out</b> what was going on.<br>他搞不清这到底是怎么回事。<br>You need to apply for a permit, as far as / can <b>make out</b>.<br>据我所知，你需要申请许可证。<br>How do you <b>make that out</b> (= how did you reach that conclusion)?<br>你怎么得出那个结论的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>make sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">开具；填写(表格或文件)<br><span class="en">to write out or complete a form or document</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>made out</b> a cheque for £100.<br>他开了一张 100 英镑的支票。<br>Who shall I <b>make the cheque out</b> to (= whose name shall I write on it)?<br>支票抬头写什么。<br>Shall I <b>make the invoice out</b> to the company?<br>发票抬头写公司的名称吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>make sb/sth ˈover <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">改变形象；改造(作新用途)；修饰<br><span class="en">to change sb/sth to give them/it a new appearance; to change sth to give it a new use</span></td><td class="c4">They decided to <b>make over</b> the whole house when they moved in.<br>他们决定搬进去时把房子整个翻新一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmakeover n</b></td><td class="c3">外观的改进；改善；修饰<br><span class="en">the process of improving the appearance of a person or a place</span></td><td class="c4">She won a complete <b>makeover</b> (= new clothes, hairstyle, etc.) in a competition.<br>她在比赛中获得革新形象奖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>make sth ˈover to sb</b></td><td class="c3">把…转让给；将…赠与<br><span class="en">to legally give sth you own to sb else</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>made his estate over to</b> his eldest son.<br>他把财产留给了长子。<br>The government has <b>made</b> a lot of its power <b>over</b> to the regions.<br>政府将很多权力下放给了各地区。<br>The house was <b>made over to</b> the charity three years ago.<br>三年前这所房子转贈给了慈善机构。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>make ˈup<br>ˌmake sb/sth ˈup<br>ˌmake yourself ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">化妆；打扮<br><span class="en">to put make-up on to make sb/yourself attractive or to prepare for an appearance in the theatre, on television, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She spends ages <b>making herself up</b>.<br>她没完没了地梳妆打扮。<br>The children had been <b>made up</b> to look like clowns.<br>孩子们化装成小丑。ˌ。<br>She's always carefully <b>made</b>-up.<br>她总是精心化妆。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake ˈup<br>ˌmake it ˈup (with sb) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…和解；言归于好<br><span class="en">to end an argument or a disagreement with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Let's kiss and <b>make up</b>.<br>我们和好吧。<br>He's <b>made it up</b> with his parents.<br>他和父母重归于好。<br>It turned out she had <b>made the whole thing up</b>.<br>后来发现事情从头到尾是她瞎编的。<br>Did you think I was <b>making it all up</b>?<br>你是不是以为我纯粹是在瞎编？四a。<br>Women <b>make up</b> 55% of the student population.<br>女生占学生人数的 55%。<br>The course is <b>made up</b> of five modules.<br>这门课程由五个模块组成。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake ˈup<br>ˌmake it ˈup (with sb) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">补足；补偿<br><span class="en">to replace sth that has been lost or missed</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>make up</b> lost time.<br>我们得弥补时间上的损失。<br>The warm welcome we received more than <b>made up</b> for our horrendous journey there.<br>我们受到的热烈欢迎尽可弥补旅途的艰辛。<br>He was late for work but he <b>made the time up</b> the following day.<br>他上班迟到了，可他第二天把时间补上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmake ˈup<br>ˌmake it ˈup (with sb) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">准备；配制；预备；配备<br><span class="en">to prepare sth; to make sth ready to use</span></td><td class="c4">The Pharmacist <b>made up</b> the prescruption (= the medicine).<br>药剂师配好了药。<br>The bed's already <b>made up</b>.<br>床已经铺好了。<br>She bought a length of material for <b>making up</b> into a skirt.<br>她买了一块布料，打算做一件裙子。<br>Have you <b>made up</b> your minds where to go for your honeymoon?<br>你们想好去哪儿度蜜月了吗。<br>Come on-it's <b>make your mind up</b> time!<br>别犹豫——该下决心了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmake-up n</b></td><td class="c3">组成成分；构成方式<br><span class="en">the different things, people, qualities, etc. that combine to form sth</span></td><td class="c4">The country has a complicated ethnic <b>make-up</b>.<br>这个国家的民族成分很复杂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmake-up n</b></td><td class="c3">补考；缓考</td><td class="c4">The <b>make-up</b> will be on Friday.<br>补考安排在星期五。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>make ˈup to sb <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">奉承；讨好；巴结<br><span class="en">to be pleasant to sb in order to get an advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>making up to</b> the boss.<br>他总是拍老板的马屁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmake with sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">做(某事)；用(某物)<br><span class="en">to do sth or use sth</span></td><td class="c4">Just <b>make with</b> the apology and buzz off.<br>道个歉，马上离开。<br>Stop talking and <b>make with</b> the duster (= start cleaning).<br>别说了，开始打扫吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>map</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmap sth on/onto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…与…对应起来；有关联；映射<br><span class="en">to link a group of qualities, items, etc. with their source, cause, position on a scale, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Grammar information enables students to <b>map</b> the structure of a foreign language <b>onto</b> their own.<br>语法信息可使学生将外语的结构与母语对应起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmap sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">详细规划；周密安排<br><span class="en">to plan or arrange sth in detail</span></td><td class="c4">She felt as though her future had been <b>mapped out</b> for her.<br>她感觉她的未来似乎被精心设计好了。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>march</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmarch ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续行进；继续快步走<br><span class="en">to continue marching; to continue walking quickly</span></td><td class="c4">Time <b>marched on</b> and we still hadn't finished.<br>时间过得飞快，我们还没有完成任务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">压低…的成绩；减分<br><span class="en">to reduce the marks given to sb in an examination, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>marked down</b> for poor spelling.<br>她因拼写错误过多被扣了分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">标低…的价格；降价；削价<br><span class="en">to reduce the price of sth</span></td><td class="c4">All goods have been <b>marked down</b> by 15%.<br>所有商品一律打八五折。a。<br>The council had the old square <b>marked down</b> for new development.<br>委员会决定开发旧广场。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sb ˈdown as sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">将某人看作；认定某人是<br><span class="en">to consider sb to be a particular type of person</span></td><td class="c4">I had him <b>marked down as</b> a promising player from the start.<br>我一开始就觉得他是个前途无量的运动员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">画线分隔；划分<br><span class="en">to separate sth by marking a line between it and sth else</span></td><td class="c4">We've <b>marked the playing area off</b> with a white line.<br>我们用白线划出了运动场地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">清单上做记号<br><span class="en">to write or draw a mark beside a name or an item on a list, for example, for a particular reason</span></td><td class="c4">The students I want to see are <b>marked off</b> on the list.<br>我在名单上对想见的学生标了记号。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>mark sb/sth ˈout (BrE also,mark sb/sth ˈoff less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">使与众不同；使有别于<br><span class="en">to make sb or sth different from other people or things</span></td><td class="c4">There was something about her which <b>marked her out</b> from the other students.<br>她有些地方和其他学生不一样。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用线画出…的范围；用线标出…的；界限(或边界)<br><span class="en">to draw lines to show the edges of sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>marked out</b> a circle on the ground.<br>她在地上画圈为界。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">标高…的价格；提价；加价<br><span class="en">to increase the price of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Shares were <b>marked up</b> by 8%.<br>股票价格上涨了8%。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmark sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">标示；修改(文本)<br><span class="en">to mark or correct a text</span></td><td class="c4">The text had already been <b>marked up</b> with corrections (= for printing).<br>文稿已校对。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>marry</b></td><td class="c2"><b>marry beˈneath you/yourself</b></td><td class="c3">与地位比自己低的人结婚；下嫁<br><span class="en">to marry sb who belongs to a lower social class than your own</span></td><td class="c4">She thought her son was marrying <b>beneath</b> him.<br>她觉得儿子娶的媳妇配不上他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmarry ˈupi<br>marry sth ˈup (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使两物；或两部分结合起来；(使)连接上<br><span class="en">to join up or connect successfully; to make two things or two parts do this</span></td><td class="c4">He couldn't <b>marry</b> up the two parts of the lock.<br>他锁不上锁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmarry ˈupi<br>marry sth ˈup (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使两；事物相称；匹配<br><span class="en">to match; to make two things match</span></td><td class="c4">The two versions of the story don't quite <b>marry</b> up.<br>这件事的两种说法有出入。<br>The lawyers couldn't <b>marry</b> up her story with the facts.<br>律师无法将她的说法和事实对上号。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>marvel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmarvel at sth</b></td><td class="c3">深感惊奇；大为赞叹<br><span class="en">to be very surprised or impressed by sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Everyone <b>marvelled at</b> his courage.<br>他的勇气人人钦佩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>match</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmatch sth against sth</b></td><td class="c3">比较；对照<br><span class="en">to compare sth to sth else to see how the two things are similar or different</span></td><td class="c4">We are able to <b>match</b> the details he gave us <b>against</b> the information held on the computer.<br>我们可以拿他提供的详情与计算机存储的信息相互参照。<br>The two statements don't <b>match</b> up.<br>这两个说法有出入。<br>They were unable to <b>match</b> up his tissue type with any of the possible donors.<br>在可能的捐赠者中，他们未能找到与他匹配的身体组织类型。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>max</b></td><td class="c2"><b>max ˈout<br>ˌmax sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">达到最大极限；达到极点<br><span class="en">to reach the limit at which nothing more is possible</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>maxed out</b> at 180 mph.<br>这辆车跑出了180英里的最高时速。<br>I just <b>maxed out</b> my credit card.<br>我刚用完了信用卡的最高限额。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>measure</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmeasure sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">量出(长度)<br><span class="en">to mark out a particular length on sth such as a piece of cloth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>measured off</b> two metres of cloth.<br>她量了两米布。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>measure sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">量出；取出(所需量)<br><span class="en">to measure the quantity of sth that you need from a larger amount</span></td><td class="c4">He measured out the ingredients <b>for</b> the cake.<br>他称好了做蛋糕的配料。<br>The procedures don't <b>measure</b> up to today's standards.<br>这些程序不符合现在的标准。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>meet</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmeet with sb</b></td><td class="c3">会见<br><span class="en">to have a meeting with sb</span></td><td class="c4">The Prime Minister <b>met with</b> other European leaders this morning.<br>首相今晨与欧洲其他领导人会晤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmeet with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">遭遇；遭受(令人不快的事)<br><span class="en">to experience sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">The chief witness <b>met with</b> an accident on his way to the court.<br>主要证人在前往法庭的途中出事了。<br>Our attempts to save her <b>met with</b> failure.<br>我们救援她的努力失败了。<br>My explanation <b>met with</b> a blank stare.<br>我的解释换来一脸茫然。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmeet sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…作为；回应<br><span class="en">to react to sth in a particular way, especially a bad or negative way</span></td><td class="c4">The proposal was <b>met with</b> anger and dismay.<br>该项议案使人们感到愤怒和沮丧。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mellow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>mellow ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">悠然自得；放松<br><span class="en">to relax and do very little</span></td><td class="c4">We could just put on some music and <b>mellow out</b>.<br>我们可以放点音乐轻松一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>mellow sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使心情轻松；使放松<br><span class="en">to make sb more relaxed</span></td><td class="c4">A week on the beach should <b>mellow him out</b>.<br>在海滨过一周他就会放松下来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>melt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmelt aˈway<br>ˌmelt sth</b></td><td class="c3">使逐渐消失<br><span class="en">a way to disappear gradually; to make sth disappear gradually</span></td><td class="c4">His anger <b>melted away</b>.<br>他的怒气渐渐消了。<br>The crowd dispersed, <b>melting away</b> into the side streets.<br>人群散了，慢慢消失在街巷里。<br>His smile <b>melted away</b> all the tension.<br>他浅浅一笑，紧张气氛消散殆尽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>melt sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使熔化；使回炉<br><span class="en">to heat sth until it is in a liquid state, usually so that it can be made into sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Aluminium cans can be <b>melted down</b> and recycled.<br>铝罐可回炉再用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmelt into sth</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐融入；与…成为一体<br><span class="en">to gradually become part of sth and difficult to see</span></td><td class="c4">I tried hard to <b>melt into</b> the background.<br>我想方设法隐身幕后。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>merge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmerge ˈin (with sth)<br>merge ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">与…合而为一；同…融为一体；和…不分彼此<br><span class="en">if sth merges in (with sth) or merges into sth, it is so similar to the second thing that you cannot really see the differences between them or where one ends and the other begins</span></td><td class="c4">The new college building does not <b>merge</b> in with the old buildings.<br>大学的新楼和旧楼群不协调。<br>Autumn is <b>merging</b> <b>into</b> winter.<br>不经意间秋去冬来。<br>Saturday and Sunday seemed to <b>merge</b> <b>into</b> each other.<br>那个星期六和星期天似乎是连在一起过的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mess</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmess sb aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">糊弄；耍弄；公正地对待<br><span class="en">to treat sb badly, making them waste time, changing your mind a lot, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>messed us around</b> so much, I wrote to complain.<br>他们这样耍我们，我已写信去投诉了。<br>I don't like being <b>messed about</b>.<br>我讨厌被人愚卉。<br>Children love to <b>mess about</b> in water.<br>儿童喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmess sb aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；瞎混<br><span class="en">(with sb/sth) to behave in a silly way, especially when you should be working or doing sth else</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>messing around</b> in class.<br>他在课堂上捣乱。<br>She <b>messed about</b> all year and failed her exams.<br>她一年到头在鬼混，结果考砸了。<br>Stop <b>messing around</b> with Tony and get on with your work.<br>别和托尼瞎混了，快干活吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmess sb aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开玩笑；胡说<br><span class="en">to joke, to say silly things</span></td><td class="c4">I'm not <b>messing about</b>, it's true!<br>我不开玩笑，这是真的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmess sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">扰乱某人的生活；使心情恶劣；使精神痛苦<br><span class="en">to spoil sb’s life; to make sb suffer emotionally or mentally</span></td><td class="c4">His Parents really <b>messed him up</b>.<br>他爸妈真的把他给毁了。<br>He came back into her life and <b>messed her up</b> again.<br>他回到她的身边，再次搅乱了她的生活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmess with sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…摆弄坏；把…捣鼓坏</td><td class="c4">Who's been <b>messing with</b> the answering machine?<br>谁把电话答录机搞坏了。<br>Read the label carefully before you start <b>messing with</b> dangerous products.<br>使用危险品前，先仔细阅读标签。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmess with sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">陷入；卷入(危险)<br><span class="en">to get involved with sth dangerous</span></td><td class="c4">How long has he been <b>messing with</b> drugs?<br>他吸毒有多久了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>militate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmilitate aˈgainst sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">防止；妨碍<br><span class="en">to prevent sth; to make it difficult for sth to happen</span></td><td class="c4">Lack of funds <b>militated against</b> the success of the campaign.<br>资金短缺使这一活动难以成功。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mind</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmind ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用于警告小心；注意<br><span class="en">used to warn sb to be careful</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Mind out</b>! You nearly knocked me off my bike!<br>看着点！你险些把我从自行车上撞下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>minister</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈminister to sb/sth <span class="tag">(old-fashioned formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">照料；服侍；满足…所需<br><span class="en">to care for sb; to make sure that sb/sth has everything necessary</span></td><td class="c4">She felt it was her vocation to <b>minister to</b> the sick.<br>她觉得护理病人是她的天职。<br>Servants <b>ministered to</b> his needs.<br>仆人们鞍前马后地伺候他。<br>He would not be <b>ministered to</b> by strangers.<br>他不肯让陌生人照顾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>minor</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈminor in sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">辅修<br><span class="en">to study another subject as well as your main subject at a university or college</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>minored in</b> Art History.<br>他选择辅修了艺术史。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>miss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>miss ˈout (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">错失(机会)<br><span class="en">to lose an opportunity to benefit from sth or enjoy yourself, by not doing sth or taking part in an activity</span></td><td class="c4">Have I <b>missed anybody out</b>?<br>我有没有漏掉谁。<br>She <b>missed out</b> a few chapters in the middle.<br>她漏了中间的几章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mist</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmist ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">玻璃蒙上水汽<br><span class="en">if glass mists over, it becomes covered with very small drops of water so that you cannot see through it</span></td><td class="c4">As soon as I stepped inside, my glasses <b>misted over</b>.<br>我一踏进屋里，眼镜上就蒙了一层雾。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmist ˈup<br>ˌmist sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">玻璃；镜子等蒙上；雾气<br><span class="en">to cover gqlass,a mirror, etc. with small drops of water so that you cannot see Clearly</span></td><td class="c4">The inside of the car was beginning to <b>mist up</b>.<br>车内开始蒙上雾气了。<br>The windows were <b>misted up</b>.<br>窗户蒙了一层水汽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mix</b></td><td class="c2"><b>mix sth ˈin (with sth)<br>mix sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指烹调时使与…混合；掺入；和入<br><span class="en">to combine one substance with others, especially in cooking</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Mix</b> the eggs in slowly.<br>慢慢把鸡蛋。<br><b>Mix</b> a little cream <b>into</b> the sauce.<br>在调味酱里搀一点奶油。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>mix sb ˈup<br>be/get ˌmixed ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…搞糊涂；使弄不清<br><span class="en">to make sb unable to think clearly or understand what is happening; to be in or get into this state</span></td><td class="c4">Now you've <b>mixed me up</b> completely! I'm really confused.<br>你现在把我彻底搞懵了！我实在是弄不懂了。<br>The hospital <b>mixed up</b> the babies' name tags.<br>医院把婴儿的姓名牌弄混了。<br>She always gets her left and right <b>mixed up</b>.<br>她总是分不清左右。<br>People who are colour-blind usually get red and green <b>mixed up</b>.<br>色育的人通常区分不了红色和绿色。<br>My letters have all been <b>mixed up</b> with yours.<br>我和你的信全混在一起了。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmix-up n</b></td><td class="c3">混乱；杂乱<br><span class="en">a mistake that causes confusion; a situation that is full of confusion</span></td><td class="c4">There was a <b>mix-up</b> over the tickets.<br>票弄混了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌmixed ˈup in sth</b></td><td class="c3">卷入；陷入(危险或非法之事)<br><span class="en">to be/become involved in sth dangerous or illegal</span></td><td class="c4">He would never have <b>got mixed up in</b> anything criminal.<br>他绝不会参与任何犯罪活动的。<br>How did you <b>get mixed up in</b> all this?<br>你是怎样被牵连进这一切的。<br>He was <b>mixed</b> up with the wrong crowd for a while.<br>他和一些不三不四的人交往过一阵。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmix it ˈup with sb <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…打架<br><span class="en">to fight with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Some guys came into the bar obviously in the mood to <b>mix it up with</b> someone.<br>几个家伙走进酒吧，显然想要找人干上一架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmix it ˈup with sb <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…争吵；与…争执起来<br><span class="en">to start an argument with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Do they really mean what they say, or are they just trying to <b>mix it up with</b> the other side?<br>他们说的话是当真的吗，还是他们只想和对方吵上一架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmix it with sb <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和…较量；与…吵架；与…打架<br><span class="en">to compete with sb; to argue or fight with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Hell be <b>mixing it with</b> the world's best players.<br>他将和世界顶级好手决一雌雄。<br>He can <b>mix it with</b> the best of them.<br>他能够和他们中的强手一较高低。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmix it with sb <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和…交往；同…相处<br><span class="en">to meet spend time with people in a friendly way</span></td><td class="c4">She loves <b>mixing it with</b> the rich and famous.<br>她喜欢结交富人与名流。单独使用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmock sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">制作…的实体模型<br><span class="en">to produce a copy of sth that is going to be made, so that it can be tested or people can see what it will be like</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>mocked up</b> the front page to see how it would look.<br>我们把头版编排了出来，看看效果如何。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>monkey</b></td><td class="c2"><b>monkey aˈbout/aˈround (with sth) <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；瞎弄；乱改<br><span class="en">to behave in a silly way; to touch or change sth in a careless way</span></td><td class="c4">They were monkeying <b>around</b> in class.<br>他们那会儿正在课堂上捣蛋。<br>He' monkeyed <b>about</b> with the original words of the song.<br>他改动歌词闹着玩儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>moon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈmoon over sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出神地思念(钟爱的人)；对…魂牵梦萦<br><span class="en">to spend your time in a dream thinking about sb that you love</span></td><td class="c4">He spends most of his time <b>mooning over</b> Helen.<br>他大部分时间都在痴想着海伦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>mop ˈup<br>ˌmop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用光；用完<br><span class="en">to use up all of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The new factory should <b>mop up</b> the pool of surplus labour.<br>新工厂应该把剩余劳力全部用上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>mop ˈup<br>ˌmop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">控制；支配<br><span class="en">to take control of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The company started <b>mopping up</b> smaller firms.<br>这家公司开始兼并小公司。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmop sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">肃清(残敌)；完成余下的；工作<br><span class="en">to get rid of the last few people who continue to oppose you; to finish tasks that remain</span></td><td class="c4">The army <b>mopped up</b> some isolated pockets of resistance.<br>部队剿灭了一些孤立的抵抗势力。<br>There are a few things to <b>mop up</b> before we go.<br>我们走之前还有几件事儿要完成。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mope</b></td><td class="c2"><b>also<br>mope aˈbout<br>mope aˈbout sth</b></td><td class="c3">无聊地闲荡；闲逛<br><span class="en">to walk about a place in an unhappy way, with no particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">He's been <b>moping</b> <b>about</b> all day.<br>他百无聊赖地转悠了一整天。<br>You spend too much time <b>moping</b> around the house.<br>你闷在家的时间太多了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mount</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmount ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">大小或数量渐增；缓升<br><span class="en">to increase gradually in size or quantity</span></td><td class="c4">The paperwork soon <b>mounts up</b> if you don't deal with it immediately.<br>一不及时处理，文案工作很快就攒成堆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmouse ˈover sth (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">滑动鼠标至(计算机屏幕某处)；鼠标悬停于<br><span class="en">to move a computer mouse so that you point to a particular area on the screen</span></td><td class="c4">When you <b>mouse over</b> these hot spots, they change colour.<br>移动鼠标指向这些热点，他们会变颜色。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mouth</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmouth ˈoff (at/about sb/sth) <span class="tag">(informal often used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行</td><td class="c4">I could hear him <b>mouthing off</b> about how they should have won.<br>我听到他在高谈阔论他们如何如何本应取胜。<br>She was <b>mouthing off</b> at all the other drivers on the road.<br>她扯着嗓门大骂所有其他路过的司机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>move</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈcross<br>move aˈcross sth</b></td><td class="c3">移到另一边；穿过<br><span class="en">to move from one side of sth to the other</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>moved across</b> to the window and looked out.<br>他走到对面的窗前向外张望。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈhead</b></td><td class="c3">耽搁之后发展；进展<br><span class="en">to advance or develop, often after there has been a delay</span></td><td class="c4">The project is <b>moving ahead</b> again now.<br>这个项目现在又有了进展。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈhead of sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">比…移动得快；比…进展迅速；领先…一步<br><span class="en">to move faster than sb/sth; to develop more quickly than sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Our foreign competitors are <b>moving ahead of</b> us.<br>国外竞争对手走在我们前面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈlong ˌmove aˈlong sth</b></td><td class="c3">沿着…前行<br><span class="en">to go forward</span></td><td class="c4">The convoy of cars was <b>moving</b> slowly <b>along</b> the road.<br>车队在公路上缓慢行进。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈlong/ˈon<br>ˌmove sb aˈlong/on</b></td><td class="c3">使挪动；(使)移动<br><span class="en">to leave a particular place or go to a new position; to make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Move along</b> now. You're blocking the entrance.<br>往前走。你挡住门啦。<br>The police arrived to <b>move the demonstrators along</b>.<br>警察到场让示威人群移动起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">分开；分离<br><span class="en">if two or more things or people move apart, they become separated by a distance</span></td><td class="c4">They quickly <b>moved apart</b> when I walked in.<br>我走进来，他们马上分开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈbout/ˈround<br>move aˈbout/round sth especially BrE</b></td><td class="c3">不停移动；走来走去<br><span class="en">to keep moving from one place to another</span></td><td class="c4">Use the mouse to <b>move</b> around the screen.<br>用鼠标在屏幕上来回移动。<br>I have to <b>move</b> around a lot with my job.<br>我的工作需要我到处跑动。<br>She sang as she <b>moved</b> <b>about</b> the room.<br>她在房间里边走边唱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈround sth (also,move ˈround sth especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">绕过去；兜过去<br><span class="en">to move in a circle around sth that is blocking your path</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>moved</b> <b>round</b> the table to open the window.<br>她绕过桌子去开窗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把…挪到一边；移开(以腾出空间)<br><span class="en">to put sb/sth to one side away from the centre of a place, usually to make room for sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>moved the tables aside</b> so that we could dance.<br>我们把桌子都搬到边上以便跳舞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>move aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">搬家；迁离<br><span class="en">to leave the place where you live to go and live in another place</span></td><td class="c4">All her friends have <b>moved away</b> from the area.<br>她的朋友都从这个地方迁走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">歇手不干；不再追随；不再相信<br><span class="en">to stop doing, following or believing sth</span></td><td class="c4">The party seems to be <b>moving away from</b> its original aims.<br>该党似乎在背离其原来的宗旨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>move ˈback<br>ˌmove sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">使退后；(使)后移<br><span class="en">to go, or to move sth, to a new position at a distance away from the front or behind sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>moved back</b> a few steps.<br>他后退了几步。<br>She <b>moved her chair back</b> from the fire.<br>她把椅子从炉火旁往后挪了一挪。<br><b>It</b> took a long time to move the furniture back after the party.<br>聚会过后花了很长时间才把家具放归原位。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…移到；把…挪到<br><span class="en">to take sb/sth and put them/it in a new place</span></td><td class="c4">Weve <b>moved the phone into</b> the hall.<br>我们把电话移到了门厅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈoff <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出发；起程；启动<br><span class="en">to start a journey; to begin to move</span></td><td class="c4">Check your mirrors before you <b>move off</b>.<br>车启动之前注意看一下反光镜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈoff sth<br>ˌmove sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">离开；(把…)移开<br><span class="en">to leave the place where you are; to remove sb/sth from a particular place</span></td><td class="c4">Farmers are rapidly <b>moving off</b> the land.<br>农民正快速离开土地。<br>Can you <b>move your car off</b> the pavement please?<br>请把你的车开离人行道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">短暂；停留后继续行进；离开<br><span class="en">to continue your journey after stopping for a short while; to leave the place where you are and go to a new place</span></td><td class="c4">After a few minutes, the bus <b>moved on</b> again.<br>几分钟后公共汽车又往前开了。<br>The police told them to <b>move on</b> and go home!<br>警察命令他们离开这里回家去。<br>When I looked round, I realized everyone else had <b>moved on</b>.<br>我环顾四周，发现其他人都走掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">思想；信念等变化发展<br><span class="en">if ideas, beliefs, etc. move on, they change and develop</span></td><td class="c4">Things have <b>moved on</b> a lot since my parents were young.<br>与我父母年轻时相比，世事已经大变。<br>The debate does not seem to have <b>moved on</b> much.<br>争论似乎没有多大进展。<br>Fashions are <b>moving on</b> all the time.<br>流行时尚总是日新。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>move ˈout<br>ˌmove ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">搬出去住；(从…)迁出<br><span class="en">to leave your home and go to live somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">The lodger <b>moved</b> Yesterday.<br>房客昨天搬走了。<br>He wants to <b>move out</b> of London.<br>他想搬出伦敦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove sb ˈout<br>ˌmove sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">让…离开(尤指住所)<br><span class="en">to make sb leave a place, especially their home</span></td><td class="c4">The landlord is <b>moving the tenants out</b>.<br>房东要房客搬走。<br>The emergency services are <b>moving people out</b> of their homes.<br>紧急救援人员正将民众疏散出住所。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove sth ˈout<br>ˌmove sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…移开；挪开以腾出；空间<br><span class="en">to remove sth from a place, especially in order to make more space</span></td><td class="c4">We'll need to <b>move some chairs out</b> to make more room.<br>我们得搬走几张椅子，以便多腾出些地方。<br>When can you <b>move your belongings out</b> of my apartment?<br>你什么时候能把你的东西从我公寓里搬走。<br>That table will have to be <b>moved out</b> of the way.<br>那张桌子得挪开让道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">离开；脱离<br><span class="en">to leave a particular place, area Or Situation</span></td><td class="c4">We watched the boat <b>moving out of</b> the harbour.<br>我们看着那艘船驶离了港口。<br>The country is <b>moving out of</b> recession.<br>该国正从衰退中复苏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">退出；不再从事某项；活动或工作<br><span class="en">to stop being involved in a particular activity or area of business</span></td><td class="c4">Many people have been forced to <b>move</b> <b>out</b> offarming.<br>很多人被迫放弃了务农。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈover sth<br>ˌmove sb/sth ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">使缓慢走过(平面)<br><span class="en">to go forward slowly across a surface; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">The tank adapts to the ground it is <b>moving over</b>.<br>坦克能适应它驶过的地面。<br>Just <b>move the brush lightly over</b> the paper.<br>把画笔在纸上轻轻描画就行啦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈover sth<br>ˌmove sb/sth ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">用手抚摩；(用目光)打量；(使)缓缓移过<br><span class="en">if sb's hands, eyes, etc. move over sth, or sb moves them over sth, they slowly move across sth</span></td><td class="c4">His eyes <b>moved over</b> her face.<br>他的目光在她脸上游移。<br>She <b>moved her hands gently over</b> his injured ankle.<br>她用双手轻抚他受伤的脚踝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈpast sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…前面经过<br><span class="en">to pass in front of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>moved past</b> her into the lounge.<br>他在她面前走过，进了休息室。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove toˈwards sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">接近；靠近<br><span class="en">to approach sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She began to run as the car <b>moved towards</b> her.<br>车子冲她开来时她跑了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove to ward sth<br>move toˈward doing sth often</b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">We are <b>moving</b> <b>towards</b> a better understanding of the situation.<br>我们对局势有了更深入的了解。<br>Is the group <b>towards</b> finding a solution?<br>小组有望找到解决 o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">比率；水平或数量<br><span class="en">of a rate, a level or an amount</span></td><td class="c4">What will we do if interest rates <b>move up</b>?<br>如果利率上调，我们该怎么办。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmove ˈup<br>ˌmove sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使升级；(使)升入快班<br><span class="en">to move, make sb move, to a higher level, grade or</span></td><td class="c4">She's been <b>moved up</b> into the Advanced class.<br>她被调到了快班。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sth ˈup<br>ˌmove sb/sth ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">使上移；(使)升高<br><span class="en">to move from a lower to a higher position; to make sb/sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">Hold the ladder tightly and move <b>up</b> a rung at a rime.<br>抓紧梯子，一级一级往上爬。<br>Move your hand <b>up</b> and down.<br>上下挥动你的手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmow sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用枪杀死；撂倒；射杀(常指成群的人)<br><span class="en">to kill sb, often large numbers of people, with a gun</span></td><td class="c4">The demonstrators were <b>mown down</b> by the soldiers.<br>示威者被士兵开枪打死了。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>muck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuck aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">游手好闲；闲荡<br><span class="en">(with sb/sth) to spend time and enjoy yourself doing sth with no particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>mucking about</b> outside, kicking a ball around.<br>他们在外面玩耍，把一只球踢来踢去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuck aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">游手好闲；游荡；胡混<br><span class="en">(with sb/sth) to behave in a sily way, especially when you should be working or doing sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>mucking around</b> and go to bed.<br>别胡闹啦，睡觉去吧。<br>She <b>mucked around</b> all year and failed her exams.<br>她一年到头浑浑噩噩，结果没通过考试。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuck aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">玩笑；胡说八道<br><span class="en">to joke; to say silly things</span></td><td class="c4">I thought he was <b>mucking about</b> until I saw it was real blood on his face.<br>我还以为他是闹着玩儿，直到我看见他脸上真的有血。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuck aˈbout/aˈround with sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">瞎弄；胡搞；乱改<br><span class="en">to keep touching, moving or changing sth in an annoying way</span></td><td class="c4">Who's been <b>mucking about with</b> my computer?<br>谁摆弄过我的计算机啦。<br>Don't <b>muck around with</b> the words of the song-I think they're fine.<br>歌词别再改来改去了———我觉得不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>muck ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">加入；合伙(以完成工作)<br><span class="en">to join in with other people in order to complete a task</span></td><td class="c4">If we all <b>muck in</b>, we'll soon get the job finished.<br>如果我们大伙一块儿干，活儿很快就能做完。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>muck ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">分享；分摊<br><span class="en">to share food, accommodation, costs, etc. with other people</span></td><td class="c4">Money was short, but we all <b>mucked in</b> together.<br>钱不够用，但我们都同舟共济。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuck ˈout<br>ˌmuck sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">打扫畜栏；尤指马厩<br><span class="en">to clean the place where an animal lives, especially a horse</span></td><td class="c4">It's your turn to <b>muck out</b> today.<br>今天轮到你清扫马棚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>muddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>muddle aˈlong (also,muddle ˈon less frequent) <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">浑浑噩噩混日子；得过且过<br><span class="en">to continue living or doing sth with no clear purpose or plan</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>muddle along</b> from day to day.<br>我们一天天地混日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>muddle A ˈup with B <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…错认为；误当作<br><span class="en">to confuse one person or thing with another; to think that sb/sth is sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>muddled</b> up our passports and gave me back the wrong one.<br>他把我们的护照搞混了，把别人的发还给了我。<br>I keep <b>muddling</b> her up with her sister.<br>我老是把她当成她姐姐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>muddle sth ˈup (with sth) <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">随便弄乱；使混乱<br><span class="en">to carelessly put things in the wrong order; to mix things together in an untidy way</span></td><td class="c4">The money was <b>muddled up</b> with everything else in his pocket.<br>他衣兜里的钱和其他东西乱作一团。<br>The kids have <b>muddled up</b> all the photos.<br>孩子们把照片全都翻得乱七八糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>mug</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmug ˈup (on sth)<br>mug sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指考试前临时抓紧学习；临阵磨枪；临时抱佛脚<br><span class="en">to quickly learn sth, especially sth that you should already know, before an exam, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I'm going to <b>mug</b> up as much as I can about Delhi before 1 go there.<br>去德里前我要尽量多地了解那里的情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>muscle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuscle ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">锻炼肌肉；健身<br><span class="en">to develop your muscles so that you become stronger and fitter</span></td><td class="c4">Once you <b>muscle up</b>, youll find that your body burns more calories.<br>一旦开始锻炼肌肉，你将发现身体会消耗更多热量。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuscle ˈup<br>ˌmuscle sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使变得；更强壮；(使)变得更强大<br><span class="en">to become stronger, better or more powerful; to make sth stronger, better or more powerful</span></td><td class="c4">The unions need to <b>muscle up</b> if they want to become a force in this country again.<br>工会如果想再次成为这个国家的一股力量，就需要使自身不断壮大。<br>The is trying to <b>muscle up</b> its winter schedules.<br>英国广播公司正在强化冬季节目安排。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>muster</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌmuster sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">鼓起勇气；劲头；振作起来<br><span class="en">to find the courage, strength, etc. that you need in order to do sth difficult or unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">She could barely <b>muster up</b> the strength to get out of bed.<br>她几乎连起床的力气都没有了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈnag at sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…无休止地抱怨；不断指责；对…反复唠叨<br><span class="en">to keep complaining to sb about their behaviour; to keep asking sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">He keeps <b>nagging at</b> me to get more exercise.<br>他不断唠叨，叫我多锻炼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈnag at sb</b></td><td class="c3">不断烦扰；使一直困扰<br><span class="en">to worry or irritate sb continuously</span></td><td class="c4">The suspicion that she was lying continued to <b>nag at</b> me.<br>我怀疑她撒谎，这使我烦恼不已。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnail sb ˈdown (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">迫使明确说出想法；计划等<br><span class="en">to force sb to state exactly what they think, what they intend to do,etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He says he'll come, but I can't <b>nail him down</b> to a date.<br>他说要来，但我无法让他敲定日期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnail sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用钉子将…固定住；将…钉住<br><span class="en">to fasten sth down with nails</span></td><td class="c4">She got him to <b>nail the loose floorboard down</b>.<br>她让他把松动的木地板钉牢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnail sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">确切知道；准确理解<br><span class="en">to know or understand exactly what sth is</span></td><td class="c4">Something seems strange here, but I can't <b>nail it down</b>.<br>这里有点不对劲，可我搞不清究竟是什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnail sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">达成(协议)；作出(决定)<br><span class="en">to reach an agreement or a decision, usually after a lot of discussion</span></td><td class="c4">They managed to <b>nail down</b> an agreement with the management.<br>他们总算与资方达成了协议。四町。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnail sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用钉子将…固定到墙壁；柱子；上等<br><span class="en">to attach sth to a wall, a post, etc. with nails</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>nailed up</b> a notice saying: Keep out!<br>我钉了一块牌子，上面写着：禁止入内！2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>name</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈname sb/sth ˈafter sb/sth (AmE also ˈname sb/sth ˈfor sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以…命名；给…取名<br><span class="en">to give sb/sth the name of sb/sth else that you like or admire, for example a family member or a famous person or place</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>named her after</b> her grandmother.<br>我们给她取了她祖母的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nestle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnestle ˈup (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">温暖；舒适地紧贴着；偎依<br><span class="en">to make yourself warm and comfortable by moving close to sb</span></td><td class="c4">Jamie <b>nestled up</b> to his mother on the sofa.<br>杰米在沙发上偎依着母亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nibble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈnibble at sth</b></td><td class="c3">小口吃；一点点咬<br><span class="en">to eat sth by taking very</span></td><td class="c4">The <b>nibbled at</b> the peanuts.<br>老鼠一点一点地啃着花生。<br>Youve only <b>nibbled at</b> your lunch.<br>你午饭只吃了几小口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈnibble at sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…略感兴趣<br><span class="en">to show a slight interest in sth</span></td><td class="c4">Several companies have <b>nibbled at</b> our offer.<br>几家公司表示对我们的出价有点兴趣。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnibble aˈway at sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">慢慢消耗；蚕食<br><span class="en">to gradually reduce or use up the total amount of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Inflation began to <b>nibble away at</b> their savings.<br>通货膨胀让他们的存款开始缩水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnip sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">掐掉；夹断；剪去<br><span class="en">to remove a part of sth by squeezing it with your fingers, cutting it quickly with scissors, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>nipped off</b> the dead leaves.<br>她剪掉了枯叶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nod</b></td><td class="c2"><b>nod ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打盹；打瞌睡<br><span class="en">to fall asleep</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>nodded off</b> in front of the television.<br>她在电视机前睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nose</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnose sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以微小差距战胜；以微弱优势胜过；险胜<br><span class="en">to defeat sb by a small amount, for example in a race or an election</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>nosed out</b> of first place by her old rival.<br>她被老对手以微弱优势击败，丢掉了冠军。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnose sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打探到；探听到；查出<br><span class="en">to discover some information by searching for it</span></td><td class="c4">That man can <b>nose a news story out</b> anywhere.<br>那人到任何地方都能挖出新闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>notch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnotch sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">嬴取；获得(高分)<br><span class="en">to achieve a win or a high score</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>notched up</b> ten points in the first five minutes of the game.<br>在比赛开始的前五分钟里，他直取十分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnote sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">记下；记录<br><span class="en">to write sth down so that you will remember it</span></td><td class="c4">The class <b>noted down</b> every word she said.<br>全班学生把她说的每个字都记了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>number</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈnumber sb/sth among sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…算作；使属于；将…列入<br><span class="en">to include sb/sth in a particular group</span></td><td class="c4">He is <b>numbered among</b> the world's top experts.<br>他跻身世界顶尖高手之列。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>nuzzle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌnuzzle ˈup against/to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">用头；脸等紧贴；挨擦表示爱意；取暖等<br><span class="en">to press your head, face, etc. against sb/sth to show affection or keep warm, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>nuzzled up to</b> his mother with a happy sigh.<br>他依偎着妈妈，愜意地舒了口气。0o。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>object</b></td><td class="c2"><b>obˈject to sb doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">同意；不赞成；反对<br><span class="en">to say that you disagree with, disapprove of or oppose sth</span></td><td class="c4">Many local people <b>object</b> to the new airport.<br>当地很多居民反对建设新机场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>occur</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ocˈcur to sb</b></td><td class="c3">主意或想法突然出现在脑海；闪现在脑际<br><span class="en">if an idea or a thought occurs to you, it suddenly comes into your mind</span></td><td class="c4">A strange thought suddenly <b>occurred to</b> me.<br>当时我忽发奇想。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>offend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ofˈfend against sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">违反；有悖于(情理)<br><span class="en">to go against what people believe is morally right</span></td><td class="c4">The book <b>offends against</b> good taste.<br>这本书品位不高。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>offer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>offer sth ˈup (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">奉献；祭献(给上帝)<br><span class="en">to give sth to God</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>offered up</b> a prayer for her husband's safe return.<br>她祈求上帝保佑丈夫平安归来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>open</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen ˈinto/ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">门或房间直接通向；通往<br><span class="en">if a door or a room opens into/onto sth, it leads directly to it</span></td><td class="c4">The door <b>opened onto</b> a small yard.<br>门外是一个小院。<br>The kitchen <b>opens into</b> a large sitting room.<br>厨房对着大客厅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">门或房间与…相连；相通<br><span class="en">if a door or a room opens off sth, it connects directly with it</span></td><td class="c4">Several doors <b>opened off</b> the hall.<br>有几道门通往大厅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">变宽；变大；变得开阔<br><span class="en">(into/onto sth) to become wider or bigger; to become more open and not surrounded by anything</span></td><td class="c4">The valley <b>opened out</b> in front of us.<br>宽阔的山谷展现在我们面前。<br>The narrow lane <b>opened out</b> into a field.<br>狭窄的小路尽头是一大片田野。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">展开；打开；变得开阔；变得平坦<br><span class="en">to spread out; to become open and larger or flatter</span></td><td class="c4">The buds on the trees have all <b>opened out</b>.<br>树上的花蕾都。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">展开；摊开<br><span class="en">to spread sth out; to make sth open and flat</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>opened the map out</b>.<br>他铺开了地图。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">给…开刀(做手术)<br><span class="en">to cut sb open in order to do a medical operation</span></td><td class="c4">The whole region has been <b>opened up</b> for trade by the new rail link.<br>新铁路线把整个地区的贸易搞活了。<br>They <b>opened up</b> the sports hall to house the flood victims.<br>他们开放体育馆安置水灾灾民。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">开业；开张<br><span class="en">to start a new business</span></td><td class="c4">The company are <b>opening up</b> a new factory in Wales.<br>公司将在威尔士开新工厂。<br>United have <b>opened up</b> a three-point lead after five games.<br>五场比赛过后，联队以三分领先。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopen sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使张开；裂开；拓展<br><span class="en">to become wider; to make sth wider, especially sth that has been closed</span></td><td class="c4">Coughing might <b>open up</b> your wound.<br>咳嗽可能震裂你的伤口。<br>She wished the floor would <b>open up</b> and swallow her (= because she felt very embarrassed).<br>她窘得恨不得地上开个口子让她钻进去。<br>Cutting down the trees <b>opened up</b> the view from the house.<br>那些树砍掉后，房子的视野开阔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>open sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">打开；开启<br><span class="en">to make sth that is shut, locked, etc. open</span></td><td class="c4">Can you open up that box of books <b>for</b> me?<br>请帮我打开那箱书。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>opt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈopt for sth</b></td><td class="c3">选择；决定<br><span class="en">to choose sth; to make a decision about sth</span></td><td class="c4">More students are now <b>opting for</b> computer courses.<br>现在更多的学生选修计算机课程。<br>You can stay in the hotel or <b>opt for</b> one of the bungalows near the beach.<br>你可以住在旅馆，或在海滩附近选择一套平房。</td></tr>
