<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopt ˈin<br>ˌopt ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">决定加入；选择参加<br><span class="en">to choose to take part in sth</span></td><td class="c4">We offer a pension plan, and all staff have the chance to <b>opt in</b>.<br>我们提供养老金计划，所有职员均可参加。<br>The government decided to <b>opt into</b> the new European treaty.<br>政府决定加入新的欧洲条约。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌopt ˈout<br>ˌopt ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">决定退出；选择不参加<br><span class="en">to choose not to take part in sth</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>opt out</b> of the company's pension plan.<br>你可以选择不加入公司的养老金计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈopt-out n often</b></td><td class="c3">脱离<br><span class="en">(in Britain) the action of a school or a hospital that decides to manage its own money and is therefore no longer controlled by a local authority</span></td><td class="c4">Nurses and health workers voted against the <b>opt-out</b>.<br>护士和保健员投票反对脱离地方当局管理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>order</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌorder sb aˈround (BrE also,order sb aˈbout)</b></td><td class="c3">不断地命令；使唤<br><span class="en">to keep on telling sb to do things in an unpleasant way</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>ordering me around</b>!<br>别再对我呼来喝去了。<br>Even as a child, he <b>ordered</b> his friends <b>about</b>.<br>他从小就爱支使朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>order ˈout (for sth) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打电话让餐馆送外卖食物；电话叫(…)外卖</td><td class="c4">We could <b>order out</b> for a Chinese.<br>我们可以打电话要份外卖中餐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pace</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pace ˈout sth (also ˌpace ˈoff sth less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">以步丈量；步測<br><span class="en">to measure sth by taking regular steps across it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>paced out</b> the length of the room.<br>她步测出了房间的长度。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpack aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">能折叠；可收拢<br><span class="en">if sth packs away, it can be folded up small when you are no longer using it</span></td><td class="c4">The jacket <b>packs away</b> neatly into its own pocket.<br>这件夹克衫可以巧妙地折进衣服口袋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">用后收拾好；把…装进盒子；柜子等里<br><span class="en">to put sth into a box, cupboard, etc. when you are no longer using it</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>packed away</b> the picnic things and put them in the car.<br>我们把野餐用品收拾好放到车里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">猛吃；胃口大<br><span class="en">to eat a lot of sth</span></td><td class="c4">She can certainly <b>pack it away</b>!<br>她可真能吃。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">演出；戏剧；等吸引(大批观众)<br><span class="en">to attract large numbers of people to a show, a play, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The film is still <b>packing in</b> the crowds.<br>这部电影依然吸引着大批观众。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sb/sth ˈin<br>.pack sb/sth ˈin/into sth</b></td><td class="c3">把要做的；要见的人等挤在(有限的时间)里<br><span class="en">to do a lot of things, see a lot of people, etc. in a limited period of time</span></td><td class="c4">She managed to <b>pack</b> a lot of sightseeing <b>into</b> three days.<br>她设法用三天时间游览了许多地方。<br>We <b>packed in</b> a lot yesterday afternoon.<br>我们昨天下午做了很多事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sb/sth ˈin<br>.pack sb/sth ˈin/into sth</b></td><td class="c3">把大量的；人或物挤在(有限的空间)里<br><span class="en">to put a lot of things or people into a limited space</span></td><td class="c4">Somehow we managed to <b>pack everyone in</b>.<br>我们总算让每个人都挤了进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">停止；放弃(尤指工作)<br><span class="en">to give sth up, especially a job</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>packed in</b> her job as a teacher.<br>她辞去了教师工作。<br>Smoking's bad for you. You ought to <b>pack it in</b>.<br>吸烟有害健康。你应该戒掉。<br>I was depressed I felt like <b>packing it all in</b>.<br>我心灰意冷，想彻底放弃。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">人挤进…里；使爆满<br><span class="en">if people pack into a place, they go there in large numbers and fill it completely</span></td><td class="c4">All six of us <b>packed into</b> the tiny car.<br>我们六个都挤进了小车。<br>More than 70 000 people <b>packed into</b> Trafalgar Square on New Year's Eve.<br>除夕有7万多人涌入特拉法尔加广场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sb ˈoff (to .. ) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…打发走；把…赶走(到某处)<br><span class="en">to send sb away, especially because you do not want YOu</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>packed off</b> to boarding school at the age of eight.<br>她八岁就被送进了寄宿学校。<br>He <b>packed the children off</b> to bed.<br>他打发孩子们去睡觉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">表演；演员等吸引大批观众；使满座<br><span class="en">if a show, a performer, etc. packs out a place, large numbers of people go to see it/them</span></td><td class="c4">The band <b>packs out</b> venues all over the country.<br>这支乐队在全国各地的演出都是观众爆满。<br>The movie has been <b>packing out</b> cinemas for weeks.<br>这部电影使影院连续几周爆满。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>packed ˈout adi <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">爆满的；挤得水泄不通的</td><td class="c4">The town is <b>packed</b> <b>out</b> with tourists in the summer.<br>夏天城里游人如织。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pack ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">机器；发动机等失灵；出故障<br><span class="en">if a machine, an engine, etc. packs up, it stops working</span></td><td class="c4">All our things were <b>packed up</b>, waiting to be moved.<br>我们所有东西都打包好了等着运走。<br>You'd feel better if you <b>packed up</b> smoking.<br>把烟戒了，你就会感觉好些的。<br>When did you <b>pack up</b> your job at the shop?<br>你什么时候辞去了店里的工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>package</b></td><td class="c2"><b>package sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">将…包裹好<br><span class="en">to wrap sth and make it into a package so that you can send it somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>packaged up</b> his books and mailed them to him.<br>她把他的书包好，邮寄给了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pad</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pad sth ˈout (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">给(衣服)加(软填料)<br><span class="en">to put soft material into a piece of clothing in order to change its shape</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>padded the costume out</b> with foam.<br>她给戏服填衬了泡沫材料。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pad sth ˈout (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用废话拉长书；文章；讲话；充篇幅<br><span class="en">to make sth, such as a book, an article, a speech, etc., longer by adding unnecessary material</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>padded out</b> the article with lots of quotations.<br>我在文章中塞进了大量引语。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>page</b></td><td class="c2"><b>page ˈdown/ˈup (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">计算机文档；网页等向前；向后翻页<br><span class="en">to move forward/backwards in a computer document, web page, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>page up or down</b> using the scroll bar at the side of the screen.<br>用屏幕旁边的滚动条可以上下翻页。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpage ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">浏览；翻阅<br><span class="en">to turn the pages of a book, a magazine, etc. and look at them without reading them in detail</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>paged through</b> the report looking for her name.<br>她翻看报告，查找自己的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>paint</b></td><td class="c2"><b>paint ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">用油漆；徐料等覆盖；遮盖<br><span class="en">to cover sth with a layer of paint</span></td><td class="c4">Well have to <b>paint over</b> the dirty marks on the wall.<br>我们得刷层油漆把墻上的污斑涂抹掉。<br>The name had been <b>painted over</b>.<br>名字用颜料涂掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>paint sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">刷油漆；颜料等粉刷；装饰<br><span class="en">to paint sth, decorating it in a bright, attractive way</span></td><td class="c4">Their house had been <b>painted up</b> in amazing colours.<br>他们的房子粉刷得五颜六色。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pair</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pair ˈoff<br>pair sb ˈoff (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">使结对；配对；成为；恋人<br><span class="en">to form a pair or pairs, especially in order to have a romantic relationship; to bring two people together in this way</span></td><td class="c4">By the end of the course, everyone had <b>paired off</b>.<br>课程结束时大家都成双结对了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpair ˈup<br>.pair sb ˈup (with sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">工作；比赛等中组对；配对；使配对<br><span class="en">to form a pair or pairs (with sb/sth) in order to work, play a game, etc. together; to bring two people together for this purpose</span></td><td class="c4">The job is a Lot easier if you <b>pair up</b> with someone else.<br>你如果找个人搭档，这活儿就轻松多了。<br>Writers have been <b>paired up</b> with artists to write articles on paintings.<br>作家和艺术家联手作画赋文。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pal ˈup (with sb) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人结成朋友<br><span class="en">to become friends with sb</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>palled up</b> at college.<br>他们是在大学结为好友的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>palm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>palm sb ˈoff (with sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向某人；骗售(无价值或不需要的东西)<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to accept sth that has little value or is not what they really want</span></td><td class="c4">Make sure he doesn't <b>palm you off</b> with faulty goods.<br>当心别让他以次充好把劣质产品卖给你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>palm sth ˈoff as sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指售出把…充作…；以次充好；以假乱真<br><span class="en">to persuade sb that sth is better than it really is, or is sth different, especially in order to sell it</span></td><td class="c4">She was trying to <b>palm copies off as</b> original paintings.<br>她企图以复制品假冒原画出售。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>palm sb/sth ˈoff on/onto sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把自己不；想要的人或物推诿给；塞给<br><span class="en">to get rid of sb/sth that you do not want by persuading sb else to accept them/it</span></td><td class="c4">He tried to <b>palm his uncle off on</b> me for the whole afternoon.<br>他花了整整一下午时间想把他叔叔硬推给我。<br>I think she <b>palmed off the stolen necklace on</b> some unsuspecting old lady.<br>我想她把偷来的项链脱手给了一位毫无戒心的老太太。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pander</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpander to sb/sth <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">逢迎；投…所好<br><span class="en">to try to sb by doing or providing what they want although you know it is probably wrong to do so</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>panders to</b> her every whim.<br>他对她百依百顺。<br>His movies never <b>pandered to</b> public taste.<br>他的电影从不迎合公众的口味。<br>I don't think children should be <b>pandered to</b>.<br>我觉得不应该迁就孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>panic</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpanic sb into sth<br>ˈpanic sb into doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">使因恐慌而仓皇行事<br><span class="en">to make sb do sth too quickly because they are afraid</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let them <b>panic you into</b> a decision.<br>别被他们吓得匆忙作决定。<br>She refused to be <b>panicked into</b> making rash promises.<br>她不肯因为害怕而草率承诺。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>paper</b></td><td class="c2"><b>paper ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">用纸；裱糊住；用厚纸遮盖<br><span class="en">to cover sth such as a wall with thick paper in order to hide sth</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>papered over</b> the stains on the wall.<br>我们把墙上的污斑用纸糊上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>paper ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">慌忙掩盖；权且掩饰问题；分岐等<br><span class="en">to hide sth such as a problem, a disagreement, etc., especially quickly or not very well</span></td><td class="c4">The divisions in the party had been <b>papered over</b> during the election campaign.<br>竞选期间，该党的内部分歧被暂时掩盖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>parcel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>parcel sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">分批出售；分期转让<br><span class="en">to sell or transfer a set of things that are part of a larger set</span></td><td class="c4">Theyll <b>parcel off</b> some of the stores to the other companies.<br>他们将把部分店铺分批出售给其他公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌparcel sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把…分成(若干份)；划分<br><span class="en">to divide sth into parts</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>parcelled out</b> the land into small plots.<br>他们把地分成了若干小块。<br>The work was <b>parcelled out</b> among the staff.<br>工作分派给了各职员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>parcel sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">包裹好；打包<br><span class="en">to wrap sth and make it into a parcel</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>parcelled up</b> the books ready to send.<br>她把书包起来准备寄走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pare</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pare sth aˈway/ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">削皮；去皮<br><span class="en">to remove the thin outer layer from sth in thin strips</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pare off</b> the rind from the orange using a sharp knife.<br>用快刀子削去橙子皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>parlay</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌparlay sth ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">利用金钱；技术等优势获得；使(优势)增值为<br><span class="en">to use an advantage that you have, such as money or a skill, in order to get sth or make it worth more</span></td><td class="c4">He parlayed his relationship with his boss <b>into</b> an important job.<br>他利用和老板的关系得到了一份重要工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>part</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpart with sth</b></td><td class="c3">割舍；放弃<br><span class="en">to give sth away that you would prefer to keep</span></td><td class="c4">He hates <b>parting with</b> (= spending) his money.<br>他不舍得花钱。o8n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pass</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pass beˈtween sb</b></td><td class="c3">两人之间互传神色；言语<br><span class="en">if sth such as a look, a word, etc. passes between two people, they look quickly at each other, speak to each other, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">A look of understanding <b>passed between</b> Ann and Carla.<br>安和卡拉心照不宜地交换了一下眼神。<br>I never knew what <b>passed between</b> them (= what they said to each other) on that day.<br>我根本不知道那天他们之间说了些什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass ˈby</b></td><td class="c3">时间过去；逝去<br><span class="en">if time passes by, it goes past</span></td><td class="c4">The weeks <b>passed by</b> and she didn't call.<br>几个星期过去了，她没有打电话过来。<br>The boat <b>passed close by</b> the island.<br>那艘小船紧挨着岛驶过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sb/sth ˈby</b></td><td class="c3">对…没有影响<br><span class="en">to happen without affecting sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She feels that life is <b>passing her by</b> (= that she is not enjoying the opportunities and pleasures of life).<br>她觉得人生的机遇乐趣都与她无缘。<br>The whole business <b>passed him by</b> (= he was hardly aware that it was happening).<br>他对发生的事全然不知。<br>Some of the furniture has been <b>passed</b> down through the family.<br>有些家具是一代代传下来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpass for/as sb</b></td><td class="c3">因相似被当作；被认为是某人或某类<br><span class="en">to be so much like another person, or another type of person, that people could easily think you were that person or type</span></td><td class="c4">He speaks French well enough to <b>pass for</b> a Frenchman.<br>他法语说得好，很容易被当成法国人。<br>They could <b>pass as</b> twins.<br>他俩长得像双胞胎。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpass into sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">成为…一部分；融入；纳入<br><span class="en">to become a part of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Many foreign words have <b>passed into</b> English.<br>许多外来词已被英语吸收了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">事件；以特定方式发生；结束；进行；完成</td><td class="c4">The election has <b>passed off</b> without incident.<br>选举顺利结束了。<br>The celebrations <b>passed off</b> peacefully.<br>庆祝活动平静地结束了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">疼痛；药效等逐渐消失；消退<br><span class="en">if pain, the effects of a drug, etc. pass off, they gradually disappear</span></td><td class="c4">The symptoms should <b>pass off</b> within 24 hours.<br>症状应该在24小时内消失。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">对困难；尴尬的话语或状况淡化处理；从容应对<br><span class="en">to act as if a difficult or awk. ward remark or situation is less important than you really think it is</span></td><td class="c4">He had really upset her, but she smiled and tried to <b>pass it off</b>.<br>他着实让她难过，但她笑了笑，尽量不去理会。<br>He managed to <b>pass the question off</b> lightly.<br>他把那个问题轻轻带过，就算应付过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sth ˈon (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把(成本)转嫁给(顾客)<br><span class="en">if a company, a shop/store, etc. passes on higher or lower costs to its customers, it makes them pay more or less for sth</span></td><td class="c4">The supermarket did not <b>pass on</b> its profit to customers by cutting prices.<br>超市没有削减价格向顾客让利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">分发；分配<br><span class="en">to give something to each person in a group</span></td><td class="c4">The teacher asked me to <b>pass the books out</b>.<br>老师让我把书发给大家。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpass ˈover sb (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">升职等时忽视<br><span class="en">to not consider for a better job, especially when they deserve it or think they deserve it</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>passed over</b> for promotion again.<br>晋升又没有考虑我。<br>He was <b>passed over</b> in favour of a younger man.<br>他未获擢升，一个比他年轻的人却受提拔了。<br>Often used in the <b>passive</b>.<br>常用于被动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpass ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…上方经过<br><span class="en">to move over the top of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The eye of the storm was <b>passing over</b> us.<br>那时暴风中心正从我们上方通过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpass ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">忽略过去；对…不予考虑<br><span class="en">to ignore or avoid sth</span></td><td class="c4">They chose to <b>pass over</b> her rude remarks.<br>他们决定不理会她的出言不逊。<br>For years this painting was <b>passed over</b> by experts.<br>这幅画多年被专家冷落在一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sb/sth ˈover (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">将…交给(某人)；让(某人)照看；由(某人)掌管<br><span class="en">to give sth to sb, especially when they ask for it or you do not want it any more; to give sb, or the responsibility for sb, to sb else</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor <b>passed the baby over</b> to the nurse.<br>医生把婴儿交给护士照料。<br>Control of the budgets has been <b>passed over</b> to individual schools.<br>预算管理权已交给了各学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>pass ˈthrough<br>pass ˈthrough sth togo or travel through</b></td><td class="c3">经过；路过</td><td class="c4">We're not staying here, we're just <b>passing through</b>.<br>我们只是路经此地，不会久留的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pass sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">放过；不要机会；提议等<br><span class="en">to decide not to take advantage of an opportunity, an offer, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Imagine <b>passing up</b> an offer like that!<br>真想不到居然放弃人家提供的大好机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>patch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>patch sb/sth ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">暂时接通；连通(电话或电子设备)<br><span class="en">to connect telephone or electronic equipment temporarily</span></td><td class="c4">The radio was <b>patched through</b> to army headquarters.<br>无线电接通了陆军总部。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>patch sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">匆匆拼凑；草草拼合<br><span class="en">to arrange sth quickly, especially by putting several different parts together, without taking any care over it</span></td><td class="c4">An interim government was quickly <b>patched together</b>.<br>临时政府仓促组建起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>patch sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">匆忙处；暂时包扎<br><span class="en">to give quick or temporary medical treatment to sb who is injured</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>patched him up</b> and sent him back onto the field (= for example in a game of football).<br>他们给他处理了一下伤口，就让他回到了赛场。<br>The doctor did his best to <b>patch up</b> their wounds.<br>医生尽最大努力很快给他们包扎了伤口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>patch sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指快速或暂时修理；修补<br><span class="en">to repair sth, quickly or temporarily</span></td><td class="c4">The car was <b>patched up</b> and resold.<br>汽车草草修理了一下又卖掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>patch sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">平息(争论)；消除(分歧)；重归于好<br><span class="en">to end an argument or disagreement with sb and be friends again</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>patched up</b> their differences.<br>他们消除了分歧。<br>Can't you two try to <b>patch things up</b>?<br>你们俩就不能尝试和好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pawn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pawn sth ˈoff as sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…充作…；假冒；以次充好<br><span class="en">to pretend that sth is better,more valuable, etc. than it really is</span></td><td class="c4">There is so much misinformation <b>pawned off as</b> fact these days.<br>如今很多虚假信息被当成事实。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pay</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pay sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">付…作为首期款；先支付<br><span class="en">to give an amount of money as the first payment for sth</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>pay</b> $200 <b>down</b> and the rest in 12 monthly instalments.<br>你可以付200元的首期，其余的分期12个月支付。<br>You need to <b>pay</b> Paul for all that work he did for you.<br>保罗给你干了那么多活儿，你得付他工钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pay sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">为做错的事；说错的话或相信；的事吃苦头(或受惩罚)<br><span class="en">to suffer or be punished ' for sth wrong that you have done or said, or for sth you believe</span></td><td class="c4">Someone's to <b>pay</b> for this!<br>一定得有人为这事付出代价。<br>They are <b>paying</b> dearly for their mistake.<br>他们正因其自身失误大吃苦头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pay ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">冒险的事成功；奏效；达到目的<br><span class="en">if sth that involves risk pays off, it is successful and brings the results that you want</span></td><td class="c4">All the training youve been doing seems to have <b>paid off</b> handsomely (= has had very good results).<br>你接受的那些训练似乎大有成效。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpay-off n <span class="tag">(informal a)</span></b></td><td class="c3">封口费；行賄钱<br><span class="en">payment you make to sb to persuade them not to do sth or not to tell sb about sth illegal or dishonest you have done</span></td><td class="c4">Police have been accused of receiving <b>pay-offs</b> from local gangs.<br>警方被控接受当地黑帮的贿赂。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pay sth/sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">付清…的款项；清偿…的；欠款<br><span class="en">to finish paying money that you owe for sth</span></td><td class="c4">I used the money to <b>pay off</b> my overdraft.<br>我把钱用来偿还透支款了。?。<br>The government <b>pays</b> out millions of pounds in benefits.<br>政府支出数百万英镑救济金。01。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpayout n</b></td><td class="c3">支付的巨款<br><span class="en">a large amount of money that is given to sb</span></td><td class="c4">People injured in the crash won record <b>payouts</b> from the rail company.<br>撞车事故中的受伤人员获得了铁路公司数额空前的赔款。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pay sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">从手中放出(绳索等)<br><span class="en">to pass a rope, etc. through your hands</span></td><td class="c4">He started <b>paying out</b> the rope.<br>他开始放出绳子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>peck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpeck at sth</b></td><td class="c3">因不饿；而一点一点地吃；小口啃<br><span class="en">to eat only very small amounts of sth, because you are not hungry •</span></td><td class="c4">He was so nervous he only <b>pecked at</b> his lunch.<br>他紧张得午饭只吃了几口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>peel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>peel aˈway/ˈback (from sth), .pee! aˈway/ˈback (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">剥落；除掉(外层)<br><span class="en">to come off the surface of sth; to remove a thin layer from the surface of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The wallpaper had started to <b>peel</b> <b>away</b>.<br>墙纸开始脱落。<br>The paint was <b>peeling</b> <b>away</b> from the wood.<br>木头上的油漆一片一片地剥落下来。<br>She <b>peeled</b> <b>back</b> the blankets and jumped into bed.<br>她掀开毯子跳到了床上。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>peel ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">剥落；脱落<br><span class="en">to come away from the surface of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The wallpaper was <b>Peeling off</b>.<br>墙纸正在脱落。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>peel sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">脱去(尤指紧身衣服)<br><span class="en">to remove some or all of your (rare) clothing, especially sth that fits tightly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>peeled off</b> his wet clothes.<br>他脱掉了湿衣服。<br>She <b>peeled all the wallpaper off</b> the bathroom ceiling.<br>她把浴室天花板的墻纸全撕掉了。四D。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpeel ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开着车；骑着摩托等快速离开；呼啸而去<br><span class="en">to leave quickly and in a noisy way, especially in a car, on a motorcycle, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>peeled out</b> of the driveway and sped down the street.<br>她驱车快速驶离车道开上大街。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>peer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpeer at sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指看不清时贴近看；仔细看；盯着看<br><span class="en">to look closely or carefully at sth, especially when you cannot see it clearly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>peered closely at</b> the dusty old letters.<br>她贴近细瞧那些布满灰尘的旧信件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>peg</b></td><td class="c2"><b>peg aˈway (at sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">坚持不懈地工作；孜孜不倦地努力<br><span class="en">to continue to work hard at or try to achieve sth difficult</span></td><td class="c4">He keeps <b>pegging away</b> at his novel.<br>他笔耕不辍，创作小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>peg sb/sth ˈback (sport)</b></td><td class="c3">止住；拖住(领先者)；拉低(分差)<br><span class="en">to stop sb/sth from winning or from increasing the amount by which they are ahead</span></td><td class="c4">Italy were winning 2-0, but were <b>pegged back</b> to a draw by Spain's late goal.<br>意大利队以 2:0领先，但西班牙队后来的进球把比分追平。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pelt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpelt down <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大雨；下暴雨<br><span class="en">to rain very heavily</span></td><td class="c4">It's <b>pelting down</b> (with rain) outside.<br>外面大雨如注。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pen sb/sth ˈin<br>.pen sb/sth ˈin sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…关起来(或圈起来)<br><span class="en">to shut sb/sth in a small space with walls or fences, etc. all around</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>penned the sheep in</b> the yard.<br>我们把绵羊关在院子里。<br>The troublemakers were <b>penned in</b> by the police.<br>那些闹事者被警方关押了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pension</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pension sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">尤指给老人或；病人发退休金准子…退休；强迫…退休<br><span class="en">to allow or force sb to retire, especially because they are old or ill/ sick, and pay them a pension</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>pensioned off</b> at the age of 56.<br>她56 岁时获准退休。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pep sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">增加…的趣味；使兴致勃勃；使活跃；激励<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth more interesting; to make sb feel more lively or full of energy</span></td><td class="c4">The company needs to <b>pep up</b> its image.<br>这家公司需要改善形象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pepper</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpepper sb/sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">以子弹等；小发射物连续击打(或射击)<br><span class="en">to hit sb/sth with lots of small things such as bullets</span></td><td class="c4">They said they were <b>peppered with</b> shotgun pellets as they walked in the forest.<br>他们说在森林中行走时被猎枪发射的弹丸击中。°。<br>Her hair is <b>peppered with</b> grey.<br>她满头花白。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>perk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌperk ˈup<br>.perk sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使增值；(使)增加<br><span class="en">to improve or increase in value, to make sth increase in value, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The weather seems to be <b>perking up</b>.<br>天气似乎要好起来了。<br>The recent demand for houses has <b>perked up</b> the prices.<br>最近对住房的需求抬高了房价。<br>House prices are expected to <b>perk up</b>.<br>房价预计会上涨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>perk sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使更有趣；使更；诱人<br><span class="en">to make sth more interesting or more attractive</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Perk up</b> a dark kitchen with a coat of paint.<br>把昏暗的厨房油漆一下，让它变亮堂。<br>A vegetable stew can be <b>perked up</b> with a dash of chilli sauce.<br>给炖菜加点辣椒酱能使味道更佳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>permit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>perˈmit of sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使有可能；允许…发生<br><span class="en">to make sth possible; to allow sth to happen</span></td><td class="c4">The situation does not <b>permit of</b> any delay.<br>形势刻不容缓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pertain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>perˈtain to sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…相关；关于<br><span class="en">to be connected with a particular subject, person, event or situation</span></td><td class="c4">The committee was reviewing all the laws <b>pertaining to</b> adoption.<br>委员会在重新审议有关收养的所有法律。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>peter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpeter ˈout (into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐减少；逐渐；减弱；渐趋消失<br><span class="en">to decrease or fade gradually before coming to an end</span></td><td class="c4">The road <b>petered out</b> into a dirt track.<br>大道逐渐变窄，成了一条泥土小径。<br>By midday their enthusiasm had <b>petered out</b>.<br>他们的热情到中午就烟消云散了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>phase</b></td><td class="c2"><b>phase sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">逐步减少；分阶段；削减<br><span class="en">to reduce sth gradually in stages over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">We are <b>phasing down</b> production of less profitable items.<br>我们正分阶段减少利润较低的产品产量。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>phase sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">逐步引入；分阶段采用<br><span class="en">to introduce sth gradually or in stages</span></td><td class="c4">The government will <b>phase in</b> the new tax.<br>政府将逐步推出新税种。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>phase sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">逐步废除；分阶段废除<br><span class="en">to stop using sth gradually or in stages</span></td><td class="c4">They agreed to <b>phase out</b> chemical weapons.<br>他们同意逐步停止使用化学武器。<br>The old system is being <b>phased out</b>.<br>旧体制正在一步步地废除。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>phone</b></td><td class="c2"><b>phone ˈback<br>phone sb ˈback <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给某人再打电话；(给某人)回电话<br><span class="en">to telephone sb again or to telephone sb who telephoned you earlier</span></td><td class="c4">I left a message but they never <b>phoned back</b>.<br>我留言了，可他们从没回过电话。<br>Tom called while you were out. He asked if you could <b>phone him back</b>.<br>你外出时汤姆来电话了。他请你给他回个电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>phone ˈin <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给电视(或电台)节目打电话；打观众(或听众)热线电话<br><span class="en">to phone a television or radio programme</span></td><td class="c4">Hundreds of listeners <b>phoned in</b> to complain.<br>有几百名听众打来热线电话表示不满。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌphone sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">往工作单位；打电话(汇报信息)<br><span class="en">to make a telephone call to the place where you work in order to give sb some information</span></td><td class="c4">Our reporter <b>phoned the story in</b> this afternoon.<br>我们的记者今天下午来电话报道了这一新闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌphone sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在电影表演；体育比赛等中不卖力；走过场；敷衍<br><span class="en">to do sth such as play a role in a film/movie, play in a sports competition, etc. without making much effort</span></td><td class="c4">Cruise is just <b>phoning it in in</b> this new release.<br>在新发行的这部影片中，克鲁斯演技平平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>phone sth ˈthrough <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打电话详细告知<br><span class="en">to phone sb with details of or information about sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Phone your order through</b> to the store.<br>给商店打电话告知订单详情。<br><b>Phone</b> Mike up and ask him if he wants to come.<br>给迈克打个电话，问他想不想来。<br>I <b>phoned</b> up the bank this morning.<br>我今天上午给银行打了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">因不饿；而小口吃；少量地吃<br><span class="en">to shoot a person, an nick at sth to eat very small amounts of pid off by per food because you are not hungry</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>picked</b> at her food for a while, then left the table.<br>她吃了几小口就离开了餐桌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpick sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">瞄准射击(一群中的一个目标)<br><span class="en">to shoot a person, an animal, a bird, an aircraft, etc. especially one of a group, after aiming carefully</span></td><td class="c4">One of our men was <b>picked off</b> by a sniper.<br>狙击手射中了我们的一个人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sth ˈoff<br>ˌpick sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">用指甲；或工具除去；剪除<br><span class="en">to remove sth from sth with your nails or a tool</span></td><td class="c4">The manager was accused of <b>picking</b> on a member of the department.<br>有人指责经理百般刁难部门中的一名职员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sth ˈoff<br>ˌpick sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">指定某人做(尤指苦差)<br><span class="en">to choose sb for a task, especially an unpleasant one</span></td><td class="c4">The teacher always <b>picked</b> on Tom to answer the difficult questions.<br>老师总是点汤姆回答难题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>pick sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">看出；认出；分辨出<br><span class="en">to manage to see sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">We could just pick out a car <b>in</b> the distance.<br>我们只能隐隐约约看见远处有一辆车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">经仔细研究发现；认识<br><span class="en">to discover or recognize sth after careful study</span></td><td class="c4">It was duffcult to <b>pick out</b> the important points from the mass of facts.<br>从一大堆资料中很难理出要点。<br>They were asked to <b>pick out</b> exactly what made his style so distinctive.<br>他们被要求悉心领会是什么成就了他与众不同的风格。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不看乐谱慢慢弹奏出(曲调)<br><span class="en">if you pick out a tune on a musical instrument, you play it slowly, note by note, without using written music</span></td><td class="c4">Buddie was <b>picking out</b> a sumple tune on his guitar.<br>巴迪在吉他上缓缓弹着一首简单的曲子。8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ally be .picked ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用对比色醒日；地画(或写)<br><span class="en">to paint, draw or write sth in such a way that it is very easy to see, especially by using a colour that is dif. ferent from the background</span></td><td class="c4">The details of the flowers were picked <b>out</b> in blue and gold.<br>花的纹理用蓝色和金黄色勾画得很鲜艳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpick ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">改善；好转<br><span class="en">to become better; to improve</span></td><td class="c4">The market always <b>picks up</b> in the spring.<br>市场总是在春季开始向好。<br>The game started very slowly but <b>picked up</b> in the second half.<br>比赛开始时节奏缓慢，但在下半场有了起色。<br>We're waiting until the weather <b>picks up</b> a bit.<br>我们等天气有所好转再说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpick ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">风变大；增强<br><span class="en">if the wind picks up, it starts to blow more strongly</span></td><td class="c4">The wind seems to be <b>picking up</b>.<br>风似乎越刮越大。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpick ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">重新开始；继续<br><span class="en">to start again; to continue</span></td><td class="c4">The new sertes <b>picks up</b> where the old one left off.<br>新的系列接续上一系列。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpickup n</b></td><td class="c3">改进；改善；好转</td><td class="c4">There are no signs of a <b>pickup</b> in consumer spending.<br>没有迹象显示消费者支出会增长。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick ˈup<br>.pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">接听(电话)<br><span class="en">to answer the telephone</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pick up</b> if you're there, Tom!<br>汤姆，你在的话就接电话。<br>At last someone <b>picked up</b> the phone.<br>最后终于有人接了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick ˈup<br>.pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">逮捕；拘押(以审问)<br><span class="en">to arrest sb; to take sb somewhere in order to question them</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>picked up</b> by the police as she was leaving her hotel.<br>她正要离开旅馆时被警察逮住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick ˈup<br>.pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">为发生性关系而搭讪；勾搭(陌生人)<br><span class="en">to start talking to sb you do not know, because you want to have a sexual relationship with them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>picked her up</b> at a club.<br>他是在俱乐部勾搭上她的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick ˈup<br>.pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使振作；提神<br><span class="en">if sth picks you up, it makes you feel better</span></td><td class="c4">A cup of tea will soon <b>pick you up</b>.<br>喝杯茶你就会有精神的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpick-me-up n <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">提神之物；振奋精神的事物</td><td class="c4">The country air was the perfect <b>pick-me-up</b>.<br>乡下的空气让人神清气爽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpickup n</b></td><td class="c3">搭车；搭载<br><span class="en">an occasion when sb gets in a car, on a bus, etc. to be taken to another place</span></td><td class="c4">The coach driver made several <b>Pickups</b> before heading for the airport.<br>长途汽车司机停了几次车搭载乘客，然后开往机场。0a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpickup n</b></td><td class="c3">为发生性关系与陌生人的搭讪；偶然结识的性伙伴<br><span class="en">a situation in which sb is trying to start a sexual relationship with a person they do not know; the person they are trying to start a sexual relationship with</span></td><td class="c4">Nothing ever came of his <b>pickups</b>.<br>他的搭讪从来都没成功。0a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>pick sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">拿起；提起；举起；抱起<br><span class="en">to take hold of and lift sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">I always <b>pick the baby up</b> when she cries.<br>孩子一哭我就把她抱起来。<br>I <b>picked up</b> your bag by mistake.<br>我错拿了你的包。<br><b>Pick your coat up</b> off the floor!<br>把你的外套从地板上捡起来。<br>He <b>picked up</b> a hitchhiker.<br>他带上了一个搭便车的人。<br>I went to <b>pick her up</b> from the airport.<br>我开车去机场接她了。<br>We can <b>pick up</b> the tickets an hour before the show starts.<br>我们可以在开演前一小时取票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">轻松学会语言；技能等；轻易得到(信息)<br><span class="en">to learn a language, a skill, etc., or to get information, without making an effort</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>picks up</b> languages really easily.<br>她学习语言确实很轻松。<br>I showed her the software ana she <b>picked it up</b> quickly.<br>我向她演示了这个软。<br>I <b>picked up</b> lots of tips on home entertainment from the magazine.<br>我从杂志上找到冢庭娱乐的很多小窍门。<br>The children have <b>picked up</b> the local accent.<br>孩子们学会了当地口音。<br>Signals from the satellite are <b>picked up</b> at ground stations.<br>地面站接收卫星发回的信号。<br>We were able to <b>Pick up</b> the World Service.<br>我们能收到英国厂播公司国际广播节目。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>pick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指以低价或幸运地买到<br><span class="en">to buy sth, especially cheaply or by good luck</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>picked up</b> some bargains in the sales.<br>他在打折期间买了些便宜货。<br>You can <b>pick up</b> a second-hand bike for about £60.<br>你花 60 英镑左石就能头到一辆二手摩托车。<br>The French police <b>picked up</b> the trail and traced her to Lille.<br>法国警方发现了她的踪迹，并跟踪到了里尔。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpick yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指跌倒后站起；爬起<br><span class="en">to get to your feet, especially after a fall</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>picked herself up</b> and stumbled on.<br>她爬起来，踉跟跄跄地继续走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick ˈup on sth</b></td><td class="c3">发现；注意到<br><span class="en">to notice sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>picked up on</b> her feelings of unease.<br>他觉察到了她的不安情绪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pick sb ˈup on sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">纠正(某人)在…方面的错误<br><span class="en">to correct sth that sb has said or done</span></td><td class="c4">If you make a mistake, he always <b>picks you up on</b> it.<br>他总爱挑别人的毛病。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>piece</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpiece sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">拼合；整合(各种证据以便了解事实)；理清(头绪)<br><span class="en">to discover a story, etc. by putting together separate pieces of evidence</span></td><td class="c4">Detectives are <b>piecing together</b> the events of the last hours of his life.<br>侦探正在拼接连缀他死亡之前数小时发生的事。<br>Investigators are still trying to <b>piece together</b> the evidence to find out what caused the crash.<br>调查人员仍然在努力厘清证据，以找出撞车原因。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pig</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpig ˈout (on sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大吃；猛吃<br><span class="en">to eat too much or a lot of food</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>pigged out</b> at lunch for four bucks each.<br>午餐时我们每人出四块钱大吃一顿。<br>It isn't a good idea to <b>Pig out</b> on sugar.<br>吃糖太多不好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpig-out n</b></td><td class="c3">大吃；猛吃<br><span class="en">an occasion on which you eat too much or a lot of food</span></td><td class="c4">We had a real <b>pig-out last night</b>.<br>我们昨晚吃得真够多的。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pile</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpile ˈin/out<br>ˌpile ˈinto/out of sth</b></td><td class="c3">蜂拥而入；而出；涌入；涌出<br><span class="en">to go in or out of somewhere without order or control</span></td><td class="c4">The taxi arrived and we all <b>piled in</b>.<br>出租车一到，我们一拥而上。<br>Crowds of children <b>piled out</b> of the building.<br>一群群孩子闹哄哄地从楼里跑出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pile ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">和…碰撞；撞上<br><span class="en">to crash into sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She stopped dead in the middle of the pavement and we all <b>piled into</b> her.<br>她在人行道中间突然停住了，我们全撞到她身上。<br>As many as 30 cars and trucks <b>piled into</b> each other in the fog this morning.<br>今天上午在大雾中多达30辆汽车和货车连环相撞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpile ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">体重剧增；猛增<br><span class="en">if sb's weight piles on, it increases rapidly</span></td><td class="c4">The pounds have just <b>piled on</b> since I got married!<br>结婚以来我的体重一个劲儿地增加。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pile sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">大量给子；过度施加<br><span class="en">to give sb a lot or too much of sth</span></td><td class="c4">United <b>piled on</b> the pressure in the second half (= of the football game).<br>联队在下半场给对手施加了很大压力。<br>The team were <b>piling on</b> the points.<br>该队连连得分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpile-up n</b></td><td class="c3">数车相撞；连环撞车事故</td><td class="c4">Eleven cars were involved in a <b>pile-up</b> on the motorway.<br>有十一辆车在高速公路上相撞。<br>Three people were killed in a multiple <b>pile-up</b>.<br>连环撞车事故中有三人丧生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pin</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pin sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">确认；确切理解<br><span class="en">to identify or understand sth exactly</span></td><td class="c4">There's something wrong with this photograph but I can't quite <b>pin it down</b>.<br>这张照片有些不对劲儿，可我说不太清楚。<br>Doctors have been unable to <b>pin down</b> the cause of her symptoms.<br>医生们还不清楚她为什么会有这些症状。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpin sth on sb</b></td><td class="c3">使(无辜者)受过；冤枉；嫁祸于<br><span class="en">to make sb seem responsible or take the blame for sth they have not done</span></td><td class="c4">They tried to <b>pin the blame on</b> me!<br>他们居然想让我背黑锅。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pin sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用大头针固定；钉住<br><span class="en">to fasten sth to a waill, etc. with pins</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pinned up</b> a notice on the board.<br>他把通告钉在布告板上。<br>Can I <b>pin this poster up</b>?<br>我可不可以把海报钉上去？2。<br>He was football's first <b>pin</b>-up boy.<br>他是首位登上海报的足球偶像。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pine</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpine aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">因忧伤而憔悴；病病歪歪；消瘦<br><span class="en">to become very sad, and sometimes ill/sick or weak because sb has died or gone away</span></td><td class="c4">After his wife died, he just <b>pined away</b>.<br>妻子死后，他日渐憔悴。<br>He seemed to be <b>pining away</b> from love.<br>他好像为爱而憔悴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pipe</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pipe ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用寸劝告；命令安静些；别说话<br><span class="en">to tell sb to be less nolsy or to stop talking</span></td><td class="c4">OK, everybody <b>pipe down</b>!<br>好了，大家安静啦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>piss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>piss aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE,A,slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">游手好闲；混日子；瞎混<br><span class="en">to waste time by acting in a silly way</span></td><td class="c4">We haven't got time to <b>piss about</b>.<br>我们没时间胡闹了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>piss sb aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">耍弄；湖弄(某人)<br><span class="en">to treat sb in a way that wastes their time</span></td><td class="c4">Dont <b>piss me about</b>, just tell me the truth!<br>别跟我绕弯子了，直截了当告诉找具相吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>piss down<br>ˈpiss it down <span class="tag">(BrE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">下大雨<br><span class="en">to rain very heavily</span></td><td class="c4">It's still <b>pissing</b> (it) <b>down</b> out there.<br>外面依然兩大得要命。<br>The rain was <b>Pissing down</b>.<br>正在下大雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>piss sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使生气；使厌频<br><span class="en">to make sb annoyed or bored</span></td><td class="c4">Everybody's <b>pissed off</b> with what's going on.<br>大家都对目前的情况很恼火。<br>It really <b>pisses me off</b> when I see people behaving like that.<br>看到人们的那种行为确实让我生气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pit ˈout<br>pit sth ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因出汗太多损坏；糟蹋(衬衫等)<br><span class="en">to spoil a shirt, etc. by sweating a lot</span></td><td class="c4">I was so nervous, and my T-shirt was totally <b>pitted out</b>.<br>我太紧张了，T恤衫全被汗水打湿了。<br>I tried to defend myself, turned red, and totally <b>pitted out</b>.<br>我想为自己辩解，变得面红耳赤，汗流浃背。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pitch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pitch ˈin (with sb/sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">志愿；加入；参与；支援<br><span class="en">to join in willingly with sb to help with an activity</span></td><td class="c4">We all <b>pitched in</b> and soon finished the job.<br>我们都上手帮忙，很快便干完了工作。<br>Lots of people <b>pitched in</b> with advice.<br>很多人主动出主意。<br>Ruth <b>pitches in</b> with the adults before she goes to school.<br>露丝上学前和大人一起干活。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pitch ˈinto sb <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">攻击；批评<br><span class="en">to attack or criticize sb</span></td><td class="c4">They really <b>pitched into</b> me when I refused to cooperate.<br>我拒绝合作，他们便对我大肆攻击。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pitch ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大干起来；积极投入；蓬勃开展<br><span class="en">to start doing sth with energy and enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">I rolled up my sleeves and <b>pitched into</b> the cleaning.<br>我挽起衣袖，劲头十足地动手大扫除。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pivot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpivot on/around sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…为核心；围绕…展开<br><span class="en">to depend on a central point; to develop from a central idea or Point</span></td><td class="c4">The success Of the project <b>pivots on</b> investment from abroad.<br>这个项目的成功主要依靠国外投资。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plan</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌplan aˈhead (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">提前安排；预先计划<br><span class="en">to make arrangements in advance</span></td><td class="c4">It's impossible to <b>plan ahead</b> when things keep changing!<br>情况不断变化，不可能提前计划好。<br>We need to <b>plan ahead</b> for our retirement.<br>我们得为退休作准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plaster</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plaster ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">用灰泥涂抹裂缝；墙壁等<br><span class="en">to cover sth such as a crack or a wall with plaster</span></td><td class="c4">The old brick had been <b>plastered over</b>.<br>旧砖上已抹了灰泥。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plate ˈup<br>.plate sth ˈup in</b></td><td class="c3">在餐馆等</td><td class="c4">The food was <b>plated up</b> and ready to go.<br>莱已盛盘，可以端上去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>play</b></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>play aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE also,play a bout)</span></b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；乱弄<br><span class="en">(with sb/sth) to behave in a careless way, without thinking about the results</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>playing</b> about and get on with your work!<br>别瞎折腾了，干你的活儿去吧。<br>Don't <b>play around</b> with matches!<br>别玩火柴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈplay at doing sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">敷衍；应付<br><span class="en">to do sth without any effort or real interest</span></td><td class="c4">He's just <b>playing</b> at being in love.<br>他谈恋爱只不过是逢场作戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play sth ˈback (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">为某人播放录音；录像<br><span class="en">to play music, sound, images, etc. that have been recorded on a tape,video, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>play back</b> what we've just recorded?<br>把我们刚录制的内容播放一下好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">降低…的重要性；贬低；淡化<br><span class="en">to try to make sth appear less important than it is</span></td><td class="c4">The government is trying to <b>play down</b> its involvement in the affair.<br>政府正极力淡化与此事的牵连。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌplay ˈoff <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">平局后；为决出胜负进行加赛；进行决胜比赛<br><span class="en">if two teams, players, etc. that have the same number of points in a competition play off, they play a final game to decide who has won</span></td><td class="c4">The two Germans <b>played off</b> for a place in the final.<br>两名德国选手加赛一场以争夺决赛权。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈplay-off n</b></td><td class="c3">平局后决出胜负的加时赛；延长赛<br><span class="en">a game or games between two players or teams with equal points in a competition to decide who the winner is</span></td><td class="c4">We're unlikely to reach the <b>play-offs</b>.<br>我们不大可能进入加时赛。<br>The title was decided by a suddendeath <b>play-off</b>.<br>冠军是由采取突然死亡法赛制的加时赛决出的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续比赛；恢复比赛<br><span class="en">(sport) to continue to play; to start playing again</span></td><td class="c4">They claimed a penalty but the referee told them to <b>play on</b>.<br>他们要求判罚，但裁判却要他们继续比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续奏乐<br><span class="en">to continue to play music</span></td><td class="c4">Despite the uproar, the musicians <b>played on</b>.<br>乐手们不顾喧闹继续演奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">乐队等演出<br><span class="en">if a band, etc. plays out, it performs in front of an audience</span></td><td class="c4">Serious bands should be <b>playing out</b> regularly.<br>正规乐队应该定期演出。<br><b>Playing out</b> is the best way for a to build a following.<br>现场表演是流行音乐节目主持人贏得拥趸的最佳途径。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使发生；出现<br><span class="en">when an action is played out, or sb plays it out, it happens</span></td><td class="c4">The negotiations are being <b>played out</b> behind closed doors.<br>谈判正在秘密进行。<br>She continued to <b>play out</b> her role of dutiful daughter.<br>她继续恪守她作为女儿的本分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">继续将(比赛等)完成<br><span class="en">(espe Cially ame) to continue to play sth until it finishes</span></td><td class="c4">Well <b>play out</b> this game and then go to bed.<br>我们这一局结束就去睡觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈup<br>.play sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出问题；给…添麻烦<br><span class="en">if sth plays up or plays you up, it causes you problems</span></td><td class="c4">The computer's been <b>playing me up</b> recently.<br>计算机最近总是给我添堵。<br>My leg's <b>playing up</b> again (= it is painful).<br>我的腿又疼起来了。<br>My back <b>plays me up</b> from time to time.<br>我的背不时出现胶涌。2。<br>All kids <b>play new teachers up</b>.<br>所有孩子都戏弄新老师。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈup to sb <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">献媚；讨好；奉承；迎合<br><span class="en">to behave towards sb in a way that you think they will like and will bring you an advantage</span></td><td class="c4">She always <b>played up to</b> her father.<br>她总是讨好她的父亲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>play ˈup to sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">迎合<br><span class="en">to behave in the way that people expect you to</span></td><td class="c4">People think she's only twenty, and she <b>plays up to</b> this all the time.<br>别人以为她只有二十岁，于是她干脆装嫩充小。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈplay with sb/sth <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻率对待；对…虚情假意<br><span class="en">to behave towards sb in a way that is not serious, especially by pretending to feel sth you do not feel</span></td><td class="c4">She was just <b>playing with</b> my emotions.<br>她只不过是在玩弄我的感情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plod</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plod aˈway (at sth)</b></td><td class="c3">坚持不懈地；做(艰难或枯燥的工作)<br><span class="en">to work steadily but slowly at a difficult or boring task</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>plodded away</b> all night at his project to get it finished.<br>他为完成课题通宵埋头苦干。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plough. sth ˈback (into sth)<br>ˌplough sth back ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把(利润)再投资于原；项目<br><span class="en">to put profits back into the business that produced them</span></td><td class="c4">All the profits are <b>ploughed</b> <b>back</b> into the company.<br>所有的利润又反哺给了该公司。<br>The director confirmed that every penny had been <b>ploughed</b> <b>back</b> in.<br>董事确认每分钱都又投了回去。p8J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plough ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或司机<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or a driver</span></td><td class="c4">The car hit a lamp post before <b>ploughing into</b> a wall.<br>汽车碰了灯柱后又撞上一堵墙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plough ˈon (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">不顾；困难坚持说；继续做<br><span class="en">to continue to say or do sth even though it becomes difficult</span></td><td class="c4">No one was listening to him but he <b>ploughed on</b> regardless.<br>没人在听他讲话，但他依然坚持讲下去。<br>The path was steep, but we <b>ploughed on</b> until we got to the top.<br>小路坡度很陡，然而我们坚持不懈，走到了山顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plough sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用犁开垦；开荒<br><span class="en">to break the surface of an area of land that has not been used for growing crops before, and turn it over using a plough</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ploughed up</b> the field ready for sowing.<br>他犁了那片地准备播种。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plough sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">走坏；碾坏；轧翻(地面)<br><span class="en">to break up the surface of the ground by walking or driving across it</span></td><td class="c4">He got so angry he <b>ploughed up</b> his neighbour's lawn with his motorbike.<br>他火冒三丈，开着摩托车把邻居的草坪碾得稀烂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plug</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plug ˈin<br>plug into sth</b></td><td class="c3">能与电源或另；一电器连接<br><span class="en">to be able to be connected to a source of electricity or another piece of electrical equipment</span></td><td class="c4">Where does the <b>plug in</b>?<br>电视机的电源在哪儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plug ˈin<br>plug into sth</b></td><td class="c3">接入(计算机网络)<br><span class="en">(computing) to have access to a computer network</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>plug into</b> the Institute's research network.<br>我们能进入学院的研究网。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plug sth ˈin<br>plug sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">接通(电源或另一电器)；插头插入(插座)<br><span class="en">to conprep nect a piece of electrical equipment to the electricity supply or to another piece of electrical equipment</span></td><td class="c4">Don't forget to <b>plug the printer in</b>.<br>别忘了给打印机接上电源。<br>Where can I <b>plug in</b> my hairdryer?<br>电吹风的插头插在。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈplug-in n</b></td><td class="c3">车库或<br><span class="en">an electric socket in a garage or car park where a car can be plugged in when it is parked, used to heat the engine and prevent it from freezing</span></td><td class="c4">Medicine Hat Hotel offers free parking with <b>plug-ins</b>.<br>梅迪辛哈特酒店提供免费停车，配有防冻插座。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plugged ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">知道；了解<br><span class="en">to be aware of or understand sth</span></td><td class="c4">Colin is always <b>plugged</b> in to what is fashionable with the kids.<br>孩子们中间流行什么，科林总是一清二楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plug sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">填塞；封堵<br><span class="en">to fill or block a hole with a substance or a piece of material that fits tightly into it</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>plugged up</b> all the holes around the window to stop the wind coming in.<br>我们堵上了窗户周围的缝隙，以免漏风。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plumb</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plumb sth ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把洗衣机；浴缸等与水管连接<br><span class="en">to connect a washing machine, a bath, etc. to a water system</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>plumbed in</b> the new washing machine for me.<br>他帮我给新洗衣机接上了水管。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plump ˈdown<br>.plump yourself ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛地坐下；重重坐下<br><span class="en">to sit down quickly and heavily</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>plumped herself down</b> in the armchair.<br>她一屁股坐到扶手椅上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plump sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛然丢下；扔下<br><span class="en">to put sth down suddenly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>plumped his books down</b> on the table.<br>他砰的一声把书丢在桌子上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plump ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">变圆；变胖<br><span class="en">to become rounder or fatter</span></td><td class="c4">Soak the raisins until they <b>plump up</b>.<br>把葡萄干泡在水里发好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plump sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把(羽绒填充品等)拍得蓬松柔软<br><span class="en">to make sth which is stuffed with feathers, etc. rounder and softer by shaking it</span></td><td class="c4">Let me <b>plump up</b> your pillows for you.<br>我来帮你把枕头拍松。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>plunge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>plunge ˈin<br>ˌplunge ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">用力跳进；(重重地)跌入<br><span class="en">to jump or fall into sth, usually with some force</span></td><td class="c4">We ran down to the sea and <b>plunged in</b>.<br>我们跑到海边，纵身跳入海水中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plunge ˈin<br>ˌplunge ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">贸然行动；唐突讲话；冒失地开始做(或讲)<br><span class="en">to begin doing sth or talking about sth without preparing for it or thinking carefully</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>plunged into</b> the task of clearing the office.<br>他二话没说就开始清理办公室。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>plunge sth ˈin<br>ˌplunge sth ˈin/into sth</b></td><td class="c3">猛力插入；扎进<br><span class="en">to put sth quickly and with force into sth eise</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>plunged the knife into</b> his leg.<br>她猛地把刀子扎进他的腿部。<br>He opened the sack and <b>plunged his arm in</b>.<br>他打升袋子，于臀一下于伸了进去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>point</b></td><td class="c2"><b>point sb/sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">把…指出来(给某人看)<br><span class="en">to show sb which person or thing you are referring to, for example by moving your head, by describing them/it, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Will you <b>point his wife out</b> to me if you see her?<br>如果看见他的妻子，你就指给我看好吗。<br>The guide <b>pointed out</b> various historic monuments.<br>导游介绍了各处历史遗迹。<br>I must <b>point out</b> that my part in the rescue was very small.<br>我必须说明，在这次营救行动中我的作用很小。1t。<br>He doesnit like having his faults <b>pointed out</b> to him.<br>他听不进别人的指正。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpoint to sb/sth - AT/ SB/ point to sth</b></td><td class="c3">提出；指出重要的事项或；原因<br><span class="en">to mention sth that you think is important and/or the reason why a particular situation exists</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pointed</b> to unemployment as a reason for rising crime.<br>她强调失业导致了犯罪率上升。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpoint to sb/sth - AT/ SB/ point to sth</b></td><td class="c3">暗示；显示<br><span class="en">if a fact, event or situation points to sth, it suggests that this is true or likely to happen</span></td><td class="c4">All the signs <b>pointed</b> to a successful year ahead.<br>所有迹象都预示来年将一帆风顺。<br>The facts seem to <b>point</b> to him having been murdered.<br>事实似乎表明他是被谋杀的。<br>She had symptoms which <b>pointed</b> to a diagnosis of kidney failure.<br>从症状来看，她很可能患了肾衰竭。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>poke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>poke aˈlong <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">缓慢移动<br><span class="en">to move somewhere very slowly</span></td><td class="c4">The bus <b>poked along</b> at about 30 mph, stopping in every tiny town.<br>公共汽车以大约每小时 30 英里的时速缓慢行驶，在每座小镇都停车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>poke aˈround<br>ˌpoke aˈround sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">闲散地移动(或行事)；闲荡；从容做事<br><span class="en">to move or do things slowly, without hurrying</span></td><td class="c4">I was just <b>poking around</b> in town all morning.<br>我整个上午都在城里闲逛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpoke at sth</b></td><td class="c3">用手指；棍子等；反复地捅<br><span class="en">to push your finger, a stick, etc. into sth, often several times</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>poked at</b> her salad with her fork.<br>她用叉子拨弄着色拉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrough,, poke ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中突出；探出；露出<br><span class="en">if sth pokes out or pokes out of sth, you can see it because a small part is coming through a hole or is no longer covered</span></td><td class="c4">His toes were <b>poking</b> <b>through</b> the holes in his socks.<br>他的脚趾从袜子的破洞处露了出来。<br>Two feet <b>poked</b> out from under the bed.<br>床底下伸出了两只脚。<br>There were flowers <b>poking</b> out of holes in the wall.<br>花儿从墙洞里伸出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpoke sth ˈout poke sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">忽然；前移；突然从…出来<br><span class="en">to move sth suddenly forwards or out of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The door opened and Max <b>poked</b> his head <b>out</b>.<br>门开了，马克斯猛地探出头来。<br>The pony <b>poked</b> its nose <b>out</b> of the door as I went past.<br>我走过时，小马一下子把鼻子伸出门来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>poke ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">突出；露出<br><span class="en">to become visible because a small part is coming through a hole, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The grass had begun to <b>poke up</b> through the snow.<br>草开始破雪而出了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>polish</b></td><td class="c2"><b>polish sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">杀死；干掉<br><span class="en">to kill sb</span></td><td class="c4">She hired an assassin to <b>polish</b> him of.<br>她雇了杀手来除掉他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpolish sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">很快做完；迅速吃光(或喝干)<br><span class="en">to finish sth quickly, especially food or drink</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>polished off</b> the pudding in no time.<br>他们眨眼工夫就把布丁扒拉下肚了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>polish sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">改善；修饰<br><span class="en">to make changes to sth in order to improve it</span></td><td class="c4">The college needs to <b>polish up</b> its image.<br>这所学院得提升下形象了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ponce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ponce aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指为引人注意胡闹；招摇；浪费时光<br><span class="en">to do silly things in a way that looks ridiculous, especially to attract attention; to waste time</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ponces around</b> on the show, interviewing members of the audience.<br>他在节目中装模作样地采访观众。<br>I could have finished that job while you've been <b>poncing around</b>!<br>有你无所事事瞎折腾的那点时间，我就能把那活儿干完了！s v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>poop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>poop ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">没做(安排好的事)；(因劳累或害怕)停止做<br><span class="en">to fail to do sth that you have arranged to do; to stop doing sth because you are very tired or afraid</span></td><td class="c4">I was supposed to go <b>out</b> last night but I <b>pooped</b> <b>out</b>.<br>我昨晚没有按原定计划出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>poop ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">机器停止运转；抛锚<br><span class="en">(on sb) if a machine poops out, it stops working</span></td><td class="c4">The horn on my old Toyota <b>pooped</b> <b>out</b> on me.<br>我的旧丰田车喇叭坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>poop sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使筋疲力尽；使疲惫不堪<br><span class="en">to make sb very tired</span></td><td class="c4">A long day at the office <b>poops me out</b>.<br>在办公室忙了一整天，把我累垮了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pop ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">怒气冲冲地说；当众指责<br><span class="en">(to sb) (ame) to talk angrily about sb/sth or to criticize sb/sth in public</span></td><td class="c4">The assistant coach <b>popped off</b> to the press about the team's poor performances.<br>助理教练在媒体面前公开批评本队的糟糕表现。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pop sth ˈon <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">迅速穿上(衣服)<br><span class="en">to put on a piece of clothing quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>popped on</b> his jacket and went out.<br>他披上夹克就出去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pop ˈover/ˈround <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">上门短暂拜访<br><span class="en">to visit sb's home for a short time</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pop over</b> if you feel lonely.<br>你要是觉得孤单就来我家里坐坐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pop ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">冷不防冒出；突然出现；意外发生<br><span class="en">to appear or happen when you do not expect it</span></td><td class="c4">He seems to <b>pop up</b> in the most unlikely places.<br>他好像神出鬼没。<br>When you click with the mouse, a menu <b>pops up</b>.<br>点击鼠标就会弹出菜单。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pop ˈup<br>.pop sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">棒球</td><td class="c4">He <b>popped it up</b> into left field and Haines caught i.<br>他打出了左外野高飞球，海恩斯接住了。<br>Miller <b>popped up</b> and the inning was over.<br>米勒击出腾空球，一局随之结束。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpop-up n <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">棒球</td><td class="c4">He hit a <b>pop-up</b> into center field.<br>他打出了中外野高飞球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pore</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpore over sth</b></td><td class="c3">打量；审视；钻研<br><span class="en">to study sth by looking at it or thinking about it very carefully</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>poring over</b> an old map.<br>她全神贯注地看一张旧地图。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>post</b></td><td class="c2"><b>post sth ˈoff (to sb) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给某人邮寄；邮递<br><span class="en">to send sth to sb by post/mail</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>posted a letter off</b> to you this morning.<br>我今天上午给你寄了封信。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>post sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">贴出通告；公布<br><span class="en">to put a notice, etc.up on a wall so that people can see it</span></td><td class="c4">The exam results will be <b>posted up</b> in the hall.<br>考试成绩将在礼堂张榜公布。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>potter</b></td><td class="c2"><b>potter aˈbout/aˈround<br>potter aˈbout/aˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">从容做事；欣然从事；漫步；闲荡<br><span class="en">to do things or move without hurrying, especially when you are doing sth that you enjoy and that is not important</span></td><td class="c4">They spent the day <b>pottering about</b> by the river.<br>他们在河边逍遥了一天。<br>She was happy just <b>pottering around</b> the house.<br>她就乐意在家里晃悠。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pounce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpounce on sb/sth (also ˈpounce upon sb/ sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">抓住不放；一把揪住(进行抨击)<br><span class="en">to quickly notice sth that sb has said or done, and criticize it or use it for your own advantage</span></td><td class="c4">As soon as I opened my mouth, the teacher <b>pounced on</b> me.<br>我刚一张嘴就被老师抓住了错。<br>He said something silly and the other boys <b>pounced on it at once</b>.<br>他说了句傻话，马上遭到了其他男孩的嘲笑。<br>His mistake was <b>pounced on</b> by the press.<br>他的失误立刻被新闻界揪住并大做文章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpounce on sth also ˈpounce upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">急切地抓住；把握(机会等)<br><span class="en">to accept an opportunity, etc. with enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pounced</b> on the opportunity to work with them.<br>有机会同他们一起工作，她求之不得。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pound</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pound sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用乐器大声弹奏<br><span class="en">to play a tune on a musical instrument very loudly</span></td><td class="c4">Cole was <b>pounding out</b> a tune on the piano.<br>科尔正在用力弹一首钢琴曲。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pour</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pour sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">倒掉；倾倒(液体)<br><span class="en">to get rid of a liquid by emptying it out of its container</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>poured the water away</b> after he finished washing the car.<br>他洗完车把水倒掉了。<br>The rain <b>poured</b> down all weekend.<br>整个周末都在下暴雨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pour ˈforth<br>pour ˈforth sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">涌现；大量产生<br><span class="en">to appear or to produce sth from somewhere in large numbers or amounts</span></td><td class="c4">The doors opened and a crowd of people <b>poured forth</b>.<br>门开了，一群人蜂拥而出。<br>He <b>poured forth</b> a stream of bitter accusations.<br>他连珠炮般提出了一连串严厉指控。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pour ˈin<br>.pour ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">涌进；(向…)源源而来<br><span class="en">to arrive somewhere in large numbers or amounts</span></td><td class="c4">Complaints <b>poured in</b> after last night's programme.<br>昨晚节目播出后，投诉纷至沓来。<br>Sunlight <b>poured in</b> through the windows.<br>阳光从窗户倾泻而入。<br>Fans were still <b>pouring into</b> the stadium.<br>球迷继续涌入体育场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpour sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">投入(大量金钱)到；大量投资于<br><span class="en">to provide a large amount of money for sth</span></td><td class="c4">The council has been <b>pouring money into</b> the area.<br>议会一直在向这个地区投入大笔资金。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpour sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">倒出(容器中的部分液体)<br><span class="en">to remove some of the liquid from a container, cooking pot, etc. by pouring</span></td><td class="c4">When the fish is cooked, <b>pour off</b> the water.<br>鱼煮熟后，把水滗出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpour it ˈon <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">运动队或选手发挥出色；难以击败<br><span class="en">(of a team or sports player) to play very well against your opponent, so that you are difficult to defeat</span></td><td class="c4">The Rangers came onto the ice and <b>poured it on</b> from the very beginning.<br>流浪者队上了冰球场，从开局起便稳操胜券。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpour it ˈon <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为引人注目而言行夸张；表现过火<br><span class="en">to talk or behave in an exaggerated way in order to impress sb</span></td><td class="c4">She was really <b>pouring it on</b>, making sure he knew she was available.<br>她一个劲儿卖弄风情，想让他明白她仍待字闺中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈout of sth, ˌpour sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">涌出；大量产生<br><span class="en">to come out or to produce sth from somewhere in large amounts or numbers</span></td><td class="c4">Black smoke <b>poured</b> <b>out</b> of the engine.<br>发动机排放出滚滚黑烟。<br>People <b>poured</b> <b>out</b> through the gates.<br>人们涌出大门。<br>Factory chimneys <b>Poured</b> <b>out</b> smoke.<br>工厂烟囱喷出了浓烟。<br>The whole story then <b>poured</b> <b>out</b>.<br>接着，事情的来龙去脉被。<br>He <b>poured</b> <b>out</b> his troubles to me.<br>他对我倾诉了他的烦恼。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>predispose</b></td><td class="c2"><b>prediˈspose sb to sth (also prediˈspose sb towards sth less frequent) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使倾向于做；使易患(疾病)<br><span class="en">to make sb more likely to do sth or to suffer from a particular illness</span></td><td class="c4">Cigarette advertising <b>predisposes children to</b> smoking.<br>烟草广告会诱导儿童抽烟。<br>His lifestyle <b>predisposed him to</b> high blood pressure.<br>他的生活方式使他易患高血压。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>prefix</b></td><td class="c2"><b>prefix A to B<br>ˈprefix A with B</b></td><td class="c3">在…前面加字母；数字或；字词<br><span class="en">to add letters, numbers or words to the beginning of a number or word</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Prefix</b> 020 to the number you want to call.<br>在你要拨打的号码前加 020。<br><b>Prefix</b> the number you want to call with 020.<br>在你要拨打的号码前加020。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>preside</b></td><td class="c2"><b>preˈside over sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">主持会议；仪式等；担任(会议等)的主席<br><span class="en">to lead or be in charge of a meeting, ceremony, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>presided over</b> the meeting.<br>她主持了会议。<br>The court is <b>presided over</b> by a single judge.<br>该法愿只有一名法官负责审案。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>press</b></td><td class="c2"><b>press aˈhead/on (also ˌpress ˈforward less frequent) (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">继续快速前进；坚持不懈地做<br><span class="en">to continue moving forward quickly; to continue to do a task in a determined way</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pressed on</b>, even though it was now dark.<br>尽管夜幕降临，他仍继续赶路。<br>They decided to <b>Press ahead</b> with their plans.<br>他们决定继续推进他们的计划。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpress ˈin (on/upon sb)</b></td><td class="c3">逼近；进逼<br><span class="en">to move nearer to sb in a way that seems likely to cause harm</span></td><td class="c4">He felt as if the walls were <b>pressing in</b> on him.<br>他觉得四周的墙壁仿佛要向他压过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpress ˈon - AHEAD/ press sth on sb</b></td><td class="c3">强迫(某人)接受；把…强加于<br><span class="en">to try to make sb accept sth, even though they may not want it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pressed</b> cake and tea on US.<br>她执意要我们吃蛋糕、喝茶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>presume</b></td><td class="c2"><b>preˈsume on/upon sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不正当地利用<br><span class="en">to use sb's friendship or kindness for your own advantage in an unfair way</span></td><td class="c4">I felt it would be <b>presuming on</b> our friendship to keep asking her for help.<br>如果一再央求她帮忙，我觉得是过分利用了我们之间的交情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pretty</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pretty sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">装饰；修饰；美化<br><span class="en">to make sth look or seem better than before</span></td><td class="c4">She had <b>prettied up</b> the front porch with a few plants.<br>她用些花花草草装饰了前廊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>prevail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>preˈvail on/upon sb (to do sth) <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">劝说；说服<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>prevail on</b> you to play the piano for us?<br>烦请您为我们弹奏钢琴好吗。<br>She was <b>prevailed upon to give one</b> final performance.<br>她被说服最后再演一场。</td></tr>
