<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>prey</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈprey on sth (also ˈprey upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">乌兽捕食；猎食<br><span class="en">if a bird or an animal preys on/upon another bird or animal, it hunts and kills it for food</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>prey on</b> small mammals.<br>它们捕食小型哺乳动物。<br>These small fish are <b>preyed</b> <b>upon</b> by sharks and other fish.<br>这些小鱼是鲨鱼和其他鱼类的猎物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pride</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pride yourself on sth<br>ˈpride yourself on doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">引以为傲；为…而自豪<br><span class="en">to be proud of sth such as a personal quality or a skill</span></td><td class="c4">She had always <b>prided herself on</b> her appearance.<br>她总是对自己的容貌洋洋自得。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>print</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈprintout n</b></td><td class="c3">计算机打印件；打印资料<br><span class="en">a printed copy of information in a computer file</span></td><td class="c4">She asked for a <b>printout</b> of the previous year's accounts.<br>她索要了一份去年账目的打印件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>print sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指；快速或大量打印出<br><span class="en">to produce sth in printed form, especially quickly or in large quantities</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>printed up</b> 200 000 catalogues for the new season.<br>他为新的一个季度打印了20万份产品目录。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>prise sth ˈout of sb<br>ˈprise sth from sb</b></td><td class="c3">用尽手段诱供；逼问；强迫；透露<br><span class="en">to obtain some information, etc. from sb with great difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">She had a way of <b>prising secrets from</b> people.<br>她打探秘密很有一手。<br>Youll be lucky to <b>prise any money out of</b> him!<br>要是能从他那里弄到钱，算你走运。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>proceed</b></td><td class="c2"><b>proˈceed against sb <span class="tag">(formal, law)</span></b></td><td class="c3">起诉；控诉<br><span class="en">to start a court case against sb</span></td><td class="c4">I shall instruct my solicitor to <b>proceed against</b> you for trespass.<br>我要委托我的律师控告你非法侵入他人土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>proˈceed from sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">由…而引起；是…的结果<br><span class="en">to be caused by or be the result of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The dispute <b>proceeded from</b> a wrong interpretation of the law.<br>争端起因于对法律的错误解释。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pronounce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>proˈnounce on/upon sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">就…表态；对…作出判断<br><span class="en">to express an opinion or give a judgement on sth</span></td><td class="c4">The minister will <b>Pronounce on</b> the situation today.<br>部长今天将对局势发表讲话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>prop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>prop sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">支撑；托起(某人)<br><span class="en">to support sb by putting sth under or behind them</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>propped her up</b> with a pillow.<br>我们给她垫了一个枕头。<br>He tried to <b>prop himself up</b> on his elbow.<br>他努力用胳膊肘撑起身子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>prop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">撑起；支起<br><span class="en">to keep sth standing or stop sth from falling by putting sth under or behind it</span></td><td class="c4">A family photo was <b>propped up</b> against some books on her desk.<br>她的书桌上靠着书立着一张全家福。<br>The tree had to be <b>propped up</b> with thick posts.<br>那棵树得用些粗棍子顶住。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>prop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">支持；扶持；援助<br><span class="en">to support sth that is having financial,political, etc. difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">The regime is being <b>propped up</b> by foreign aid.<br>这个政权依靠外援维持着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>provide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>proˈvide against sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">预防；防备；未雨绸缪<br><span class="en">to make plans in order to deal with or prevent a bad or unpleasant situation</span></td><td class="c4">Does your insurance <b>provide against</b> loss of income?<br>你的保险是否赔付收入损失。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>proˈvide for sb</b></td><td class="c3">为…提供生活所需<br><span class="en">to give sb the things that they need to live, such as food, money and clothing</span></td><td class="c4">How will she <b>provide for</b> six children?<br>她将如何养活六个孩子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>psych</b></td><td class="c2"><b>psych sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(对手)心虚胆怯；震慑(对手)<br><span class="en">to make an opponent feel less confident by saying or doing things that make you seem better, stronger, etc. than them</span></td><td class="c4">The other team tried to <b>psych us out</b> before the game started.<br>对方运动队试图在比赛开始前就把我们从心理上打垮。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>psych sb ˈup<br>ˌpsych yourself ˈup (for sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为困难的事作好思想准备<br><span class="en">to prepare sb/yourself mentally for sth difficult, such as a game, an exam, an interview, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Boxers need to <b>psych themselves up</b> for the fight.<br>拳击手需要为比赛作好心理准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>puff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>puff aˈway (at/on sth) <span class="tag">(informal usually used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时</td><td class="c4">He stood looking out of the window, <b>Puffing away</b> at his pipe.<br>他站在那里，一边眺望窗外一边吸着烟斗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>puff sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使充气；吹胀<br><span class="en">to make sth Jarger and rounder by filling it with air</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>puffed out</b> her cheeks in anger.<br>她气得鼓起了腮帮子。<br>Her hair was <b>puffed out</b> round her face.<br>她披头散发。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>puff ˈup<br>. puff sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使膨胀；肿胀<br><span class="en">to swell or to make sth swell and increase in size</span></td><td class="c4">The medicine makes my ankles <b>puff up</b>.<br>这种药把我的脚踝弄肿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pull</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pull aˈhead<br>.pull aˈhead of sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">突然或出人意料地抢先；领先<br><span class="en">to move in front of sb/sth, especially suddenly or unexpectedly</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>pulled ahead</b> of the other runners on the last straight.<br>在直道冲刺时，我一下子超过了其他选手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">毁坏；拆散；拆卸<br><span class="en">to destroy sth or separate sth into pieces by pulling parts of it in different directions</span></td><td class="c4">The fox was <b>pulled apart</b> by the dogs.<br>几条狗把狐狸撕成了碎片。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把某人拉到一旁(私下说话)<br><span class="en">to take sb to a quiet corner or place to talk to them privately</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>pulled him aside</b> to warn him not to say anything.<br>我把他拉到一边，警告他什么也别说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">拉开(帘子等)<br><span class="en">to move sth such as a curtain so that you can see sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pulled the curtain aside</b> to reveal a small door.<br>她揪开帘子，露出了一扇小门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull aˈway (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">车辆开动<br><span class="en">when a vehicle pulls away, it begins to move</span></td><td class="c4">The train was <b>pulling away</b> as we reached the station.<br>我们赶到车站时火车刚刚启动。<br>I started the engine and <b>pulled away</b> from the kerb.<br>我发动引擎驶离了路边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull aˈway (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐拉大(与对手的)距离或；比分；获胜在望<br><span class="en">to gradually move further in front of sb/sth; to start to win a game or competition by getting more points than your opponent</span></td><td class="c4">The British boat began to <b>pull away</b> from the Italians (= in a race).<br>英国赛艇渐渐甩开了意大利赛艇。<br>The German pair <b>pulled away</b> to finish three games ahead (=in tennis).<br>德国双打选手以胜三局领先。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">退回；缩回<br><span class="en">(from sb/sth) to move backwards away from sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pulled back</b> and stared at her in disbelief.<br>他倒退一步，疑惑地盯着她。<br>The camera then <b>pulled back</b> to a wider view.<br>然后摄影机镜头拉回，使取景变宽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">退却；反悔<br><span class="en">to decide not to do sth you were intending to do, usually because of possible problems</span></td><td class="c4">Their sponsors <b>pulled back</b> from financing the movie.<br>赞助商打了退堂鼓，不再资助该部影片。<br>They <b>pulled back</b> a goal in the last few minutes of the game.<br>在比赛结束前几分钟，他们扳回了一球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb/sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">向后拉；拉到一旁；拽开<br><span class="en">to hold sb/sth and move them/it backwards, sideways or away from sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pulled back</b> the curtain.<br>他拉开了窗帘。<br>She <b>pulled the sheet back</b> to show us the wound.<br>她掀开被子，让我们看伤处。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使虚弱；使扫兴<br><span class="en">to have a bad effect on sb's health or happiness</span></td><td class="c4">The strain is really <b>pulling me down</b>.<br>压力着实把我拖垮了。<br>He dried his hands and <b>pulled down</b> his sleeves.<br>他擦干手，放下衣袖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpull for sb/sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">支持；激励<br><span class="en">to support and encourage sb/sth and hope they will be successful</span></td><td class="c4">Hang in there, we're all <b>Pulling for</b> you to win!<br>坚持下去，我们都在为你加油，希望你取胜！K。<br>The coach <b>pulled</b> into bay 27.<br>该辆长途汽车驶进了 27号站台。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpull for sb/sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">车辆或司机驶向路边停靠<br><span class="en">if a vehicle or a driver pulls in, they move to the side of the road and stop</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pull</b> in in front of the bus.<br>开到路边，停在公共汽车前。<br>He <b>pulled</b> into the parking lot and turned off the engine.<br>他把车开进停车场熄了火。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">拘留(盘问)<br><span class="en">to bring sb to a police station in order to ask them questions</span></td><td class="c4">The police have <b>pulled him in</b> for questioning.<br>警方把他扣起来讯问。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth ˈin (also .pull sth ˈdown) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">挣(钱)<br><span class="en">to earn a particular amount of money</span></td><td class="c4">He must be <b>pulling in</b> a hundred thousand.<br>他肯定能赚十万。<br>I <b>pulled</b> off the main road and stopped.<br>我把车驶离大路然后停下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb/sth ˈoff<br>pull sb/sth ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">用力拉开(进攻的人或动物)<br><span class="en">to strongly pull away sb/sth that is attacking sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">They tried to <b>pull off</b> the dogs with their hands.<br>他们试图徒手把那些狗拽开。<br>He had to be <b>pulled off</b> the older man by two policemen.<br>两名警察才把他从老人身边拉开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速或费力地脱；下(衣物)<br><span class="en">to remove an item of clothing quickly or with difhiculty</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pulled off</b> her hat and gloves.<br>她一把摘掉帽子和手套。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">迅速或费力地穿；上(衣物)<br><span class="en">to put an item of clothing on quickly or with difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>pulled my shorts on</b> and ran outside.<br>我套上短裤，跑了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpull on/at sth</b></td><td class="c3">猛抽；狠吸(香烟等)<br><span class="en">to take long deep breaths from a cigarette, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>pulled on</b> her cigar.<br>她深深地吸了口雪茄。<br>A white van suddenly <b>pulled</b> out in front of me.<br>一辆白色小货车突然超车到 F。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>out<br>ˌpull sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">使脱离；退出<br><span class="en">to move or to make sb/sth move away from sth or stop being involved in it</span></td><td class="c4">They are pulling their troops <b>out</b> of the war zone.<br>他们正从战区撤军。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sth<br>pull sb/sth ˈout of doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">使退却；反悔<br><span class="en">to stop being involved in sth or decide not to do sth you had promised to do; to make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">The other firm wanted to Pull <b>out</b> of the deal.<br>对方公司想退出交易。<br>The company is pulling <b>out</b> of sponsoring the team.<br>那冢公司停止赞助该队了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sb ˈthrough<br>.pull sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助康复；(使)痊愈<br><span class="en">to get better after an illness; to help sb get better after an illness</span></td><td class="c4">Few people expected him to pull <b>through</b> after the accident.<br>几乎没人认为事故后他会康复。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpull sth ˈto</b></td><td class="c3">拉上；关上；带上(门)<br><span class="en">if you pull a door to, you close it or almost close it by pulling it towards you</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pull the door to</b> on your way out.<br>出去时把门带上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使(组织等)团结一心；使(行动等)协调一致<br><span class="en">to make all the different parts of an organization, an activity, etc. work together in a successful way</span></td><td class="c4">His inspired leadership <b>pulled the party together</b>.<br>他的卓越领导才干使全党上下同心同德。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">有系统地集中；组合；整合(思想等)<br><span class="en">to organize a variety of ideas, etc. in a logical and careful way</span></td><td class="c4">This lecture <b>pulls together</b> several recent theories.<br>这次讲座系统地介绍了几个新理论。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>pull yourself toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">控制住情绪；恢复镇定<br><span class="en">to gain control of your feelings and start to act in a calm and sensible way</span></td><td class="c4">She made a great effort to <b>pull herself together</b>.<br>她咬紧牙关，保持冷静。<br>Stop crying and <b>pull yourself together</b>!<br>别哭了，振作起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull sb/sth ˈunder</b></td><td class="c3">把…卷进水中<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth become completely covered in water</span></td><td class="c4">He felt the waves <b>pulling him under</b>.<br>他觉得波浪要把他吞没了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpull-up n</b></td><td class="c3">单杠引体向上</td><td class="c4">She does 50 <b>pull-ups</b> and 100 sit-ups every morning.<br>她每天早晨做50次引体向上和100次仰卧起坐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">尤指紧紧抓住某物用力站起来<br><span class="en">to move your body into a standing position, especially by holding sth firmly and using force</span></td><td class="c4">Julia <b>pulled herself up</b> from the sofa.<br>朱莉娅使劲从沙发上站起身来。<br>I <b>pulled myself up</b> to my full height and glared angrily at Dan.<br>我昂首挺胸站立起来，对丹怒目而视。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pull yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">猛然；停止；突然打住<br><span class="en">to stop doing or saying sth very suddenly</span></td><td class="c4">I started to ask about her family, but <b>pulled myself up</b> sharply when I saw she was getting upset.<br>我开始询问她的家庭情况，见她变得心烦意乱，便立刻打住了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pump sth ˈout<br>ˌpump sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">用泵(从…)排出；吸出<br><span class="en">to remove a gas, liquid, etc. from inside sth with a pump</span></td><td class="c4">The fire brigade <b>pumped out</b> the basement.<br>消防队把地下室的水抽了出来。<br>The fire brigade <b>pumped the water out</b> of the basement.<br>消防队把地下室的水抽了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pump sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">为(轮胎等)充气(或打气)<br><span class="en">to fill a tyre, etc. with air using a pump</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Pump your tyres up</b> before you set off.<br>出发前给轮胎打足气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>pump sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增加数量；价值或体积<br><span class="en">to increase the amount, value or volume of sth</span></td><td class="c4">They always <b>pump their prices up</b> before Christmas.<br>他们总是在圣诞节之前提价。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>punch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>punch ˈin/ˈout<br>ˌpunch sb ˈin/out <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">替某人用计时卡登录上班；下班时间；(替某人)刷计时卡<br><span class="en">to record the time that you arrive at or leave work, by putting a card into a machine; to do this for sb else</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>punched in</b> ten minutes late.<br>他上班刷卡迟到了十分钟。<br>I was in such a hurry to leave that I forgot to <b>punch out</b>.<br>我下班时过于匆忙，忘了刷卡。<br>Would you <b>punch me in</b>? I'm going to be late.<br>你可以帮我刷卡吗？我要迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpunch sth ˈin<br>ˌpunch sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将(信息)键入(计算机等)<br><span class="en">to put information into a computer, etc. by pressing keys</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>punched in</b> the security code and the door opened.<br>她输入密码，门开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>punch sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">按键输入号码；字符等<br><span class="en">to press a combination of buttons or keys on a computer, telephone, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He picked up the phone and <b>punched out</b> Donna's number.<br>他拿起电话，拨打唐娜的号码。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>punch sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">在…上打孔；打破；打掉<br><span class="en">to hit sth very hard and make a hole in it or make sth fall out</span></td><td class="c4">The burglar had <b>punched out</b> a pane of glass to open the window.<br>窃贼打碎一块玻璃，弄开了窗户。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>push</b></td><td class="c2"><b>push aˈhead/ˈforward/ˈon (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">毅然推行(计划)<br><span class="en">to continue with a plan in a determined way</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>pushed ahead</b> with the modernization programme.<br>他们坚定地推进现代化方案。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">推开；移开(妨碍前进的人或物)<br><span class="en">to move sb/sth to a position where you are not prevented from going somewhere or doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pushed her aside</b> and went into the room.<br>他推开她，进了房间。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">将…置之不理；把…抛诸脑后<br><span class="en">to treat sb/sth as if they are/it is not important; to avoid thinking</span></td><td class="c4">When his sister brought home a school friend, he felt <b>pushed aside</b> and abandoned.<br>他妹妹带了一位同学回家，他觉得自己被扔在一边，无。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpush sb/sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把不；需要的人或物推开<br><span class="en">to remove sb/sth from in front of you with your hands or arms, to show that you do not want them/it</span></td><td class="c4">He offered to help, but she <b>pushed him away</b>.<br>他主动来帮忙，却被她推开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpush ˈback (at sb) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向负责人投诉；抱怨；拒绝<br><span class="en">to respond to sth that you think is wrong by telling the person responsible that you do not like it</span></td><td class="c4">Minority <b>pushing back</b> at the city's police department, after years of being mistreated.<br>由于年复一年饱受不公正待遇，少数族群不断向市警察局发难。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">把(人)向后推<br><span class="en">to use force to make sb move backwards, especially by using your hands or arms</span></td><td class="c4">The police <b>pushed the protesters back</b>.<br>警察把示威者挡了回去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">迫使士兵；部队等撤离；打退<br><span class="en">if sb pushes soldiers, an army, etc. back, they force them to move away from a place</span></td><td class="c4">Magnus's army was gradually <b>pushed back</b> into a defensive circle.<br>马格努斯的部队被迫一步步撤回防守圈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">把…向后推<br><span class="en">to make sth move backwards by using your hands, arms, legs, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pushed his chair back</b> and stood up.<br>他把椅子向后一推，站了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">推迟；延迟<br><span class="en">to make the time or date of a meeting, etc. later than originally planned</span></td><td class="c4">The release of their new album has been <b>pushed back</b> until early next year.<br>他们的新专辑推迟到明年年初。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpush for sth<br>ˈpush sb for sth</b></td><td class="c3">不断要求；争取；敦促<br><span class="en">to keep asking for sth, or asking sb to do sth, because you think it is very important</span></td><td class="c4">We are <b>pushing hard for</b> electoral reform.<br>我们强烈要求选举改革。<br>They're <b>Pushing me for</b> a decision on the matter.<br>他们在催促我就此事作出决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb/yourself ˈforward</b></td><td class="c3">使引人注目；出风头<br><span class="en">to try to make sb notice sb/yourself, especially in order to obtain sth such as a job or a move to a more important job</span></td><td class="c4">He's not the sort of person who <b>pushes</b> himself <b>forward</b>.<br>他不是想方设法表现自己的那种人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpush ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">插队；加塞儿<br><span class="en">to move in front of other people who are waiting in a line</span></td><td class="c4">They thought I was trying to <b>push in</b> at the head of the queue.<br>他们以为我想插到队列前面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpush ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">滚开；一边去<br><span class="en">used to tell sb rudely to go away</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Push off</b> and leave me in peace!<br>滚远点，让我安静一会儿！2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">向…继续行进<br><span class="en">(to . ) to continue travelling somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">We decided to <b>push on</b> to Stonehaven.<br>我们决定继续前往斯通黑文。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpush sth on/onto sb</b></td><td class="c3">迫使；接受；强迫买下；强人所难<br><span class="en">to try to make sb accept or buy sth they do not really want</span></td><td class="c4">He keeps <b>pushing his attentions on</b> her.<br>他没完没了地向她大献殷勤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌpush sb ˈout<br>.push sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">驱逐；开除<br><span class="en">to make sb leave a place or an organization</span></td><td class="c4">He refused to resign, so his colleagues <b>pushed him out</b>.<br>他拒绝辞职，于是同僚把他赶下了台。<br>Patients are being <b>pushed out</b> of hospital before they are really ready.<br>病人还没痊愈就要被赶出医院。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">降低…的重要性；使失势；替换<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth less important than before; to replace sb/sth with sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">My parents didn't want me to feel <b>pushed out</b> by my younger brother.<br>父母不想让我因为我弟弟而感到失宠。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">推倒；推翻<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth fall to the ground; to make sth fall onto its side or turn over</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>pushed over</b> in the playground.<br>我在运动场上被撞倒了。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push ˈthrough<br>.push ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">冲过(障碍物)；挤过(人群)<br><span class="en">to uise force to cross a barrier, especially one formed by a crowd of people</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>pushed his way through</b> to the front of the crowd.<br>他挤到了人群前面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sth ˈthrough<br>push sth ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">使通过；使获批准<br><span class="en">to get a new law, plan or proposal officially accepted</span></td><td class="c4">We're trying to <b>push through</b> the reforms as quickly as possible.<br>我们正在争取尽快促成这些改革。<br>The Prime Minister promised to <b>push the bill through</b> Parliament quickly.<br>首相允诺让议会从速通过这项法案。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>push sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">上升；使增长<br><span class="en">to make sth rise or increase</span></td><td class="c4">A shortage of land <b>pushed property prices up</b>.<br>士地短缺推高了房地产价格。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>pussyfoot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>pussyfoot aˈbout/aˈround</b></td><td class="c3">不正面表达；支支吾吾<br><span class="en">to be careful or anxious about expressing your opinion in case youl upset sb</span></td><td class="c4">Alison should stop <b>pussyfooting around</b> and tell him what she really thinks.<br>艾莉森不该再闪烁其词了，得对他表明她自己的真实想法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>put</b></td><td class="c2"><b>put aˈbout (technical)</b></td><td class="c3">船改变航向；转向<br><span class="en">if a ship puts about, it changes direction</span></td><td class="c4">The ship <b>put about</b> and headed back to port.<br>船掉头驶回港口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put it aˈbout (also ˌput yourself aˈbout) <span class="tag">(BrE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与多人有染；滥交<br><span class="en">to have sexual relationships with a lot of different people</span></td><td class="c4">He had a reputation for <b>putting it about</b> when he was at college.<br>他上大学时出了名地爱乱搞。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth aˈbout <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">散布；传播<br><span class="en">to spread information, stories, etc. among a group of people</span></td><td class="c4">Someone has been <b>putting it about</b> that youre leaving.<br>有人散布消息说你要走了。<br>This was an idea <b>put about</b> by the government.<br>这一构想是从政府传出的。<br>Rumours were <b>put about</b> that the shop was closing.<br>传言说商店要关门了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put yourself aˈbout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指为了出名喜欢交际；待人友善<br><span class="en">to be sociable and friendly in public, especially in order to become well-known</span></td><td class="c4">Politicians like that are always <b>putting themselves about</b> at parties.<br>那种政客总是出没于各类聚会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put yourself aˈbout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">比赛中全身心投入；奋力拼搏<br><span class="en">sport to be very involved in a game and play with enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">Christian is a no-nonsense defender who <b>puts himself about</b> and is popular with the fans.<br>克里斯蒂安是一名敬业的后卫，比赛中积极投入，深受球迷喜爱。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把…放在一边<br><span class="en">to place sth to one side</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>put the newspaper aside</b> and stood up.<br>她把报纸放在旁边站了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">积蓄；储存；积攒(钱款)<br><span class="en">to save some money to use later</span></td><td class="c4">He had been <b>putting</b> some money aside every month.<br>以前他一直每月攒点钱。<br>They decided to <b>put</b> aside their differences.<br>他们决定搁置双方的分歧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>put sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">把…放回<br><span class="en">to return sth to its usual place; to return sth to the place it was before</span></td><td class="c4">He uses my things and never <b>puts them back</b>.<br>他用了我的东西从来不放回原处。<br><b>Put the book back</b> on the shelf, will you?<br>把书放回书架好吗。<br>She carefully put the letters back where she'd <b>found</b> them.<br>她小心翼翼地把信放回。<br>The game has been <b>put back</b> 24 hours.<br>比赛推迟了24小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput sb/sth before sb/sth (also ˈput sb/sth above sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…看得比…重要；把…放在…之上<br><span class="en">to give sb/sth more importance than sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>puts his children before</b> anyone else.<br>他把子女看得比谁都重要。<br>They have always <b>put business before</b> pleasure.<br>他们一直是正事在先，享乐在后。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth beˈfore sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">向…展示；把…提交给<br><span class="en">to present sth to sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She will <b>put her arguments before</b> the committee.<br>她将向委员会陈述自己的观点。<br>The new evidence was <b>put before</b> the court.<br>新的证据已呈交法庭。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth beˈhind you</b></td><td class="c3">把…置之脑后<br><span class="en">to try to forget about sth unpleasant that has happened and not allow it to affect your future</span></td><td class="c4">She wanted to <b>put</b> the past <b>behind</b> her.<br>她想忘掉过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">飞机或飞行员降落；着陆<br><span class="en">if a plane or its pilot puts down, the plane comes down to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">The plane <b>put down</b> at Manchester airport.<br>飞机降落在曼彻斯特机场。<br>He had to <b>put down</b> in a field.<br>他只好降落在一块田里。<br>Dont <b>put yourself down</b>!<br>别妄自菲薄。<br>Ask the driver to <b>put you down</b> outside the City Hall.<br>告诉司机让你在市政厅外下车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput-down n <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">令人难堪的话(或行为)；噎人的话<br><span class="en">a remark or an action that is intended to make sb look stupid</span></td><td class="c4">She produces some wonderful <b>put-downs</b>.<br>她真会奚落人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>g<br>put sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；搁下<br><span class="en">to place sb/sth that you are holding onto the floor or another surface</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>put her bag down</b> by the door.<br>她把包放在门边。<br>Could you <b>put down</b> in writing what you feel?<br>请把你的感受写下来好吗。<br>The rain stopped so she <b>put her umbrella down</b>.<br>雨停了，她把伞收了起来。4。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈdown as sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指在不太了解；的情况下把某人看作；把某人视为<br><span class="en">to think that sb is a particular type of person, especially when you do not know them very well</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>put the boy down as a troublemaker as</b> soon as I saw him.<br>我一见到这孩子就认为他很顽皮。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput sb ˈdown for sth</b></td><td class="c3">为…登记预购(或认捐等)<br><span class="en">to write down that sb is willing or wishes to buy sth, give an amount of money, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Put me down for three tickets for</b> the Saturday show.<br>给我预订三张星期六的演出门票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈforth <span class="tag">(ormal or literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用劲；费心；尽心尽力<br><span class="en">FORWARD (ame) to make a strong physical or mental effort to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">He isn't <b>putting forth</b> the necessary effort.<br>他没有尽力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈforward</b></td><td class="c3">将…提前<br><span class="en">to move sth to an earlier time or date</span></td><td class="c4">We've <b>put the meeting forward</b> a couple of days.<br>我们把会期提前了两三天。<br>France is an hour ahead, so youll have to <b>put your watch forward</b> when you get there.<br>法国早一个小时，所以你到了那里得把表拨快。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put ˈin (at .. ), .put ˈinto . <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">船或船员<br><span class="en">of a ship or its sailors</span></td><td class="c4">The ship <b>put</b> in at Lisbon.<br>轮船时停靠里斯本港。<br>The captain was instructed to <b>put</b> <b>into</b> Calais for repairs.<br>船长得到指令驶入加来港检修。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈin <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">选举(执政党)；任命(某人)<br><span class="en">to elect a political party as the government; to choose sb officially to do a particular job</span></td><td class="c4">The voters <b>put the Conservatives in</b> with a large majority.<br>选民以压倒性多数票选举保守党上台。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈin/ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把某人送进学校；医院等<br><span class="en">to make sb go to a particular institution, such as a school, hospital, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>put in</b> prison for five years.<br>他入狱五年。<br>An accident <b>put him in</b> hospital for three weeks.<br>车祸后他入院治疗三个星期。<br>We had to <b>Put granny in</b>/into a nursing home.<br>我们不得不把奶奶送到养老院。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈin/ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">给某人指派(工作)<br><span class="en">to give sb a particular job to do</span></td><td class="c4">They had central heating <b>put in</b> when they moved into the flat.<br>他们搬进这所公寓时安装了中央供暖设备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈin/ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">种植；栽种<br><span class="en">to plant sth in the ground</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>put any bulbs in</b> this autumn?<br>今年秋天你种鳞茎植物了吗？m。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put ˈin for sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">申请<br><span class="en">to apply formally for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Are you going to <b>put in for</b> that job?<br>你想申请那份工作吗。<br>She's going to <b>Put in for</b> a transfer.<br>她打算申请调职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb/sth/yourself ˈin for sth</b></td><td class="c3">给…登记；报名(参加比赛)<br><span class="en">to enter sth/yourself for a competition</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>Put</b> herself in for the 100 metres.<br>她已报名参加100 米赛跑。<br>You should <b>put</b> that photo in for the competition.<br>你应该拿那张照片参赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…注入；使融入<br><span class="en">to add a quality to sth</span></td><td class="c4">Do you need to <b>put some excitement into</b> your life?<br>你需要给生活加点刺激吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">取消；撤销(与某人的会面或安排)<br><span class="en">to cancel a meeting or sth you had arranged with sb</span></td><td class="c4">He was supposed to come yesterday, but I <b>put him off</b>.<br>他本来昨天要来的，可我把他打发掉了。<br>Tell her you want to talk to her and don't be <b>put off</b>.<br>告诉她你想跟她谈谈，别让她推三阻四。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">车辆；司机；船舶等<br><span class="en">of a vehicle, a driver, a ship, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I asked the bus driver to <b>put me off</b> near the town centre.<br>我请公共汽车司机在快到市中心时让我下车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈon<br>ˌput sb ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">让某人接听电话<br><span class="en">to give sb the telephone so that they can speak to the person calling</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>put Tim on</b> the phone.<br>她让蒂姆接电话。<br><b>Put Jane on</b> for a minute, will you?<br>让简接听一下电话好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…送上飞机；火车<br><span class="en">to make sure that sb gets on a plane, train, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>put Ruth on</b> the bus to Carlisle.<br>我们把鲁思送上了开往卡莱尔的公共汽车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">使遵照(规定饮食)；服用(某种药物)<br><span class="en">to make sb follow a particular diet, take a particular medicine, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor <b>put him on</b> antibiotics.<br>医生让他服用抗生素。<br>Tim's been <b>put on</b> a low-fat diet.<br>蒂姆被要求只吃低脂肪食物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">决定由…做(某工作)<br><span class="en">to decide that sb should do a particular job</span></td><td class="c4">Hang on, I need to <b>put my glasses on</b>.<br>等一下，我得戴上眼镜。<br>I can't find anything clean to <b>put on</b>!<br>我找不到一件干净衣服穿。<br>Could you <b>put his shoes on</b> for him?<br>请帮他穿上鞋好吗。<br>Make sure you <b>put some sun cream on</b> before you go out.<br>出去前别忘了搽防晒箱。<br>Let's <b>put the kettle on</b> and have a cup of tea.<br>我们烧壶水沏杯茶吧。<br>She <b>put on</b> the brakes suddenly.<br>她猛地踩下刹车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">专门；提供<br><span class="en">to provide sth specially</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>put on</b> extra trains during the holiday period.<br>假期额外增开了列车。<br>A splendid lunch was <b>put on</b> for the visitors.<br>专门为客人们准备了丰盛的午餐。<br>The museum <b>put on</b> a special exhibition about dinosaurs.<br>博物馆专门举办了恐龙展。<br>Can you <b>put on</b> an American accent?<br>你能模仿美国口音吗。<br>He seemed furious, but I think it was all <b>put on</b>.<br>他似乎怒不可遏，可我想这都是在演戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈonto sb/sth (also ˌput sb on to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">为…介绍；提供；信息<br><span class="en">to tell sb about a person, an organization, etc. that could help them, or sth that they might like or find useful</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>put me onto</b> a good accountant?<br>你能给我介绍个好会计师吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">船只或船员<br><span class="en">(to/from..) (bre) of a boat or a crew</span></td><td class="c4">The ship <b>put out</b> to sea by night.<br>轮船在夜间出海了。<br>We <b>put out</b> from Liverpool.<br>我们从利物浦起航。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使入睡；使昏迷<br><span class="en">to make sb go to sleep or become unconscious</span></td><td class="c4">These pills should <b>put him out</b> for a few hours.<br>这些药片能让他昏睡几个小时。<br>He <b>put his cigarette out</b>.<br>他捻灭了香烟。<br>She <b>put the washing out</b> to dry.<br>她把洗好的衣服晾出去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">使(身体部位)探出(门或窗)；把…弄出门或<br><span class="en">to put a part of your body through a door or window to the outside</span></td><td class="c4">She opened the window and <b>put</b> her head <b>out</b>.<br>她打开窗户探出头来。<br>Sam <b>put the cat out of</b> the door roughly.<br>萨姆粗暴地把猫赶出门外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">播放；出版；公布<br><span class="en">to broadcast sth; to publish or issue sth</span></td><td class="c4">The programme will be <b>put</b> <b>out</b> on Channel 4.<br>该节目将在第四频道播出。<br>The was <b>put</b> <b>out</b> for the American market.<br>这张。<br>The police <b>put</b> <b>out</b> an urgent appeal for witnesses.<br>警方发出了寻找目击证人的紧急呼吁。<br>They <b>put</b> <b>out</b> a new software package last month.<br>他们上个月开发了一个新软件包。<br>The cleaning contract was <b>put</b> <b>out</b> to tender (= companies were asked to make offers to supply these services).<br>清洁合同对外招标了。<br>I <b>put</b> my back <b>out</b> lifting those boxes.<br>我扛那些箱子时扭伤了背。<br>His musical <b>output</b> has diminished in recent years.<br>他近年的音乐作品减少了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput yourself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">特意为…忙活；专诚为…做事<br><span class="en">to make a special effort to do sth for sb</span></td><td class="c4">Please don't <b>put yourself out</b> on our account.<br>请别特意为我们费心了。<br>She really <b>put herself out</b> for the visitors.<br>她悉心招待来客。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈover + A put one ˈover on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">蒙骗；诱骗<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to accept sth that is not true; to trick sb</span></td><td class="c4">No <b>one</b> is going to <b>put</b> <b>one</b> <b>over</b> on him.<br>没人能让他上当。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈover + A put one ˈover on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">占上风；压倒；击溃<br><span class="en">to show that you are better, stronger, etc. than sb else by defeating them</span></td><td class="c4">We'd love to <b>put</b> <b>one</b> <b>over</b> on the Welsh team.<br>我们要战胜威尔士队。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sth ˈpast sb (to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">对某人做错事；违法等感到吃惊<br><span class="en">to be surprised that sb has done sth wrong, lllegal</span></td><td class="c4">I wouldn't <b>put it past</b> him to use force to get what he wants.<br>即使他为了达到目的使用暴力，我也不会感到惊讶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput sb/yourself ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">使经受(痛苦或磨炼)；折磨<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself experience sth unpleasant or difficult</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>put</b> his Parents <b>through</b> hell.<br>他让他的父母饱受折磨。<br>Why <b>put yourself through</b> it?<br>你何必自讨苦吃呢。<br>She never forgot the terrible ordeal he had <b>put</b> her <b>through</b>.<br>她永远忘不了他带来的深重苦难。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput sb/yourself ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">供某人上(学)<br><span class="en">to pay for sb to attend a school, college, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She worked parttime to <b>put</b> herself <b>through</b> university.<br>她靠打零工挣钱读完了大学。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>put sb/sth ˈthrough (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">给…接通(电话)；为…转接(至…)<br><span class="en">to connect sb to sb else by telephone</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>put me through</b> to the manager,please?<br>请找经理接电话好吗。<br>The call was <b>put through</b> to the wrong extension.<br>电话接错分机了。<br>Hold the line, I'm <b>putting you through</b>.<br>别挂电话，我这就给你转接过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb/sth ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">检验；测试能力；或性能<br><span class="en">to test sb/sth to see what they are able to do</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>put the machines through</b> a series of tests.<br>我们对机器进行了一系列检测。<br>The team are <b>put through</b> a fitness programme.<br>该队接受了体能项目测试。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput sb to sth</b></td><td class="c3">给…增添麻烦；问题；工作<br><span class="en">to make trouble, Problems or extra work for sb</span></td><td class="c4">I hope we're not <b>putting you to too</b> much trouble.<br>但愿我们没有给你添太多的麻烦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput sth to sb</b></td><td class="c3">建议；给…提出(建议)<br><span class="en">to suggest sth to sb for them to consider</span></td><td class="c4">Your proposal will be <b>put to</b> the board of directors.<br>你的建议将提交董事会。<br>The question of strike action must be <b>put to</b> union members.<br>采取罢工行动的问题必须提交工会成员讨论。<br>When are you going to <b>put the idea to</b> your parents?<br>你打算什么时候把这个想法告诉父母。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>put sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">组装；装配；拼接<br><span class="en">to make or repair sth by fitting parts together</span></td><td class="c4">He took the clock apart and couldn't <b>put it together</b> again.<br>他把钟拆开却装不起来了。<br>The band are putting their <b>first</b> album together.<br>这支乐队正在制作他们的第一张专辑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>put sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">组合；结合<br><span class="en">to combine things</span></td><td class="c4">What reaction will we get if we <b>put these two chemicals together</b>?<br>把这两种化学试剂放在一起会产生什么反应呢。<br>This painting is worth more than all the rest <b>put together</b>.<br>这幅画比其他的加起来还要值钱呢。1,3v+ n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput sth towards sth</b></td><td class="c3">攒钱买；为…凑钱<br><span class="en">to use or give an amount of money to pay part of the cost of sth</span></td><td class="c4">We will <b>put the money towards</b> a new computer.<br>我们要把这笔钱攒起来买台新计算机。<br>The city council will <b>put</b> £5 000 <b>towards</b> equipment for the nursery.<br>市议会将拨出5000英镑用于购置幼儿园的设备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">激烈抵抗；奋力斗争；坚持争辩<br><span class="en">to resist strongly or fight hard in a game, a contest, an argument, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The other team didn't <b>put up</b> much of a fight.<br>对方队伍没怎么抵抗。<br>She's not likely to <b>put up</b> much resistance to the idea.<br>她不会强烈反对这个想法。<br>They <b>put us up</b> at a hotel in town.<br>他们安排我们住在城里的家旅馆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌput ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">提名；推荐<br><span class="en">(for sth) to present sb as a candidate in an election; to propose sb for an official position</span></td><td class="c4">We hope to <b>put up</b> more women candidates in the next election.<br>我们希望在下次选举时推举更多女性候选人。<br>We want to <b>put you up</b> for club secretary.<br>我们想推荐你当俱乐部干事。四。<br>It started raining so I <b>put my umbrella up</b>.<br>下雨了，我撑起了伞。<br>Annie's <b>put posters up</b> all over her bedroom.<br>安妮在她的卧室挂满了海报。<br>We had trouble <b>putting the tent up</b> in the dark.<br>我们摸黑支帐篷很费劲儿。<br>We need to <b>put some shelves up</b> for our books.<br>我们得摆几个书架放书。<br>The have <b>put up</b> their interest rates again.<br>银行再次提高利率。<br>The landlord wants to <b>put up</b> the rent by £20 a month.<br>房东打算把月租提高20英镑。<br>Why did Jess <b>put her baby up</b> for adoption?<br>杰丝为什么要让别人收养她的孩子呢？I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>put sb ˈup to sth<br>put sb ˈup to doing sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">怂恿；撺掇<br><span class="en">to encourage or persuade sb to do sth wrong or stupid</span></td><td class="c4">Some of the older boys must have <b>put him up to</b> it.<br>那件事准是一些大孩子唆使他干的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>put ˈup with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">宽容；忍受<br><span class="en">to accept sb/sth that is annoying or unpleasant without complaining</span></td><td class="c4">I don't see why I should <b>put up with</b> being spoken to like that.<br>我不明白我为什么要对那种话忍气吞声。<br>She has a lot to <b>put up with</b>.<br>她得处处忍让。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈput upon sb <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">利用(某人)的善意；占…的便宜<br><span class="en">to use sb's kindness for your own advantage by asking them to do things for you that you should not expect them to do</span></td><td class="c4">She is the most <b>put</b>-<b>upon</b> member of the family.<br>在家里她是最受欺负的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>puzzle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>puzzle sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">琢磨出…的答案；找到…的解决办法<br><span class="en">to find the solution to a dif. ficult problem by thinking carefully about it</span></td><td class="c4">I can't <b>puzzle out</b> how the box opens.<br>我搞不懂怎么打开这个盒子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈpuzzle over/about sth</b></td><td class="c3">认真琢磨；苦苦思索<br><span class="en">to think hard about sth because you want to understand it</span></td><td class="c4">Police are still <b>puzzling over</b> the incident.<br>警方仍然在追查事件发生经过。<br>She <b>puzzled over</b> the postmark on the letter.<br>她想弄明白信封上的邮戳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>quarrel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈquarrel with sth/sb <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于否定句<br><span class="en">usually used in negative sentences</span></td><td class="c4">Few would <b>quarrel with</b> the principle of free education for all.<br>绝少有人会反对普及义务教育这一原则。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>queue</b></td><td class="c2"><b>queue ˈup (for sth/to do sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">排队等候<br><span class="en">to wait or stand in a line with other people in order to get sth or do sth</span></td><td class="c4">They spent four hours <b>queueing up</b> for tickets.<br>他们排了四个小时队买票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˌqueuing ˈup for sth/to do sth</b></td><td class="c3">纷纷等待；争先恐后；趋之若鹜<br><span class="en">if you say that people are queuing up for sth, you mean that a lot of people want to have sth or do sth</span></td><td class="c4">Actors are <b>queuing</b> up to work with this company.<br>演员都期待与这家公司合作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>quit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈquit on sb <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">离开最需要获得帮助；合作或；支持的人；撇下(某人)不管<br><span class="en">to stop helping, working with or supporting sb when they need you most</span></td><td class="c4">I can't believe he <b>quit on</b> the team after only two games!<br>我无法相信他只打了两场比赛就离队了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rabbit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrabbit ˈon (about sb/sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, dis. approving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">没完没了地闲谈；闲扯；唠叨；喋喋不休<br><span class="en">to taik about sth for a long time in a boring way</span></td><td class="c4">What's he <b>rabbiting on</b> about?<br>他在瞎唠叨些什么啊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rack ˈup sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">累积盈利；亏损等；累计(得分)；聚集<br><span class="en">to get or collect a large amount or quantity of sth, such as profits or losses in a business or points in a competition</span></td><td class="c4">The company <b>racked up</b> $20 billion in sales.<br>公司销售额累计达 200亿元。<br>Bush has <b>racked up</b> victories in another five states.<br>布什在另外五个州又获得了胜利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>raffle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>raffle sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">以…为抽彩奖品<br><span class="en">to offer sth as a prize in a raffle</span></td><td class="c4">The cake will be <b>raffled off</b> to raise money for the school.<br>抽奖活动是为学校筹款，奖品是这个蛋糕。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrag on sb <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">抱怨；责难；责骂<br><span class="en">to complain to sb about their behaviour, work, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">My boss is always <b>ragging on</b> me.<br>老板总是责骂我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be,rained ˈoff (BrE) (AmE be ˌrained ˈout) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">体育比赛等活动因雨中断；因雨取消<br><span class="en">if an event such as a sports game is rained off, it stops or it does not take place because of rain</span></td><td class="c4">The game was rained <b>off</b>.<br>比赛因雨中断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rake</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrake sth ˈin <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易地赚(大钱)<br><span class="en">to earn large amounts of money without difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">The company <b>rakes in</b> about £190 million.<br>公司轻而易举地赚了大约 1.9 亿英镑。<br>Since she moved to London she's been <b>raking it in</b>.<br>她从搬到伦敦以来钱已经赚得数不清。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrake sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">从…中抽头；吃回扣；拿佣金<br><span class="en">to take part of the profits of sth, especially secretly or dishonestly</span></td><td class="c4">Landlords have been <b>raking off</b> commission from inflated insurance premiums.<br>房东们一直在从高额保险费中抽取佣金。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rake ˈover sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">翻出；重提(往事)<br><span class="en">to examine sth that happened in the past in great detail and keep talking about it, when it should be forgotten</span></td><td class="c4">There's no point in <b>raking over</b> the events of the past.<br>唠叨旧事毫无意义。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrake sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">重提；翻出令人不快的；往事<br><span class="en">to talk about sth unpleasant that has happened in the past, which people would like to forget</span></td><td class="c4">I didn't come here to <b>rake up</b> old arguments.<br>我不是来重提以前的争吵的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rally</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rally aˈround/round<br>ˌraily aˈround/ ˈround sb</b></td><td class="c3">聚集；在一起；集结起来(帮助支持某人)<br><span class="en">if people rally around or rally around sb, they work together to help and support sb who is in a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">When she was ill, the neighbours all <b>rallied round</b> to help her.<br>她生病期间，左邻右舍都来帮助她。<br>His friends <b>rallied around</b> him when they heard the news.<br>朋友们一得到消息就都来支持他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ram</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌram ˈinto sb/sth<br>ˌram sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使猛撞；猛击<br><span class="en">to hit sth violently; to make sth hit sth violently</span></td><td class="c4">He was going too fast and <b>rammed into</b> the car in front.<br>他速度太快，猛地撞上了前面的车。<br>The thieves <b>rammed their truck into</b> the jeweller's window.<br>窃賊开着货车猛地撞进了珠宝店的橱窗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ramble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌramble ˈon (about sb/sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">漫谈；闲扯；漫笔<br><span class="en">to talk or write a lot about sb/sth in a confused and boring way</span></td><td class="c4">What is she <b>rambling on</b> about?<br>她在东拉西扯些什么呢。<br>There's me <b>rambling on</b>, and you haven't told me your news yet.<br>光我一个人在说个不停，你还没把你的事儿告诉我呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ramp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ramp ˈup<br>ˌramp sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使分阶段提高；使逐步增加；使缓升<br><span class="en">to increase in stages; to make sth increase in stages</span></td><td class="c4">The manufacturer has <b>ramped up</b> production of this popular new model.<br>生产商逐步增加了这款畅销新品的产量。<br>Internet sales have been <b>ramping up</b> over the past year.<br>在过去一年里，互联网上的销售额一直稳步上升。n+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>range</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˌranged aˈgainst/ˈwith ˌsb/sth<br>range yourself</b></td><td class="c3">联合<br><span class="en">a gainst/with sb/sth formal to join with other people to oppose sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He felt as though the whole family <b>was ranged against</b> him.<br>他感觉好像全家人合伙对付他。<br>She <b>ranged</b> herself more with her parents than with her brother.<br>她多数时候是站在父母而不是兄弟一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrap sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">迅速厉声说出；喝(令)<br><span class="en">to say sth quickly and sharply</span></td><td class="c4">The officer <b>rapped out</b> orders.<br>军官大声下令。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrat on sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打小报告；告发；出卖<br><span class="en">to give information to people in authority, causing trouble for sb</span></td><td class="c4">Say what you like about Ali but he has never <b>ratted on</b> his friends.<br>随便你怎么说阿里，但他从未打过朋友的小报告。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrat on sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">违背(诺言)<br><span class="en">to fail to keep a promise you have made</span></td><td class="c4">They accused the government of <b>ratting on</b> promises to the disabled.<br>他们指责政府背弃了对残疾人的承诺。p8J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ratchet</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ratchet sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">逐步提高(价格等)<br><span class="en">to make prices, etc. increase a little at a time</span></td><td class="c4">The interest rates have been <b>ratcheted up</b> sharply.<br>利率渐渐调得很高。<br>The hormone rushes around the brain, <b>ratcheting the heart rate up</b> from 60-80 to about a hundred.<br>荷尔蒙在脑中四处窜动，把心率从60-80逐渐提高到大约 100。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ration</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌration sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">分配；配给(有限的东西)<br><span class="en">to divide sth that there is not very much of between a group of people in such a way that everyone gets a small share</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>rationed the water out</b> among the survivors.<br>他们把水分给了幸存者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rattle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrattle aˈround<br>rattle aˈround sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在空荡荡的地方居住(或工作等)<br><span class="en">to live, work, etc. somewhere that is much too big for your needs</span></td><td class="c4">There are only two of us, <b>rattling around</b> in this massive office.<br>这么大的办公室空落落的，只有我们两个人。<br>They're <b>rattling around</b> that house now that the children have left.<br>孩子们走后就剩下他们住在空荡荡的房子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrattle sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">不假思索地说出(或背诵)；脱口而出<br><span class="en">to say or repeat sth from memory, quickly and without any effort</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>rattled off</b> the names of the movies Hitchcock had directed.<br>她顺口就报出了希区柯克所执导的电影的片名。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrattle ˈon (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">喋喋不休地说(无谓或无趣的话)<br><span class="en">to talk quickly and for a long time about sth that is not important or interesting</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rattled on</b> about his job for over an hour.<br>他喋喋不休地聊他的工作，说了一个多小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrattle ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">迅速地做<br><span class="en">to do sth very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rattled through</b> his homework then went out.<br>他急急忙忙写完作业就出去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reach</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌreach sth ˈdown (for sb)</b></td><td class="c3">为某人从高处取下<br><span class="en">to get sth down from a high place</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>reach that vase down</b> for me?<br>请帮我把那个花瓶拿下来好吗。<br>She <b>reached down</b> a box from the top shelf.<br>她从架子最上层把盒子拿了下来。<br>I <b>reached</b> out a hand to touch her face.<br>我伸手摸她的脸。<br>The child <b>reached</b> out for her hand.<br>孩子伸过手来握她的手。n+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌreach ˈout to sb</b></td><td class="c3">某人表示感兴趣；伸出援助之手；试图吸引…的注意力<br><span class="en">to show sb that you are interested in them and/or want to help them; to try to get people's interest or attention</span></td><td class="c4">The organization is trying to <b>reach out to</b> people of all ages and from all levels of society.<br>该组织试图吸引各年龄段以及社会各阶层人士。<br>The party has failed to <b>reach out to</b> young people.<br>该党不能吸引年轻人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>read</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌread sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">认为…另有深意；对…作过度解读<br><span class="en">to think that sth has a meaning an importance that it probably does not have</span></td><td class="c4">It's a mistake to <b>read too much into</b> the results of one opinion poll.<br>对一次民意调查结果作过度的解读是错误的。<br>You can <b>read anything you want into</b> horoscopes.<br>占星术算命怎么理解都行。<br>Her voice was cold and I wasn't sure what to <b>read into</b> it.<br>她语气冷淡，我弄不清该作何解释。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>read sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">看(机器或测量设备)上的读数<br><span class="en">to look at the measurement shown on a machine or measuring device</span></td><td class="c4">The speed can be <b>read off</b> from the graph.<br>速度可以从图表中读取。<br>I looked at the thermometer and <b>read off</b> the temperature.<br>我看了看温度计上的读数。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>read ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续读；接着读<br><span class="en">to continue reading</span></td><td class="c4">The book was so exciting he <b>read on</b> until dawn.<br>那本书太精彩了，他一口气读到天亮。<br>The idea is to make the <b>reader want to read on</b>.<br>目的是吸引读者继续读下去。<br>If you want to find out more, <b>read on</b>!<br>欲知后事，请看下文。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,read sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">大声读给某人；朗读<br><span class="en">to read sth aloud, especially to other people</span></td><td class="c4">She read <b>out</b> the names of the winners.<br>她宣读了获胜者的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈread-out n (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">数据；的读取；读出<br><span class="en">a record or display of information on a computer screen</span></td><td class="c4">The computer will work out the best route for you and give you a <b>read-out</b> on the screen.<br>计算机会为你设计出最佳路线并显示在屏幕上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌread sth ˈthrough (also,read sth ˈover less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">通读(以便检查核对)<br><span class="en">to read sth from the beginning to the end, usually in order to find any mistakes</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>read through</b> my translation, checking for mistakes.<br>我把我的译文从头到尾校了一遍。<br>When she <b>read her letter through</b> the next day, she decided not to send it.<br>第二天她把信通读之后便决定不发了。<br>When she'd finished, Emily <b>read</b> <b>over</b> what she'd written.<br>她写完以后，埃米莉通读了一遍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrear sb/sth on sth</b></td><td class="c3">用…喂养；饲养；(以…)培育；娱乐<br><span class="en">to give a person or an animal a particular tye of food, entertainment, etc. when they are young</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas <b>reared on</b> jazz, but later discovered rock.<br>我是听爵士乐长大的，后来才接触到摇滚乐。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrear ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">马等用后腿支撑直立<br><span class="en">if a horse, etc. rears up, it stands on its back legs with its front legs in the air</span></td><td class="c4">The horse <b>reared up</b> and she fell off.<br>这匹马用后腿支撑直立起来，把她摔了下去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrear ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">楼房；峭壁等危立；陡立<br><span class="en">if a building, mountain, etc. rears up, it seems to lean over you in a threatening way</span></td><td class="c4">The cliff <b>reared up</b> before them.<br>在他们面前悬崖壁立。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reason</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌreason sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">推论；琢磨(原因)<br><span class="en">to think carefully about sth in a logical way in order to understand it</span></td><td class="c4">Let's try to <b>reason out</b> why he behaved as he did.<br>我们来想一想，他为什么会有这种行为。<br><b>Reason it out</b> for yourselfwhy do you think she didn't say where she was going?<br>你自己想想—你觉得她为什么不说她要上哪儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreason with sb</b></td><td class="c3">和某人讲道理；规劝<br><span class="en">to talk to sb in order to persuade them to be more sensible</span></td><td class="c4">It' impossible to <b>reason with</b> her when she's in this mood.<br>她情绪不好，不可能听得进劝告。<br>He can't be <b>reasoned with</b>.<br>他这人不可理喻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rebound</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈbound on sb (also reˈbound upon sb more formal, less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">反作用于；使反受其害；使搬起石头砸自己的脚<br><span class="en">if sth that you do, especially sth that is intended to be unpleasant for sb else, rebounds on you, it has an unpleasant effect for you instead</span></td><td class="c4">His trick seems to have <b>rebounded on</b> him.<br>他的伎俩似乎使他自食其果。<br>These measures could <b>rebound on</b> the poorest families (= affect them instead of the people they were intended affect).<br>这些措施反而会殃及那些最贫困的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reckon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sth<br>ˈreckon on sb/sth doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">指望；依赖；寄希望于<br><span class="en">to rely on sb/sth or on sth happening; to expect sb to do sth or sth to happen</span></td><td class="c4">We were <b>reckoning</b> on a profit of about half a million.<br>我们希望有大约50万的盈利。<br>You can <b>reckon</b> on my support.<br>你放心，我会支持你。<br>The company thought they would easily get permission to build a hotel, but they hadn't <b>reckoned</b> on the local people.<br>公司认为能轻而易举获得建造宾馆的许可，但他们并未寄希望于当地人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreckon with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于否定句<br><span class="en">usually used in negative sentences</span></td><td class="c4">Unfortunately, we hadnit <b>reckoned with</b> Emily.<br>可惜我们忘了考虑埃米莉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreckon with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">考虑；处理；应付对手；或问题<br><span class="en">to consider or deal with sb/sth as a serious opponent or problem</span></td><td class="c4">The team are still a force to be <b>reckoned with</b> (= they will be difficult to defeat).<br>该队依然不容小觑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreckon without sb/sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">没考虑到；预料到；没有顾及<br><span class="en">to not consider sb/sth as a possible problem and therefore not be prepared for it</span></td><td class="c4">We allowed an hour to get there, but we'd <b>reckoned without</b> the traffic.<br>我们原打算用一个小时赶到那里，但没考虑到交通状况。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reconcile</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreconcile sb/yourself to sth<br>ˈreconcile sb/yourself to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">无奈地接受；将就；顺从于<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself accept an unpleasant situation because nothing can be done to change it</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>reconciled</b> to the fact that he wouldn't be coming back.<br>他不会回来了，对此他们也无可奈何。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reduce</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈduce sb/sth to sth</b></td><td class="c3">使陷入(更糟的)境地；使陷入窘境<br><span class="en">to bring sb/sth to a particular state, especially a worse one</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>reduced to</b> tears by their criticism.<br>他们的批评使她落泪。<br>Her questioning <b>reduced him to</b> a state of confusion.<br>她的提问使他越听越糊涂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈduce sb to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">迫使某人做某事；使沦落到做某事的地步<br><span class="en">to make sb do sth they do not approve of or are ashamed of because there is no other choice for them</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>reduced</b> to borrowing money from friends.<br>我迫不得已向朋友借钱。总是用于被动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈduce sth to sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…简化为；将…概括成<br><span class="en">to change sth into a simpler or more general form</span></td><td class="c4">His arguments can be <b>reduced to</b> four points.<br>他的论据可以概括成四点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reek</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈreek of sth <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">散发(难闻的气味)<br><span class="en">to smell very strongly of sth unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">His breath <b>reeked of</b> tobacco.<br>他满嘴烟臭味。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reel sth ˈin/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">卷轴绕起；从卷轴上放开<br><span class="en">to wind sth on/off a reel</span></td><td class="c4">He slowly <b>reeled the fish in</b>.<br>他慢慢收卷钓线，把鱼钓上来。<br>The firefighters <b>reeled out</b> the hose.<br>消防队员放开了水龙软管。<br>The line caught on something in the water as he <b>reeled it in</b>.<br>他收绕钓线时钩到了水里的什么东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌreel sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">滔滔不绝地讲出；一口气说出<br><span class="en">to say a long list of things quickly and without having to think about it</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>reeled off</b> the names of the people he'd invited.<br>他一口气报出了他邀请的人的名字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>refer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈfer to sth</b></td><td class="c3">查阅；查询；参考<br><span class="en">to look at sth for information</span></td><td class="c4">You don't need to <b>refer to</b> a dictionary for this exercise.<br>做这个练习不必查词典。<br>It is important to provide a record that can be <b>referred to</b>.<br>提供可以查阅的记录十分重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈfer sb/sth to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…移交(或委托)…处理；让…去(找)<br><span class="en">to send sb/sth to a different place or person in order to get help, advice or a decision</span></td><td class="c4">The case was <b>referred to</b> the Court of Appeal.<br>该案已提交上诉法院审理。<br>My tutor <b>referred me to</b> a counsellor.<br>导师让我去找辅导员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reflect</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈflect on sb/sth also reˈflect upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">使对…有(某种看法)；反映<br><span class="en">to make sb have a particular opinion of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">When the department performs badly, it <b>reflects</b> on me as manager (= it makes people think I am a bad manager).<br>部门表现欠佳，我这个经理就会遭人非议。<br>This incident <b>reflects</b> badly on everyone involved.<br>这件事令所有当事人蒙羞。<br>When our students are successful it <b>reflects</b> well on the whole school.<br>如果我们的学生学业有成，整个学校也有光彩。<br>The young orchestra's performance <b>reflected</b> great credit on their training.<br>从青年管弦乐队的演出可以看出他们训练有素。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>regale</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈgale sb with sth</b></td><td class="c3">通过故事；笑话等愉悦(某人)<br><span class="en">to entertain sb with stories, jokes, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>regaling us with</b> tales of her youth.<br>她讲她年轻时的事，逗我们开心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rein</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrein sth ˈback less frequent</b></td><td class="c3">尤指简略地提及；谈起<br><span class="en">to pull on the reins of a horse = the leather bands that go mention sth/sb to write or speak about sth/sb, especially without giving much information</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>reined</b> in her horse and waited for John to catch up.<br>她勒住马等着约翰赶上来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>relate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>relˈate to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">理解并认同；谅解；体恤<br><span class="en">to feel that you can understand a person, a situation, sth that sb does or feels, etc. and have sympathy with them/it</span></td><td class="c4">She was unable to <b>relate to</b> her youngest child.<br>她没办法理解她最小的孩子。<br>I just couldn't <b>relate to</b> that movie at alL.<br>我根本无法欣赏那部电影。<br>She could <b>relate to</b> his feelings of guilt about his children.<br>她体谅他对自己孩子的愧疚感。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>relieve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈlieve sb of sth</b></td><td class="c3">替…做(难事或苦差)；减轻…的负担<br><span class="en">to carry out a difficult or unpleasant task for sb else, or instead of them</span></td><td class="c4">Robots can <b>relieve people of</b> dull and repetitive work.<br>机器人可以代做单调重复的工作。<br>Can I <b>relieve you of some of</b> your bags (= carry them for you)?<br>我帮你提几个包好吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈlieve sb of sth</b></td><td class="c3">偷取；抢走<br><span class="en">ironic to rob sb of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The thief <b>relieved him of</b> his wallet.<br>扒手偷走了他的钱包。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>remind</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈmind sb of sb/sth not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the ake sb back to make sb remember a time in not used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">When Clare smiled, she <b>reminded</b> me of her mother.<br>克莱尔的微笑让我回想起她的母亲。<br>Listening to her, he was <b>reminded</b> of Helen.<br>听着她的声音，他想起了海伦。<br>Watching his serious face, with its big round glasses, she was <b>reminded</b> of an owl.<br>看着他那又大又圆的眼镜和严肃的面孔，她想到了猫头鹰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>renege</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈnege on sth</b></td><td class="c3">违背；违反承诺；协定等<br><span class="en">to break a promise, an agreement, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Clarke claimed that she had <b>reneged on</b> her promise to marry him.<br>克拉克声称她违背了婚誓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rent</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrent sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">出租；租借(给某人)<br><span class="en">to allow sth that you own to be used by another person in retum for payment</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>rented the house out</b> to students.<br>他们把房子租给了学生。<br>Most of these houses are <b>rented out</b>.<br>这些房子大多租出去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>report</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈport to sb (business) not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>reports</b> directly to the chief executive.<br>她受总裁直接领导。<br>A new team will be put together for the project, <b>reporting</b> to me.<br>这个项目将组建一支新团队，由我负责。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>reside</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈside in sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在于；由…引起(或造成)<br><span class="en">to be in sb/sth; to be caused by sth</span></td><td class="c4">The attraction of the book <b>resides in</b> its illustrations.<br>这本书的魅力在于它的插图。<br>The interests of the child <b>reside in</b> getting the best possible education.<br>对孩子来说，其权益体现在能否得到尽可能好的教育。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈside in/with sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">存在于；隶属于；属于<br><span class="en">to be present in or belong to sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Supreme authority <b>resides with</b> the President.<br>最高权力属于总统。<br>Political power seems to <b>reside increasingly in</b> Brussels.<br>布鲁塞尔的政治力量似乎在不断增强。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>resign</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsign yourself to sth<br>reˈsign yourself to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">无奈；地接受；顺从于<br><span class="en">to be ready to accept sth unpleasant because you cannot avoid it</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>resigned herself to</b> her fate.<br>她听天由命。<br>They <b>resigned themselves to</b> being defeated.<br>他们只得认输了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>resolve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsolve into sth<br>reˈsolve sth into sth</b></td><td class="c3">分成；分解为(若干部分)<br><span class="en">to separate or to be separated into its parts</span></td><td class="c4">The design <b>resolved into</b> a number of different patterns.<br>设计图分成若干不同的图案。o a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsolve into sth<br>reˈsolve itself into sth</b></td><td class="c3">远处的景物或声音逐渐呈现为<br><span class="en">if sth you see or hear at a distance resolves into sth or resolves itself into sth, you gradually see it or hear it clearly as a particular thing</span></td><td class="c4">The grey shape <b>resolved into</b> a group of walkers.<br>灰影渐渐清晰起来，原来是一群徒步赶路的人。<br>The white light <b>resolved itself into</b> the headlights of a car.<br>白色亮光渐渐看得出来是一辆汽车的前灯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsolve into sth<br>reˈsolve itself into sth</b></td><td class="c3">逐步变成；逐渐被理解为<br><span class="en">to gradually become or be understood as sth</span></td><td class="c4">The discussion eventually <b>resolved itself into</b> two main issues.<br>讨论最终集中在两大主要议题上。<br>The questton <b>resolves itself into</b> whether individuals should be allowed to choose such a course of action.<br>问题逐步归结为是否应该允许个人选择这种做法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>resonate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈresonate with sth <span class="tag">(formal not usually used in the)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常不用于进行时</td><td class="c4">She makes a simple story <b>resonate with</b> complex themes and emotions.<br>她使一个简单的故事充满了复杂的主题和情感。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>resort</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsort to sth<br>reˈsort to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">常指迫不得已而诉之于；采取<br><span class="en">to make use of sth, especially sth bad or unpleasant, as a way of achieving sth, often because no other course of action is possible</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>resorted to bribery to</b> get what they wanted.<br>他们最后靠行贿达到目的。<br>Various measures were <b>resorted to</b>.<br>已采取了各种措施。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rest</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrest on sb/sth also ˈrest upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">寄托在…上<br><span class="en">to depend on sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Britain's hopes of a medal now <b>rest</b> on Henderson.<br>英国现在寄希望于享德森摘得奖牌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrest on sb/sth also ˈrest upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">视线落在…上<br><span class="en">if your eyes rest on sb/sth, you look at them/it</span></td><td class="c4">Her eyes <b>rested</b> on a photograph on the desk.<br>她的目光停留在桌上的一张照片上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrest on sth (also ˈrest upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">基于；以…为基础<br><span class="en">to be based on sth</span></td><td class="c4">His argument seemed to <b>rest on</b> a false assumption.<br>他的论点似乎建立在错误的假设之上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rest ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">因病或；因伤休息；养病；养伤<br><span class="en">to rest after an illness or injury</span></td><td class="c4">He was advised to <b>rest up</b> for a week after his fall.<br>他摔了一跤，要遵医嘱歇息一个星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rest ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">因病休养；为准备；比赛等养精蓄锐<br><span class="en">(espe cially ame) to rest in order to gain energy and strength, for example after an illness or before a sports competition</span></td><td class="c4">You should <b>rest up</b> if youre going to be fit for the game.<br>你要想以最佳状态参加比赛，就应该养养劲儿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrest with sb (to do sth) (formal) not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The decision <b>rests</b> entirely with you.<br>这个决定完全得由你来作。<br>The responsibility for bringing up children <b>rests</b> with the parents.<br>养育子女是父母的责任。<br>It <b>rests</b> with the bus company to prove they were not responsible for the accident.<br>公共汽车公司应当拿出证据证明他们对这一事故没有责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>result</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈsult in sth</b></td><td class="c3">产生(某种效果)；导致<br><span class="en">to have a particular effect; to make sth happen</span></td><td class="c4">The accident <b>resulted in</b> 67 deaths.<br>这场事故造成67 人死亡。<br>The agreement will <b>result in</b> employers working more closely with students and teachers.<br>协议将促成雇主和师生更加紧密地合作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>return</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈturn to sth</b></td><td class="c3">回复；恢复(先前的状态)<br><span class="en">to go back to a previous state</span></td><td class="c4">Train services have <b>returned to</b> normal after the strike.<br>罢工过后，铁路运营已恢复正常。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rev</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rev ˈup (for sth)<br>ˌrev sb/sth ˈup (for sth) <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">起来</td><td class="c4">It's his job to <b>rev</b> up the audience before the show starts.<br>他负责在表演开始前鼓动观众的情绪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>revel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrevel in sth<br>ˈrevel in doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">陶醉于；沉迷于；纵情于<br><span class="en">to enjoy a situation or an experience very much</span></td><td class="c4">I think he's secretly <b>revelling in</b> all the attention.<br>我觉得他对于能够引起广泛关注正暗自得意。<br>She seems to <b>revel in</b> annoying her parents.<br>她似乎以惹父母生气为乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>revert</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈvert to sb (law)</b></td><td class="c3">财产或土地<br><span class="en">of property and land</span></td><td class="c4">After his death the house <b>reverted to</b> its original owner.<br>他死后房子归还给了原先的主人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈvert to sth<br>reˈvert to doing sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">恢复；退回(尤指较差的状况)<br><span class="en">to go back to a previous condition or activity, especially a worse one</span></td><td class="c4">When the pressure is on, players <b>revert to</b> bad habits.<br>遇到压力，运动员就会恢复坏习惯。<br>After a good year the team <b>reverted to</b> type in their last game (= they played badly again).<br>该队的表现好了一年，上一场比赛中又故态复萌。<br>After 80 years as a school, the building has <b>reverted back to</b> being a house again.<br>这座建筑用作校舍 80年后又重新成为住宅。</td></tr>
