<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>revolve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>reˈvolve around sth (also reˈvolve round sth especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">绕…旋转<br><span class="en">to move around sth in a circle</span></td><td class="c4">The earth <b>revolves around</b> the Sun.<br>地球围绕太阳转动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rid</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrid sb/sth/yourself of sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">去除；清除；(使)摆脫<br><span class="en">to remove sth/sb unpleasant from a person, a place or an organization</span></td><td class="c4">The government pledged to <b>rid</b> the country of nuclear weapons.<br>政府承诺销毁本因的所有核武器。<br>How could she <b>rid</b> herself of Charles?<br>她怎样才能摆脱查尔斯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>riddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈriddle sb/sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">使布满；使遍布子弹或；窟窿<br><span class="en">to fill sb/sth with bullets or with holes</span></td><td class="c4">His body was <b>riddled with</b> bullets.<br>他被子弹打得体无完肤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈriddled with sth</b></td><td class="c3">充满；弥漫；充斥<br><span class="en">to be full of sth, especially sth unpleasant or bad</span></td><td class="c4">The whole organization <b>is riddled with</b> corruption.<br>整个组织从上到下腐败透顶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ride</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈride on sth usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">My whole future is <b>riding</b> on this interview.<br>我的未来全押在这场面试上。<br>There's a lot of money <b>riding</b> on this deal.<br>这宗交易关系到一大笔钱。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌride sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">安然疲过(难关)；经受住<br><span class="en">to manage to survive a difficult period or situation without suffering serious harm</span></td><td class="c4">Do you think the president will be able to <b>ride out</b> this latest crisis?<br>你认为总统能挺过最近这次危机吗。<br>Of course your parents were angry, but you should have stayed to <b>ride out</b> the storm.<br>你父母当然生气，但你应当留下来挨过那一刻的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌride ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">衣服慢慢向上移；渐渐缩上去<br><span class="en">if an item of clothing rides up, it gradually moves upwards, out of position</span></td><td class="c4">His waistcoat was <b>riding up</b> over his stomach.<br>他的西装背心缩到腹部以上了。<br>My skirt tends to <b>ride up</b>.<br>我的裙子老是向上拱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rifle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rifle ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">迅速搜寻；匆忙翻找<br><span class="en">to search quickly through sth such as drawers, cupboards or papers, in order to find or steal sth</span></td><td class="c4">Sally <b>rifled through</b> her wardrobe looking for something to wear.<br>萨莉翻腾着衣柜找穿的。<br>The room looked as if a burglar had <b>rifled through</b> it.<br>房间看上去像遭过劫似的。<br>The drawers had been <b>rifled through</b>.<br>有人翻检过抽屉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rig</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrig sb/sth ˈout (in/with sth) <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为…提供(衣服或设备)<br><span class="en">to provide sb/sth with clothes or equipment</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>rigged them out</b> from top to bottom (= bought them new etc.).<br>我们给他们从头到脚穿戴一新。<br>The ship had been <b>rigged out</b> with state-of-the-art equipment.<br>这艘轮船安装了最先进的设备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrig-out n <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一套服装；全套服饰；装束</td><td class="c4">Where are you going in that <b>rig-out</b>?<br>你穿了那身衣服去哪儿啊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrig sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">安装；装配<br><span class="en">to fix a piece of equipment into place</span></td><td class="c4">Weve <b>rigged up</b> lights in the garden for the party.<br>为开晚会我们在花园里安了灯。<br>He was <b>rigged up</b> to a machine so that the nurses could check his heartbeat.<br>他身上连接了机器，让护士检查心跳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrig sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用现有材料匆匆做成；草草搭建<br><span class="en">to make or build sth quickly, using whatever materials are available</span></td><td class="c4">He had <b>rigged up</b> a sort of tent, using his jacket and shirt.<br>他用夹克衫和衬衣匆忙搭了个帐篷样的东西。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ring</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌring ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">往工作单位打电话<br><span class="en">to telephone the place where you work</span></td><td class="c4">The boss <b>rings in</b> several times a day, even when he's on holiday.<br>老板一天打几次电话过来，即使他休假也不例外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌring ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给电台节目等打电话<br><span class="en">to telephone a radio programme, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Listeners were asked to <b>ring in</b> with their opinions.<br>电台欢迎听众拨打电话发表意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ring ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">挂断电话</td><td class="c4">He rang <b>off</b> before I could explain.<br>我还没来得及解释他就把电话挂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌring ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">清脆；响亮；发出响声<br><span class="en">to be heard loudly and clearly</span></td><td class="c4">His clear voice rang <b>out</b> across the hall.<br>他清脆的嗓音响彻大厅。<br>Suddenly shots rang <b>out</b> nearby.<br>附近突然响起一阵枪声。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌring ˈthrough (to sb/sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给同一楼内的人打电话<br><span class="en">to make a telephone call to sb, especially within the same building</span></td><td class="c4">Reception rang <b>through</b> to say my visitor had arrived.<br>服务台打来电话说我的客人到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rinse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrinse sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">冲洗；洗刷干净<br><span class="en">to make sth clean by washing it in water</span></td><td class="c4">Ruth finished her coffee and <b>rinsed out</b> her cup under the tap.<br>鲁思喝完咖啡就到水龙头前把杯子冲洗干净。<br><b>Rinse your mouth out</b> to get rid of the taste.<br>漱漱口，去去嘴里的味道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrinse sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把(肥皂等)冲掉；漂洗<br><span class="en">(also ˌrinse sth ˈout of sth) to remove sth such as soap from sth else with water</span></td><td class="c4">Leave the conditioner on your hair for three minutes and then <b>rinse it out</b>.<br>让护发素在头发上留三分钟，然后冲洗干净。n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rip sb/sth aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">痛斥；抨击<br><span class="en">to criticize sb/sth very severely</span></td><td class="c4">After she'd gone, we <b>ripped her apart</b>.<br>她走后，我们把她大骂了一通。<br>My tutor <b>ripped my essay apart</b>.<br>导师把我的文章批驳得一无是处。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rip sth aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">完全摧毁；全部毁掉<br><span class="en">to destroy sth completely</span></td><td class="c4">The hooligans had <b>ripped the place apart</b>.<br>那伙流氓把这个地方全毁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrip at sth</b></td><td class="c3">猛烈撕扯；用力割<br><span class="en">to attack sth violently and tear it or cut it</span></td><td class="c4">The bird <b>ripped at</b> its rival's throat.<br>那只鸟猛啄对手的喉咙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrip ˈinto sb/sth (with sth) (for sth/for doing sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因…怒骂；呵斥<br><span class="en">to criticize sb in an angry way for sth they have done or said</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ripped into</b> me for being late.<br>他因为我迟到而训了我一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rip ˈinto/through sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">猛地钻入；穿透<br><span class="en">to go very quickly or violently into or through sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">An explosion <b>ripped through</b> a four-storey apartment building.<br>剧烈的爆炸穿透了一座四层公寓楼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rip sb ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以劣质品等欺骗；敲…竹杠；宰(客)<br><span class="en">to cheat sb, for example by charging them too much for sth, selling them sth of poor quality, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The tickets were very expensive. We felt we'd been <b>ripped off</b>.<br>票价很贵。我们觉得被宰了。<br>The law protects tenants from being <b>ripped off</b> by landlords.<br>法律保障租户免受房东欺诈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rip sb/sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">抄袭；盗版；仿冒<br><span class="en">to copy sb/sth, by stealing ideas, designs, etc. especially in order to make money for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">Another band has <b>ripped</b> of our song.<br>另一支乐队剽窃了我们的歌曲。<br>She was accused of <b>ripping off</b> other people's ideas.<br>她被控抄袭他人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrip-off</b></td><td class="c3">山寨产品；盗版产品；冒牌货；仿制品</td><td class="c4">He has a stall that sells designer <b>rip-offs</b> (= clothes).<br>他开了个店铺，卖仿冒品牌服装。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrip sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">偷窃；盗取<br><span class="en">to steal sth</span></td><td class="c4">Thieves broke in and <b>ripped off</b> five computers.<br>盗贼破门而入，偷走了五台计算机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrip-off n <span class="tag">(informal an)</span></b></td><td class="c3">盗窃；偷盜盗<br><span class="en">act of stealing sth</span></td><td class="c4">It was a scandalous <b>rip-off</b> of public funds.<br>那是一起盗用公款的丑闻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rip sth ˈoff<br>rip sth ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">猛地拉下(或拽下)；迅速；脱下<br><span class="en">to remove sth, especially clothing, very quickly by pulling sharply</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>ripped the poster off</b> the wall.<br>她把海报从墻上一把扯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrip on sb <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">嘲笑；开…的玩笑；拿…寻开心<br><span class="en">to laugh at sb or make jokes about them</span></td><td class="c4">My buddies were <b>ripping on</b> me about a poem I had written.<br>朋友们拿我写的一首诗取笑我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rise</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrise aˈbove sth</b></td><td class="c3">不受…影响(或局限)；克服；超越<br><span class="en">to not be affected Or limited by problems, insults, etc.; to be able to deal with problems</span></td><td class="c4">She was able to <b>rise above</b> her disability.<br>她战胜了自身的残疾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrise aˈbove sth</b></td><td class="c3">不为…所；高出；超脱于(常人)<br><span class="en">to be too wise or good to do sth wrong or to think or behave in the way other people do</span></td><td class="c4">He had an unusual ability to <b>rise above</b> the prejudices of his generation.<br>他能力超群，能够摆脱同代人所持的偏见。<br>There will always be gossip. You have to try and <b>rise above</b> it.<br>流言蜚语总会有。你必须尽量置之不理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrise aˈbove sth</b></td><td class="c3">超出(同类事物)；出类拔萃<br><span class="en">to be better than other</span></td><td class="c4">Her articles never <b>rise above</b> the level of a gossip column.<br>她的文章从未超出过八卦专栏的水准。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrise to sth</b></td><td class="c3">成功应对非常情况；突发问题等<br><span class="en">to deal successfully with a situation or problem that you do not expect or do not usually have to face</span></td><td class="c4">The job wasn't easy but Sam was ready to <b>rise to</b> the challenge.<br>那份工作并不轻松，可萨姆愿意迎接挑战。<br>The play was a challenge for the actors but they <b>rose to</b> the occasion.<br>这部戏对演员是个挑战，但他们应付裕如。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrise to sth</b></td><td class="c3">上当；中圈套；入陷阱<br><span class="en">to react when sb is deliberately trying to make you angry or get you interested in sth</span></td><td class="c4">I refuse to <b>rise to</b> that sort of comment.<br>对此类言论，我拒绝置评。<br>I decided to flatter him and he <b>rose to</b> the bait (= he reacted in the way that I wanted).<br>我决定奉承他一番，结果他上钩了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrise ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">反抗；起义；反叛<br><span class="en">(against sb/sth) (formal) to start to fight against or refuse to obey people in authority, for example a government or king</span></td><td class="c4">The people <b>rose up</b> against the invaders.<br>人们起来抗击侵略者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈuprising n</b></td><td class="c3">起义；暴动；造反<br><span class="en">a situation in which a group of people join together to fight against or to refuse to obey people in authority</span></td><td class="c4">The <b>uprising</b> was ruthlessly suppressed.<br>起义被残酷镇压下去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>roll</b></td><td class="c2"><b>roll sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">展开；铺开；摊开(卷起之物)<br><span class="en">to open out a piece of clothing, etc. that has been folded over and over</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>rolled down</b> her sleeves and buttoned the cuffs.<br>她放下衣袖，扣上袖口的纽扣。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">时间</td><td class="c4">As the years <b>rolled on</b> the painful memories began to fade.<br>光阴荏苒，痛苦的回忆开始被淡忘。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续进行；持续不变<br><span class="en">to continue without changing very much</span></td><td class="c4">For the next few weeks the debate <b>rolled on</b>.<br>在随后的几周里，争论仍在继续。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll sb/sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">动员；动用<br><span class="en">to use sb/sth to help you achieve sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rolled out</b> all his old friends to help him win the election.<br>他发动了所有的老友故交来帮他贏得选举。<br>The circus <b>rolled out</b> bears to announce its arrival.<br>马戏团以狗熊表演拉开了演出序幕。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">将…轧平；把…辗薄<br><span class="en">to make a substance flat and thin by rolling sth over it</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Roll out</b> the pastry with a clean rolling pin.<br>用干净的擀面杖把油酥面团擀平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈover <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不作抵抗；轻易认输；東手就擒<br><span class="en">to be easily defeated without even trying</span></td><td class="c4">We can't expect them to just <b>roll over</b> for us.<br>我们不能指望他们向我们举手投降。<br>They thought the unions would <b>roll over</b>.<br>他们认为工会会坐等失败。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈover<br>ˌroll sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">车船等<br><span class="en">of a vehicle, a boat, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>rolled over</b> into a ditch.<br>汽车翻进了沟里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈover sth (computing)</b></td><td class="c3">滑动鼠标至(屏幕某处)<br><span class="en">to move a computer mouse so that you point to a particular area on the screen</span></td><td class="c4">When you <b>roll over</b> these hot spots, they change colour.<br>移动鼠标指向这些热点，它们会变色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>roll sb ˈover <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻松击败<br><span class="en">to defeat sb easily</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>rolled us over</b> in the replay.<br>他们在重赛中轻而易举地打败了我们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">准许；延期偿还；将(债务)转期<br><span class="en">(finance) to allow money that sb owes to be paid at a later date</span></td><td class="c4">The government agreed to <b>roll over</b> the debt.<br>政府批准将债务展期。B。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">悠闲自在地到达；不打招呼来到<br><span class="en">to arrive, especially in a relaxed way or without giving advance warning</span></td><td class="c4">He finally <b>rolled up</b> an hour late.<br>他最后迟到了一小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈroll-up n <span class="tag">(BrE informal a)</span></b></td><td class="c3">自制的烟卷；卷烟</td><td class="c4">Simon lit a <b>roll-up</b>.<br>西蒙点了根烟卷。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroll sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">击败；占…的上风<br><span class="en">to defeat or gain an advantage against a group of enemy soldiers, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Counter-intelligence services <b>rolled up</b> many of Moscow's spy networks.<br>反情报机构捣毁了莫斯科的多个间谍网。<br>Numerous terrorist cells have been <b>rolled up</b>.<br>众多恐怖分子的基层组织被破获。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>romp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌromp aˈhead/aˈway <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">进步神速；快速增加；轻易获胜<br><span class="en">make to progress, increase or win quickly and easily</span></td><td class="c4">The home team <b>romped away</b> to win by three goals.<br>主队轻而易举地以三分取胜。这个动词主要用于报章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌromp ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易而快速地做<br><span class="en">to do sth easily and quickly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>romped through</b> the exam questions.<br>她轻松答完了考试题。这个动词主要用于报章。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>root</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sth (BrE also ˌroot aˈbout, ˌroot aˈbout sth) (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">翻找；搜寻<br><span class="en">to move things around to try to find sth</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>rooting</b> around in the drawer for his keys.<br>他翻抽屉找他的钥匙。<br>Someone had been <b>rooting</b> through the rubbish.<br>有人一直在垃圾堆里翻来翻去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌroot sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">肃清；铲除；根除<br><span class="en">to find the person or thing that is causing a problem and remove or gqet rid of them/it</span></td><td class="c4">The government has promised to <b>root out</b> police corruption.<br>政府承诺要杜绝警务人员腐败。<br>The troublemakers seem to have been <b>rooted out</b>.<br>惹是生非的人似乎都已被揪出来了。8J。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrot aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐腐烂<br><span class="en">to gradually decay</span></td><td class="c4">The window frame had <b>rotted away</b>.<br>窗框已经烂了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rough</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrough sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">画…的草图；草拟<br><span class="en">to draw or write the main parts of sth without including all the details</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>roughed out</b> the design on the back of an envelope.<br>她在信封背面勾画设计草图。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>round</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈround on sb</b></td><td class="c3">突然责骂；突然指责；突然攻击<br><span class="en">to suddenly speak angrily to sb and criticize or attack them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rounded on</b> her angrily and told her to keep her mouth shut.<br>他突然怒气冲冲地呵斥她，并让她闭嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rub</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rub aˈgainst sb/sth<br>ˌrub ˈup against sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">动物在六上蹭<br><span class="en">if an animal rubs (up) against sb/sth, it moves backwards and forwards and presses itself against them/it</span></td><td class="c4">The cat <b>rubbed</b> (up) <b>against</b> her.<br>猫在她身上蹭来蹭去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrub sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用专用的纸等将…打磨光滑<br><span class="en">to make the surface of sth smooth by rubbing it with special paper, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rubbed the woodwork down</b> with sandpaper.<br>他用砂纸把木制品打磨光滑。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>rub sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">提及(令人尴尬或愧疚的事)；触及(痛处)；揭开(伤疤)<br><span class="en">to say sth to sb which reminds them of sth that they feel embarrassed or gquilty about and would like to forget</span></td><td class="c4">I already know it was my fault-there's no need to <b>rub it in</b>.<br>我早知道是我错了——没必要再提了。<br>Was he trying to <b>rub in</b> the fact that he didn't like me?<br>他是不是还想说他不喜欢我？c。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrub ˈoff (on/onto sb)</b></td><td class="c3">良好品质等感染；传给<br><span class="en">if sth, such as a good quality that sb has, rubs off onto you, you gain some of that quality by spending time with the person</span></td><td class="c4">Let's hope some of his good luck <b>rubs off</b> on me!<br>希望他的好运能分给我一些吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrub ˈoff<br>ˌrub sth ˈoff<br>ˌrub sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">被擦掉；抹掉<br><span class="en">to be removed from sth by rubbing; to remove sth from sth by rubbing</span></td><td class="c4">Somebody's used the wrong kind of pen on the whiteboard and it won't <b>rub off</b>.<br>有人在白色书写板上用错了笔，擦不掉了。<br>He quickly <b>rubbed the mud off</b> his face.<br>他迅速擦掉了脸上的泥。+ n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrub sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">千掉；除掉<br><span class="en">to murder sb</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>rubbed out</b> before he could talk.<br>他还没来得及开口说话就被人杀了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrub sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">擦掉(字迹等)<br><span class="en">to remove the marks made by a pen, pencil, etc. from a piece of Paper, a board, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Draw the outline with a soft pencil, so that you can <b>rub it out</b> later.<br>用软芯铅笔勾画轮廓，便于以后擦去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ruck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌruck ˈup<br>ˌruck sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使起皱褶<br><span class="en">to form untidy folds; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">Your blouse has <b>rucked up</b> at the back.<br>你的衬衫后面起褶儿了。<br>Her Skirt was <b>rucked up</b>.<br>她的裙子皱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rule</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrule sth ˈin<br>ˌrule sth ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">认为…有可能；发生<br><span class="en">if sb rules sth in, they decide that it is possible, or that it can or should happen</span></td><td class="c4">He asked for all possible results to be <b>ruled into</b> the discussions.<br>他要求讨论时要考虑到所有可能出现的结果。<br>The producer <b>ruled</b> out an older actress for the role.<br>制片人认为年长的女演员不适合该角色。<br>Ramsay has been <b>ruled</b> out as too old for the job.<br>拉姆齐被认为年纪太大，不适合做那份。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrule sth ˈin<br>ˌrule sth ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(某人)被排除；使(某人)不适合<br><span class="en">if sth rules sb out, it makes it impossible for sb to have done sth or to do sth, or makes them not suitable for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Several people saw her at the restaurant at 9.00 p.m. so that seems to <b>rule</b> her out as the murderer.<br>有几个人晚上9点在饭店见过她，因此似乎排除了她是区手的可能性。<br>Beckham has been <b>ruled</b> out of tonight's game with a knee injury.<br>贝克汉姆因膝部受伤不可能参加今晚的比赛了。<br>I wouldn't <b>rule</b> anything out.<br>我不会排除任何可能性。<br>Detectives have not <b>ruled</b> out the possibility that she was abducted.<br>探员们尚未排除她被绑架的可能性。<br>Paris has been <b>ruled</b> out as the site for the next Olympics.<br>巴黎已经没有可能成为下届奥运会的主办地了。<br>Sabotage was <b>ruled</b> out of the investigation.<br>蓄意破坏未列入本次调查。<br>The size of the house <b>ruled</b> it out as a family home.<br>房子太小，住不下一家人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrule yourself ˈout<br>ˌrule yourself ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">认为自己不想做或没有能力；不适合<br><span class="en">to decide you do not want to or are not able to do sth; to decide that you are not suitable for sth</span></td><td class="c4">Smith has not <b>ruled himself out</b> of Saturday's game.<br>史密斯并未排除自己参加星期六比赛的可能性。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rumble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrumble ˈon <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">辩论；争执等拖得很长；拖拖拉拉<br><span class="en">if an argument, a disagreement, etc. rumbles on, it continues slowly and steadily for much longer than it should</span></td><td class="c4">The dispute <b>rumbled on</b> through the summer.<br>整个夏天都在没完没了地争论。<br>The row has been <b>rumbling on</b> for two years.<br>争吵已经持续两年之久。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>run</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈcross sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">偶然遇见；碰巧发现<br><span class="en">to meet sb or find sth by chance</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>ran across</b> Mary in town yesterday.<br>我昨天在城里巧遇玛丽。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈbout/round<br>ˌrun aˈbout/ˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">兴奋地各处跑；东奔西跑<br><span class="en">to run in different directions, especially in an excited way</span></td><td class="c4">It's a lovely park to <b>run</b> around in.<br>这个公园不错，可以在里面四处跑跑。<br>The children were <b>running</b> <b>round</b> the house with no clothes on.<br>孩子们光着身子在房子里跑来跑去。<br>They stopped the car to let the dogs <b>run</b> <b>about</b>.<br>他们停车让狗下去遛選。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈbout/round<br>ˌrun aˈbout/ˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">奔走忙碌；疲于奔命<br><span class="en">to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy</span></td><td class="c4">He's been <b>running</b> <b>about</b> the place organizing the party.<br>他一直在这里四处奔走组织聚会。<br>He's had the police <b>running</b> around in circles (= being very busy but not achieving anything).<br>他搞得警察四处扑空。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈround after sb (BrE also,run ˈround after sb)</b></td><td class="c3">替…做其力所能及的事；替…忙活<br><span class="en">to be very busy doing a lot of things for sb, when they should be able to do them for themselves</span></td><td class="c4">His mother shouldn't have to <b>run around after</b> him.<br>他的母亲不该替他忙活。<br>She spends all her time <b>running</b> <b>round</b> <b>after</b> the children.<br>她所有的时间都花在为孩子瞎忙活上了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>run aˈround with sb <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…厮混；和…泡；在一块儿<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of time with sb</span></td><td class="c4">Their son is <b>running around with</b> a bad crowd.<br>他们的儿子与一帮环人混在一起。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun at sb</b></td><td class="c3">冲过去袭击；冲向<br><span class="en">to run towards sb to attack them or as if you were going to attack them</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ran at</b> me with a knife.<br>他拿着刀朝我冲过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun at sth often</b></td><td class="c3">常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Inflation is <b>running</b> at 26%.<br>通货膨胀率为 26%。<br>Interest rates were <b>running</b> at record levels.<br>利率接近历史最高水平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>run aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">迅速离开；逃离<br><span class="en">(from sb/sth) to move quickly away from sb/a place; to escape from sb/a place</span></td><td class="c4">A man was seen <b>running away</b> from the shop.<br>有人看见一名男子从商店里跑了出去。<br>His first instinct was to <b>run away</b>.<br>他的本能反应就是逃走。+。<br>He <b>ran away</b> and joined a circus.<br>他离家出走后进了马戏团。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>run aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">用于命令儿童走开；别捣乱<br><span class="en">used to tell a child to go away and not disturb you</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Run away</b> and play.<br>一边玩儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈway/off together</b></td><td class="c3">与某人私奔<br><span class="en">to leave your home, husband, wife, etc. secretly with sb else in order to marry them or have a sexual relationship with them</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>ran</b> <b>away</b> to Scotland.<br>他们私奔到了苏格兰。<br>We think John and Susie have <b>run off together</b>.<br>我们认为约翰和苏茜一起私奔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">逃避；回避(困难等)<br><span class="en">to try to avoid dealing with or thinking about sth because it is difficult or unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">He is <b>running away from</b> his responsibilities.<br>他在逃避责任。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈway with sth</b></td><td class="c3">轻松贏得<br><span class="en">to win sth clearly or easily</span></td><td class="c4">Their team are <b>running away with</b> the championship.<br>他们队即将轻松获得冠军。<br>She <b>ran away with</b> the show (= she was easily the best performer).<br>她轻而易举地当选最佳演员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun aˈway with sth</b></td><td class="c3">偷走；未经允许拿走；携…潜逃<br><span class="en">(also ˌrun ˈoff with sth) to escape with sth that you have stolen or taken without asking</span></td><td class="c4">The treasurer <b>ran away with</b> all the funds.<br>出纳携带所有资金潜逃了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>run ˈdown<br>.run sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使耗尽能量；停止工作<br><span class="en">to lose power or stop working; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">Oil supplies in the region will start to <b>run down</b> in the next decade.<br>未来十年内这个地区的石油资源将开始枯竭。<br>Businesses in the town have been allowed to run down during the last <b>few</b> years.<br>在过去几年，该市的商业机构被压缩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈdown sth<br>ˌrun sth ˈdown sth</b></td><td class="c3">快速浏览；迅速读出<br><span class="en">to look quickly at a list; to quickly read and mention the items on it</span></td><td class="c4">Her eyes <b>ran down</b> the figures on the page.<br>她快速浏览了一下这一页上的数字。<br>She <b>ran her eyes down</b> the page.<br>她匆匆扫了一眼这一页。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈdown sth<br>ˌrun sth ˈdown sth</b></td><td class="c3">使沿…向下移动<br><span class="en">to pass, or to make sth pass, downwards over</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>ran her finger down</b> the page.<br>她用手指往下点着浏览了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或司机<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or its driver</span></td><td class="c4">The cyclist was <b>run down</b> by a lorry.<br>骑自行车的人被一辆货车撞倒了。<br>You nearly <b>ran down</b> that pedestrian.<br>你差点撞了那个行人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun yourself ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">过分自责；妄自非薄<br><span class="en">to criticize yourself, often unfairly</span></td><td class="c4">Youre always <b>running yourself down</b>!<br>你总是自轻自贱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun sb ˈin <span class="tag">(old-fashioned informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把某人扭送警察局<br><span class="en">to arrest sb and take them to a police station</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>run in</b> for shoplifting.<br>她因为在商店里偷东西被抓到局子里去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈinto sb</b></td><td class="c3">偶然退见；碰到(某人)<br><span class="en">to meet sb by chance</span></td><td class="c4">Guess who I <b>ran into</b> today?<br>猜猜我今天碰见谁了。<br>You rarely <b>run into</b> people you know in London.<br>在伦敦很难撞见熟人。<br>The lory behind <b>ran into</b> the back of me (= my car).<br>后面的货车追尾撞了我的车。<br>He <b>ran his car into</b> a tree.<br>他开车撞到了树上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速离开；逃离<br><span class="en">to move quickly away from sb/a place; to escape from sb/a place</span></td><td class="c4">The thief <b>ran off</b> down a side street.<br>小偷从小巷逃跑了。<br>They <b>ran off</b> laughing.<br>他们笑着跑开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈoff<br>ˌrun ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">道路等从…通出；从…开出<br><span class="en">if a road, path, etc. runs off or runs off a place, it leads away</span></td><td class="c4">Can you see that road <b>running off</b> to the right?<br>看到通向右边的那条路了吧。<br>Several doors <b>ran off</b> the corridor.<br>走廊上开了几道门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈoff sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…流出<br><span class="en">to flow away from sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Water <b>runs off</b> the fields into the valley.<br>水从田野流进峡谷。<br>Sweat was <b>running off</b> her.<br>她汗流浃背。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈoff sth<br>ˌrun sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">机器等<br><span class="en">of a machine, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The outboard motor <b>runs off</b> an ordinary car battery.<br>舷外发动机以一个普通汽车蓄电池来推动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">用机器复印；复制<br><span class="en">to produce copies of a piece of writing, etc. on a machine</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>ran off</b> hundreds of copies of the leaflet.<br>他们复印了几百张传单。<br>Can you <b>run these letters off</b> for me?<br>帮我把这些信件复印出来好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速流畅地写出；一气呵成<br><span class="en">to produce sth that is usually difficult to write, such as a poem, speech, etc. quickly and easily</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>ran off</b> a fantastic speech in no time at all.<br>她转眼间就写好了一份精彩的演讲稿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">没完没了地唠叨；不停地啰唆<br><span class="en">(about sth) (especially ame) to continue talking for a long time about unimportant things</span></td><td class="c4">She does tend to <b>run on</b>!<br>她真能唠叨。<br>She <b>ran on</b> with great enthusiasm about her latest project.<br>她喋喋不休地大谈特谈她的最新课题。4 +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">文字的一行接排；不分段<br><span class="en">(of a line of text) to continue into the next line</span></td><td class="c4">This line <b>runs on</b> into the next verse of the poem.<br>这一行接下一个诗节。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>gˈrun on sth<br>ˈrun sth on sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…为动力<br><span class="en">to use a particular type of power or fuel to make a machine or a vehicle work</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>run the car on</b> any type of unleaded petrol.<br>这辆车可使用任何类型的无铅汽油做燃料。+。<br>We have to eat quickly as time is <b>running</b> out.<br>时间不多了，我们必须快点吃。<br>One day his luck will <b>run</b> out.<br>总有一天他会不再这么走运。<br>My patience with her suddenly <b>ran</b> out.<br>我突然对她失去了耐心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈout on sb</b></td><td class="c3">弃…而去；拋弃<br><span class="en">to leave sb that you live or work with, especially when they need your help</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>ran out on</b> him soon as things got difficult.<br>情况一变得艰难，她就离他而去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">溢出；流出<br><span class="en">if a container or the liquid in it runs over, the liquid flows out of it over the edge</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let the bath <b>run over</b>!<br>别让浴缸的水漫出来。<br>The tea <b>ran over</b> into the saucer.<br>茶水溢到了茶碟上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈover sb/sth<br>ˌrun sth ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使在…表面经过<br><span class="en">to move over a surface; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">I let the cold water <b>run over</b> me.<br>我让凉水淋到身上。<br>She <b>ran her eye over</b> the figures on the page.<br>她浏览了一下那一页上的数字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">快速兇读(或思索)；练习<br><span class="en">to read through or think about sth quickly; to practise sth</span></td><td class="c4">Let's <b>run over</b> the plans again.<br>我们再把计划快速过一遍吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f,run sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或司机<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or its driver</span></td><td class="c4">Two children were run <b>over</b> by a truck and killed.<br>两名儿童被一辆卡车轧死了。<br>I ran <b>over</b> a cat last night.<br>我昨晚轧了一只猫。<br>You nearly ran me <b>over</b>!<br>你差点轧了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>run ˈthrough sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">感觉迅速传遍；快速穿过<br><span class="en">if a feeling runs run through sth to be present in every through sb/sth, it passes quickly through them/it</span></td><td class="c4">A thrill of excitement <b>ran through</b> her.<br>一阵兴奋传遍了她的全身。<br>She felt a tremor <b>run through</b> his body.<br>她感到他全身一阵颤抖。<br>An angry murmur <b>ran through</b> the crowd.<br>愤怒的抱怨声在人群中迅速蔓延。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>run ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">遍布<br><span class="en">to be present in every part of sth</span></td><td class="c4">There is a common theme <b>running through</b> all of her novels.<br>一个共同主题贯穿她所有的小说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>run ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">匆匆讨论(或检查)；快速阅读<br><span class="en">to discuss, examine or read sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>ran through</b> his list one more time.<br>他又浏览了一遍清单。<br>Can you <b>run through</b> some of these figures with me?<br>和我一起核对一下这里的一些数据好吗。<br>She mentally <b>ran through</b> the list of who to invite.<br>她在脑子里匆匆过了一遍邀请来宾的名单。<br>Let's <b>run through</b> what I'm meant to do again.<br>咱们再来简要讨论一下我要做的事吧。g0。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun-through n</b></td><td class="c3">从头至尾的排练；试演；预演</td><td class="c4">Were having the main technical <b>run-through</b> of the play tonight.<br>我们今晚进行这部戏的主要技术排练。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun to sb</b></td><td class="c3">找某人寻求帮助；建议；保护<br><span class="en">to go to sb for help, advice, protection, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">If you get hurt, don't come <b>running to</b> me.<br>你要是受伤了，可别来找我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun to sth</b></td><td class="c3">达到某一；较大的数量或规模<br><span class="en">to reach the amount, or size mentioned, especially a large one</span></td><td class="c4">The total cost <b>runs to</b> hundreds of pounds.<br>全部费用高达数百英镑。<br>The report already <b>runs to</b> 800 pages.<br>报告已经长达800页。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun to sth</b></td><td class="c3">常与<br><span class="en">often used in negative sentences and with can</span></td><td class="c4">We couldn't quite <b>run to</b> private education for the children.<br>我们的钱不太够让孩子们接受私立学校教育。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun to sth</b></td><td class="c3">喜好；能做<br><span class="en">if your taste or your mind, etc. runs to sth, you enjoy it or can do it</span></td><td class="c4">His taste in music <b>runs to</b> pop and jazz, but that's about it.<br>他喜爱流行乐和爵士乐，但也就听听而已。1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrun ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增长；增加<br><span class="en">to increase</span></td><td class="c4">Product prices have <b>run up</b> faster than expected.<br>产品涨价的速度出乎预料。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun-up n <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">助跑；距离<br><span class="en">(sport) the act of running or the distance you run in order to gain speed before you throw a ball, jump, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She took a <b>run-up</b> and kicked the ball.<br>她助跑踢球。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun-up n <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">重大活动的准备阶段；酝酿期<br><span class="en">(also ˈrun-in less frequent) (to sth) the period of preparation before an important event</span></td><td class="c4">She's been training hard in the <b>run-up</b> to the big competition.<br>她在大赛开始前的这段时间里刻苦训练。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>run sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">积欠；累积账单；债务<br><span class="en">to allow a bill, debt, etc. to reach a large total</span></td><td class="c4">Could you <b>run me up</b> some curtains/run me some curtains up?<br>请帮我赶制几块窗帘好吗？'3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>run ˈup against sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">遭遇；经历(困难或问题)<br><span class="en">to experience a run with sth to accept or start to use a rush /raj/ run ˈup against sb/sth to experience a run with sb →</span></td><td class="c4">The project keeps <b>running up against</b> the problem of lack of funds.<br>这个项目接二连三地遭遇资金短鉠问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈrun with sth</b></td><td class="c3">接受；采纳主意或；方法<br><span class="en">to accept or start to use a Particular idea or method</span></td><td class="c4">OK, let's <b>run with</b> Jan's suggestion.<br>好吧，我们就采用简的建议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rush</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush aˈround<br>.rush aˈround sth (BrE also, rush aˈbout/ˈround,,rush aˈbout/ˈround sth)</b></td><td class="c3">奔走忙碌；疲于奔命<br><span class="en">to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>rushed</b> <b>about</b> the room tidying.<br>他跑来跑去忙着收拾房间。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">贸然行事；仓促决定<br><span class="en">to do or decide sth very quickly, often without thinking about it for long enough</span></td><td class="c4">He's very wary of <b>rushing in</b> and making changes.<br>他十分谨慎，不愿轻率作出改变。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush ˈinto sth<br>ˌrush ˈinto doing sth<br>ˌrush sb ˈinto doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">使贸然行事；仓促决定<br><span class="en">to do or decide sth quickly without thinking about it carefully; to make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">Don't go <b>rushing into</b> anything.<br>不要贸然行事。<br>You shouldn't <b>rush into</b> getting married.<br>你不应当草率结婚。<br>She won't be <b>rushed into</b> a decision.<br>她不会受外界影响而轻率作出决定。<br>Dont let anyone <b>rush you into</b> accepting the job.<br>不要受任何人的影响以致冒冒失失接受那份。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速离开<br><span class="en">to leave quickly</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>rush off</b>, I haven't finished.<br>别忙着走，我还没弄完呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">匆忙生产；赶制<br><span class="en">to produce sth very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>rushed out</b> the posters in time for the festival.<br>他们及时为庆祝活动赶制出了海报。<br>The book was <b>rushed out</b> by the publishers.<br>出版商仓促付印了这本书。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌrush sth ˈthrough<br>ˌrush sth ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">快速通过(法规等)<br><span class="en">to make sth become official policy, etc. much quicker than normal</span></td><td class="c4">The legislation has been <b>rushed through</b>.<br>立法匆匆通过了。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>rustle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>rustle sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">仓促准备或；提供某物；迅速找到某人<br><span class="en">to prepare or provide sth for sb very quickly without planning; to find sb very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">TIl <b>rustle some lunch up</b> for you.<br>我给你马上弄些午饭来。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sack ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">躺下休息<br><span class="en">to lie down to rest or relax</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sacked out</b> on the couch and watched a video.<br>我们躺在沙发上看录像。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>saddle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>saddle ˈup<br>ˌsaddle sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">给(马)备鞍<br><span class="en">to prepare to ride a horse by placing a saddle on it</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>saddled up</b> the horses yet?<br>你给马套好鞍了吗。<br><b>Saddle up</b>, we're leaving right away.<br>备鞍，我们马上就走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsaddle sb/yourself with sb/sth<br>ˈsaddle sb/yourself with doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">使担负难活儿；苦差或责任<br><span class="en">to give sb/yourself a difficult or unpleasant task or responsibility to deal with</span></td><td class="c4">He had <b>saddled</b> himself with huge debts.<br>他背上了沉重的债务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>safeguard</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsafeguard aˈgainst sth<br>ˌsafeguard sb/sth/yourself</b></td><td class="c3">防止；保护…以免(伤害或损失)<br><span class="en">a gainst sth formal to prevent sth bad from happening; to keep sth safe from harm damage</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Safeguard against</b> theft by installing a burglar alarm.<br>可安装防盗警报器防盜。<br>The leaflet shows you how to <b>safeguard your home against</b> accidents.<br>宣传单上说明如何预防家中各类事故。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sally</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsally ˈforth (also ˌsally ˈout less frequent) <span class="tag">(old-fashioned or literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">坚决或；兴冲冲地动身；出发；外出<br><span class="en">to leave a place in a determined or enthusiastic way</span></td><td class="c4">After lunch she <b>sallied forth</b> for a short walk.<br>午饭后她兴致勃勃地出去散步了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sandwich</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsandwich A and B toˈgether (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用…接合；粘合<br><span class="en">to put sth between two things to join them</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Sandwich</b> the cakes <b>together</b> with cream.<br>用奶油把蛋糕粘在一起。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>save</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsave on sth<br>ˈsave sth on sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…上节省；节约<br><span class="en">to use less of sth or not more than necessary</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>saved on</b> electricity by using candles.<br>他为了省电使用蜡烛。<br>Get your tickets early and <b>save</b> $5 on the cost of an adult ticket.<br>早点买票，一张成人票可少花5元钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>save ˈup<br>ˌsave sth ˈup (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">为…积蓄；攒钱<br><span class="en">to keep your money instead of spending it, especially because you want to buy a particular thing</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>saving up</b> for a new computer.<br>她在攒钱买新计算机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>saw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>saw sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">锯倒；锯下<br><span class="en">to cut sth down and bring it to the ground, using a saw</span></td><td class="c4">We had to <b>saw down</b> two trees.<br>我们只好锯掉两棵树。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>saw sth ˈoff<br>ˌsaw sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…锯掉；锯去<br><span class="en">to remove sth from sth by cutting it with a saw</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>sawed the lower branches off</b> the apple tree.<br>我锯掉了苹果树低处的树枝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>saw sth ˈup (into )</b></td><td class="c3">把…锯成(小块或碎片)<br><span class="en">to cut sth into pieces using a saw</span></td><td class="c4">All the trees were <b>sawn up</b> into logs.<br>所有的树都被锯成一段段的木材。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scale</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscale sth ˈdown (AmE also ˌscale sth ˈback)</b></td><td class="c3">缩减；降低(规模或重要性)<br><span class="en">to reduce sth in size or importance</span></td><td class="c4">The company has <b>scaled down</b> its training programmes this year.<br>公司削减了今年的培训项目。<br>Police are <b>scaling down</b> the search for the attacker.<br>警方正在缩小对袭击者的搜寻范围。<br>Colin's tools were a <b>scaled</b>-<b>down</b> version of his father's.<br>科林的工具是比照他父亲工具的尺寸按比例缩小的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>scale sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增加；扩大(规模或重要性)<br><span class="en">to increase the size or importance of sth</span></td><td class="c4">We're deciding how to <b>scale up</b> our operation.<br>我们正在考虑如何扩大我们的行动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scan</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scan sth ˈin<br>ˌscan sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">扫描…输入(计算机)<br><span class="en">to pass light over a picture or document using a special machine (a scanner) in order to copy it and put it in the memory of a computer</span></td><td class="c4">Text and pictures can be <b>scanned into</b> the computer.<br>文本和图像都可扫描输入计算机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscan ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">粗略地看；扫视；浏览<br><span class="en">to look quickly but not very carefully at a document, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>scanned through</b> the newspaper over breakfast.<br>她边吃早饭边浏览报纸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scare</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈscare sb into sth<br>ˌscare sb ˈinto doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">威胁；恐吓(使某人做某事)<br><span class="en">to make sb do sth by frightening them</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>scared into</b> signing a confession.<br>他迫于威吓在供状上签了字。<br>Her threats finally <b>scared him into</b> action.<br>她的威胁最终吓得他采取了行动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>scare sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">不经意间吓退；吓走<br><span class="en">to accidentally make sb afraid of or nervous about sth they are planning to do</span></td><td class="c4">Many investors were <b>scared off</b> by the rumours.<br>很多投资者都给传闻吓跑了。<br>Don't act too interested or youll <b>scare him off</b>.<br>别表现得太投入，不然你会把他吓跑的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scarf</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scarf sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">飞快地吃；狼吞虎咽<br><span class="en">to eat sth very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He came home and <b>scarfed down</b> a piece of blueberry pie.<br>他回到家，风卷残云般吃下一块蓝莓馅饼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscarf sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">快地吃；狼吞虎咽<br><span class="en">to eat sth very quickly</span></td><td class="c4">The kids sat down and started <b>scarfing up</b> everything in sight.<br>孩子们坐下来，开始狂吃眼前所有的食物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scoop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscoop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">轻松赢得；轻易得到(尤指巨款或奖项)<br><span class="en">to win or get sth easily, especially a large sum of money or a prize</span></td><td class="c4">The Liberals <b>scooped up</b> four fifths of the seats.<br>自由党人不费吹灰之力便贏得了五分之四的席位。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scoot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscoot ˈover <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给某人挪出座位<br><span class="en">to move along on a seat to make room for another person</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Scoot over</b> and make room for your sister.<br>挪一挪，给你妹妹腾个座儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scope</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scope sb/sth ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">寻找；物色<br><span class="en">to look for sb/sth interesting or attractive; to search out sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>scoped out</b> a place to spend the weekend.<br>我们找到了一个地方过周末。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>score</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈscore off sb <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">驳倒；挫败<br><span class="en">to show that you are better than sb, especially by making clever remarks, for example in an argument</span></td><td class="c4">He's always trying to <b>score off</b> his colleagues.<br>他总是和同事抬杠。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscore sth ˈout/ˈthrough <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">画线于；删去<br><span class="en">to draw a line or lines through sth in a text to show that you do not want it</span></td><td class="c4">The last paragraph had been <b>scored out</b>.<br>最后一段给画掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scout</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scout sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">通过搜寻发现；找到<br><span class="en">to find out what sth is like or where sth is, by searching</span></td><td class="c4">A team travelled to Moscow to <b>scout out</b> possible places for a meeting.<br>一个小组去了莫斯科寻找可以开会的地方。<br>The company is <b>scouting out</b> business opportunities in Vietnam.<br>公司正在越南寻找商机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrabble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scrabble aˈround (BrE also,scrabble a bout, ˌscrabble ˈround) (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">手指迅速或困难地摸索；摸找<br><span class="en">to use your fingers to search for sth quickly or with difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>scrabbled around</b> in her bag for her glasses.<br>她在包里摸来摸去找眼镜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrabble at sth</b></td><td class="c3">动作匆忙地抓<br><span class="en">to scratch at sth with small, hurried movements</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>scrabbling at</b> the earth with her fingers.<br>她用手指不断扒拉着泥土。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrape</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scrape ˈby (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">靠…勉强维生；艰难度日；糊口<br><span class="en">to manage to live on the money you have, although you do not have much</span></td><td class="c4">I can just <b>scrape by</b> on what my parents give me.<br>我靠父母给的那点钱只能糊口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrape ˈin<br>ˌscrape ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">勉强获得工；职位；入学资格等<br><span class="en">to manage to get a job, a position, a place at college, etc., but with difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">I just managed to <b>scrape into</b> university.<br>我勉强升入了大学。<br>He <b>scraped in</b> with 180 votes.<br>他以 180 票勉强当选。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>scrape sth ˈoff<br>scrape sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">刀子等从…上刮掉；削去<br><span class="en">to remove sth from a surface by moving sth sharp and hard like a knife across it</span></td><td class="c4">He spent all day <b>scraping paint off</b> the walls.<br>他花了整整一天时间刮掉墙上的油漆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>scrape ˈthrough<br>scrape ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">艰难完成；勉强通过(考试)<br><span class="en">to succeed with difficulty in doing sth, especially in passing an exam</span></td><td class="c4">She just <b>scraped through</b> law school.<br>她勉强从法学院毕业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrape sth toˈgether (also ˌscrape sth ˈup less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">勉强；凑集；费力积攒；艰难筹措<br><span class="en">to obtain or collect sth such as an amount of money with difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">They managed to <b>scrape together</b> $1 200.<br>他们好不容易凑了1200 元钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scratch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscratch aˈround (BrE also ˌscratch aˈbout) (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">茫无头绪地搜寻；查寻；查找<br><span class="en">to search for sth in a way that is not very organized, by looking at different things, looking on the ground, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>scratching around</b> on the ground for clues.<br>他在地面上四处寻找线索。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>scratch sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">画去；删除名字<br><span class="en">to remove a word, especially a name, from sth written, usually by putting a line through it</span></td><td class="c4">Their names had been <b>scratched out</b>.<br>他们的名字被画掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scream</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scream ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">因受伤；惊恐等尖叫；放声大叫<br><span class="en">to give a loud, high cry, because you are hurt, frightened, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>screamed out</b> in pain.<br>她疼得大叫起来。<br>The cake was <b>screaming out</b> to be eaten.<br>那块蛋糕令人垂涎欲滴。<br>The market has been <b>screaming out</b> for a product like this.<br>市场上亟缺此类产品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>screen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>screen sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">用家具等隔开；遮去(房间的一部分等)<br><span class="en">to separate or hide an area of a room, etc. from another area by putting a tall piece of furniture or equipment in front of it or around it</span></td><td class="c4">Part of the room had been <b>screened off</b> with a curtain.<br>房间的一部分用帷幔隔开了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>screen sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把…排除；在外；不准某人加入；拒绝某人入境<br><span class="en">to not include sb/sth, or not allow sb to join an organization, enter a country, etc. because you think they may not be suitable or may cause trouble</span></td><td class="c4">Unsuitable candidates were <b>screened out</b>.<br>不合格的候选者被淘汰了。<br>His job is to <b>screen out</b> inquiries unlikely to result in a sale.<br>他的工作是筛除不可能带来销售的客户咨询。<br>Insurance companies often <b>screen out</b> people who are high risk.<br>保险公司常常对高风险人群拒保。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>screen sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">遮挡；遮住<br><span class="en">to prevent sth harmful from entering or going through sth</span></td><td class="c4">It is essential to <b>screen out</b> ultraviolet rays.<br>挡住紫外线很有必要。<br>A window blind will <b>screen out</b> too much light.<br>窗帘会挡住太多的光线。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>screw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>screw aˈround <span class="tag">(A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">胡闹；闲荡<br><span class="en">to waste time doing silly or useless activities</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>screwing around</b> and do some work!<br>别瞎晃荡了，干点正事吧！A。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew sb aˈround <span class="tag">(BrE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和…绕弯子；糊弄；耍弄<br><span class="en">to treat sb in a way that is deliberately not helpful to them or wastes their time</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>screwing me around</b> and tell me the truth!<br>别跟我兜圈子，跟我说实话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用螺丝钉固定；拧紧<br><span class="en">to attach sth firmly to sth else using screws</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Screw</b> the lid of the box <b>down</b> securely.<br>用螺丝钉把箱子盖拧牢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew sth ˈon<br>ˌscrew sth ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将(容器的盖子)拧紧；旋紧<br><span class="en">to fasten the top on a container by twisting it around</span></td><td class="c4">Is the top <b>screwed on</b> tightly?<br>盖子拧紧了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>screw sb ˈout of sth <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">骗取某人应得的东西<br><span class="en">to cheat sb and prevent them from having sth that they should have</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>screw him out of</b> his winnings.<br>她企图把他赢的钱骗走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew sth ˈout of sb <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">从某人处勒索(或榨取)某物<br><span class="en">to force sb to give you sth; to get sth from sb with great difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>screwed</b> the money <b>out</b>.of her by threatening to hit her.<br>他们威胁要揍她，逼她交出了钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>screw sb ˈover <span class="tag">(AmE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">欺诈；不公平对待<br><span class="en">to trick sb in order to obtain sth valuable from them; to treat sb badly, especially by telling lies</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>screwed her over</b> and took all her money.<br>他骗走了她所有的钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew ˈup<br>ˌscrew sth ˈup <span class="tag">(slang, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">搞槽；搅乱<br><span class="en">to do sth badly or spoil sth</span></td><td class="c4">There was a <b>screw</b>-up over the bookings.<br>预订情况一团糟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrew sb ˈup <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使烦恼得不能正常生活；使神经兮兮<br><span class="en">to make sb so upset or confused that they are unable to deal with problems in life</span></td><td class="c4">Her parents have really <b>screwed her up</b>.<br>她的父母实在是把她逼疯了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>screw sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…揉成团<br><span class="en">to squeeze sth into a tight ball</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>screwed up</b> the note and threw it away.<br>她把字条揉成一团扔掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scribble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscribble sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">草草地写；匆匆记下<br><span class="en">to write sth quickly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>scribbled down</b> the directions on her pad.<br>她在便笺簿上潦草地记下了指示。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrimp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈscrimp on sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…方面；俭省；为省钱购买(劣质产品)<br><span class="en">to spend too little money on sth or buy sth that is of poor quality</span></td><td class="c4">If you're going to do a good job of renovating an old house, don't <b>scrimp on</b> materials.<br>要想好好改造旧房，材料上可别舍不得花钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scroll</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scroll ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">粗略地读；滚屏浏览计算机屏幕上；的文本<br><span class="en">to move through a text on a computer screen quickly, without reading everything</span></td><td class="c4">You can <b>scroll through</b> the document using the wheel on your mouse.<br>你可以用鼠标滚轮来滚屏浏览这份文件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrounge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scrounge aˈround (for sth) <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指费力地四处寻找；到处；搜寻<br><span class="en">to search around in different places for sth, especially if it is difficult to find or there is not much available</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>scrounged around</b> in his desk drawer for a paper clip.<br>他在书桌抽屉里翻来翻去找回形针。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrounge sth ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通过搜寻或询问发现；找到<br><span class="en">to discover information about sb/sth by searching or asking questions</span></td><td class="c4">It would be great if you could <b>scrounge up</b> some information on this.<br>你要是能搞到一些这方面的情报，那就太好了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrub</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrub sth ˈoff<br>ˌscrub sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">用刷子等从…上刷掉；擦掉<br><span class="en">to remove sth from the surface of sth by rubbing it hard with a brush, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Scrub all that mud off</b> the walls.<br>把墙壁上的泥全刷掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌscrub sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用刷子；肥皂；水等擦洗；擦净(某物的內部)<br><span class="en">to clean the inside of sth by rubbing it hard with a brush and usually with soap and water</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>scrubbed out</b> the pans.<br>他把平底锅都刷干净了。<br>The cupboards are <b>scrubbed out</b> every week.<br>每周都要清洁碗柜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>scrunch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>scrunch sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…揉成小团<br><span class="en">to squeeze sth into a small round shape in your hands</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>scrunched up</b> the piece of paper and threw it at me.<br>他把那张纸揉成一个小团，朝我扔过来。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>seal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌseal sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…密封在容器里<br><span class="en">to keep sth inside a container so that none of it can escape</span></td><td class="c4">The foil packet <b>seals in</b> the flavour.<br>锡纸包装保存住了味道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>seal sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">警察；军队等封锁；封闭(某处)<br><span class="en">if the police, the army, etc. seal a place or an area off, they put barriers there to prevent anyone from entering it</span></td><td class="c4">The police have <b>sealed off</b> the town centre.<br>警察已经封锁了市中心。<br><b>Seal off</b> all the exits!<br>封锁所有出口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>seal sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">粘上(信封等)<br><span class="en">to close an envelope, etc. by sticking the edges of the opening together</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>sealed up</b> the envelope and wrote the address on it.<br>他粘好信封，然后写上地址。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>seal sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">将…关严<br><span class="en">to close sth completely so that nothing can get in or out</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>sealed up</b> the windows to keep out the fumes.<br>我关紧窗户挡住浓烟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>search</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsearch sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">找出；查到；搜寻到<br><span class="en">to look for sb/sth until you find them</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>searching out</b> some old pictures to show us.<br>他在找些旧照片给我们看。<br>John <b>searched me out</b> and gave me a note.<br>约翰找到我，交给我一张便条。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>see</b></td><td class="c2"><b>see sb ˈin<br>ˌsee sb ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">送某人进去；护送<br><span class="en">to go with sb into a room, building, etc. to make sure that they get there safely</span></td><td class="c4">After <b>seeing her in</b> (= into her home), he rode off without a word.<br>把她送到家后，他一句话也没。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>see sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">度过(新年等)；迎接…的到来<br><span class="en">if you see in an occasion such as New Year, you are there when it happens</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>saw in</b> the New Year with friends.<br>他们和朋友一起跨年。<br>He lived long enough to <b>see in</b> the new millennium.<br>他活到了新千年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsee sth in sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">认为…具有某种良好的；品质或特征<br><span class="en">to believe that sb/sth has a particular quality or characteristic, especially a good one</span></td><td class="c4">I dont know what she <b>sees in</b> him (=I can't understand why she likes him or finds him attractive).<br>我弄不明白她看中他哪儿了。<br>I can <b>see value in</b> each argument.<br>我认为每次辩论都有价值。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">为…送行；送别<br><span class="en">to go to a station, an airport, etc. to say goodbye to sb who is going on a journey</span></td><td class="c4">We all went. to the airport to <b>see her off</b>.<br>我们全都去机场给她送行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">赶走；驱逐<br><span class="en">to force sb to leave a place, for example by chasing them</span></td><td class="c4">The dogs soon <b>saw off</b> the burglars.<br>几条狗不一会儿就撵走了窃贼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">打败；击败<br><span class="en">to defeat sb</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>saw off</b> her opponent and now goes into the final.<br>她战胜对手进入了决赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">经受得住；能够抵挡<br><span class="en">to be strong enough to resist sth</span></td><td class="c4">The company <b>saw off</b> the threat of a takeover.<br>公司面对收购威胁挺了过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>see sb/yourself ˈout<br>see sb/yourself ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">送某人出去；送走<br><span class="en">to go with sb out of a building, etc. to make sure that they find the way</span></td><td class="c4">Jay <b>saw</b> the last guests <b>out</b> and locked the door.<br>杰伊送走最后几位客人后就锁上了门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sth ˈout not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">She promised to <b>see</b> <b>out</b> the rest of her contract.<br>她答应坚持干到合同期满。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>see ˈover/ˈround sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">细看；察看(某处)<br><span class="en">to visit and look at a place carefully</span></td><td class="c4">Wed like to <b>see over</b> the fat again before we rent it.<br>租下公寓之前我们想再好好看看。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee ˈthrough sb/sth not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>saw</b> <b>through</b> him straight away.<br>我们一下子就识破了他。<br>I can <b>see</b> <b>through</b> your little game (= trick).<br>我看穿了你的小把戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsee sb ˈthrough<br>ˌsee sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助(或支持)某人渡过(难关)<br><span class="en">to give sb support to enable them to survive a difficult experience or a particular period of time</span></td><td class="c4">His courage and good humour <b>saw him through</b>.<br>他靠勇气和乐观的性格挺了过来。<br>She <b>saw him through</b> the months after his accident.<br>在他出事故后的几个月中，她一直陪伴着他。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsee to it that ..</b></td><td class="c3">确保；务使<br><span class="en">to make sure that sth happens</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>see</b> to it that everyone knows the date of the meeting?<br>你负责把会议日期通知到每个人，能做到吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>seek</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌseek sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">尤指竭力寻求；挑选；物色<br><span class="en">to look for and find sb/sth, especially when this means using a lot of effort</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>sought her out</b> to ask her advice.<br>他找到她讨主意。<br>She's always <b>seeking out</b> new business opportunities.<br>她不断发掘新的商机。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>seize</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈseize on sth also ˈseize upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">突然大为关注；一把抓住可利用的；事物<br><span class="en">to suddenly show a lot of interest in sth, especially because you can use it to your advantage</span></td><td class="c4">The scandal was immediately <b>seized</b> <b>upon</b> by the press.<br>新闻界立即紧紧盯住了这一丑闻。<br>Peter <b>seized</b> eagerly on all opportunities for conversation.<br>彼得逮谁跟谁聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌseize ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">机器或部件停止运转；发生故障；失灵<br><span class="en">if a machine or a part of machine seizes up, it stops moving or working correctly</span></td><td class="c4">The engine <b>seized up</b> after only three weeks.<br>发动机只用了三个星期就坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsell sb/sth ˈout (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">向…出卖；变节<br><span class="en">to not be loyal to</span></td><td class="c4">They discovered who had <b>sold them out</b> to the enemy.<br>他们已弄清是谁向敌人出卖了他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sell ˈup<br>.sell sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">卖光；卖掉家当；企业等<br><span class="en">to sell your home, possessions, business, etc., usually because you need the money, are moving to another place or are stopping work</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>sold up</b> and moved to France.<br>他们变卖了家当，移居法国。<br>We decided to <b>sell up</b> everything and buy a farm.<br>我们决定卖掉所有财产，然后买个农场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>send</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb/sth aˈhead</b></td><td class="c3">提前运送；派…打头阵<br><span class="en">to arrange for sb/sth to go or be taken to the place you are going to, before you arrive there</span></td><td class="c4">The rest of the equipment was <b>sent ahead</b> by air.<br>其余的设备先行空运走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>send sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">某人打发走<br><span class="en">to tell sb to leave</span></td><td class="c4">The reporters were <b>sent away</b> empty-handed (= without any news).<br>记者都被打发走了，空手而回。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>send sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">安排；某人离开家(去某处)<br><span class="en">(to …)to arrange for sb to go somewhere away from home</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>sent away</b> to boarding school at the age of seven.<br>他七岁时就被送进了寄宿学校。<br>You can <b>send</b> the goods back if you're not satisfied.<br>不满意可退货。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…送进监狱；判…坐牢<br><span class="en">to send sb to Prison</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>sent down</b> for ten years.<br>他被判了十年刑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsend for sth</b></td><td class="c3">让人带来(或送来)某物<br><span class="en">to ask sb to bring or deliver sth to you</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Send for</b> an ambulance.<br>叫救护车吧。<br>Have you <b>sent for</b> a catalogue (= by post/mail)?<br>你去信索要目录了吗。<br>More equipment has been <b>sent for</b>.<br>已经要求发送更多设备来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">派…去(应付困难局面)<br><span class="en">to order sb to go to a place to deal with a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">Troops were <b>sent in</b> to restore order.<br>已派军队前去恢复秩序。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>send ˈoff (also ˌsend aˈway especially AmE) (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">函索<br><span class="en">to write to sb and ask them to send you sth by post/mail</span></td><td class="c4">If you save enough packets, you can <b>send off</b> and get a free toy.<br>攒够包装纸可寄来免费换取玩具。<br>You can <b>send off</b> for a free booklet.<br>可来信免费索取小册子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">体育比赛</td><td class="c4">He was <b>sent off</b> for a foul.<br>他因犯规被罚下。<br>Three players got <b>sent off</b> in the first half.<br>上半场比赛有三名运动员被罚下场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">派…去；派遣<br><span class="en">(to .) to ask or tell sb to go somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">The bank <b>sent him off</b> for four months' study at Harvard.<br>银行派他去哈佛进修四个月。<br>I always <b>send the kids off</b> to school looking clean and tidy.<br>我总是让孩子们干净整洁地去上学。<br>The men were <b>sent off</b> to find water.<br>那些人被派出去找水。1v+ n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>send sth ˈoff (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">寄某物(给某人)；邮送<br><span class="en">to send sth by post/mail</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>sent that letter off</b> yet?<br>你把信寄出去了吗？08。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>send sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">先期发运(或送达)；提前送到<br><span class="en">to send sth to a place so that it arrives before you get there</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sent our furniture on</b> by ship.<br>我们把家具先行水运过去了。<br>Weve arranged for your belongings to be <b>sent on</b>.<br>我们已经安排把你的东西提前发送过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">派出某人到某处执行任务；派遣<br><span class="en">to send sb somewhere for a particular purpose</span></td><td class="c4">If I'm not back by midnight, <b>send out</b> a search party!<br>要是半夜我还回不来，就派出搜索队。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsend sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">分发；散发<br><span class="en">to send sth to a lot of different people or places</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>sent out</b> fifty invitations.<br>我发出了五十份请柬。<br>Have we <b>sent letters out</b> to all the applicants?<br>我们给所有的申请人都发信了吗。<br>His brain was <b>sending out</b> warning signals telling him to be careful.<br>他的大脑不断发出警报，提醒他小心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsend-up n <span class="tag">(BrE informal an)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对人或事物的滑稽模仿；戏仿取乐<br><span class="en">act of making sb/sth look silly by copying them/it in an amusing way</span></td><td class="c4">The movie is a hilarious <b>send-up</b> of the Hollywood western.<br>这部电影是对好莱坞西部片的戏仿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>separate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>separate sth ˈoff (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">从…分出；分离；分割<br><span class="en">to remove sth from a larger thing or group; to keep sth apart</span></td><td class="c4">The property agency has been <b>separated offfrom</b> the main business.<br>房地产经纪业务从主营业务中拆分出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌseparate ˈout<br>ˌseparate sb/sth ˈout (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使分开；划分<br><span class="en">to divide into different parts; to divide sb/sth into different parts or groups</span></td><td class="c4">The mixture <b>separates out</b> into layers.<br>这种混合物会分层。<br>Plastics must be <b>separated out</b> into different types for recycling.<br>塑料必须先行分类，再回收利用。<br>The process <b>separates out</b> the different gases.<br>这个过程可将各种气体分离出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>serve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈserve as/for sth</b></td><td class="c3">凑合着当…用；权且用作<br><span class="en">to be used instead of sth else when there is nothing better available</span></td><td class="c4">An old box <b>served as</b> a table.<br>用一个旧箱子将就着当桌子用。<br>Small temporary buildings had to <b>serve for</b> offices.<br>狭小的临时建筑权且作办公室用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌserve sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">做…直至期满<br><span class="en">to continue doing sth until the end of a fixed period of time</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>served out</b> the rest of her sentence in an open prison.<br>她在一座开放式监狱服满了剩下的刑期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>set</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈset about sb (with sth) <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">袭击；攻击；抨击<br><span class="en">to attack sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>set about</b> me with a stick.<br>他用棍子打我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈset about sth<br>ˈset about doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始进行；开展活动<br><span class="en">to begin a task or an activity, especially with energy or enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>set about</b> the task of cleaning the apartment.<br>我们动手打扫公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈset about sth<br>ˈset about doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">着手；处理(问题)；展开(工作)<br><span class="en">to approach a problem or task in a particular way</span></td><td class="c4">Youve <b>set about</b> this problem the wrong way.<br>你处理这个问题的方式错了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈset sb aˈgainst sb</b></td><td class="c3">使反对朋友；亲人等<br><span class="en">to make sb oppose a friend, relative, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The civil war <b>set brother against</b> brother.<br>内战造成手足相残。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sth aˈgainst sth</b></td><td class="c3">权衡；掂量；比较(得失或优劣)<br><span class="en">to consider sth by comparing good points with bad ones</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Set against</b> the benefits of the new technology is the possibility that jobs will be lost.<br>权衡利弊，新技术固然有种种好处，但亦可能使一些人失去工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sb/sth aˈpart (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">与众不同；使突出；使优于<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth different from or better than others</span></td><td class="c4">His confidence <b>sets him apart</b> from his classmates.<br>他的自信使他有别于同班同学。<br>It's the service at the restaurant that <b>sets it apart</b>.<br>这家餐馆的服务独具特色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把…放到一旁；把…搁到一边<br><span class="en">to place sth to one side</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sets aside</b> £50 every month for her daughter's college fees.<br>她每月存下50英镑留作女儿上大学的费用。<br>We need to <b>set aside</b> some time to deal with this.<br>我们得抽点时间处理这件事。<br>Let's <b>set aside</b> my personal feelings for now.<br>眼下咱们就不要顾及我个人的感受了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sb ˈback sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使花费；使破费<br><span class="en">to cost sb a large amount of money</span></td><td class="c4">That new car must have <b>set her back</b> a bit.<br>新汽车一定让她破费了一笔。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sb/sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">耽搁…的进展；耽误；使延误<br><span class="en">to delay the progress of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The rain <b>set the building programme back</b> by several weeks.<br>建筑计划因雨延误了几周。<br>He was starting to play very well, but his injury has really <b>set him back</b>.<br>他开始表现得非常好，但伤病着实拖了他的后腿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsetback n</b></td><td class="c3">挫折；障碍<br><span class="en">a problem or difficulty that delays the progress of sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Parry's broken ankle was a major <b>setback</b> for the team.<br>帕里脚踝骨折对该队是一大打击。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be,set ˈback (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">建筑物远离(公路等)<br><span class="en">if a building is set back, it is a long way from sth, especially a road</span></td><td class="c4">Their house is the only one that's set <b>back</b> (from the road).<br>只有他们的房子位置(离公路)远。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset ˈdown<br>ˌset sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">飞机；飞行员；乘客等<br><span class="en">of a plane, a pilot, passengers, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>set down</b> on the beach.<br>我们在沙滩上着陆了。<br>The pilot <b>set the plane down</b> in afield.<br>飞行员把飞机降落在一块田里。</td></tr>
