<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">车辆或驾驶员<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or its driver</span></td><td class="c4">The taxi <b>set me down</b> at the end of the road.<br>出租车在路的尽头让我下了车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；搁下<br><span class="en">(on sth) (literary) to place an object down on a surface</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>set his glass down</b> before he spoke.<br>他放下玻璃杯开始说话。<br>She <b>set the tray down</b> on the table.<br>她把托盘放在桌上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset ˈforth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">出发；动身；起程<br><span class="en">to start a journey</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>set forth</b> for Crete.<br>他们动身前往克里特岛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set ˈforth sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">明确陈述；声明<br><span class="en">to state sth clearly; to make sth known</span></td><td class="c4">The President <b>set forth</b> his views in a long television broadcast.<br>总统在长篇电视讲话中阐述了自己的观点。<br>Her beliefs have been clearly <b>set forth</b>.<br>她已经表明了自己的信念。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">恶劣天气；不快感觉；疾病等到来；开始<br><span class="en">if bad weather, an unpleasant feeling, an illness, etc. sets in, it begins and seems Iikely to continue</span></td><td class="c4">I need to mend the roof before winter <b>sets in</b>.<br>冬天到来前我得把屋顶修好。<br>Panic <b>set in</b> when she realized how much work there was to do.<br>意识到有那么多活儿要干后，她一下子就慌了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sth ˈin/ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…嵌入(…之内)</td><td class="c4">A small safe had been <b>set into</b> the wall.<br>墙壁里放了个小保险箱。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈinset n</b></td><td class="c3">套印在大图；地图等中的小图；小地图</td><td class="c4">The committee members' names appeared in an <b>inset</b>.<br>委员会成员名字列在了插图中。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sb ˈoff<br>set sb ˈoff doing sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使笑起来；使哭起来；使说起话来<br><span class="en">to make sb start doing sth such as laughing, crying or talking</span></td><td class="c4">Check all the doors and windows are locked before <b>setting off</b>.<br>出发前检查一下所有门窗是否都锁好了。<br>The group <b>set off</b> for Rome the next day.<br>第二天那伙人起程去罗马。<br>They <b>set the bomb off</b> as soon as they were a safe distance away.<br>他们一退到安全距离就引爆了炸弹。<br>If you burn the toast youll <b>set the smoke alarm off</b>.<br>面包片如果烤焦，烟雾报警器就会响。<br>The girl's death <b>set off</b> a terrible chain of events.<br>女孩之死引发了一连串可怕的事情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈset sb/sth on sb</b></td><td class="c3">使攻击(或袭击)某人<br><span class="en">to make a person or an animal attack sb</span></td><td class="c4">The farmer threatened to <b>set his dogs on</b> us if we didn't leave at once.<br>农夫威胁说，如果我们不马上离开，他就放狗咬我们。<br>We <b>set</b> out at dawn.<br>拂晓时分，我们上路了。2。<br>They succeeded in what they had <b>set</b> out to do.<br>他们实现了既定的目标。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">摆列；陈列；排列<br><span class="en">to arrange or display sth</span></td><td class="c4">She began <b>setting out</b> plates and glasses.<br>她开始摆放盘子和玻璃杯。<br><b>Set out</b> your answers neatly.<br>把答案写得工整些。2t0。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set ˈto</b></td><td class="c3">起劲地干起来；毅然开始做<br><span class="en">! to begin doing sth in a busy or determined way</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>set to</b> with a scrubbing brush (= she started cleaning).<br>她拿起刷子起劲地擦洗起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set ˈto</b></td><td class="c3">开始打架<br><span class="en">to begin fighting</span></td><td class="c4">They took off their jackets and <b>set to</b>.<br>他们脱掉外衣就打了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset ˈup<br>ˌset sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">安装好；装配好；调试好机器；设备等<br><span class="en">to make a machine, some equipment, etc. ready to use</span></td><td class="c4">He helped me to carry my equipment in and <b>set up</b>.<br>他帮我把设备搬进来并调试好。<br>It took hours to <b>set up</b> all the equipment.<br>花了好几个小时才把所有的设备安装好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset ˈup<br>ˌset yourself ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">立业；创业<br><span class="en">to start running your own business</span></td><td class="c4">He left the firm and <b>set up</b> in business on his own.<br>他离开了公司自己创业。<br>She <b>set herself up</b> as a hairdresser.<br>她自己开了个美发店。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">资助；经济上扶持(某人)<br><span class="en">to provide sb with the money they need, for example to start a business, buy a home, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">A bank loan helped to <b>set her up</b> in business.<br>她靠一笔银行贷款做起了生意。<br>He <b>set his daughter up</b> in her own apartment.<br>他资助女儿买了她自己的公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">栽赃诬陷；冤枉(某人)<br><span class="en">informalto trick sb, especially by making them appear to be guilty of sth that they have not done</span></td><td class="c4">He claimed he had been <b>set up</b> by che police.<br>他说警方冤枉了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使更健康；使更强壮；使更活泼<br><span class="en">to make sb feel healthier, stronger, more active, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">A good breakfast will <b>set you up</b> for the day.<br>早餐吃好一天都精力充沛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>set sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">介绍某人(和…)约会；给…当红娘；为…搭桥<br><span class="en">(with sb) (informal)to arrange for sb to meet sb so that they can have a romantic or sexual relationship</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>set me up</b> with his sister.<br>他介绍我和他妹妹约会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌset yourself ˈup as sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…自居；自诩为；自夸为<br><span class="en">to claim to be very important, know a lot about sth, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>set himself up as</b> an authority on modern art.<br>他自我标榜为现代艺术权威。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>settle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>settle ˈdown<br>.settle sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使某人安静下来；平静下来<br><span class="en">to become or to make sb become calmer, less excited, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The children finally <b>settled down</b> and started work.<br>孩子们终于安静下来开始干活了。<br>The teacher had trouble <b>settling the class down</b>.<br>老师没法让班上的同学安静下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsettle ˈdown to sth (also ˈsettle to sth BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">开始认真对待；安下心来；专心致志于<br><span class="en">to begin to think about sth or give your attention to doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">They had just <b>settled down to</b> dinner when the phone rang.<br>他们刚刚开始吃饭，电话铃就响了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsettle for sth<br>ˈsettle for doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">无奈地接受；将就；凑合着(做…)<br><span class="en">to accept sth that is not quite what you wanted but is the best that you can get</span></td><td class="c4">Both teams were happy to <b>settle for</b> a draw.<br>两队都乐于接受平局的结果。<br>He'd hoped to get £8000 for the car but had to <b>settle for</b> a lot less.<br>他本想把车卖到 8000 英镑，但最后不得不以低得多的价格成交。<br>I refuse to <b>settle for</b> (being) second best!<br>我决不甘心屈居第二。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>settle ˈin<br>ˌsettle ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">安顿下来；习惯于；适应新事物；新环境等<br><span class="en">to become used to sth new, such as a new home, school or job</span></td><td class="c4">She soon <b>settled in</b> at school.<br>她很快便适应了学校生活。<br>It took her a while to <b>settle into</b> her new job.<br>她过了一段时间才适应了新工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsettle on sth (also ˈsettle upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">选定；决定<br><span class="en">to choose sth; to make a decision about sth</span></td><td class="c4">We couldn't decide where to go but we eventually <b>settled on</b> Italy.<br>我们定不下来去哪儿，最终决定去意大利。<br>A date was finally <b>settled on</b>.<br>最后敲定了日期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>settle ˈup (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">向某人还钱；结算；结账<br><span class="en">to pay sb the money you owe them</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>settle up</b> with them for the hire of the room.<br>我们得跟他们结清房租。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sew</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sew sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">缝拢；缝补<br><span class="en">to join or repair sth using a needle and thread</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Sew up</b> the tear before it gets any worse.<br>把撕破的地方及时缝补好。<br>They cleaned the wound and <b>sewed it up</b>.<br>他们清洗了伤口，然后缝合。日。<br>By half-time they had the game <b>sewn up</b>.<br>比赛进行到一半他们就已胜券在握。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shade</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshade sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">把…涂暗；画阴影<br><span class="en">to make part of a picture darker, either with colours or using black</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shaded in</b> part of the graph.<br>他把曲线图的一部分涂了暗色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshade ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">界线模糊地渐变<br><span class="en">to gradually change into sth else so that you cannot tell where one thing ends and the other begins</span></td><td class="c4">The blue gradually <b>shades into</b> purple.<br>蓝色逐渐变成了紫色。<br>Sometimes nervousness can <b>shade into</b> fear.<br>有时紧张可能慢慢转变为恐惧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shake</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">融入新；环境；适应新情况<br><span class="en">to become comfortable and confident in a new situation</span></td><td class="c4">Once the team <b>shakes down</b>, results should improve.<br>一旦整个队伍熟悉了情况，成绩应该可以提高。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">敲诈；勒索<br><span class="en">to threaten sb in order to get money from them</span></td><td class="c4">They've found the guy who <b>shook George down</b>.<br>他们找到了勒索乔治的家伙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshakedown n <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">敲诈；勒索<br><span class="en">an act of trying to get money from sb with violence or threats</span></td><td class="c4">He was stabbed during a <b>shakedown</b>.<br>他遭勒索时被刺伤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb/sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">彻底搜查(某人或某处)<br><span class="en">to search a person or place in a very thorough way</span></td><td class="c4">Police <b>shook down</b> the club, looking for drugs.<br>警方彻底搜查了那家俱乐部，意图找到毒品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">摆脱；甩掉(某人)<br><span class="en">to escape from sb; to get rid of sb who is following you</span></td><td class="c4">He twisted and turned in a desperate attempt to <b>shake off</b> his pursuer.<br>他左拐右转，拼命想甩掉追他的人。<br>I think we've <b>shaken them off</b>.<br>我相信我们已经甩开他们了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">摆脱；挣脱(某人)<br><span class="en">to escape from sb who is holding you and will not let go</span></td><td class="c4">She clung to him, but he <b>shook her off</b>.<br>她紧紧抱着他，可他挣脱了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shake sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">摆脱；消除；驱除(疾病等)<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth, such as an illness, that is causing you problems</span></td><td class="c4">She struggled to <b>shake off</b> her image as a beauty with no brains.<br>她努力摆脱自己的花瓶形象。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshake on sth</b></td><td class="c3">就…握手确认(达成共识)<br><span class="en">to shake hands with sb in order to show that you agree to sth</span></td><td class="c4">Let's <b>shake on</b> it.<br>咱们握手为定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">抖开<br><span class="en">to open or spread sth by shaking it</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shook the blanket out</b> and spread it on the grass.<br>他把毯子料开铺在草地上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">将(某物)抖干净<br><span class="en">to open sth by shaking it in order to get rid of bits of dirt, dust, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She went outside to <b>shake out</b> the tablecloth.<br>她到外面把桌布抖落干净。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使吃惊；使不安<br><span class="en">to shock or upset sb</span></td><td class="c4">She has been badly <b>shaken up</b> by the experience.<br>那次经历让她大受刺激。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">震动；激励；使振作<br><span class="en">to surprise sb in order to make them think or behave in a different way, become more active, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He was asked to <b>shake the staff up</b> a bit.<br>有人要求他调动一下员工的积极性。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshake sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">彻底调整；重组机构；行业等<br><span class="en">to make important changes in an organization, a profession, etc. in order to make it more efficient</span></td><td class="c4">The company needs <b>shaking up</b> a bit.<br>公司需要进行重大改组。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shame</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshame sb into sth<br>ˈshame sb into doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">使感到；羞愧而不得不做某事<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to do sth by making them feel ashamed not to do it</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shamed him into</b> apologizing.<br>他们弄得他很羞愧，只好道歉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shape</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshape ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">进展；发展(良好)</td><td class="c4">Our Plans are <b>shaping up</b> nicely.<br>我们的计划进展顺利。<br>How's the new team <b>shaping up</b>?<br>新队伍的表现怎么样？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sharpen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sharpen ˈup<br>ˌsharpen sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使变得更好或技术更高；更有效率等；提高…的水平或技术；效率等<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb/sth, better, more skilful, more effective, etc. than before</span></td><td class="c4">She needs to <b>sharpen up</b> before next month's competition.<br>下个月比赛之前，她的水平需要再提高一步。<br>This exercise will help students <b>sharpen up</b> their reading skills.<br>这个练习将帮助学生进一步提高阅读能力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shave</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshave sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">剃掉；剪去胡须；头发等<br><span class="en">to remove hair from your face, head, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Dad's <b>shaved his beard off</b>.<br>爸爸刮掉了胡子。<br>She shocked everyone by <b>shaving</b> all her hair of.<br>她剃光了头发，让大家吃惊不小。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shave sth ˈoff<br>ˌshave sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…上削掉；刨去；切掉<br><span class="en">to cut very thin pieces from the surface of a piece of wood, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I had to <b>shave a bit off</b> the door to make it shut.<br>我把边缘部分刨去了一点门才能关上。<br>Use a Sharp knife to <b>shave off</b> thin rolls of chocolate.<br>用锋利的刀子片下薄薄的巧克力卷儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shave sth ˈoff<br>ˌshave sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">微量地减少；缩小<br><span class="en">to make sth smaller or lower by a very small amount</span></td><td class="c4">We managed to <b>shave</b> 5% <b>off</b> the cost.<br>我们设法把成本降低了 5%。<br>He <b>shaved half a second off</b> the world record.<br>他把世界纪录缩短了半秒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shear ˈoff<br>.shear sth ˈoff (technical)</b></td><td class="c3">受压断裂；剪切；切断<br><span class="en">to break under pressure; to cut through sth and make it break</span></td><td class="c4">The bolts holding the wheel in place <b>sheared off</b>.<br>固定轮子的螺栓压断了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sheer</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsheer aˈway/ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">急转；急拐(以避开某物)<br><span class="en">to suddenly move away in a different direction, especially to avoid hitting sth</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>sheered wildly away</b>, just missing the truck.<br>汽车猛地一个转向，勉强避开了卡车。<br>Her mind <b>sheered away</b> from images she did not wish to dwell on.<br>她刻意不去想那些她不愿细想的场景。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshell ˈout (for sth)<br>shell sth ˈout (for sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为…花很多钱；破费<br><span class="en">to pay for sth, especially when it is a lot of money or you do not really want to</span></td><td class="c4">I had to <b>shell</b> <b>out</b> $500 for the air fare.<br>我只得拿出500元买飞机票。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shin</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shin ˈdown/ˈup<br>.shin ˈdown/ˈup sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向下；向上攀爬<br><span class="en">to climb down or up sth, using your hands and legs to hold it tightly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shinned down</b> the drainpipe.<br>他顺着排水管爬下来。<br>You might be able to see if you <b>shin up</b> that tree.<br>爬上那棵树，你就有可能看见了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shine</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shine ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">突出；出众；鹤立鸡群<br><span class="en">if a person or a thing shines out, you notice them because they are very much better than the others</span></td><td class="c4">She seemed to <b>shine out</b> from the rest.<br>她看上去非常出众。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shine ˈthrough<br>ˌshine ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">显现出来；显而易见<br><span class="en">to be seen clearly and easily</span></td><td class="c4">In the last game her talent really <b>shone through</b>.<br>在上一场比赛中，她真正展露了才华。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ship</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌship sb ˈoff (to ... ) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">送走某人；遣送某人(到…)<br><span class="en">to send sb away somewhere, especially when they do not want to go</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shipped the children off</b> to camp.<br>他们把孩子们送去宿营。1。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ship sb/sth ˈoff (to ... )</b></td><td class="c3">用船运走<br><span class="en">to send goods or people somewhere by ' ship</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shipped all their possessions off</b> to Australia.<br>他们把所有财物都海运到了澳大利亚。<br>The goods were <b>shipped off</b> last week.<br>货物上个星期装船运走了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ship sb/sth ˈout (to .. )</b></td><td class="c3">尤指用船运走<br><span class="en">to send goods or people somewhere, especially by ship</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shipped the sculpture out</b> to the States.<br>他们把雕塑海运到了美国。<br>Fresh supplies were <b>shipped out</b>.<br>新的补给品装船运走了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shoo</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshoo sb/sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">通过挥动手臂；发出嘘声等轰走；赶走<br><span class="en">to get rid of sb/sth by waving your arms, making a noise, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We tried to <b>shoo the flies away</b>.<br>我们试图撵走苍蝇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shoot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshoot for sth <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">They're <b>shooting for</b> another victory this season.<br>他们争取这个赛李再赢一场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshoot sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">开枪打掉<br><span class="en">to remove sth by shooting</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shot the lock off</b>.<br>他们开枪把锁打掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shoot ˈthrough <span class="tag">(informal, AustralE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">离去；躲避<br><span class="en">to leave, especially in order to avoid sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">I was only five when my dad <b>shot through</b>.<br>爸爸离开时我才五岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shoot ˈthrough <span class="tag">(informal, AustralE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">迅速长高<br><span class="en">to grow taller in a short time</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>shot</b> up in the last few months.<br>在过去的。<br>Burglaries in the city have <b>shot</b> up by nearly seventy per cent.<br>本市的入室盗窃案骤升了近七成。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shoot sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">开枪打伤(或打坏)；击伤(或击毁)<br><span class="en">to injure sb or damage sth severely by shooting</span></td><td class="c4">An armed gang <b>shot up</b> the nightclub.<br>一个武装团伙开枪把夜总会打得千疮百孔。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shop aˈround (for sth)<br>shop aˈround sth (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">就某种商品或服务比较…的；价格；逐店选购；货比三家<br><span class="en">to look at different shops/ stores to compare the prices of goods or services so that you can buy the ones that are the best value</span></td><td class="c4">It's worth <b>shopping</b> <b>around</b> the travel agents to find the best deal.<br>比较各家旅行社，选择最划算的是值得的。<br>When you open a bank account, it's a good idea to <b>shop</b> <b>around</b> first.<br>开立账户前，不妨先比较一下各家银行的服务。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shore</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shore sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用梁柱等支撑(建筑物)<br><span class="en">to support part of a building or other large structure by placing large pieces of wood or metal against or under it so that it does not fall down</span></td><td class="c4">Engineers <b>shored up</b> the tunnel with wooden beams.<br>工程师用木梁支撑隧道。<br>The building was <b>shored up</b> to make it safe.<br>这座建筑物被支撑起来加固。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shout</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshout sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用叫喊声压倒某人的讲话<br><span class="en">to shout to prevent sb who is speaking from being heard, because you do not like what they are saying or you disagree with them</span></td><td class="c4">I tried to explain but they just <b>shouted me down</b>.<br>我试图解释，可他们大喊大叫，把我的声音压下去了。<br>The speaker was <b>shouted down</b> by angry protesters.<br>愤怒的抗议者大叫大囔，盖过了讲话人的声音。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshout ˈout (to sb)<br>shout sth ˈout (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">突然(向某人)喊叫<br><span class="en">to suddenly say sth in a loud voice</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>shouted</b> <b>out</b> to them but they didn't hear me.<br>我朝他们大喊一声，可他们没听见。<br>She <b>shouted</b> <b>out</b> a warning.<br>她大声发出警告。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shove</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshove ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">挪出空位<br><span class="en">used to ask sb to move to make a space for sb else to sit down</span></td><td class="c4">We can get one more in if you <b>shove up</b>.<br>你挪动一下，我们就能再坐下一个。<br><b>Shove up</b> a bit!<br>稍挪一挪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>show</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshow sb ˈover sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">领某人参观；带某人查看<br><span class="en">to take sb around a place they are visiting and show them what is interesting</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>showed me over</b> the house.<br>他们带我看了房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>show ˈthrough<br>ˌshow ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中透出；显出；透视<br><span class="en">to be visible through sth or behind sth</span></td><td class="c4">This paper is so thin the ink <b>shows through</b>.<br>这纸薄得能透墨迹。<br>His skull <b>showed through</b> his thin hair.<br>他的脑壳在稀疏的头发下清晰可见。<br>When he spoke, his bitterness <b>showed through</b>.<br>他的言语流露出内心的酸楚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshow ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">如约赶到；出现；露面<br><span class="en">to arrive or appear at the place you have arranged</span></td><td class="c4">I arranged to meet him but he didn't <b>show up</b>.<br>我约了和他见面，可他没来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshow ˈup<br>ˌshow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使惹眼；显眼；显而易见<br><span class="en">to become or to make sth easy to see</span></td><td class="c4">His striped rie <b>showed up</b> well against his dark red shirt.<br>他的条纹领带搭配深红色的衬衫显得十分醒目。<br>Her lack of experience was <b>shown up</b> by the test.<br>她缺乏经验，这在测试中看得出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshow sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使难堪或尴尬；丢脸；使下不了台<br><span class="en">to make sb else feel embarrassed by behaving badly or by doing sth better than them</span></td><td class="c4">You really <b>showed me up</b> by snoring during the concert!<br>你在音乐会上鼾声连连，真给我丢脸。<br>Don't worry about being <b>shown up</b> by the kids.<br>不要顾虑输给孩子们没面子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshow sb/sth ˈup as/for sth</b></td><td class="c3">揭露；揭示…为…<br><span class="en">to show what sb/sth is really like, when this is worse than people thought</span></td><td class="c4">The book <b>shows her up for</b> what she really is:a fraud.<br>这本书揭穿了她的真面目——个骗子。<br>We were <b>shown up as</b> the second-rate team that we were.<br>我们暴露出了二流球队的真实水平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shower</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshower sb with sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…向某人拋撒<br><span class="en">to drop a lot of small things onto sb</span></td><td class="c4">The bride and groom were <b>showered with</b> rice as they left the church.<br>新娘新郎离开教堂时，大家向他们身上撒大米。<br>The roof collapsed, <b>showering us with</b> dust and debris.<br>房顶塌了，灰尘和瓦砾雨点般落到我们身上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shrink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shrink aˈway/ˈback (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">躲避；退避；畏缩<br><span class="en">to move backwards or away from sb/sth, especially because you are frightened or disgusted .</span></td><td class="c4">She shrank <b>away</b> from him in horror.<br>她惊恐万分地躲避他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshrink from sth<br>ˈshrink from doing sth often</b></td><td class="c3">常用于否定句<br><span class="en">used in negative sentences</span></td><td class="c4">She recognized her responsibility and did not <b>shrink from</b> it.<br>她意识到自己的责任，没有退缩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shrivel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shrivel ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">干瘪；打蔫儿；枯萎<br><span class="en">to become dry and develop deep lines because of heat, lack of water, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The apples left on the tree had <b>shrivelled up</b>.<br>留在树上的苹果都蔫儿了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shroud</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈshrouded in sth</b></td><td class="c3">被…遮盖；被…掩藏<br><span class="en">to be covered or hidden by sth</span></td><td class="c4">The city <b>was shrouded in</b> mist.<br>城市笼罩在雾霭中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈshrouded in sth</b></td><td class="c3">消息等被掩盖；被隐藏<br><span class="en">if information, etc. is shrouded in mystery, it is hidden or kept secret</span></td><td class="c4">His family background <b>is shrouded in</b> mystery.<br>他的家庭背景扑朔迷离。<br>Their work <b>is shrouded in</b> secrecy.<br>他们的工作神秘莫测。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shuck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>shuck sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">随意地剥去；去(衣服)<br><span class="en">to take off a piece of clothing in a careless way</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shucked off</b> his bathrobe and got into the shower.<br>他脱掉浴袍，进了淋浴房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shut</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshut sb/sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">把…藏起来；隔离；禁闭<br><span class="en">to put sb/sth in a place where other people cannot see or find them/it</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shut the files away</b> in the safe.<br>他把文件锁在保险柜里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut yourself aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">独自躲起来；隐藏<br><span class="en">to stay in your room or go somewhere where you will be completely alone</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>shut himself away</b> in his study to finish the book.<br>他独自躲进书房把书看完。<br>You can't just <b>shut yourself away</b> from the world.<br>你不能把自己封闭起来，不与外界接触。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshut down<br>.shut sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使关张；停业；倒闭；关闭<br><span class="en">to stop opening for business; to stop sth from opening</span></td><td class="c4">The mine <b>shut down</b> last month.<br>煤矿上个月关闭了。9。<br>The computer system will be <b>shut down</b> over the weekend.<br>周末将关闭计算机系统。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut sb/sth ˈin<br>sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…关；在房间；建筑；车辆等里面；在…里呆着<br><span class="en">to put sb/sth in a room, a vehicle, etc. and keep them there; to go into a room, a building, a vehicle, etc.and stay there</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>shut the animals in</b> at night.<br>他们夜间把牲畜圈起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈshut sth in sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…卡在或轧；在…中<br><span class="en">to trap or injure sth by closing sth tightly around it</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>shut my finger in</b> the car door.<br>我的手指被车门夹伤了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut ˈoff<br>ˌshut sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">机器停止运转；关闭(机器)<br><span class="en">if a machine shuts off, or sb shuts it off, it stops working</span></td><td class="c4">I stopped the car and <b>shut off</b> the engine.<br>我停下车，关闭了发动机。<br>A valve <b>shuts off</b> the gas when the lid is closed.<br>盖子一闭合，阀门就会切断煤气。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut sb/sth ˈoff (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使(与…)隔离；隔绝<br><span class="en">to keep sb/sth separate from other people or things</span></td><td class="c4">A range of mountains <b>shuts Bosnia off</b> from the Adriatic.<br>波斯尼亚和亚得里亚海之间有山脉相隔。<br>The kitchen area is <b>shut off</b> from the rest of the room.<br>做饭的地方与房间的其他部分隔开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut sb/sth ˈout<br>ˌshut sb/sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">使不能进入(某处)；挡住；遮住<br><span class="en">to stop sb/sth from entering a place</span></td><td class="c4">He closed the door firmly, <b>shutting us out</b> of the room.<br>他用力关上门，不让我们进房间。<br>I drew the curtains to <b>shut out</b> the light.<br>我拉上窗帘遮挡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut sth ˈout<br>ˌshut, sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">克制(某种感情或想法)；不去想<br><span class="en">to stop yourself from having particular feelings or from thinking about particular things</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>shut out</b> all the painful memories.<br>她尽力回避这一切痛苦的回忆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>shut sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把(房屋等)暂时关闭<br><span class="en">to close a room, house, etc. and not use it for a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>shut the summer house up</b> again for another year.<br>我们再次关好避暑别墅的门窗，待明年再来。<br>Will you tell Mike to <b>shut up</b>?<br>你叫迈克闭嘴好吗。<br>Somebody should <b>shut him up</b>.<br>该有人叫他闭上嘴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>shy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌshy aˈway (from sth/from doing sth)</b></td><td class="c3">因紧张或害怕而躲避；回避<br><span class="en">to avoid doing sth because you are nervous or frightened</span></td><td class="c4">She shies <b>away</b> from close friendships.<br>她不愿跟人深交。<br>Don't <b>shy away</b> from saying what you think.<br>别吞吞吐吐的，说出你的想法吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sick sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">呕吐；吐出<br><span class="en">to bring food up from the stomach</span></td><td class="c4">The baby <b>sicked up</b> her milk.<br>婴儿吐奶了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sicken</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsicken for sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">You look as if youre <b>sickening for</b> flu.<br>你看上去像是要患流感。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>side</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈside with sb (against sb)</b></td><td class="c3">支持某人；某人站在一起(反对…)<br><span class="en">to support sb in an argument, a disagreement, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The children always <b>sided with</b> their mother (against their father).<br>孩子们总是站在妈妈一边(反对爸爸)。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sidle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sidle ˈover/ˈup (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">羞怯；犹豫或悄悄地走向；走近(某人)</td><td class="c4">She <b>sidled up</b> to him and whispered in his ear.<br>她悄悄地走到他身边，对着他的耳朵低语。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sift</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sift sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">从众多；东西中去掉(不适合的东西)；剔除；淘汰<br><span class="en">to separate sth, ustally sth you do not want, from a group of things</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>sift out</b> unsuitable applications.<br>我们需要剔出不合格的申请表。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sign</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsign for sth</b></td><td class="c3">运动员和球队签约；正式同意为；球队效力<br><span class="en">(sport) if a player signs for a club, he/she formally agrees to play for</span></td><td class="c4">When did Rooney <b>sign for</b> United?<br>售尼什么时候和曼联签约的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sign ˈin<br>ˌsign sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">替客人签到<br><span class="en">to write your name or the name of a guest when you arrve at an office, a club, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">All visitors must <b>sign in</b> on arrival.<br>来客均须签到。<br>You have to be <b>signed in</b> by a member.<br>你必须由会员帮你签到。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsign sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">签字认可；签名同意<br><span class="en">to give your formal approval to sth, by signing your name</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>signed off</b> all the invoices.<br>她在所有发票上签了名。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsign ˈoff on sth <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">式批准<br><span class="en">to express your approval of sth formally and definitely ie</span></td><td class="c4">The President hasn't yet <b>signed off on</b> this report.<br>这份报告总统还没有正式批准。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sign ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">开始广播<br><span class="en">to announce the start of broadcasting for the day</span></td><td class="c4">This is Jack Grainger <b>signing on</b>.<br>我是杰克•格兰杰，现在开始播音。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sign ˈout<br>ˌsign sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">替客人签退；签字离开<br><span class="en">to write your name or the name of a guest when you leave an a club, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Don't forget to <b>sign out</b> when you go.<br>离开时别忘了签退。<br>You must <b>sign your guests out</b> when they leave the club.<br>客人离开俱乐部，你必须替他们签退。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsign sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">签字(同意)取走(或带出)<br><span class="en">to sign a document to say officially that sth can be removed from a place or that you have taken it</span></td><td class="c4">There is no record of the file being <b>signed out</b> again.<br>没有文件再次借出的签字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsign sth ˈover (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">签字转让(权利或财产)<br><span class="en">to give your rights or property to sb else by signing a document</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>Signed the house over</b> to his daughter.<br>他签署文件，把房产过户到了女儿名下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>silt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>silt ˈup<br>ˌsilt sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使淤塞<br><span class="en">to become blocked with silt; to block sth in this way</span></td><td class="c4">The old harbour has <b>silted up</b>.<br>老港口已经淤塞了。<br>Mud is <b>silting up</b> the stream.<br>泥沙淤积，阻塞了河道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sing</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sing aˈlong (with sb/sth)<br>ˌsing aˈlong (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">随着某人；唱片；广播；或乐器唱<br><span class="en">to sing together with sb who is already singing or while a record, radio, or musical instrument is playing</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sang</b> <b>along</b> to all the songs.<br>我们跟唱了所有的歌曲。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sing ˈout<br>sing sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">叫出；唱出<br><span class="en">to sing or say sth clearly and loudly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Sing out</b> so that everyone can hear.<br>亮开嗓门唱，让大家都能听见。<br>If you need anything, just <b>sing out</b>.<br>需要什么就喊一声。+ n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sing ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">更大声地唱；放开嗓门唱<br><span class="en">to sing more loudly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Sing up</b>, I can't hear you.<br>大点声唱，我听不见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>single</b></td><td class="c2"><b>single sb/sth ˈout (for sth/as sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">为某事单独挑出；单独选出…(作为…)<br><span class="en">to choose sb/sth from among a group for special comment or treatment</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>singled her out</b> for particular praise.<br>他们特别表扬了她。<br>He was <b>singled out</b> as the best student.<br>他被评选为最佳学生。<br>Why had Aidan been <b>singled out</b> for special treatment?<br>为什么对艾丹特对待。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsink ˈback (into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">向后靠；向后倒(在…上)；躺下<br><span class="en">to move or fall backwards, or lie down, especially when you are feeling tired</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sank back</b> into her chair.<br>她向后一倒坐进椅子里。<br>He <b>sank back</b> against the pillows, exhausted.<br>他筋疲力尽地靠到枕头上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sink ˈin<br>ˌsink ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">of liquids</span></td><td class="c4">The rain <b>sank into</b> the dry ground.<br>雨水渗进了干旱的土地里。话语等。<br>He paused to let his words <b>sink into</b> her brain.<br>他停了一下，好让她充分领会他的意思。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsink into sth</b></td><td class="c3">渐渐进入不活跃或消沉；不快乐的状态<br><span class="en">to go gradually into a less active, happy or pleasant state</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sank into</b> a deep sleep.<br>她沉沉睡去。<br>He <b>sank deeper into</b> depression.<br>他越来越优郁。o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsink ˈinto sth<br>ˌsink sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…插入<br><span class="en">to go deep into sth solid, to make sth sharp do this</span></td><td class="c4">Sharp teeth <b>sank into</b> his arm.<br>尖利的牙齿咬住了他的胳膊。<br>The dog <b>sank its teeth into</b> my leg.<br>狗猛咬我的腿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sink sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把(资金)投入(企业或活动)<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of money on a business or an activity, for example in order to make money from it in the future</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sank all our savings into</b> the new company.<br>我们把所有的积蓄都投进了新公司。o a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsip at sth</b></td><td class="c3">小口小口地喝；浅啜<br><span class="en">to drink sth slowly, taking a very small amount each time</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sipped at</b> her coffee.<br>她一点一点 o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>siphon sth ˈoff (from sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">非法将金钱或；资源抽走(或转移)<br><span class="en">to move money or resources from one place to another, usually illegally</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>siphoned off</b> profits into her own bank account.<br>她擅自将盈利转到了她本人的银行账户上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sit aˈround<br>ˌsit aˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">无所事事地坐着；(在…)闲坐<br><span class="en">to spend time sitting down doing very little</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sat</b> about talking for most of the morning.<br>我们大半上午都坐着闲聊。<br>AlL we could do was <b>sit around</b> and wait.<br>我们能做的就是无聊地坐着等。<br>They were <b>sitting around</b> the house chatting.<br>他们闲散地坐在屋里聊天。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">放松下来(做某事)<br><span class="en">(and do sth) to relax, especially by not getting too involved in or anxious about sth</span></td><td class="c4">Now all the work's done we can <b>sit back</b> and enjoy things!<br>活儿全干完了，我们可以尽情玩啦。<br>Are you going to <b>sit back</b> and let me do everything?<br>你打算在一旁歇着，让我包揽所有的活儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit ˈby</b></td><td class="c3">坐视不管；袖手旁观；无动于衷<br><span class="en">to do nothing to stop sth bad or unpleasant happening</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sat</b> down on the sofa.<br>我们在沙发上坐下。<br>When everyone was <b>sitting</b> down,he began.<br>大家还没落座，他就开始了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit yourself ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">坐下；就座<br><span class="en">to lower your body until you are sitting on a chair, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Come in and <b>sit yourself down</b>.<br>进来坐下吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">为…做模特<br><span class="en">to be a model for an artist or a photographer</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sat for</b> some of the most famous artists of her day.<br>她为她那个时代一些最知名的艺术家当过模特。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit ˈin (on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">列席(会议)；旁听(课程)<br><span class="en">to attend a meeting, a class, etc. to watch it, not to take part</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas allowed to <b>sit in</b> on the meeting.<br>我获准列席会议。<br>I <b>sat in</b> on some English classes.<br>我旁听了一些英语课。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit-in n</b></td><td class="c3">拒绝离开工厂；建筑物等的静坐示威；静坐；抗议<br><span class="en">a form of protest in which people refuse to leave a factory, a building, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Workers decided to stage a <b>sit-in</b>.<br>工人们决定发起静坐罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit ˈin for sb</b></td><td class="c3">代某人顶班；替某人履行职责<br><span class="en">to do sb's job or perform sb’'s duties while they are away</span></td><td class="c4">The chief reporter often <b>sat in for</b> George as editor.<br>主任记者常顶替乔治做编辑。<br>Where were you <b>sitting</b>?<br>当时你坐在哪儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit on sth</b></td><td class="c3">是(委员会等)的成员<br><span class="en">to be a member of a group of people such as a committee</span></td><td class="c4">How many people <b>sit on</b> the committee?<br>委员会有多少成员。<br>My mother <b>sat on</b> the jury during a famous murder trial.<br>我母亲曾经是一宗有名的谋杀案审判的陪审团成员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sit ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">坐在外面<br><span class="en">to sit outside somewhere rather than inside</span></td><td class="c4">It's too cold now to <b>sit out</b>.<br>这会儿在外面坐着太冷了。<br>Let's <b>sit out</b> on the balcony.<br>咱们到阳台去坐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">坐在一旁不参加跳舞；游戏等活动<br><span class="en">to not take part in a dance, game Or other activity</span></td><td class="c4">We'll just have to <b>sit it out</b> here until things improve.<br>我们只好一直在这儿耐着性子熬到事情有转机。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit over sth</b></td><td class="c3">悠闲地吃(或喝)<br><span class="en">to have a meal or a drink in a slow relaxed way</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>sat over</b> breakfast and planned the day ahead.<br>我们慢悠悠地吃着早餐，安排一天的日程。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit through sth</b></td><td class="c3">一直坐到冗长的；演出；演讲；会议等结束<br><span class="en">to stay until the end of a performance, speech, meeting, etc. that you think is boring or too long</span></td><td class="c4">We had to <b>sit through</b> a whole dinner without a cigarette.<br>我们一根烟都不能抽，一直熬到晚餐结束。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sit ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">坐起来；坐直<br><span class="en">to be or to move yourself into a sitting position, for example, from lying down</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>sat up</b>, turned the light on, and looked at his watch.<br>他坐起来开灯，看了看表。<br>Do you feel well enough to <b>sit up</b> yet?<br>你感觉怎么样，能坐起来了吗？2。<br>This will make them <b>sit up</b> and listen.<br>这样他们就会聚精会神用心听。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsit-up n</b></td><td class="c3">仰卧起坐<br><span class="en">an exercise in which you move from lying down to a sitting position</span></td><td class="c4">I do about sixty <b>sit-ups</b> a day.<br>我每天做大约六十个仰卧起坐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsit sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">让…坐起来<br><span class="en">to move sb from lying to a sitting position</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sat the baby up</b> in the pram.<br>她把孩子放在婴儿车里坐着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>skate</b></td><td class="c2"><b>skate ˈover/aˈround sth (BrE also ˌskate ˈround sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把(困难或尴尬的事)轻轻带；对…轻描淡写<br><span class="en">to talk about sth difficult or embarrassing quickly, without giving attention to details</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>skated over</b> the next part of her story.<br>她对自己经历的下一个片段一带而过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sketch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sketch sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">补充说明；给…补充细节<br><span class="en">to give more information or details about sth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>sketched in</b> the background to the case.<br>他补充说明了此个案的背景。<br>You need to <b>sketch in</b> his character a little more.<br>对他的性格你应当刻画得再细致一些。<br>I <b>sketched in</b> the outline of the house.<br>我又草草勾画了房子的轮廓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsketch sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">画出…的草图</td><td class="c4">He <b>sketched out</b> some preliminary designs.<br>他简单地勾画了几个初步的设计。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsketch sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">简述；概述；草拟<br><span class="en">to give a brief general description of a plan or an idea</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sketched out</b> the plots of her novels in an exercise book.<br>她在练习册上勾勒了她小说的情节。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>skim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌskim sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">撇去液体；表面的油脂等<br><span class="en">to remove a substance such as fat from the surface of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Skim off</b> the fat and reheat the stew.<br>把油撇掉后，再把炖菜热一热。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌskim sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">提取；攫取；捞取(精华部分)<br><span class="en">to take the best part of sth for yourself, often in an unfair or dishonest way</span></td><td class="c4">She's been <b>skimming off</b> a percentage of the profits for years.<br>她多年来一直在捞取一定份额的利润。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>skimp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈskimp on sth</b></td><td class="c3">节省金钱；或时间；省吃俭用<br><span class="en">to spend less money or time on sth than is normal or necessary</span></td><td class="c4">Older people shouldn't <b>skimp on</b> food or heating.<br>老年人不应过分吝情食品或取暖方面的开销。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>skip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>skip ˈoff (BrE) (also .skip ˈout AmE, BrE) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指出；于不正当的原因突然离去；溜走<br><span class="en">to leave a place secretly or suddenly, especially for a dishonest reason, for example to avoid paying for sth</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>skipped off</b> without paying.<br>他们没付钱就溜了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>skip ˈout on sb/sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指不顾某人离开；溜走；(为摆脫困境)逃避；远遁<br><span class="en">to leave sb, especially when they need you; to try to avoid a difficult situation by leaving a place</span></td><td class="c4">He just <b>skipped out on</b> his wife leaving her with four kids to take care of.<br>他撇下妻子跑了，留下四个孩子让她照料。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>skive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>skive ˈoff<br>ˌskive ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">旷工；逃学；早退<br><span class="en">to avoid work or school by staying away or leaving early</span></td><td class="c4">Where's Tom? I expect he's <b>skiving</b> again!<br>汤姆在哪儿？我想他又溜了吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slack ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">松懈；放松；懈息<br><span class="en">to do sth more slowly or work less hard than before</span></td><td class="c4">We can't <b>slack off</b> until everything is finished.<br>等一切都完成了，我们才能松劲儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slacken</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slacken ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">闲下来；变懒散<br><span class="en">to become less busy or active</span></td><td class="c4">Weve been really busy, but things are starting to <b>slacken off</b> now.<br>我们忙极了，不过现在事情开始减少了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slam</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslam sth ˈdown (on/onto sth)</b></td><td class="c3">猛力放下；砰地摔下(落在…上)<br><span class="en">to put sth down with a lot of force, especially when you are angry</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>slammed the book down</b> on the table.<br>她把书摔在桌子上。<br>I <b>slammed down</b> the phone (= put the receiver down and ended the phone conversation) in a rage.<br>我愤怒地摔了电话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slam ˈinto/aˈgainst sb/sth<br>.slam sb/sth ˈinto/aˈgainst sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使重重撞上；猛撞到<br><span class="en">to crash, or to make sth crash, into sth with a lot of force</span></td><td class="c4">The jeep <b>slammed into</b> the wall.<br>吉普车撞到了墙上。<br>In the crash she was <b>slammed against</b> the back of the seat.<br>撞车时她被甩到了座位靠背上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslam sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">用力踩(剎车)<br><span class="en">if you slam on the brakes of a vehicle, you operate them suddenly and with force</span></td><td class="c4">A child suddenly ran out into the road and I had to <b>slam on</b> the brakes.<br>一个小孩突然跑上公路，我只好猛踩刹车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslap sb aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">常常打；动辄殴打(尤指男性打女性)<br><span class="en">to hit sb regularly or often, used especially of a man hitting a woman</span></td><td class="c4">He used to come back drunk and <b>slap his wife around</b>.<br>他过去经常醉醺醺地回家打他老婆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slap sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">公开且不公平地奚落；指责；责骂<br><span class="en">to criticize sb or their ideas or suggestions in an unfair way, often in public</span></td><td class="c4">He tried to object, but was immediately <b>slapped down</b>.<br>他想表示反对，可立即遣到了喝止。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslap sth ˈdown (on/onto sth)</b></td><td class="c3">啪的一声把…放下(落在…上)<br><span class="en">to put sth onto a surface in a quick and often noisy way, especially because you are angry</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>slapped down</b> a copy of the book on the table.<br>他把一册书猛地丟到桌子上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslap sth ˈon<br>ˈslap sth on sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">突然强制实行(惩罚)；突然强迫遵守(新规则等)<br><span class="en">to announce suddenly that sb must have a punishment, obey a new rule, etc., often when this is unfair</span></td><td class="c4">Judges have been <b>slapping on</b> longer prison sentences.<br>法官量刑时一直是选择判处较长的刑期。<br>The government <b>slapped a new tax on</b> high earners.<br>政府突然对高收入者强制征收新税。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈslash at sb/sth (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用刀等猛砍；猛击<br><span class="en">to attack sb Violently with a knife, etc. and try to cut them/it</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>slashed at</b> his opponent's face with a knife.<br>他用刀子猛划对手的脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sleep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sleep ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">比平常迟起；睡懒觉<br><span class="en">to remain in bed longer than usual in the morning</span></td><td class="c4">She usually <b>sleeps in</b> on Sundays.<br>她星期天通常睡懶觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsleep sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">以睡眠消除；睡一觉熬过(尤指酒劲)<br><span class="en">to get better after sth, especially drinking too much alcohol, by sleeping</span></td><td class="c4">He's still <b>sleeping off</b> yesterday's hangover.<br>他还在睡觉消解昨天的宿醉呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsleep on sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…留待次日决定；把…拖；到第二天再说<br><span class="en">to delay making a decision about sth until the next day so that you can think about it</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Sleep on</b> it and let me know tomorrow.<br>晚上好好想想，明天给我个答复。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsleep ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">在户外睡；譯宿<br><span class="en">to sleep outdoors</span></td><td class="c4">We slept <b>out</b> most nights when we were in Greece.<br>我们在希腊时大多露宿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsleep ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">在别人家过夜；借宿<br><span class="en">to stay the night at sb else's home</span></td><td class="c4">The kids are <b>sleeping over</b> with friends.<br>孩子们在朋友家过夜。<br>It's very late now-why don't you <b>sleep over</b>?<br>现在已经很晚了 —为什么不就睡这儿呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsleep ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">不被(吵闹或混乱)吵醒；睡觉不受…影响<br><span class="en">to not be woken up by sth such as a loud noise or a lot of activity</span></td><td class="c4">She slept right <b>through</b> the thunderstorm.<br>她完全没被暴风雨吵醒。<br>Did he <b>sleep through</b> the whole incident?<br>发生这事时自始至终他都在睡觉吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsleep together<br>ˈsleep with sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人(尤指非配偶)发生性关系<br><span class="en">to have sex with sb, especially sb you are not married to</span></td><td class="c4">They have been <b>sleeping together</b> for months now.<br>他们一块儿睡觉已经有几个月了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slice</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslice sth ˈoff<br>ˌslice sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…上切下；下(薄片)<br><span class="en">to remove a thin piece of sth from sth larger by cutting</span></td><td class="c4">The top of his finger was <b>sliced off</b> in an accident.<br>他的指尖在一次事故中被切掉了。<br>She <b>sliced</b> a piece of meat <b>off</b> the joint.<br>她从那一大块带骨肉上切下一片。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslice sth ˈoff<br>ˌslice sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…减少(某数量)；使削减<br><span class="en">to reduce sth by a particular amount</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>sliced two seconds off</b> the world record.<br>他把世界纪录缩短了两秒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slice ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易地切开；通过</td><td class="c4">The axe <b>sliced through</b> the wood like butter.<br>这把斧子劈柴如同切黄油块一样轻松。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslice sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…切成薄片<br><span class="en">to cut sth into flat thin pieces</span></td><td class="c4">Would you <b>slice the cucumber up</b>?<br>请把黄瓜切成片好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslick sth ˈback/ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使(头发)平整光滑<br><span class="en">if you slick your hair back/down, you make it lie fat by putting oil, water, etc.on it</span></td><td class="c4">His hair was <b>slicked back</b>.<br>他的头发梳得溜光。<br>He still <b>slicks down</b> his hair with oil.<br>他仍然用发油梳平头发。c。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslim ˈdown<br>ˌslim sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">精简(机构)；裁减(人员)；减少(岗位)<br><span class="en">to make sth, such as an organization or a company, smaller by employing fewer people, reducing the amount of work done, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The coal industry has had to <b>slim down</b>.<br>煤炭产业还得精简。<br>The firm had to <b>slim down</b> its workforce.<br>公司不得不裁员。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slip ˈby</b></td><td class="c3">机会等溜走；失去<br><span class="en">if an opportunity, etc. slips by, it passes and you do not use it</span></td><td class="c4">I try never to let a chance to travel <b>slip by</b>.<br>我争取不错过任何旅行机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslip sth ˈin<br>slip sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">在说话或文字中插入(几句话等)<br><span class="en">to add sth to a speech, conversation or written text quickly or secretly</span></td><td class="c4">He usually <b>slips</b> a couple of jokes <b>into</b> his lectures.<br>他讲课时常捎带穿插几个笑话。<br>She <b>slipped in</b> a few comments about her boyfriend.<br>她插话讲了讲她的男友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slip ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">迅速轻松地穿上<br><span class="en">to put clothes on quickly and easily</span></td><td class="c4">The economy has <b>slipped into</b> recession.<br>经济陷入衰退。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslip sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">迅速轻松地脱下<br><span class="en">to take clothes or shoes off quickly and easily</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>slipped her shoes off</b> by the door.<br>她在门旁一下子踢掉了鞋子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slip ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">滑倒；失足<br><span class="en">to slide a short distance and fall</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>slipped over</b> on the ice and broke his leg.<br>他在冰上滑了一跤，摔断了腿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slip ˈthrough<br>slip ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">漏网；被漏掉；蒙混过关<br><span class="en">if sth or sb slips through or slips through system, etc., a person or a system fails to find and deal with it/them</span></td><td class="c4">Mistakes occasionally <b>slip through</b>.<br>偶尔有些错误会被忽略。<br>Somehow he <b>slipped through</b> the company's screening process.<br>他不知用何种方法混过了公司的审查程序。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈslip-up n <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">粗心导致的错误；疏忽；纰漏</td><td class="c4">One small <b>slip-up</b> could cost us the election.<br>一个小小的失误就会让我们输掉选举。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slob</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slob aˈround/out<br>ˌslob aˈround sth <span class="tag">(BrE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">游手好闲；无所事事；混日子<br><span class="en">to spend time being lazy and doing nothing</span></td><td class="c4">We just <b>slobbed out</b> in front of the telly Last night.<br>我们昨晚就看了看电视打发时间。<br>Are you going to <b>slob around</b> in your pyjamas all morning?<br>你是不是要穿着睡衣晃荡一上午？!。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slobber</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈslobber over sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">毫无自尊或节制地对…示爱<br><span class="en">to show, without any pride or control, how much you like or want sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">I know he's in love with you but does he have to <b>slobber over</b> you in public?<br>我知道他爱上了你，但是他非得在大庭广众之下对你大秀恩爱吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslog ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">勤勤恳恳地做<br><span class="en">to work hard and steadily at sth,especially a boring or difficult task, for a long time</span></td><td class="c4">I seem to have been <b>slogging through</b> this book for weeks.<br>我啃这本书似乎有好几个星期了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slop aˈbout/aˈround</b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">(in sth) of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Water was <b>slopping about</b> in the bottom of the boat.<br>水在船底晃。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslop ˈover<br>slop ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Some tea had <b>slopped</b> <b>over</b> into the saucer.<br>一些茶水泼到了茶托上。<br>Water <b>slopped</b> <b>over</b> the edge of the bath.<br>水从浴缸边上溢出来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slope</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slope ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">溜掉；悄悄走开；不告而别<br><span class="en">to go away, espe cially without being noticed, in order to avoid doing work, talking to sb, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Where are you trying to <b>slope off</b> to?<br>你要躲到哪儿去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slosh</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslosh aˈround (also ˌslosh aˈbout especially BrE) (in sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">The water was <b>sloshing</b> <b>about</b> in the bucket.<br>水在桶里哗啦哗啦地直晃荡。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslot ˈin<br>ˌslot ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">正好插入；恰好嵌入(制作或设计好的空间)<br><span class="en">if sth slots in or slots into sth, it fits easily and exactly into a space, especlallly the space made or designed for it</span></td><td class="c4">This bit <b>slots in</b> neatly just here.<br>这一块正好插在这儿。<br>This piece is meant to <b>slot into</b> this groove.<br>这个部件应该插在这个槽里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslot sb/sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">为…安排时间；抽空(见某人或做某事)<br><span class="en">to manage to find a time to see sb or to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">I can <b>slot you in</b> tomorrow at four.<br>我可以把你安排在明天四点钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>slot toˈgether<br>slot A and B toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使严丝合缝地拼合；完全吻合<br><span class="en">if two things slot together, or sb slots them together, they fit together easily and exactly</span></td><td class="c4">The base comes in sections that simply <b>slot together</b>.<br>底座由几个部分插接而成。<br>The parts are ready to be <b>slotted together</b>.<br>部件可随时拼装。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slough</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌslough sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">除掉；去掉(死皮等)<br><span class="en">to remove or get rid of a layer of dead skin, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Slough off</b> dry skin once a week.<br>每周除一次于。<br>Responsibilities not <b>sloughed off</b> so easily.<br>推卸责任绝非易事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈslowdown n</b></td><td class="c3">怠工</td><td class="c4">The union threatened a <b>slowdown</b> if their demands were not met.<br>工会威胁说，如果不答应要求他们就怠工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>slug</b></td><td class="c2"><b>slug it ˈout (BrE also,slog it ˈout) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">斗争；比出胜负；决一雌雄<br><span class="en">to fight; to compete until sb has won</span></td><td class="c4">The two companies <b>slugged it out</b> for their share of the market.<br>两家公司为争夺市场份额一较高下。<br>The Democrats and the Republicans will be <b>slugging it out</b> in November.<br>民主党和共和党将于 11 月一决胜负。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sluice</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sluice sth ˈdown/ˈout <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用水流冲刷；洗净(表面)<br><span class="en">to wash or clean the surface of sth with large amounts of water</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>sluice the streets down</b> every morning.<br>他们每天早晨冲洗街道。<br>An attendant was <b>sluicing out</b> the changing rooms.<br>一名服务员正在冲洗更衣室。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsmack of sth</b></td><td class="c3">带有令人不快；的态度；含有(消极意味)<br><span class="en">to seem to contain an unpleasant attitude or quality</span></td><td class="c4">His comments <b>smack of</b> racism.<br>他的评论带有种族歧视的味道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smart</b></td><td class="c2"><b>smart ˈoff (to sb) <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">言语冒犯；激怒；惹恼(权威人士)<br><span class="en">to say sth that does not show respect to sb in authority</span></td><td class="c4">You are more likely to get a ticket from a cop if you <b>smart off</b> to him or her.<br>对警察说话莽撞放肆，更有可能吃罚单。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smarten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsmarten sb/sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(人或地方)整洁起来；使光彩夺目<br><span class="en">to make a person or a place neater, tidier or more attractive</span></td><td class="c4">The hotel has been <b>smartened up</b> by the new owners.<br>新业主把旅馆修葺一新。<br>She did her best to <b>smarten her husband up</b>.<br>她竭尽全力把丈夫打扮得英俊潇酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmash sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用力击倒；打翻<br><span class="en">to make sth fall by hitting it very hard and breaking it</span></td><td class="c4">The police decided to <b>smash the door down</b>.<br>警察决定破门而入。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmash sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">用力打破；撞坏；毁坏<br><span class="en">to make a hole in sth or destroy it by hitting it very hard</span></td><td class="c4">The doll's face had been <b>smashed in</b>.<br>玩具娃娃的脸被打瘪了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmash ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">车辆或驾驶员<br><span class="en">of a vehicle or a driver</span></td><td class="c4">The car <b>smashed into</b> a tree.<br>汽车猛地撞到树上。<br>I <b>smashed into</b> the car in front.<br>我的汽车猛地撞上前面的汽车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>smash sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">揭毁；破坏<br><span class="en">to damage or destroy sth by hitting it very hard</span></td><td class="c4">A bunch of thugs broke in and <b>smashed the place up</b>.<br>一帮暴徒闯进来把这个地方砸了个稀巴烂。<br>He <b>smashed his car up</b> last week (= he had a crash).<br>他上个星期把汽车撞坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>smell sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">觉察到；意识到危险；麻烦等<br><span class="en">to be aware of fear, danger, trouble, etc. in a situation</span></td><td class="c4">He could <b>smell out</b> weakness in others.<br>他能够抓住他人的弱点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>smell sth ˈout (BrE) (AmE smell sth ˈup)</b></td><td class="c3">使(某处)充满难闻气味；使臭气熏天<br><span class="en">to fill a place with an unpleasant smell</span></td><td class="c4">That fish smelt the whole house <b>out</b>.<br>那鱼让整个房子充满腥味。<br>I burned some milk and <b>smelled</b> up the whole house.<br>我烧糊了牛奶，整个屋子全是一股焦味儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smile</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsmile on/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal or literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">运气；命运等垂青；厚待<br><span class="en">if fortune, fate, etc. smiles on you, you are very lucky and successful</span></td><td class="c4">Fortune <b>smiled on</b> us that night and the plane landed safely.<br>那天夜里我们福星高照，飞机安全着陆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smoke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmoke sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用烟熏<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth come out of a place by filling it with smoke</span></td><td class="c4">The fire is used to <b>smoke the bees out</b>.<br>用火把蜜蜂熏出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmoke sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">查出(坏人或问题根源)；揭露(秘密)；使水落石出<br><span class="en">to find sb/sth that is causing a problem; to make sth that is secret publicly known</span></td><td class="c4">The police are determined to <b>smoke out</b> the leaders of the gang.<br>警方决心揪出犯罪团伙的头目。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>smooth</b></td><td class="c2"><b>smooth sth aˈway/out</b></td><td class="c3">减少；排除；克服(问题或困难)<br><span class="en">to reduce or remove problems and difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">The group was set up to <b>smooth away</b> local difficulties.<br>成立这个组的目的是解决当地的困难。<br>His anxieties were quickly <b>smoothed away</b>.<br>他的忧虑很快就消除了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmooth sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用手将(头发或衣服)弄光滑平整<br><span class="en">to make your hair or your clothes smooth and flat with your hands</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>smoothed down</b> his hair.<br>他把头发抚平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmooth sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">将纸张；布等抚平；使平滑<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a piece of paper or cloth smooth and flat with your hands</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to <b>smooth out</b> the crumpled letter.<br>她试着把皱巴巴的信神平。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsmooth sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">缓和；调解；斡旋<br><span class="en">to make a problem or difficulty seem less serious or easier to deal with, especially by talking to the people involved</span></td><td class="c4">She tried to calm her parents down and <b>smooth things over</b>.<br>她努力让父母冷静下来，同时尝试居中调停。<br>The leaders managed to <b>smooth over</b> their differences.<br>领导们设法消除了他们之间的分歧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsnack on sth</b></td><td class="c3">吃小吃；吃零食<br><span class="en">to eat small amounts of food between or instead of meals</span></td><td class="c4">It's healthier to <b>snack on</b> fruit rather than chocolate.<br>以水果当零嘴比吃巧克力更有益健康。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>snap sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">厉声说出；气势涵汹地说；恶声恶气地说<br><span class="en">to say sth in a sharp or unpleasant way</span></td><td class="c4">The sergeant <b>snapped out</b> an order.<br>中士厉声下达命令。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsnap ˈto it <span class="tag">(informal used)</span></b></td><td class="c3">快点干；加把劲<br><span class="en">to tell sb to start working harder or more quickly</span></td><td class="c4">This place has to be clean by this evening so <b>snap to it</b>!<br>这个地方今晚之前必须弄干净，抓紧干吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsnap sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">争购；疯抢<br><span class="en">to buy or take sth quickly and with enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">Fans quickly <b>snapped up</b> the tickets.<br>狂热的爱好者很快就把门票抢购一空。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snatch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsnatch at sth</b></td><td class="c3">伸手抓；试图夺<br><span class="en">to try to take hold of sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>snatched at</b> the letter in his hand.<br>她伸手去抢他手里的信。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sniff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sniff aˈround<br>ˌsniff aˈround sth/sb (BrE also, sniff ˈround, ˌsniff ˈround sth/sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">探查；打探；访查<br><span class="en">to go somewhere to try to find secret information about sth/sb or to look for a particular person or thing</span></td><td class="c4">The studio was <b>sniffing around</b> for new talent.<br>电影公司在四处物色新秀。<br>It won't be long before the press come <b>sniffing around</b> the club.<br>记者很快就会到这个俱乐部访查的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsniff at sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…嗤之以鼻；对…不眉一顾<br><span class="en">to show a lack of interest in or respect for sth</span></td><td class="c4">At first he <b>sniffed at</b> her foreign ways.<br>起初他对她的洋做派不以为然。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sniff sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">尤指狗</td><td class="c4">These dogs can <b>sniff out</b> explosives.<br>这些犬能嗅出炸药。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌsnowed ˈin/ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">被大雪困住；因大雪滞留<br><span class="en">to be unable to go anywhere or leave a place because of heavy snow</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>got snowed in</b> for three days.<br>我们被大雪困了三天。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get ˌsnowed ˈunder (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">因工作量大不胜负荷；不堪应付；应接不暇<br><span class="en">to have so much work that you have problems dealing with it</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>snowed</b> <b>under</b> with work at the moment.<br>我们现在被工作压得直不起腰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get .snowed ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">道路等</td><td class="c4">The driveway was still snowed <b>up</b>.<br>车行道依然被积雪封阻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snuff</b></td><td class="c2"><b>snuff sb ˈout <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">谋杀；干掉(某人)<br><span class="en">to kill sb</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>snuffed out</b> by the Mafia.<br>他被黑手党干掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>snuff sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">熄灭；扑灭(火焰)<br><span class="en">to stop a flame from burning</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>snuffed out</b> the candles.<br>她掐灭了蜡烛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>snuff sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">突然；结束；扼杀；消灭(某事物)<br><span class="en">to suddenly end or destroy sth</span></td><td class="c4">A moment of mindless violence <b>snuffed out</b> his life.<br>一时无谓的暴力夺去了他的生命。<br>The revolution was quickly <b>snuffed out</b>.<br>那场革命被迅速扼杀了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>snuggle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>snuggle ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">温暖舒适地躺在床上<br><span class="en">to make yourself warm and comfortable in your bed</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>snuggled down</b> and went to sleep.<br>他舒舒服服地躺在床上睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>soak</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsoak ˈin<br>soak ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Apply the oil to the wood and leave it to <b>soak</b> in.<br>把油涂在木头上，让油渗进去。<br>The wine had <b>soaked</b> <b>into</b> the carpet.<br>葡萄酒渗进了地毯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsoak ˈthrough<br>.soakˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">液体<br><span class="en">of a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Blood had <b>soaked through</b> the bandage.<br>血渗透了绷带。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsoak sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">吸收；吸掉(尤指液体)<br><span class="en">to take in or absorb sth, especially a liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Use a Paper towel to <b>soak up</b> the excess oil.<br>用厚纸巾把多余的油吸去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sober</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsober ˈup<br>ˌsober sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使醒酒；清醒<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sb, no longer drunk</span></td><td class="c4">I decided to walk home to <b>sober up</b>.<br>我决定步行回家醒醒酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsock sth aˈway <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通过银行存钱；股票等储存；积攒(钱)<br><span class="en">to save money by putting it in a bank or by buying shares in a company, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She already has $500 <b>socked away</b> for college.<br>她已经存了500元用来上大学。<br>He <b>socks away</b> half his salary every month for the house.<br>他每月将工资的一半攒起来用于买房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsock it to sb <span class="tag">(informal or humorous)</span></b></td><td class="c3">面试；放心大胆地说以给面试官；评委等留下深刻印象<br><span class="en">used to encourage sb to do or say sth that wil have a strong effect, for example before an interview, a sports game, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Youll be fine. Just get in there and <b>sock it to</b> them.<br>没事的。你就直接上那儿给他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sod</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsod ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE, A, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">走开；滚开<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to go away</span></td><td class="c4">Just <b>sod off</b> and leave me in peace!<br>走还点，让我安静会儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>soften</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsoften sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">讨好；打动；诱导<br><span class="en">to try to make sb more willing to do sth for you by being very nice to them first</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>softened the voters up</b> with promises they had no intention of keeping.<br>他们为取悦选民，许下了他们无意兑现的承诺。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>soften sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">软化；削弱；瓦解(敌人)<br><span class="en">to make an_enemy weaker and easier to attack</span></td><td class="c4">The artillery was used to <b>soften up</b> the advancing enemy.<br>炮兵部队被用来遏制向前推进的敌军。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>soldier</b></td><td class="c2"><b>soldier ˈon (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">坚持不懈；不屈不挠；硬挺<br><span class="en">to continue with sth you are doing although it is difficult or unpleasant</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>soldiered on</b> with the course in spite of her personal problems.<br>尽管有些个人困难，她还是坚持上课。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sort</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sort sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">整治；对付；收拾(某人)<br><span class="en">to deal with sb who has been causing trouble</span></td><td class="c4">They sent the lads round to <b>sort him out</b>.<br>他们派了些小伙子去教训他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsort sb/yourself ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">解决某人；自己的问题<br><span class="en">to find a solution to sb's/your own problems, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">It took her months to <b>sort</b> herself <b>out</b> after the divorce.<br>离婚后，她过了好几个月才缓过来。<br>He was so upset it took us an hour to calm him down and <b>sort</b> him <b>out</b>.<br>他十分难过，我们用了一个小时才让他恢复平静、振作起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsort sb ˈout with sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">挑选；选定<br><span class="en">to decide on sth</span></td><td class="c4">I need to <b>sort</b> <b>out</b> what clothes to take with me on the trip.<br>我得想好旅行带什么衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsort sb ˈout with sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">解决(问题)<br><span class="en">to solve a problem</span></td><td class="c4">Weve <b>sorted</b> the problem <b>out</b>.<br>我们把问题解决了。<br>She <b>sorted</b> <b>out</b> the clothes that she didn't wear any more.<br>她把不再穿的衣服挑了出来。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsort itself ˈout <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">问题自行化解<br><span class="en">if a problem sorts itself out, it stops being a problem without anyone having to do anything</span></td><td class="c4">He woke up feeling ill, but thought the problem would soon <b>sort itself out</b>.<br>他醒来后感觉不适，可他认为很快就会自动好起来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsort ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">翻找；归整<br><span class="en">to look through a number of things either in order to find a particular thing or to put them in groups</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>sorted through</b> her wardrobe for something to wear.<br>她翻遍衣柜找衣服穿。<br>They <b>sorted through</b> thousands of old photos.<br>他们收拾整理了几千张旧照片。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sound</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sound ˈoff (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大声或盛气凌人地高谈阔论；夸夸其谈<br><span class="en">to express your opinions loudly or in an aggressive way</span></td><td class="c4">He should check his facts before <b>sounding off</b> like that.<br>他应该先核实一下实情再那样大发宏论。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsound sb/sth ˈout (about/on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">试探某人(对某事)的看法；向…探口风<br><span class="en">to try to discover sb's views, opinions, etc. on sth, especially in an indirect way</span></td><td class="c4">I want to <b>sound him out</b> about a possible job.<br>我想探探他的口风，看能不能得到一份工作。<br>We should <b>sound out</b> opinions on these changes.<br>我们应该试探一下人们对这些变革的看法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>soup</b></td><td class="c2"><b>soup sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">改装汽车；计算机等以增强功能<br><span class="en">if you soup up a car, a computer, etc., you make changes to it so that it is more powerful or exciting</span></td><td class="c4">He makes a living buying old cars and <b>souping them up</b>.<br>他买来旧车进行改装，加大马力，并以此为生。</td></tr>
