<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>space</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌSpace especially AmE</b></td><td class="c3">因服用药物等精神恍惚；使神志不清<br><span class="en">to be confused, unable to think clearly, or not aware of what is happening around you, for example as a result of taking drugs; to put sb in a state like this</span></td><td class="c4">I was supposed to meet her for lunch but I <b>spaced</b> out and forgot.<br>我本应该和她共进午餐，可我迷迷糊糊地给忘了。<br>The drugs I was taking for my illness <b>spaced</b> me out so 1 couldn't think clearly.<br>我火治病吃的药把我弄得头昏脑涨，神志不清。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>space sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使拉开(空间或时间上)的间距；使隔开</td><td class="c4">Try <b>spacing the words out</b> more on the page.<br>把页面上的字间距再拉大些。<br>Should I <b>space out</b> the baby's feeds over 24 hours?<br>我是不是应该在 24 小时中分多次喂宝宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spark</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spark sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使爆发(或发展)；引发；导致<br><span class="en">to cause sth to suddenly happen or develop</span></td><td class="c4">The incident <b>sparked off</b> riots across the country.<br>这一事件激起了全国各地的骚乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spark ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">死灰复燃<br><span class="en">if a fire sparks up, it starts to burn brightly again after a period when it was almost out</span></td><td class="c4">The fire is still smoking and could <b>spark up</b> at any moment.<br>那火堆还在冒烟，随时会再燃烧起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spark sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">突然开始交谈；争论；交友等<br><span class="en">if you spark up a conversation, a debate, a friendship, etc., you start one, often suddenly</span></td><td class="c4">I sat down beside Helen and tried to <b>spark up</b> a conversation with her.<br>我在海伦旁边坐下，想和她攀谈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spark sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给…增添趣味；增加…的兴致<br><span class="en">to add interest or excitement to sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Spark up</b> pasta dishes with fresh herbs.<br>用新鲜香草给意大利面食调味。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>speak</b></td><td class="c2"><b>speak for yourˈself</b></td><td class="c3">表达自己的观点；发表个人；意见<br><span class="en">to express your own opinion, although you know that others might not agree with you</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>speaks for</b> himself when he says we need a smoking area.<br>他说我们需要一个吸烟区，这是他个人的意见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈspeak of sth <span class="tag">(formal, literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为…提供证据；说明；意味着<br><span class="en">to be evidence of sth; to suggest sth</span></td><td class="c4">The pictures in the room <b>spoke of dreams of</b> faraway places.<br>房间里的图画表达了对遥远地方的向往之情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,speak ˈout (against/in favour of/on sth)</b></td><td class="c3">大胆地说；挺身而出；站出来表示反对；支持等<br><span class="en">to say what you think clearly and publicly, often criticizing or opposing sb/sth, in a way that needs courage</span></td><td class="c4">People are no longer afraid to speak <b>out</b>.<br>人们再也不怕站出来说话了。<br>She spoke <b>out</b> forcefully against the regime.<br>她公开拌击该政权。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈspeakout n <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">座谈会<br><span class="en">an organized public meeting at which people talk about their experiences of a particular subject</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Speakouts</b> are good because they encourage people to talk about things in a positive way.<br>畅言聚会很不错，因为它鼓励人们以正面态度谈论各种事情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>speed</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspeed aˈway/ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">驾车；骑车等迅速离开<br><span class="en">to leave very quickly, usually in a vehicle of some kind</span></td><td class="c4">The car sped <b>away</b> from the house.<br>那辆车快速驶离了那所房子。<br>She sped <b>off</b> on her bike.<br>她骑着自行车飞驰而去。<br>Parking restrictions were introduced to try to <b>speed</b> up the traffic.<br>为了使交通提速推行了限制停车的措施。<br>They worked slowly at first, <b>speeding</b> up as they got used to it.<br>他们一开始慢慢地做，等熟练后便加快了进度。<br>The new tool <b>speeds</b> things up.<br>新工具提高了效率。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spell sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">讲清楚；解释明白；详细解释<br><span class="en">to make sth clear and easy to understand; to explain sth in detail</span></td><td class="c4">His reasons for leaving are spelt <b>out</b> in detail in his letter.<br>他在信中详细解释了他离开的原因。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spew</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spew ˈup<br>spew sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">呕吐；呕出<br><span class="en">to bring food from the stomach back out through the mouth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>spewed up</b> all over my jacket.<br>他把我的夹克衫吐得到处都是。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spice</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspice sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用调味品给(食物)调味<br><span class="en">to add spice to food in order to give it more flavour and make it more interesting</span></td><td class="c4">Casseroles can be <b>spiced up</b> with a dash of tabasco sauce.<br>炖锅菜里可加一点塔巴斯科辣椒酱调调味。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spill ˈout<br>.spill ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从容器中意外地流出；溢出；泼出<br><span class="en">to accidentally flow out of a container</span></td><td class="c4">The contents of her bag <b>spilled out</b> everywhere.<br>她袋子里的东西撒得到处都是。<br>Water had <b>spilled out</b> onto the floor.<br>水溅到了地板上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spill ˈout<br>.spill ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">大量出现；涌出<br><span class="en">to come out in large numbers or amounts</span></td><td class="c4">The theatre crowds <b>spilled out</b> onto the pavement.<br>剧院的观众纷纷涌上人行道。<br>The children <b>spilled out</b> into the yard.<br>孩子们蜂拥到院子里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spill ˈout<br>spill sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">不经意间倾诉；倾吐；吐露秘密；畏惧；忧虑等<br><span class="en">to tell sb a secret, your fears, worries, etc. without intending to</span></td><td class="c4">When she started to speak, the words just came <b>spilling Out</b>.<br>她一张开嘴便全说了出来。<br>She <b>spilled out</b> her troubles to her parents.<br>她向父母倾吐了烦恼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspill ˈover (into/to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">波及；带动；影响到(另一范围)；嬗变；蜕变成另；一局面<br><span class="en">to start in one situation or area and then have an effect on another situation or in another area</span></td><td class="c4">Unrest has spilt <b>over</b> into areas outside the city.<br>骚乱已经波及城市的周边地区。<br>Anger <b>spilled over</b> into violence at yesterday's demonstration.<br>在昨天的示威游行中，愤怒演化成了暴力。<br>Her excitement <b>spilled over</b> to the rest of the group.<br>她的兴奋情绪感染了这个组的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspill ˈover<br>spill ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">溢出；漫出<br><span class="en">to flow over the edge of a container that is too full</span></td><td class="c4">The water <b>spilled over</b> the rim of the glass.<br>水从玻璃杯口溢出来了。<br>Her tears suddenly <b>spilled over</b> (= she started to cry).<br>她突然眼泪奔涌而出。<br>The goods were <b>spilling over</b> from the shops onto the pavements.<br>货物从店铺里一直摆到了人行道上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spin</b></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌspin ˈround<br>spin sb/sth ˈround</b></td><td class="c3">使迅速转身；猛然后转<br><span class="en">to turn very quickly to face in the opposite direction; to turn sb/sth in this way</span></td><td class="c4">She heard her name and <b>spun</b> around to see the speaker.<br>她听到自己的名字，马上回过身去看说话的人。<br>He <b>spun</b> her <b>round</b> to face him.<br>他拉她转过身面对着自己。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌspin ˈround<br>spin sb/sth ˈround</b></td><td class="c3">使快速旋转<br><span class="en">to turn round and round quickly; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">The propeller started to <b>spin</b> around.<br>螺旋桨开始飞速旋转起来。?。<br>The wheels were <b>spinning</b> <b>round</b> in the mud.<br>轮子在泥中空转个不停。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spirit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spirit sb/sth aˈway/ˈoff (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">迅速；秘密或变魔术般地弄走；带走；转移；不翼而飞<br><span class="en">to remove sb/sth quickly, secretly or as if by magic</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>spirited away</b> by his friends before the police arrived.<br>朋友们赶在警察到来前把他悄悄转移了。<br>An enormous amount of money had been <b>spirited away</b> in only two months.<br>一笔巨款仅仅两个月就被神秘转走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spit it ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">说出来；有什么尽管说<br><span class="en">used to tell sb to reveal a piece of information or to say sth when they are feeling nervous or unwilling to speak</span></td><td class="c4">Come on, <b>spit it out</b>! Who did it?<br>爽快点，说出来吧！是谁干的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spit sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">吐出<br><span class="en">to force sth out of your mouth</span></td><td class="c4">It tasted so horrible he had to <b>spit it out</b>.<br>那东西味道差极了，他只好吐了出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>splash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>splash sth aˈbout/aˈround <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">随意地乱花(钱)；大肆挥霍<br><span class="en">to spend money freely or carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>splashes his wages about</b> just to impress her.<br>他大手大脚地花工资只是为了讨好她。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>splash sth aˈcross/oˈver sth</b></td><td class="c3">把照片；在(引人注目的位置)刊载<br><span class="en">to publish a photograph, a news story, etc. in a place where a lot of people will see it, especially in a newspaper</span></td><td class="c4">The next day her name was <b>splashed across</b> all the front pages.<br>第二天，她的名字出现在所有报纸头版的显著位置。<br>I don't want my private life <b>splashed all over</b> the tabloids.<br>我不想让我的私生活被那些小报大肆曝光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsplash aˈround (BrE also ˌsplash aˈbout) (in sth)</b></td><td class="c3">在水中起水花行进；便水花<br><span class="en">to move about in water making it fly everywhere</span></td><td class="c4">The children <b>splashed about</b> in the river all afternoon.<br>孩子们整个下午都在河里玩水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsplash ˈout (on sth)<br>ˌsplash sth ˈout (on/for sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">花大笔的钱(买某物)<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of money on sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>splashed</b> <b>out</b> on a new pair of shoes.<br>她花很多钱买了双新鞋。<br>The band <b>splashed</b> <b>out</b> thousands on new equipment.<br>乐队花了好几千购置新设备。<br>Don't <b>splash</b> it all <b>out</b> at once!<br>别把钱一下子挥霍光！n+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>split</b></td><td class="c2"><b>split aˈway/ˈoff (from sth)<br>split sth aˈway/ˈoff (from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">从…中脱离；分裂出去；分离<br><span class="en">to separate from, or be separated from, a large object or a group</span></td><td class="c4">The branch had <b>split</b> <b>away</b> from the trunk.<br>那根树枝是从树干上折下的。<br>The wind <b>split</b> the door <b>away</b> from its frame.<br>风把门从门框上刮了下来。<br>Should the ownership of the rail track be <b>split</b> <b>off</b> from the running of the train services?<br>铁路的所有权是否应该从火车服务营运中分离出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsplit on sb (to sb) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向某人告发某人；揭发某人<br><span class="en">to tell sb in authority about sth bad or wrong that sb has done</span></td><td class="c4">Promise you won't <b>split on</b> me.<br>你要答应不出卖我。<br>The band <b>split</b> up at the height of their fame.<br>乐队在最走红的时候散伙了。<br>My friend is doing her best to <b>split</b> Maria and me up.<br>我的朋友竭力想拆散我和玛丽亚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>split ˈup (into sth)<br>split sb/sth ˈup (into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把集体或家庭分散；化整为零<br><span class="en">if a group of people or a family splits up, or sb splits it up, the members separate and do not stay together</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>split</b> up into groups to discuss the question.<br>我们分组讨论了那个问题。<br>The class was <b>split</b> up into groups.<br>已在班上分了组。<br>We got <b>split</b> up in the crowd.<br>我们在人群中走散了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>split sth ˈup (into sth)</b></td><td class="c3">划分；分解(若干部分)<br><span class="en">to divide sth into smaller parts</span></td><td class="c4">The day was <b>split up</b> into six one-hour classes.<br>一天分成六节课，每节课一小时。<br>We <b>split the profits up</b> between us.<br>我们把利润分了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spoil</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈspoiling for sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">只用于进行时<br><span class="en">only used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>was spoiling for</b> a fight.<br>他攒足了劲儿想打架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sponge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sponge sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用湿布(或软材料)清洗<br><span class="en">to wash sb/sth with a wet cloth or a soft material</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>sponged the coat down</b> to remove the mud.<br>我用湿布擦洗掉外套上的泥。<br>She tried <b>sponging the baby down</b> to lower his temperature.<br>她试着用湿毛巾给孩子降体温。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsponge off sb (also ˈsponge on sb less frequent) <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">某人处白拿钱；食物等；蹭吃蹭喝；揩油<br><span class="en">to get money, food, etc. from other people, without doing anything for them or offering to pay</span></td><td class="c4">He's constantly <b>sponging off</b> his friends.<br>他经常占朋友的便宜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sponge sth ˈoff<br>ˌsponge sth ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用湿布(或软材料)除掉污渍；灰尘<br><span class="en">to remove a mark, some dirt, etc. with a wet cloth or a piece of a soft material</span></td><td class="c4">It was impossible to <b>sponge the mark off</b>.<br>这块污斑不可能擦掉。<br>I couldn't <b>sponge the stain off</b> my dress.<br>我擦不掉我连衣裙上的污渍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spout</b></td><td class="c2"><b>spout ˈoff/ˈon (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…喋喋不休；唠叨<br><span class="en">to talk about sth in a borig or annoying way</span></td><td class="c4">He's always <b>spouting off</b> about the behaviour of young people today.<br>他总是没完没了地数落如今年轻人的行为。<br>What are you <b>spouting on</b> about now?<br>你在啰唆什么呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spread</b></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>spread ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐扩展；扩散；蔓延<br><span class="en">to gradually cover a wider area</span></td><td class="c4">The city has <b>spread out</b> into what used to be countryside.<br>城市渐渐延伸到了从前的乡村。<br>The ripples <b>spread out</b> across the water.<br>连漪在水面荡开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>spread ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">人群散开<br><span class="en">(also,spread yourselvesˈout) to move away from others in a group so as to cover a wider area</span></td><td class="c4">The search party <b>spread out</b> over the moor.<br>搜索队在旷野四面散开。<br>Don't all sit together. <b>Spread yourselves out</b>.<br>别都挨在一块儿坐，分开坐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>spread ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">伸展身体；摊开<br><span class="en">(also,spread yourself ˈout) to stretch your body or arrange your things over a large area</span></td><td class="c4">There's more room to <b>spread out</b> in business class.<br>商务舱宽敞些，伸得开腿。<br>Do you have to <b>spread yourself out</b> all over the sofa?<br>你就非得摊开手脚，把整个沙发全占了？1v+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspread ˈout<br>be ˌspread ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">伸展开来<br><span class="en">to cover a wide area</span></td><td class="c4">The valley <b>spread out</b> beneath us.<br>开阔的山谷出现在我们脚下。<br>We looked down at the city <b>spread out</b> below us.<br>我们俯瞰下面面积广大的城市。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>spread sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">摆开；摊开(一组物品)<br><span class="en">to arrange a group of objects on a surface so that you can see them all clearly</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Spread out</b> all the pieces before you begin the jigsaw.<br>拼图之前先把所有的小拼片摊开。<br>All the brochures were <b>spread out</b> on the floor.<br>小册子全都摆放在地板上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>spread sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">打开；展开折起的；东西<br><span class="en">to open sth that is folded and put it down on a flat surface</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>spread the blanket out</b> on the grass.<br>他们把毯子铺在草地上。<br>The map had been <b>spread out</b> on the table.<br>地图在桌上摊开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>spread sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">时间或按人分摊；分派；把…分期(或分担)完成<br><span class="en">(over sth) to separate sth into parts and arrange them over a period of time or divide them between different people</span></td><td class="c4">The cost can be <b>spread out</b> over two years.<br>成本可分摊到两年中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spring</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈspring from sth</b></td><td class="c3">由…造成；起源于<br><span class="en">to be caused by sth; to start from sth</span></td><td class="c4">Aggression often <b>springs from</b> fear.<br>攻击行为常常出自恐惧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈspring from sth</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于；疑问句<br><span class="en">usually used in questions</span></td><td class="c4">Where on earth did you <b>spring from</b>?<br>你究竟是从哪儿冒出来的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>spring ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">迅速或突然出现；发展；生长<br><span class="en">to appear, develop, grow, etc. quickly or suddenly</span></td><td class="c4">Weeds were <b>springing up</b> everywhere.<br>到处杂草丛生。<br>New industries were <b>springing up</b> all over the country.<br>各种新行业如雨后春笋般在全国各地出现。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spur</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌspur sb ˈon (to sth/to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">鼓励；激励；鞭策<br><span class="en">to encourage sb to act in a particular way, especially to work harder or to try to achieve sth</span></td><td class="c4">Her difficult childhood <b>spurred her on</b> to succeed.<br>她苦难的童年促使她努力争取出人头地。<br>His parents' encouragement <b>spurred him on</b> to greater efforts.<br>父母的鼓励促使他更加努力。<br><b>Spurred on</b> by this victory, we went on to win the championship.<br>在这次胜利的鼓舞下，我们接着赢得了冠军。<br>Their shouts of encouragement <b>spurred us on</b>.<br>他们助威的吶喊声激励着我们。态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spurt</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sth ˈout<br>ˌspurt sth ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…中喷出；冒出；涌出<br><span class="en">to come out of sth in a sudden or fast stream; to pour out a sudden fast stream of liquid or flames</span></td><td class="c4">Water spurted <b>out</b> of the hole.<br>水从小孔中喷射出来。<br>The volcano was spurting <b>out</b> rivers of molten lava.<br>火山喷涌着熔岩。n。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>spy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈspy on sb/sth (also ˈspy upon sb/sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">暗中监视；窥探；侦查<br><span class="en">to watch sb/sth secretly</span></td><td class="c4">He hired a detective to <b>spy on</b> his wife.<br>他雇了侦探暗中监视他的妻子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>square</b></td><td class="c2"><b>square ˈoff (against sb) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">和某人打斗；摆好架势(和某人)打斗<br><span class="en">to fight or to prepare to fight sb</span></td><td class="c4">The two candidates will <b>square off</b> in a debare tomorrow.<br>两名候选人将在明天的电视辩论中交锋。<br>Protesting students <b>squared off</b> against police.<br>抗议的学生和警察发生了冲突。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>square ˈoff (against sb) <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">勇敢面对；毅然面对<br><span class="en">(to sb/sth) to face a difficult situation determined way</span></td><td class="c4">He must <b>square</b> up to the reality of being out of work.<br>他必须直面失业的现实。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsquare with sth<br>ˈsquare sth with sth</b></td><td class="c3">使与…一致；与…相符<br><span class="en">to agree with another fact, idea or situation; to make two facts, etc. agree with each other</span></td><td class="c4">This doesn't <b>square with</b> what you told us earlier.<br>这与你先前告诉我们的有出入。<br>How do you <b>square your profession with</b> your religious beliefs?<br>你如何使你从事的职业和你的宗教信仰协调一致。<br>The interests of farmers need to be <b>squared with</b> those of consumers.<br>农场主的利益要和消费者的利益相一致。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsquare sth with sb</b></td><td class="c3">就…征得某人批准(或认可)<br><span class="en">to get sb's approval before you do sth</span></td><td class="c4">You'd better <b>square it with</b> the boss if you want to leave early.<br>你要是想提前下班，最好征得老板的同意。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>squeak</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsqueak ˈby <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">艰难地(或勉强)取得成功<br><span class="en">to achieve successful result with great difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">We just <b>squeaked by</b> in the semi-final.<br>我们在半决赛中险胜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>squeakˈthrough<br>ˌsqueak ˈthrough sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">勉力取得成功；勉强通过<br><span class="en">to manage to achieve sth or get a successful result with great difficulty</span></td><td class="c4">Andrew <b>squeaked through</b> the qualifying rounds of the championship.<br>安德鲁侥幸通过了锦标赛的资格赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>squirrel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsquirrel sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">储藏；贮存<br><span class="en">to put sth, especially money, in a safe place so that you can use it later</span></td><td class="c4">She had money <b>squirrelled away</b> in various accounts.<br>她把钱存在不同的银行账户上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstack ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">积聚成一大垛(或一长排等)；加起来<br><span class="en">to increase gradually until there is a large pile, a long line, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Over the months he just let the paperwork <b>stack up</b>.<br>几个月间，他就那么让文案工作积压成堆。<br>The traffic quickly <b>stacked up</b> behind the bus.<br>公共汽车后面的车辆很快排成了长龙。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstack ˈup<br>ˌstack sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">飞机作分层盘旋(等待降落)<br><span class="en">if planes stack up or are stacked up over an airport, there are a lot of them flying around waiting to land</span></td><td class="c4">Planes <b>stacked up</b> at Heathrow after an accident on the runway.<br>由于跑道上出了事故，K机在希思岁机场上空作分层盘旋。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stack sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">堆起；摞起<br><span class="en">to arrange things in a tall pile</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stacked up</b> the dishes on the draining board.<br>他把碟子摞在滴水板上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stack sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐得到更多；累积<br><span class="en">to gradually get more of sth</span></td><td class="c4">She's <b>stacking up</b> the college credits with all of her night classes.<br>她上很多晚上的课程来积累大学学分。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stake</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstake sth on sth<br>ˈstake sth on doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">以…打赌<br><span class="en">to risk money or sth very important on the result of sth or on sth happening</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>staked twenty pounds on</b> the favourite (= in horse racing, for example).<br>他在那匹众人看好的马上押了二十英镑。<br>Several journalists <b>staked their reputation on</b> Bush winning the election.<br>有几个记者拿声誉担保布什能贏得选举。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">界定(属于自己的地区)；划出(自己的势力范围)；圈(地)<br><span class="en">to mark the position and the limits of a piece of land or an area to show that you own it</span></td><td class="c4">The male <b>stakes out</b> his territory and defends it from other birds.<br>雄鸟标出自己的地盘，保护它不受其他鸟侵犯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">表明(立场或意见)<br><span class="en">to state your position or opinion on sth clearly</span></td><td class="c4">The President <b>staked out</b> his position on the issue.<br>总统阐明了他在这个问题上的立场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">警方监视(某处)<br><span class="en">if police stake out a building, they watch it secretly and continuously because they think sth illegal is happening there</span></td><td class="c4">Armed police have been <b>staking out</b> the house for two weeks.<br>武装警察监视这所房子已两个星期了。<br>The cops had the building <b>staked out</b>.<br>警察把这处建筑监视了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstake-out n</b></td><td class="c3">警方监视<br><span class="en">a situation when police watch a building continuously and secretly because they think sth illegal is happening there</span></td><td class="c4">The <b>stake-out</b> at the house produced nothing.<br>监视这所房子没有什么收获。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stamp</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstamp on sth</b></td><td class="c3">重踩；用力跺<br><span class="en">to bring your foot down on sth with force</span></td><td class="c4">The child <b>stamped on</b> the spider.<br>小孩使劲踩那只蛛。<br>She <b>stamped on</b> his foot as hard as she could.<br>她使出全身力气踩他的脚。<br>The victim had been kicked and <b>stamped on</b>.<br>受害者遭人踢踹踩踏。<br>A child ran out into the road and I had to <b>stamp on</b> the brakes.<br>有个小孩跑到马路上，我只好用力踩刹车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstamp on sth</b></td><td class="c3">压制；镇压<br><span class="en">to control sth or stop sth from happening by force</span></td><td class="c4">This kind of disobedience must be <b>stamped on at once</b>.<br>此类反抗行为必须立刻压制住。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstamp sth on sth</b></td><td class="c3">在…上打；上…印记；把…铭刻在…中<br><span class="en">to make sth have an important effect or influence on sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stamped her own interpretation on</b> the role.<br>她赋予这一角色自己的诠释。<br>The date is forever <b>stamped on</b> her memory.<br>那个日子永远铭刻在她的记忆中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stamp sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">通过暴力或不懈努力消除；消灭；摧毁<br><span class="en">to destroy or get rid of sth bad or unpleasant by force or with a lot of effort</span></td><td class="c4">They aim to <b>stamp out</b> drug dealing in schools.<br>他们力争取缔校园里的毒品交易。<br>The party chairman is determined to <b>stamp out</b> corruption.<br>党主席决心杜绝腐败现象。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">站到一边；站开；让开<br><span class="en">to move to one side to let sb/sth pass</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stand aside</b> please and let her through.<br>请站开，让她过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">参与；不介入<br><span class="en">to take no part in events; to do nothing</span></td><td class="c4">I can't <b>stand aside</b> and let you waste an opportunity like that.<br>我不能不管不问，让你把那样的机会浪费掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">退居一旁；让位于人<br><span class="en">to stop doing a job so that sb else can do it</span></td><td class="c4">It's time he <b>stood aside</b> and let somebody younger take his place.<br>他该引退并让位给年轻 E。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">位于远离…的地方<br><span class="en">to be located at a distance from sth</span></td><td class="c4">The house <b>stands</b> back from the road.<br>房子离公路有一段距离。<br>This is an opportunity to <b>stand</b> back and think about what you have achieved.<br>这是一个客观思考自己有何建树的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand beˈtween A and B</b></td><td class="c3">在…和…之间隔着；阻止<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from doing or having sth, or being in a particular situation</span></td><td class="c4">Only three people <b>stood</b> <b>between</b> him and the crown(= becoming king).<br>妨碍他登上王位的只有三个人。<br>Your lack of confidence is all that <b>stands</b> <b>between</b> you and a much better job.<br>缺乏自信是你得到更好工作的唯一障碍。<br>I can't <b>stand</b> by and see you ruin your life.<br>我不能眼睁睁看着你毁了自己的一生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand beˈtween A and B</b></td><td class="c3">作好准备(以便随时行动)；待命；候命<br><span class="en">(for sth) to be ready to take appropriate action</span></td><td class="c4">The pilot was instructed to <b>stand</b> by for take-off.<br>飞行员接到指示作好随时起飞飞的准备。<br>Fire crews are <b>standing</b> by in case of an explosion.<br>消防队员严阵以待，如有爆炸立刻出动。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈbystander n</b></td><td class="c3">旁观者</td><td class="c4">Two innocent <b>bystanders</b> were hit by stray bullets.<br>两名无辜的旁观者被流弹击中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstand by sth</b></td><td class="c3">遵守原先的诺言；协议<br><span class="en">to continue to believe sth you said earlier even though the situation may now be different</span></td><td class="c4">Ill <b>stand by</b> what I said earlier.<br>我会恪守我说过的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">离职；下台；退出(比赛等)<br><span class="en">(as/from sth) to leave a job or position; to stop taking part in a race or a competition, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stood down</b> after only three months as chairman.<br>她只当了三个月主席就下台了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">命令(人员)撤离；指示(设备)停工<br><span class="en">to give an official order that a group of people, equipment, etc. should no longer be in operation</span></td><td class="c4">The regiment will be <b>stood down</b> from next month.<br>该团自下月起将被撤回。<br>I hated him and all he <b>stood</b> for.<br>我讨厌他，也讨厌他的一切主张。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand ˈin (for sb)</b></td><td class="c3">代替；顶替(某人)<br><span class="en">to take sb's place</span></td><td class="c4">We'll need someone to <b>stand in</b> for you while you're away.<br>你不在期间，我们需要有个人顶替你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstand-in n</b></td><td class="c3">职位或工作的临时替代者</td><td class="c4">Tom as my <b>stand-in</b> while 1 was abroad.<br>我出国期间由汤姆代职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand ˈover sb</b></td><td class="c3">监督；监视(某人)<br><span class="en">to remain close to sb and watch them, usually to make sure that they behave or do sth correctly</span></td><td class="c4">She won't do her homework unless Istand <b>over</b> the cast, two in particular <b>stood</b> out.<br>在所有演员当中，有两位演技特别出众。<br>There will be lots of applications for the job, so yours really needs to <b>stand</b> out.<br>这份工作会有很多人应聘，所以你确实需要胜人一筹才行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stand ˈround<br>ˌstand ˈround sb/sth (BrE) AROUND, A SB/ B<br>stand ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">站立；站起；起立<br><span class="en">to rise to your feet from a sitting or lying position; to be on your feet</span></td><td class="c4">Darcy <b>stood up</b> when Emma came into the room.<br>埃玛一进房间，达西就站了起来。<br>There was silence when the President <b>stood up</b> to speak.<br>总统起身讲话，会场静了下来。<br><b>Stand up</b> straight instead of slouching.<br>站直身子，别歪歪斜斜的。<br>Horses can sleep <b>standing up</b>.<br>马能站着睡觉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stand ˈround<br>ˌstand ˈround sb/sth (BrE) AROUND, A SB/ B<br>stand ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">经得起考验；审查等；站得住脚<br><span class="en">(to sth) to remain true or correct tested, examined closely, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Your theory doesn't <b>stand up</b> to close examination.<br>你的理论经不起仔细推敲。<br>His story won't <b>stand up</b> under cross-examination.<br>他的陈述经不起详细请问。<br>He <b>stood</b> tour well.<br>演员们在巡回演出中丝毫未显疲态。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stand ˈround<br>ˌstand ˈround sb/sth (BrE) AROUND, A SB/ B<br>stand ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">争论；打斗；等激烈的</td><td class="c4">He had a <b>stand</b>-up row with the team captain.<br>他和队长大吵了一架。3。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stand sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指恋人故意失约使某人空等<br><span class="en">to deliberately fail to meet sb you have arranged to meet, especially sb you are having a romantic relationship with</span></td><td class="c4">We agreed to meet at the cinema but she <b>stood me up</b>.<br>我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>stand ˈup for sb/sth/yourself</b></td><td class="c3">支持；维护<br><span class="en">to support or defend sb/sth/yourself, especially when sb is criticizing them/it/you</span></td><td class="c4">She's always <b>stood</b> up for her friends.<br>她总是为朋友辩解。<br>He's always telling her what to do. It's time she <b>stood</b> up for herself!<br>他总是对她指手画脚。现在她该挺身保护自己了。<br>James doesn't need you to <b>stand</b> up for him.<br>詹姆斯不需要你为他辩护。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstand ˈup to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">抵抗；勇敢维护；反抗(不公正待遇)<br><span class="en">to resist sb/sth; to defend your position against a more powerful organization that is treating you badly or unfairly</span></td><td class="c4">It was difficult for Paul to <b>stand</b> father's rage.<br>保罗难以招架父亲的暴怒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stare</b></td><td class="c2"><b>stare sb ˈout (BrE) (also.,stare sb ˈdown AmE, BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">盯得某人转移目光(或慌了神)<br><span class="en">to look sb directly in the eyes for a long time until they feel forced to lower their eyes or look away</span></td><td class="c4">He was looking at her intently but she <b>stared him out</b>.<br>他热切地看着她，可她盯得他移开了目光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>start</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstart ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">动身(或启程)返回<br><span class="en">to begin to return somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">It's time we <b>started back</b>.<br>我们该回去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstart for</b></td><td class="c3">动身去；启程前往<br><span class="en">to leave one place to go to another</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>started for</b> home.<br>我们动身回家了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstart ˈin (on sth) <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始做(某事)<br><span class="en">to begin to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">Let's <b>start in</b> now and get the job done quickly.<br>咱们现在就动手快点把活儿干完吧。<br>It's time you <b>started in</b> on your homework.<br>你该做家庭作业了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>start ˈover<br>start sth ˈover <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">重新开始；从头开始再做(某事)<br><span class="en">to begin doing sth again, especially because you were not successful the first time</span></td><td class="c4">I messed up and had to <b>start</b> <b>over</b>.<br>我搞砸了，不得不返工。<br>It took me a while to <b>start</b> up the generator.<br>我费了点时间启动发电机。<br>I heard the car <b>starting</b> up.<br>我听见汽车发动了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>start ˈover<br>start sth ˈover <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始营运或；经营；创办<br><span class="en">(in sth) to start operating or trading; to establish a business</span></td><td class="c4">When I <b>started</b> up in business, I needed a lot of help.<br>创业之初，我需要诸多帮助。<br>There are a lot of small businesses <b>starting</b> up in the area.<br>区内小企业大量涌现。<br>My father helped me <b>start</b> up my own company.<br>父亲帮助我创办了自己的公司。p。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstart-up n</b></td><td class="c3">新公司；创业公司；(尤指)新网络公司<br><span class="en">a company that is just beginning to operate, especially an Internet company</span></td><td class="c4">This is just one of the problems facing <b>start-ups</b> in this highly competitive area.<br>这只是新互联网公司在这个竞争激烈的领域中面临的诸多问题中的一个。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>starve</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstarve for sth<br>ˈstarve sb/sth for sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">渴求；急需；使缺乏<br><span class="en">to feel you do not have sth that you really need; to prevent sb/sth from having sth necessary or very important</span></td><td class="c4">Sam was <b>starving for</b> a kind word from Clare.<br>萨姆渴望听到克莱尔一句体贴的话。<br>The children were <b>starved for</b> affection.<br>这些孩子渴望关爱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstarve sb into sth<br>ˈstarve sb into doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">某事<br><span class="en">to force sb to do sth or accept sth by preventing them from getting food or</span></td><td class="c4">The aim was to <b>starve</b> the enemy <b>Into</b> submission.<br>目的是断绝敌人的粮食，迫使他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>stash sth aˈway <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">藏起；隐藏<br><span class="en">to store sth in a secret or safe place</span></td><td class="c4">She has a fortune <b>stashed away</b> in various bank accounts.<br>她在不同的银行账户上秘密存了一大笔钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stave</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstave sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">使向内塌陷；压凹<br><span class="en">to break sth by hitting it with force and making part of it fall</span></td><td class="c4">The side of the boat was <b>staved in</b> when it hit the rocks.<br>船撞上了礁石，把船舷撞扁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stay</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay aˈhead<br>ˌstay</b></td><td class="c3">保持；领先；占上风</td><td class="c4">We need to keep an eye on our competitors if we want to <b>stay ahead</b>.<br>我们要保持领先地位，就得时刻留神竞争对手。<br>He <b>stayed ahead</b> of me throughout the race.<br>整个赛跑过程中他一直冲在我前面。<br>More investment is needed if we are to <b>stay ahead</b> of the game (= be more successful than our competitors).<br>我们要想立于不败之地就得追加投资。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>stay aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">离开；不接近危险；讨厌的人或事物；不去(某处)；不沾染(某物)<br><span class="en">to not go near sb/sth dangerous or unpleasant; to have nothing to do with sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stay away</b> from the edge!<br>不要靠近边缘。<br>He advised us to <b>stay away</b> from drugs.<br>他告诫我们远离毒品。<br>The police have asked the public to <b>stay away</b>.<br>警方已要求公众保持距离。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">呆在原地；退后<br><span class="en">to remain in a place and not move forward</span></td><td class="c4">The police shouted to the crowd to <b>stay back</b>.<br>警方向人群叫喊，让他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay beˈhind (after sth)</b></td><td class="c3">活动结束后留下<br><span class="en">to remain in a place at the end of an event after other people have left</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stayed behind</b> after the meeting for a chat.<br>会议结束后，她留下来和人闲聊。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">保持在低处<br><span class="en">to remain in a low position</span></td><td class="c4">The blind won't <b>stay down</b>.<br>窗帘总是放不下来。<br>Get down and <b>stay down</b> or hell see you!<br>趴下别起来，不然他就看见你了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">固定在里面<br><span class="en">to remain in a position inside sth</span></td><td class="c4">This nail won't <b>stay in</b>.<br>这颗钉子就是钉不牢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">呆在家里；不外出<br><span class="en">to remain at home or inside a building</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas ill and had to <b>stay in</b> all week.<br>我生病了，只好在家休息了整整一周。<br>Let's <b>stay in</b> this evening.<br>咱们今晚呆在家里吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stay ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">避开；离开；不恢复<br><span class="en">to keep away; to not return</span></td><td class="c4">If the rain <b>stays off</b>, well got out for a walk.<br>雨要是不下了，我们就出去散散步。<br>She's always dieting, but she can never get the weight to <b>stay</b> of.<br>她一直在节食，不过体重总是反弹。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stay ˈoff<br>stay ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指因病不上班；不上学<br><span class="en">to not go to work, school, etc., especially because you are ill/sick</span></td><td class="c4">He injured his back and <b>stayed off</b> for a week.<br>他背部受伤，一个星期没上班。<br>Can I <b>stay off</b> school today?<br>我今天可以不上学吗？o8。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">不再吃(或喝)；戒掉<br><span class="en">to stop yourself from eating or drinking sth, especially sth that could be harmful</span></td><td class="c4">The doctor told him to <b>stay off</b> alcohol.<br>医生劝他戒酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">留在上面<br><span class="en">to remain in position on top of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The lid won't <b>stay on</b>.<br>这个盖子就是盖不上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">留下来继续学习；工作等<br><span class="en">to not leave a job,school, place, etc. when you are expected to, or when other people do</span></td><td class="c4">We hope he will <b>stay on</b> as manager at the end of his contract.<br>我们希望合同期满后他能留下来继续当经理。<br>We couldn't persuade Jane to <b>stay on</b> at school for an extra year.<br>我们无法说服简留在学校继续学习一年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">继续运作<br><span class="en">to continue operating</span></td><td class="c4">The light <b>stays on</b> until dawn.<br>灯一直亮到拂晓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">尤指晚上呆；在户外；不在冢<br><span class="en">to remain out of the house or outdoors, especially at night</span></td><td class="c4">Sam was allowed to <b>stay out</b> until 11.30 on a Saturday.<br>有个星期六萨姆获准在外呆到 11:30。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">不介入；不干预<br><span class="en">to not become involved in sth that does not concern you</span></td><td class="c4">I try to <b>stay out of</b> their little quarrels.<br>他们斗嘴，我尽量不掺和。<br><b>Stay out of</b> this, it's none of your business.<br>别插手，这事与你无关。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">避开；远离<br><span class="en">to avoid sth</span></td><td class="c4">Try to <b>stay out of</b> trouble!<br>尽量别惹麻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstay ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">别人家过夜；留宿<br><span class="en">to sleep at sb's house for a night</span></td><td class="c4">It got late, so we <b>stayed over</b>.<br>当时已经很晚，我们就留下过夜了。<br>Can I <b>stay over</b> at Gareth's (house) tonight?<br>我今晚可以在加雷思家过夜吗？F。<br>We let him <b>stay</b> up to watch the movie.<br>我们让他熬夜看那部电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstay with sth/sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">坚持做困难或不愿做；的事；等某人(做完某事)<br><span class="en">to continue to do sth, especially when it is difficult or you do not really want to</span></td><td class="c4">Several students weren't enjoying the course, but they <b>stayed with</b> it.<br>有几个学生不喜欢这门课程，但还是坚持下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>steal</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsteal aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">偷偷离开；溜走<br><span class="en">to go away from a place quietly and secretly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stole away</b> under cover of darkness.<br>他在夜幕的掩护下溜掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsteal ˈover sb <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">感觉油然而生；慢慢出现<br><span class="en">if a feeling steals over you, you gradually feel it</span></td><td class="c4">A chill <b>stole over</b> her body.<br>她渐渐感觉到一丝寒冷。<br>Exhaustion <b>stole over</b> me as I sat there.<br>我坐在那儿，不知不觉地感到浑身疲乏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsteal ˈup (on sb)</b></td><td class="c3">悄悄；走近(某人)<br><span class="en">to approach sb quietly so that they do not see or hear you coming</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stole up</b> on him in the dark.<br>她在黑暗中悄悄靠近他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>steam</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsteam sth ˈoff<br>ˌsteam sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">用蒸汽使(从…)脱离<br><span class="en">to remove a piece of paper from another piece using steam to melt the glue that is holding them together</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>steamed the stamp off</b> the envelope.<br>他用蒸汽嘘了嘘，把信封上的邮票取了下来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsteam ˈup<br>ˌsteam sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使蒙上水汽<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sth become, covered with steam</span></td><td class="c4">The windows had <b>steamed up</b>.<br>窗户蒙了一层雾气。<br>The warmth in the room <b>steamed all the windows up</b>.<br>房间里的热气使所有窗户都起了一层客。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>steep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsteep sth in sth</b></td><td class="c3">将(食物)浸渍在(液体)中<br><span class="en">to put food in a liquid and leave it for some time so that it becomes soft and flavoured by the liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Raspberries are delicious <b>steeped in</b> brandy.<br>用白兰地浸泡悬钩子的味道很好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stem</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstem from sth not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Many of her problems <b>stem</b> from the fact that her parents are famous.<br>她的很多问题之所以会产生，就在于她父母是名人。<br>Their opposition <b>stems</b> from fear and ignorance.<br>他们反对是出于恐惧和无知。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>step</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstep aˈside/down (as/from sth)</b></td><td class="c3">下台；退位；辞职；让出；职位<br><span class="en">to leave an important job or position in order to let sb eise take your place</span></td><td class="c4">After ten years as party leader, it's time for him to <b>step aside</b>.<br>他当了10年的党魁，现在该让贤了。<br>He decided to <b>step aside</b> as director to make way for his son.<br>他决定把公司董事的位置让给儿子。<br>I intended to <b>step down</b> as Chairman.<br>我想辞去主席职务。<br>She's <b>stepping down</b> from her post next year.<br>她明年就要离职了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstep ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">置身事外(冷静思考)；旁观<br><span class="en">(from sth) to try to think calmly about a situation in which you have been closely involved, as if you are not involved in it</span></td><td class="c4">You should try to <b>step back</b> from the problem and look for a new way to deal with it.<br>你应该试着从旁观者的角度看待这个问题，寻找新的处理方法。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstep ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">施以援手；居间调停；居中斡旋<br><span class="en">to help in an argument or a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">When my mum was ill, my aunt <b>stepped in</b> to help.<br>我妈妈生病时，姨妈前来帮忙。<br>The Youth Club was going to close, but a local bank <b>stepped in</b> with a generous donation.<br>青年俱乐部即将关闭时，一象当地银行出来慷慨相助。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstep on it <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤用于要求加速行驶开快；赶快<br><span class="en">used especially to tell sb to drive faster</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Step on it</b>! We're late!<br>开快点！我们迟到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>step ˈout <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">离开一小会儿；暂时离开<br><span class="en">to leave a place for a short period</span></td><td class="c4">He's just <b>stepped out</b> for ten minutes.<br>他刚出去了十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstep ˈup (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">走上前去<br><span class="en">to come forward</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stepped up</b> to receive his award.<br>他走上前去了穷人的痛苦。<br>Security has been <b>stepped up</b> in response to the recent threat.<br>已经加强了安全措施来应对近期的威胁。<br>The runners <b>stepped up</b> to the line.<br>赛跑运动员走向起跑线。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>step sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">增加；提高速度；水平；数量等<br><span class="en">to increase the rate, level, amount, etc. of sth</span></td><td class="c4">Security has been <b>stepped up</b> at the airport since the bomb scare.<br>自遭遇炸弹恐吓以来，机场已加强了安全措施。<br>Police have <b>stepped up</b> their search for the missing schoolgirl.<br>警方加紧搜寻失踪女学生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick at sth</b></td><td class="c3">坚持不懈地做；持之以恒地做(某事)<br><span class="en">to work continuously at sth in a determined way</span></td><td class="c4">If we <b>stick at</b> it, we should finish the job today.<br>我们只要不停地干，今天应该能把活儿干完。<br>She never <b>sticks at</b> anything for very long.<br>她做任何事都缺乏恒心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick sth ˈback <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…放回(原位)<br><span class="en">to return sth to its usual place; to return sth to the place it was before</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stick the cake back</b> in the oven for ten minutes.<br>把蛋糕放回烤箱里烤十分钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick by sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">忠于；不背弃(处于困境的人)<br><span class="en">to be loyal to sb and continue to support them in difficult times</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stuck by</b> him through thick and thin.<br>她和他同甘共苦，对他忠贞不渝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick by sth</b></td><td class="c3">信守；遵守；贯彻原先的计划；承诺等<br><span class="en">to do what you said, planned or promised you would do, even though the situation might have changed</span></td><td class="c4">In spite of what's happened, we must <b>stick by</b> our decision.<br>尽管出了这种事，我们仍必须坚持执行我们的决定。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用胶水把…粘住；把…贴好<br><span class="en">to fix a piece of paper, etc. to sth else using glue</span></td><td class="c4">I can't <b>stick</b> the corners of this wallpaper <b>down</b>.<br>我没法粘住墙纸的角。<br>The envelope hadn't been <b>stuck down</b> properly.<br>信封没粘好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；放好<br><span class="en">to place sth that you are holding onto the floor or another surface</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stick</b> your coat on the chair and come and sit <b>down</b> here.<br>把你的外套放在椅子上，过来坐这儿吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick sth ˈon <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">播放<br><span class="en">to make a</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stick on</b> some music, if you like.<br>想听的话就放点音乐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stick sth ˈon<br>stick sth ˈon/onto sth</b></td><td class="c3">粘贴(到…工)<br><span class="en">to attach sth frmly to a surtace, using glue, tape, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He sealed the envelope, and <b>stuck a stamp on</b> it.<br>他封好信封，在上面贴了一枚邮票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stick sth ˈon sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…随便放在某处<br><span class="en">to Put sth somewhere in a careless or rough way</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stick your report on</b> my desk when you've finished it.<br>你写完报告后就放在我的办公桌上吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">显眼；夺目；引人注目<br><span class="en">to be very noticeable or easy to see</span></td><td class="c4">They wrote the notice in red so that it would <b>stick out</b>.<br>他们用红字写出通知，这样会醒目一些。?。<br>It <b>stuck out</b> a mile that she was lying.<br>她显然在说谎。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stick it/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">坚持到底；忍受下去<br><span class="en">to continue doing sth difficult or boring until it is finished</span></td><td class="c4">I don't like being on my own, but T! <b>stick it out</b> until my parents come back.<br>我不喜欢独自一个，但我会坚持熬到爸妈回来的。'm。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick ˈout for sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">坚持索要；得不到…不罢休<br><span class="en">to refuse to give up until you get what you want</span></td><td class="c4">They're <b>sticking out for</b> a higher pay rise.<br>他们坚持要求提高加薪幅度。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick ˈthrough<br>stick ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…的一边伸到另一边；穿过<br><span class="en">if sth sticks through or sticks through sth, it goes from one side to the other and it is partly outside</span></td><td class="c4">His head was <b>sticking through</b> the railings.<br>他的脑袋伸过 Yˈ。<br>That's her story and she's <b>sticking</b> to it.<br>那是她本人的说法，并且她仍坚持那么说。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>stick toˈgether <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">彼此友好忠诚；团结在一起<br><span class="en">to remain friendly and loyal to one another; to sup port each other</span></td><td class="c4">The family should <b>stick together</b> at a time like this.<br>在这样的关头，全家人应该团结一致。<br>The children <b>from</b> the village tended to stick together.<br>这个村的孩子喜欢抱团。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>stick toˈgether <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">互相挨近(或靠近)<br><span class="en">to stay physically close to each other</span></td><td class="c4">Let's all stick together until we <b>find</b> the way out.<br>找到出去的路之前，我们大家不要。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">将(零散物品或散件)拼合；把…粘在一起<br><span class="en">to attach things or parts of things to each other</span></td><td class="c4">Cut out the shapes and <b>stick them together</b> to make a bird.<br>先剪出各个形状，然后把它们拼贴成一只鸟儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>stick ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">向上突出；坚立<br><span class="en">to point upwards</span></td><td class="c4">The branch was <b>sticking up</b> out of the water.<br>树枝从水中冒了出来。<br>Is my hair <b>sticking up</b>?<br>我的头发翘起来了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">张贴<br><span class="en">to attach sth to a wall, a board, a window, etc. so that people can see it</span></td><td class="c4">They had <b>stuck up</b> posters everywhere advertising the show.<br>他们在各处张贴海报宣传这次演出。<br>If you want to sell your bike, just <b>stick a notice up</b> in the shop window.<br>你要是想卖自行车，就在商店橱窗上贴一张布告。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstick ˈup for sb/yourself/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">支持；维护；捍卫<br><span class="en">to support or defend sb, yourself or sth, when they are being criticized</span></td><td class="c4">She always <b>sticks</b> up for her little sister.<br>她总是护着妹妹。<br>You must <b>stick</b> up for what you believe in.<br>你一定要捍卫你的信念。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick with sb</b></td><td class="c3">紧跟；靠近(某人)<br><span class="en">to stay physically close to sb</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stick with</b> me until we get out of the forest.<br>走出森林之前跟紧我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstick with sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">顶着困难坚持；继续(做某事)<br><span class="en">to continue to do sth in spite of difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">If we <b>stick with</b> it we should finish soon.<br>我们要是坚持下去，很快就能做完。<br>I <b>stuck with</b> the job for as long as I could.<br>我一直坚持工作，直到无法继续。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sting</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsting sb for sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指强人所难向某人借钱<br><span class="en">to borrow money from sb, especially when they are unwilling to give it to you</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>sting you for</b> a fiver?<br>能借给我五英镑吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stink</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstink sth ˈout (BrE) (AmE ˌstink sth ˈup) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使(某处)充满恶臭；使臭气冲天<br><span class="en">to fill a room, a building, etc. with a very unpleasant smell</span></td><td class="c4">He stank the whole place <b>out</b> with his cigarettes.<br>他弄得到处都是难闻的香烟味。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stir</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstir sth ˈin<br>ˌstir sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…搅入(…)<br><span class="en">to mix one substance into another by moving a Spoon, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stir the pasta into</b> the sauce.<br>把意大利面加到调味汁里调拌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstir sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">激励；鼓动(某人)<br><span class="en">to encourage sb to do sth; to make sb feel they must do sth</span></td><td class="c4">He was accused of <b>stirring up</b> the slaves against their masters.<br>有人指责他鼓动奴隶反抗主人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstir sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">煽动；挑起<br><span class="en">to cause trouble, especially by making people feel strong emotions</span></td><td class="c4">I don't want to <b>stir up</b> any more trouble.<br>我不想挑起更多麻烦了。<br>The government has been accused of <b>stirring up</b> racial hatred.<br>有人谴责政府煽动种族仇恨。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stitch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>stitch sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">缝拢；缝合<br><span class="en">to join things together using a needle and thread</span></td><td class="c4">This wound has to be <b>stitched up</b> urgently.<br>这个伤口必须立刻缝合。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stock</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstock ˈup (on/with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">储备；备足(某物)<br><span class="en">to buy or get a lot of sth so that you can use it later</span></td><td class="c4">The shops are very busy with people <b>stocking up</b> for the holidays.<br>各个店铺非常繁忙，挤满了采购节日用品的顾客。<br>I need to <b>stock up</b> on food before all the family arrive.<br>我得赶在全家人到来之前备足食物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stoke</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstoke sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">往(火等)里添燃料<br><span class="en">to keep a fire, etc. burning by adding more fuel</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stoked up</b> the fire before going to bed.<br>他临睡前给炉子加了煤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stoop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstoop to sth<br>ˈstoop to doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">为私利不择手段；卑鄙(或堕落)到做某事<br><span class="en">to do sth bad or unpleasant in order to gain an advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">I can't believe he would <b>stoop to</b> blackmail.<br>我没法相信他会如此下作，竟然会勒索别人。<br>He's the kind of person who would <b>stoop to</b> making personal attacks on a rival.<br>他是那种能卑鄙到对竞争对手进行人身攻击的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stop</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstop aˈround<br>ˌstop aˈround sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">去看望(某人)；去(某人家)小坐<br><span class="en">to make a short visit to sb, usually at their home</span></td><td class="c4">Let's <b>stop around</b> the Smiths' house for a drink.<br>咱们去史密斯家坐坐喝点东西吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stop aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">有意选择不去(某处)<br><span class="en">to deliberately decide not to go somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">Many of the people invited to the dinner had <b>stopped away</b> in protest.<br>接到邀请的很多人故意不赴宴，以示抗议。更常见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstop ˈby<br>ˌstop ˈby sth</b></td><td class="c3">过来小坐；顺路造访<br><span class="en">to make a short visit to sb/sth, especially when you are on the way to somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Stop by</b> for a chat on your way home.<br>你回家时顺便过来聊聊吧。<br>Could you <b>stop by</b> the store for some milk?<br>你能不能顺路到那家店里买点牛奶。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstop ˈin <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">呆在家里(不外出)<br><span class="en">to stay at home rather than go out</span></td><td class="c4">Weve decided to <b>stop in</b> tonight because it's raining.<br>下雨了，我们打算今晚留在家里。常见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstop ˈoff (at/in .. )</b></td><td class="c3">在某处中途停留<br><span class="en">to stop somewhere for a short time when you are on the way to somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>stopped off</b> for lunch just north of Paris.<br>我们就在巴黎以北中途停下来吃了午饭。<br>I <b>stopped off</b> at the supermarket on the way home.<br>我回家途中去了一趟超市。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>stop ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">熬夜；迟睡<br><span class="en">to not go to bed until later than usual</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stopped up</b> to see the football match.<br>她熬夜看足球赛。常见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstop sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">盖上；堵塞孔穴；缝隙等<br><span class="en">to cover or fill a hole, a crack, etc. so that nothing can get through</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>stopped up</b> all the holes to keep out the draught.<br>我把洞全堵上了，想挡住穿堂风。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>store</b></td><td class="c2"><b>store sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">贮存；储备；贮藏<br><span class="en">to put sth in a safe place and keep it there so that you can use it later</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>stored away</b> the baby clothes.<br>我们把婴儿服装全都收起来了。<br>It's amazing how much knowledge he's got <b>stored away</b> in his memory.<br>他头脑中储存的知识多得令人惊叹。<br>I <b>stored away</b> the information for future use.<br>我存了这条信息等以后用。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstore ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">带来；遗留(后患)<br><span class="en">to make trouble for yourself in future</span></td><td class="c4">Smokers may be <b>storing up</b> health problems for their unborn children.<br>吸烟的人可能给他们的胎儿留下健康隐患。<br>Children who <b>store up</b> their bad feelings often develop headaches or stomach pains.<br>儿童如果情绪低落郁结在心头，常常会导致头疼或腹痛。o日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstore sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">在脑中记下；记住(信息或事实)<br><span class="en">to keep information or facts in your memory to use later</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stored up</b> all the amusing and interesting things that happened during the day to tell his family in the evening.<br>他把白天发生的好笑和有趣的事儿都记在心里，等到晚上讲给家人听。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>storm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>storm ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">愤怒地；突然离开<br><span class="en">to leave a place or a person suddenly because you are very angry</span></td><td class="c4">We had a big argument and he <b>stormed off</b>.<br>我们大吵一架，然后他怒冲冲地夺门而出。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstow sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">将…收好；把…保存好<br><span class="en">to put sth in a place where it will be safe or will not be found</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stowed his passport away</b> safely in a drawer.<br>他把护照妥善存放在抽屉里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>straighten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstraighten ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">挺直身子；站立起来<br><span class="en">to stand up straight from a bent position</span></td><td class="c4">She slowly <b>straightened up</b> and rubbed her back.<br>她慢慢站起来揉了揉背。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>strain</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstrain at sth</b></td><td class="c3">拉紧；用力拽(某物)<br><span class="en">to pull very hard on sth</span></td><td class="c4">The dog was <b>straining at</b> its lead.<br>那只狗用力拖拽着牵狗绳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strain sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">滤掉；滤去(液体)<br><span class="en">to separate a liquid from sth solid by pouring it through sth that has very small holes in it</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Strain off</b> any excess liquid.<br>把多余的液体都过滤掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>strap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>strap sth ˈon<br>strap sth ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">用带子系或；绑(在…上)<br><span class="en">to attach sth to sth else with straps</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>strapped on</b> his helmet and rode away.<br>他系好头盔就开车走了。<br>She <b>strapped the suitcases onto</b> the roof of the car.<br>她把衣箱绑在车顶上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strap sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用绷带包扎(受伤部位)<br><span class="en">to tie bandages around sth, especially an injured part of the body, to support it or prevent it from moving</span></td><td class="c4">Your wrist needs to be <b>strapped up</b>.<br>你的手腕需要包扎一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stress</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstress sb ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使过度焦虑劳累；使心力交瘁<br><span class="en">to make sb very anxious and tired so that they are unable to relax</span></td><td class="c4">My dad <b>stressed me out</b> by criticizing me all the time.<br>爸爸没完没了地数落我，都快把我逼疯了。ˌ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stretch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstretch ˈout<br>ˌstretch yourself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">尤指为；休息或睡觉舒展四肢躺下<br><span class="en">to lie down, with your arms or legs out straight, especially in order to relax or sleep</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stretched out</b> on the floor and fell asleep.<br>他摊开手脚躺在地板上睡了。?。<br>He leant back and <b>stretched his legs out</b> in front of him.<br>他靠后仰，双腿前伸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>strew</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈstrewn with sth</b></td><td class="c3">撒满；遍布(某物)<br><span class="en">to be covered with a lot of things</span></td><td class="c4">The floor <b>was strewn with</b> clothes.<br>满地都是衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>strike</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstrike at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">用武器朝…打去<br><span class="en">to try to hit sb/sth, especially with a weapon</span></td><td class="c4">She screamed and <b>struck at</b> the wolf with a stick.<br>她尖叫着用棍子朝那只狠打去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstrike at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">损害；有损于；严重影响到<br><span class="en">to cause damage or have a serious effect on sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The Proposals <b>struck at</b> the roots of community life.<br>这些提议动摇了社区生活的根基。<br>This legislation <b>strikes at</b> the most vulnerable people in society.<br>这项法律损害了社会上最弱势群体的利益。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrike ˈback (at/against sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">反击；回击<br><span class="en">to criticize or attack sb who has criticized or attacked you</span></td><td class="c4">Sarah used the article to <b>strike back</b> at her critics.<br>萨拉借这篇文章驳斥批评她的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrike sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">疾病使丧命；使病倒；侵袭</td><td class="c4">She was <b>struck down</b> by polio at the age of four.<br>她四岁那年得了小儿麻痹症。<br>I was <b>struck down</b> by flu and had to cancel the trip.<br>我得了流感，不得不取消行程。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrike sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">击倒；撞倒；使丧命<br><span class="en">to hit sb very hard so that they fall to the ground; to kill sb</span></td><td class="c4">Fights broke out near the shop and one girl was <b>struck down</b> by a handbag.<br>商店附近发生了斗殴，一名女孩被一只手提包击倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strike sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">驳回；废止；麥除<br><span class="en">to reject sth; to make sth no longer valid</span></td><td class="c4">Only the Supreme Court has the power to <b>strike down</b> this legislation.<br>只有最骨法院有权否决这项法律。<br>Parents tried to have the ban <b>struck down</b>.<br>父母们试图使禁令得以取消。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strike sb/sth ˈoff<br>strike sb/sth ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…从某职业；中除名；取消…的从业资格<br><span class="en">to remove sb's name from the list of members of a profession so that they can no longer work in that profession</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>struck off</b> for professional misconduct.<br>她因为渎职被除名了。<br>These doctors should be <b>struck off</b> the medical register.<br>这些医生应该被吊销行医资格。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrike ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">猛打<br><span class="en">(at sb/sth) to aim a violent blow at sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>struck out</b> at me with his fist.<br>他给了我一记重拳。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strike ˈout<br>ˌstrike sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">棒球</td><td class="c4">He <b>struck out</b> in the third inning.<br>他在第三局三击不中出局了。<br>The pitcher <b>struck out</b> three batters.<br>投手使三名击球员三击未中出局。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strike sth ˈout/ˈthrough <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">画掉；删去；勾销<br><span class="en">to remove sth from a text or a list by drawing a line through it</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>struck out</b> some words to make the message shorter.<br>我删掉一些文字，缩短了信息内容。<br>He insisted that I <b>strike out</b> all references to his family.<br>他坚持要我删除所有提及他家庭的内容。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strike ˈup (with sth)<br>ˌstrike ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">乐队开始弹奏<br><span class="en">if musicians strike up, they begin to play</span></td><td class="c4">Everyone was waiting for the band to <b>strike</b> up.<br>大家都在等着乐队开始演奏。<br>The orchestra <b>struck</b> up a lively tune.<br>管弦乐队奏起一首欢快的曲子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrike ˈup sth (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">和某人建立友谊；开始来往；交谈起来<br><span class="en">to begin a friendship, a relationship, a conversation, etc. with sb</span></td><td class="c4">My mother will <b>strike up</b> a conversation with anyone she meets.<br>我母亲逮谁跟谁聊。<br>Children of the same age don't always <b>strike up</b> friendships (with each other).<br>同龄的孩子不一定会成为朋友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>string</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstring aˈlong (with sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">闲时跟随；陪伴(某人)</td><td class="c4">Can I <b>string along</b> with you when you go to the shops?<br>我能跟你去商店吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstring sb aˈlong <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">一直让…误信；欺骗；戏弄<br><span class="en">to allow sb to believe sth that is not true for a long time, especially when you encourage them to have false hopes</span></td><td class="c4">They never intended to give her a job. They were just <b>stringing her along</b>.<br>他们从未真正想过要给她一份工作。他们只不过是吊吊她的胃口。<br>He strung her <b>along</b> for years and then married Kate.<br>他哄骗了她好几年，后来抛弃她娶了凯特。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstring ˈout (across/along sth)</b></td><td class="c3">分开成一列<br><span class="en">to spread out in a line</span></td><td class="c4">As we climbed, we tended to <b>string out</b>, with the fittest people taking the lead.<br>我们爬山时一般会排成一列，由最强壮的人领头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstring sth toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">把单词；短语；句子等连成；有意义的语言单位<br><span class="en">to combine words, phrases, sentences, etc. to form sth that has some meaning</span></td><td class="c4">I can barely <b>string together</b> two words of German.<br>我德语说不成句。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstring sb ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指非法地吊死<br><span class="en">to kill sb by hanging them, especially illegally</span></td><td class="c4">They'll <b>string him up</b> if they catch him.<br>他们抓住他，就会把他吊死。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>strip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>strip sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">剥去；剥下；揭去<br><span class="en">(from sth) to completely remove a layer of sth that is covering sth else</span></td><td class="c4">The bark has been <b>stripped away</b> from the tree.<br>树皮已经剥光了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strip sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">揭去；揭穿；清除(虚假或不必要的东西)<br><span class="en">to remove anything that is not true and necessary to reveal what sb/sth is really like</span></td><td class="c4">When you <b>strip away</b> the jargon, he really has nothing sensible to say.<br>去掉术语之后，他实际上没有说任何有意义的东西。<br>The programme <b>stripped away</b> the mystery surrounding the royal family.<br>这个节目揭开了王室的神秘面纱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strip sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">夺走；去除(存在已久的事物)<br><span class="en">to remove or get rid of sth that has existed for a long time</span></td><td class="c4">Our basic rights are being <b>stripped away</b> by these laws.<br>这些法律正在剥夺我们的基本权利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstrip sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">拆开；拆卸(机器或引擎)<br><span class="en">to separate a machine or an engine into parts, especially in order to clean or repair it</span></td><td class="c4">We had to <b>strip down</b> the engine and replace the worn parts.<br>我们不得不拆开引擎，更换了磨损的部件。<br>The car was <b>stripped down</b> and sold for parts.<br>车子已拆成零件卖了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strip ˈdown to sth</b></td><td class="c3">脱得只剩下<br><span class="en">to take off your clothes until you are only wearing the items mentioned</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>stripped down to</b> my underwear for the massage.<br>我脱得只剩下内衣，接受按摩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstrip sb/sth of sth</b></td><td class="c3">剥夺…的权利(或财产等)；使丧失权利或财产<br><span class="en">to take away a right, property, etc. that sb has, as a punishment</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>stripped of</b> his title for refusing to fight in Britain (= for example, in boxing).<br>他因为拒绝在英国比赛而被取消了冠军头衔。<br>They <b>stripped me of</b> my citizenship and deported me.<br>他们剥夺了我的公民资格，将我驱逐出境。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strip ˈoff<br>strip sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">几乎脱光(衣服)<br><span class="en">if you strip off, or strip sth off, you take off all or nearly all your clothes</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stripped off</b> and dived into the water.<br>她脱去衣服，跳入了水中。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>strip sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">将(不需要的东西)全部挪走；清空(某处)<br><span class="en">to completely remove things you do not want; to remove everything from a place and leave it empty</span></td><td class="c4">They had <b>stripped out</b> all the original features of the house.<br>他们把房子本来的特色全毁了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>struggle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>struggle aˈlong/ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">在困难中坚持；勉力维持<br><span class="en">to manage to continue in spite of great difficulties</span></td><td class="c4">The government <b>struggled on</b> with a tuny majority.<br>政府以微弱多数勉力支撑着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stub</b></td><td class="c2"><b>stub sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把(香烟等)弄灭；捻熄<br><span class="en">to stop a cigarette, etc. burning</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>stubbed the cigarette out</b> with his foot.<br>他把香烟踩灭了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stumble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>stumble aˈcross/ˈon/uˈpon sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">意外发现；偶然遇见<br><span class="en">to find sb/sth unexpectedly or by chance</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>stumbled on</b> the solution by accident.<br>我们是无意中找到这个解决方法的。<br>I <b>stumbled across</b> an old school friend today.<br>我今天碰到了一位老校友。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈstumble into sth</b></td><td class="c3">无意间涉足<br><span class="en">to become involved in sth by chance</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>stumbled into</b> engineering because of her love of maths.<br>她因为喜欢数学而偶然涉足工程领域。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>stump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌstump ˈup (for sth)<br>stump ˈup sth (for sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不情愿地为…付钞票；掏腰包<br><span class="en">to pay the amount of money for sth that sb asks, often when you do not want to</span></td><td class="c4">He had no money so I had to <b>stump</b> up for his ticket.<br>他没带钱，于是我只好替他出钱买票。<br>We had to <b>stump</b> up an extra five hundred pounds for insurance.<br>我们不得不又付了五百英镑买保险。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>succeed</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sucˈceed in doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">做成某事；获取某物；实现目标；达到目的<br><span class="en">to achieve sth that you have been trying to do or get; to have the result or effect that was intended</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>succeeded</b> in getting top marks in chemistry.<br>他拿到了化学课的最高分。<br>The Labour Party <b>succeeded</b> in capturing the female vote (=they Persuaded women to vote for them).<br>工党成功地贏得了女性的选票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>suck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsuck sb ˈin<br>ˌsuck sb ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">逐渐把某人卷入(某事)<br><span class="en">to gradually involve sb in an activity, a situation, etc., especially one that they do not at first want to be involved in</span></td><td class="c4">There is a danger we could be <b>sucked into</b> a war.<br>我们有被卷入战争的危险。<br>Don't let yourself get <b>sucked in</b>.<br>别把自己给牵扯进去。<br>In his youth he had been <b>sucked into</b> a hippy cult.<br>他年轻的时候一度崇尚嬉皮士式的生活。总是用于被动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>suck it ˈup <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">认命；接受现实；忍耐一下<br><span class="en">to accept an unpleasant or difficult situation, and continue living, working, etc. in the usual way</span></td><td class="c4">I know he has a cold, but he'll just have to <b>suck it up</b> like everyone else does.<br>我知道他感冒了，但他只能同其他人一样忍着点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>suck ˈup to sb <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">奉承；巴结<br><span class="en">to try to please sb by helping them, saying nice things to them, etc. in order to gain advantage for yourself</span></td><td class="c4">We don't <b>suck up to</b> anyone!<br>我们不会讨好巴结任何人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sucker</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sucker sb ˈinto sth<br>ˌsucker sb ˈinto doing sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">蒙骗某人做某事；诱使某人做某事<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to do sth they do not really want to do, especially by using their lack of knowledge or experience</span></td><td class="c4">He got <b>suckered into</b> the scheme.<br>他落进了圈套。<br>I was <b>suckered into</b> helping.<br>我上了当去帮忙。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>suit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈsuit sth to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">使适合；使适应；使适宜<br><span class="en">to make sth appropriate for sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He can <b>suit his conversation to</b> whoever he's with.<br>无论跟谁在一起，他都能聊得投机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sum</b></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>sum ˈup<br>ˌsum sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">总结；概括<br><span class="en">to give the main points of sth in a few words</span></td><td class="c4">Before we conclude the meeting, let me <b>sum up</b>.<br>会议结束之前，我来总结一下。<br>To <b>sum up</b>, there are three main ways of tackling the problem .<br>概括来说，这一问题主要有三种处理办法…。<br><b>In</b> her conclusion, she summed up what had been agreed.<br>她最后概括了已达成的共识。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>sum sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">扼要描述；概述<br><span class="en">to describe or show the most typical characteristics of sb/sth, especially in a few words</span></td><td class="c4">His speech <b>summed up</b> the mood of the whole country.<br>他的讲话概括了整个国家的气氛。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>sum sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">估量；判断；把…视为<br><span class="en">(as sb/sth) to decide or express what you think about sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The two of them stood there, <b>summing each other up</b>.<br>他们俩站在那儿，相互打量着。<br>He had already <b>summed her up</b> as someone who hated to admit defeat.<br>他已经把她归为那种不愿认输的人。<br>I <b>summed up</b> the situation immediately (= realized what was happening and what needed to be done).<br>我立刻看出是怎么回事。</td></tr>
