<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>summon</b></td><td class="c2"><b>summon sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">设法激起(感情)；鼓起(勇气)；振作(精神)<br><span class="en">to manage to produce a particular feeling in yourself, although this is difficult</span></td><td class="c4">She eventually <b>summoned up</b> the courage to knock at the door.<br>她最终鼓起勇气敲了门。<br>He managed to <b>summon up</b> a smile.<br>他挤出了一丝笑容。<br>I can't <b>summon up</b> much enthusiasm for grammar!<br>我对语法无法产生多大热情。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>surge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>surge ˈup <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">情绪高涨<br><span class="en">if an emotion surges up in you, you suddenly feel it very strongly</span></td><td class="c4">Panic <b>surged up</b> inside her.<br>她突然惊恐万状。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>surrender</b></td><td class="c2"><b>surˈrender to sb/sth<br>surˈrender yourself to sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">任由某人；感觉等控制；对…放弃抵抗<br><span class="en">to stop trying to resist a feeling, a particular person, etc. and let them control what you do</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>Surrendered to</b> his natural instinct to run away.<br>他出于本能，不由自主地逃了。<br>She <b>surrendered to</b> Leo's charm.<br>她抵挡不住利奥的魅力。<br>He <b>surrendered himself to</b> sleep.<br>他不知不觉睡着了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>suss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsuss sb/sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">发现…的真相；了解…的本质<br><span class="en">to find out what sb/sth is really like; to understand the important things about sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">We'll need to <b>suss out</b> our opponents before the game.<br>我们在比赛前要摸清对手的底细。<br>Jen had <b>sussed out</b> right away that there was something strange going on.<br>珍一眼就看出情况有些不对头。<br>Simon always did what his family wanted. I soon <b>sussed that out</b>.<br>西蒙总是顺着家人的意思去做。我很快就瞧出了这一点。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swallow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌswallow sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">吞没；淹没<br><span class="en">to completely cover sb/sth or absorb them, so that they can no longer be seen or do not exist separately</span></td><td class="c4">He watched them walk until the darkness <b>swallowed them up</b>.<br>他目送他们走远，直到消失在夜色里。<br>She was so embarrassed she wished that the ground would open and <b>swallow her up</b>.<br>她尴尬极了，简直希望地面能裂开个洞，让她钻进去。<br>The countryside is rapidly being <b>swallowed up</b> by building developments.<br>乡村地区正被建筑开发项目迅速侵占。<br>Many small businesses have been <b>swallowed up</b> by larger companies.<br>很多小公司被大公司兼并了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌswallow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用光；用尽；耗尽钱；资源等<br><span class="en">to use sth such as money or resources completely</span></td><td class="c4">Practising the piano <b>swallows up</b> all her free time.<br>练钢琴占用了她所有的闲暇时间。<br>Pay rises were quickly <b>swallowed up</b> by Price increases.<br>增加的工资很快就被上涨的物价抵消了。<br>Nuclear weapons <b>swallowed up</b> a third of the country's defence spending.<br>核武器用掉了国防开支的三分之一。<br>The extra money was <b>swallowed up</b> by debts.<br>剩余的钱都用来还债了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swan</b></td><td class="c2"><b>swan aˈbout/aˈround<br>.swan aˈbout/ aˈround sth <span class="tag">(BrE, informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">悠闲自得地晃荡；闲逛<br><span class="en">to move around or go from one place to another enjoying yourself, but with no real Purpose</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>swanning about</b> pretending to be clever.<br>别自以为是地晃荡了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌSWap sb/sth aˈround/over/ˈround <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">替換<br><span class="en">to replace sb/sth with sb/sth else</span></td><td class="c4">At half-time the manager <b>swapped</b> some of the players <b>around</b>.<br>主教练在半场时把几名队员换下了场。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>swap ˈover (to sth),.swap sb/sth ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">位置转换到(另一种)<br><span class="en">to change from one situation, Position, etc. to another; to make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>swapped</b> <b>over</b> from an electric cooker to gas.<br>我们把电炉灶具换成了煤气炉。<br>Have you been <b>swapped</b> <b>over</b> to the new computer system yet?<br>有人给你装新的计算机系统了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swarm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈswarm with sb/sth usually</b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">The museum was <b>swarming</b> with tourists.<br>博物馆里游客摩肩接踵。<br>The room was hot and <b>swarming</b> with fies.<br>房间里很热，到处是苍蝇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈswear by sth/sb not</b></td><td class="c3">不用于进行时<br><span class="en">used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">My brother <b>swears</b> by lemon and honey drinks as a cold remedy.<br>我哥哥深信柠檬加蜂蜜饮料能治疗感冒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌswear sb ˈin<br>ˌswear sb ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使宜誓就职；使宣誓效忠某个组织；国家等<br><span class="en">to introduce sb publicly to a new position, responsibility, etc. by getting them to promise that they will do the job correctly, be loyal to the organization, their country, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The new President was hurriedly sworn <b>into</b> office.<br>新总统仓促宣誓就职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>swear ˈoff sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">发誓；戒除<br><span class="en">to make a serious promise that you will give sth up, especially sth that is bad or harmful</span></td><td class="c4">He's intending to <b>swear off</b> alcohol.<br>他打算从此滴酒不沾。<br>Ever since her boyfriend left she has sworn <b>off</b> men.<br>自从她的男友离开之后，她发誓不再和男性交往。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sweat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sweat sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">通过排汗减轻(体重)<br><span class="en">to lose weight by doing a lot of hard exercise</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>sweated off</b> the extra weight by playing squash every day.<br>我靠每天打壁球出一身汗，减掉多余的体重。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sweat sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">通过发汗治好感冒；发烧等<br><span class="en">to get rid of a cold, fever, etc. by staying warm so that you produce sweat</span></td><td class="c4">Whenever I get a bad fever 1 go to bed and <b>sweat it out</b>.<br>我每次发高烧都是通过卧床发汗治好的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>sweep</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sweep sb aˈlong/aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">使激动万分；使专注于<br><span class="en">to make sb feel very enthusiastic about sth or involved in sth; to affect sb so much they forget everything else</span></td><td class="c4">Ana was swept <b>along</b> by her father's enthusiasm.<br>父亲的热情深深感染了安娜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sweep sb aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">轻松打败<br><span class="en">to defeat sb easily</span></td><td class="c4">United swept Liverpool <b>aside</b> with ease.<br>联队轻而易举地击败了利物浦队。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌsweep sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">对…置之不理；不理会；无视<br><span class="en">to ignore sth; to treat sth as though it is not important</span></td><td class="c4">All their objections were swept <b>aside</b>.<br>他们的反对全都没人理会。<br>She <b>sweeps aside</b> every suggestion I make.<br>她把我的所有建议都当成了耳旁风。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sweep sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">消灭；彻底消除；完全打消<br><span class="en">to destroy or get rid of sth completely</span></td><td class="c4">The President's speech swept <b>away</b> all our doubts.<br>总统的讲话消除了我们的一切疑虑。<br>Poverty will be swept <b>away</b>!<br>贫困将会消除。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sweep sth ˈoff<br>sweep sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…扫走；擦掉<br><span class="en">to remove sth from somewhere, especially by brushing with your hands, a brush, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He swept the crumbs <b>Off</b> the table.<br>他把桌上的面包屑扫掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>sweep sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">打扫；清扫干净房间；橱柜等<br><span class="en">to clean a room, a cupboard, etc. with a large brush with a long handle (a broom)</span></td><td class="c4">Brad was busy <b>sweeping out</b> the yard.<br>布拉德忙着扫院子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌswell ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">身体；部位肿胀；隆起<br><span class="en">if part of the body swells up, it becomes much larger and rounder than usual as a result of illness, injury, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">My foot <b>swelled up</b> to twice its normal size.<br>我的脚肿得有平时的两倍大。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swill</b></td><td class="c2"><b>swill sth ˈdown <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛喝；痛饮；牛饮<br><span class="en">to drink a large amount of sth quickly</span></td><td class="c4">He just <b>swilled down</b> his beer and walked out.<br>他一口气把啤酒灌下肚，然后走了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>swing</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌswing aˈround<br>ˌswing sb/sth aˈround (BrE also ˌswing ˈround,, swing sb/sth ˈround)</b></td><td class="c3">使某人猛地转身；猛地掉转(某物)<br><span class="en">to turn around fast to face the other way; to make sb/sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">Luke suddenly <b>swung</b> <b>round</b> and glared at me.<br>卢克突然转过身来瞪着我。1。<br>You should be able to <b>swing</b> people <b>round</b> to your point of view.<br>你应该有能力扭转人们的看法来接受你的观点。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈswing at sb<br>ˈswing sth at sb</b></td><td class="c3">用…朝某人打去<br><span class="en">to try to hit sb</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>swung at</b> me with the iron bar.<br>她抢着根铁棍向我打过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>swing ˈby<br>swing ˈby sth <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">短暂拜访(某人或某处)；順路看望<br><span class="en">to visit a person or place for a short time, especially when you are going somewhere else</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>swung by</b> (= came here) on her way home.<br>她回家时顺便过来了一趟。<br>Let's <b>swing by</b> Dave's house after the movie.<br>看完电影后，咱们顺便到戴夫家去坐坐吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>switch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>switch ˈoff <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">不再想着；不去考虑；失去兴趣；觉得乏味<br><span class="en">to stop giving your attention to sb or sth</span></td><td class="c4">Do YOu find it hard to <b>switch off</b> (= stop thinking about work) when you get home?<br>你回到家后是不是觉得很难放下工作？K。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>switch ˈover (to sth)<br>switch sth ˈover (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">换台；换频道<br><span class="en">to change from one television station to another</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>switched</b> <b>over</b> to watch the news.<br>我换了个频道看新闻。<br>The country gradually <b>switched</b> <b>over</b> from imperial to metric.<br>该国逐渐从英制转用公制。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tack</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtack sth ˈon<br>ˌtack sth ˈon to sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">漫不经心地添加；附加；增补<br><span class="en">to add sth as an extra item, especially in a careless way</span></td><td class="c4">The last paragraph seems to have been <b>tacked on</b> at the last minute.<br>最后一段像是在最后一刻加上的。<br>An extra day has been <b>tacked onto</b> the New Year holiday.<br>新年休假额外增加了一天。o a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tag</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tag aˈlong (behind/with sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指未经邀请跟随；尾随<br><span class="en">to go somewhere with sb, especially when you have not been invited</span></td><td class="c4">The children <b>tagged along</b> behind their mother.<br>孩子们跟在妈妈后面。<br>Can I <b>tag along</b> (with you) when you go to the shops?<br>我跟着你去商店好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtag ˈon<br>ˌtag ˈon to sb/sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">未经邀请紧跟；紧随；寸步不离<br><span class="en">to follow sb closely and go somewhere with them, although you have not been invited</span></td><td class="c4">Kate's friend <b>tagged on</b> and spoiled the day.<br>凯特的朋友黏着她，弄得一天都很扫兴。<br>We <b>tagged on</b> to the end of the procession.<br>我们紧紧地跟在游行队伍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtag sth ˈon<br>ˌtag sth ˈon to sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">漫不经心地添加；附加；增补<br><span class="en">to add sth as an extra item to the end of sth, especlally in a careless way</span></td><td class="c4">An apology was <b>tagged on</b> to the end of the letter.<br>信的末尾顺便附了一句抱歉的话。<br>Online security is being built into the system, not <b>tagged on</b>.<br>在线安全保护程序内置在系统中不是外挂的。语态。+。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tail ˈback <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">受阻车辆排成长龙<br><span class="en">if traffic tails back, it forms a long line that moves very slowly or not at all</span></td><td class="c4">After the accident, traffic <b>tailed back</b> ten miles.<br>事故发生后，受阻车辆排了十英里长。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtail ˈoff (also ˌtail aˈway less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">变小或；变少；变弱等；逐渐消失<br><span class="en">to become smaller, fewer, weaker, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Sales <b>tailed off</b> in the summer.<br>夏季销售额不断下滑。<br>The number of tourists starts to <b>tail off</b> in September.<br>从9月起，游客人数开始逐步减少。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tailor</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtailor sth</b></td><td class="c3">定做；特制；使适应<br><span class="en">to/for sb/sth to make or adapt sth for a particular purpose, a particular person, etc. (…)</span></td><td class="c4">Special programmes of study are <b>tailored</b> to the needs of specific students.<br>针对具体学生的需要安排特别的课程。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>take</b></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb aˈback</b></td><td class="c3">使震惊；使吃惊<br><span class="en">to shock or surprise sb</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>taken aback</b> by his rudeness.<br>我对他的粗魯无礼感到吃惊。动语态。<br>Your daughter doesn't <b>take</b> after you at all.<br>你女儿一点儿都不像你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb aˈback</b></td><td class="c3">开始；追赶；跟踪<br><span class="en">to begin to follow sb quickly in order to catch them</span></td><td class="c4">She ran out into the night and he <b>took</b> after her.<br>她冲入了夜幕，他紧随其后赶了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake aˈgainst sb/sth <span class="tag">(old-fashioned, BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始不喜欢<br><span class="en">to begin to dislike sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Why have you suddenly <b>taken against</b> Laura?<br>你为什么突然讨厌劳拉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth aˈlong (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">随身带着；携带<br><span class="en">to take sb or sth with you when you go somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">Tom <b>took his sister along</b> to the party.<br>汤姆带看妹妹去参加聚会。<br>When You travel with young children, <b>take along</b> some favourite toys or a book.<br>和孩子们旅行要带些他们喜欢的玩具，或者带一本书。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb/sth aˈpart <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">体育运动中轻松打败；把…打得一败涂地<br><span class="en">(sport) to defeat sb easily</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>took the American apart</b> in the third set (= in a game of tennis).<br>他在第三盘轻而易举地击败了美国选手。9。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb/sth aˈpart <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛烈攻击；严厉批评<br><span class="en">to attack or criticize sb/sth severely</span></td><td class="c4">Her second novel was <b>taken apart</b> by the critics.<br>她的第二部小说被评论家批得体无完肤。i。<br>You can <b>take the mixer apart</b> to clean it.<br>你可以把搅拌器拆开来清洁。<br>The police <b>took the room apart</b> (= examined everything very carefully), looking for evidence.<br>警察仔细搜查了房间的每个角落，寻找证据。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">把…带到一边(私下谈话)<br><span class="en">to separate sb from the rest of a group in order to talk to them privately</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>took me aside</b> and explained the situation.<br>她把我拉到旁边解释情况。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…送走；带…去别处；将…转；到别处<br><span class="en">to remove sb from somewhere; to lead or move sb to another place</span></td><td class="c4">The injured were <b>taken away</b> by ambulance.<br>伤者被救护车送走了。<br>I can <b>take you away</b> from all this (= all this trouble).<br>我可以带你远离这一切烦扰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">带…旅行；携…度假<br><span class="en">to take sb with you on a trip or holiday/vacation</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>takes the whole family away</b> for two weeks in the summer.<br>他夏天带全家旅游两个星期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使(暂时)离开<br><span class="en">to make it necessary for sb to leave a place, especially temporarily</span></td><td class="c4">Sam's work <b>takes him away</b> from his family for months at a time.<br>萨姆因工作需要每次要离家好几个月。<br>You can <b>take the book away</b> with you.<br>你可以把书带走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">解除；消除感觉；痛苦等<br><span class="en">to make a feeling, pain, etc. disappear</span></td><td class="c4">If you <b>take four away</b> from ten, that leaves six.<br>十减去四等于六。<br>Ten <b>take away</b> four leaves six.<br>十减四得六。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">使(效果)减弱；使(价值)降低<br><span class="en">to make the effect or value of sth seem less</span></td><td class="c4">I don't wish to <b>take away from</b> his achievements, but he couldn't have done it without our help.<br>我不想贬低他的成就，但没有我们援手相助，他是做不成的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">使从…上转移注意力<br><span class="en">to take sb's attention away from sth</span></td><td class="c4">These minor problems are <b>taking us away from</b> the real issue.<br>这些次要问题使我们减少了对主要问题的关注。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">将…送回原处；把…送回家<br><span class="en">(to sth) to go with sb to the place where they were or to your/their home</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>take me back</b> to the hotel?<br>你能把我送回旅馆吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">与…重归于好；允许…复职<br><span class="en">to allow sb such as your husband, wife or partner to come home after they have left because of a problem; to allow sb to return to their job</span></td><td class="c4">I agreed to <b>take her back</b> if she promised to be faithful in future.<br>我同意让她回家，但她要保证今后对我忠诚。<br>An employer cannot be forced to <b>take you back</b>.<br>不能逼迫雇主让雇员复职。<br>That song <b>takes me back</b> a bit!<br>那首歌勾起了我无限的回忆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">退回(商品)；收回(退货)<br><span class="en">(to sb/sth) if you take sth back to a shop/store, or a shop/store takes sth back, you return sth that you have bought because it is the wrong size or does not work, for example</span></td><td class="c4">The sweater had a hole in it so I <b>took it back</b>.<br>毛衣上有个洞，于是我把它退了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">外出后带回(所买的物品等)<br><span class="en">to take sth you have bought, etc.home with you after you have been away</span></td><td class="c4">We were looking for presents to take back for the <b>kids</b>.<br>我们在选购回去后带给孩子们的礼物。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">收回；拿到(借出的物品)<br><span class="en">to receive or take sth that you own from sb who has borrowed it</span></td><td class="c4">No attempt was ever made to <b>take back</b> the land (= to take control of it again).<br>从未有人试图收回这块土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">收回；撒回(说过的话)<br><span class="en">to admit that sth you said was wrong or that you should not have said it</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>take back</b> what I said about you being lazy.<br>我把说你懒惰的话收回。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尤指在体育运动中使倒地；撞倒；使摔倒<br><span class="en">to make sb fall to the ground, especially in a sport</span></td><td class="c4">He ran for 40 yards before being <b>taken down</b>.<br>他跑了40码后被人放倒在地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtakedown n <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">撞倒；摔倒；拉倒<br><span class="en">a situation in which sb is made to fall to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">When it comes to the <b>takedown</b>, we only take the best officers along.<br>抓捕时我们只带最优秀的警官同去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth ˈdown<br>ˌtake sb/sth ˈdown sth</b></td><td class="c3">带…去下一层；南方或别处<br><span class="en">to go with sb/sth to a lower level, to a more southern part of a country, etc., or to a different part of a building, town, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The nurse will <b>take you down</b> in the lift.<br>护士将带你乘电梯下去。<br>The injured climbers were <b>taken down</b> the mountain on a sledge.<br>受伤的登山者用雪橇送下了山。<br>You promised to <b>take me down</b> to London next time you went!<br>你答应过下次去伦敦时带上我的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>take sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">留宿；收留<br><span class="en">to allow sb to stay in your home</span></td><td class="c4">She takes <b>in</b> paying guests.<br>她让交费的客人留宿。<br>When my parents died, my uncle took me <b>in</b>.<br>父母去世后，伯伯收留了我。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>take sb ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">欺骗；蒙骗；哄骗<br><span class="en">to make sb believe sth that is not true</span></td><td class="c4">How could <b>I</b> have been taken in by his charm?<br>我怎么会被他的风度蒙蔽了呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sth ˈin<br>ˌtake sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">吸入；吞入(体内)<br><span class="en">to absorb sth into the body by breathing or swallowing it</span></td><td class="c4">Fish <b>take in</b> oxygen through their gills.<br>鱼用鳃吸取氧。<br>When we breathe we <b>take oxygen into</b> the body.<br>我们呼吸时把氧气摄入体内。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">接纳…加入机构；组织等<br><span class="en">to accept sb into an institution, an organization, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They had to <b>take the children into</b> care (= to be looked after by the local authority).<br>他们不得不把孩子们交给当地政府照看。<br>They <b>took him into</b> the firm as a partner last year.<br>他们去年接纳他为公司合伙人。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…带进特定状况；活动；时期等<br><span class="en">to bring sb/sth into a particular situation, activity, period of time, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Owen's goal <b>took England into</b> the lead (= they were winning).<br>欧文的进球让英格兰队取得领先。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>take ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">飞机等<br><span class="en">of an aircraft, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The Flight was due to take off <b>from</b> Heathrow at 13.15.<br>航班预定于 13:15 从希思罗机场起。<br>The high jumper <b>took off</b> at a bad angle.<br>那名跳高运动员的起跳角度不好。<br>Her career is just starting to <b>take off</b>.<br>她的事业刚刚开始步入快车道。<br>Sales of mobile phones have really taken off in the last <b>few</b> years.<br>移动电话在过去几年中十分畅销。ˈ。<br>She <b>took</b> in the scene at a glance.<br>她将那个场面一览无余。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake ˈoff<br>ˌtake yourself ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">匆忙离去；突然离开<br><span class="en">to leave somewhere suddenly or in a hurry</span></td><td class="c4">Whenever things get tough, she <b>takes off</b>.<br>一遇到困难她就立刻开溜。<br>He stayed for a year, then <b>took off</b> for a job in New York.<br>他呆一年，就匆匆到纽约找了份工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb off <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">以令人生厌的方式模仿；学…的样子<br><span class="en">to copy sb in an annoying way</span></td><td class="c4">She was <b>taking off</b> the woman next door.<br>她在模仿隔壁女人的样寸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb ˈoff<br>ˌtake sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从船上；山上；寺营救；搭救<br><span class="en">to rescue sb from a ship, a mountain, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The injured men were <b>taken off</b> the boat by helicopter.<br>受伤人员被直升机从船上救走了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake sb/sth ˈoff (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">带走；取走<br><span class="en">to make sb go with you to another place; to take sth to another place</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>took him off</b> to the police station.<br>他们把他带到了警察局。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">使停止服用药物；接受治疗等<br><span class="en">to stop sb from continuing a particular medicine, treatment, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">His doctor <b>took him off</b> tranquillizers.<br>医生让他停服镇静剂。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">脱下；摘下(衣物)<br><span class="en">to remove an item of clothing from your/sb's body</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>took her coat off</b> and hung it up.<br>她脱掉外衣，把它挂了起来。<br>It's the custom to <b>take off</b> your shoes when you go into the house.<br>进屋脱鞋是这里的风俗。<br>Can you <b>take off</b> Tommys jacket for me?<br>帮我把汤米的夹克衫脱掉好吗。<br>The play was <b>taken off</b> after a week.<br>该剧目上演一周后停演了。<br>She <b>took off</b> her glasses, rubbed her eyes, then put them back on again.<br>她摘下眼镜，揉了揉眼睛，然后又把眼镜戴上了。<br>His leg had to be taken off above the <b>knee</b>.<br>他的腿不得不从膝盖以上锯掉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>take sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">通过运动或节食减去(体重)<br><span class="en">to lose weight by exercising or following a diet</span></td><td class="c4">Several people reported that they had <b>taken off</b> more than 15 pounds.<br>有几个人反映他们已减重15磅以上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f,take sth ˈoff, ˌtake sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…移走；拿开；除去<br><span class="en">to remove sth from somewhere</span></td><td class="c4">Sam <b>took</b> <b>off</b> the lid and looked inside.<br>萨姆揭开盖子朝里看了看。<br>Sam <b>took</b> the lid <b>off</b> the box.<br>萨姆打开了盒盖。<br>Can you <b>take</b> your feet <b>off</b> the sofa?<br>把脚从沙发上挪开好吗。<br>Always <b>take</b> your make-up <b>off</b> before you go to bed.<br>睡前一定要卸妆。<br>Marks will be <b>taken</b> <b>off</b> for bad spelling.<br>拼写错误要扣分。a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f,take sth ˈoff, ˌtake sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">单子上勾掉；删除<br><span class="en">to remove a name, an item, etc. from a list</span></td><td class="c4">The soup has been <b>taken</b> <b>off</b> (the menu).<br>这道汤已(从菜单上)删掉了。<br>I <b>took</b> my name <b>off</b> the list.<br>我把自己的名字从名单上勾掉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sth ˈoff sb <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">从某人处抢夺；没收(某物)</td><td class="c4">That hairstyle <b>takes ten years off</b> you!<br>这个发型让你看上去年轻了十岁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>take ˈon sth</b></td><td class="c3">呈现；具有某种特质；外观等<br><span class="en">to begin to have a particular quality, appearance, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Lisa's voice <b>took on</b> a more serious tone.<br>莉萨说话的语气变得严肃起来。<br>His words suddenly <b>took on</b> a different meaning.<br>他的话突然弦外有音了。<br>The car suddenly seemed to take on a life of <b>its</b> own (= move by itself without anyone controlling it).<br>那辆车突然自已开动起来。<br>They <b>take on</b> extra staff for summer.<br>他们夏天雇用额外员工。<br>The rebels <b>took on</b> the entire Roman army.<br>反叛者与整个罗马军队作战。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">公共汽车；飞机；船只等<br><span class="en">of a bus, plane, ship, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The bus stopped to <b>take on</b> more passengers.<br>公共汽车停下让其他乘客上车。9。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">决定做；同意负责(某事)；承担(责任)</td><td class="c4">She <b>took on</b> more responsibilities when she was promoted.<br>她晋升后责任更大了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake sth on/upon yourself</b></td><td class="c3">未经允许或商议自行决定做；某事；自作主张<br><span class="en">to decide to do sth without asking permission or talking to anyone else</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>took</b> the responsibility for what had happened <b>upon</b> herself.<br>她主动为所发生的事承担了责任。<br>Reg <b>took it upon</b> himself to tell the newspapers the truth.<br>雷吉攜自把真相告诉了报界。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈout<br>ˌtake sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…弄走；领…出去；带…离开<br><span class="en">to remove sb from a place; to take sb outside a building</span></td><td class="c4">The prisoners were <b>taken out</b> and shot.<br>囚犯被带出去枪毙了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">杀死；捣毁；摧残<br><span class="en">to kill sb or destroy sth; to injure or damage sb/sth so that they cannot work or be used</span></td><td class="c4">Enemy missiles <b>took out</b> two of our planes.<br>敌人的导弹击毁了我们两架飞机。<br>Police think he was <b>taken out</b> by a rival gang.<br>警方认为他是被一个敌对团伙干掉的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">切除；摘除(人体器官)<br><span class="en">to remove a part of the body from inside sb</span></td><td class="c4">She had to have her appendix <b>taken out</b>.<br>她只得切除了阑尾。<br>Did you remember to <b>take out</b> travel insurance?<br>你没忘记去购头旅行保险吧。<br>How many books did you <b>take out</b> of (= borrow from) the library?<br>你从图书馆借了几本书。<br>He <b>took out</b> his wallet and pulled out a £50 note.<br>他拿出钱包，抽出一张 50 英镑的钞票。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake it/sth ˈout of sb</b></td><td class="c3">使筋疲力尽；使极度疲劳<br><span class="en">to make sb feel very tired</span></td><td class="c4">Looking after three young children really <b>takes</b> a lot <b>out</b> of you.<br>照看三个小孩能把你累死。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈout of themselves <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使摆脱苦恼；为…消愁释闷<br><span class="en">to make sb forget their worries, thoughts, concerns,etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Seeing his old friends again <b>took</b> him <b>out</b> of himself.<br>再次见到老朋友使他忘却了烦恼。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sth ˈout on sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">向…发泄；拿…撒气<br><span class="en">to behave in an unpleasant way towards sb/sth because feel angry, disappointed, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">When he's had a bad day, he always <b>takes it out on</b> me.<br>他哪天不順心就拿我当出气筒。<br>You shouldn't <b>take your frustrations out on</b> the kids.<br>你遭受挫折，别拿孩子们出气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">替代；取代<br><span class="en">(from sth) (as sth) to become more important than sth else and replace it</span></td><td class="c4">Patras <b>took over</b> from Cork as European Capital of Culture.<br>帕特雷取代了科克成为欧洲文化之都。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">占据上风；变得明显<br><span class="en">to become stronger, more powerful or more noticeable</span></td><td class="c4">It's hard not to let negative feelings <b>take over</b>.<br>很难遏制消极的情绪。<br>When she saw the accident, her training as a doctor immediately <b>took over</b>.<br>看到这场事故时，她因受过医师培训而跃跃欲试。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,take ˈover<br>ˌtake sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">按替；接任；接管；接手<br><span class="en">(from sb) (as sth) to take responsibility for sth after sb else has finished; to do sth instead of sb else</span></td><td class="c4">Who's going to <b>take over</b> from Bill as manager when he retires?<br>比尔退休后，谁来接替他的经理职务。<br>Anita <b>took the business over</b> from her father.<br>安妮塔从父亲手中接管了这家企业。<br>More and more jobs are being <b>taken over</b> by machines.<br>越来越多的工作正被机器取代。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,take ˈover<br>ˌtake sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">控制；接管；治理政党；国家等<br><span class="en">to gain control of a political party, a country, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Things will change when the Socialist Party <b>takes over</b>.<br>社会党上台后情况就会不同了。<br>In the film, aliens <b>take over</b> the world.<br>在影片中外星人统治了地球。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">带…參观<br><span class="en">to go with sb around a building and show them what is interesting or important</span></td><td class="c4">A guide <b>took us over</b> the house.<br>导游带我们参观了这所房子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb/sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">强烈影响；使心无旁骛；主宰<br><span class="en">to affect sb so strongly that they are unable to think of anything else or do anything else</span></td><td class="c4">His ambition had <b>taken him over</b>.<br>他的野心左右着他。<br>My job is starting to <b>take over</b> my life.<br>我的工作开始支配我的生活。2 +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>take sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">收购；接管；接收企业；公司等<br><span class="en">to gain control of a business, a company, etc. by buying it or by buying most of its shares</span></td><td class="c4">The company was <b>taken over</b> last September.<br>这家公司去年9月被收购了。<br>They have already <b>taken over</b> several smaller airlines.<br>他们已经收购了几家小航空公司。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>take sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">迁入；开始使用(某处)<br><span class="en">to start living in a place or using it</span></td><td class="c4">The <b>flat</b> was a mess when we took it over.<br>我们搬进那套公寓时，里面一团糟。<br>This building used to be a school until the hotel <b>took it over</b>.<br>这座建筑曾经是所学校，后来改成旅馆了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助…了解；给…讲解<br><span class="en">to discuss sth with sb or explain it to them so that they know what to do</span></td><td class="c4">Your solicitor will <b>take you through</b> the contract.<br>你的律师会为你解释这份合同。<br>The director <b>took us through</b> the play scene by scene.<br>导演一场一场地给我们说戏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">开始；喜欢；对…产生好感<br><span class="en">to start liking sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">He hasn't <b>taken to</b> his new school.<br>他还没喜欢上新学校。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake to sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指为逃避困难或危险逃往；躲到<br><span class="en">to go away to a particular place, especially to escape from sth difficult or dangerous</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>took to</b> their heels and fled.<br>他们撒腿就跑，逃走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtake sth to sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用(工具或设备)做某事；(尤指)用…击打<br><span class="en">to use a tool or piece of equipment in order to do sth, especially sth violent</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>took a hammer to</b> the radio(= he destroyed it).<br>他用锤子把收音机砸了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">继续；接下去<br><span class="en">to continue with sth, especially after sb/sth else has finished</span></td><td class="c4">The band's new album <b>takes up</b> where the last one left off.<br>这支乐队的新专辑是接上一专辑的乐曲录制的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sb/sth ˈup<br>ˌtake sb/sth ˈup sth</b></td><td class="c3">和(某人)去较高处(或别处)；把(某物)带到；较高处(或别处)<br><span class="en">to go with sb or take sth to a higher place or to another part of a building, country, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Someone will <b>take you up</b> to your room.<br>有人会带你去你的房间的。<br>Why don't we <b>take our picnic up</b> the hill?<br>我们为什么不到山上去野餐呢。<br>She <b>took a hot drink up</b> to bed with her.<br>她端了杯热饮上床。<br>He <b>took</b> her a cup of tea up.<br>他给她端来一杯茶。<br>Alex only <b>took up</b> the piano when he was 14.<br>亚历克斯14 岁时才开始学钢琴。s 3。<br>Paula <b>took up</b> the story.<br>葆拉接着来讲这个故事。<br>The idea was never <b>taken up</b>.<br>这个主意从未得到重视。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake sb ˈup on sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">质问；查问<br><span class="en">to question sb or argue with sb about sth because you do not agree</span></td><td class="c4">I thought he was wrong but I didn't <b>take him up on</b> it.<br>我认为他错了，但我没有提出异议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtake ˈup with sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开始结交尤指可能带来坏影响的<br><span class="en">to become friendly with sb; to start a relationship with sb, especially sb who might have a bad influence on you</span></td><td class="c4">I heard Tom has <b>taken up with</b> a supermodel!<br>我听说汤姆傍上了个超级模特儿。<br>She's <b>taken up with</b> a bunch of losers.<br>她结交了一帮碌碌无为的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>take sth ˈup with sb</b></td><td class="c3">向…提出；与…交涉<br><span class="en">to speak or write to sb about sth they may be able to help you with</span></td><td class="c4">Youll have to <b>take your complaint up with</b> the manager.<br>你得向经理投诉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈtaken with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">迷上；被…吸引；对…感兴趣<br><span class="en">to find sb/sth attractive or interesting</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>were all very taken with</b> Zoe.<br>我们都觉得佐伊非常讨人喜欢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>talk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk aˈround sth (BrE also ˌtalk ˈround sth)</b></td><td class="c3">泛泛而谈；避实就虚地谈；不着边际地谈<br><span class="en">to talk in a general way about a subject or a problem without discussing the difficult or important parts of it</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>talked around</b> the subject for some time before coming to the real issue.<br>我们围绕这个话题东拉西扯了一会儿才言归正传。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtalk at sb</b></td><td class="c3">对…自顾自地谈；滔滔不绝地对…说<br><span class="en">to speak to sb without listening to what they say in reply</span></td><td class="c4">I was being <b>talked at</b> rather than talked to.<br>我只有听的份儿，没有说的份儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk aˈway (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">对某人喋喋不休；说个；不停<br><span class="en">to talk without stopping for a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">They were soon <b>talking away</b> to each other as i they'd known each other for years.<br>他们很快就像老相识一般聊个没完。<br>Marie was <b>talking away</b> nineteen to the dozen (= talking a lot without stopping).<br>玛丽不住嘴地唠叨着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk ˈback (to sb)</b></td><td class="c3">对上司回嘴；反驳<br><span class="en">to reply rudely to sb in authority</span></td><td class="c4">She was sent out for <b>talking back</b> to the teacher.<br>她因为顶撞老师被赶了出去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">劝阻(要从高处跳下自杀的人)<br><span class="en">to talk to sb who is threatening to kill themselves by jumping from a tall building, etc. and persuade them not to</span></td><td class="c4">The police were trying to <b>talk down</b> a youth threatening to jump from the bridge.<br>警察正在规劝一名威胁要从桥上跳下自杀的青年。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">不让；插话<br><span class="en">to prevent sb from speaking by talking loudly or without stopping</span></td><td class="c4">I tried to argue but they <b>talked me down</b>.<br>我试图争辩，可他们不给我说话的机会。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">引导(飞行员或飞机)着陆<br><span class="en">to help a pilot bring a plane to the ground by giving detailed instructions from the ground</span></td><td class="c4">The pilots were <b>talked down</b> by the Ground Controllers.<br>地面导航人员引导飞行员安全着陆。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">与…讲价；和…还价；对…压价<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to lower their prices</span></td><td class="c4">He's asked for $1 000. Can we <b>talk him down</b> any further?<br>他开价 1000元。咱们能不能和他再砍砍价？3。<br>He tends to <b>talk his achievements down</b>.<br>他常常贬低自己的成绩。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk ˈdown to sb</b></td><td class="c3">以居高临下的姿态对…说话<br><span class="en">to speak to sb as if they are younger or less intelligent than you or than they really are</span></td><td class="c4">He makes the mistake of <b>talking down to</b> his students.<br>他不该以高高在上的态度跟学生说话。<br>I hate being <b>talked down to</b>.<br>我讨厌别人自命不凡地对我说话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk yourself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">言无不尽；倾谈<br><span class="en">to talk until you have nothing left to say</span></td><td class="c4">They spent all the evening discussing the problem until they <b>talked themselves out</b>.<br>他们彻夜畅谈这个问题。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb ˈround (to sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">说服；劝说某人接受(或同意)<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to accept sth or to agree to sth</span></td><td class="c4">My parents didn't want me to go to study in Britain, but I managed to <b>talk them round</b> (to the idea).<br>我父母不想让我去英国学习，但我总算说服了他们。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">向某人详细解释<br><span class="en">to explain sth to sb in detail so that they understand it</span></td><td class="c4">The technical support staff will <b>talk you through</b> any difficulties you have with the software.<br>技术支持人员将给你详细讲解使用软件时遇到的困难。<br>I can <b>talk you through</b> the applicationform.<br>我可以详细告诉你如何填写申请表。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sth ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">把…谈透；彻底讨论以了解情况；达成协议；作出；决定等<br><span class="en">to discuss sth thoroughly so that you can understand it, come to an agreement, or make a decision about it</span></td><td class="c4">Throughout their marriage they have always <b>talked things through</b>.<br>他们婚后一直是商量着解决问题。<br>It's helpful to <b>talk the problem through</b> with a counsellor.<br>找个顾问把问题谈透会有帮助。?。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtalk sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">炒作；过分夸奖；吹捧<br><span class="en">to praise sb/sth in order to make other people interested in them/it; to describe sb/sth in a way that makes them sound better or more successful than they really are</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>talked up</b> the tourist attractions to encourage more visitors.<br>他们对这些旅游景点大肆炒作，以吸引更多游客。<br>He was being <b>talked up</b> as a future Presidential candidate.<br>他被吹捧成了未来的总统候选人。<br>It's too early to tell if the new President will <b>talk the dollar up</b> or down.<br>现在断言新总统会炒高还是炒低美元为时尚早。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tamper</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtamper with sth</b></td><td class="c3">篡改；擅自改动；胡乱摆弄<br><span class="en">to do sth to sth to change it without permission</span></td><td class="c4">Two policemen were accused of <b>tampering with</b> the evidence.<br>两名警察被控篡改证据。<br>The lock has been <b>tampered with</b>.<br>这把锁被做过手脚。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tangle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtangle with sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">争执；争吵；打架<br><span class="en">to become involved in an argument or a fight with sb</span></td><td class="c4">You've chosen the wrong man to <b>tangle with</b>.<br>你吵架找错人了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tank</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tank ˈup (on sth) <span class="tag">(slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">大量喝(酒)<br><span class="en">to drink a lot of alcohol</span></td><td class="c4">The lads had spent all evening <b>tanking up</b> on scotch.<br>小伙子们整晚都在狂饮苏格兰威士忌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tap</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtap sb for sth</b></td><td class="c3">向…索要；向…乞讨(尤指钱)<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to give you sth, especially money</span></td><td class="c4">Can't you <b>tap your father for</b> a loan?<br>你不能找你父亲要点钱吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtap sb for sth</b></td><td class="c3">选择(或指定)…做<br><span class="en">to choose sb for a particular role or job</span></td><td class="c4">A British actress has been <b>tapped for</b> a part in the movie.<br>已选定一名英国女演员出演这部电影的一个角色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtap sth ˈin/ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">录入；敲进信息；数字；字母等<br><span class="en">to put information, numbers, letters, etc. into a machine by pressing</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Tap in</b> your password.<br>请输入密码。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtap ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">用计算机获取…的信息<br><span class="en">to use a computer to obtain information from another computer</span></td><td class="c4">He had managed to <b>tap into</b> the company's database.<br>他设法进入了公司的数据库。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtap ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">利用；开发；发掘资源；知识等<br><span class="en">to use sth from a supply of energy, knowledge, etc. for your own advantage</span></td><td class="c4">Schools should <b>tap into</b> the knowledge and experience of people in the local community.<br>学校应该利用当地社区居民的知识和经验。<br>His talk about bullying <b>tapped into</b> parents' anxieties.<br>他的关于霸道行为的讲话是利用了父母的担忧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtap ˈout<br>ˌtap sb/sth ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使资金；资源；思想等枯竭；榨干<br><span class="en">to have nothing left of a supply of money, resources, ideas, etc., or to make sb have nothing left</span></td><td class="c4">If the were to <b>tap out</b>, the global system would lose its best customer.<br>假如美国财源枯竭，全球体系将失去最好的客户。<br>The city has <b>tapped out</b> the groundwater supply.<br>这座城市已经耗尽地下水供给。ˌ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtap sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">轻轻敲出(节奏)<br><span class="en">to hit a surface lightly, making a rhythm</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>tapped out</b> the rhythm with his foot.<br>他用脚轻轻打着节拍。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tape</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtape sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用绷带包扎<br><span class="en">to tie a bandage firmly around a wound</span></td><td class="c4">That's a nasty cut-come on, we'll get it all <b>taped up</b>.<br>伤口很深—快，我们用绷带把它包扎好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>taper</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtaper ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">规模；体积；数量等逐渐减少<br><span class="en">to gradually become smaller in size, volume, amount, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Our profits have begun to <b>taper off</b>.<br>我们的利润开始逐渐下滑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tart</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tart sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…装饰得很俗气；把…弄得花里胡哨<br><span class="en">to decorate or improve the appearance of sth, often in a way that other people do not think is attractive</span></td><td class="c4">They've <b>tarted up</b> the restaurant but the food hasn't improved.<br>他们把餐馆弄得花里胡哨，然而饭菜却没有改进。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tear'</b></td><td class="c2"><b>also ˌtear aˈbout/ˈround<br>ˌtear aˈbout/ˈround sth</b></td><td class="c3">忙碌地四处跑动<br><span class="en">to move very quickly from place to place, being very busy</span></td><td class="c4">The children were <b>tearing</b> around shouting.<br>孩子们吵吵嚷嚷地跑来跑去。<br>No wonder you're tired, <b>tearing</b> <b>about</b> like that all the time.<br>你成天那么东奔西走的，难怪要累呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtear at sth (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用…撕扯；撕裂；撕破；扯开<br><span class="en">to attack sth violently, especially by pulling pieces off it</span></td><td class="c4">The brambles <b>tore at</b> her legs.<br>荆棘划破了她的腿。<br>He <b>tore at</b> the meat with his bare hands.<br>他就用手把肉撕开了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtear sb/yourself/sth aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使依依不舍地；停止；(使)忍痛离去<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself stop doing sth they/you enjoy in order to do sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Come and visit us, if you can <b>tear</b> Bill <b>away</b> from his computer!<br>你要是能说服比尔离开计算。<br>He couldn't <b>tear</b> his eyes <b>away</b> from (= stop looking at) Mina.<br>他目不转睛地望着米娜。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtear sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">用力撕下；猛地拉掉<br><span class="en">to pull sth violently from the thing it is attached to</span></td><td class="c4">The foods had <b>torn away</b> the base of the bridge.<br>洪水把桥墩冲走了。<br>Thomas was <b>torn</b> between going to college or working for his father.<br>托马斯在上大学和为父亲打工之间难以取舍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtear sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">拆毁；拆除建筑物<br><span class="en">to pull or knock down a building, a wall, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They're <b>tearing down</b> some old houses to for money.<br>他们为了找钱把房问翻了个底朝天。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>tear ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">攻击；袭击；痛斥；抨击<br><span class="en">to attack sb/sth physically or with words</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>tore into</b> Jed with his fists.<br>他给了杰德几拳。<br>She <b>tore into</b> the students if they were late.<br>学生要是迟到，她就训斥他们。<br>They <b>tore into</b> their food (= started eating) as if they were starving.<br>他们狼吞虎咽地吃起来，好像饿坏了似的。<br>The door was nearly <b>torn</b> off its hinges.<br>门几乎要从铰链上拽下来了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtear ˈround<br>tear ˈround sth (BrE) AROUND, A E<br>tear sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">撕毁；撕碎纸；信等<br><span class="en">to destroy a piece of paper, a letter, etc. by pulling it into pieces</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>tore</b> up all the letters he had sent her.<br>她把他寄来的信都撕了。<br>Ray Charles was <b>tearing</b> it up at the piano, and the crowd was going wild.<br>雷•查尔斯激情四射地弹奏着钢琴，众人如痴如醉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>teem</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌteem ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">下暴雨；大雨倾盆<br><span class="en">to rain hard</span></td><td class="c4">It was absolutely <b>teeming down</b>.<br>大雨真是滂沱而下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tell</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtell aˈgainst sb <span class="tag">(formal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">对…极为不利<br><span class="en">to be a serious disadvantage to sb</span></td><td class="c4">Her lack of experience <b>told against</b> her.<br>她缺乏经验对她十分不利。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i tell sb/sth aˈpart</b></td><td class="c3">能够区分；能够分辨<br><span class="en">to be able to distinguish ¡'tell sb/sth from sb/sth to distinguish sb/ sb/sth from other similar people or things</span></td><td class="c4"><b>I can never tell the twins apart</b>.<br>我从来分不清这对双胞胎。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtell of sth <span class="tag">(formal, literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">公布；讲述<br><span class="en">to make sth known; to give an account of sth</span></td><td class="c4">The report <b>told of a series of</b> design errors.<br>这份报告披露了一系列设计上的失误。<br>Did you get <b>told off</b>?<br>你挨训了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtell on sb</b></td><td class="c3">主要是儿童用语<br><span class="en">used mainly by children</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>tell on</b> me, will you?<br>别告发我，好吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tend</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtend to sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">尤指出现问题时照看；照料；照管<br><span class="en">to care for sb/sth, especially when there is a problem</span></td><td class="c4">The injured were already being <b>tended to</b>.<br>伤员已经有人在护理了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtend towards sth<br>ˈtend towards doing sth <span class="tag">(less frequent)</span></b></td><td class="c3">趋向；倾向；趋于<br><span class="en">to take a particular direction or have a particular opinion; to have a lot of a particular quality</span></td><td class="c4">We're <b>tending towards</b> the view that all students should study two languages.<br>我们倾向于认为所有学生都应该学习两门语言。<br>His views <b>tend towards</b> the extreme.<br>他的观点趋于偏激。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tense</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tense ˈup<br>ˌtense sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使肌肉绷紧；拉紧<br><span class="en">if you tense up or tense sth up, you make your muscles stiff and tight because you are not relaxed</span></td><td class="c4">If you feel that you're <b>tensing up</b>,take a few moments to relax.<br>如果你觉得紧张，就放松会儿。<br><b>Tense up</b> your arm and leg muscles and then let them go.<br>绷紧胳膊和腿部肌肉，然后放松。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>test</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtest for sth<br>ˈtest sb/sth for sth</b></td><td class="c3">查验(成分等)；对(人或物)作…检测<br><span class="en">to examine sb/sth to see if a particular substance, etc. is present</span></td><td class="c4">They are <b>testing</b> for oil in the area.<br>他们正在这个地区勘探石油。<br>She was <b>tested</b> for hepatitis.<br>她作过肝炎检查。<br>The software has been <b>tested</b> for viruses.<br>这个软件已作过病毒检查。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtest sth ˈout (on sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">用人或物作…测试<br><span class="en">to try an idea, a machine, a product, etc. to see if it works well or if people like it</span></td><td class="c4">Let me <b>test this idea out</b> on you.<br>让我在你身上检验一下这个想法。<br>When you buy a bed, <b>test it out</b> in the shop.<br>买床时要在商店里试一试。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>testify</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtestify to sth</b></td><td class="c3">证明；证实；表明<br><span class="en">to show or be evidence that sth is true</span></td><td class="c4">Jamesssschool reports <b>testified to</b> his ability.<br>詹姆斯的在校成绩单说明了他的能力。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>thaw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthaw ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">冰或雪融化；解冻<br><span class="en">if ice or snow thaws out, it melts</span></td><td class="c4">Britain is <b>thawing out</b> after the freeze.<br>严寒过后，英国开始冰消雪化。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthaw ˈout<br>thaw sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使冷藏食物解冻；化冻<br><span class="en">to become, or to let frozen food become, soft and ready to cook</span></td><td class="c4">He took the meat <b>out</b> of the freezer and left it to <b>thaw</b> <b>out</b>.<br>他把肉从冰箱拿出来解冻。<br>My feet are frozen! I need to <b>thaw</b> them <b>out</b>.<br>我的脚冻僵了！我得把它们焐热。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>thin</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthin sth ˈdown (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">掺水等稀释；冲淡<br><span class="en">to make a liquid less thick or strong, for example by adding water to it</span></td><td class="c4">The paint needs to be <b>thinned down</b> with water before you use it.<br>颜料使用前需要加水调稀。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthin ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">减少；变稀薄<br><span class="en">to become fewer in number, or less thick</span></td><td class="c4">The crowd had <b>thinned out</b> and only a few people were left.<br>人群渐渐散去，只剩下几个人。<br>Once they were clear of the city, the traffic started to <b>thin out</b>.<br>他们一出城，来往车辆就开始减少了。<br>The trees began to <b>thin out</b> as we climbed higher.<br>我们再往上爬，树木就变得稀疏起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>think</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthink of sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">考虑；顾及；替…着想<br><span class="en">to consider sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">It's time you stopped being so selfish and started <b>thinking</b> about other people!<br>别这么自私了，该为别人想想了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthink aˈhead (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">预先考虑；事前筹划<br><span class="en">to think carefully about what might happen in the future; to plan for the future</span></td><td class="c4">Even when their children are very young, parents are <b>thinking ahead</b> to exams and jobs.<br>甚至在孩子年纪尚小的时候，父母就开始考虑他们将来的考试和就业了。<br>Pilots are trained to <b>think ahead</b>.<br>飞行员接受训练，学习预判本领。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthink ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">回想；追忆<br><span class="en">to remember or think about sth that happened in the past</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>thought back</b> to the day they first met.<br>她回想起他们初次见面的那一天。<br><b>Thinking back</b>, I'm sure I noticed there was something strange.<br>回想起来，我敢说我注意到了有些地方不太对劲儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthink for yourˈself</b></td><td class="c3">独立思考；自行决定<br><span class="en">to make your own decisions, form your own opinions, etc. without depending on other people</span></td><td class="c4">You need to learn to <b>think for</b> yourself.<br>你需要学会独立思考。<br>Our parents always encouraged us to <b>think for</b> ourselves.<br>父母总是鼓励我们自己拿主意。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthink sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">认真思索；仔细盘算<br><span class="en">to consider all the details of sth carefully, especially in order to find an answer or a solution to a problem</span></td><td class="c4">She needed to be alone to <b>think things out</b>.<br>她需要单独呆着把事情考虑清楚。1。<br>Take my advice and <b>think</b> things through before you do anything.<br>听我的劝，要三思而行。<br>Can't you <b>think</b> up a better excuse than that?<br>难道你就想不出一个更像样的借口。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>thirst</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthirst for sth <span class="tag">(literary)</span></b></td><td class="c3">渴望；渴求<br><span class="en">to want sth very much</span></td><td class="c4">Our opponents were <b>thirsting for</b> revenge.<br>我们的对手迫不及待地想复仇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>thrash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrash aˈround (also ˌthrash aˈbout especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">剧烈扭动；翻来覆去<br><span class="en">to move about in a violent, uncontrolled way</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>thrashed around</b> in the water, gasping for breath.<br>他在水中挣扎，急促地喘着气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrash sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">彻底讨论；坦诚地探讨(以寻求解决办法)<br><span class="en">to discuss sth thoroughly and in an open and honest way to try to find a solution</span></td><td class="c4">He called a meeting to <b>thrash out</b> the problem.<br>他召开了会议研讨这个问题。<br>Eventually they <b>thrashed out</b> an agreement.<br>他们经过讨论最终达成了协议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>thrive</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrive on sth</b></td><td class="c3">在(某种环境等)中自得其乐；乐意做(令人不快的事)<br><span class="en">to enjoy or be successful in a situation or condition that other people would not like</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>thrives on</b> hard work.<br>他以苦干为乐事。<br>Sue and Jack seem to <b>thrive on</b> arguments.<br>休和杰克似乎专爱吵架。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>throw</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth aˈbout/ˈround sth especially BrE</b></td><td class="c3">常指因生气四处扔；到处撒<br><span class="en">to send sth from your hand in different direc tions, often because you are angry</span></td><td class="c4">How do you stop babies <b>throwing</b> their food around?<br>怎样才能不让小孩子把食物撒得到处都是呢。<br>People were <b>throwing</b> glasses <b>round</b> the room.<br>人们在房间里到处扔玻璃杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">常指因生气或匆忙把…搁在一边<br><span class="en">to put sth quickly to one side, often because you are angry or in a hurry</span></td><td class="c4">She read the letter and immediately <b>threw it aside</b>.<br>她读完信便立刻把它丟到一边。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrow sth at sb</b></td><td class="c3">给…出难题；考验<br><span class="en">to do sth or give sb sth that tests their abilities and skills</span></td><td class="c4">You never know what life's going to <b>throw at</b> you.<br>人生的考验从来都是不可预见的。<br>We can cope with anything our opponents <b>throw at</b> us.<br>我们能应付对手的任何挑战。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrow yourself at sb <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">为建立恋爱关系对…大献殷勤；拼命讨好；百般勾引<br><span class="en">to be too anxious to try to attract sb, because you want to have a romantic relationship with them</span></td><td class="c4">He was flattered that such an attractive woman as Nell was <b>throwing herself at</b> him.<br>有内尔这样漂亮的女子向他献媚，他心里飘飘然起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrow yourself at sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">向…猛扑过去；冲向<br><span class="en">to rush or jump violently towards or onto sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The dogs <b>threw themselves at</b> the gate.<br>几条狗扑向大门。<br>The team <b>threw</b> away a 2-0 lead (= they were winning, but then lost the game).<br>该队在以2:0领先的情况下输掉了比赛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow yourself aˈway (on sb)</b></td><td class="c3">和诸方面与己不相配者交往；屈就<br><span class="en">to have relationship with sb, or work for sb, who is not good enough for you or does not deserve you</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>throw yourself away</b> on somebody like him.<br>不要屈尊和他这种人来往。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">扔回；抛回；掷还<br><span class="en">to return sth with a sharp movement of your arm or wrist</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>throw the ball back</b> to me?<br>帮我把球扔回来好吗？2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈback at sb</b></td><td class="c3">尤指为使人烦恼使想起；提醒；再提<br><span class="en">to remind sb of sth they have said or done in the past, especially to upset or annoy them</span></td><td class="c4">His unwise remark was frequently <b>thrown back at</b> him by his colleagues.<br>他的同事经常在他面前提起他的蠢话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be, thrown ˈback on sth</b></td><td class="c3">被迫依靠；无奈启用(弃用的旧东西)<br><span class="en">to be forced to rely on sth which you have not needed for a while because nothing else is available</span></td><td class="c4">The television broke down so we were <b>thrown</b> <b>back</b> on our own resources (= we had to entertain ourselves).<br>电视机坏了，我们只好自娱自乐。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">尽情；地干；尽兴地做<br><span class="en">to do sth with as much energy and pleasure as possible</span></td><td class="c4">We were <b>throwing down</b> at the party last night.<br>昨晚我们在聚会上玩了个痛快。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow ˈdown <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打架；争吵；挑衅叫板<br><span class="en">to fight or argue with sb, or to say sth that starts a fight or argument</span></td><td class="c4">She was mad as hell and ready to <b>throw down</b>.<br>她气得发疯，想大吵一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrowdown n <span class="tag">(AmE, slang)</span></b></td><td class="c3">打架；争吵</td><td class="c4">You could tell he was ready for a <b>throwdown</b>.<br>看得出来，他想大吵一通。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">放下；扔掉(武器)<br><span class="en">to drop or put your weapons down to show that you do not wish to fight any longer</span></td><td class="c4">The rebels have <b>thrown down</b> their arms.<br>反叛者已经放下武器。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使勉强做不想做；或做不到的事；强人所难<br><span class="en">to Suggest that sb should do sth you think they will not be willing or able to do</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>threw down</b> a direct challenge for him to tell them the truth.<br>她直接要求他告诉他们真相。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow yourself ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">猛地倒(或躺)在地上<br><span class="en">to move suddenly and violently so that you fall down to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>threw herself down</b> on the grass.<br>她扑倒在草地上。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb ˈin/into sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…关进(监狱)；监禁<br><span class="en">to force or order sb to enter a prison and stay there</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>thrown into</b> a police cell overnight.<br>他被抓进警察局，在拘留室过了一夜。动语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">额外赠送；奉送；白送<br><span class="en">to include sth with what you are selling or offering, without increasing the price</span></td><td class="c4">The job Pays £25 000, with a company car <b>thrown in</b>.<br>这份工作薪金为 25000 英镑，此外公司还配车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">未经细想加上；随口插进；漫不经心地加插话语；评论等<br><span class="en">to add a remark, comment, etc. without careful thought</span></td><td class="c4">Jack <b>threw in</b> the odd encouraging comment.<br>杰克意外地插了一句鼓舞人心的话。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使突然陷入…境地<br><span class="en">to put sb/sth suddenly in a particular state, especially a bad</span></td><td class="c4">The future of the company has been <b>thrown into</b> question by recent events.<br>最近的事件使人们对公司前景产生了疑虑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">使情况；问题等暴露出来；使更加明显<br><span class="en">to make a particular situation, problem, etc. more noticeable than before</span></td><td class="c4">Their differences have been <b>thrown into</b> sharp relief by the present crisis.<br>当前的危机将他们的分歧暴无遗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把(大量精力或资源等)投入；向…注入<br><span class="en">to use a lot of energy or resources to try to make sth successful</span></td><td class="c4">He's <b>thrown all his energy into</b> this project.<br>他所有的精力都投入了这个项目。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb ˈoff<br>ˌthrow sb ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">命令某人离开(某地)；驱逐；逐出<br><span class="en">to order sb to leave a place</span></td><td class="c4">Farmers are being <b>thrown off</b> their land.<br>农民正被赶出他们的土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈoff<br>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">打扰；扰乱；使慌乱<br><span class="en">to disturb sb/sth who is trying to do sth, making them fail or not behave as usual</span></td><td class="c4">The director came in while I was speaking and that <b>threw me off</b> a bit.<br>我讲话时主任走了进来，让我有点着慌。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈoff<br>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">使慌张；使张皇失措<br><span class="en">to make sb surprised and no longer calm</span></td><td class="c4">The senator was <b>thrown off</b> balance by the unexpected question.<br>这个出人意料的问题让参议员乱了方寸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">匆匆脱掉；拽下；扯掉(衣服等)<br><span class="en">to remove your clothes or sth covering your body quickly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>threw off</b> her clothes and leapt into the river.<br>她脱下衣服跳进了河里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth/yourself ˈoff<br>throw sb/ sth violently from</b></td><td class="c3">用力将…从高处扔下(或推下)；从高处跃下<br><span class="en">a high place; to jump from a high place</span></td><td class="c4">The sledge hit a bump and <b>threw</b> me off into the snow.<br>雪橇撞上了一处地面突起，把我摔到了雪地里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">匆匆穿上(衣服)<br><span class="en">to put on a piece of clothing quickly and carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>threw on</b> his clothes and ran downstairs.<br>他匆忙穿上衣服跑下楼去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈonto sth<br>ˌthrow yourself ˈon/ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">用力推向(或扔向)；朝…猛掷<br><span class="en">to send or push sb/sth violently onto sth</span></td><td class="c4">Jamie angrily threw the book <b>onto</b> the table.<br>杰米生气地把书摔到桌上。<br>The fire wasn't burning well, so we <b>threw on</b> more wood.<br>火烧得不旺，于是我们又添了些柴。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrow sth on sb/sth also<br>throw sth uˈpon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">使对…产生(怀疑或疑虑)<br><span class="en">if sb/sth throws doubt or suspicion on sb/sth, people start to wonder if sth is true, will continue, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">New evidence <b>threw</b> doubt on Tom's innocence.<br>新的证据令大家开始怀疑汤姆是否真的清白。<br>This controversy <b>throws</b> doubt on her political future.<br>这一争论使人们对她的政治前途产生了疑问。<br>They tried to <b>throw</b> suspicion on us.<br>他们企图让我们受到猜疑。回时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈthrow yourself on sb/sth (alsoˈthrow yourself onto sb/sth less frequent)</b></td><td class="c3">扑向；倒进<br><span class="en">to run towards sb/sth and fall onto them</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>threw herself on</b> him and burst into tears.<br>她扑到他怀里哭了起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb ˈout<br>throw sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">撵走；轰开；逐出<br><span class="en">to force sb to leave a place, their home, a job, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Tim's parents <b>threw him out</b> when he was 18.<br>蒂姆18 岁时父母就把他赶出了家门。<br>When the mine closed down, 50 people were <b>thrown out</b> of their jobs.<br>煤矿倒闭，有50人失去了工作。<br>When she failed her exams, she was <b>thrown out</b> of college.<br>她考试不及格，被学院开除了。<br>Many families have been <b>thrown out</b> into the street (= out of their homes).<br>很多家庭被迫流落街头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使混乱；使出错<br><span class="en">to confuse sb/sth; to make sb make a mistake; to make sth wrong</span></td><td class="c4">One of the figures was wrong and it <b>threw me out</b> completely.<br>有一个数字有误，把我完全搞糊涂了。<br>Some unexpected costs <b>threw our calculations out</b> by £4 000.<br>一些计划外的开销使我们的计算差了4000英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb ˈover <span class="tag">(old-fashioned)</span></b></td><td class="c3">同某人绝交；拋弃某人<br><span class="en">to end a relationship with sb</span></td><td class="c4">His girlfriend <b>threw him over</b> for somebody else.<br>他的女友为了新欢抛弃了他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈover (to sb) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">将…随手；扔出(给某人)<br><span class="en">to pass sth to sb in a careless or rough way</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>threw the paper over</b> to me.<br>他把报纸扔给了我。<br>Will you <b>throw over</b> those keys?<br>你把那些钥匙扔过来好吗。<br>Will you <b>throw me the paper over</b>?<br>把报纸扔过来好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb toˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">使意外相聚；使不期而遇<br><span class="en">to bring people into contact with each other, often unexpectedly</span></td><td class="c4">Fate had <b>thrown them together</b>.<br>命运使他们聚在一起。<br>We were strangers, <b>thrown together</b> by circumstance.<br>我们萍水相逢。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow ˈup<br>ˌthrow sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">呕吐；呕出<br><span class="en">to bring food you have eaten back out of your mouth</span></td><td class="c4">The smell made me want to <b>throw up</b>.<br>这种气味令我作呕。<br>He ate the meal and immediately <b>threw it all up</b>.<br>他吃了饭，但马上全吐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sb/sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">猛地举高；举起；拾起<br><span class="en">to lift sb/sth and make them move upwards into the air by moving your hand quickly</span></td><td class="c4">The baby loved being <b>thrown up</b> into the air.<br>那孩子喜欢被一下子举到空中。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌthrow sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">产生；使显眼；使引起；注意<br><span class="en">to produce sth; to show or make people notice sth</span></td><td class="c4">Her research has <b>thrown up</b> some interesting facts.<br>她的研究有些很有意思的发现。<br>The competition <b>threw up</b>. some promising players.<br>这次比赛让一批有潜力的运动员崭露头。<br>She <b>threw her arms up</b> in horror.<br>她惊恐地举起了双臂。s。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>tick aˈway<br>tick sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">钟表发出嘀嗒声；嘀嗒地走<br><span class="en">if a clock ticks away or ticks the minutes or seconds away, it makes continuous short light regular sounds to mark time passing</span></td><td class="c4">The clock <b>ticked away</b> in the silence.<br>那只钟在寂静中嘀嗒作响。<br>We waited as the clock <b>ticked away</b> the last few seconds of the old millennium.<br>我们静候着时钟嘀嗒走过旧千年的最后几秒钟。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtick aˈway/by/ˈpast</b></td><td class="c3">时间</td><td class="c4">The seconds <b>ticked by</b> as I tried to think of something to say.<br>时间一秒一秒地过去，我搜肠刮肚想找话说。<br>Two long minutes ricked <b>past</b>.<br>漫长的两分钟过去了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>tick ˈover <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">通常用于进行时<br><span class="en">usually used in the progressive tenses</span></td><td class="c4">Don't leave the engine <b>ticking over</b> while you are in the shop.<br>你去商店的时候别让引擎空转。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tide</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtide sb ˈover<br>tide sb ˈover sth</b></td><td class="c3">帮助某人渡过(难关)；协助；某人克服(困难)<br><span class="en">to help sb through a difficult period by providing what they need</span></td><td class="c4">Weve got enough money to <b>tide us over</b> until next month.<br>我们有足够的钱凑合到下个月。<br>Our savings should <b>tide us over</b> the next couple of months.<br>我们的积蓄应该够我们挺过以后几个月。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tidy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtidy sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">清理；整理房间；橱柜等<br><span class="en">to make a room, a cup board, etc. tidy by removing things you do not want and arranging the rest neatly</span></td><td class="c4">Its time to <b>tidy out</b> the kitchen cupboards.<br>该清理厨房里的橱柜了。<br>The whole place needs <b>tidying</b> up.<br>这个地方需要彻底整理。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtidy sb ˈup<br>ˌtidy yourself ˈup <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使更整洁帅气；梳理打扮<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself look cleaner and neater</span></td><td class="c4">How about <b>tidying yourself up</b> before we go out?<br>我们出去前你捯饬一下好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtidy sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">修饰；润色书面材料<br><span class="en">to finish sth such as a piece of written work by dealing with the last details well or correctly</span></td><td class="c4">My lecture still needs <b>tidying up</b>.<br>我的讲稿。<br>She was always <b>tidying up</b>.<br>她总是在抬掇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtidy sth ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">妥善处理；料理<br><span class="en">to make sure that things are dealt with correctly</span></td><td class="c4">He had to go to Boston to <b>tidy up</b> his brother's affairs (= after his brother died).<br>他得去波士顿料理他哥哥的后事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tie</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtie ˈin (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">与…相配；相符<br><span class="en">to fit or be in agreement with sth</span></td><td class="c4">This new evidence <b>ties in</b> with the witness's statement.<br>这一新证据和目击者的证词相吻合。<br>That doesn't <b>tie in</b> with what you said yesterday.<br>这个跟你昨天说的有。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>tie ˈin (with sth),.tie sth ˈin (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使(与…)连接在一起；(使)同时进行<br><span class="en">to link sth or be linked to sth; to happen or to arrange for sth to happen at the same time as sth else</span></td><td class="c4">The book was intended to <b>tie</b> in with the series.<br>这本书是为配合这部电视系列剧的播出而出版的。<br>Jack couldn't be <b>tied</b> in with the murder.<br>杰克不可能与这起谋杀案有关联。<br>The release of their new album will be <b>tied</b> in with the tour.<br>他们的新专辑将在巡演时发行。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtie sb ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">限制；束缚；约束<br><span class="en">to restrict sb to a particular situation, person, organization, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">They were <b>tied into</b> an agreement to buy from particular suppliers.<br>他们受协议约束，必须从特定供应商处进货。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtie sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">结扎；绳索等封口<br><span class="en">to put a knot in the end of sth; to close sth with string, thread, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">We moored <b>off</b> the north coast ofthe island.<br>我们在该岛北部海岸停船。1。<br>They tried to find a sheltered spot where they could <b>tie</b> the boat up.<br>他们试图找个有遮蔽的地方停船。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtie-up n</b></td><td class="c3">停滞不前；停顿；(尤指)交通阻塞</td><td class="c4">A <b>tie-up</b> on the highway caused major delays.<br>公路上的交通拥堵造成重大延误。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tighten</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtighten ˈup<br>ˌtighten sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使变紧；变得更牢固<br><span class="en">to become or to make sth tight or tighter</span></td><td class="c4">His face muscles <b>tightened up</b> in anger.<br>他生气地紧绷着脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtighten ˈup<br>ˌtighten sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">变得更仔细(或严格)；使更严格<br><span class="en">to become more careful or strict about sth; to make sth more strict</span></td><td class="c4">Laws on gambling have <b>tightened up</b> recently.<br>有关赌博的法律最近变得更加严厉。<br>The police are <b>tightening up</b> on drink-driving.<br>警方正在采取更加严厉的措施对付酒驾。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>time</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtime ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">超时中止；过期失效<br><span class="en">if sth times out, it goes beyond a particular time limit and stops working, is no longer valid, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Your Internet session will <b>time out</b> after a few minutes if there is no activity.<br>如果几分钟无操作，互联网访问将中止。<br>The demo will <b>time out</b> after three weeks.<br>体验版将在三周后到期。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tinker</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtinker aˈround (also ˌtinker aˈbout especially BrE) (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">作(不起作用的)小修小补<br><span class="en">to make small changes to sth in order to repair or improve it, especially in a way that may not be helpful</span></td><td class="c4">He's outside <b>tinkering around</b> with his bike.<br>他在外面捣鼓他的自行车。<br>They haven't made any real changes to the systemthey've just been <b>tinkering around</b> a bit.<br>他们对系统没有作任何真正的改进——只不过是一点小修小补。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtinker with sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…作(不起作用的)小修小补<br><span class="en">to make small changes to sth in order to repair or improve it, especially in a way that may not be helpful</span></td><td class="c4">The government should stop <b>tinkering with</b> the education system.<br>政府必须停止对教育制度瞎调整。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtip sb ˈoff (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">暗中警告；密报；泄露(尤指非法的事情)<br><span class="en">to give sb a warning about sth which they should know about, especially sth illegal</span></td><td class="c4">The police were <b>tipped off</b> about the bank robbery.<br>警方获得了抢劫银行的密报。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtip ˈover<br>ˌtip sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">使跌倒；翻倒<br><span class="en">to become no longer stable and fall over; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">The bottle <b>tipped over</b> and all the water spilled out.<br>瓶子倒了，水全洒了。</td></tr>
