<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtip ˈup<br>ˌtip sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使翻倒；倾覆<br><span class="en">to become unsteady and fall forwards, backwards or sideways; to make sth do this</span></td><td class="c4">One after another the canoes <b>tipped up</b>.<br>划艇一艘接一艘地翻了。<br>The pile of books on the end of the table nearly <b>tipped it up</b>.<br>桌子一头的一摞书几乎把桌子压翻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtip sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使倾斜；使倾側<br><span class="en">to change the angle of sth so that it leans to one side</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>tipped her glass up</b> and drained it.<br>她倾斜玻璃杯把水倒掉。<br>He <b>tipped his face up</b> towards the light.<br>他朝灯光侧过脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tire</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtire of sb/sth<br>ˈtire of doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…感到厌倦；对…腻烦<br><span class="en">to become bored with sb/sth or begin to enjoy them/it less</span></td><td class="c4">They soon <b>tired of</b> the beach and went for a walk.<br>他们很快就觉得海滩腻味了，便去散步。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtire sb ˈout<br>tire yourself ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使筋疲力尽；疲惫不堪<br><span class="en">to make sb/yourself feel very tired</span></td><td class="c4">Try not to <b>tire yourself out</b> too soon in the race.<br>赛跑时尽量不要过早地把力气用光。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tog</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be/get,togged ˈout/ˈup (in sth) <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">穿着(适合某场合的)服装；专门穿戴<br><span class="en">to be wearing clothes for a particular activity or occasion</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>were all togged out</b> in our best clothes.<br>我们都穿上了最漂亮的衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>toil</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtoil aˈway (at sth)</b></td><td class="c3">辛苦地做困难或乏味的<br><span class="en">to work extremely hard at sth difficult or boring</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>toiled away</b> at his homework all the evening.<br>他一晚上都在费劲地做作业。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tone</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtone sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">降低语气；调子等；使讲话；意见等缓和；使温和<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a speech, an opinion, etc. less offensive, critical or unkind than it was originally</span></td><td class="c4">He had to <b>tone down</b> his article before it was published.<br>他得在文章发表前把措辞改缓和些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtone sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使(衣服等)暗淡；使不太艳丽；使不太扎眼<br><span class="en">to make sth, especially your clothes, less bright and noticeable</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>toned down</b> her style of dress when she started her new job.<br>她干上新工作后穿得庄重了些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtone sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使(颜色)柔和<br><span class="en">to make a colour less bright</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>toned down</b> the yellow paint with a little white.<br>我们掺了一点白色，使黄漆显得柔和些。<br>Petra used powder to <b>tone down</b> her rosy cheeks.<br>佩特拉在红红的面颊上搽了些粉遮盖一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtone ˈup<br>ˌtone sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使(肌肉或身体)更结实；使更强壮；使更健康<br><span class="en">to make your muscles Or a part of your body firmer, stronger, and healthier</span></td><td class="c4">It's time I <b>toned up</b> and slimmed down.<br>我应该把身体练得更壮更瘦。<br>This exercise will <b>tone up</b> your stomach muscles.<br>这项运动有助于增强腹肌。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tool</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtool aˈround<br>ˌtool aˈround sth <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">驾车兜风；开车；闲逛<br><span class="en">to drive a car around an area</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>tooled around</b> Canada in his van.<br>我们开着他的大众牌面包车在加拿大兜了一圈。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>top</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtop sth ˈoff (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以…圆满结束；(用…)完成<br><span class="en">to complete sth in a successful or pleasant way, especially by adding one final thing</span></td><td class="c4">Jane was wearing a very colourful outfit, <b>topped off</b> with a dramatic hat.<br>简穿了一身色彩鲜艳的套装，头戴一顶引人注目的帽子，十分好看。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtop ˈout (at sth)</b></td><td class="c3">达到顶点；到最高点<br><span class="en">to stop increasing after reaching a high level</span></td><td class="c4">Your annual salary will <b>top out</b> at seventy thousand dollars.<br>你的年薪最高是七万元。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtop sb ˈup <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">给某人的杯子斟满；满上某人的杯子；给某人续满杯<br><span class="en">to fill sb’s glass or cup by adding some more liquid</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>top you up</b>?<br>给你把杯子加满好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtop. sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">斟满；注满；装满(未满的容器)<br><span class="en">(with sth). to add some more liquid to some already in a glass, cup or other container in order to fill it</span></td><td class="c4">We should top the car <b>up</b> with oil before we set off.<br>我们出发前应该给车子加满汽油。<br>I need to top <b>up</b> my mobile (= pay money in advance to be able to make mobile phone/cellphone calls).<br>我得给手机充值了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>topple</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtopple ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">倾斜翻倒；倒下<br><span class="en">to become unsteady and fall over</span></td><td class="c4">The vase wobbled and then <b>toppled over</b>.<br>花瓶摇晃了几下就倒了。心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>toss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>toss sth aˈround (also, toss sth aˈbout especially BrE)</b></td><td class="c3">漫不经心地讨论；对…泛泛而谈<br><span class="en">to discuss ideas in a casual or general way</span></td><td class="c4">We sat and <b>tossed around</b> a few suggestions.<br>我们坐着随意讨论了几项提议。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtoss sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">生气或匆忙把…丢到一边<br><span class="en">to put sth quickly to one side because you are angry or in a hurry</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>tossed aside</b> the newspaper angrily and stood up.<br>他生气地把报纸往旁边一扔，站起身来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtoss sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">随意扔掉；丟掉<br><span class="en">to throw sth away carelessly</span></td><td class="c4">She finished her drink and <b>tossed the can away</b>.<br>她喝完饮料就随手把罐子扔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtoss sth ˈoff <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">粗枝大叶或不费力气地很快做好；轻而易举；地完成<br><span class="en">to do sth quickly, easily and often with little care or effort</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>tossed this novel off</b> in two months.<br>他用了两个月就把小说轻松写完了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtot sth ˈup <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…加起来；计算…的总和<br><span class="en">to add together several numbers or amounts in order to get a total</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>tot up</b> how much I owe you?<br>你能算一下我总共欠你多少钱吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>total</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtotal ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">总数达到；总共是<br><span class="en">to reach a particular total</span></td><td class="c4">The costs <b>total up</b> to over a million.<br>费用总计超过一百万。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtotal sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">把…加起来；计算…的总和<br><span class="en">to add amounts together to get a total</span></td><td class="c4">Let's <b>total up</b> what weve spent.<br>咱们算一算总共花了多少钱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>touch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtouch sb for sth <span class="tag">(BrE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">向…讨要；劝…借出(钱)<br><span class="en">to persuade sb to give or lend you money</span></td><td class="c4">He tried to <b>touch me for</b> twenty pounds.<br>他想让我给他二十英镑。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtouch sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">触发；激起；引发爆炸；暴力或困难局面<br><span class="en">to make sth begin, especially an explosion or a violent or difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">The explosion was <b>touched off</b> by a single spark.<br>爆炸是由一个火星引起的。<br>His arrest <b>touched off</b> a riot.<br>他被逮捕触发了一场暴乱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtouch on/upon sth</b></td><td class="c3">简略；地论及；谈及；提及<br><span class="en">to mention or deal briefly with a topic, a problem, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>touched on</b> the need for increased funding.<br>他提到有必要增加资金。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtouch sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">稍加修饰；润色；修改；增补<br><span class="en">to improve sth by making small changes or additions</span></td><td class="c4">He had to <b>touch up</b> the paintwork to cover the scratches.<br>他只好稍稍涂了点漆，把漆面上的划痕遮盖上。<br>The photo had been <b>touched up</b>.<br>照片被修饰过。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tough</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtough sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">坚持；熬过<br><span class="en">to stay firm and determined in a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">He decided not to resign, but to stay and <b>tough it out</b>.<br>他决定不辞职，而是留下来撑到底。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>toughen</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtoughen sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">加强；强化法律；规定<br><span class="en">to make sth such as a law or a rule more strict</span></td><td class="c4">The legislation on this trade needs to be <b>toughened up</b>.<br>这一行业的法规需要加严格。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>towel</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtowel ˈoff <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">用毛巾擦干(身体)<br><span class="en">to dry your body with a towel after a shower, swim, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">OK, kids, time to get out of the pool and <b>towel</b> of.<br>好了，孩子们，到时间了，从游泳池出来用毛巾揩干身体。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tower</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtower aˈbove/over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">高于；超过(周边的人或物)<br><span class="en">to be much higher or taller than other things or people that are near</span></td><td class="c4">The new offices <b>tower above</b> the rest of the town.<br>新的办公楼耸立于城中。<br>Amy <b>towers over</b> her mother.<br>埃米个子比母亲高一大截。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtower aˈbove/over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">胜过<br><span class="en">to be much better, more famous, etc. than other people or things</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>towers above</b> all other poets of his generation.<br>他在同时代诗人中出类拔萃。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>toy</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtoy with sth</b></td><td class="c3">漫不经心地想；不太；认真地考虑；把…当作儿戏<br><span class="en">to consider sth but not very seriously or for very long</span></td><td class="c4">He had <b>toyed with</b> the idea of living in Germany.<br>他曾经动过定居德国的念头。<br>The possibility had been <b>toyed with</b> but rejected.<br>这种可能性曾经想到过，但被排除了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trace</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrace sth ˈback (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">探究事物的本源；追溯(到…)<br><span class="en">to find the origin or cause of sth by following evidence backwards from the present time</span></td><td class="c4">Many different childhood illnesses can be <b>traced back</b> to certain foods.<br>众多儿童疾病的起因都可溯源到某种食物。<br>Boston has a large population that <b>traces its roots back</b> to Ireland.<br>波士顿有大量人口祖籍在爱尔兰。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrace sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">清晰地勾画；标出<br><span class="en">to draw a shape or a mark clearly</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>traced out</b> our route on the map.<br>我在地图上描出我们的路线。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>track</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrack sb/sth ˈdown (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">在某处搜寻到；追踪到；追查到<br><span class="en">to find sb/sth after a long and difficult search</span></td><td class="c4">We finally <b>tracked Sam down</b> to his parents'house.<br>我们终于在他父母家中找到了萨姆。<br>It has taken ten years to <b>track down</b> the wreckage of the plane.<br>用了十年时间才搜寻到飞机的残骸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trade</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrade ˈdown (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">降低消费<br><span class="en">to spend less money on things than you used to</span></td><td class="c4">People are <b>trading down</b> and buying cheaper food.<br>人们都减少开销，购买廉价食品。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrade ˈdown (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">卖好买次；卖大买小；卖高价的买低价的<br><span class="en">to sell sth large or expensive and buy sth smaller or less expensive</span></td><td class="c4">They <b>traded down</b> to a house with fewer bedrooms.<br>他们卖掉房子，买了个卧室少些的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrade sth ˈin (for sth)</b></td><td class="c3">以旧换新；折价贴换<br><span class="en">to give sth that you have used to sb you are buying sth new from as part of your payment</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>traded his motorbike in</b> for a new van.<br>他把摩托车折价卖掉，添钱买了辆新客货车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrade sth ˈoff (against sth)</b></td><td class="c3">权衡；平衡；调和<br><span class="en">to balance two things or situations that are opposed to each other</span></td><td class="c4">They were willing to <b>trade off</b> information to keep the hostages alive.<br>为丁保住人质性命，他们愿意交出信息。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrade on sth (also ˈtrade upon sth more formal, less frequent) <span class="tag">(disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">利用…(谋私利)<br><span class="en">to unfairly make use of sth for your own advantage</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>traded on</b> his father's name to get himself a job.<br>他倚仗父亲的名望为自己谋了份差事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrade ˈup (to sth)</b></td><td class="c3">卖次买好；卖小买大；卖低价的买高价的<br><span class="en">to sell sth small or not expensive in order to buy sth larger or more expensive</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>traded up</b> to a larger car.<br>他卖掉了汽车，买了辆更大的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trail</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrail aˈway/off</b></td><td class="c3">话语逐渐减弱到停止；逐渐消失<br><span class="en">if sb's speech trails away/off, it gradually becomes quieter and then stops</span></td><td class="c4">Mark's voice <b>trailed away</b> to a whisper.<br>马克的声音越来越低，最后听不到了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>train</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrain sth on/upon sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把(枪口)瞄准；把(相机)对准；把(灯光)指向<br><span class="en">to point sth such as a gun, a camera, a light, etc. at sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>trained the camera on</b> the bride.<br>她把照相机对准了新娘。<br>He kept his eyes <b>trained on</b> the road ahead.<br>他的眼睛一直盯着前方的路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrain sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">培养；训练<br><span class="en">to make sb ready to do a job or an activity by teaching them the skills they need</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>train up</b> extra staff for Christmas.<br>我们得培训额外职员，为圣诞节作准备。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>traipse</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtraipse aˈround<br>ˌtraipse aˈround sth (BrE also,traipse ˈround,,traipse ˈround sth) <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">疲惫地到处走；拖着脚步走<br><span class="en">to walk from place to place slowly because you are tired and unwilling</span></td><td class="c4">We spent the afternoon <b>traipsing around</b> the town.<br>我们拖着疲惫的身子在城里转了一下午。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trample</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrample on/over sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">践踏；蹂躏；摧残情感；权利<br><span class="en">to ignore sb's feelings or rights and treat them as if they are not important</span></td><td class="c4">The government is <b>trampling on</b> the views of ordinary people.<br>政府在践踏民意。<br>Don't let Jack <b>trample all over</b> you!<br>不要让杰克肆意伤害你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trawl</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrawl ˈthrough sth (for sth/sb)</b></td><td class="c3">在…中搜找；搜寻；查阅<br><span class="en">to search through a large amount of information or a large number of people, places, etc., looking for a particular thing or person</span></td><td class="c4">The police are <b>trawling through</b> their files for similar cases.<br>警方正在档案中搜寻类似的案例。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>treat</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtreat sb to sth</b></td><td class="c3">用…招待；以…款待<br><span class="en">to entertain sb with sth special</span></td><td class="c4">Visitors will be <b>treated to</b> a spectacular show.<br>届时会让参观者观看一场精彩绝伦的演出。<br>We were <b>treated to</b> (= we had to suffer) a two-hour lecture.<br>我们不得不忍受折磨，听了两小时的讲座。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trick</b></td><td class="c2"><b>trick sb ˈinto sth<br>ˌtrick sb ˈinto doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">诱使某人做某事<br><span class="en">to manage to get sb to do sth by tricking them</span></td><td class="c4">She felt she'd been <b>tricked into</b> marriage.<br>她觉得自己结婚是上当受骗丁。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrick sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从某人处骗取某物<br><span class="en">to take sth away from sb by tricking them</span></td><td class="c4">An go year old woman was <b>tricked out of</b> her life savings.<br>一位80岁老妇一辈子的积蓄都被骗走了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trifle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrifle with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">息慢；轻视；小看<br><span class="en">to treat sb/sth without respect as if they are not very important</span></td><td class="c4">He is not a man to be <b>trifled with</b>.<br>他这个人小觑不得。<br>He was a man who <b>trifled with</b> women's affections.<br>他是个玩弄女性感情的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trigger</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrigger sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">使爆发；引发；促发；激发</td><td class="c4">Nuts can <b>trigger off</b> a violent allergic reaction.<br>坚果会引起严重的过敏反应。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trim</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrim sth aˈway/ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">切去；修剪不；需要的部分<br><span class="en">to cut off a small part of sth because it is not needed</span></td><td class="c4">My hair is too long now. Can you <b>trim off</b> about two centimetres?<br>我的头发太长了。你给我剪掉大约两厘米好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrim ˈdown<br>ˌtrim sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">减少；缩减<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sth, smaller in size</span></td><td class="c4">The movie was <b>trimmed down</b> to two and a half hours.<br>电影经过剪辑时长减为两个半小时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trip</b></td><td class="c2"><b>trip ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">电器；电气系统等停机；跳闸<br><span class="en">(of an electrical device, system, etc.) to stop working because the electricity stops flowing</span></td><td class="c4">The device can operate at low temperatures without <b>tripping out</b>.<br>此装置可在低温下运行，不会断电停机。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrip sb ˈout <span class="tag">(AmE informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">意外；使震惊；使紧张<br><span class="en">to make sb feel surprised, shocked, or nervous</span></td><td class="c4">Girl, you're <b>tripping me out</b>! Are you OK?<br>小姑娘，你吓了我一跳！你没事吧？I。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>trip ˈover<br>ˌtrip ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">绊倒；绊趔起<br><span class="en">to fall or almost fall because you have accidentally hit your foot against sth while you are walking or running</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>tripped over</b> the rug and fell heavily.<br>我给小地毯绊了一下，重重地摔了个跟头。<br>He <b>kept</b> tripping over.<br>他不断地绊倒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>trip ˈover<br>ˌtrip ˈover sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">故意使犯错误；出差错<br><span class="en">to make a mistake, to deliberately make sb do this</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>knew</b> I had to think carefully in the interview or I might trip up.<br>我知道面试时我必须思路清晰，否则就会出错。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trot</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrot ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">快步走；小跑(去某处)<br><span class="en">to go somewhere, walking quite quickly</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>trotted off</b> to school happily with her new lunch box.<br>她带着新午饭盒高高兴兴地跑去上学了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrot sth ˈout <span class="tag">(informal, disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">随口说出；假意重提惯用的；托词；解释等<br><span class="en">to say or repeat sth such as an excuse, an explanation, etc. without thinking about it or being sincere about it</span></td><td class="c4">The airline <b>trotted out</b> the same old excuses to explain the delays.<br>航空公司又用那老一套的借口来解释延误。<br>He's just <b>trotting out</b> the party line again (= in politics).<br>他又老调重弹重提该觉的方针。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trump</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtrump sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">捏造(罪名)；编造(谣言)；制造(借口)</td><td class="c4">Several of his colleagues <b>trumped up</b> a complaint to get him removed from the job.<br>他的几位同事诬陷他，使他丢掉了工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>truss</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtruss sb/sth ˈup. <span class="tag">(old-fashioned)</span></b></td><td class="c3">将(人或动物)捆紧；绑牢<br><span class="en">to tie a person or an animal up very tightly so that they cannot move or escape</span></td><td class="c4">The victims had been <b>trussed</b> up with rope and beaten.<br>受害者被人用绳子捆绑起来进行殴打。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>trust</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrust in sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">相信；信任；信赖<br><span class="en">to have confidence in sb/sth; to rely on sb completely</span></td><td class="c4">I was scared before the operation, but I <b>trusted in</b> the skill of the doctors.<br>手术前我很害怕，但我相信医生的医术。<br>He urged them to <b>trust in</b> God.<br>他力劝他们相信上帝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtrust sb with sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…委托；给…照管；托付；托交<br><span class="en">to give sb/sth to a person to take care of because you believe they will be careful with them/it</span></td><td class="c4">Would you <b>trust her with</b> the children?<br>你把孩子们交给她照看好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>try</b></td><td class="c2"><b>try ˈback<br>.try sb ˈback <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">因未通上话再打电话(给某人)<br><span class="en">to telephone sb again when you have already telephoned them but have not managed to speak to them</span></td><td class="c4">Can you <b>try back</b> later?<br>你过会儿再打过来好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtry for sth <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">试图获得；力争贏得<br><span class="en">to make an attempt to get or win sth</span></td><td class="c4">Are you going to <b>try for</b> that job?<br>你打算争取那份工作吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtry it ˈon (with sb)</b></td><td class="c3">摸(某人的)脾气；探底细；探虚实<br><span class="en">to behave badly towards sb or try to get sth from them just to see what you can do before they become angry or stop you</span></td><td class="c4">The kids sometimes <b>try it on</b> with a new babysitter.<br>孩子们有时会摸摸新保姆的脾气。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f<br>try sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">试穿(衣物)<br><span class="en">to put on a piece of clothing to see if it fits and how it looks</span></td><td class="c4">Can I <b>try on the blue one</b>?<br>我能试试那件蓝色的吗。<br>If you like it, why don't you <b>try it on</b>?<br>你要是喜欢为什么不试穿一下呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtry ˈout (for sth) <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">参加(…的)选拔；参加(…的)试演<br><span class="en">to compete for a place in a sports team, a part in a play, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He tried <b>out</b> for the school band.<br>他参加了学校乐队的遴选。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtryout n <span class="tag">(AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">选拔；试演<br><span class="en">a test, etc. to choose players for a team, actors for a play, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The team is holding <b>tryouts</b> this Thursday.<br>该队将于本周四进行选拔。<br>Did you have a <b>tryout</b> for the school play?<br>你参加学校戏剧演员遴选了吗？E。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>tuck /tsk/ try sb/sth ˈout (on sb)</b></td><td class="c3">试用；试验；测试<br><span class="en">to test sb/sth to see how good and useful they are or how suitable for a particular task or purpose before you decide to use them/it</span></td><td class="c4">We've been <b>trying</b> <b>out</b> some new musicians for our band.<br>我们一直在为我们的乐队试找一些新乐手。<br>He couldn't wait to <b>try</b> <b>out</b> his new invention.<br>他迫不及待地想试验一下自己的新发明。<br>The drug has not been tried <b>out</b> on humans yet.<br>这种药尚未进行人体临床试验。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tuck</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtuck ˈin<br>ˌtuck ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">酣畅淋漓地吃；狼吞虎咽地吃<br><span class="en">to eat food, especially quickly or with enthusiasm</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>tucked in</b> hungrily.<br>我们如饿虎扑食般大吃一迪。<br>He was <b>tucking into</b> a huge plateful of pasta.<br>他在狼吞虎咽地吃一大盘意大利面。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtuck sb ˈin/up</b></td><td class="c3">把(孩子等)的被褥掖好；给…盖；好被子<br><span class="en">to cover sb, especially a child, comfortably in bed by pulling the covers around them</span></td><td class="c4">Will you come and <b>tuck me in</b>, Mummy?<br>妈妈，来给我掖掖被子好吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtuck sth ˈin<br>ˌtuck sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把衣服；床单；绳索；头发等的松散末端收拢好；把…掖在…里<br><span class="en">to push or fold the loose end of a piece of clothing, a sheet, rope, hair, etc., in sth, to make it tidy or hold it in position</span></td><td class="c4">Tom, <b>tuck your shirt in</b>!<br>汤姆，披好你的衬衣。<br><b>Tuck</b> the flap of the envelope in.<br>把信封的封盖折好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtuck sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">将…收起；把…塞进安全或舒适；的狭小空间<br><span class="en">to move or put sth in a small space, especially to hide it or keep it safe or comfortable</span></td><td class="c4">She kicked off her shoes and <b>tucked her feet up</b> under her.<br>她踢掉鞋子，盘起双腿。<br>She sat with her legs <b>tucked up</b> under her.<br>她盘腿坐着。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tug</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtug at sth</b></td><td class="c3">使劲拉；用力扯；猛拽<br><span class="en">to give sth a quick, strong pull</span></td><td class="c4">Daniel <b>tugged at</b> my sleeve.<br>丹尼尔拽了拽我的衣袖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tumble</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtumble ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">突然倒塌；轰然坍塌<br><span class="en">to fall suddenly to the ground in a dramatic way</span></td><td class="c4">One push and the wall came <b>tumbling down</b>.<br>那堵墙一推就倒塌了。<br>Her long dark harr <b>tumbled down</b> around her face.<br>她那乌黑的长发垂在她的脸庞周围。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtumble ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">倒下；落下<br><span class="en">to fall to the ground</span></td><td class="c4">She knocked the statue and it <b>tumbled over</b>.<br>她碰到塑像上，塑像就翻倒了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>tune</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtune ˈin (to sth)<br>tune ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">收听(广播节目)；收看(电视节目)<br><span class="en">to turn on the radio or television in order to listen or watch a programme or channel</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>tuned</b> in to watch the football.<br>我们打开电视看了那场足球比赛。<br><b>Tune</b> <b>into</b> next week's exciting episode!<br>下周剧集精彩，敬请收看！2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtune sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">给收音机或；电视微调；调…的频道<br><span class="en">to adjust the controls on a radio or television so that you can hear or see a programme or channel clearly</span></td><td class="c4">The radio isn't Properly <b>tuned in</b>.<br>收音机没有调好台。<br>I keep the radio <b>tuned in</b> to the BBC.<br>我把收音机调定在英国广播公司的频道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtune sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">收听(广播节目)；收看(电视节目)<br><span class="en">to turn on the radio or television in order to listen to or watch a programme</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Tune in</b> our special tonight at nine.<br>今晚九点敬请收看我们的电视特别节目。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˌtuned ˈin (to sth)<br>be ˌtuned ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">明白；理解<br><span class="en">to be aware of or understand sth, especially other people's feelings</span></td><td class="c4">Parents should be <b>tuned</b> in to the needs of their child.<br>父母应该理解孩子的需要。<br>I'm <b>tuned</b> in to what I have to do.<br>我知道我该做什么。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>tune ˈout<br>ˌtune sb/sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">对不用心听；不予理睬；听而不闻</td><td class="c4">When Lee started talking about her job, Tim just <b>tuned out</b>.<br>当李开始谈她的工作时，蒂姆就走神了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈtune sth to sth</b></td><td class="c3">把收音机或；电视机调到(某个频道)上<br><span class="en">to adjust the controls of a radio or television so that you can listen to or watch a particular programme</span></td><td class="c4">All the TVs in the store were <b>tuned to</b> the same channel.<br>店里所有的电视机都调在同一频道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtune ˈup<br>ˌtune sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">为乐器调音；定弦<br><span class="en">when musicians tune up or tune up their instruments, they adjust them so that they can play together</span></td><td class="c4">We could hear the orchestra <b>tuning up</b>.<br>我们听到管弦乐队在试音。<br>The quartet <b>tuned up</b> and began to play.<br>四重奏乐队调音之后就开始了演奏。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>turf</b></td><td class="c2"><b>sth (also,turf sb off, ˌturf sb ˈoff sth) <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…赶出；把…驱逐；出地点；组织等<br><span class="en">to force sb/sth to leave a particular place or an organization</span></td><td class="c4">We need to <b>turf</b> the governing party out.<br>我们应该把执政觉撵下台。<br>Several families have been <b>turfed</b> out of their homes.<br>有几户人家被逐出了家园。<br>The boys should have been <b>turfed</b> <b>off</b> the bus.<br>这些男孩早就应该被赶下公共汽车的。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturf sth ˈout <span class="tag">(BrE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">丢弃；扔掉(不需要的东西)<br><span class="en">to get rid of sth you do not want</span></td><td class="c4">The shop is full of beautiful clothes that people have <b>turfed out</b>.<br>这家商店里全是人们处理掉的漂亮衣服。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>turn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn aˈbout <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">急向后转；飞快转身；回头<br><span class="en">to turn around quickly so as to face in the opposite direction</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>turned about</b> and went into the kitchen.<br>她一转身进了厨房。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn aˈgainst sb/sth<br>ˌturn sb</b></td><td class="c3">使与…反目成仇；不再支持</td><td class="c4">Her old friends were <b>turning against</b> her.<br>她的老朋友都跟她翻脸了。<br>He's trying to <b>turn his family against</b> me.<br>他试图让他的家人与我作对。<br>What has made them <b>turn against</b> government?<br>是什么使他们转而反对政府了呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn aˈround (BrE also,turn ˈround)</b></td><td class="c3">突然变卦<br><span class="en">if sb turns around and does sth, they do sth unexpectedly and often unfairly</span></td><td class="c4">What willl we do if he <b>turns around</b> and says it was all our fault?<br>要是他突然反咬一口说全是我们的错，我们该怎么办呢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn sth aˈround (BrE also ˌturn sth ˈround)</b></td><td class="c3">故意误解；曲解；歪曲(某人的话)<br><span class="en">to deliberately understand sth that sb says in the wrong way, especially for your own advantage</span></td><td class="c4">You <b>turn everything I say around</b> to make me look stupid.<br>你成心曲解我的话，让我看上去像个傻瓜。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">避开；让开</td><td class="c4">He <b>turned aside</b> in embarrassment.<br>他尴尬地转过脸去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb/sth aˈside</b></td><td class="c3">使躲开；使闪开<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth move to one side, especially in order to avoid sth difficult or dangerous</span></td><td class="c4">As he bent to kiss her, she <b>turned her head aside</b>.<br>他弯腰想去亲吻她，她把头扭了过去。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn aˈway<br>turn sth</b></td><td class="c3">转身；转头(以避开困难或危险)；转(头)</td><td class="c4">Will <b>turned</b> away and walked out of the door.<br>威尔掉头走出门去。<br>Tina <b>turned</b> her head away and looked out of the window.<br>蒂娜扭头望着窗外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn sb aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">拒绝帮助某人<br><span class="en">to refuse to help sb</span></td><td class="c4">They had nowhere to stay so I couldn't just <b>turn them away</b>.<br>他们无处投宿，所以我不能就这么把他们打发走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn aˈway from sth<br>ˌturn sb aˈway from sth</b></td><td class="c3">使不再支持；对…失去兴趣<br><span class="en">to stop, or to make sb stop, Supporting sb/sth or being interested in sth</span></td><td class="c4">Younger voters are <b>turning away from</b> the party.<br>年轻选民渐渐不支持该党了。<br>The recent scandals have <b>turned many people away from</b> politics.<br>最近的丑闻使很多人不愿再过问政治。<br>We were <b>turned</b> back at the border.<br>我们在边境被挡了回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sth ˈback</b></td><td class="c3">折转；翻开<br><span class="en">to fold sth back on itself</span></td><td class="c4">She straightened the bedclothes and <b>turned back</b> the top sheet.<br>她整理了盖被，然后把床罩掀开。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈdown <span class="tag">(rare)</span></b></td><td class="c3">悲伤或恼怒撇嘴；闭紧嘴<br><span class="en">if your mouth turns down, it forms a line with the ends curved downwards, because you are sad or annoyed</span></td><td class="c4">He asked her to marry him, but she <b>turned him down</b>.<br>他向她求婚，但她回绝了。<br>They <b>turned down</b> my offer of help.<br>我提出帮忙，但他们没有理会。<br>She <b>turned the job down</b> because it paid too little.<br>她没有接受那份工作，因为薪水太少。<br>My book was <b>turned down</b> by eight publishers.<br>我的书稿被八家出版商拒之门外。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k,turn sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">提议均未被采纳<br><span class="en">to adjust the controls on a piece of equipment in order to reduce the</span></td><td class="c4">Why did she turn <b>down</b> your invitation?<br>她为什么回绝了你的邀请。<br>He has been turned <b>down</b> for ten jobs so far.<br>到目前为止，他已经十次求职遭拒了。<br>He asked her to marry him but she turned him <b>down</b>.<br>他向她求婚，但她没有答应。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn ˈin <span class="tag">(old-fashioned informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">上床睡觉<br><span class="en">to go to bed</span></td><td class="c4">It's time for me to <b>turn in</b>.<br>我该去睡觉了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈin<br>ˌturn sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">使面朝内；向里拐；内倾<br><span class="en">to place or fold sth so that it bends or faces towards the centre; to be placed or folded in this way</span></td><td class="c4">Her feet <b>turn in</b> as she walks.<br>她走路时两脚呈内八字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈin sth</b></td><td class="c3">取得(佳绩)；表现(优异)；获得(高利润)<br><span class="en">to achieve a good result, Performance,profit, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The champion <b>turned in</b> a brilliant performance.<br>冠军表现得十分出色。<br>The company <b>turned in</b> $150 000 last month.<br>公司上月的盈利达15万元。o时。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">交还；退还<br><span class="en">to give back sth that you no longer need or should have</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Turn in</b> your Pass before you leave.<br>你离开时要交还通行证。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>turn sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">呈交；递交；上交<br><span class="en">to give sth such as a piece of written work to the person who asked you to do it</span></td><td class="c4">Have you <b>turned in</b> your assignment yet?<br>你作业交了吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈin on yourself</b></td><td class="c3">只关注自己而不与人交往；闭门谢客；离群索居<br><span class="en">to become very concerned with your own problems and stop communicating with others</span></td><td class="c4">He completely <b>turned in on</b> himself after his wife left him.<br>妻子离开后，他完全把自己封闭起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn inside ˈout<br>ˌturn sth inside ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">把(…的)内部翻到外面；翻出<br><span class="en">to make the inside of sth face out</span></td><td class="c4">It was so windy my umbrella <b>turned inside out</b>.<br>风很大，把我的伞吹翻了。<br>She pulled off her jumper, <b>turning the sleeves inside out</b>.<br>她脱下套衫，把袖子翻了过来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb/sth inside ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使(某人的生活)发生巨变<br><span class="en">to make great changes in sb's life</span></td><td class="c4">The shock <b>turned her world inside out</b>.<br>这次打击改变了她的一切。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>f,turn ˈinto sth<br>ˌturn sb/sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">把…变成；(使)成为<br><span class="en">to change, or to make sth change, into sth dif. ferent</span></td><td class="c4">We need to stop this problem from <b>turning into</b> a crisis.<br>我们应该防止这个问题演化成一场危机。<br>The house had been <b>turned into</b> three apartments.<br>房子被改建成了三套公寓。<br>As the fruit ripens, the starch <b>turns into</b> sugar.<br>水果成熟时，淀粉就变成了糖。9。<br>In one year she <b>turned</b> from a problem child <b>into</b> a model student.<br>一年之间，她从一个问题儿童转变成为模范学生。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈoff<br>ˌturn ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">拐弯(离开…)；转入另一条路<br><span class="en">to leave one road in order to travel on another</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>turned off</b> onto a side street.<br>她拐进一条小巷。<br>The car <b>turned off</b> the main road.<br>那辆车驶离了主干道。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn on sb</b></td><td class="c3">突然攻击<br><span class="en">to attack sb suddenly and unexpectedly</span></td><td class="c4">The dog <b>turned on</b> him and bit his finger.<br>那条狗突然扑过去咬伤了他的手指。<br>She suddenly <b>turned on</b> me and started shouting.<br>她突然冲着我喊叫起来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn on sth (also ˈturn upon sth more formal)</b></td><td class="c3">依靠；视乎；取决于<br><span class="en">to depend on sth in order to have a successful result</span></td><td class="c4">Her future career <b>turns on</b> this interview.<br>她的事业前途就押在这次面试上了。<br>The case <b>turns on</b> whether the police can prove that the driver knew he had hit something.<br>这件案子取决于警方能否证明司机知道他撞到了东西。<br>Much <b>turns on</b> the outcome of the peace talks.<br>事情主要取决于和谈的结果。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈon <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使兴奋；使感兴趣<br><span class="en">to make sb enthusiastic about sth</span></td><td class="c4">What really <b>turns him on</b> is motorbikes.<br>他真正感兴趣的是摩托车。<br>If live theatre <b>turns you on</b>, there is plenty to choose from.<br>如果你喜爱舞台剧，选择余地很大。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈon <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使产生性冲动<br><span class="en">to make sb feel sexually excited</span></td><td class="c4">That's not the kind of thing that <b>turns me on</b>.<br>那种事不能激起我的情欲。<br>I get <b>turned on</b> by men in uniform.<br>我一见到穿制服的男人就欲火攻心。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i, turn sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">打开；接通电流；煤气；水等</td><td class="c4">Did you <b>turn</b> the central heating on?<br>你把中央暖气打开了吗。<br><b>Turn</b> the tap on slowly.<br>慢慢打开水龙头。<br>I checked the fuses and <b>turned</b> the electricity back on.<br>我检查保险丝后，重新接通了电源。<br>Leo <b>turns</b> the television on as soon as he comes home from school.<br>利奥放学一回到家就打开电视。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn sth on sb/sth also ˈturn sth upon sb/ sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">把枪口；相机；灯光等瞄准(或指向)<br><span class="en">to point sth such as gun, a camera, a light, etc. at sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">Officers <b>turned</b> hoses on the demonstrators.<br>警察用水龙带对准不威者。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈon to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">使对…产生兴趣；使初尝<br><span class="en">to make sb interested in sb/sth or use sth for the first time</span></td><td class="c4">I'm not going to <b>turn</b> out to meet you in this weather.<br>这种天气我可不打算去见你。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈon to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与副词或形容词连用；用于以<br><span class="en">used with an adverb, an adjective or in questions with how</span></td><td class="c4">The article she wrote had <b>turned</b> out well.<br>她的文章反响不错。<br>The day <b>turned</b> out fine again.<br>天气又转好了。<br>You never know how things will <b>turn</b> out.<br>你永远不知道情况会变成什么样。<br>I couldn't have gone anyway, as it <b>turned</b> out.<br>结果证明，我无论如何就是走不掉。<br>The children have <b>turned</b> out well.<br>这些孩子结果都还不错。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈon to sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">原来；证明是；结果是<br><span class="en">to be discovered to be; to prove to be</span></td><td class="c4">It <b>turned</b> out that she was a friend of my sister.<br>她原来是我姐姐的朋友。<br>My decision <b>turned</b> out to have been a mistake.<br>结果发现我的决定是个错误。<br>Ruth's illness <b>turned</b> out not to be serious after all.<br>最后查出鲁思的病并不严重。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈout<br>ˌturn sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使向外；外倾<br><span class="en">to point, or to make sth point, towards the outside</span></td><td class="c4">His feet <b>turn out</b> as he walks.<br>他是外八字脚。<br>She <b>turns her toes out</b> when she walks.<br>她走路时脚趾向外撇。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb ˈout (from sth)<br>turn sb ˈout of sth</b></td><td class="c3">从…赶走；撵走；逐出<br><span class="en">to force sb to leave or go out of a place</span></td><td class="c4">The landlord <b>turned</b> them <b>out</b> of their house just before the New Year.<br>就在新年之前，房东把他们赶出了房门。<br>You can't <b>turn</b> us <b>out</b> in this storm!<br>暴风雨这么大，你不能赶我们走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sth/sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">制造；培育<br><span class="en">to produce sth/sb</span></td><td class="c4">The factory <b>turns out</b> 900 cars a week.<br>这家工厂每周生产 900 辆汽车。<br>This school has <b>turned out</b> several well-known engineers.<br>这所学校培养了几位赫赫有名的工程师。<br>I'm going to <b>turn out</b> my bedroom during the holidays.<br>假期时我打算把卧室彻底打扫一下。<br><b>Turn out</b> your pockets.<br>把你衣兜里的东西全掏出来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈover ˌturn sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">发动机<br><span class="en">of an engine</span></td><td class="c4">This is boring. Let's <b>turn</b> it <b>over</b>.<br>这个没意思。我们换换频道吧。<br><b>Turn</b> to page 23.<br>翻到第23页。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈover ˌturn sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">售出并补进(货物)；周转</td><td class="c4">Large supermarkets <b>turn</b> <b>over</b> their stock very rapidly.<br>大超市的库存周转很快。<br>This brand <b>turns</b> <b>over</b> twice as fast as the others.<br>这个牌子的周转速度是其他牌子的两倍。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sb/sth ˈover (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">移交；送交当局；尤指；警方<br><span class="en">to deliver sb/ sth to the control and care of sb in authority, especially the police</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>turned over</b> to the Belgian police at the border.<br>他在边境被移交给了比利时警方。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sth ˈover</b></td><td class="c3">仔细思考；深思熟思<br><span class="en">to think about sth carefully</span></td><td class="c4">Diana <b>turned over</b> what James had said in her mind.<br>黛安娜脑子里仔细琢磨了詹姆斯的话。<br>He lay in the dark, <b>turning over</b> the day's extraordinary events.<br>他躺在黑暗中，反复思索着那天不寻常的事。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈover to sth<br>ˌturn sth ˈover to sth</b></td><td class="c3">改变土地；工厂等的用途<br><span class="en">if an area, a factory, etc. turns over or sb turns it over to sth, it starts to be used for sth different</span></td><td class="c4">The whole area has <b>turned over to</b> rice production.<br>整个地区已改种大米。<br>The factory was <b>turned over to</b> the production of aircraft parts.<br>这象工厂转产飞机零部件。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn to sb</b></td><td class="c3">把脸转向；转身朝向(某人)<br><span class="en">to move your head or body so as to face sb</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>turned to</b> me and smiled.<br>他转过身对我笑了。<br>You're the only person I can <b>turn to</b> for advice.<br>你是我唯一能求教的人。<br>I always <b>turn to</b> my dictionary when I come across a word I don't know.<br>遇到生词，我总是查词典。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn to sth</b></td><td class="c3">诉诸(违法行为或有害处的事)；落到做…的田地<br><span class="en">to start to become involved in sth or start to do sth, especially sth illegal or harmful, often because you are in a difficult situation</span></td><td class="c4">He was forced to <b>turn to crime to</b> pay off his debts.<br>为了还债，他迫不得已走向了犯罪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈturn to sth<br>ˈturn sth to sth</b></td><td class="c3">将注意力；思路等转至(新课题)<br><span class="en">to turn your attention, your thoughts, etc. to a new subject</span></td><td class="c4">Our conversation soon <b>turned to</b> the kind of music that we liked.<br>我们的谈话很快就转到我们喜欢的音乐类型上。<br>Let's <b>turn our attention to</b> next week's conference.<br>大家关注一下下周的会议吧。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>turn ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">机会<br><span class="en">of an opportunity</span></td><td class="c4">I haven't got a job at the moment, but I'm sure that something will <b>turn up</b>.<br>我眼下还没工作，但我确信会有机会找到的。<br>References to Irina <b>turn up</b> in many of his poems.<br>他在很多诗作中提到艾里娜。<br>That was a wonderful meal! You've <b>turned up</b> trumps again.<br>这顿饭棒极了！你又露了一手。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn ˈup<br>ˌturn sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使指向上方<br><span class="en">to point, or to make sth point, upwards</span></td><td class="c4">Her nose <b>turns up</b> at the end.<br>她是个翘鼻子。<br>She <b>turned her face up</b> towards him.<br>她冲着他仰起脸。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sth upside ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">把翻得乱七八糟；把…翻个底朝天<br><span class="en">to make a place very untidy while you are searching for sth</span></td><td class="c4">The burglars <b>turned the flat upside down</b>.<br>窃贼把这套公寓翻得一片狼藉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌturn sth upside ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">打乱；扰乱某人的；生活<br><span class="en">to make large changes and confusion in sb's life</span></td><td class="c4">The divorce <b>turned his whole world upside down</b>.<br>离婚把他的一切都搞得颠三倒四。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>twist</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtwist sth ˈoff<br>ˌtwist sth ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">上拧开；扭脱；拗断<br><span class="en">to remove sth or break sth off by turning and pulling it with your hand</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>twisted off</b> the lid and looked inside.<br>他扭开盖子往里面看。<br>She <b>twisted the cap off</b> the bottle and took a mouthful of water.<br>她柠开瓶盖，喝了一口水。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>type</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtype sth ˈin<br>ˌtype sth ˈinto sth</b></td><td class="c3">将(数据)输入(计算机等)<br><span class="en">to put data into a document using a computer, etc.</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Type in</b> the file name then press return.<br>输入文件名，然后按回车键。<br><b>Type the relevant details into</b> the boxes provided.<br>把相关细节键入预设的方框内。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌtype sth ˈout/ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">用计算机等打出；敲出(文字)<br><span class="en">to produce a copy of sth on a computer, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Pm <b>typing up</b> the report this morning.<br>我今天上午就把报告打出来。<br>It took me ages to <b>type my notes out</b>.<br>我花了很长时间打笔记。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>urge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌurge sb/sth ˈon (to sth/to do sth)</b></td><td class="c3">鼓励；激励(做某事)；为…加油<br><span class="en">to encourage sb; to support sb so that they can do sth better</span></td><td class="c4">The supporters were <b>urging the team on</b>.<br>支持者在为这个队助威。<br><b>Urged on</b> by the Prime Minister, the police tried to end the strike.<br>在首相的敦促下，警方力图终止罢工。<br>The driver <b>urged the horses on</b>.<br>车夫策马前行。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>usher</b></td><td class="c2"><b>usher sth ˈin <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">开创；开始；开启<br><span class="en">to mark or be the start of sth new</span></td><td class="c4">The elections <b>ushered in</b> a new period of change in the country.<br>这些选举使该国进入了一个新的变革期。<br>Firework displays <b>ushered in</b> the New Year.<br>炸火表演标志着新年的开始。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>veg</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌveg ˈout <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">消闲；休闲<br><span class="en">to relax and do very little</span></td><td class="c4">All she does is <b>veg out</b> in front of the telly.<br>她成天泡在电视机前混日子。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>venture</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈventure into/on sth also ˈventure upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">敢于做；冒险做<br><span class="en">to dare to do sth that could involve risk</span></td><td class="c4">As soon as he arrived, he <b>ventured</b> on a trip up the Amazon.<br>他一到这里，就沿亚马孙河溯流而上冒险旅行去 I。<br>This is the first time the company has <b>ventured</b> <b>into</b> movie production.<br>这是该公司首次涉足电影制作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>verge</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈverge on sth also ˈverge upon sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">极接近；濒于<br><span class="en">to be very close or similar to an extreme state or condition</span></td><td class="c4">Iwas treated with suspicion that <b>verged</b> on hostillity.<br>我受到了几近敌意的猜疑。<br>Her hair was dark brown, <b>verging</b> on black.<br>她的头发是深棕色，近乎黑色。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>vest</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈvest in sb/sth. (law)</b></td><td class="c3">权利；财产等<br><span class="en">of power, Property, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">In the case of bankruptcy the property shall <b>vest</b> in the trustee.<br>如果破产，财产归受托人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈvest sth in sb/sth<br>ˈvest sb with sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">授子；赋予；给予(正式或合法权力)<br><span class="en">to officially or legally give sb the power or authority to do sth</span></td><td class="c4">It is unwise to <b>vest absolute power in</b> a single institution.<br>将绝对权力赋予单一机构是不明智的。<br>The court is <b>vested with</b> certain rights.<br>法庭拥有某些权力。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>visit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈvisit with sb <span class="tag">(AmE, informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">与…聊天；闲谈<br><span class="en">to spend time with sb talking in an informal and casual way</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>visited with</b> my neighbour yesterday.<br>昨天我和邻居闲聊了一会儿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>vomit</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌvomit sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">呕吐；吐出<br><span class="en">to bring food you have eaten back out of your mouth</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>vomited up</b> his breakfast.<br>他把早饭吐了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>vote</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌvote sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">投票否决；投票；击败<br><span class="en">to reject or defeat a candidate or a proposal by voting</span></td><td class="c4">The Senate has <b>voted down</b> efforts to raise taxes.<br>参议院投票否决了试图增税的议案。矿。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌvote sb ˈin<br>ˌvote sb ˈinto/ˈonto sth</b></td><td class="c3">投票选出某人(任职)<br><span class="en">to choose sb for a particular position by voting</span></td><td class="c4">I was <b>voted in</b> as treasurer.<br>我当选为财务主管。<br>When was this government <b>voted into</b> office?<br>这届政府是什么时候获选上台的。<br>Who <b>voted her onto</b> the Board of Governors?<br>谁投票把她选进理事会的？语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈvote on sth</b></td><td class="c3">就…投票表决<br><span class="en">to make a decision about sth by voting</span></td><td class="c4">The committee is <b>voting on</b> the proposal tonight.<br>今晚委员会将投票表决该议案。<br>Workers have begun <b>voting on</b> whether to hold a series of one-day strikes.<br>工人已经开始投票，决定是否举行一连串的持续一天的罢工。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌvote sb ˈout ˌvote sb ˈout of/ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">投票免去某人职务；投票使某人落选<br><span class="en">to decide as a group to remove sb from a particular position by voting</span></td><td class="c4">The government may be <b>voted</b> <b>out</b> of <b>office</b> at the next election.<br>这届政府在下次大选时可能被选下台。<br>What will he do if he gets <b>voted</b> <b>out</b>?<br>如果落选他会做什么呢。<br>Parsons was <b>voted</b> <b>off</b> the Board.<br>经投票帕森斯被免去了委员一职。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌvote sth ˈthrough</b></td><td class="c3">投票；同意；表决通过(提议等)<br><span class="en">to approve sth or bring a proposal, etc. into force by voting for it</span></td><td class="c4">Congress <b>voted the bill through</b> without a debate.<br>国会未经辩论就投票通过了该法案。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>vouch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈvouch for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">替…担保；保证<br><span class="en">to say that you know sb, that you believe they have a good character and that you are prepared to be responsible for their actions</span></td><td class="c4">They asked whether I was prepared to <b>vouch for</b> him.<br>他们问我是否愿意为他作担保。<br>You should give the names of two people who can <b>vouch for</b> your honesty and reliability.<br>你应该提供两个能担保你诚实可信的人的名字。<br>I can <b>vouch for</b> the fact that he is a good worker.<br>我保证他是名好员工。<br>I can't <b>vouch for</b> this hotel (= 1 have no personal experience of it) but it looked wonderful from the brochure.<br>我没住过这家旅馆，可从宣传册上看它很棒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wad</b></td><td class="c2"><b>wad sth ˈup <span class="tag">(especially AmE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">把…卷为；一卷；将…压成；一叠<br><span class="en">to fold or press sth into a tight mass</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>wadded up</b> the first draft and threw it away.<br>她把初稿揉成一团扔了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wade</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwade ˈinto sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">猛烈攻击；抨击<br><span class="en">to attack sb physically or with words</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>waded straight into</b> her critics.<br>她直截了当地驳斥了批评她的人。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwade ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">费时费力地阅读；艰难地处理<br><span class="en">to spend a lot of time and effort reading sth or dealing with sth</span></td><td class="c4">I had to <b>wade through</b> pages and pages of statistics.<br>我不得不硬着头皮啃一页页的统计数字。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>waffle</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwaffle ˈon (about sth) <span class="tag">(informal, especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">喋喋不休；胡扯；絮叨<br><span class="en">to talk or write a lot about sth without giving any useful information</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>waffled on</b> for ages about his garden.<br>他东拉西扯没完没了地唠叨他的花园。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wait</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwait aˈround (BrE also ˌwait aˈbout) (for sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">在某处等待；等候<br><span class="en">to stay in a place without doing anything, waiting for sth to happen or for sb to arrive</span></td><td class="c4">I wouldn't bother <b>waiting around</b> for him.<br>我不介意留下来等他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>wait beˈhind <span class="tag">(especially BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">太久期盼；梦寐以求<br><span class="en">to hope or watch for sth to happen, especially for a long time</span></td><td class="c4">Leeds United had <b>waited</b> for success for eighteen years.<br>利茲联队盼望胜利已经十八年了。°。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwait ˈin (for sb/sth) <span class="tag">(BrE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">在家等候(人或电话)<br><span class="en">to stay at home because you are expecting sb to arrive or telephone</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>waited in all day in</b> case he called.<br>她一整天都守在家里，因为他可能打电话来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwait on sb/sth <span class="tag">(informal, especially AmE, ScotE)</span></b></td><td class="c3">等待；等到<br><span class="en">to wait until sb arrives or until sth is available</span></td><td class="c4">Judd was late and she was sick of <b>waiting on</b> him.<br>贾德迟到了，她讨厌一直等着他。<br>She was <b>waiting on</b> my decision.<br>她等着我拿主意。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwait sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">等待(困难或令人不快的事)结束；挨过(难关)<br><span class="en">to stay in a place until sth difficult or unpleasant has passed or finished</span></td><td class="c4">We sheltered in a doorway to <b>wait out</b> the storm.<br>我们躲在门口等候暴风雨过去。<br>It was difficult to <b>wait out</b> the hours until I could phone her to hear the news.<br>我能给她打电话听取消息之前的那几个小时真难熬。<br>Their strategy has always been to <b>wait the recession out</b>.<br>他们的策略一直是等着经济衰退结束。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwait ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">等着不睡；熬夜等待<br><span class="en">(for sb) to not go to bed until sb comes home or arrives</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>wait up</b> (for me), I may be late.<br>不要熬夜等我，我可能要晚回来。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wake</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwake ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">苏醒；恢复知觉<br><span class="en">to become conscious again</span></td><td class="c4">When she <b>woke up</b> after the operation, her sister was sitting beside her bed.<br>她手术后醒来时，妹妹正坐在她床边。吗。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwake ˈup to sth</b></td><td class="c3">意识到；认识到<br><span class="en">to become aware of sth; to realize sth</span></td><td class="c4">People are finally <b>waking up to</b> the fact that the natural world must be conserved.<br>人们终于意识到一定要保护自然界。<br>The hospitals have <b>woken up to</b> the value of experienced nurses.<br>医院已经意识到资深护士的价值。<br>He hasn't yet <b>woken up to</b> the seriousness of the situation.<br>他还没有认识到形势有多严峻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>walk</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk aˈway (from sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">在事故等中免受重伤；平安脱身<br><span class="en">if you walk away from an accident, etc., you are not seriously</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>walked away</b> unhurt.<br>他毫发未损地平安脱险了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk aˈway/ˈoff with sth</b></td><td class="c3">轻易取胜；轻松赢得<br><span class="en">to win sth very easily</span></td><td class="c4">The team <b>walked away with</b> the championship.<br>该队轻而易举地获得了冠军。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk aˈway/ˈoff with sth</b></td><td class="c3">顺手牵羊；顺便偷走<br><span class="en">to steal sth; to take sth without the owner's permission</span></td><td class="c4">The thief <b>walked away with</b> jewellery worth £24 000.<br>窃贼偷走了价值 24000 英镑的珠宝。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈinto sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">走路时撞到<br><span class="en">to crash into sb/sth while you are walking</span></td><td class="c4">Look where you're going! You <b>walked straight into</b> me.<br>看着点路！你把我撞了个正着。<br>He keeps bumping into things and <b>walking into</b> walls.<br>他不断地碰到东西撞到墻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">意外落入；不小心陷入(令人不快的境地)<br><span class="en">to become caught in sth that you are not expecting, especially because you are not careful</span></td><td class="c4">He realized he'd <b>walked into</b> a trap.<br>他意识到自己稀里糊涂落入了陷阱。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈinto sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易获得(工作)<br><span class="en">to succeed in getting a job without having to make an effort</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>walked straight into</b> a job in publishing.<br>她不费吹灰之力谋得了一份出版行业的工作。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈoff<br>ˌwalk ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">愤然离去；拂袖而去<br><span class="en">to leave a place or a person suddenly because you are angry or upset</span></td><td class="c4">She turned and <b>walked off</b> without a word.<br>她二话没说，转身离去。<br>The rest of the team <b>walked off</b> the field in protest.<br>其他队员愤然退场表示抗议。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">散步消食(或消气等)<br><span class="en">to go for a walk in order to get rid of the feeling that you have eaten too much or an emotion such as anger</span></td><td class="c4">I need to <b>walk off</b> that lunch.<br>我要散散步把午饭消化一下。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>walk ˈoff with sth <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">遗弃；抛弃；舍弃；离开<br><span class="en">(on sb/sth) informal to leave sb you have a close relationship with and a responsibility for</span></td><td class="c4">He <b>walked</b> out on his wife/marriage after 35 years.<br>结婚35年之后，他抛弃了妻子放弃了婚姻。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwalkout n</b></td><td class="c3">突然罢工</td><td class="c4">The staff staged a one-day <b>walkout</b>.<br>职员突然罢工一天。2 a。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈover sb <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易打败；举击败<br><span class="en">to defeat sb easily in a competition</span></td><td class="c4">Don't let yourselves be <b>walked over</b>.<br>不要一下子被打败。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwalkover n <span class="tag">(informal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">轻易取胜；不战而胜<br><span class="en">an easy victory in a game or competition; a situation in which you are considered to have won a game although you did not in fact play</span></td><td class="c4">The race was no <b>walkover</b> (= it was not easy to win).<br>这场比赛的胜利得来不易。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk sb ˈthrough sth</b></td><td class="c3">给…详细解释；为…分步演示(操作方法等)<br><span class="en">to show or tell sb how to do sth by carefully explaining or showing each part separately</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>walked me through</b> the complicated document.<br>她给我详细讲解了那份复杂的文件。<br>Hell <b>walk you through</b> the procedure.<br>他将给你分步演示整个程序。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwalk ˈup (to sb/sth)</b></td><td class="c3">自信地走向；走近<br><span class="en">to approach sb/sth in a confident way</span></td><td class="c4">She <b>walked straight up</b> to the desk and asked to see the manager.<br>她信步直接走到前台，要求面见。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wall</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwall sth ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">用墙或屏障围住；圈起；环绕<br><span class="en">to put a wall or a barrier around sth</span></td><td class="c4">Apartment blocks <b>walled in</b> the playground completely.<br>公寓楼群把操场围得严严实实。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwall sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">用墙或屏障把…隔开；分隔<br><span class="en">to build a wall or a barrier around an area to separate it from another area</span></td><td class="c4">Part of the yard had been <b>walled off</b>.<br>院子的一部分已经隔起来了。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wallow</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwallow in sth <span class="tag">(often disapproving)</span></b></td><td class="c3">纵乐于<br><span class="en">to enjoy sth that gives you pleasure, especially when it is sth unpleasant and you do it in a way that makes other people think you enjoy being unhappy or want sympathy from them</span></td><td class="c4">Stop <b>wallowing in</b> selfpity.<br>不要一味地自怜了。<br>She <b>wallows in</b> nostalgia for the past.<br>她沉湎于对过往的怀恋。四日。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wander</b></td><td class="c2"><b>wander ˈoff/aˈway<br>ˌwander ˈfrom/ˈoff sth</b></td><td class="c3">走散；走失<br><span class="en">to leave the place where you ought to be, or the person or group of people you are with without thinking about it</span></td><td class="c4">Don't <b>wander off</b> and get lost.<br>别乱走迷了路。<br>The child had <b>wandered away</b> from her mother.<br>那孩子和她妈妈走散了。<br>We had <b>wandered Off</b> the path.<br>我们偏离了道路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>ward</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌward sb/sth ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">防止；挡住；避开危险或不快之<br><span class="en">to prevent sb/sth dangerous or unpleasant from affecting or harming you</span></td><td class="c4">She put up a hand to <b>ward off</b> the blows.<br>她抬起手阻挡打击。<br>He keeps dogs to <b>ward off</b> unwanted visitors.<br>他养了狗，防止有不速之客上门。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>warm</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwarm to sth</b></td><td class="c3">对…更感兴趣；更热衷于<br><span class="en">to become more interested in or enthusiastic about sth</span></td><td class="c4">The speaker was <b>warming to</b> his theme now.<br>演讲者就他的主题越讲越起劲。<br>When spring comes, the earth begins to <b>warm</b> up.<br>春天来临时，大地开始回暖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwarm to sth</b></td><td class="c3">锻炼；表演等之前做准备活动；做适应性练习；热身<br><span class="en">to do gentle exercise or practice to prepare for exercise, a performance, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">I'm always careful to <b>warm</b> up before 1 go jogging.<br>我慢跑之前总是注意热身。<br>Peter was <b>warming</b> up with a few scales.<br>彼得正在做音阶练习。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>warm ''up<br>ˌwarm sb/sth ˈup ito become, or</b></td><td class="c3">使(某人或身体部位)暖和；变暖<br><span class="en">to make sb or a part of sb's body, feel warmer</span></td><td class="c4">Come and <b>warm up</b> by the fire.<br>过来烤火取取暖吧。<br>They stamped their feet to <b>warm them up</b>.<br>他们跺脚取暖。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>warm ''up<br>ˌwarm sb/sth ˈup ito become, or</b></td><td class="c3">使活跃起来；热烈起来<br><span class="en">to become, Or to make sb/sth, more lively or enthusiastic</span></td><td class="c4">His role is to <b>warm up</b> the audience before the main event.<br>他的任务是在正式演出之前调动观众情绪活跃气氛。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>i<br>warm sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">使暖和；使变暖<br><span class="en">to make sth become warmer</span></td><td class="c4">The fire had begun to <b>warm the room up</b>.<br>炉火让屋子开始暖和了起来。2。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>warn</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwarn sb/sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">警告人；飞机；等不要靠近<br><span class="en">to tell a person, a ship, an aircraft, etc. not to come near a place because it is dangerous</span></td><td class="c4">The male birds sing to <b>warn other males away</b>.<br>雄鸟鸣叫着警告其他雄鸟走开。<br>An electric fence <b>warned away</b> anyone who came too close.<br>电子围栏提醒人们不得靠近。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwarn sb ˈoff doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">常指威胁着让某人离开；叫某人不得靠近<br><span class="en">to tell sb to leave or not to come near a place, often in a threatening way</span></td><td class="c4">The farmer <b>warned</b> us of his land when we tried to camp there.<br>我们想在那里露营，可是农场主警告我们不得靠近他的土地。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwarn sb ˈoff doing sth</b></td><td class="c3">劝告某人不要；建议某人停止(做某事)<br><span class="en">to advise sb not to do sth or to stop doing sth</span></td><td class="c4">He was <b>warned</b> <b>off</b> smoking after his first heart attack.<br>他心脏病初次发作后，别人就劝他戒烟。<br>She <b>warned</b> him <b>off</b> a career in acting.<br>她建议他放弃在演艺圈发展。<br>We were <b>warned</b> <b>off</b> renting the apartment.<br>有人劝我们不要租这套公寓。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wash</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">用水冲洗；洗刷<br><span class="en">(with sth) to clean sth by using a large quantity of water</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>washed the car down</b> with a hose.<br>我用水龙带冲洗了汽车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">就着(食物)喝(饮料)<br><span class="en">(with sth) to drink sth after, or at the same time as, eating food</span></td><td class="c4">We <b>washed our lunch down</b> with iced tea.<br>我们喝着冰茶吃了午饭。<br>He had a huge plate of pasta <b>washed down</b> with several bottles of beer.<br>他吃了一大盘通心粉，喝了几瓶啤酒。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">洪水等<br><span class="en">of a river, a flood, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Tons of earth had been <b>washed down</b> by the storm.<br>暴风雨冲走了大量泥土。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sb ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">使筋疲力尽；使十分疲乏<br><span class="en">to make sb very tired</span></td><td class="c4">That long walk has <b>washed me out</b>.<br>走那么长的路把我累得疲惫不堪。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth out</b></td><td class="c3">洗净；清洗(容器内部)<br><span class="en">(with sth) to wash the inside of a container in order to remove dirt, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">He carefully <b>washed the bottles out</b> with disinfectant.<br>他用消毒剂把瓶子里面仔细清洗干净。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth out</b></td><td class="c3">体育比赛；活动等提前结束；阻止…的举行<br><span class="en">if rain washes out a sports game, an event, etc., it makes it end early or prevents it from</span></td><td class="c4">The game was <b>washed out</b>.<br>这场比赛因下雨无法举行了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth out</b></td><td class="c3">洪水或暴雨冲毁；毁坏(道路)<br><span class="en">(of a flood or heavy rains) to destroy a road</span></td><td class="c4">The storm surge <b>washed out</b> a huge chunk of the highway.<br>风暴潮冲垮了一大段公。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwash sth out</b></td><td class="c3">结束；终止<br><span class="en">to end sth</span></td><td class="c4">Baltimore <b>washed out</b> the Indians' six-game win streak with an 8-3 win.<br>巴尔的摩队以8:3 终结了印第安人队的六连胜。ˈ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>wash ˈup<br>ˌwash sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">餐后洗刷餐具<br><span class="en">to wash dirty plates, glasses, etc. after a meal</span></td><td class="c4">It's your turn to <b>wash up</b>.<br>轮到你洗碗了。<br>Don't forget to <b>wash up</b> the glasses as well.<br>别忘了捎带洗洗玻璃杯。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>wash ˈup<br>ˌwash sth ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">被冲上岸；把…冲上岸<br><span class="en">to be carried along in the water and then left on land; to carry sth along and leave it in this way</span></td><td class="c4">A number of dead dolphins have <b>washed up</b> on the shore.<br>一些死海豚被冲到了岸上。<br>His body was <b>washed up</b> on the beach two days later.<br>两天后，他的尸体被冲上了海滩。ˌ。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>waste</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwaste aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">身体部位等<br><span class="en">of a person, part of the body, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The muscles in her arm had <b>wasted away</b>.<br>她的手臂越来越瘦。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>watch</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈwatch for sb/sth</b></td><td class="c3">观察等待；守候(某事发生或某人出现)<br><span class="en">to look and wait for sth to happen or for sb to come</span></td><td class="c4">My parents were <b>watching for</b> me coming off the plane.<br>父母翘首等候着我下飞机。<br><b>Watch for</b> the sign.<br>注意观察信号。2 +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwatch ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">用于表示警告小心；留神；注意<br><span class="en">used to warn sb about sth dangerous</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Watch out</b>, there's a car coming!<br>当心，有车。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwatch ˈover sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">照管；守卫；保护<br><span class="en">to take care of sb/sth, by being near them; to protect or guard sb/sth</span></td><td class="c4">The child needed to be <b>watched over</b> 24 hours a day.<br>那个孩子需要每天 24 小时看护。<br>He believed his mother was still <b>watching over</b> him, even though she had died when he was very young.<br>尽管母亲在他很小的时候就去世了，他相信她依然在守护着他。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>water</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwater sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">加水冲淡；掺水稀释(液体)<br><span class="en">to make a liquid weaker by adding water</span></td><td class="c4">The beer had been <b>watered down</b>.<br>啤酒掺水了。<br>The government has <b>watered down</b> its policy to make it more acceptable.<br>政府已经缓和了政策，使之更易被接受。<br>It's a <b>watered</b>-<b>down</b> version of the original proposal.<br>这份提案比最初的语气缓和了些。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wave</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwave sth aˈside/aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">对…不屑一顾；对…不予理会<br><span class="en">to not accept sth because you think it is not important or necessary</span></td><td class="c4">Their protests were <b>waved aside</b>.<br>他们的抗议未被理睬。<br>He <b>waved away</b> my question without trying to answer it.<br>他对我的问题根本不屑回答。c。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwave sb ˈoff</b></td><td class="c3">挥手送别<br><span class="en">to wave goodbye to sb as they leave</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>waved the children off</b> to school and went back inside.<br>我挥手与上学的孩子们告别，然后回到屋里。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwave sb/sth ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">对…挥手示意前行<br><span class="en">to signal to sb/sth to go forwards, by waving your hand or arm</span></td><td class="c4">We stopped, but the cab driver <b>waved us on</b>.<br>我们停下了，但出租车司机招手叫我们往前走。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wean</b></td><td class="c2"><b>be ˈweaned on sth</b></td><td class="c3">自幼年；开始了解；经历<br><span class="en">to have learned about or experienced sth from an early age</span></td><td class="c4">I <b>was weaned on</b> a regular diet of Hollywood fantasy.<br>我从小就时常看好菜坞奇幻电影。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>wear</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwear aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">时间慢慢流逝<br><span class="en">if time wears away, it passes very slowly</span></td><td class="c4">The afternoon was <b>wearing away</b>.<br>那个下午的时间过得很慢。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>k<br>wear aˈway<br>wear sth aˈway</b></td><td class="c3">因长期使用而变薄；变光滑；磨薄；磨光滑<br><span class="en">to become, or to make sth become thinner, smoother, etc by using or rubbing it over a long period of time</span></td><td class="c4">The picture on the coin had <b>worn away</b>.<br>硬币上的图案已经磨没了。<br>The steps had been <b>worn away</b> by the feet of thousands of visitors.<br>成千上万的游客把台阶踏得很光滑。n +。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwear ˈdown<br>ˌwear sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">因重复使用而变小；变薄；磨短；磨薄<br><span class="en">to become or to make sth become, gradually smaller, thinner, etc. by continuously using or rubbing</span></td><td class="c4">The tyres had <b>worn right down</b>.<br>轮胎完全磨损了。<br>The path has been <b>worn down</b> in places to bare rock.<br>这条小路有些地方已经磨得露出了的石头。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwear sb/sth ˈdown</b></td><td class="c3">使意志薄弱<br><span class="en">to make sb/sth weaker or less determined, especially by continuously attacking or putting pressure on them/it over a period of time</span></td><td class="c4">Constantly being criticized was <b>wearing her down</b>.<br>她因为不断受到指责而意志消沉。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌwear ˈon</b></td><td class="c3">时间慢慢流逝<br><span class="en">when time wears on, it passes in a way that seems slow</span></td><td class="c4">As the evening <b>wore on</b>, she became more and more nervous.<br>随着夜色渐深，她越来越紧张。<br>I <b>wore</b> out to pairs of boots on the walking trip.<br>我这次徒步旅行穿坏了两双靴子。<br>The kids have <b>worn</b> me out today.<br>孩子们今天把我累坏了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>weigh</b></td><td class="c2"><b>weigh aˈgainst sb/sth <span class="tag">(formal)</span></b></td><td class="c3">妨碍；阻碍(某人做成某事)；对…不利<br><span class="en">to make sb less likely to achieve sth or to be successful</span></td><td class="c4">The fact that he's had five jobs in two years will <b>weigh against</b> his application.<br>他两年里做过五份工作，这将不利于他的申请。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh sth aˈgainst sth</b></td><td class="c3">将…和…进行对比；权衡<br><span class="en">to consider the importance or the advantages of sth compared to sth else</span></td><td class="c4">Potential benefits need to be <b>weighed against</b> the obvious risks.<br>需要权衡潜在的利益和明显的风险。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh sb ˈdown (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">使焦虑；使沮丧<br><span class="en">to make sb feel anxious or depressed</span></td><td class="c4">The responsibilities of the job are <b>weighing her down</b>.<br>工作上的责任压得她喘不过气来。<br>He was <b>weighed down</b> with grief.<br>他悲痛欲绝。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh sb/sth ˈdown (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">把…压得动弹不得；重压<br><span class="en">to. put a heavy weight on sb/sth so that it is difficult for them to move easily</span></td><td class="c4">We were <b>weighed down</b> with bags of shopping.<br>一袋袋买来的东西把我们压得走不动路。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">尤指比赛前测体重<br><span class="en">(at sth) to have your weight measured, especially before a race, a competition, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">Both boxers <b>weighed in</b> at several pounds below their limit.<br>两名拳击手赛前称的体重都比规定的上限值少几磅。<br>Baby Sam <b>weighed in</b> at four kilos.<br>婴儿萨姆体重四公斤。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh ˈin</b></td><td class="c3">在讨论；辩论等中发表有分量的意见；做有；助益的事<br><span class="en">(with sth) (informal) to join in a discussion, an argument, etc. by saying sth important or doing sth to help</span></td><td class="c4">Weall <b>weighed in</b> with helpful suggestions.<br>我们纷纷献计献策。于，成就了。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˈweigh on sb/sth also ˈweigh upon sb/sth more formal</b></td><td class="c3">使担忧；使沮丧；加重…的思想负担；对…是艰巨的任务<br><span class="en">to make sb feel worried or depressed; to be a difficult duty or task for</span></td><td class="c4">The responsibilitles clearly <b>weighing</b> heavily on his shoulders.<br>他显然肩负重任，忧心忡忡。<br>The debt burden <b>weighs</b> heavily on the government.<br>政府债务负担沉重。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh sth ˈout</b></td><td class="c3">量出；称出(一定重量的东西)<br><span class="en">to measure a quantity of sth by weight</span></td><td class="c4"><b>Weigh out</b> all the ingredients before you start making the cake.<br>做蛋糕之前要先把配料都称好。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweigh sb ˈup</b></td><td class="c3">通过观察或交谈形成对…的看法；品评；判断<br><span class="en">to form an opinion of sb by watching them or talking to them</span></td><td class="c4">She stared at him, <b>weighing him up</b>.<br>她一边注视一边揣摩着他。<br>The two women <b>weighed each other up</b> for a few moments.<br>两个女人相互打量了一会儿。<br>He's certainly got Jeff <b>weighed up</b>.<br>他确实看透了杰夫。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 cont"></td><td class="c2"><b>weigh sth ˈup (against sth)</b></td><td class="c3">仔细考虑；斟酌；估量(情形)<br><span class="en">to think carefully about a situation before you decide what to do</span></td><td class="c4">I's important to <b>weigh up</b> all possible courses of action.<br>对所有可能的行动方案进行斟酌很重要。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>weight</b></td><td class="c2"><b>ˌweight sth ˈdown (with sth)</b></td><td class="c3">加重…的负荷以致其下弯；下沉等<br><span class="en">to add weight to sth so that it feels very heavy, bends down, sinks, etc.</span></td><td class="c4">The canvas sheet was <b>weighted down</b> to stop it blowing away.<br>帆布用重物压住了，防止被风刮走。<br>My pockets were <b>weighted down</b> with lots of small coins.<br>我的衣兜里装了很多小硬币，沉甸甸的。语态。</td></tr>
<tr><td class="c1 newword"><b>weld</b></td><td class="c2"><b>weld sb/sth ˈinto sth<br>ˌweld sb/sth to ˈgether</b></td><td class="c3">将…有效结合起来<br><span class="en">to unite sb/sth into an effective whole</span></td><td class="c4">The manager has <b>welded the players into</b> a strong team.<br>主教练把运动员组织成了一支强大的队伍。<br>The crisis helped to <b>weld</b> the community together.<br>这场危机促使整个社区紧密团结起来。</td></tr>
